The comparison characterizes complete implementations in this task; differences in preparation and hyperparameters limit attribution to feature representations or update rules alone.

papers.title: DeePEn - A Depth sensitive benchmark for Protein Engineering
papers.abstract: Recent progress in modeling techniques and high-throughput screening has significantly enhanced the accessibility of protein engineering. Nevertheless, further progress gets hindered by the lack of robust benchmarks that capture the practical challenges for real-world protein engineering. Here, we introduced DeePEn, a Depth-sensitive benchmark for Protein Engineering that quantifies model generalization to held-out variants at increasing mutational distance from the wild type. We defined distance as the number of simultaneous point mutations, i.e., single amino acid variants (SAVs), moving from wild-type to mutant (edit distance in computer science jargon). DeePEn retrospectively evaluates prediction and prioritization using experimentally labelled variants from deep mutational scanning (DMS) datasets; it does not benchmark prospective sequence generation or goal-directed optimization. Specifically selecting four DMS datasets with sufficient multi-mutation data points from ProteinGym, we assessed recent predictive models, including general and biophysics-informed protein Language Models (pLMs), and a non-transformer neural network. Our results highlight how the performance of all models deteriorates with increasing mutational distance and that no single metric sufficiently captures the diverse requirements of protein engineering. To overcome these shortcomings, DeePEn provides a readily available resource for multi-metric benchmarking that focuses on variant-effect prediction of variants distant from the wild type.

papers.title: Vermeer: Autoregressive generative modeling of microscopy predicts protein localization
papers.abstract: Fluorescent microscopy provides a rich view into how proteins localize within cells, but it remains experimentally infeasible to image human proteins across all of the different factors that can impact localization. We introduce Vermeer, a channel-adaptive autoregressive generative model for in silico generation of microscopy images of protein localization. Vermeer conditions generations on protein sequences and landmark stains showing the morphology of cells, which enables it to generalize to unseen proteins and cell lines. We show that Vermeer, trained on the Human Protein Atlas, can generate images with substantially improved perceptual quality and biological fidelity over previous proposals. Additionally, Vermeer's autoregressive framework enables flexible generation using varying channel subsets and orderings, enabling zero-shot transfer to data collected under different imaging conditions and channel configurations than those used for training. These results position Vermeer to enable scalable modeling of protein localization and is a step towards generative foundation models that can operate over distinct microscopy datasets. Code is publicly accessible at https://github.com/microsoft/vermeer.git.

papers.title: Impaired Sensory-motor Reconfiguration and Pupil-linked Arousal in Aging
papers.abstract: Mounting evidence points to a key role of the brainstem arousal systems in controlling the adaptation of behavior to changing contexts. Both, brainstem arousal systems and cognitive flexibility seem to deteriorate in aging. We hypothesized that these two impairments are related. To test this hypothesis in humans, we compared adaptive behavior and arousal dynamics between older and younger adults (60% women). Arousal dynamics were measured by means of luminance-independent pupil responses. Participants performed a hierarchical decision-making task, which required frequent switches between two stimulus-response mapping rules for reporting a perceptual categorization judgment. These rule switches were hidden, and participants needed to infer them from noisy evidence. Older adults were less accurate than younger adults. This impairment was due to more frequent use of the incorrect rule. Neither the perceptual categorization nor the detection of rule switches differed between age groups. Moments of high probability of rule switches were associated with pupil dilation in both age groups, which was, however, reduced in older people. We propose that impaired cognitive recruitment of pupil-linked arousal in aging might limit the ongoing reconfiguration of the neural pathways that support flexible cognitive behavior.

papers.title: Brain states recur during longitudinal viewing and relate to content across narratives and sensory formats
papers.abstract: Models of brain dynamics propose that brain activity revisits a repertoire of configurations, and that current input influences which configuration is expressed. How broadly this holds across a person's extended experience is unknown. We analyzed 38-57 hours of fMRI per participant in six adults watching the television series Friends. Participant-specific hidden Markov models identified 42-47 active brain states, and independent fits to separate portions of viewing recovered similar states with similar tendencies to recur. States matched across participants' separately fitted models tended to occur at the same moments of the episodes. Among states retained after temporal screening, features from pretrained video, audio, and language networks partly predicted state identity, most strongly from intermediate-to-late layers. Predictions learned from Friends generalized without retraining to new films, and language-based predictions extended to reading and audiobook listening. State usage corresponded across stimuli little beyond what each recording's spectra and covariance reproduced.

papers.title: Fast pairwise coalescence enables gene-resolution scans for selection in diverse human populations
papers.abstract: Pairwise coalescence times provide a way to compare genealogical variation across genomes and populations. We introduce \texttt{gamma\_smc\_cu}, a GPU implementation of \texttt{gamma\_smc} with accuracy comparable to the reference method in simulations. It processes 63{,}190 haplotype pairs in 15.91 seconds, 67.7-fold faster than the CPU reference. Applied to the 1000 Genomes Project, we use \texttt{gamma\_smc\_cu} to produce gene lists conspicuous for their low coalescence time across 26 populations and a catalog of 143 genomic regions of interest. We quantified genomic covariates, such as recombination rates and the relation with haplotype statistics to evaluate the regions. We further benchmark extensively using independent simulations to compare with summary statistics such as iHS and XP-EHH. Case studies at \textit{GRK2} and \textit{TREML1}/\textit{TREM2} illustrate these coalescence patterns and other regional evidence such as potential background selection or ancient genomic data derived tracks. We emphasise that positive and purifying selection can generate similar inferred profiles and provide a parameter search to show how both processes can lead to the same local signal. The software implemented here targets fast analysis capability of genealogical variation alongside a prioritization approach for regions of evolutionary significance.

papers.title: Input-dependent directionality of interactions between cortical areas
papers.abstract: Studying the temporal coordination of activity signals across areas is essential for understanding brain function. Recent studies using cross-covariances show that activity directionality can shift rapidly with behavioral or task demands; yet, the circuit mechanisms underlying these changes remain unclear. Here, we use recurrent network models to investigate how directional interactions emerge and are flexibly reconfigured in multi-area cortical circuits. We show that, for fixed connectivity, directionality is shaped by how common inputs align with recurrent connectivity and the associated internal timescales of activity. In multi-area circuits with locally balanced excitation and inhibition, this reveals a predominant role for inputs to excitatory over inhibitory populations in controlling directionality. These inputs govern the directionality of the latent signals that account for most of the shared activity across areas, predominantly reflecting widespread and coherent activity fluctuations. Our models capture key features of cross-covariances from primate areas V1 and V2 and suggest parsimonious candidate mechanisms for the shift in directionality reported in these areas. This work establishes a mechanistic framework for understanding dynamic changes in temporal coordination across brain areas.

papers.title: Emergent representations of graphical structure in mechanistic neural models of causal judgment
papers.abstract: Humans have a remarkable ability to judge causal relationships from a limited number of unreliable observations. Past work on causal cognition has largely focused on normative accounts of human behavior, leaving unknown how biologically plausible neural systems can learn causal relationships from observations and update representations of causal structure with additional evidence. Here, we leverage task-optimized recurrent neural networks to discover candidate implementation-level neural mechanisms of causal judgment. We propose a novel cognitive task in which a subject observes stochastic samples from an unknown causal structure (e.g. among variables A, B, and C with unknown causal relationships), and must judge whether a specific causal relationship is present given a query (e.g. "does A cause C?"). We found that, after training, recurrent neural networks perform the task at high accuracy, adopt strategies that incorporate observations from non-queried variables to form judgments, and exhibit neural activity with an emergent geometry reflecting underlying causal structure. We then use dynamical systems analysis to identify a set of low-level neural mechanisms that implement causal judgment and form representations of causal relationships. Together, these findings lay the groundwork for a "bottom-up" approach to causal cognition, providing a potential basis for experimental study in the brain.

papers.title: Default Feature Representations of the Cognitive Map
papers.abstract: Cognitive maps allow animals and artificial agents to predict where they are likely to go next, and computational models show how such predictive maps guide planning. Environments, however, rarely stay fixed. When the goal changes, a door closes, or a barrier appears, the predictive map needs to be updated. However, given that predictive maps look far ahead, a local change in the environment potentially influences what is predicted from many other states, including distant ones, even though the agent experiences it only locally. Here, we propose Default Feature Representations (DFR) to address this problem. Our solution separates a predictive map into a fixed set of features shared across environments and an operator that carries the current environment. We show that the operator has a model-based closed form when the structural change is known (DFR-MB), and we present a temporal-difference rule for learning it from sampled transitions (DFR-TD) and prove that it converges to the same solution. Using samples alone, DFR-TD efficiently learns the perturbed map, plans about as well as the model-based solution, and outperforms successor-representation baselines on replanning. The model also reproduces the local remapping of grid cells under environmental change, mirroring the stability of entorhinal grid fields across environments.

papers.title: Cell death and growth dynamics shape DNA-replication-based estimates of microbial growth
papers.abstract: A widely used approach for estimating bacterial growth rates is the origin-to-terminus ratio, or peak-to-trough ratio (PTR), which estimates DNA replication activity from origin and terminus copy numbers. Although PTR is theoretically related to bacterial growth rate, it is often compared with, or used to reason about, changes in population size, which reflect the balance between cell division and loss. These quantities may therefore diverge when cell death is appreciable. Here, we used stochastic, cell-based modelling and controlled laboratory experiments to examine how cell death affects the relationship between PTR and changes in population size. We show that transient stress-induced mortality and heterogeneous survival can cause PTR to fail to reflect changes in population size but still reflect bacterial growth rate. We experimentally validated these predictions by exposing \textit{Escherichia coli} to osmotic shock or antibiotics, and measuring change in population size and DNA replication activity. We further show that initial physiological state, lag before replication resumes, and abrupt growth arrest can alter the relationship between PTR and change in population size. In the presence of mortality, lag can make PTR more reflective of changes in population size whereas it decreases its correspondence with bacterial growth rate. Together, these results demonstrate how cell death and changes in replication dynamics can bias the interpretation of PTR-based estimates of population change under controlled laboratory conditions.

papers.title: Proteomic signatures of sublethal deltamethrin exposure in the European earwig
papers.abstract: Pesticides are ubiquitous in agroecosystems and pose substantial risks to non-target organisms. Traditional ecotoxicological assessments focus on survival, reproduction, or overt behavior, yet these endpoints may fail to detect subtle, molecular-level stress. Here, we investigated the effects of sublethal deltamethrin exposure on the head proteome of field-collected European earwig (Forficula auricularia) females, sampled at two life stages (pre-oviposition and post-family life) to account for physiological context. Our results reveal that deltamethrin induces a robust proteomic response shared across developmental stages, including the regulation of key detoxification enzymes (NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase, arginine kinase). In parallel, stage-specific responses were observed, involving proteins related to metabolism, stress response, and cellular organization. Strikingly, these molecular perturbations occurred without detectable changes in reproductive traits, highlighting a disconnect between cellular stress and organismal phenotypes. Several uncharacterized proteins were consistently regulated, representing promising targets for future studies on pesticide adaptation and potential detoxification pathways. Overall, these findings suggest that classical phenotypic assays may underestimate sublethal pesticide effects, and that proteomic profiling provides a sensitive framework to uncover underlying molecular responses. By integrating natural variability, realistic exposure, and reproductive physiology, our study emphasizes the need for molecular approaches in environmental risk assessment and offers a new perspective on the subtle, cryptic effects of agrochemicals.

papers.title: Inhibiting the interaction between the mitochondrial receptor Tom70 and SARS CoV 2 Orf9b with small molecules
papers.abstract: The SARS CoV 2 accessory protein Orf9b is in a complex monomer-dimer equilibrium that influences its interactions with the host mitochondrial receptor Tom70. This interaction is critical for viral suppression of a Type-1 interferon response during infection. Modulating this equilibrium with a small molecule, either by stabilizing the Orf9b dimer or blocking its interaction with Tom70, represents a promising strategy for restoring interferon signaling and the antiviral response. To build tool molecules that could test this concept, we performed two screens: a crystallographic fragment screen against the Orf9b homodimer and a high-throughput fluorescence polarization screen for competitors of an Orf9b-derived peptide binding to Tom70. Fragment screening revealed two binding sites with potential to be developed into an inhibitor: one located at the peripheral dimer interface and the other just outside the lipid-binding channel that defines the central dimer interface. Functionalization of the fragments outside of the lipid-binding channel with hydrophobic moieties stabilized the Orf9b dimer thereby indirectly inhibiting association with Tom70. In parallel, the high throughput screen for competitive inhibitors of the Tom70:Orf9b interaction discovered a separate series of molecules. These molecules display dynamic structure activity relationship (SAR) and could be improved in the future to modulate the interaction between Tom70 and potentially a wide range of substrates. Collectively, these results demonstrate the feasibility of two distinct strategies to manipulate the Orf9b-Tom70 equilibrium, which is critical to the host response to SARS CoV 2 infection.

papers.title: Subthreshold Asynchronous States and Computations in Biophysically Detailed Populations of Neurons
papers.abstract: Spikes are metabolically costly to generate and transmit, and spiking rates should be kept to a minimum for efficient coding. Many invertebrate circuits do not fire spikes or fire spikes at extremely low rates by using graded synaptic transmission as the communication mechanism between neurons. We show that computations and asynchronous states based on excitatory/inhibitory balance can exist without firing any spikes through self-sustaining subthreshold voltage fluctuations powered by graded synaptic transmission in networks of biophysically detailed Hodgkin-Huxley neurons. This novel subthreshold asynchronous state, which we call subthreshold voltage chaos, can be controlled for useful computation and pattern generation, also without firing spikes. Further, we identify candidate ion channels, low-voltage-activated T-Type calcium channels that provide a biophysical mechanism for this type of subthreshold computation. Our work demonstrates a mechanism for computation with graded synaptic release with very few spikes.

papers.title: Identifying molecular instructions to hard-wire a sensory neuron's synaptic connectivity
papers.abstract: The neural circuitry underlying innate behaviours must be pre-specified using precise molecular instructions. However, it is not clear what specific molecules are required to generate one neuron's wiring pattern that make it distinct from a neighboring neuron's wiring pattern. Here, we repeatedly sequenced three identified Drosophila sensory neurons that each have a unique and stereotyped hard-wired synaptic connectivity, to determine the cell-surface molecules that distinguish their identities. Repeated sequencing of the same neuron across different animals revealed that the variability of transcription is < 1%. We find that fewer than 100 cell-surface molecules can distinguish a mechanosensory neuron from a chemosensory neuron. Functional characterization of the cell-surface receptors verified their different roles in axonal and synaptic targeting. Finally, we expressed combinations of the different cell-surface receptors to mis-wire the chemosensory neuron and increase its axonal branching.

papers.title: Integrating citizen science and state agency data expands environmental coverage of occurrence data in invasive species distribution models
papers.abstract: Species distribution models (SDMs) are widely used to support risk assessment for invasive non-native plant species (invasive plants), but their performance is constrained by the coverage of occurrence data. Combining occurrences from citizen science (CS) platforms with data from state agency (StAg) monitoring may provide advantages, as these datasets follow different sampling strategies, yet they are rarely integrated. Here, we systematically compare how CS, StAg, and combined data influence the inferred environmental spaces, predictive discrimination, and spatial applicability of SDMs for three widespread invasive plants (A. altissima, H. mantegazzianum, I. glandulifera) in central Germany. We quantified overlap of sampled environmental space between datasets using PCA and Schoener's D and applied a hierarchical SDM utilizing boosted regression trees. We then assessed the Area of Applicability to identify environmental conditions outside of the training data for either model, which could represent priorities for additional monitoring. CS data were biased toward lower-elevation, urbanized environments, whereas StAg data captured higher-elevation, remote habitats, particularly along watercourses. Overlap was lowest for A. altissima, which is spreading, intermediate for H. mantegazzianum, associated with linear habitats, and highest for I. glandulifera, a widespread species, which may reflect differences in invasion stage and habitat associations as well as in sampling. Combined models had slightly higher mean AUC (0.85 +/- 0.07) and TSS (0.58 +/- 0.15), but overall discrimination did not differ significantly among data sources, and the best-performing source differed among species. Applicability (>59%) was high across data sources and species, with combined models showing weaker increases in environmental dissimilarity along environmental gradients. Thus, CS and StAg records sampled distinct parts of the environmental space, a difference reflected in suitability patterns and extrapolation but not detected by AUC and TSS. Integrating both sources broadened the environmental representation of occurrence records without removing their individual biases, which is relevant for invasive plants risk assessments.

papers.title: Multi-target biocontrol by avocado fungal endophytes and their metabolites
papers.abstract: Background: Endophytic fungi can contribute to host defense against pests and pathogens through insecticidal and/or antifungal activity. Here, we evaluated the multi-target biocontrol potential of 11 avocado endophytic fungal strains against three plant pathogens (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides, Fusarium solani and Phytophthora cinnamomi) and two insect pests (Sitophilus zeamais and Xyleborus bispinatus) and analyzed the metabolomic profile of the two fungal strains with strongest bioactivity. Results: Trichoderma species exhibited the strongest pathogen inhibition in dual-culture and diffusible compound assays. Purpureocillium and Pochonia strains combined pathogen inhibition through diffusible metabolites with strong insecticidal activity, supporting their multi-target potential. Ethyl acetate (EtOAc) extracts from strain Trichoderma 3 inhibited all phytopathogens, whilst strain Purpureocillium extracts were most active against P. cinnamomi. Compounds tentatively identified as macrocyclic trichothecenes (Trichoderma 3) and cyclosporine-like cyclic peptides (Purpureocillium) were potentially responsible for the displayed bioactivity. Conclusion: Avocado endophytic fungi and their crude extracts show promising potential for multi-target biocontrol, whilst their metabolomic profiles provide candidate compounds for further chemical isolation and bioactivity evaluation.

papers.title: Bulk transcriptomic subtypes in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSC) are readouts of tumor cellular composition
papers.abstract: High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSC) is classified into four transcriptomic subtypes that are reproducible across cohorts but have not informed treatment. These subtypes are associated with stromal and immune content, yet they are assigned from bulk expression, from which composition is also estimated. We tested whether composition alone determines subtype. In tumors constructed from single cells with epithelial cells held constant, varying a single cell type within the range observed in primary tumors reassigned the subtype, and known composition distinguished all four subtypes. Varying epithelial cell identity at fixed composition displaced tumors approximately half as far in expression space. Across 2,161 primary tumors from ten cohorts, composition structured the leading axes of expression and predicted subtype in held-out cohorts (ROC-AUC 0.817 to 0.963). The consequence is prognostic. Adjustment for composition largely attenuated subtype associations with survival, whereas fibroblast content remained prognostic. Subtype-associated biology and prognosis therefore largely reflect the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Genomic offsets predict observed kelp declines and suggest benefits of assisted migration in the Northeast Pacific
papers.abstract: Kelp forests are widely distributed along temperate and polar coastlines worldwide and are among the world's most productive and diverse marine ecosystems. Yet, due in part to ocean warming, they are declining in many parts of the world. While genomic tools can identify local adaptation and have shown potential to predict species' responses to global change, these predictions have rarely been validated, hampering their widespread use in conservation practice. Here, we applied a seascape genomics approach to investigate environmental adaptation in the two main canopy-forming species of the Northeast Pacific, Macrocystis tenuifolia and Nereocystis luetkeana. We leveraged whole-genome sequences of 598 individuals across 94 sites along the British Columbia and Washington coasts, together with 37 environmental variables. Both species showed genomic signatures of local adaptation, with distinct environmental drivers shaping adaptation in each species despite their co-occurrence across much of the studied area. Using gradient forests, we modelled the genetic turnover across environmental gradients and estimated genomic offsets under projected environmental conditions. Genomic offsets differed greatly among regions in both species and help explain contrasting patterns of kelp vulnerability and resilience observed in local-scale studies. For Macrocystis, genomic offsets strongly predicted population declines observed to date, validating the link between genomic models and outcomes in the field and allowing us to translate genomic predictions into an ecologically meaningful metric: the risk of extirpation under global change. For Nereocystis, genomic offsets did not predict population declines well, suggesting that the environmental factors we modelled are not the primary drivers of Nereocystis persistence. Our models predict that assisted migration, even short-distance migration, could significantly attenuate kelp's vulnerability to global change. Our results highlight the potential of seascape genomics to predict vulnerability of populations to global change and can inform conservation strategies to improve the resilience and sustainable management of these vulnerable ecosystems.

papers.title: Panmap: Scalable phylogeny-guided alignment, genotyping, and placement on pangenomes
papers.abstract: Pangenomes capture population-level variation but remain computationally challenging at scale. We present Panmap, a tool that leverages evolutionary structure to place, align, and genotype sequencing reads against mutation-annotated pangenomes containing up to millions of genomes. Panmap introduces a phylogenetically compressed k-mer index that stores only sequence differences along branches, enabling efficient comparison of reads to both sampled genomes and inferred ancestors. This approach reduces index size by up to 600-fold and construction time by over three orders of magnitude relative to existing tools. Panmap places a 100x coverage SARS-CoV-2 sample onto 20,000 genomes in 0.4 seconds and onto 8 million genomes in under two minutes. Furthermore, it enables accurate haplotype identification and abundance estimation in metagenomic samples and sensitive placement of ancient environmental DNA without prior alignment. Our approach makes large-scale pangenomes directly amenable to read mapping, genome assembly, alignment-free phylogenetic placement, and metagenomic analysis.

papers.title: Shared Molecular Signatures and Pathways in Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder, Schizophrenia, and Bipolar Disorder: An Integrative Transcriptomic and Machine-Learning Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective: Psychiatric disorders such as post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder (BD) are complex conditions with overlapping molecular features that remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify shared molecular abnormalities and potential therapeutic targets associated with these disorders. Methods: RStudio (version 4.4.1) was used to process and analyze gene expression datasets from the NCBI database to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs). FunRich, DAVID, STRING, and NetworkAnalyst were used for gene ontology and pathway enrichment, protein-protein interaction analysis, transcription factor and microRNA regulatory network analysis, and protein-chemical interaction analysis. The discriminatory ability of prioritized hub genes and transcription factors was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Four machine-learning algorithms (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM-RBF, and Gradient Boosting) were compared using leave-one-out cross-validation on the GSE403628 dataset, comprising 14 controls and 14 cases. Results: Among 32 common genes, several candidate hub proteins were identified, including HLA-DRA, HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-DOB, and BRD2. The analysis also identified transcription factors (FOXC1, NFYA, RELA, GATA2, FOXL1, SRF, and NFIC), miRNAs (hsa-mir-129-2-3p, hsa-mir-148b-3p, hsa-mir-196a-5p, hsa-mir-26a-5p, hsa-mir-27a-3p, hsa-mir-23b-3p, hsa-mir-500a-3p, hsa-mir-423-5p, hsa-miR-142-5p, and hsa-miR-671-5p), and chemicals, including estradiol, antirheumatic agents, and valproic acid. ROC analysis showed the highest AUC for HLA-DRA (0.760) among hub genes and FOXC1 (0.658) among transcription factors. The hub-gene set consistently outperformed the transcription-factor set across all four machine-learning algorithms, with Logistic Regression achieving the highest AUC (0.800). Random Forest and SVM-RBF achieved the highest accuracy (0.679) under leave-one-out cross-validation. Conclusion: This computational approach identified potential biomarkers linking PTSD, schizophrenia, and BD to immune-related and infectious disease pathways. ROC and machine-learning analyses highlighted HLA-DRA as a promising discriminator between disease and control samples, providing candidate molecular targets for further investigation.

papers.title: DemuxHMM: Large-Scale Single-Cell Embryo Profiling via Recombination Barcoding
papers.abstract: High-resolution developmental time-courses with single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) increasingly target trajectory inference and other analyses in the study of development and disease. Researchers can efficiently generate these datasets by pooling individuals and inferring cell-to-individual mappings after sequencing, in a process called demultiplexing. Existing demultiplexing methods face limitations in the number of timepoints they can support, due to either the need for individual-by-individual processing or reduced accuracy at large numbers of individuals. To address these limitations, we introduce a computational framework for demultiplexing large-scale, individual-resolved datasets. Our framework includes a recombination-aware demultiplexing method, DemuxHMM, which uses a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) to explicitly model contiguous SNP patterns that arise from simple breeding schemes. We demonstrate substantial performance and scalability gains from this recombination-aware approach on both a real Diversity Outbred (DO) mouse data and a simulated Drosophila dataset. This performance demonstrates the value of the method when used for common applications on model organisms such as time series, crossover position inference, and eQTLS, among others.

papers.title: Ex vivo autologous immune cell assay to study modulation of type 2 Inflammation by processed- or novel food extracts in peanut allergy
papers.abstract: Peanut allergy represents a major food-allergy burden, raising concerns about food processing and novel dietary products. Current diagnostics assess primarily allergic endpoints rather than immune mechanisms initiating and maintaining type 2 inflammation, particularly DC2-mediated Th2 polarization. Here, an ex vivo autologous type 2 inflammatory monocyte-derived dendritic cell (moDC) DC2/T cell and B cell assay has been introduced enabling to study immunomodulatory effects induced by unprocessed (P-D) versus processed (P-DH (heated) or P-DHG (heated and glycated)) peanut proteins. Separately, different emerging food samples were assessed (protein concentrates or whole biomass) enabling to study their capacities to modify inflammatory DC2/T cell responses. CD14+ monocytes, CD4+ T cells and CD19+ B cells were isolated from six peanut-allergic patients' PBMCs. MoDCs generated with IL4/GM-CSF were exposed (48h) to type 2 polarizing cytokine (DC2) mix, or DC2 mix combined with the food samples. Next, DC2s were co-cultured with T cells (5d), followed by B cells incubation with DC2/T cell supernatant and food samples (10d). Supernatants and cells were analyzed for Th1/Th2/Th-regulatory (Treg) cells, IgE and IgG profiles. DC2 induced a strong Th2 phenotype and activity, P-D DC2 further enhanced IL13 secretion and %Tregs. P-DH DC2 favored Th2, whereas P-DHG DC2 increased IFN{gamma}, with neither increasing %Treg. P-D and P-DH DC2 increased CD40L+CD25+ memory Th2, and P-DHG showed the same tendency. Wheat, whey and seaweed biomass had little effect on DC2/Th2 driven type 2 inflammation at the dose studied, whereas algae showed distinct immunomodulatory, adjuvant-like activity upon co-exposure during inflammatory DC2 maturation. In conclusion, this autologous in vitro assay captures modification of type 2 inflammatory response in DC2-Th2 interaction, which can compile both allergen-specific and generic reactivity to food samples, supporting the potential future use of this assay as an additional tool to assess type 2-driving potential and possible allergenicity of emerging foods and processing methods in peanut-allergic patients.

papers.title: Substrate binding and activation mechanism of the essential bacterial septal cell wall synthase FtsW
papers.abstract: Septal peptidoglycan (sPG) synthesis in most bacteria is driven by the essential, highly conserved FtsWIQLB synthase complex, comprising the SEDS (Shape, Elongation, Division, and Sporulation) glycosyltransferase FtsW, the monofunctional transpeptidase FtsI, and the scaffolding and regulatory subcomplex FtsQLB. Although apo structures of FtsWIQLB are known, no substrate-bound structures exist, likely due to the intrinsic flexibility of lipid II (L2) substrates. Here, we combined all-atom molecular dynamics simulations of E. coli FtsWIQLB with cysteine-based mutagenesis and cell-based assays to investigate donor and acceptor L2 binding sites in FtsW and to elucidate the complex's activation mechanism. We show that conserved arginine residues adjacent to membrane-accessible cavities in FtsW coordinate donor and acceptor L2 pyrophosphate groups, stabilizing substrate binding. The FtsWIQLB complex appears to adopt a self-inhibitory architecture in which gating elements and a periplasmic loop prevent the donor and acceptor from approaching FtsW's catalytic residue D297. Activation by FtsN or a superfission FtsW variant relieves these constraints, stabilizes acceptor-site binding, and reorients both substrates into a catalytically primed state. Long donor glycan chains further stabilize this activated conformation at the acceptor site, possibly promoting processive sPG polymerization. Comparative modeling of ESKAPE pathogen homologs reveals both conserved and divergent features of binding-site engagement and activation. We corroborate these computational findings with cysteine-based mutagenesis and crosslinking experiments. These results establish a mechanistic framework for FtsW substrate recognition and functional activation, highlighting tractable sites for structure- and mechanism-based antibiotic discovery targeting SEDS-class cell wall synthases.

papers.title: The TRIM32 granule promotes TDP-43 inclusion formation and amyloid aggregation through shuttle condensates
papers.abstract: Aberrant protein aggregation and inclusion formation are hallmarks of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD), which share overlapping genetic and pathological features. Similar aggregates are increasingly recognized in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy (LATE). However, it remains unclear whether a shared molecular pathway drives this pathological aggregation. Here, we report the formation of stress-responsive cytoplasmic TRIM32 granules, distinct from stress granules. The E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM32, together with the shuttle factor UBQLN2 and the autophagy adaptor p62/SQSTM1, drive condensation of TRIM32 granules that depend on E3 ligase activity and a network of intermolecular interactions. These condensates act as scaffolds that capture client proteins, including TDP-43 and ANXA11, and modulate their mobility. A unique hydrophobic loop within TRIM32's substrate-binding domain mimics low-complexity motifs in ANXA11 and TDP-43, enabling selective retention via competitive binding mediated by the UBQLN2 STI1 domain. Moreover, TRIM32 granules promote amyloid aggregation of TDP-43, an effect that is exacerbated by a pathogenic UBQLN2 mutation. In brains from individuals with diverse neurodegenerative diseases, TRIM32 co-localizes with pathological phospho-TDP-43 (pTDP-43) inclusions, supporting a model that TRIM32-driven granules function as selective proteostasis sorting compartments that broadly contribute to TDP-43 proteinopathy.

papers.title: Intellectual disability risk gene RFX4 regulates cortical neurogenesis by restraining neuronal differentiation
papers.abstract: Despite the recent identification of RFX4 as a neurodevelopmental disorder risk gene, its role in cortical development remained unclear. Here, we derived human stem cell models of deficiency and pathogenic mutation and demonstrated that RFX4 restrains neurogenesis by repressing pro-neuronal gene expression, while maintaining lineage-specific roles in regulating proliferation during cortical inhibitory neuron development. We also defined requirements for RFX4 in recruiting RFX3 to chromatin to regulate synaptic and activity-dependent gene expression in progenitors and neurons, respectively. RFX4 deficiency persistently dysregulated neuronal differentiation in cortical organoids, while not affecting neurons generated by direct differentiation. Finally, we modeled pathogenic mutation of the RFX4 DNA-binding domain, finding that DNA binding was strongly reduced but gene expression was dysregulated differently from our deficiency models, supporting a mechanism of pathogenicity distinct from haploinsufficiency. Together, this work identified requirements for RFX4 during cortical development, building a necessary foundation for elucidating the etiology of RFX4-associated disorders.

papers.title: Nanocellulose hydrogels as bio-interface analogs for studying nanomaterial transport and accumulation
papers.abstract: Nanoparticles have been proposed as drug delivery vehicles to enhance targeting and efficiency of traditional and novel therapeutics. Previous studies have identified size, surface charge, and volume exclusion as factors that influence nanoparticle diffusion and retention. However, there is little accepted or successful quantification of how these parameters influence nanoparticle penetration relative to biological adaptation and biological response. Part of the challenge is the response of living biological interfaces to many of these nanoparticle delivery vehicles and nanosized drugs. This study aimed to emulate key physicochemical barriers to diffusion found in living biomaterials by developing a tunable, synthetic hydrogel. Through the controlled exposure of 150 kDa and 2 MDa nanodextrans with neutral and negative surface charge, we evaluated the system's ability to emulate three core physicochemical features often implicated in biofilm-associated transport resistance: size exclusion, charge interactions, and volume exclusion. We demonstrated a 30% statistically significant decrease in partition coefficients for 2 MDa nanodextran from 150 kDa nanodextran, confirming the ability of the nanocellulose-based microcaps to size based exclusion of hydrated biomaterial matrices. We combined our results with bioaccumulation data from the literature and found only the interaction of size and charge had a statistically significant effect (p-value < 0.05, F-statistic = 4.8). This controllable system can be coupled with in silico modeling to understand interfacial transport phenomena for nanomaterial-biomaterial interactions.

papers.title: The performance of genetic-constraint metrics varies significantly across the human noncoding genome
papers.abstract: A longstanding goal in human genetics is to prioritize noncoding loci that, when disrupted, lead to developmental disorders and other Mendelian traits. In pursuit of this goal, multiple metrics have been developed to distinguish neutrally evolving sequences from those subjected to purifying selection. These metrics are commonly evaluated genome-wide, e.g., by computing a precision-recall curve on windows tiling the entire noncoding genome. Here, we identify parts of the noncoding genome where these metrics are distorted due to "bias" in the underlying models of neutral genetic variation and underperform due to a low "signal-to-noise ratio" in the genetic data. The most extreme effects are found for Gnocchi (Chen et al. 2024), the performance of which declines as GC content increases. We trace the source of the bias in Gnocchi to a mismatch between the training set of de novo mutations (DNMs) used to adjust expected SNP counts and the genomic windows on which those expected counts are computed. Resolving that mismatch produces a more calibrated version of Gnocchi, significantly improving its interpretability in applications. Looking forward, we suggest annotating constraint scores of noncoding genomic intervals with robust measures of the bias of the corresponding model, allowing users to gauge confidence in those scores.

papers.title: An expanded structural and biochemical map of GLI-SUFU recognition identifies binding-defective disease variants
papers.abstract: The tumor suppressor SUFU is a key negative regulator of oncogenic GLI transcription factors. SUFU mutations predispose to medulloblastoma and can cause Gorlin and Joubert syndromes. Limited structural information is available on the GLI-SUFU complex, contributing to the fact that the vast majority of SUFU missense variants sequenced from affected patients are of unknown clinical significance. Using AlphaFold3 and complementary computational analysis, we predicted structures of the three human GLI-SUFU complexes and the orthologous Drosophila Ci-Sufu complex, revealing previously unrecognized contact interfaces. By site-directed mutagenesis and GLI-SUFU binding assays, we validated the importance of key interface residues, many of which are mutated in familial medulloblastoma and Gorlin syndrome. These findings provide new structure-function insights into a signaling complex mutated in cancer and rare congenital diseases, and offer an expanded framework for interpreting clinically observed SUFU variants and mechanisms that tune SUFU repression.

papers.title: Auditory cortex deviance detection represents a canonical difference signal
papers.abstract: Context modulates neural processing of sensory stimuli. Excitatory neuron responses are most often suppressed to stimuli that are typical of the current context and augmented to stimuli that are deviant. These effects have been extensively studied in basic and clinical neuroscience using oddball paradigms, involving the repeating of standard stimuli and the insertion of rare deviant stimuli. Augmented neural responses to deviants - referred to as deviance detection - have been interpreted within predictive coding frameworks as prediction errors, signaling the difference between internal predictions and actual sensory input. However, most oddball paradigms simultaneously alter both predictions and input, so cannot test for a true difference signal. As yet, no studies have demonstrated that neural deviance detection during oddball paradigms specifically encodes the difference between internal predictions and unexpected sensory input, as opposed to, e.g., a generalised surprise signal or augmented bottom-up signaling. Here we compare neural responses to auditory stimuli across oddball paradigm variants.In a classical oddball paradigm, responses of putative excitatory neurons in the primary auditory cortex (A1) to auditory deviants contain information about recent frequency change and retain a memory trace of previous stimulus context. Interestingly, in a fixed-deviant oddball paradigm where the standards (theoretical predictions) were altered between blocks, but deviant stimulus features remain unchanged, neural response patterns encoded standard-to-deviant frequency difference. Together, these findings support the interpretation that A1 deviance detection contains a sensory prediction error that represents the difference between prediction and sensory input, a corollary of the predictive coding framework.

papers.title: Lipid-Mediated Control of ER Function During Apoptosis
papers.abstract: Lipid-derived metabolites act as potent regulators of cell fate by disrupting organelle homeostasis, yet the mechanisms by which they trigger apoptosis remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigate how the sphingolipid-derived aldehyde trans-2-hexadecenal (t-2-hex) promotes apoptotic signaling through coordinated effects on endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and mitochondrial function in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. We show that t-2-hex induces ER stress and activates the unfolded protein response via the canonical Ire1-Hac1 pathway, while simultaneously impairing mitochondrial protein import. Mechanistically, we identify the ER chaperone Kar2/BiP as a direct target of covalent lipidation by t-2-hex at a conserved cysteine residue, resulting in defective protein folding and proteostasis collapse. We further define the ER-associated short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase Fmp52 as a critical protective factor that, together with the mitochondrial aldehyde dehydrogenase Hfd1, counteracts lipid-induced stress. Notably, the human ortholog Tip30 functionally substitutes for Fmp52, highlighting evolutionary conservation. Our findings uncover a lipid-mediated mechanism that coordinately disrupts ER and mitochondrial proteostasis to drive apoptosis, and identify Fmp52/Tip30 as a conserved safeguard against lipid-induced cytotoxicity.

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of Assumption Lean Community Detection Methods for Human Connectome Networks
papers.abstract: Community detection on resting-state functional connectivity provides a principled lens on mesoscale organization in functional brain networks. The choice of community count K, lacks a standardized or principled guideline. We conducted a benchmark of three approaches that do not a priori restrict communities to an assortative mesoscale topology: the Weighted Stochastic Block Model, Spectral Clustering, and K-means Clustering. Performance was assessed on synthetic networks with ground truth and on three neuroimaging cohorts which included adult and infant datasets. We compared several strategies for selecting K, including the silhouette index and other approaches commonly used in the literature. These were evaluated alongside a likelihood-based criterion for the weighted stochastic block model that employs bootstrap confidence intervals for differences in log-likelihood between successive values of K. For the synthetic networks, WSBM and Spectral Clustering correctly identified the true number of communities, whereas K-means Clustering did not. In adult datasets, most indices did not yield a unique optimum, whereas the likelihood-based criterion selected K=11, which is consistent with established sensory and association systems. In infants and toddlers, the same procedure supports a larger K around 15 and reveals developmentally distinct mesoscale architecture, including anterior and posterior subdivisions within default mode and frontoparietal systems.

papers.title: Detection of zoonotic Cryptosporidium parvum in invasive beavers from southern Tierra del Fuego, Chile
papers.abstract: Since their introduction to Tierra del Fuego in 1946, invasive beavers have expanded their population and caused extensive environmental degradation across the subantarctic region. Beaver dams have profoundly impacted peatlands, mature sub-Antarctic forests, and watercourses. Here, we report a pathogen in invasive beavers in Patagonia and discuss their potential role as a reservoir of waterborne zoonotic pathogens. We detected Cryptosporidium through microscopy using the Ziehl-Neelsen staining technique in beaver collected from southern Tierra del Fuego. Out of the 105 beavers examined, three tested positive to optical microscopy, which were then identified molecularly as Cryptosporidium parvum by sequence analysis of the 18S ribosomal DNA (rDNA). Given the potential impacts of Cryptosporidium parvum upon native species, wildlife, and human health, this finding highlights the potential risks associated with the ongoing expansion of beavers into other areas of the sub-Antarctic region. A potential role of invasive beavers as reservoirs of zoonotic Cryptosporidium spp. in Patagonia emphasizes the unknown consequences of human-introduced exotic species on pristine ecosystems.

papers.title: Activity drives local CaMKII synthesis and subcellular localization via autophosphorylation-dependent pathways
papers.abstract: Strong repeated stimulation of a neuron triggers an increase in local protein synthesis along with a change in localization of proteins, allowing the neuron to rapidly adjust its proteome in response to activity. One of these proteins, calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII), is involved in mediating structural and functional changes after activity. While postsynaptic CaMKII translation has been studied, very little is known about presynaptic synthesis, including its mechanisms and the functional consequences. We utilized the Drosophila larval neuromuscular junction (NMJ) as a model to study the molecular requirements for activity-dependent synthesis along with the localization of CaMKII protein. Presynaptic-specific tagging of endogenous CaMKII demonstrates that spaced stimulation rapidly increases presynaptic CaMKII through local translation of pre-existing mRNA, independently of somatic factors. This activity-dependent synthesis requires the distal 3' untranslated region (3'UTR) of the CaMKII mRNA, which is also necessary for steady-state synaptic accumulation. Additionally, we show that activity-dependent synthesis requires CaMKII T287 autophosphorylation-induced activation of the PI3K/Akt/mTor pathway. While activity-dependent redistribution of CaMKII has been previously identified, very little is known about how local synthesis and translocation may interact to define different pools of protein that may have distinct functions. We demonstrate that CaMKII with a T287D phosphomimetic mutant localizes to the synaptic membrane and pulse-chase experiments show that the localization of newly-synthesized CaMKII differs from pre-existing CaMKII, indicating neuronal activity generates spatially distinct, and likely functionally distinct, CaMKII populations which may underlie long-lasting plasticity.

papers.title: Exponential Map Models as an Interpretable Framework for Generating Neural Spatial Representations
papers.abstract: A foundational challenge in neuroscience and AI is understanding how physical space is mapped into neural representations. While artificial neural networks can learn brain-like spatial representations, their ``black-box'' nature obscures whether these representations reflect general principles or artifacts of specific architectures, objectives or optimization choices, offering no guarantee that solutions for tasks like path integration generalize beyond training data. Here, we use a first-principles framework based on the matrix exponential, in which generator matrices map physical locations to neural population vectors without gradient-based optimization. Within this formalism, navigational properties follow directly from algebraic constraints on the generators: commuting generators enable trajectory-invariant, exact path integration, while skew-symmetry yields equinorm representations with translation-invariant similarities. Preserving the flat Euclidean metric further constrains the generator spectra to balanced wavevector configurations, such as the roots-of-unity constellations that generate periodic grid fields. Similarity preservation further produces localized place-like fields, and extending the generators to a context signal models context-dependent remapping. Beyond its algebraic relation to continuous attractor and oscillatory interference models, the framework natively supports goal-oriented multi-map navigation through hyperdimensional bundling and binding, fits recorded grid and place cell data, extrapolates their rate maps far beyond the fitted region, and makes testable predictions for entorhinal circuits. By grounding spatial representations in exact algebraic conditions, this work offers a transparent alternative to empirical representation learning, revealing the conditions under which a coherent neural map of space arises.

papers.title: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase organization is crucial for mammalian brain development
papers.abstract: Central nervous system development relies on spatially regulated protein synthesis, which includes the aminoacylation of tRNAs. Developmental brain disorders, such as leukodystrophies, can be caused by the exclusion of Arginyl-tRNA synthetase (RARS1) from the multi-tRNA synthetase complex, which does not affect its enzymatic function. To understand the purpose of aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase complex formation, we engineered a mouse line where RARS1 is untethered from the complex in forebrains. We observed profound behavioral phenotypes and anatomical changes originating from a severe reduction in oligodendrocytes and subsequent myelination defects. On the molecular level, disruption of the multi-tRNA synthetase complex caused RARS1 mis-trafficking, which resulted in lost colocalization with ribosomes, leading to the concomitant activation of integrated stress response. Proteomics analysis of newly synthesized proteins suggested that mRNA translation in cellular projections was specifically reduced, affecting myelin structural proteins. In summary, exclusion of RARS1 from the multisynthetase complex led to its altered subcellular localization and decreased protein synthesis in oligodendrocyte projections, directly linking molecular effects to white matter pathologies. Altogether, our results reveal the necessity of aminoacylation organization for mammalian neurodevelopment.

papers.title: A Proteome-Wide Gain-of-Function Atlas Mapping the Landscape of Chemotherapy Response
papers.abstract: Background: Conventional chemotherapies remain the core therapeutic backbone of cancer treatment, yet the rapid emergence of chemoresistance often compromises their clinical efficacy. Although large-scale functional genomics has transformed precision oncology, existing reference maps rely predominantly on loss-of-function paradigms and lack systematic data on gain-of-function (GOF) events that commonly drive clinical resistance. Methods: To address this gap, we engineered a site-specific Bxb1 integrase landing-pad system in HeLa cells, enabling single-copy integration of a human proteome-wide library [18,388 open reading frames (ORFs)] at the AAVS1 locus under a uniform EF1 promoter. We systematically profiled cellular fitness across 16 chemotherapeutics. We integrated this GOF perturbation screen with bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, FACS-based lysosomal functional screening, clinical cohort survival analyses, and preclinical xenograft modeling. Results: Stratified modeling of over 230,000 gene-drug interactions defined distinct functional categories that are strongly enriched for clinical cancer biomarkers and prognostic relevance. Global network analysis and organelle-specific lysosomal functional screening uncovered that chemotherapeutic agents, most prominently the nucleoside analog TAS-102 (Lonsurf), converge upon a shared survival hub centered on the BCL-2 family-associated autophagy-endolysosomal network. Mechanistically, TAS-102 triggered lysosomal activation as an adaptive survival response. Co-treatment with the BCL-2 family inhibitor ABT-263 (Navitoclax) attenuated this TAS-102-induced lysosomal response and synergistically reversed TAS-102 resistance across colorectal and pancreatic cancer models in vitro and in colorectal cell line- and patient-derived xenograft (CDX, PDX) models in vivo. Conclusions: Our study establishes an open-access, proteome-wide GOF reference atlas that systematically maps chemotherapeutic responses, recapitulates canonical resistance biology, and nominates rational drug combinations. This systems-genomics resource bridges massive-scale perturbation mapping with actionable target discovery, providing a translational framework to overcome therapeutic resistance and reprogram cancer drug responses.

papers.title: Interplay of immigration and coevolution constrains the structure of specialist-generalist communities
papers.abstract: Species and populations in nature fall along a specialist-generalist continuum in habitat preferences and resource use. Despite a rich literature on the evolution of specialization at the population level, most studies focusing on community assembly, species packing and diversification have considered solely niche positions within a community. Yet, empirical evidence suggests that generalism levels in communities respond dynamically to the current biotic environment and species interactions. Here, we jointly consider niche positions and generalism, and ask how different modes of community assembly - from evolutionary assembly to repeated immigration - shape the resulting community. We find that coevolution can lead to diversification, including spontaneous emergence of asymmetric configurations of generalist and specialist phenotypes. We further observe distinct alternative evolutionary endpoints, comprising communities consisting of either many specialists or fewer generalists, some of which are only locally uninvasible. More broadly, we show how the history of local coevolution and dispersal events jointly influence community dynamics and structure. By modeling assembly along a continuum from pure coevolution to pure dispersal, we highlight how high rates of evolution constrain richness while promoting generalism, partly because evolutionary assembly can get stuck at local optima. In contrast, communities shaped by immigration tend to be more species-rich, with diverse and specialist characters. Finally, higher rates of evolution decrease invasion success in mixed-assembly scenarios, a pattern consistent with community monopolization. We discuss how our theoretical findings match observational and experimental evidence for community assembly across scales.

papers.title: Organ-specific transcriptomic and proteomic changes in thermomorphogenesis in Arabidopsis thaliana seedlings
papers.abstract: Plant acclimatisation to mild, yet prolonged temperature increases is critical for survival amid global warming. Temperature increases within the physiological range (24-30C, for the model Arabidopsis thaliana Col-0) promote coordinated response across the different plant organs, termed thermomorphogenesis. However, most transcriptomic studies analyse whole-seedling material, hindering insights into organ-specific responses. Here, we analysed public whole-seedling transcriptomes and produced transcriptomic and proteomic data for root, hypocotyl, and cotyledon in Arabidopsis under warm temperature (28C vs 21C). Although independent whole-seedling datasets showed broad rank-order concordance, standard thresholding for differentially expressed genes (DEGs) yielded limited cross-study overlap. We compared DEGs in whole seedling and dissected organs and observed that 67% of up-regulated and 78% of down-regulated genes in whole seedling are not DEGs in any individual organ, evidencing a need for organ-specific data. We then found that warm temperature mostly suppressed protein accumulation in hypocotyl, likely through translational inhibition. Furthermore, comparison of differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) and DEGs revealed widespread post-transcriptional regulation and transcriptional buffering. We identified several promising genes still uncharacterized for a function in thermomorphogenesis, such as DRG1-3 (up DEG in all organs and seedling), MSRB6 (up DEG in all organs and seedling, but down DEP in root and hypocotyl), AGL20/SOC1 (down DEG in all organs and most seedling datasets), and TPX2/PRXIIC (up DEP and DEG in root and most seedling datasets). Our organ-specific resource presents a detailed view on plant response to warm temperature and open new questions and research avenues in thermomorphogenesis.

papers.title: Originality in creative ideation evolves along nonlinear axes in the human brain
papers.abstract: The ability to think creatively is fundamental to human cognition, shaping how we interact with the world and navigate complex problems. Creativity depends on the activity of multiple large-scale brain networks, but the neural representations that underlie creative thought and distinguish it from other cognitive states remains unclear. Here, we use multiscale intracranial electrophysiology--from single-unit recordings to local field potentials across distributed brain networks--to discover how the human brain generates creative ideas. Our results demonstrate that cortical networks in the human brain display activity patterns that differentiate creative thinking from non-creative cognitive processes such as arithmetic calculations. We found that the underlying geometry of neural activity in the default mode network is shaped by instantaneous cognitive state. Further, in the dorsal attention network, we uncovered nonlinear, high-dimensional representations of moment-by-moment fluctuations in creative performance. These representations define a neural creativity axis that is shared between network-level and single-neuron computations. Our findings reveal widespread neural representations of cognitive state and suggest distinct roles of specific cortical networks in controlling creativity, with the default mode network enabling creative states, while higher-dimensional dorsal attention network activity, associated with attentional selection or other context-dependent constraints, reflects the production of more original responses.

papers.title: Cerebrospinal Fluid Inflammation in Prodromal Parkinson's Disease
papers.abstract: We hypothesized that prodromal Parkinson's disease (PD), characterized by rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (RBD) and/or hyposmia, begins with inflammation in the central nervous system that evolves into neurodegeneration. We combined clinical phenotyping and proteomics with single-cell RNA sequencing of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and blood from individuals with RBD, PD, and healthy controls, with multiple sclerosis as a comparator. CSF immune cell numbers were increased in RBD, particularly in those with lower prodromal PD probability scores, a composite score associated with time to phenoconversion. In these participants, CSF macrophages showed enhanced TNF, IL-6/JAK/STAT3, and interferon-{gamma} signaling and predicted crosstalk with CD4+ T cells involving TNF, antigen presentation, and costimulatory pathways. CSF Macrophages resembled mouse dural macrophages and shared TNF signaling with gut immune cells from -synuclein mouse models. These findings uncover a stage-specific TNF-associated inflammation involving crosstalk between CSF Macrophages and CD4+ T cells in prodromal PD.

papers.title: Retrieval practice is associated with attenuated stress-related inference impairment and stronger reactivation of bridge-related category information
papers.abstract: A hallmark of human memory is its ability to form novel inferences by linking discrete but related events. We examined whether acute stress impairs memory inference and if retrieval practice can buffer this effect. Participants were trained on image pairs, AB and BC, to establish interconnected triads (ABC) with a shared bridge element B. Twenty-four hours later, we induced acute stress in half of the participants and then tested their capacity to infer the indirect AC associations. Behavioral results indicated that acute stress reduced inference accuracy and slowed responses, and retrieval practice was associated with attenuation of stress-induced impairment in A-C inference accuracy and speed. Using multivariate decoding analysis of human electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings, we found neural evidence of rapid reactivation of bridge-related category information during inference, a neural signature predictive of subsequent successful inference. Importantly, stress was associated with reduced bridge-related category reactivation, whereas retrieval practice was associated with stronger reactivation under stress. Collectively, our findings link rapid reactivation of bridge-related category information to successful memory-based inference. Although susceptible to stress, this reactivation was stronger following retrieval practice, suggesting that robust memory traces may contribute to more resilient inference under stress.

papers.title: Deconstructing evolutionary histories of complex genomic rearrangements in lung malignancies
papers.abstract: Complex genomic rearrangements (CGRs) are hallmarks of tumor genomes, yet their architectures and origins remain poorly understood. We utilized optical mapping to profile the genomic landscapes of lung tissues across various stages - from normal and benign lesions to advanced carcinomas - to characterize genome disorganization during carcinogenesis. We developed omcplR to resolve the CGR architectures and predict their genesis using the genome-graph framework. Our findings reveal that many CGRs arise from hierarchical combinations of localized structural variations that are unlikely due to break-fusion-bridge, chromothripsis, or chromoplexy. We termed this process chromodiadochi: a cascade of nested rearrangements accumulating over multiple generations during carcinogenesis. Early intra-chromosomal junctions in CGRs typically localized within specific chromatin domains, while late junctions in advanced tumors occurred in more heterogeneous contexts and showed signs of positive selection. A composite signature of genomic alterations, including the CGRs, captures the trajectory of progressive genomic structural disorganization and instability from benign tissue to malignancy.

papers.title: Apoptotic caspases cleave DRP1 to promote mitochondrial fusion and anti-viral immune responses
papers.abstract: Apoptosis has been recognized as a suicidal host-defense programmed cell death pathway against invading pathogens. However, recent evidences showed that viruses can employ caspases to cleave and inactivate immune signaling molecules to facilitate infection. Whether caspases can instead promote anti-viral immune responses is currently unknown. Here, we demonstrated that the NSs protein of RVFV triggers activation of apoptotic caspases, which cleave the mitochondrial fission factor DRP1 resulting in mitochondrial elongation. Elongated mitochondria promote MAVS aggregation leading to enhanced anti-viral immunity. Apoptotic caspases, including caspase-3, -6, -7 and -8, cleave DRP1 at the motifs of D500FAD503 and/or AEAD556, suggesting that this cleavage event may occur during infection of different viruses. Indeed, infection of H1N1, SeV and HSV-1 all triggered apoptotic caspases activation to cleave DRP1 promoting anti-viral immune responses. Compared with wild-type DRP1, introduction of caspase-resistant DRP1 strongly attenuated immune responses triggered by virus infection. These results revealed a mechanism through which apoptotic caspases promote anti-viral immunity by regulating mitochondrial morphodynamics.

papers.title: FoxO factors preserve airway epithelial homeostasis by coordinating adaptive stress responses
papers.abstract: Airway epithelia must maintain functional and structural homeostasis despite exposure to diverse environmental stressors. FoxO transcription factors are well suited to this task, acting as integration hubs that translate extrinsic and intrinsic signals into appropriate physiological responses. We show that FoxO factors in Drosophila, mouse, and human airway epithelial cells (AECs) undergo nuclear translocation in response to stressors including hypoxia, temperature, and oxidative stress. In human airway epithelial cell lines, individual hFOXO factors show distinct, cell-type-specific activation patterns. In Drosophila, hypoxia was the only stressor among those tested that triggered a dfoxo-dependent innate immune response. Because Drosophila possesses a single FoxO ortholog, loss-of-function analysis directly demonstrated that dfoxo is required for stress resistance in the airway epithelium. Reduced FoxO expression was similarly observed in mouse models of asthma and in airway samples from asthma patients, paralleling the increased stress sensitivity seen upon FoxO loss in flies. While our data do not establish that reduced FOXO levels cause asthma, they indicate that FoxO-dependent stress pathways are altered in diseased airways across species. Together, these findings support a model in which FoxO coordinates adaptive epithelial stress responses that maintain airway homeostasis under environmental challenge.

papers.title: Expansion of human hematopoietic stem cells by inhibiting translation
papers.abstract: Hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) transplantation using umbilical cord blood (UCB) is a potentially life-saving treatment for leukemia and bone marrow failure but is limited by the low number of HSCs in UCB. The loss of HSCs after ex vivo manipulation is also a major obstacle to gene editing for inherited blood disorders. HSCs require a low rate of translation to maintain their capacity for self-renewal, but hematopoietic cytokines used to expand HSCs stimulate protein synthesis and impair long-term self-renewal. We previously described cytokine-free conditions that maintain but do not expand human and mouse HSCs ex vivo. Here we performed a high-throughput screen and identified translation inhibitors that allow ex vivo expansion of human HSCs while minimizing cytokine exposure. Transplantation assays show a ~4.3-fold expansion of long-term HSCs from UCB after one week of culture in low cytokine conditions that include the translation initiation inhibitor 4E1RCat. Single cell transcriptomic analysis demonstrates maintenance of the HSC/MPP transcriptional signature and reduced expression of stress markers under culture conditions that maintain or expand functional long-term HSCs. Addition of 4E1RCat induces a dose-dependent increase in autophagic vacuoles and reduces expression of oxidative phosphorylation and cell cycle gene expression programs. These culture conditions maintain adult HSCs after CRISPR/Cas9 editing of the BCL11A+58 enhancer, overcoming a major obstacle to ex vivo gene correction for human hemoglobinopathies.

papers.title: A novel behavioral paradigm for characterizing anticipatory postural adjustments in mice
papers.abstract: Voluntary movements perturb the body's equilibrium, and the nervous system limits this disturbance by generating anticipatory postural adjustments (APAs) that redistribute body weight before and during movement. APAs have been characterized extensively in humans and larger animal models, but the absence of a tractable behavioral assay in mice has limited access to the genetic and circuit-level tools needed to investigate their neural basis. Here, we describe a force-plate behavioral paradigm in which freely moving mice stand on four independent load cells, receive an auditory GO cue and initiate locomotion voluntarily without task-specific training. Using force recordings, high-speed video and markerless pose estimation, we show that mice initiate a step with a stereotyped sequence of weight shifts: the center of pressure (CoP) moves anteriorly and then laterally away from the swing side, the swing forepaw and diagonally opposite hindpaw unload, and body weight is carried by the remaining diagonal pair. A single principal component explained approximately 80% of the variance in the average trial, compared with approximately 50% when paw identity was shuffled. Pressure recordings identified rapid swing-forepaw unloading beginning, on average, 87.9 ms before lift-off. Head and ear movement began approximately 200 ms before lift-off, and an operational multimodal estimate placed the interval between the earliest detected postural movement and the onset of forepaw rotation at approximately 160-180 ms. Neuropixels recordings from the pontine reticular nucleus (PRN) and supplementary motor area (SMA), monosynaptic tracing of inputs to reticulospinal PRN neurons, and preliminary cell-ablation experiments identify the PRN as a candidate node in the circuitry supporting anticipatory postural control. This paradigm provides a platform for circuit-level investigation of postural control and its disruption in disease.

papers.title: SubCellSeg: A generalist model for subcellular structure segmentation in 3D fluorescence microscopy
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) segmentation of subcellular structures from fluorescence microscopy images is the foundation of many analyses in quantitative cell biology. The prevailing approach addresses 3D segmentation one structure at a time, with a separate model trained for each structure type. By developing SubCellSeg, we demonstrate that a single model, trained jointly across a diverse range of structures, substantially and consistently outperforms structure-specific specialist models. SubCellSeg is a 3D segmentation model trained on expert-curated fluorescence images and their computationally generated reference masks, of 13 morphologically distinct subcellular structures in human induced pluripotent stem (hiPS) cell lines from the Allen Cell Collection, spanning compact puncta, planar junctions, reticular networks, and tubular structures. Without any structure-specific input, SubCellSeg achieves a mean Dice score of 0.909 across the 13 structures and outperforms each of the 13 specialist models on the structure it was trained for (specialist mean Dice 0.773). SubCellSeg also achieves zero-shot generalization, segmenting subcellular structures with morphologies not represented in the training data. This generalization extends to images acquired on different microscopes and with different imaging configurations, to cells under drug perturbation, and to a morphologically distinct cell type, hiPS cell-derived cardiomyocytes. Where zero-shot results are insufficient for a specific application, SubCellSeg can be fine-tuned: starting from its pretrained weights, 10% of the labeled images (16 images) gave better results than training a new model from scratch on all of them. SubCellSeg is distributed through the napari plugin allencell-segmenter-ml[1] with pretrained checkpoints, so it can be run on new data without any training; the training and evaluation code is available at https://github.com/AllenCell/SubCellSeg.

papers.title: Desiccation stress enhances virulence potential of group B Streptococcus
papers.abstract: Streptococcus agalactiae (Group B Streptococcus, GBS) asymptomatically inhabits the gastrointestinal and female reproductive tracts but can also cause invasive diseases in susceptible individuals. Despite its clinical importance, relatively little is known about its ability to survive outside the host and whether environmental persistence contributes to transmission and infection. Here we investigate the GBS survival under nutrient starvation and desiccation, characterizing phenotypic and genomic adaptations associated with environmental persistence. GBS remained viable for 30 days during starvation at room temperature and for more than 80 days under desiccated conditions, with GBS grown to stationary-phase bacteria exhibiting greater survival than actively growing bacteria. Survival under desiccation was conserved among several clinically relevant GBS serotypes. Following rehydration desiccated GBS exhibited enhanced biofilm formation compared to control non-desiccated strains. Whole-genome sequencing identified mutations in genes involved in capsule biosynthesis, cell-envelope homeostasis, nutrient transport, and carbohydrate metabolism, suggesting that multiple adaptive pathways may contribute to environmental persistence. Importantly, desiccated GBS retained the capacity to colonize the vaginal mucosa and displayed increased invasion of reproductive tissues in a murine vaginal colonization model. In a systemic infection model, desiccated GBS exhibited enhanced virulence compared to control non-desiccated GBS, demonstrating that environmental survival does not diminish pathogenic potential. This environmental persistence may represent an underappreciated factor contributing to GBS transmission and the epidemiology of late-onset neonatal disease.

papers.title: Herbivore and carnivore microbial signatures indicate diet and health variation in human gut microbiota
papers.abstract: Diet is a key factor shaping gut microbiota in mammals, with herbivores and carnivores harboring distinct microbial communities. However, despite humans being highly omnivorous, it remains unclear whether their gut microbiota more closely resembles that of herbivores or carnivores or how individual-level variations along this spectrum are associated with human health status. We compared gut microbiota profiles of 858 samples from 109 mammalian species and constructed a Herbivore-Carnivore (HC) index based on bacterial groups characteristic of each diet. The HC-index positioned humans between herbivores and carnivores and showed that traditional hunter-gatherers and nonhuman apes retained herbivore-leaning profiles, whereas urbanized humans exhibited a shift toward a carnivore-leaning state. By applying the HC-index to >72,000 participants across multiple cohorts worldwide, we found that elevated HC-index values were associated with plant-based and fiber-rich diets, greater microbial diversity, enhanced potential to degrade plant-derived carbohydrates, favorable clinical measures, and lower prevalence of self-reported disease. We demonstrated that the HC balance of gut microbiota captures a conserved diet-related gradient across mammals and provides an interpretable framework linking human diet, microbial function, and health.

papers.title: Learned associations constrain anticipatory visual dynamics and enhance sensory and motor readiness to facilitate perceptual decisions
