They also point to 28S rsRNA-CTC_L20 as a potential target for treating vascular remodeling.

papers.title: TREM2-stimulated, PDGF-dependent macrophage-fibroblast crosstalk induces beneficial plaque remodeling in clonal hematopoiesis
papers.abstract: Background: In Jak2V617F clonal hematopoiesis, inflammatory signaling suppresses macrophage TREM2 and promotes features of plaque instability, while therapeutic TREM2 agonism reverses plaque instability by increasing fibroblasts and fibrous cap formation. We tested whether macrophage-derived PDGFB and stromal cell PDGFR? signaling mediate this response. Methods: Low allele burden (LAB) Jak2V617F atherosclerosis models were combined with inducible Pdgfb deletion in CX3CR1-lineage monocytes/macrophages or Pdgfra deletion in Col1a2-lineage fibroblast-enriched stromal cells. Mice were treated with the TREM2 agonist 4D9. Plaque composition, macrophage-fibroblast interactions, and aortic stromal cell populations were analyzed. Human WT and JAK2V617F iPSC-derived macrophages were used for validation. Results: TREM2 activation with 4D9 increased macrophage PDGFB production and promoted fibrous cap formation in LAB Jak2V617F atherosclerosis. Deletion of Pdgfb in CX3CR1-lineage cells markedly attenuated the 4D9-mediated increase in fibrous cap area and lesional PDGFR?+ cells, establishing macrophage-derived PDGFB as a key signal for the stromal response. Consistently, Col1a2-lineage Pdgfra deletion abolished the 4D9-induced fibrous cap response without significantly altering lesion or necrotic core area. Single cell RNA-seq identified increased Fmod+ and CD26/Dpp4+ fibroblast populations associated with 4D9 treatment. Fmod+ fibroblasts represented an abundant matrix-associated population, whereas CD26+ fibroblasts showed greatest enrichment, prominent extracellular matrix, collagen organization, and matrix-remodeling programs that were enhanced by 4D9 and attenuated by Pdgfra deletion. The stromal response was also associated with reduced macrophage migration-related programs and predicted chemokine communication from CD26+ fibroblasts to macrophages which was verified by macrophage migration studies. Moreover, stromal Pdgfra deletion increased lesional CCR2+ and CCR5+ macrophages. Conclusions: In a CH model of inflammatory atherosclerosis, TREM2 activation promotes a macrophage PDGFB-stromal PDGFR? pathway that expands Fmod+ and CD26+ fibroblast populations and increases fibrous cap matrix formation. CD26+ fibroblasts impair macrophage chemotaxis in a DPP4-dependent manner, suggesting reciprocal macrophage-fibroblast communication that coordinates matrix remodeling and inflammatory cell trafficking in the plaque.

papers.title: Scientific Figure Library connects visual examples with reusable plotting code
papers.abstract: Code-generating assistants can adapt plotting scripts, while researchers select visual examples and assess their relevance. Reusing those examples requires the image, implementation, and input context to remain connected. Scientific Figure Library (SFL) organizes visual examples, plotting code, input descriptions, and provenance as reusable figure assets. A user-selected local library retains working revisions and published releases, while a common provider interface makes local and externally maintained collections available through the same discovery workflow. Researchers browse candidate figures, inspect an exact preview, confirm a selection, and materialize the corresponding assets into a project for adaptation and execution. Local clients and external agents access a shared service, connecting visual selection with code-based analysis across research environments. An accompanying open resource, ScientificFigureLibrary-personal, supplies modular examples through the Open Figure Modules provider. Its organization combines previews, reusable scripts, example inputs, and licensing information, making it a concrete resource for learning and adapting scientific visualization patterns. We describe the asset model, retrieval and confirmation workflow, execution handoff, and resource organization, supported by implementation inspection and automated software checks. In a public lung single-cell case study, we reused a cell-composition template for 32 idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and 28 control donors and verified the donor-level inputs and plotted proportions. SFL provides a practical connection between finding a figure and obtaining the materials needed to work with it, while preserving the identity and provenance of the selected example.

papers.title: OligoFragger: spectrum graph-guided analysis of modified RNA oligonucleotides by mass spectrometry
papers.abstract: RNA modifications are widespread modulators of RNA function, but comprehensive identification remains technically challenging. This is especially true for densely modified RNAs such as tRNAs, where multiple modified residues and many possible chemistries occur within short sequence contexts. Tandem mass spectrometry provides direct chemical and positional evidence for modified oligonucleotides, but current database-search strategies struggle when dozens of candidate modifications must be considered simultaneously. Here, we present OligoFragger, a spectrum graph-guided computational tool that uses fragment evidence to constrain modified-oligonucleotide searches before full database scoring, enabling rapid and robust oligonucleotide identification. Using controlled RNA samples and tRNA datasets from E. coli and human cells, we demonstrate that OligoFragger increases identifications under stringent FDR control while recovering known modification patterns and supporting label-free quantification. This strategy enables sensitive, FDR-controlled identification and label-free quantification of modified RNA oligonucleotides in complex epitranscriptomic search spaces.

papers.title: Sleep deprivation differentially recruits amygdala subregions in male and female mice
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD) acutely increases negative affect, and chronic insufficient sleep is associated with an increased risk of depression. Since the amygdala regulates both emotional processing and sleep, and SD dysregulates amygdalar function, amygdala functionality may link sleep loss to emotional outcomes. To better understand this, the specific sleep-impacted amygdalar nuclei need to be fully defined. To determine the impact of acute sleep loss on the relative activation of specific amygdalar regions, we screened for the neuronal activity marker c-Fos in wildtype mice that slept undisturbed, underwent 4-h SD, or 4-h SD with 2-h recovery sleep (RS). Application of whole-brain clearing and automated cell counting identified increased c-Fos expression within the cortical subplate of both male and female mice that was localized to amygdalar regions. As the amygdala comprises multiple distinct subnuclei, we parcellated and quantified c-Fos expression within each amygdalar subnucleus. Interestingly, we found that SD-induced differential c-Fos expression patterns between sexes. In male mice, SD increased c-Fos expression across several amygdalar subnuclei, which largely reversed with RS. By contrast, SD in females increased c-Fos expression only in the anterior basolateral amygdala and the intercalated amygdala, and both subnuclei remained activated even with RS. These findings highlight sex-specific spatial distribution of SD-activated amygdala cells, which may contribute to differences in emotional processing following sleep loss and offer potential anatomical targets for mitigating SD-related mood deficits.

papers.title: Sphingolipid Hydroxylation Governs Fungal Pathogenicity and Drug Susceptibility: Scs7 as a Druggable Target in Candida albicans
papers.abstract: Sphingolipids are essential structural components of the fungal plasma membrane and key signaling hubs that orchestrate pathogenicity. While both fungi and mammals perform sphingolipid hydroxylation, they rely on evolutionarily divergent enzymatic systems, establishing a biochemical divergence exploitable for selective targeting. Here, through a screening of sphingolipid metabolic genes, we identify the sphingolipid -hydroxylase Scs7 as a central regulator of membrane homeostasis, virulence, and caspofungin susceptibility in Candida albicans. Genetic ablation of SCS7 depletes hydroxylated sphingolipids, disrupts memberane organization, and compromises cell wall integrity, which collectively impair hyphal morphogenesis, biofilm formation, and stress tolerance through blockade of the cAMP-PKA signaling axis. In a murine cutaneous infection model, SCS7 deletion markedly attenuates fungal burden, hyperinflammation, and epidermal barrier disruption, underscoring its non-redundant role in host-pathogen interaction. Leveraging the fungus-specific architecture of Scs7, we performed virtual screening and identified resveratrol as a natural Scs7 inhibitor. Resveratrol recapitulates the lipidomic and phenotypic defects of SCS7 deletion and synergizes with caspofungin to enhance fungal killing. Our study establishes sphingolipid -hydroxylation as a master determinant of fungal membrane fitness and validates Scs7 as a promising, fungus-specific antifungal target with dual anti-virulence and chemosensitizing activities.

papers.title: Neuropathological assessment of cerebrovascular integrity in Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy
papers.abstract: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy neuropathological change (CTE-NC) is defined by perivascular deposits of phosphorylated tau, with lesions preferentially located at sulcal depths. We investigated whether CTE-NC is associated with structural changes to perivascular spaces (PVSs) or microvascular degeneration. Post-mortem middle frontal gyrus tissue from 11 CTE-NC cases and 11 age-matched controls was examined using immunohistochemistry. All CTE-NC cases exhibited pathognomonic lesions in this region. We quantified PVS width along with vessel lumen and PVS area, string vessel burden, pericyte density, and aquaporin-4 (AQP4) polarisation to the astrocytic endfoot. Total PVS width did not differ significantly between the groups in grey matter (P = 0.543) nor white matter (P = 0.468). Neither PVS area (sulcal depth, P = 0.097; gyral crest, P = 0.645) nor PVS-to-lumen area ratio (sulcal depth, P = 0.454; gyral crest, P = 0.307) differed significantly. Similarly, there were no significant differences in total microvascular length (p = 0.693), string vessel burden (p = 0.128), pericyte density (p = 0.589), or AQP4 endfoot enrichment (p = 0.538). We therefore found no evidence of large-scale PVS enlargement, lumen narrowing, capillary degeneration, pericyte loss, or altered AQP4 endfoot enrichment in CTE-NC at the locations and spatial scales investigated. Taken together, these findings suggest that the pathognomonic perivascular tau lesion is not associated with a classical small vessel degenerative phenotype in CTE-NC. However, that does not exclude more subtle molecular, functional, or ultrastructural changes at the interface between vessels, the perivascular space, and surrounding brain tissue.

papers.title: SilencioMA: A single compound that targets both MAPT and APP as a potential disease modifying therapeutic for Alzheimer's Disease
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is the most common age-related neurodegenerative disease and the leading cause of dementia worldwide. AD pathogenesis involves aggregation of amyloid-beta (A{beta}), produced from amyloidogenic proteolytic processing of Amyloid Precursor Protein (APP), and accumulation of misfolded, pathological tau (Microtubule Associated Protein Tau, MAPT). Current efforts focus on developing disease modifying therapeutics (DMTs) against single targets: A{beta} or tau. However, DMTs that concurrently target both tau and A{beta} are likely to have the greatest impact since they target both culprits of AD pathogenesis. Here we describe the development of SilencioMA, a single compound that targets both MAPT and APP messenger RNAs (mRNAs) based on silencing connected interfering oligonucleotides against MAPT and APP. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) administration of SilencioMA reduces A{beta} and tau and pathology after a single intracerebroventricular injection in 5XFAD/PS19 mice, an animal model of severe amyloidosis and tauopathy. SilencioMA does not rely on lipid nanoparticles or lipophilic conjugates for CSF administration. At the same time its modular design permits conjugation of ligands that facilitate transcytosis through the blood brain barrier, allowing systemic administration. Our findings provide proof-of-concept for a strategy that targets the dual A{beta} and tau pathologies of AD, and establishes a compelling foundation for further development of SilencioMA as a next-generation DMT for AD.

papers.title: An auditable harness for biomolecular dynamics simulations by AI agents
papers.abstract: AI agents now generate biological hypotheses faster than they can be tested. Hypotheses stated at the atomic level can be examined with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. For new questions without a reference, trust in an agent-run simulation rests on a tool-written process record, not the agent's account. Existing MD agents leave this record to the language model. Here we present MDClaw, a harness whose validating tools and directed acyclic graph (DAG) check stages before execution and record every simulation stage. On MDDataBench, which grades outputs against deposited simulations, four open-weight models with MDClaw passed all three runs on 81-100% of 31 test systems. The DAG complements this outcome check. An ablation without the DAG revealed 11 successful runs that had skipped minimization or equilibration, or simulated a different structure. MDClaw carried questions from human and AI scientists through simulation to trajectories traceable to their inputs and settings.

papers.title: Hippocampal dorsal and ventral CA2 enable social discrimination after acute social defeat
papers.abstract: Remembering the valence of conspecifics based on past aggressive compared to non-aggressive interactions is important for proper adaptive social behaviors. How a single naturalistic encounter establishes a lasting memory of the valence of the experience remains unclear. Our recent work shows that the CA2 region in ventral hippocampus, unlike dorsal CA2, is not required for social novelty discrimination but does contribute with dorsal CA2 to promote social aggression. How CA2 contributes to valence-associated social memory across the dorsoventral axis remains unresolved. We developed an acute defeat-associated social threat discrimination memory (AD-STDM) paradigm after which a male mouse preferentially interacted with a familiar non-aggressor male compared to a familiar aggressor male 24 h after a single defeat episode. Chemogenetic inhibition of Avpr1b-expressing CA2 neurons in either dorsal or ventral hippocampus during learning impaired subsequent discrimination. Acute defeat also increased cFos expression in ventral CA2 neurons relative to non-aggressive social interaction. Thus, although ventral CA2 is not required for social novelty recognition memory, it is required for social memory of an aversive social experience, with a relatively greater level of neural activation during aversive compared to non-aversive social encounters. In contrast, dorsal CA2 is required for both non-aversive and aversive forms of social memory.

papers.title: BryoCAD: Extending Plant DNA Foundation Models Beyond Flowering Plants
papers.abstract: Bryophytes exhibit diverse genome architectures and gene repertoires, yet their functional interpretation remains constrained by incomplete genomic annotations and limited experimental resources. Although DNA foundation models offer promising solutions, their applicability to evolutionarily divergent bryophytes remains largely unexplored. Here, we introduce BryoCAD, a DNA language model developed through continued pre-training of the angiosperm-specific PlantCAD2 model on 17 bryophyte genomes spanning hornworts, liverworts, and mosses. Across three representative bryophyte genomes and four gene-boundary motif recovery tasks, BryoCAD-Small improved mean zero-shot accuracy from 45.7% to 57.0%, a 24.8% relative increase over PlantCAD2-Small, while the over 200-fold larger Evo2-20B achieved a mean accuracy of only 39.3%. Remarkably, BryoCAD-Small outperformed PlantCAD2-Large in 11 of 12 motif-recovery comparisons across the three bryophytes, highlighting the benefits of lineage-specific adaptation over model scaling alone. These improvements extended to all six tested algal species, increasing mean accuracy from 26.3% to 37.5%, although performance varied across ferns and gymnosperms. BryoCAD also enhanced gene structure annotation: replacing PlantCAD2-Small with BryoCAD-Small increased transcript-level F1 scores from 0.578 to 0.625 in Marchantia polymorpha and from 0.485 to 0.530 in Physcomitrium patens. Together, our findings demonstrate that lineage-specific continued pre-training enhances genomic sequence interpretation and gene annotation across bryophytes, providing a transferable framework for extending DNA foundation models to evolutionarily diverse, understudied plant lineages.

papers.title: SilencioM: silencing connected interfering oligonucleotides against MAPT as a potential disease modifying therapeutic for tauopathies
papers.abstract: Tauopathies are a diverse group of neurodegenerative diseases whose pathogenesis involves brain accumulation of misfolded, pathological tau (Microtubule Associated Protein Tau, MAPT). More than twenty tauopathies have been identified thus far that collectively impact millions of people worldwide, of which the most common is Alzheimer's disease (AD). Despite substantial efforts to develop drugs for tauopathies, no effective treatments currently exist, highlighting the urgent need for therapeutics to combat these prevalent and ruinous neurodegenerative diseases. Strategies that target tau are likely to have the greatest impact since tau is the proximal cause of their pathogenesis. Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) have emerged as a powerful class of precision therapeutics that silence disease-causing genes through RNA interference with favorable safety profiles. Delivery challenges are rapidly being addressed, and siRNA-based approaches are poised to transform the therapeutic landscape of neurological diseases. In this study, we describe SilencioM (Silencing connected interfering oligonucleotides against MAPT) and show its efficacy in markedly reducing tau pathology after a single intracerebroventricular injection in PS19 mice, a mouse model of severe tauopathy. SilencioM targets human, primate, rat and mouse ortholog genes; thus, the same compound can proceed from efficacy studies to Investigational New Drug Application (IND)-enabling studies. SilencioM is simple to manufacture and is administered without encapsulation in lipid nanoparticles and without requirements for lipophilic conjugation, making it a promising candidate for further development as a novel therapeutic for tauopathies, including AD.

papers.title: Affordable 96-parallel SPPS: hardware and software add-on for automated liquid handling platforms
papers.abstract: ParSynt-P is a hardware and software add-on that converts a liquid-handling robot already available in a proteomics laboratory (Tecan Freedom EVO) into a parallel plate-format peptide synthesizer for generating libraries of candidate peptide standards for targeted blood plasma proteomics. The manifold is milled from polytetrafluoroethylene and has ports for an inert gas and a vacuum line; a standard commercially available 96-well filtration plate is secured to it with an airtight seal. The software layer generates robot worklists from a table of peptide sequences and controls switching of the N?/vacuum lines, including pulsed gas mixing. The system performs up to 96 syntheses per run, and coupling of one residue takes 94 min. Workability of this 96-well format was verified on three fully loaded plates. The uniformity of synthesis conversion across the plate was measured quantitatively using a characterized NAT/SIL standard pair. The add-on cost $351, while the synthesis cost is $0.23 per coupling and $1.14 per milligram of crude product, an order of magnitude below the market price of custom synthesis.

papers.title: Hyperactivation of Mincle in exacerbated apical periodontitis in an autoinflammatory mouse model for cherubism
papers.abstract: Aims: To examine the role of Mincle, a C-type lectin (Clec) pathogen recognition receptor (PRR), in exacerbated apical periodontitis (AP) in an autoinflammatory mouse model for cherubism (CBM). Methodology: Patients with immune system dysfunction have higher prevalence of AP but the mechanism remains largely unknown. We studied a knock-in (KI) mouse model carrying a Sh3bp2 mutation for CBM. We performed pulp exposure in one lower 1st molar of 5- to 6-week-old mice to introduce pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMP)-induced endodontic infection. We determined the expression levels of Clec subfamily genes by qPCR. To suppress Mincle, we generated Sh3bp2+/+Mincle+/+, Sh3bp2+/KIMincle+/+, and Sh3bp2+/KIMincleKO/KO mice or injected Sh3bp2+/KI mice with a Mincle-binding DNA aptamer (AptMincle). Mice were analyzed 42 days after pulp exposure by micro-CT (mCT), qPCR and immunoblotting. Statistical analysis was performed by one-way ANOVA followed by post-hoc analysis with Tukeys test or two-way ANOVA followed by Sidak correction. p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: Expression of Clec4e (Mincle) was significantly increased in Sh3bp2 mutant mice after pulp exposure compared to WT littermates (p<0.0001). Sh3bp2+/KIMincle+/+ and Sh3bp2+/KIMincleKO/KO mice had a comparable response to pulp exposure, including the degree of bone loss and induction of inducible NOS (iNOS), IL-1b, and TNF-a. Sh3bp2+/KI mice injected with AptMincle after pulp exposure for 21 days showed significant amelioration of bone loss compared to mice with vehicle injection (p<0.0001). Conclusions: These seemingly conflicting data of suppressing Mincle by crossing with Mincle KO mice and AptMincle injection suggest that Mincle has dual functions upon PAMPs stimulation, consistent with a previous study showing that Mincle enhances tissue destruction during the inflammatory stage and is subsequently needed for inflammation resolution. Fine-tuned suppression of Mincle significantly reduces the severity of AP in Sh3bp2+/KI mice. This study suggests that patients with CBM may benefit from more frequent dental examinations and early intervention to reduce or prevent severe progressive bone loss in periapical tissues.

papers.title: Chronic FMNL2 overexpression is associated with changes in brain histology and exploratory behavior in adult zebrafish
papers.abstract: Formin-like protein 2 (FMNL2) has been associated with Alzheimer`s disease and cerebrovascular pathology and regulates gliovascular remodeling following amyloid exposure. However, the consequences of sustained FMNL2 elevation remain unclear. We generated a transgenic zebrafish line expressing human FMNL2 under the her4.1 promoter and examined adult brain histology and behavior under baseline conditions and following acute amyloid-{beta}42 (A{beta}42) exposure. Histological analyses assessed FMNL2 immunoreactivity, overlap between the glial marker BLBP and endothelial tight-junction marker ZO1, synaptic vesicle protein SV2 labeling, and microglial counts. Exploratory behavior was evaluated using the novel tank test and free-movement pattern Y-maze. Compared with uninjected wild-type controls, uninjected FMNL2-overexpressing fish showed higher FMNL2 immunoreactivity, lower BLBP-ZO1 overlap, fewer normalized SV2 puncta, and higher counts of total and morphologically activated microglia. Acute A{beta}42 exposure in wild-type animals produced changes in the same direction across these histological endpoints. No significant additional histological changes were detected following A{beta}42 exposure in the overexpression background. In the novel tank test, uninjected FMNL2-overexpressing fish had a higher composite boldness index than uninjected wild-type controls. These findings indicate that sustained FMNL2 overexpression is associated with histological changes resembling several responses to acute A{beta}42 exposure, together with altered exploratory behavior. They support further investigation of persistent FMNL2 elevation as a contributor to altered glial-vascular organization and cellular responses relevant to Alzheimer`s disease.

papers.title: Elevational variation in gut microbial community composition and predicted functional potential across three Himalayan redstart species
papers.abstract: Environmental gradients and seasonal migration may influence host-associated microbial communities, yet their contributions to gut microbiome variation in montane birds remain poorly understood. We investigated gut microbial communities across 1,300 to 4,200 m in three Himalayan redstarts (Phoenicurus fuliginosus, P. leucocephalus, and P. frontalis) exhibiting contrasting seasonal movement strategies. Using 16S rRNA gene sequencing of 46 fecal samples, we characterized microbial diversity, community composition, distance decay relationships, co-occurrence networks, and predicted functional potential. Elevation was significantly associated with microbial community composition, explaining approximately 3% of variation, whereas host species showed no significant association after accounting for elevation. P. fuliginosus exhibited significant compositional differences among most sampled elevations, whereas P. leucocephalus showed significant positive distance decay relationships. Alpha diversity showed no consistent elevational trend, while core microbial taxa and co-occurrence networks varied among elevational groups. PICRUSt2 analyses identified 28 predicted KEGG Level 3 pathways differing significantly among elevations, including pathways associated with amino acid, lipid, glycan, carbohydrate, and bile acid metabolism. Together, these findings highlight elevation as a significant correlate of gut microbial community composition and predicted functional potential, with distinct patterns of microbial turnover among closely related Himalayan redstarts.

papers.title: Male-specific genome sequences for non-invasive sex identification in Nishikigoi (Cyprinus carpio)
papers.abstract: Nishikigoi, ornamental cultivars of the common carp (Cyprinus carpio), are economically valuable aquaculture teleosts in which mature females command significantly higher market prices due to superior body conformation and coloration. Consequently, early and non-invasive sex identification is highly desirable for commercial breeding. Although sex determination in common carp follows an XX/XY system, sex-chromosome-specific markers and field-applicable diagnostic methods for Nishikigoi have remained limited. In this study, we conducted sequence-based bulked segregant analysis using whole-genome shotgun sequencing of female and male pools in Kohaku, a representative Nishikigoi lineage. We identified male-specific candidate contigs and successfully developed PCR-based male-specific markers. Validation across multiple Nishikigoi varieties and wild common carp demonstrated that primary primer pairs achieved high diagnostic accuracy. Comparative genomic analysis revealed that these candidate contigs mapped to the genomic region on chromosome 25B containing the male-determining gene Pangu, with the primary marker located in immediate physical proximity to the gene. To enable field diagnostics, we combined non-invasive epidermal mucus DNA extraction, loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP), and chromatography-printed array strip (C-PAS) technology, establishing a rapid on-site detection workflow. Overall, this study provides highly reliable PCR markers associated with the sex-determination locus and establishes a non-invasive, field-applicable diagnostic platform to streamline commercial Nishikigoi breeding and sex-selected stock management.

papers.title: B cells dominate the heart immune infiltrate during chronic infectious cardiomyopathy
papers.abstract: Recent advances in single-cell and spatially resolved multi-omics have revolutionised our understanding of the cellular and molecular niches governing cardiac homeostasis and acute injury. However, the immune-stromal networks sustaining long-term, chronic heart pathology remain poorly defined, largely due to a paucity of physiologically relevant experimental models. Here, through a side-by-side multi-omic comparison of Trypanosoma cruzi-infected mouse models displaying contrasting degrees of chronic myocardial pathology and fibrosis, we define the long-term cellular landscape of the inflamed fibrotic heart. We reveal that class-switched, antibody-secreting plasma B cells represent the predominant immune subset infiltrating the fibrotic myocardium. CellChat intercellular communication modelling identifies plasma cell-fibroblast crosstalk as the strongest immune-stromal interaction in the fibrosis-prone heart, driven by predicted matrix anchoring (CD44-collagen/laminin) and molecular survival axes (App-Cd74, C3-Cr2). Supporting these computational predictions, immunofluorescence and spatial profiling confirm close proximity between plasma B cells and fibroblasts, alongside a striking accumulation of B cells embedded within extracellular matrix-rich cardiac scars. This localised B cell response maintains prominent pools of parasite-reactive and heart-autoreactive antibody-secreting cells despite a lack of detectable parasite signal in their immediate micro-vicinity. Together, these findings identify a matrix-associated plasma B cell-fibroblast niche as a central driver of chronic cardiac remodelling, revealing how persistent tissue scarring can become decoupled from direct local pathogen presence.

papers.title: Beyond Sequence and Structure: Pretraining PLMs on Continuous Biophysical Fields
papers.abstract: We introduce the Biophysical Transformer, a protein language model that adds continuous biophysical fields as a third pretraining signal beside sequence and structure. A Poisson-Boltzmann solver computes the electrostatic potential around each three-residue token, and the model learns to predict it from sequence alone. A rotationally invariant spherical-harmonic descriptor serves as the loss target, eliminating the need for frame alignment during training and for coordinates at inference. Against a matched, one-flag control on the FLIP Meltome thermostability benchmark, the field objective raises Spearman correlation on every trained head of both human splits.The gain on human survives residualizing dipeptide composition under two architecturally different readouts and survives removing the test proteins that overlap the pretraining corpus. No effect survives on the organism-mixed split. At 1.1M parameters, both the Biophysical Transformer and its sequence-only control exceed FLIP's one-hot CNN and untrained-ESM baselines on every split. All results rest on a single pretraining run per arm,and the current design does not separate field content from generic regularization.

papers.title: Cytotoxic CD4+ exTregs expressing KLRG1 retain immunosuppressive function in cancer
papers.abstract: The role of cytotoxic CD4+ T cells in cancer remains controversial, with both pro- and anti-tumor functionality described. Based on a prior observation that putatively cytotoxic KLRG1+ FoxP3- conventional T cells (Tconv) associated with tumor progression, we deeply investigated the phenotype and function of KLRG1+ Tconv in multiple murine tumor models and in human clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) specimens. We found KLRG1+ Tconv have a conserved, highly activated, terminally differentiated phenotype across species. In murine tumors, KLRG1+ Tconv resemble tumor-infiltrating regulatory T cells (Tregs) at both transcriptional and proteomic levels, upregulating a spectrum of exhaustion-related checkpoint receptors, producing IL-10 and granzyme B (GzmB), and silencing expression of IFN{gamma} and TNF. Functionally, KLRG1+ Tconv exhibited immunosuppressive function in ex vivo assays. Using an in vivo Treg fate mapping approach in tumor-bearing mice, we found a subset of KLRG1+ Tconv are derived from Tregs that have lost FoxP3 protein expression. Ex vivo functional assays demonstrated the exTreg component of the KLRG1+ Tconv compartment is responsible for IL-10 production and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. In treatment studies, we found that KLRG1-targeted antibody-mediated depletion was more efficient than anti-KLRG1 blockade at slowing tumor growth and improving survival, with responses associating with depletion of intratumoral KLRG1+ Tconv and Tregs. In sum, our study discovered a novel conserved pathway of CD4+ T cell plasticity, wherein intratumoral, cytotoxic KLRG1+ CD4+ Tconv cells can be derived from Tregs and maintain immunosuppressive function, despite loss of FoxP3, and that KLRG1-targeted depletion may outperform KLRG1 blockade as an immunotherapeutic strategy in cancer.

papers.title: Structural relationships between the SLC12 cotransporter C-terminal domain, universal stress proteins and adenylating enzymes
papers.abstract: Several SLC12 cotransporters bind ATP in a cytoplasmic C-terminal domain (CTD). We analysed 16,192 CTD-containing SLC12 sequences and compared 42,845 representative structures to examine the relationship between this nucleotide site, universal stress proteins (USPs) and adenylating enzymes. In phosphorylated NKCC1, D891 and D927 lie near the ATP phosphate chain, while R801 and K889 form a basic phosphate-binding clamp. NKCC1 retains this arrangement, whereas KCC paralogs replace or lose several corresponding groups. In structural comparisons with USP and adenylating-enzyme references, both CTD lobes score between universal stress proteins and EC-annotated domains, and the two lobes form separate lineages that include bacterial transporters. Lobe-specific and nucleotide-frame comparisons place ATP in the corresponding structural region used for -phosphate chemistry by catalytic members of this fold. Published work on UspG provides a precedent for protein-bound AMP in a natural USP. In the examined SLC12 structures and USP models, candidate protein hydroxyls lack an in-line geometry for attack at ATP P. Protein adenylation would require a change in protein or nucleotide geometry, or a different acceptor. These results define a structural basis for testing conditional protein adenylation at SLC12 nucleotide sites. The required evidence is a covalent protein-AMP adduct, identification of its acceptor and measurement of the expected pyrophosphate coproduct, with soluble nucleotide analysis to distinguish accompanying ATP reactions.

papers.title: scDeepSim: Deep Generative Simulation for Controlled Benchmarking of Single-Cell Methods
papers.abstract: Benchmarking single-cell computational methods requires both realistic data and reliable ground truth. However, annotating real datasets is costly and, even when available, may not fully represent the diverse settings where methods are used. Simulators address this gap by generating synthetic data that has fully specified ground truth and whose structure can be tailored to challenge competing methods. Existing single-cell simulators can broadly be divided into statistical and deep generative classes. Statistical simulators offer interpretable parameters for controlling simulated data, but their modeling assumptions may not accurately represent real data. Deep generative models can learn complex expression patterns, but it remains unclear how to transparently control individual biological or technical factors without introducing unintended effects. We introduce scDeepSim, a simulator that combines a structured variational autoencoder with latent diffusion to generate synthetic single-cell expression profiles. It allows users to intervene on selected biological or technical factors at user-specified strengths, producing realistic datasets with benchmark ground truth. We demonstrate this capability by benchmarking batch correction and trajectory inference methods, showing how batch-effect strength affects batch mixing and cell-type preservation, and how trajectory geometry and noise affect pseudotime recovery. scDeepSim therefore enables researchers to vary selected biological and technical factors in realistic simulated data and assess how these changes affect the performance of single-cell analysis methods, helping understand when such methods may be appropriately applied. Code for the scDeepSim simulator and experiments is available at https://github.com/LangtianM/scDeepSim.

papers.title: Biological aging and comorbidities are linked to HIV 1 reservoir size despite suppressive antiretroviral therapy
papers.abstract: Background The HIV reservoir persists in long-living immune cells after antiretroviral therapy initiation. Proviral DNA integrates at preferential host DNA sites, while HIV transcription continues under treatment, with potential biological consequences. Treated people with HIV remain at increased risk for premature aging and non-AIDS comorbidities compared to people without HIV. Whether HIV reservoir size and activity impact health outcomes during treatment remains unclear. Methods We analyzed 1895 people with HIV using antiretroviral therapy from the 2000HIV cohort to study associations between the reservoir and historic and prospective virologic and immunological response markers, comorbidity outcomes and biological aging scores. The reservoir was assessed by quantifying total and intact proviral HIV DNA in circulating CD4+ T cells, along with measures of HIV transcriptional activity, including cell-associated HIV RNA. Results HIV reservoir markers were highly correlating and associated with older aging scores and adverse virologic outcomes, including quantifiable and residual viremia at study entry and during follow-up. Total HIV DNA, unlike the minor fraction of intact HIV DNA, correlated with prevalent cardiovascular disease, subclinical atherosclerotic disease, liver fibrosis and incident malignancies independent of circulating inflammatory markers and lowest CD4 nadir. Total HIV RNA associated with prevalent cardiovascular disease and liver fibrosis. Conclusion The HIV reservoir associated with older aging scores and long-term health outcomes in people with HIV using antiretroviral therapy, independent of inflammation and immune suppression history. Whether reservoir-reducing interventions lower the risk of non-AIDS comorbidities should be studied in people with high reservoir markers. Funding and trial registration ViiV Healthcare; 2000HIV ClinicalTrials.gov number: NTC03994835

papers.title: Combined pharmacotherapy suppress ferroptosis and inflammation after neonatal intraventricular hemorrhage
papers.abstract: Neonatal intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) is a common complication of extremely premature newborns, and results in reduced neurogenesis, white matter injury, cortical atrophy, and subsequent cerebral palsy, learning and memory disabilities. However, the impact of IVH on the hippocampus, an area critical for memory and learning capabilities throughout life, remains relatively unexplored. Using a preterm rabbit pup model that structurally resembles human perinatal brain development, we report, widespread hematoma and iron accumulation in the hippocampal dentate gyrus (DG) following IVH. This accumulation is facilitated by the anatomical positioning of the hippocampus within the unidirectional CSF flow pathway and the vulnerability of the immature dentate gyrus vasculature. Sulforaphane (SFN; an activator of nuclear factor erythroid 2 related factor 2 [Nrf2] transcriptional factor and anti-inflammatory pathways) and deferoxamine (DFN; an iron chelator) reduced iron deposition, free hemoglobin, and activated glial cells (sp. astrocytes and microglia), particularly in the DG molecular layer and hilar regions. The attenuated inflammatory responses correlate with decreased ferroptosis-mediated neuronal death, and substantial restoration of the dysregulated gene pathways associated with inflammation, immune activation, and neuronal cell death in the developing hippocampal/DG region. This was associated with a gene profile favoring ferroptotic cell death rather than apoptosis or autophagy pathways. Moreover, we also identified a regional specificity to certain effects as no astrogliosis was observed in hippocampal CA1 to CA4 regions after IVH or when compared with healthy controls. Our study is the first to demonstrate hippocampal hematoma and iron accumulation associated pathologic mechanisms following neonatal IVH. The results provide mechanistic insights into hippocampal injury as well as a therapeutic proof-of-concept for targeting iron toxicity and inflammation in the developing brain to mitigate injury. These results justify extending analyses of injury reversal to long-term postnatal ages and behavior studies to assess therapeutic potential. The study illustrates novel therapeutic interventions that attenuate early mediators of injury that improves recovery of hippocampal/DG formation/maturation and neuroprotection after neonatal IVH. We speculate that these protective effects may prolong donor stem cell survival thus, potentiating benefits of living cellular therapy in the future.

papers.title: Towards a best-in-class IgE disruptor for food allergy with Claude-enabled antibody design
papers.abstract: Food allergy affects an estimated 220-250 million people worldwide, for whom the constant risk of a severe reaction weighs heavily on quality of life. Allergic reactions are triggered by the cross-linking of allergen-specific IgE bound to its high-affinity receptor, Fc{epsilon}RI, on mast cells and basophils, causing degranulation, inflammation and, in severe cases, anaphylaxis. Omalizumab (Xolair), the sole FDA-approved biologic for food allergy, neutralizes circulating IgE; however, it does not effectively remove IgE from Fc{epsilon}RI, where it can persist for weeks and where even a small residual amount can sustain sensitivity. Here we describe an agentic computational design campaign with Claude toward a disruptive inhibitor antibody that physically removes bound IgE from Fc{epsilon}RI. Guided by our research team, Claude pursued a biparatopic molecule that pairs a disruptor arm, which displaces IgE from Fc{epsilon}RI, with a non-competing anchor arm that holds the molecule on receptor-bound IgE. Of 91 experimentally characterized disruptor designs, 20 showed activity against receptor-bound IgE by competitive bio-layer interferometry, and in a dose-titration assay three variants removed more IgE than omalizumab at therapeutically relevant concentrations (25-400 nM). De novo designs for the anchor arm bound IgE at diverse epitopes with apparent affinities of 3.4-235 nM. These subcomponents provide the starting point for further characterization toward a best-in-class IgE disruptor.

papers.title: A genetic screen to identify host factors required for commensal bacterial adherence to the gut epithelia
papers.abstract: Bacterial adherence to gut epithelial cells likely involves host genetic components. We isolated a gut commensal bacterium, Lelliottia jeotgali, that can robustly colonize C. elegans through attachment to intestinal epithelial cells. Here, we developed a novel screen in C. elegans to identify host genes required for microbiome bacterial colonization. Using transgenic L. jeotgali strain expressing tdTomato, we conducted forward genetic screens in C. elegans to select for mutants that completely lost colonization. We identified multiple allelic mutations in five different C. elegans genes, termed knockout of Lelliottia adherence (kola) mutants, with a near complete loss of adherence. Each of kola-1-5 is uncharacterized and predicted to encode for a secreted or membrane-bound protein. We also identified gly-5, a GalNAc transferase that initiates O-linked glycosylation. Overall, we describe the first C. elegans screen to identify host factors that control microbiome bacterial colonization in the gut.

papers.title: Longitudinal CCR2 PET Imaging Tracks Early Inflammatory Monocyte and Macrophage Infiltration in Experimental Arthritis
papers.abstract: Objective. Recruitment of C-C motif chemokine receptor 2 (CCR2+) inflammatory monocytes and macrophages represent an early event in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) pathogenesis that cannot be tracked noninvasively with existing imaging modalities. We evaluated longitudinal Ga-DOTA-ECL1i positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) to track and quantify CCR2 cell recruitment in experimental inflammatory arthritis. Methods. Longitudinal Ga-DOTA-ECL1i PET/CT imaging was performed in K/BXN serum transfer arthritis (STA) mice. Imaging findings were validated using biodistribution, autoradiography, histopathology, immunofluorescence, microCT, cytokine profiling, clinical assessment, and pain-related behavioral testing. Results. Joint Ga-DOTA-ECL1i uptake increased during the acute arthritis and declined with disease resolution. Increased tracer signal localized to inflamed joints, coinciding with CCR2 monocyte and macrophage infiltration, synovial inflammation, cartilage damage, local CCL2 elevation, and mechanical allodynia. PET uptake correlated with ankle swelling, clinical disease severity, pain, and paw CCL2 levels, with peak tracer signal preceding progressive structural bone remodeling. Conclusion. Longitudinal Ga-DOTA-ECL1i PET/CT enables noninvasive visualization and quantification of early CCR2 monocyte and macrophage recruitment, establishing CCR2 PET imaging as a mechanism-based molecular platform for early detection, risk stratification, and therapeutic monitoring in inflammatory arthritis.

papers.title: Interpreting computational mechanism from multi-area neural recordings
papers.abstract: Distilling computational mechanisms from neural recordings requires disambiguating intrinsic dynamics from external inputs. Here, we introduce Dynamically Interacting Systems (DynISys), a multi-compartment dynamical-systems model that infers per-area dynamics and structured inter-area communication from multi-area spiking activity. DynISys combines neural ordinary differential equation (ODE) latent dynamics with injective latent-to-neural mappings to achieve expressive and trustworthy dynamical inference. When applied to simultaneous dorsal premotor (PMd) and primary motor (M1) recordings from a continuous reaching task, DynISys accurately reconstructs neuronal responses without inventing spurious latent features. Analyzing the model's dynamics reveals putative mechanisms for motor planning and execution, with PMd-to-M1 inputs positioning a stable fixed point in M1 that encodes execution dynamics for the upcoming movement, subsequently evoked by external (non-PMd) inputs. Finally, multi-session DynISys achieves consistent latents when fit to neural recordings spanning multiple days. In summary, DynISys allows distillation of multi-area recordings into an interpretable account of distributed neural computation.

papers.title: The antagonism of sex chromosomes and sex hormones dictates outcomes in Th17 cell-mediated central nervous system autoimmunity.
papers.abstract: Biological sex traits are shaped by the combined effects of both sex hormones and chromosomes. How these factors interact in sex-related autoimmune diseases, such as multiple sclerosis (MS), has been a subject of intense recent interest. Here, using the Four Core Genotype (FCG) mouse model, in which these two variables can be disentangled, we describe an antagonism between sex hormones and chromosomes that potently influences outcomes in T helper 17 (Th17)-driven progressive central nervous system (CNS) autoimmunity. Male gonadal hormones dampen disease severity, irrespective of sex chromosome complement, by promoting a Wnt/{beta}-catenin signaling program associated with a homeostatic, non-pathogenic Th17 phenotype. By contrast, XY chromosomal complement exacerbates Th17 pathogenicity in a recipient sex-dependent manner; we identify the X-linked molecule SUV39H1 as an inhibitor of inflammatory Th17 cell function. Unexpectedly, we found that hormonally and chromosomally female FCG Th17 cells induced far more severe disease than WT female counterparts despite being genetically identical, pointing to a parental imprinting effect in dictating Th17 cell pathogenicity. These latter investigations uncovered Runx2, a transcription factor previously linked to developmental programs, as a novel negative regulator of the pathogenicity of Th17 cells. Together, our findings establish biological sex as a multilayered regulator of Th17 pathogenicity, revealing distinct and sometimes opposing contributions of hormones, chromosomes, and parental inheritance.

papers.title: Tetravalent dengue mRNA vaccination orchestrates balanced four-serotype immunity with durable memory and protection in mice.
papers.abstract: An effective dengue vaccine must establish durable immunity across four dengue virus (DENV) serotypes, evade antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE), and overcome immune imprinting from prior exposure. Here, we developed TetprM-E mRNA-LNP, a tetravalent vaccine comprising LNP-formulated nucleoside-modified mRNAs encoding DENV1-4 precursor membrane-envelope (prM-E) antigens, and evaluated its immunogenicity, durability, protection and breath across serotype-specific immune backgrounds. Three immunization strategies elicited neutralizing titers greater than 1:1500 against each serotype. Passive transfer of immune sera conferred 100% survival and reduced viremia after lethal DENV2 challenge in immunocompromised mice. Vaccination induced DENV envelope (env)-specific CD8+T cells and CD4-dependent germinal-center responses. DENV env-binding antibodies persisted for 34 weeks alongside DENV env-specific memory B cells. Vaccine-elicited sera showed no measurable in vitro ADE. Although monovalent priming initially biased antibody responses, TetprM-E mRNA-LNP vaccination broadened neutralization across DENV1-4 regardless of priming serotype. Together, TetprM-E mRNA-LNP elicits broad, durable, and protective immunity despite serologic constraints from pre-existing immunity.

papers.title: Caregiver genotype influences larval body size in ants by modulating ecdysteroid production
papers.abstract: Parental genes shape the offspring's rearing environment and, consequently, offspring phenotypes. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these indirect genetic effects remain largely unknown. Here, using the clonal raider ant Ooceraea biroi, we uncover a neurohormonal mechanism by which caregiver genotypes affect larval body size and caste fate. Larval transcriptomics revealed caregiver-genotype effects on neuropeptides and an ecdysteroid biosynthesis gene, while enrichment analyses implicated changes in lipid metabolism. We found that the receptors of these candidate neuropeptides are expressed in the prothoracic gland, the site of ecdysteroid synthesis, and pharmacological manipulations revealed a neuropeptide-ecdysone axis that regulates body size in ants. The same hormonal axis also regulates multiple lipid-binding carrier protein genes expressed in larval fat-body cells. Together, we identify a neurohormonal pathway that is modulated by caregivers in developing larvae, linking lipid metabolism, systemic growth, and caste development.

papers.title: Assessing the Capacity of Genomic Language Models to Generate Informative Embeddings of Viral Genome Fragments
papers.abstract: Genomic language models (gLMs) trained on large volumes of nucleotide sequences are becoming an alternative to classical methods in metagenomic analysis, particularly for studying genomic "dark matter". In this work, we investigate the ability of four gLMs (DNABERT-2, DNABERT-S, ViraLM, and Evo2-7B) to generate taxonomically informative vector representations of short viral genome fragments. We constructed a balanced reference dataset of viruses based on the ICTV Virus Metadata Resource and compared the representations generated by gLMs with conventional k-mer profiles and MinHash sketches using clustering and neighborhood-based metrics (adjusted Rand index (ARI), precision@k, and CROSS precision@k). On the reference dataset, three of the four gLMs outperformed the 4-mer profile in terms of ARI and precision@5 under the same evaluation protocol. The best performance was generally achieved by intermediate model layers. Conventional k-mer profiles consistently outperformed MinHash sketches. We further evaluated the methods on two viral orders (egoviruses and mriyaviruses) absent from the reference dataset, with model layers and k-mer lengths selected exclusively on the reference dataset. DNABERT-S showed the most consistently strong performance across these two orders, ranking first on mriyaviruses and second on egoviruses, while k-mer profiles with Jensen-Shannon distance remained competitive. We also observed the consistency of representations between forward fragments and their reverse complements. Overall, the best-performing gLMs surpassed conventional baselines, although their advantage depended on the dataset and evaluation metric. The consistently strong performance of DNABERT-S suggests a potential benefit of contrastive fine-tuning and indicates that larger models are not necessarily more effective for generating taxonomically informative representations.

papers.title: Beyond tree-like evolution in ostariophysan fishes
papers.abstract: Phylogenetic trees have long been a powerful model of the evolutionary history. However, key processes in speciation, such as introgression and hybridization are difficult to depict with strictly binary trees alone, even with modern discordance metrics and post-hoc tests. Phylogenetic networks offer an intuitive way to estimate and interpret these reticulate events, as conflicting signal from gene trees should become evident as hybrid edges. Phylogenetic networks raise a number of challenges over tree-based analyses though, including the estimation of uncertainty and evaluating confidence among multiple competing network hypotheses. Here, we develop a new approach for assessing branch and topological support on networks using composite likelihood, and explore the utility of such statistics by revisiting competing evolutionary hypotheses in ostariophysan fishes. Our results suggest that a tree-like topology is not the best model for ostariophysans. A phylogenetic network with four reticulation events involving early-diverging lineages was the best alternative scenario. Our branch support metrics demonstrated non-negligible levels of uncertainty in the placement of those reticulation events though. An important question though, is if the uncertainty in the placement of these reticulation edges affects the qualitative conclusions of organismal evolution. To this end, we apply our network hypotheses to the biogeographic history of ostariophysans. Since no biogeographic models for networks exist, we implemented a parsimony approach using Fitch's algorithm for ancestral character state reconstruction. This represents the first biogeographic reconstruction for networks, and while simplistic, is a basis for further development. Biogeographic results are generally consistent with previous research on the presence of ancestral lineages in Laurasia and Gondwana post the break-up of Pangea, but also identify some cases of long-distance dispersal.

papers.title: Binding mechanisms of therapeutic antibodies to human claudin-18.2
papers.abstract: Claudin-18.2 (CLDN18.2) is a tight junction component with highly restricted expression in the paracellular space of nonmalignant gastric epithelial cells. It becomes accessible on tumor cell surface during malignant transformation, making CLDN18.2 an attractive target for targeted therapies against gastric cancer. Recently, zolbetuximab has become the first FDA-approved monoclonal antibody that targets CLDN18.2 in advanced gastric cancer, and others like osemitamab have entered phase 3 clinical trials. However, the high-resolution structure of CLDN18.2 is lacking, and how CLDN18.2 is recognized by therapeutic antibodies remains undefined. Here, we report cryo-EM structures of human claudin-18.2 (hCLDN18.2) in complex with the Fab fragments of zolbetuximab and osemitamab, revealing the structure of hCLDN18.2 and its binding mechanism to the therapeutic antibodies. Further analyses reveal that three residues in the first extracellular loop of hCLDN18.2 that are different from human claudin-18.1 (hCLDN18.1) play a critical role in antibody binding. Our data elucidate the structural basis for selective binding of therapeutic antibodies to hCLDN18.2, which should aid rational design of next-generation immunotherapies targeting hCLDN18.2.

papers.title: Synaptotagmin 7 differentially regulates synaptic vesicle trafficking at tonic and phasic synapses
papers.abstract: Synaptic vesicle (SV) release probability can differ across neuronal subtypes, but the molecular mechanisms establishing such differences remain incompletely understood. In the current study we demonstrate that Synaptotagmin 7 (SYT7), a calcium-sensor regulating SV trafficking, is enriched at Drosophila tonic Ib synapses compared with phasic Is synapses. Loss of SYT7 preferentially enhanced evoked release at Ib terminals, whereas overexpression strongly suppressed fusion at both neuronal subtypes. High-frequency stimulation partially overcomes this inhibition, producing robust facilitation. Ultrastructural analysis revealed that SYT7 overexpression preserved morphologically docked SVs while promoting accumulation of enlarged presynaptic cisternae and redistribution of SV-associated proteins. Conversely, SYT7 loss reduced activity-induced presynaptic cisternae, suggesting an important role in regulating the bulk endocytosis pathway. Together, these findings identify differential SYT7 abundance as a contributor to tonic and phasic synaptic diversity and reveal a role for SYT7 in coordinating SV release and presynaptic membrane cycling.

papers.title: SIFT: Syncmer-Informed Selection of Haplotypes for T2T Imputation
papers.abstract: Genome patching improves the completeness of fragmented assemblies by filling unresolved gaps with sequences from reference genomes. Pangenome panels provide diverse candidate haplotypes for this task, but identifying suitable references efficiently becomes increasingly challenging as these panels grow. We present SIFT, a compressed indexing method for selecting reference haplotypes for genome patching with ImpuT2T. SIFT combines closed-syncmer parsing, phrase-level indexing, and pseudo-maximal exact match (pseudo-MEM) queries. Closed syncmers provide a context-independent parsing rule with bounded distances between consecutive selected positions, enabling consistent parsing of reference and query sequences. We demonstrate that two closed syncmers determine the distance at which they can occur consecutively in any string, so that equal substrings of two parses represent identical sequences and no gap sequence need be stored. SIFT indexes the reference parse and its reverse using run-length compressed suffix arrays and adapts the Boyer-Moore-Li search procedure to identify pseudo-MEMs between the reference parse and query parse. It then aggregates matching evidence to identify candidate reference haplotypes for downstream patching. This framework connects compressed sequence indexing with haplotype selection and provides a basis for querying large reference panels at the phrase level. SIFT is publicly available under the GNU license at https://github.com/EddieFerro/SIFT.

papers.title: Paired-unit activation steering for context-aware protein design
papers.abstract: Activation steering in protein language models enables controllable sequence generation without changing the model weights. However, existing methods typically construct steering vectors from global differences between property-positive and property-negative protein populations, overlooking how property-improving directions vary across different protein sequence backgrounds. To address this, we propose \textit{Paired-Unit local steering of embeddings (PULSE)}, which matches positive- and negative-property proteins by maximizing their representation cosine similarity and constructs steering vectors by aggregating similarity-weighted, unit-normalized differences between matched pairs. Across three protein optimization objectives--solubility, immunogenicity, and toxicity--PULSE consistently outperforms global population-centroid steering in both final predicted property scores and optimization success rates. Further analysis reveals that conventional static steering-vector diagnostics cannot adequately explain optimization performance. To characterize steering reliability during iterative sequence editing, we introduce \textit{Local Directional Support (LDS)}, which measures how well successive representation changes align with property-improving directions from similar protein backgrounds. We show that LDS captures differences in trajectory reliability and enables predictor-free candidate prioritization, enriching successful protein designs without requiring property predictions during candidate selection. Together, these findings demonstrate the importance of context-aware steering and trajectory-level evaluation for controllable protein sequence optimization.

papers.title: Reprogramming transcription factor networks with a HOX inhibitor to address Huntington's disease biology beyond mutant huntingtin
papers.abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is an inherited neurodegenerative disorder caused by CAG-repeat expansion in the huntingtin (HTT) gene. Although inherited CAG-repeat length and the underlying somatic instability are key determinants of age at onset, they explain only part of onset variability, suggesting additional disease mechanisms. We applied the Core Coefficient (CC), a transcription-factor (TF) network-decoding technology that quantifies TF functional dominance, to >100 post-mortem neuronal transcriptomes from HD and control brain datasets. Among human TF families, the HOX family is the only family that uniformly exhibits quiescence in controls versus large and significant functional dominance in vulnerable neurons of each HD donor brain we investigated. HOX TFs are already dominant at Vonsattel grade 0 and at inherited CAG-repeat length. The magnitude of HOX CC values correlates with age at onset and increases with disease grade and CAG-Age Product. HOX TFs form a self-sustained pathological unit targeting >4,000 genes implicated in neuronal patterning, identity, stress, signaling, structure, and senescence. In zQ175 mice, abrogation of mutant huntingtin (mHTT) protein production only transiently attenuates HOX dominance and does not durably eliminate it. COR-H800, a HOX inhibitor, restored TF-network hierarchy toward wild type, normalizing the functional dominance of transcription factors involved in neuronal differentiation, cell-fate determination, and developmental patterning, and improved disease-relevant phenotypes in R6/2 mice. These findings support the direct selective inhibition of HOX TFs to address the aberrant transcriptional state that can persist despite mHTT lowering or somatic instability-targeted therapeutic interventions.

papers.title: DiffTernary: a Diffusion Model for Molecular Glue Ternary Complex Docking
papers.abstract: Molecular glues (MGs) modulate protein function by inducing or stabilizing protein interactions. However, accurately modeling MG ternary complexes remains challenging. Here, we present DiffTernary, a diffusion-based docking method for the joint prediction of relative protein arrangement and MG binding pose. We introduce Ternary-PDB, a dataset of 76,702 experimentally determined ternary complexes curated from the Protein Data Bank using structural filters and a release cutoff aligned with AlphaFold 3 (AF3). When trained on this dataset, DiffTernary achieved acceptable protein-protein interaction (PPI) predictions (DockQ > 0.23) for 50.0% of MGBench complexes with a single prediction, compared with 51.1% for AF3. In comparisons with AF3, OpenFold3, ESMFold2, Protenix-v1 and Protenix-v2, DiffTernary ranked second with a best-of-25 PPI prediction success rate of 78.4%, behind ESMFold2 (90.9%) and ahead of AF3 (72.7%). A separate DiffTernary model trained on TernaryDB achieved a mean DockQ of 0.306 on the 94 complexes in the TernaryDB MGD test set with a single prediction, compared with 0.228 for DeepTernary. Confidence-based selection among 40 samples yielded acceptable PPI predictions for 41.5% of complexes, compared with 30.9% for DeepTernary. An E2Former variant increased training and sampling throughput 6.90-fold and 4.37-fold, respectively, under the evaluated configurations. Together, DiffTernary and Ternary-PDB provide an efficient docking approach for MG complex prediction and a valuable structural resource for MG discovery and design.

papers.title: POM121 regulates lentiviral nuclear import in a capsid-host factor-dependent manner
papers.abstract: Lentiviruses such as human immunodeficiency virus 1 (HIV-1) access the nuclear lumen through the nuclear pore complex (NPC), a process coordinated by the interactions between the viral capsid and nucleoporins (NUPs). Here, using unbiased proteomic screens, we identified several capsid-associated NUPs, including POM121. Depletion of POM121 impaired HIV-1 infection in multiple cell lines and in primary CD4+ T cells, whereas equine infectious anaemia virus (EIAV) infection was enhanced, indicating that POM121 effect is virus-specific. A cytoplasmic carboxy-terminal fragment of POM121, containing its FG-rich region inhibited HIV-1 and a broader range of lentiviruses. Analysis of HIV-1 capsid mutants showed that physical interaction with POM121 does not predict functional dependence, as capsids retaining POM121 binding remained insensitive to its depletion. Strikingly, loss of cyclophilin A (CypA) completely abolished HIV-1 dependence on POM121, whereas depletion of CPSF6 produced only partial rescue, demonstrating that POM121 sensitivity is dictated by the broader network of capsid-host interactions. Finally, POM121 depletion impaired HIV-1 nuclear accumulation and selectively disrupted the nuclear import of other viral and cellular cargo. Together, these findings identify POM121 as a selective regulator of lentiviral nuclear entry whose functional contribution is determined by capsid and host-factor context.

papers.title: Accessory B Chromosomes Alter Chromatin Accessibility and Gene Expression in Maize Pollen Nuclei
papers.abstract: B chromosomes in maize (Zea mays L.) are supernumerary, nonessential chromosomes that exhibit non-Mendelian inheritance through chromosome drive. During the second pollen mitosis, they undergo nondisjunction, resulting in their preferential transmission via B-containing sperm cells. Although their transmission mechanisms have been extensively characterized, the effects on chromatin organization and transcriptional regulation in gametophytic cells remain poorly understood. Here, we combined flow cytometric sorting of pollen nuclei with an assay for transposase-accessible chromatin sequencing (ATAC-seq) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) to investigate the impact of B chromosomes on chromatin accessibility and gene expression in mature maize pollen. Using pollen nuclei isolated from a maize inbred line B73 carrying zero and two B chromosomes, we generated high-purity datasets suitable for integrated chromatin and transcriptomic analyses. We identified extensive chromatin accessibility and transcriptional activity at B-chromosome loci. Importantly, the presence of B chromosomes was also associated with altered chromatin accessibility and gene expression on the standard A chromosomes, revealing regulatory effects extending beyond the B chromosome itself. Together, these findings contribute to a broader understanding of effects of selfish genetic elements in plants.

papers.title: CellChat Hotspot: A Targeted Approach to Cell Cell Communication Analysis With Spatial transcriptomics Validation.
papers.abstract: Abstract. In recent years, single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA seq) has enabled the investigation of intercellular communication through Cell Cell Communication (CCC) tools such as CellChat. Despite their potential, these approaches remain challenging to interpret, particularly when global analyses generate complex interaction networks that may include biologically irrelevant signals. To address this limitation, we developed a framework termed CellChat Hotspot, designed to improve the biological interpretability of inferred communication networks. This approach integrates gene set enrichment analysis with a context driven filtering strategy, selecting both genes and cells based on their functional relevance prior to communication inference. Applied to stage II colon cancer data, CellChat Hotspot enabled the identification of condition-specific interaction patterns associated with recurrence. Non recurrent patients showed enrichment of immune related processes, whereas recurrent cases were characterized by pathways associated with invasion and metastasis. Notably, a loss of interaction in the HSPG pathway between CALB1+ and stromal cells was observed in recurrent patients, suggesting a potential disruption of cell matrix adhesion mechanisms. To verify the reliability of this finding, we applied the framework to spatial transcriptomics data, which confirmed the presence of the HSPG2 DAG1 interaction in non-recurrent tumors and its near absence in recurrent ones. Overall, this framework provides a biologically guided strategy for studying intercellular communication in complex systems such as the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Integrated exome-transcriptome analysis of a schizophrenia case with an exceptionally low polygenic risk score
papers.abstract: Schizophrenia liability reflects both common polygenic variation and rarer variants of larger effect. We investigated a post-mortem schizophrenia case (SZ07) with a schizophrenia polygenic risk score below the first percentile among ancestry-matched cases, asking whether individual-level genomic and transcriptomic analyses could help identify potentially novel schizophrenia-relevant variants. We used exome analysis with multiple variant-prediction tools to generate a panel of variants and corresponding candidate genes potentially implicated in the pathological process in SZ07. The prioritised variants were then assessed using RNA sequencing of three cortical regions. Of these, only an IZUMO4 splice-acceptor variant showed direct RNA-level support. Beyond variant-specific analyses, we characterised broader transcriptomic abnormalities in the SZ07 brain. Pathway analysis of gene-level expression deviations implicated innate immune processes, calcium signalling, synaptic biology, and axon remodelling. Notably, compared with conventional single-sample biological pathway analysis, the analysis we used showed only a weak association with neuronal specificity, suggesting their reduced sensitivity to the main axis of variation related to cellular composition in bulk brain tissue gene expression data. Although the candidate genes showed no significant pathway-level convergence, the broader transcriptomic profile revealed coherent biological alterations largely compatible with the documented history of cerebrovascular disease in SZ07. These results demonstrate how the integration of exome and transcriptome data at the individual level enables the formulation and constraint of hypotheses regarding patient-specific genetic features and their molecular consequences, while highlighting important limitations related to tissue composition, comorbidity, and the choice of reference cohort.

papers.title: Shared landscape, divergent genomes: Comparative population genomics of co-occurring flora in an isolated Australian mountain range
papers.abstract: Understanding how landscape heterogeneity shapes genomic variation is key to conserving biodiversity and evolutionary potential. Yet conservation genomics is typically conducted at the single species level, limiting our ability to identify shared genomic patterns or understand how co-occurring taxa differ in their response to common environmental gradients. We assessed spatial patterns of genomic variation and their associations with geographic and environmental features among populations of nine co-existing plant species with contrasting life-histories and ecological traits across Gariwerd, a threatened biodiversity hotspot in south-eastern Australia. All species exhibited weak overall genetic structure, although the magnitude and spatial distribution of differentiation varied among species. Despite this variation, broadly consistent spatial trends were apparent, with higher genomic divergence largely concentrated in central zones and higher genomic diversity localised in southern regions of the landscape. Significant associations between genetic differentiation and geographic distance were observed in three species, while another species showed associations with environmental distance. These findings demonstrate that coexisting species can show overlapping spatial patterns in genomic variation while differing markedly in their associations with geographic and environmental variation across the same landscape. This comparative approach provides a basis for spatial prioritisation and conservation planning, while highlighting the complex eco-evolutionary processes operating across heterogeneous landscapes.

papers.title: Temporal Dynamics of Multi-Item Working Memory Maintenance in Human Gaze Patterns and EEG
papers.abstract: Maintaining multiple items in working memory (WM) requires the allocation of limited resources, which may involve prioritizing individual items over others. Previous work has suggested that attentional prioritization can vary rhythmically between WM samples, but direct empirical evidence for such temporal fluctuations remains scarce. Here, we recorded eye-tracking and EEG to track the temporal dynamics of multi-item processing while participants maintained up to three object orientations in WM. Whereas EEG encoding was only short-lived, miniature gaze patterns reflected the orientations of all three items throughout the entire WM delay and showed systematic load and serial position effects. Contrary to rhythmic sampling accounts, however, we found no evidence that eye movements alternated between the concurrently maintained items. Furthermore, the strength of WM encoding in gaze was not modulated by frontal theta activity in EEG, suggesting that oculomotor encoding was not directly coupled to rhythmic neural dynamics associated with WM and internal attention. Together, our findings indicate that the oculomotor signature of visuospatial WM processing was rather stably shaped by all of the simultaneously maintained items. The results further corroborate that eye-tracking and EEG provide complementary windows into the temporal dynamics of WM.

papers.title: ACE-engineered human iPSC-derived neutrophils enhance host defense against multidrug-resistant bacterial infections
papers.abstract: Severe neutropenia predisposes patients to life-threatening infections, while donor-dependent granulocyte transfusions are limited by availability and variable cell quality. Here, we engineered human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) to constitutively or inducibly express angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) and differentiated them into functional ACE-engineered neutrophils (ACE-iNeu). ACE expression enhanced granulocytic maturation, reactive oxygen species generation, inflammatory cytokine production, and antimicrobial signaling. ACE-iNeu exhibited enhanced bactericidal activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Following adoptive transfer into neutropenic mice, ACE-iNeu significantly reduced circulating and tissue bacterial burdens. Integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses revealed ACE-associated alterations in adenine nucleotide abundance and developmental and inflammatory pathways. Together, these findings establish ACE engineering as a strategy to enhance the production and antimicrobial function of human iPSC-derived neutrophils and support further preclinical development of engineered granulocyte therapies for severe drug-resistant infections.

papers.title: GSNOR-dependent nitric oxide homeostasis shapes methylome persistence after multi-generational exposure to future climate conditions in Arabidopsis thaliana
papers.abstract: Environmental stress can modify plant DNA methylation, but the roles of nitric oxide homeostasis in methylome recovery and multigenerational persistence remain unclear. We used whole-genome bisulfite sequencing to compare Arabidopsis thaliana wild type and the GSNOR-deficient mutant (gsnor1-3) exposed to drought, elevated CO2, ozone, heat, or their combination during generation G1 to G3, followed by two generations under control conditions. Methylomes from G1, G3, and G5 were analysed for global divergence, differentially methylated regions, genomic annotation, and methylation trajectories and were integrated with matched RNA-seq and independent datasets. Control methylomes of gsnor1-3 were already distinct from those of the wild type, and the mutant accumulated substantially more DMRs, with a strong hypermethylation bias. In gsnor1-3, 44.1 to 45.7% of G1 CG DMRs retained their direction through G3 and G5, compared with 0.09 to 1.24% in wild type; persistent CHG and CHH DMRs were also markedly more abundant. Persistent regions occurred at genes, promoters, and transposable elements and were associated with broader expression responses in the mutant. Independent datasets supported a subset of these regions, including directional agreement for 211 of 292 published GSNOR-associated DMRs. These results indicate that GSNOR-dependent nitric oxide homeostasis contributes to methylome stability and resetting after repeated environmental exposure.

papers.title: A high-throughput all-optical platform for mapping gene perturbations to electrophysiology
papers.abstract: Electrical phenotyping remains a bottleneck in linking genes to cellular function. We developed a high-throughput all-optical electrophysiology platform combining an engineered human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) line, wide-field voltage imaging, and automated analysis. The hiPSC line integrates inducible NGN2, CRISPR interference, and degron-gated expression of Voltron2 and CheRiff, enabling neuronal differentiation, targeted gene knockdown, and optical electrophysiology. The microscope records approximately 1,500 spiking glutamatergic neurons at 800 Hz across a 4x4 mm field, with larger fields supporting approximately 3,000 neurons at 660 Hz. Automated analysis extracts single-cell voltage traces and quantifies firing patterns, action-potential waveforms, and subthreshold dynamics. Arrayed knockdown of five sodium- and potassium-channel genes produced distinct electrophysiological phenotypes.
