The engineered hiPSC line also supported optical electrophysiology recordings from motor neurons, astrocytes, and cardiomyocytes. These results establish a scalable platform for high-throughput electrophysiological phenotyping and functional genomics in hiPSC-derived cells.

papers.title: TaxaAudit: A statistical model of consensus in phylogenetics identifies non-monophyletic taxa
papers.abstract: Interpreting variation in genes and traits across species requires understanding their evolutionary relationships. Taxonomic hierarchies provide a practical approximation of the tree of life, with the NCBI taxonomy linking this framework directly to public sequence data. Some named groups, however, are not evolutionary clades, and recognizing these exceptions requires knowledge scattered across the phylogenetics literature. Here we introduce TaxaAudit, a statistical model that identifies taxonomic groups whose monophyly is repeatedly contradicted by published phylogenies. The model accounts for background taxonomic conflict and the ability of each study's species sampling to expose non-monophyly. Applied to 5,865 molecular phylogenies from TimeTree, TaxaAudit flagged 516 NCBI taxa at family rank and below for significant recurrent contradiction of monophyly. Excluding these taxa's monophyly requirements improved the taxonomy's agreement with independent phylogenomic reference trees and phylogenies withheld from discovery. Flagged taxa were also 3.61 times as likely as matched controls to have their monophyly challenged in publications outside the discovery set. In tree-inference experiments, excluding these monophyly constraints improved agreement with reference phylogenies relative to enforcing the unmodified taxonomy. By identifying groups whose monophyly should not be assumed, TaxaAudit lets researchers draw on published phylogenetic knowledge without reviewing the specialist literature for every taxon. This supports broader use of the NCBI taxonomy as an evolutionary framework for biological comparisons.

papers.title: Uncovering Features of ProteinMPNN with Sparse Autoencoders
papers.abstract: Customization and modification of machine learning derived sequences can be achieved by understanding the mechanics behind state-of-the-art protein design models such as ProteinMPNN. Uninterpretability is hypothesized to be due largely to polysemanticity where neural networks store more features than they have dimensions. Here, we introduce sparse autoencoders (SAEs) into ProteinMPNN which expand its latent space and uncovers correlations between the activations in sparse dimensions and the presence of protein features such as secondary structure, residue volume, residue shape, disulfide bridges, and coordination to ligands. Additionally, we show that sparse activations can be manipulated to produce a variant of the short chain variable fragment Brolucizumab that is more thermostable than variants produced by traditional machine learning methods based on high temperature molecular dynamics simulations. Thus, SAEs provide both mechanistic understanding of protein design models and allow customizable manipulation of sequence prediction.

papers.title: Necroptosis is a targetable driver of severe coronavirus pathogenesis
papers.abstract: Human-pathogenic coronaviruses differ dramatically in pathogenicity but the underlying mechanisms are incompletely understood. Here, we demonstrate that highly pathogenic coronaviruses trigger necroptosis in the infected cells and lung tissues, whereas necroptosis is not detected in cells infected by seasonal coronavirus. Mechanistically, highly pathogenic coronaviruses produce Z-RNA, activate ZBP1 and initiates necroptotic cell death signaling, triggering necroinflammation and lung injury. In contrast, seasonal coronaviruses produce little to no Z-RNA, and do not activate necroptosis. Importantly, small-molecule inhibition of necroptosis attenuates inflammatory cytokine expression and markedly ameliorates lung damage in mice infected with all three highly pathogenic coronaviruses, independent of virus clearance. Overall, our study identifies necroptosis as a dominant mediator of coronavirus pathogenesis, and positions necroptosis blockade as a new therapeutic target against severe coronavirus diseases.

papers.title: Visual object recognition in the fly: the internal representation of a predator drives defensive behaviour
papers.abstract: Animals recognize visual objects and respond to them appropriately to survive. This process is thought to unfold in stages: the visual scene is first deconstructed into constituent features, which are then reconstructed into representations of object identity and relayed to motor circuits. Here we define a neural circuit in Drosophila that underlies the visual recognition of a natural predator, the parasitoid wasp, and orchestrates defence. We found that flies exhibit a repertoire of directed defensive actions structured by the wasp's position within the fly's field of view. Expression of these behaviours is driven by visual detection of a conspicuous morphological cue -- the wasp's elongated antennae. A small subset of lobula columnar (LC) visual projection neuron types are required for defence and are activated by constituent visual features of the wasp. Three LC types respond selectively to the wasp's antennae, and relay this information to LC9, which sums antennal- and body-feature signals to form a composite representation of the wasp. Spatial filtering of this representation onto a descending premotor pathway translates the wasp's location in visual space into directed defence. Feature combination followed by spatial filtering may constitute a general mechanism for coupling object identity to context-appropriate action.

papers.title: Design of colipids with controlled lateral distance of head group moieties for targeting strategies in the field of lipid-based nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles and liposomes are nanoparticle drug formulations which are firmly established in clinics. In order to expand their application and improve efficacy, surface modifications can be a key strategy, especially for cell specific targeting. Targeting can be achieved by integrating ligand functionalized lipids or lipidoids on the nanoparticle surface. In this case, not solely the targeting ligand itself, but also the structure of the whole targeting lipid/lipidoid can affect the interaction of the targeting ligand with the binding motive on cells. Especially, distal spacer structures between lipid anchor and ligand unit, often composed of polyethylene glycol chains, provide a certain distance of the ligand from the nanoparticle surface. A concept which is currently neglected is the control of the lateral distance between ligand structures on the nanoparticle. Herein we investigated the possibility to design lipidoids with a lateral spacer composed of polyethylene glycol units. We synthesized and characterized different lipidoids which provide a primary amine in the head group for possible ligand coupling. In our model lipidoids the head groups were functionalized with a paramagnetic probe to apply electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) methods for the characterization of the lipidoid interaction with model nanoparticles, in our case liposomes. Continuous wave EPR was used to study the efficiency of the novel lipidoids to integrate into lipid bilayers of model liposomes, which was shown to depend on lipidoid structure and liposome composition. Furthermore, using double electron-electron resonance (DEER), we observed lipidoid conformational changes occurring upon integration into liposomes.

papers.title: Tracking the conformational dynamics of single molecules in live cells; GTPase cycling in Cdc42 gradients and microclusters
papers.abstract: The Rho family of GTPases play a critical role in many cellular processes by acting as molecular switches relying on conformational changes to transition between active and inactive states. The spatial distribution and kinetics of these conformational changes are complex and vary across the cell. We describe here biosensors based on environment-responsive fluorescent dyes, capable of reporting the conformational changes of individual GTPase molecules as they traffic within living cells (SPARC Cdc42 and SPARC Rac1, 'Single Particle Activation Reporter Constructs'). We use SPARC Cdc42 to determine the rates of different steps in GTPase regulation, activation/inactivation and membrane insertion, that together generate localized gradients of Cdc42 activity driving cell motility. The biosensors also revealed heterogeneously distributed clusters of Cdc42, the mechanisms of their activation, and potential roles in polarized motility.

papers.title: A protocol for cortical and deep-brain calcium imaging in freely moving mice with the Mini2P system.
papers.abstract: Two-photon calcium imaging has transformed our understanding of neuronal circuit function, yet conventional approaches require head fixation, limiting the study of neural activity during natural behavior. Miniaturized two-photon microscopy (Mini2P) overcomes this constraint by enabling calcium imaging in freely moving animals while preserving the optical single-cell resolution of conventional two-photon microscopy. However, its implementation requires the careful integration of multiple technically demanding procedures, presenting substantial challenges for laboratories adopting this approach. Here, we present a comprehensive, step-by-step protocol for implementing Mini2P calcium imaging in freely moving mice, emphasizing procedures that are unique to or particularly critical for successful implementation of this technique. This protocol covers system preparation and performance checks, optical alignment, field-of-view selection, baseplate installation, and strategies for maintaining imaging stability during microscope attachment and reattachment. We also address behavioral habituation, integration with behavioral tasks, imaging acquisition, quality control, and troubleshooting as a part of an integrated experimental workflow. Representative imaging data acquired through cranial windows in the primary visual and somatosensory cortices, and through a gradient-index lens in the medial prefrontal cortex, illustrate the applicability of this workflow across different brain regions and optical preparations. Designed for adaptation across brain regions and behavioral paradigms, the protocol provides practical guidance for identifying technical challenges and verifying successful implementation. By establishing clear decision points, validation criteria, and troubleshooting strategies at each stage, this workflow aims to improve reproducibility and facilitate the adoption of the Mini2P for investigating neuronal circuit dynamics during freely moving behavior.

papers.title: OpenDrive: An Open-Source Microdrive for Large-Scale Neurophysiology
papers.abstract: Neuropixels-NHP probes have ushered in a new era of high-density neurophysiology recording in large animal models. Here, we present OpenDrive, an open-source microdrive system designed specifically for acute insertion of Neuropixels-NHPs. OpenDrive combines a custom motorized microdrive, six-drive control console, and software platform. Compared with commercially available options, OpenDrive offers (1) low cost, (2) precise, accurate, and stable probe movement, (3) scalability to many-probe recording, and (4) open-source hardware designs and software. In our experiments, OpenDrive has already supported recordings from thousands of neurons across a variety of cortical and subcortical structures. By lowering technical barriers and enabling community-driven development with OpenDrive, we aim to accelerate Neuropixels recording in large animal models.

papers.title: An LFP-based characterization of population-level heterogeneity during motor preparation & execution
papers.abstract: The goal of the present work is to characterize mesoscale heterogeneity of population-level neural activity in the motor areas during motor preparation and execution using high-frequency local field potentials (HF-LFPs). Understanding the distribution of neural activity at this scale is necessary since ensembles of neural populations underlie most behaviors. HF-LFPs have emerged as a promising signal for such analysis due to their stability and relationship with cortical population dynamics. Here we analyzed HF-LFPs in non-human primates performing a reach-to-grasp task. We quantified three complementary aspects of heterogeneity: variance, latent dimensionality, and directional coherence. Heterogeneity varied by region and neuromotor state, and was specific to the motor behavior being implemented, even in regions exhibiting high correlation. In addition, more heterogeneous activity tended to better encode neuromotor states. Namely, regions and neuromotor states exhibiting higher variance and dimensionality yielded superior motor decoding performance. Further analyses involving low-dimensional linear projections of the signals revealed rich intra-region interactions between ensembles of populations. The present work helps establish intra-region heterogeneity as a multi-faceted and informative measure of neural activity, even on small spatial scales. It also establishes HF-LFPs as an effective signal for capturing complex intra-region dynamics, making it a suitable candidate for multi-region, systems-level analysis.

papers.title: An application of fNIRS for the prediction of hearing thresholds in sleeping infants: a proof of principle
papers.abstract: This study applied a two-component-response modelling approach to fNIRS recordings obtained from naturally sleeping infants presented with auditory stimuli at different sound intensities. We investigated whether the relationship between fNIRS response measures and stimulus intensity could be modelled to estimate individual auditory hearing thresholds. In the normal-hearing group, 75% of infants had threshold estimates for the sound /ba/ within the expected normal-hearing range, with an estimated mean equivalent normal loudness (ENL) of 10.72 dB HL (SD 8.64 dB HL). A case study further explored the potential application of this approach in an infant with hearing impairment, highlighting the importance of reliable responses at lower stimulus intensities and appropriate regression model selection. These findings provide preliminary evidence that cortical haemodynamic responses can be quantitatively related to sound intensity for estimating auditory sensitivity.

papers.title: A High-Efficiency Geranylation Platform Enabled by Rational Tuning of a Single-Residue-Coded Chemo- and Regioselective Switch in Aromatic Prenyltransferases
papers.abstract: Geranylation is an efficient post-modification strategy for enhancing or introducing new properties to molecules; however, achieving both high efficiency and precision remains challenging. Aromatic prenyltransferases (PTs) provide a mild and sustainable approach, yet their practical application is often limited by the trade-off between broad substrate scope and low selectivity, and successfully balancing these properties is rare. Here, using the pharmaceutically relevant cannabigerol framework as a model, we identify a single-residue switch in a prenyltransferase from Aspergillus terreus (AtaPT) that governs both chemo- and regioselectivity. Rational tuning of this switch preserves broad substrate scope while enhancing selectivity, enabling the selective formation of each of the three possible mono-geranylated products in the model reaction. Structural analysis reveals that this residue modulates the selectivity and activity through coupled steric and electrostatic effects. Notably, transplantation of this site into three homologous PTs similarly reprogrammed selectivity, establishing a conserved and generalizable control mechanism. Leveraging these insights, we achieved selective geranylation across 36 aromatic substrates, affording 41 products. Integration with an efficient geranyl donor regeneration system enabled preparative-scale synthesis, reaching titers up to 324 mg/L. This work defines a unifying mechanism for selectivity control in PTs and provides a high-efficiency platform for geranylation.

papers.title: A shared slowing axis and phenotype-specific rhythms link clinical EEG to FDG-PET dementia phenotypes
papers.abstract: Early and accurate identification of neurodegenerative disorders has notable implications for treatment and quality of life. Whereas neuroimaging-based biomarkers can accurately identify neurodegenerative subtypes, EEG represents a low-cost alternative that could expand access to dementia care. Here, we investigated whether six data-driven EEG latent factors, derived by nonnegative tensor decomposition of clinical EEGs, differ systematically across FDG-PET-defined neurodegenerative phenotypes. In 455 patients with EEG and FDG-PET acquired within one year of each other, factor expression was compared across 14 diagnostic classes assigned by StateViewer, a validated artificial intelligence framework for FDG-PET interpretation. To separate disease-general severity from phenotype-specific topography, each factor was also regressed on a subject-level slowing index. Finally, we related the factors to regional FDG uptake and to neuropsychological performance (n = 98) and assessed their potential utility for single-subject classification. Four factors reflecting neurophysiological oscillations (posterior alpha, Rolandic beta, frontotemporal delta-theta and posterior theta-slow alpha) varied significantly across phenotypes, with attenuation of faster and augmentation of slower rhythms most pronounced in dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), dysexecutive Alzheimer disease (AD) and posterior cortical atrophy, whereas factors dominated by eye-movement and muscle artifact showed no robust phenotypic association. Alpha and beta effects were largely attributable to overall slowing, whereas posterior theta-slow alpha became more phenotype-specific after adjustment (eta-squared 0.082 to 0.147), dissociating the Alzheimer disease spectrum from frontotemporal syndromes. The slowing index tracked with an FDG-PET pattern highly associated with DLB across the cohort, irrespective of assigned phenotype (r = 0.51, P < 0.001). Consistent with a model in which dementia phenotypes reflect altered hippocampal-neocortical oscillatory coupling (stochastic latent oscillatory diffusion), frontotemporal delta-theta tracked a limbocortical axis of metabolic pattern expression, rising with neocortical and falling with limbic-predominant involvement, independent of overall slowing and phenotype. Each factor mapped onto a distinct metabolic topography, with frontotemporal delta-theta resembling Alzheimer-type hypometabolism and posterior theta-slow alpha the medial occipital hypometabolism of DLB. In terms of neuropsychological performance, Rolandic beta was associated with executive functions, and frontotemporal delta-theta with memory, visuospatial and global performance. Using these four factors alone, an exploratory logistic regression classifier separated cognitively unimpaired participants from DLB, posterior cortical atrophy, typical AD, and dysexecutive AD (area under the curve > 0.8) but poorly discriminated frontotemporal dementia phenotypes canonically associated with 4-repeat tau. Thus, data-driven decomposition of clinical EEG separates oscillatory activity from artifact into factors that track metabolic phenotype, regional metabolism and cognition, capturing both overall slowing and phenotype-specific patterns. This work informs the further development of scalable, biology-informed EEG-based phenotyping of neurodegenerative disease.

papers.title: Ocean current models predict spatial structure for coastal biodiversity
papers.abstract: Genomic diversity provides the raw material through which all evolutionary processes occur. Accurately describing how environmental features affect patterns of diversity shows promise in predicting the resilience of populations and entire communities to dynamic environments and novel stressors. Identifying the contribution of purely neutral responses to environmental effects can be difficult, especially across large spatial ranges with many covarying environmental features. Using an individual-based model of larvae carried by ocean currents, we predict patterns of neutral genomic diversity in a passively dispersed coastal species, suggesting large geographic regions of relative homogeneity with ancestry determined by the nearest "upstream" population with limited larval input. The genomic identity that dominates each region sharply transitions at the next such interruption, generating hierarchical structure and violating assumptions of isolation-by-distance. We call these upstream populations "lineage source regions" (LSRs), and we find strong concordance between LSR model predictions and an empirical population genomic survey of a keystone salt marsh mussel (Geukensia demissa). We quantitatively validate model performance and goodness-of-fit, updating baseline predictions of genomic diversity patterns from the classic isolation-by-distance model to this LSR framework. This spatially explicit coastal ancestry model has potential for generalization across passive dispersing species.

papers.title: Prevalent Integration of both Xenotropic and Ecotropic Murine Leukemia Virus in the Human Genome of Xenografts
papers.abstract: Humanized mouse models are widely used in medical research to represent human conditions (1, 2), but their fidelity could be compromised by mouse-originated infections. However, their susceptibility to mouse pathogens are rarely questioned (3). Here we screened 1,619 publicly available genomic sequencing runs from patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models for the integration of murine leukemia virus (MLV), a rodent retrovirus exists in the mouse genome as an endogenous retrovirus (4), within the human genome. We discovered substantial enrichment of human-MLV chimeric DNA in approximately 25% of them. Analyzing the human-MLV junctions, we found about 90% of them bearing the unmistakable hallmarks of retroviral integration, including the canonical MLV boundaries and the distinctive 4-bp target site duplications (5, 6). It was also assumed that mouse strains without the highly infectious Bxv1 provirus are safe from MLV contamination in xenografts (7, 8). However, we found many PDX models derived from Bxv1- strains, including the widely used NSG strain, are also contaminated by the supposedly rodent-specific ecotropic MLV (E-MLV). We further confirmed a complete E-MLV integrated into the human genome by both HiFi and sanger sequencing. Our discovery raises concerns that mouse-to-human retroviral transmission and integration is more common and less restrictive than previously appreciated. They support examination of MLV integration as a feature of humanized mouse models with implications on the fidelity of these models in recapitulating human cells and tissues. Our discovery also has underscored the importance of comprehensively inactivation of porcine endogenous retroviruses for the clinical application of xenotransplatation (9, 10).

papers.title: CoReg, tracking-based motion compensation for in vivo calcium imaging
papers.abstract: In vivo calcium imaging enables the observation of neural activity with high spatial and temporal resolution. However, recordings are frequently affected by motion artifacts caused by animal movement, physiological processes, tissue drift, or instability of the imaging setup. These artifacts make signal extraction harder and reduce the consistency of downstream analyses. Current registration methods can correct rigid and non-rigid motion, but often estimate motion from individual frames or image patches and make limited use of temporal information. In addition, activity-driven fluorescence changes can make it difficult to distinguish changes in image appearance from actual motion. Here, we treat motion correction in calcium imaging as a point tracking problem and introduce CoReg, an open-source Python- based software tool with a graphical user interface. We benchmark CoReg against established registration methods using fluorescence imaging datasets from multiple species. CoReg performs competitively with or better than existing approaches across several settings. We further show that its performance is robust to the choice of tracked points, making the method straightforward to apply. CoReg includes implementations of both our method and the evaluated established methods. Our results show that tracking-based registration provides a simple and reliable approach for motion correction in vivo calcium imaging.

papers.title: Adult-like thick-filament protein stoichiometry in immature human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes
papers.abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) retain immature sarcomeric isoforms, raising questions about their ability to recapitulate the protein stoichiometry of adult human myocardium. We integrated two independent quantitative proteomic datasets of iPSC-CMs with published fetal and region-resolved adult human heart proteomes to compare sarcomeric protein abundance. Although iPSC-CMs clustered with fetal heart based on their global shared proteome and retained fetal troponin I expression, key thick-filament protein ratios closely matched those of adult myocardium. Myosin heavy-to-light chain ratios approached the expected 2:4 stoichiometry, while myosin-binding protein abundance relative to myosin heavy chains was comparable across iPSC-CMs and adult cardiac regions. These findings reveal that developmental immaturity in sarcomeric isoform expression does not entail altered thick-filament protein proportions. Preservation of adult-like myosin-binding protein stoichiometry supports the use of iPSC-CMs to investigate sarcomeric diseases associated with altered protein dosage, particularly MYBPC3-associated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

papers.title: Sequence context and partner availability specify divergent cell fates from a single transcription factor
papers.abstract: Transcription factors drive the gene regulatory networks that control developmental transitions, yet which of their many targets a cell uses remains unresolved. Expressing Cebp, Cebp{beta} or Cebp{delta} identically, alone or with Oct4, Sox2, Klf4 and cMyc, gave four outcomes: adipocyte from fibroblasts and neural stem cells, trophectoderm from embryonic stem cells, and myeloid from B cells. Raising Cebp levels changed how many sites it reached, not which sequence it read: clustered motifs maintained somatic enhancers, while spillover onto low-copy sites created de novo enhancers carrying composites of Cebp and cell-type-restricted partners. In fibroblasts, Cebp also redistributed Oct4, Sox2 and Klf4 from early targets, blocking iPSC formation. Supplying the predicted partners rewrote the output: Spi1 redirected Cebp into parallel adipogenic and myeloid programs, via a transient PpargCD45 state using separate enhancers for each; TFAP2C abolished adipogenic conversion. Motif density and partner composites therefore assemble a factor's instructive output in the receiving cell.

papers.title: Ecological opportunity and evolutionary relatedness predict parasite sharing differently across mammalian taxonomic scales
papers.abstract: As global change brings species into new contact, understanding the ecological and evolutionary drivers of parasite sharing is essential for anticipating and mitigating disease emergence. Yet, the relative importance of geographic proximity and evolutionary relatedness among host species in predicting parasite sharing remains unresolved. We tested whether their relative importance changes across host taxonomic scale using 30,310 recorded associations between 680 mammalian and 11,107 parasite species. Geography accounted for 86.6% importance within genera, declining to 44.7% across all mammals, shifting toward evolutionary relatedness predominating. Parasite sharing increased nonlinearly with geographic proximity and host relatedness, and the overall trend varied among parasite types. Notably, accounting for host taxonomic scale improved parasite-sharing prediction accuracy. To explore the consequences of biotic homogenization, we applied a counterfactual scenario of reducing geographic distance by 99%, which increased mean predicted parasite sharing to 13.71% within genera and 1.50% at the class level. Together, these findings suggest that ecological opportunity is especially consequential among close relatives whereas evolutionary similarity is increasingly important among geographically distant species. Accounting for evolutionary scale can therefore improve sharing predictions and help identify which new host encounters warrant surveillance for cross-species transmission and disease emergence.

papers.title: Genotype-Informed Drosophila Kinome Screening Prioritizes PRKX as a Candidate Vulnerability in Bladder Cancer
papers.abstract: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer is molecularly heterogeneous, and the basal/squamous subtype frequently exhibits elevated EGFR expression and TP53 and RB1 alterations. Functional vulnerabilities associated with these alterations remain incompletely defined, while large-scale in vivo screening in mammalian models is experimentally demanding. Therefore, we developed a genotype-defined Drosophila melanogaster model combining Egfr overexpression, mutant p53, and Rbf suppression in Malpighian tubules. The resulting 3-hit model showed increased Malpighian tubule volume and reduced adult eclosion rate. A dominant modifier screen targeting 216 kinase genes identified 72 genes whose perturbation significantly increased the eclosion rate, and a complementary RNA interference screen identified eight kinases whose knockdown increased the eclosion rate. Among these hits, Pka-C3, which is a Drosophila ortholog of human PRKX, emerged as one of the strongest suppressors of the 3-hit phenotype. PRKX was prioritized for further study because public transcriptomic datasets showed higher PRKX expression in bladder tumors than in normal bladder tissue. PRKX knockdown reduced spheroid volume in four human bladder cancer cell lines with distinct EGFR, TP53, and RB1 profiles. Both small interfering RNAs produced significant reductions in two cell lines, whereas only one siRNA reached significance in the other two. These findings nominate PRKX as a candidate vulnerability in bladder cancer and highlight a cross-species approach that combines genotype-informed Drosophila screening with functional testing in human cancer cells to prioritize targets for further investigation.

papers.title: Endogenous Mechanical Reporters Encode the Global Mechanical Landscape of Morphogenesis
papers.abstract: Developmental systems usually comprise multiple genetically programmed morphogenetic events within a mechanically continuous environment, yet how individual processes interact and contribute to the overall mechanical landscape remains unknown. Here, we introduce the concept of mechanical reporter: endogenous tissues function as in situ probes of the embedded mechanical landscape. We exemplified cephalic furrow (CF) migration as a mechanical reporter in gastrulating Drosophila. Using optogenetics and genetics, we revealed that CF displacement reflects the combined effect of both force and tissue mechanical properties. By incorporating condition-specific mechanical landscape into a continuum minimal-response model, we developed a framework to quantitatively predict the reporter dynamics. Using different genetic mutants, we successfully decoded changes in the mechanical landscape from CF dynamics in gastrulating Drosophila. Overall, we established a predictive framework that uses CF dynamics to infer changes in the global mechanical landscape. Beyond this, the concept of mechanical reporter provides a general strategy for systematically understanding and decoding complex mechanical environments in living systems.

papers.title: An architectural RNA builds a reaction crucible through molecular concentration and activated enzyme selection
papers.abstract: Architectural RNAs (arcRNAs) scaffold membraneless organelles (MLOs), yet how they organize functional proteins remains unclear. Nuclear stress bodies (nSBs), MLOs scaffolded by HSATIII arcRNAs, incorporate SRSFs during stress. During stress recovery, nSBs function as reaction crucibles that recruit the kinase CLK1 to accelerate SRSF rephosphorylation and normalize stress-induced splicing. Here, we identify the ASAP complex as a recruitment factor that recognizes Ser341-phosphorylated, catalytically activated CLK1. HSATIII-bound SRSFs recruit ASAP, assembling a platform for CLK1 recruitment. Biochemical reconstitution reveals that this platform enhances SRSF phosphorylation by concentrating SRSFs and CLK1 while selectively recruiting activated CLK1, establishing nSB reaction crucibles as molecular concentrators and selectors. The SRSF-ASAP-CLK1 interaction network is conserved between humans and mice, suggesting that primate-specific HSATIII arcRNAs co-opted this pre-existing network to establish reaction-crucible function in nSBs. Our findings reveal how arcRNAs organize functional proteins through quantitative enrichment and qualitative selection to build biochemically active MLOs.

papers.title: Multi-Structure Segmentation of Type B Aortic Dissection from CT Images with U-Net
papers.abstract: Type B aortic dissection (TBAD) is a life-threatening condition in which a tear in the intimal layer separates the aortic wall into a true and a false lumen. Assessment of the lumen, the intimal flap, and false-lumen thrombosis from CT images is important for risk analysis and treatment planning. This work applied U-Net-based deep neural networks to the automatic segmentation of these structures in TBAD. We collected 46 CT scans from 20 patients, with voxel-wise annotations of three structures: the aortic lumen, the intimal flap, and the thrombus. We explored four models: two convolutional networks, nnU-Net 2D and 3D, and two transformer-based architectures, TransUNet 2D and 3D. We observed that (1) for both nnU-Net and TransUNet, the 3D models outperformed their 2D counterparts on all three structures. The difference was small for the aortic lumen but large for the thin flap and the thrombus. The best model, nnU-Net 3D, reached a DSC of 93.05% for the lumen, 50.22% for the flap, and 69.94% for the thrombus. (2) The intimal flap was the most difficult structure for all models. Even the best 3D models showed large thrombus boundary errors in a few scans. These results provide a baseline for developing more advanced models for accurate segmentation of these structures in TBAD.

papers.title: Using Oyster Genomics to Understand Human Health
papers.abstract: As sessile filter feeders that experience continuous environmental exposure, oysters, particularly Crassostrea virginica, offer a unique opportunity to understand how environmental exposure alters the genome and influence health. Furthermore, oysters must be sorted by size for market value for premium size and taste. However, it requires intensive labor, specialized equipment (tumblers), and is susceptible to environmental risks like pollution. Therefore, it is desirable to produce uniform oysters without machines. However, limitations in the previous reference genome [2] have constrained our understanding of how genes are organized and maintained in oyster populations. To this end, we harvested 240 adult oysters in same location, 120 extremely large size and 120 extremely small, controlled with all confounding factors such as age and water temperature. We perform a genome wise associate study (GWAS) using next generation whole genome sequencing, aiming to discover genomic regions associated with oyster size. Using PacBio HiFi, Illumina, and Hi-C technologies, we generated a 99.7% complete chromosome-level genome assembly for C. virginica (NCBI RefSeq GCF_053477285.1) [75]. We identified a ~13 Mb region on chromosome 1 uniquely expanded in C. virginica and enriched for innate immune and stress-response genes. To evaluate whether these structural features are reflected at the population level, we then conducted a k-mer analysis. This revealed differential sequence patterns by size, including enrichment of bacterial DNA in smaller individuals and host variation at the RNF213 locus within this region. By highlighting genome structure as a mediator of immune resilience, this work supports the use of oysters as sentinels to advance out understanding of how the dynamic reassembly of the genome due to environmental exposures influence health in human populations.

papers.title: Population-level emulation enables fast Bayesian calibration of cardiac digital twins
papers.abstract: Purpose: Patient-specific cardiac digital twins have the potential to guide individualized therapy, but generating these in a routine clinical workflow remains challenging. This is especially true when the twins must carry quantified uncertainty: Bayesian calibration requires thousands of simulations per patient, and the emulators that reduce this cost are typically trained one patient at a time. We aimed to train a single emulator across a patient cohort, so that a new patient can be calibrated in minutes without new simulations. Methods: We trained a population-level Gaussian process emulator whose inputs included a 12-dimensional latent encoding of the clinical features of each patient, so that a single emulator represents the whole cohort. We compared spending simulation budgets on resampling the real cohort with augmenting the cohort with digital chimeras, synthetic patients interpolated between real patients. Seven parameters of a closed-loop heart and circulation model were calibrated by Markov chain Monte Carlo to ten clinical biomarkers in 26 patients with left bundle branch block, each using an emulator trained without that patient, and the calibrated posteriors were compared against the full simulator. Results: A single emulator, trained without the held-out patient, calibrated the digital twin of each patient in 59.7-63.0 s per patient, versus 15 h with the simulator. Resampling the real cohort was the more efficient training strategy, bringing every output to R2 greater than or equal to 0.9, which augmentation did not achieve for the same simulation budget. For held-out patients, both strategies performed comparably (median leave-one-out normalized root-mean-square error 11.0% vs. 10.7%; p = 0.745), and error rose with distance from the cohort centroid (Spearman rho = +0.406). The calibrated models showed no cohort-wide bias (median standardized residual -0.12 against the clinical targets), and 95% predictive intervals contained 78.5% of targets, with the largest misfit in systolic blood pressure. Conclusion: Removing the need for new simulations for every new patient is a meaningful step toward uncertainty-aware cardiac digital twins that fit within a routine clinical workflow. Because the simulator, surrogate and sampler are interchangeable, the approach used here can be applied to other (cardiac) models and cohorts.

papers.title: De novo design of ligases for programmable site-specific protein ubiquitylation
papers.abstract: Protein ubiquitylation regulates numerous cellular processes, but difficulties in generating site-specifically ubiquitylated proteins limit our understanding of individual modification events. In cells, ubiquitylation is mediated by an E1-E2-E3 enzyme cascade, with substrate recognition largely determined by more than 600 human E3 ligases, making it challenging to redirect ubiquitin transfer to a chosen lysine. Here we use RFdiffusion3 to design ubiquitin ligases from scratch that use a cysteine-based catalytic triad to conjugate an activated ubiquitin donor to a selected lysine in a chosen target substrate. Of 48 tested designs, 35 ubiquitylated a model peptide, with the most active ligases achieving near-quantitative ubiquitin transfer. We next challenged the approach with the homotrimeric sliding clamp proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA), whose ubiquitylation at lysine (K) 164 governs DNA damage tolerance while displaying 45 off-target lysines for ubiquitination. Screening of 48 designs delivered a site-selective ligase. Incorporation of a single activity-increasing substitution and coupling to E1-dependent donor activation resulted in 90% conversion from unactivated ubiquitin, delivering higher rates and superior selectivity compared to a natural promiscuous E2. Using this cascade, we transferred di-, tri- and tetraubiquitin chains of defined length to PCNA K164 through a native isopeptide bond. These results establish de novo enzyme design as a route towards programmable, site-specific protein ubiquitylation. That a single de novo designed protein can bind both an activated ubiquitin donor and a globular target, and use a proficient catalytic machinery to selectively transfer ubiquitin to one lysine among 45, illustrates the level of functional complexity now within reach of de novo enzyme design.

papers.title: Programmable amide bond formation using de novo ligases
papers.abstract: Amide bond formation is of central importance in the chemical industry, underpinning the synthesis of small bioactive molecules, macrocycles, peptides and their conjugates. Conventional methods of amide synthesis rely on stoichiometric coupling agents and costly protecting group manipulations. While biocatalysis can alleviate some of these challenges, enzymes typically operate across a narrow range of substrates and their adaptation to new coupling partners requires extensive engineering. Here we show that de novo amide ligases featuring a cysteine catalytic triad can be programmed computationally to operate across diverse substrate classes with high selectivity. We first designed complementary peptide ligases to selectively functionalise either the N-terminus or a single lysine residue of a polypeptide sequence containing 36 competing lysines. Crystal structures of both ligases show excellent agreement with the designs, with structural modelling suggesting that amidation outcompetes hydrolysis because the catalytically competent geometry forms only upon acceptor binding. We then extended our approach to the synthesis of small bioactive molecules by designing stereoselective ligases that mediate a key amide bonding forming step in the synthesis of the preventative HIV therapeutic lenacapavir. These results establish de novo enzyme design as a programmable platform for achieving selective amide bond formations across a wide range of molecular targets.

papers.title: Long-read analysis of complete human 5S rDNA arrays reveals a zoned organization with two-state unit methylation linked to chromatin architecture
papers.abstract: Despite the fundamental importance of the 5S ribosomal DNA (rDNA) to all cellular life, the landscape of its units by position along its array has remained poorly understood. Here, recent telomere-to-telomere long-read sequencing is used to resolve 5S rDNA arrays from flank to flank and to follow the state of each unit along single molecules. The array is zoned at both the sequence and the epigenetic level. Notably, methylation is bimodal at the level of the unit, and the combination of low-methylation and high-methylation units gives rise to the overall methylation pattern of the array. Moreover, the average number of low-methylation units remains relatively constant regardless of array length. Chromatin fiber sequencing (Fiber-seq) data further show that low-methylation units are more accessible, have lower nucleosome occupancy and are more frequently footprinted at the TFIIIB-binding site, consistent with analyses of ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq data from cell lines. Across species, this pattern is shared among apes, whereas other species show diverse patterns. These results provide a unit-resolved view of the human 5S rDNA array and reveal a zone-specific organization of unit methylation that is associated with chromatin architecture.

papers.title: Enhanced antitumour activity of combined PD-1 blockade and HER2-targeted therapy is associated with reduced epithelial-mesenchymal transition and extracellular matrix-remodelling signatures in gastric cancer
papers.abstract: Background The combination of PD-1 blockade, HER2-targeted therapy and chemotherapy improves outcomes in HER2-positive advanced gastric and gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma. However, chemotherapy can independently alter the tumour microenvironment, making the biological effects of PD-1 and HER2 targeting difficult to distinguish. We therefore investigated how PD-1 and HER2 blockade, alone and in combination, affect tumour growth and associated transcriptional programmes. Methods Immunodeficient NOG mice received human PBMCs by tail-vein injection. Three days later, NCI-N87 gastric cancer cells were implanted subcutaneously. Mice were randomised to vehicle, pembrolizumab, trastuzumab, or combination treatment. Tumour growth was assessed, and bulk RNA sequencing was used to identify treatment-associated changes in gene expression, pathway enrichment, and tumour, stromal, and immune cell-associated signatures. Results Combined treatment produced greater tumour growth control than either monotherapy. Trastuzumab-treated tumours showed enrichment of immune activation, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and TGF{beta}-associated signatures, whereas pembrolizumab alone produced a limited transcriptional effect. Combination treatment was associated with reduced proliferation, EMT, and stromal-remodelling signatures, alongside increased cytotoxic immune-associated signatures. Expression of extracellular matrix-associated genes, including VCAN, SPARC, POSTN, collagen genes, and FAP, was lower in combination-treated tumours. Complement-related transcriptional pathways were also enriched. Conclusions In this chemotherapy-free model, combined PD-1 blockade and HER2-targeted therapy was associated with greater tumour growth control, enrichment of cytotoxic immune-associated transcriptional signatures, and reduced EMT and extracellular matrix remodelling signatures. These findings provide hypotheses for further mechanistic validation.

papers.title: Curvature-based schedule ordering is preserved in homogeneous and heterogeneous tumors
papers.abstract: During treatment, dosing protocols with identical total dose may favor one schedule over another depending on how exposure is distributed over time. In homogeneous cell populations, Jensen's inequality has been shown to predict whether continuous or intermittent high-dose followed by low-dose is favored, based on the curvature of the concentration-effect function. Scheduling ordering can be performed based on curvature only: concave functions favor continuous dosing while convex functions favor intermittent dosing schedules with a high time-variance. However, tumors exhibit heterogeneous drug sensitivities, and treatment preferentially eliminates drug-sensitive cells, progressively shifting the surviving population toward greater drug resistance. Whether this treatment-induced selection can reverse curvature-based schedule ordering remains unclear. We develop a mathematical framework in which phenotypes share a common concentration-effect function but differ by fixed, nonnegative sensitivity scales. We prove that the ordering of equal-mean schedules is administrated solely by the scalar cumulative treatment effect, that is, by the curvature of the effect function alone. Consequently, baseline heterogeneity and treatment-induced selection can alter the magnitude of treatment response and the composition of surviving cells, but cannot reverse the ordering of equal-mean schedules predicted by the curvature of the single-cell concentration-effect function. This preservation holds across different temporal dosing profiles and repeated treatment cycles. Our work uncovers a general principle that curvature-based schedule ordering is preserved in heterogeneous tumors despite treatment-induced selection toward resistance.

papers.title: Single-Component Photo-Crosslinked Lipoic Acid Functionalized Mucin Hydrogels: Dynamic Mucus Mimetics for Antiviral Protection
papers.abstract: Native mucus protects epithelial surfaces through viscoelastic networks of disulfide-linked mucins. However, commercially available mucins often fail to reconstitute comparable mechanical and barrier properties, while synthetic and hybrid mucus mimetics require polymeric crosslinkers that may alter mucus-like composition. Inspired by the native architecture, we directly functionalized porcine gastric and bovine submaxillary mucins with -lipoic acid to develop a single-component, photo-crosslinkable hydrogels. Upon UV irradiation (365 nm), the modified mucins rapidly form disulfide-crosslinked networks without added photo-initiator/ polymeric crosslinkers, two orders of magnitude faster as compared with PEG-SH approaches. The resulting mucin-lipoic acid (MUC-LA) hydrogels exhibit mucus-relevant properties, including tunable viscoelasticity, redox responsiveness, self-healing, and size-dependent restrictions on nanoparticle transport. In transwell-based infection models, MUC-LA hydrogels (2-3%) mimicking the healthy airway mucus (G' {approx} 10-20 Pa) suppress epithelial infection by SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A virus. Crosslinked MUC-LA provides greater protection against SARS-CoV-2 than the non-crosslinked, whereas both formulations suppress influenza A infection, suggesting distinct contributions from network formation and mucin-associated interactions. These findings establish a dynamic, mucus-mimetic platform integrating rapid photo-gelation, controllable mechanics, selective transport, and antiviral barrier functionality. MUC-LA hydrogels offer opportunities to investigate mucosal transport and host-pathogen interactions, with potential applications in drug delivery, and as biomaterials.

papers.title: Advanced meditation stabilizes cortical dynamics through inhibitory gain control linked to absorptive depth
papers.abstract: Advanced meditation can shift conscious experience from ordinary body- and world-centered awareness toward absorption, detachment and dissociation-like states, yet the neural mechanisms that stabilize these immersive states remain unclear. We studied 18 long-term meditators during eyes-open rest and Rajyoga meditation, a practice in which practitioners reduce bodily identification while enhancing inner self-awareness. We combined multidimensional neural approach including frontal EEG spectral power, temporal non-stationarity and corticothalamic neural-field modeling, because these measures probe underlying complementary levels of the brain state transition: the strength of neural activity, its temporal stability, and the circuit level inhibition-excitation gain mechanisms. This framework is especially relevant to meditation because oscillatory, temporal organization may distinguish stable meditative states, and corticothalamic dynamics are closely linked to arousal and conscious state regulation. We correlated meditation induced neural changes with subjective ratings of absorption and dissociation. Compared with rest, meditation was associated with higher beta1, beta2 and gamma power, with no change in the slower bands (delta, theta and alpha), and with lower beta-band temporal non-stationarity, indicating a more stable expression of fast cortical dynamics. Fitting the corticothalamic model to the EEG spectra showed stronger cortical inhibitory gain and lower effective intracortical gain, placing meditation in an inhibition-dominant regime, with lower gain in the loop between excitatory and inhibitory neurons within the cortex. During meditation, these model estimates were related to subjective absorption and showed trend level links with dissociation. Together, these findings suggest that Rajyoga meditation stabilizes cortical dynamics through inhibitory gain control, linking absorption (deep and steady attention on the meditation) to dissociation-like self-detachment.

papers.title: Cxcr2 is required for ductal outgrowth and shapes the stromal microenvironment in postnatal mammary gland development
papers.abstract: Mammary gland development requires coordinated signaling between epithelial and stromal compartments. While CXC chemokine receptor 2 (CXCR2) is known to regulate inflammatory and tissue remodeling processes in disease, including breast cancer, its role in mammary gland morphogenesis is not well understood. Here, we examined postnatal mammary gland development in germline Cxcr2 knockout mice. Loss of Cxcr2 resulted in delayed ductal outgrowth, reduced epithelial area, and altered stromal architecture, including decreased adipocyte size and increased collagen deposition, despite preserved branching organization. These defects occurred in the context of severe systemic immune dysregulation, marked by expansion of granulocytic populations and loss of adaptive immune cells. Together, our findings indicate that CXCR2 indirectly regulates mammary gland development through coordination between the epithelium and stroma, rather than acting through epithelial cell-intrinsic mechanisms. Because the same myeloid expansion, immune suppression, and collagen-rich stromal remodeling that CXCR2 controls during normal development are hallmarks of the pro-tumorigenic breast microenvironment, these findings establish CXCR2 as a regulator of the immune and stromal landscape of the mammary gland and provide a developmental framework for understanding its contributions to the breast tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: BAF complexes cooperate with lineage-restricted transcription factors to establish cell-state-specific regulatory programs
papers.abstract: BRG1/BRM-associated factor (BAF) complexes are essential regulators of chromatin organization and cell identity. Genes encoding BAF subunits are among the most frequently mutated in human cancer. Yet, how disruption of a single subunit gives rise to distinct tumor states remains poorly understood. Atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumors (ATRTs) provide a compelling model, as they are uniformly driven by bi-allelic loss of the BAF subunit SMARCB1, yet segregate into distinct molecular subtypes. Using integrated multi-omics profiling of patient-derived ATRT organoids and primary tumor tissues, we show that transcriptional and chromatin accessibility changes upon SMARCB1 reconstitution are directed by subtype- and lineage-specific transcription factor (TF) repertoires. Genome-wide binding and transcriptomic analyses reveal that SMARCB1 reconstitution enables the lineage-specific TF RFX4 to engage regulatory elements and activate neuronal differentiation programs, partially reprogramming ATRT-MYC toward an ATRT-SHH-like identity. Together, these findings demonstrate that SMARCB1 loss disrupts TF-dependent chromatin priming, revealing that the lineage-specific regulatory output of BAF complexes is constrained by the underlying TF repertoire.

papers.title: A G-Quadruplex Containing First Intron Harbors a Functional Polyadenylation Signal in TP53
papers.abstract: First introns of mammalian genes are often longer than other introns and may contain regulatory elements, suggesting that they may have roles in gene regulation. We detected a previously unannotated, low abundance intronic transcript, TP53-INT1, using long-read direct RNA sequencing data. TP53-INT1 has low coding potential and terminates within the first and longest intron of TP53. The transcript structure and 3'-end were validated by independent experimental and in silico evidence. We identified a canonical polyadenylation signal upstream of the transcript termination site and demonstrated its functionality using reporter assays. Furthermore, a potential G-quadruplex (G4)-forming sequence was identified upstream of this polyadenylation signal. The G4-forming potential was confirmed using spectroscopic and thermal stability analyses. Complementing the in vitro characterizations, treatment with Pyridostatin, a G4-stabilizing drug, was associated with decreased TP53 expression. Together, these findings characterize a previously unannotated TP53 intronic transcript and reveal a local genomic context combining accessible chromatin, a functional polyadenylation signal, and a potential G4-forming sequence that may influence full-length transcription.

papers.title: Hyaluronic acid dynamics are regulated by neural crest cells and NEDD4 in the developing cardiac outflow tract valves
papers.abstract: The extracellular matrix (ECM) is essential for cardiac valve development, with hyaluronic acid (HA) playing a critical role in cardiac cushion formation. While HA is required for atrioventricular valve development, its role in semilunar valve formation remains poorly understood. The ubiquitin ligase NEDD4 is essential for cardiac outflow tract development, particularly within cardiac neural crest cells, however its role in semilunar valve development has been unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that neural crest-specific deletion of NEDD4 in mice disrupts outflow tract valve development, resulting in abnormal leaflet number and morphology. Analysis of valve ECM revealed a specific reduction in HA within the neural crest-derived valve mesenchyme, while other ECM components such as fibronectin and versican remained unaffected. In contrast, deletion of NEDD4 in endocardium-derived valve mesenchyme did not alter HA abundance. Using NEDD4-deficient neural crest cells, we further demonstrate a cell-autonomous requirement for NEDD4 in regulating HA abundance, with in vitro evidence supporting impaired HA synthesis rather than increased turnover of HA in the ECM. Our findings identify a previously unrecognised role for NEDD4 in regulating HA synthesis in cardiac neural crest cells, revealing a cell-type-specific mechanism governing semilunar valve development and highlighting distinct cellular requirements for ECM regulation across cardiac valve populations.

papers.title: Impacts of Environmental Nickel and Chromium Exposure on the Blood Proteome of House Sparrows (Passer domesticus) in New Caledonia
papers.abstract: New Caledonia holds some of the world's largest ultramafic mineral deposits, and nickel (Ni) smelting operations have created a gradient of Ni and chromium (Cr) contamination across the archipelago. Molecular impacts of Ni and Cr toxicity on wildlife remain largely unexplored. Here, we used the house sparrow (Passer domesticus) as a sentinel species to characterise the blood proteomic response to Ni and Cr exposure near the Doniambo smelter in Noumea. Blood was collected from 52 free-living sparrows across 18 sites classified by soil metal concentration. Plasma and blood cell pellet fractions were analysed by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Plasma proteomics identified histidine-rich glycoprotein (HRG) as the most prominent responder, with approximately 2.1-fold elevation in exposed relative to low-exposure birds. HRG contains a conserved histidine-rich region that binds cations including divalent nickel, and paired plasma-liver analysis confirmed hepatic-driven synthesis. Blood cell pellet proteomics revealed that Ni-Cr co-exposure predominantly disrupts the nuclear compartment: histone depletion indicated chromatin collapse, NUP153 dysregulation impaired nuclear pore function, and VRK1/TRIP13 upregulation suggested DNA damage response activation coupled with mitotic checkpoint override. Concurrent RNA processing collapse (DDX17, DHX15, RBMX, ALYREF) and changes in telomere-associated proteins (TERF2IP, hnRNPA1 and VRK1) implicated disrupted genome maintenance. These findings identify HRG as a candidate plasma biomarker of Ni-Cr exposure and reveal a coordinated nuclear toxicity signature linking heavy metal contamination to DNA damage and epigenetic disruption in a free-living vertebrate.

papers.title: Developmental regulator-mediated transcriptional reprogramming reveals novel regulators of somatic embryogenesis in sorghum
papers.abstract: Recalcitrance to genetic transformation remains a fundamental bottleneck in crop improvement, driven by genotype-specific barriers that include entrenched defense transcriptional states, limited embryogenic competence, and inadequate hormonal reprogramming potential. Here, we present a multi-layered transcriptomic analysis of somatic embryogenesis (SE) and regeneration in two sorghum genotypes (forage Tx2910 and grain Tx2783), two explant types (immature embryos and leaf bases), and three developmental regulator (DR) treatments (GRF-GIF, WUS, and BBM+WUS). This design lets us separate genotype, explant, and DR-specific regulatory programs. Using in-depth transcriptomics analysis (bulk RNAseq and single nucleus transcriptomics), we identified the molecular logic by which DRs override genotype-specific barriers and redirect somatic cells toward embryogenic and regeneration-competent states. Compared to Tx2910, the transformation-recalcitrant sorghum line Tx2783 shows a stronger defense response to both Agrobacterium infection plus culture stress and depends more heavily on DR-driven transcriptional reprogramming to exit this defense-locked state. WUS acts as an early, broad suppressor of defense and stress signaling while activating fate-specification programs, whereas GRF-GIF drives a delayed but pronounced transcriptional shift toward cell proliferation and morphogenesis. Integrative gene network analyses further identified a prioritized set of sorghum-specific transcription factors with potential to increase regeneration efficiency. Among the top candidates, we identified that SbEREB167 and SbEREB174 (AP2/EREBP family) efficiently induce SE and regeneration in sorghum. Collectively, this study establishes the transcriptional architecture underlying DR-mediated transformation across sorghum types and identifies novel regulators that hold potential to improve plant transformation across recalcitrant cereal species.

papers.title: Exploring subacute effects of a DMT and harmine meditation retreat on the brain's control energy landscape
papers.abstract: Modeling the brain as a controllable structural network allows the estimation of the control energy (CE) required to reach functional states, where low-CE states are more accessible. Psychedelics are thought to acutely flatten the brain's CE landscape, broadening the repertoire of reachable states, but whether this reorganization persists into the subacute ``afterglow" window is largely unknown. This exploratory study uses rs-fMRI from a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (N = 39; 19 verum [N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT) + harmine, Ayahuasca-inspired formulation], 20 placebo) scanned before and after a three-day meditation retreat. We compute CE on a group human connectome project (HCP) structural connectome under two approaches that emphasize long and short timescale dynamics. Globally, we found no systematic shift in the distribution of CE between transitions, however mean CE increased in both groups at the long timescale approach. Surviving network effects emerge when a network's intrinsic timescale matches the stabilization regime. In the long timescale regime, the central executive network (CEN) showed an increase in post-retreat CE within the verum group that survived Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR-BH) correction. Although CE and functional connectivity are distinct, this higher CEN cost may relate to the reduced within-network connectivity previously reported subacutely after psilocybin. The default mode network (DMN) also showed a post-retreat CE increase in both groups, but neither change survived FDR correction. In the short timescale approach, the visual network (VN) showed a FDR-BH CE decrease within the verum group, consistent with reduced dynamical demand in a region acutely engaged by DMT. To examine whether changes were concentrated in less accessible states, we additionally analyzed rare brain states, defined by the top decile of information content. This analysis revealed a modest session x condition interaction in the long timescale approach. Overall, the two timescale lenses surface different network effects, that align with cortical timescale hierarchies. These findings point to network- and timescale-specific, rather than global, CE changes in the afterglow window, though effects are small and heterogeneous and require confirmation in larger samples. Characterizing whether and where psychedelic effects persist into the subacute window is relevant to psychedelic-assisted therapy, including safety, therapeutic timing, and durability of drug effects. More broadly, considering cortical timescale hierarchies may help identify network-specific CE changes that might be less apparent when networks are evaluated under a single dynamical timescale.

papers.title: The MarR-family regulator TilR links biosynthesis of enterotoxin tilimycin with physiologic adaptation in Klebsiella oxytoca
papers.abstract: Members of the Klebsiella oxytoca species complex (KoSC) are ubiquitous gut colonizers that produce the DNA-damaging enterotoxin tilimycin (TM) as part of their virulence-related program. A MarR-like transcriptional regulator, herein designated TilR, controls expression of the divergently transcribed aroX- and NRPS-operons responsible for TM production. Deletion of tilR resulted in pronounced induction of both operons, elevated toxin production, and increased cytotoxicity - establishing TilR as the key repressor of TM biosynthesis. TilR is encoded downstream of the NRPS operon and binds a 20 bp motif within the aroX-NRPS intergenic region, spatially separated from the predicted promoters driving toxin gene expression. Analysis of global transcriptome profiles revealed that TilR, the most highly expressed of the seven MarRs in KoSC, links toxin biosynthesis to a broader transcriptional network involved in nutrient acquisition, stress adaptation, and central metabolism. In addition, TM production coincided with induction of multiple virulence-associated genes involved in adhesion, biofilm formation, and iron acquisition. Phylogenetic and structural analyses revealed that TilR is distinct from canonical MarRs and absent from members of the closely related, competing Klebsiella pneumoniae species complex (KpSC). These findings identify TilR as an evolutionarily specialized global regulator that coordinates TM biosynthesis with broader metabolic, stress-adaptive, and virulence-associated transcriptional responses.

papers.title: Serum extracellular vesicle proteomics reveals treatment-associated biomarkers in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
papers.abstract: Background Longitudinal biomarkers of treatment response in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) are needed. Extracellular vesicle (EV)-enriched serum proteomics may provide a minimally invasive approach for monitoring systemic and tumor-associated responses to therapy. Methods Paired pre-treatment and post-treatment serum samples were analyzed from 51 patients with pancreatic cancer, including 25 treated with FOLFIRINOX and 20 treated with gemcitabine-based therapy. EVs were enriched using the Mag-Net method and profiled by data independent acquisition mass spectrometry. After batch correction and filtering, 941 proteins were retained for differential and pathway analyses. Paired linear models and gene set enrichment analyses were used to assess treatment-associated changes. Baseline protein abundance and longitudinal changes were evaluated in relation to overall survival (OS) using Cox models. Results A total of 2,089 EV-associated proteins were identified, with an average of 1,186 proteins quantified per sample. Across the cohort, 26 proteins differed between post- and pretreatment samples. Proteins that increased after treatment were primarily related to extracellular matrix organization and cell adhesion, whereas proteins that decreased after treatment were associated with actin cytoskeletal organization, coagulation, and hemostasis. Treatment-associated changes were more pronounced in the FOLFIRINOX group, in which 32 proteins were differentially expressed. FOLFIRINOX was characterized by coordinated reductions in platelet- and coagulation-associated proteins, including PF4, PF4V1, PPBP, GP5, ITGA2B, and ITGB3, accompanied by enrichment of platelet activation, coagulation, and hemostasis pathways among down-regulated processes. No individual proteins met the same significance threshold in the gemcitabine group. A composite seven-protein platelet score decreased significantly after FOLFIRINOX but not for gemcitabine, and the between-regimen difference in score change was significant. Higher pretreatment ITGB1 abundance was associated with longer OS after multiple-testing correction (HR, 0.112; BH-FDR = 0.0063). In multivariable analysis, greater treatment-associated platelet-score depletion was independently associated with shorter OS (HR per unit increase in {Delta}score, 0.56; P = 0.030). Conclusions Longitudinal serum EV-enriched proteomics identified treatment-associated biological changes in PDAC, including a coordinated platelet-related response predominantly observed after FOLFIRINOX. Baseline ITGB1 abundance and longitudinal platelet-score changes represent potentially complementary prognostic and pharmacodynamic markers. These findings are exploratory and require validation in larger, independent cohorts incorporating platelet counts, coagulation measurements, and targeted proteomic assays.

papers.title: Illuminating duckweed: hyperspectral reflectance highlights a predictive ceiling for accurate determination of biomass
papers.abstract: Duckweed is a fast growing aquatic plant with strong potential as a sustainable, high protein crop that can be produced without expanding agricultural land. However, substantial trait variation necessitates rapid selection proxies to identify genotypes with high growth, biomass and pigment content while simultaneously suited to low input, controlled environments. Although hyperspectral reflectance phenotyping is widely applied in conventional crops, its utility for duckweed remains unexplored. We assessed 133 UK accessions from six species grown under ambient light, quantifying growth, pigment composition, photosynthetic performance and spectral reflectance. A second panel with contrasting light tolerance strategies, including growth and photosynthetic acclimation, was used to test whether hyperspectral reflectance could detect photoprotective mechanisms associated with high light resilience. Duckweed accessions displayed extensive variation across all traits. However, vegetation indices (VIs) commonly used in arable crops demonstrated only limited predictive accuracy for total chlorophyll (R2 =0.34, p<0.005) and maximum photosystem II (PSII) quantum yield (Fv/Fm) (R2 =0.25, p<0.0001), with poor performance for other traits. Under high light, VIs moderately differentiated tolerant accessions, including those maintaining higher Fv/Fm, {Phi}PSII operating efficiency and carotenoid:chlorophyll ratios. Partial least squares regression (PLSR) modelling improved predictive performance, providing reliable estimates of chlorophyll content (R2 =0.5, RMSE =2.05 mg/g freeze dry weight) maximum non-photochemical quenching (NPQ) (R2 =0.5, RMSE =0.57) and NPQ efficiency of PSII (R2 =0.53, RMSE =0.04). Although predictions of biomass and growth rate remained weak, green and red edge spectral regions were strongly associated with pigment contents and photosynthesis and indirectly linked to biomass. This study provides the first comprehensive evaluation of spectral phenotyping for duckweed crop development. Our findings indicate that broad spectrum modelling approaches, integrated with other high throughput phenotyping tools, may support selection of high vigour varieties and monitoring of commercial duckweed production systems.

papers.title: Population Genomics of the Bovine Sialic Acid Network Reveals Functional and Evolutionary Diversity Across European and South African Cattle Breeds
papers.abstract: **Background:** Sialic acids, mainly N-acetylneuraminic acid (Neu5Ac) and N-glycolylneuraminic acid (Neu5Gc), are terminal monosaccharides of glycans involved in numerous physiological processes, such as immune and neuronal function. Their biosynthesis, transport, transfer and turnover depend on a network of genes, but genetic studies in cattle have mostly addressed individual genes or genetic associations with milk oligosaccharide concentrations, leaving variation across this network largely uncharacterized. In bovine milk, sialylated glycans that depend on this network vary among animals and change rapidly during early lactation. We therefore characterized variation in 13 selected genes of the bovine sialic acid network using whole-genome sequence data from European and South African cattle. **Results:** We analyzed 346 animals from 12 European and 4 South African breeds. Of 9,724 variants in the 13 target genes, 8,675 were intronic and 62 were predicted to alter the amino acid sequence. Integration of SIFT predictions, Rate4Site conservation and protein context, with population representation as supporting evidence, identified 15 prioritized candidates, including 7 high-priority candidates in NEU3, ST8SIA2, ST8SIA4, CMAH and ST3GAL4. The most differentiated candidates were not among the 15 prioritized variants. NEU3 Y136H showed the largest regional contrast in allele frequency (0.83 in South African and 0.34 in European cattle), whereas several prioritized candidates were represented by a single allele in the South African cohort. Genome-wide principal component analysis of 950,219 linkage-disequilibrium-pruned SNPs separated South African from European cattle along the first component, which explained about 25% of the variance. None of the 220 analyzed common pathway SNPs exceeded the corresponding genome-wide differentiation thresholds at breed, country or regional level. Within the ascertained pathway SNPs, diversity was higher in South African breeds, and Tajima's D was shifted toward positive values in European breeds and centered near zero in South African breeds. **Conclusions:** This study provides a network-wide map of predicted protein-altering variation in the bovine sialic acid pathway and identifies 15 candidates for functional investigation, most of them rare. Because the most differentiated variants were not those with the strongest functional support, population contrasts, evolutionary conservation and protein context provide complementary evidence for selecting candidates. The analyzed common pathway SNPs did not show exceptional differentiation relative to the genome-wide background. The candidates provide specific targets for genotyping, enzyme-level testing and genotype-informed milk phenotyping.

papers.title: The Src family kinases Lck and Fyn promote transendothelial migration of T cells
papers.abstract: The ability of T cells to cross endothelial barriers and migrate into and within peripheral tissue is crucial for adaptive immunity. Integrins such as LFA-1 play an essential role in this process by acting as adhesion molecules and initiating signaling events that drive the cytoskeletal changes needed for cell migration, however, many of the specific signaling events that promote T cell migration are still unknown. Here, we found that the Src family kinases Lck and Fyn are needed for efficient T cell migration. Primary T cells lacking Lck, Fyn, or both kinases exhibited defects in random migration on ICAM-1 coated surfaces for parameters such as speed and mean squared displacement. Analysis of signaling revealed that Lck was required for PI3K signaling downstream of LFA-1, while Fyn was not. Mechanistically, we found that the absence of Lck disrupted the normal interaction of the PI3K regulatory subunit p85 with tyrosine-phosphorylated binding partners, suggesting that Lck may regulate PI3K activity by controlling p85 protein-protein interactions. Importantly, both Lck and Fyn were required for efficient T cell transmigration across an inflamed endothelial barrier, a critical event for tissue infiltration. Lastly, a small-molecule Lck kinase inhibitor also decreased PI3K signaling and T cell transmigration, indicating the kinase activity of Lck is needed. Together, these data identify a new role for Lck and Fyn in promoting T cell transmigration.

papers.title: Genome-wide diversity across 130 years reveals drastic post-bottleneck genetic erosion in a recovering population of golden eagles (Aquila chrysaetos)
papers.abstract: Many wild populations have experienced severe human-induced declines, but the genetic consequences of such bottlenecks are often poorly understood. In Finland, as well as in many other countries, golden eagles were heavily persecuted during the 19th-20th centuries, disappearing from southern regions and reaching their lowest population size in the 1950-1960s. Although conservation efforts facilitated demographic recovery, the long-term genomic consequences of the bottleneck remained unknown. Here, we used whole-genome sequencing data spanning 136 years to evaluate patterns of genetic diversity in 26 Finnish golden eagles before, during, and after the mid-20th century bottleneck. We found substantial loss of genetic variation, including an 82% reduction in genome-wide heterozygosity, a 42% decline in nucleotide diversity, a 67% reduction in Watterson's theta, and a substantial loss of variable sites. Analyses of the site frequency spectrum and Tajima's D confirmed historical population contraction, and runs of homozygosity analysis indicated elevated post-bottleneck inbreeding. These results indicate strong genetic erosion in Finnish golden eagles despite the census size recovery. Therefore, incorporating genomic indicators in conservation monitoring and performing regional assessments are necessary to guide management and preserve biodiversity in line with the Global Biodiversity Framework's goal of maintaining genetic variation.

papers.title: Multimodal imaging links molecular identity with nanoscale-resolved 3D cell morphology in opossum cortical cultures
papers.abstract: In the mammalian central nervous system (CNS), the ability to regenerate after injury drops sharply in the first weeks after birth, but how this change is reflected in cell morphology and organization is still not fully understood. Here we cultivated cortical cell cultures from the gray short-tailed opossum (Monodelphis domestica) and compared cells derived from early postnatal pups (postnatal day 3-6, "Pyoung") with those from older pups (postnatal day 16-18, "Pold"), which differ in their capacity to regenerate after injury. For each culture, we assessed marker-defined cellular composition using fluorescently labeled markers for neurons, glia, and immature/progenitor cells, and characterized their nanoscale-resolved three-dimensional morphology using label-free scanning ion conductance microscopy (SICM). Pyoung cultures exhibited active change in shape over time, contained a higher proportion of immature SOX2 cells, and grew more neurites (TUJ1) into the lesion site after injury.
