Moreover, Pold cultures showed more stable soma size (e.g., thickness, area, volume), a larger astroglial (SOX9) population early in culture, and a glia-dominated lesion response. These early astroglia included more immature or reactive (vimentin) astrocytes. SICM further revealed cellular bridges across the lesion, ridges left in the substrate by the injury, and aligned neurite outgrowth. Across all measurements, changes in molecular markers were associated with corresponding changes in cell morphology. This multimodal combination of fluorescence labeling and SICM therefore relates marker-defined cellular composition to physical organization across micro- and nanoscale features during and after postnatal in vitro development.

papers.title: Drought Response and Recovery in Wild, Feral, and Domesticated Brassica rapa: Implications for Crop Climate Resilience
papers.abstract: Drought poses a serious threat to agricultural production and food security. Wild relatives of crops, including pre-domesticated and feral varieties, contain genetic diversity that can serve as a breeding resource for increasing desirable crop traits such as drought resilience, but little is known about the relative ability of wild varieties to cope with climate change in most species. In this study, we investigated the drought response of wild, feral, and domesticated varieties of Brassica rapa, an important crop and model species. Twenty-five accessions were subjected to experimental drought and recovery, and variation in traits such as biomass retention, photosynthetic rate, and water use efficiency were quantified. We found several wild accessions of B. rapa had high biomass retention under drought and full recovery of maximum assimilation rate after rewatering, challenging the assumption that feralization produces stress-resilient phenotypes and suggesting that populations of wild crop progenitors are especially promising reservoirs of drought-response diversity. Our results also showed taproot biomass was positively associated with water use efficiency. Our findings provide candidate traits and genotypes for agricultural breeding aimed at increasing drought resilience in domesticated B. rapa cultivars and give insights into evolution under domestication and feralization in the context of climate change.

papers.title: Evolution of herbicide resistance through co-option of an ethylene-associated nitrilase
papers.abstract: Adaptive evolution frequently proceeds through the co-option of pre-existing biological functions, yet the molecular mechanisms by which such co-option generates new adaptive traits over contemporary evolutionary timescales remain poorly understood. Herbicide-resistant weeds provide a powerful model for addressing this question because enhanced herbicide metabolism has repeatedly evolved within only a few decades. Here, we show that resistance to cyhalofop-butyl in Echinochloa crus-galli evolved through the co-option of EcNIT4A2, which encodes a nitrilase that normally functions in ethylene-associated cyanide detoxification. Genetic mapping, transcriptomics and transgenic analyses identified EcNIT4A2 as the major determinant of resistance. A D317G substitution enhanced its herbicide-detoxifying activity. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated that this substitution facilitates substrate access to the catalytic pocket. A promoter structural variant markedly increased EcNIT4A2 expression. Our findings reveal how coding and regulatory changes can jointly drive the co-option and optimization of a conserved metabolic function during rapid adaptation under intense anthropogenic selection.

papers.title: The Phospholipase A2 Activity of Peroxiredoxin 6 Protects Hepatocarcinoma Cells Against Ferroptosis and Mitophagy Impairment
papers.abstract: Peroxiredoxin 6 (PRDX6) is a moonlighting protein that plays a key role in regulating redox homeostasis and lipid metabolism through its unique dual peroxidase and calcium-independent phospholipase A2 (iPLA2) activities. Here, we generated a stable HepG2 cell line harboring a D140A mutation to selectively ablate iPLA2 activity, and we compared its phenotype with that of wild-type (WT) and PRDX6-knockout (KO) cells. D140A exhibited low ROS leves, similar to WT cells, confirming that oxidative stress is due to peroxidase deficiency. In contrast, D140A cells displayed higher lipid peroxidation than WT cells, though significantly lower than that of KO cells. Furthermore, the D140A mutant mirrored the KO phenotype regarding intracellular ferrous iron accumulation, impaired lipid droplet biogenesis, and the downregulation of the key ferroptosis regulator GPX4. Mechanistically, integrated proteomic, lipidomic, and enzymatic analyses revealed that a deficiency in iPLA2 activity of PRDX6 disrupted the release of key lipid species necessary for cell structure and signaling. Consequently, organelles involved in lipid synthesis and trafficking, such as peroxisomes, endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondria and lipid droplet, were affected. Specifically, we found that mitochondria exhibited a reduction in cristae and a diminished capacity for mitophagy and autophagy, which ultimately makes cells much more susceptible to erastin-induced ferroptotic cell death. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that PRDX6 iPLA2 activity uniquely coordinates organelle lipid homeostasis and mitophagy to protect cancer cells from ferroptotic cell death. Consequently, the use of iPLA2 inhibitors such as MJ33, which decreased PRDX6 iPLA2 activity to a level comparable to the mutant D140A, could represent a promising therapeutic strategy for inducing ferroptotic cell death in hepatocellular carcinoma.

papers.title: Bacterial major vault protein homologs form divergent vault structures
papers.abstract: Vaults are large, enigmatic macromolecular protein complexes composed of symmetrically arranged major vault protein (MVP) subunits with a wide variety of proposed functions. While MVP is conserved in most eukaryotes, its prevalence in other domains of life has not been well studied. Furthermore, whether bacterial MVP homologs assemble into vaults remains unknown. Here, we identify and examine a subset of bacterial MVP homologs and report cryoEM structures of an intact vault from Corallococcus praedator and a half-vault from a Deltaproteobacteria bacterium. Both bacterial vault complexes exhibit architectures unlike any other previously characterized vault with barrel/cap symmetries of D35/C13 and C48/C16, respectively. These data demonstrate that bacterial MVP homologs can assemble into vault structures and highlight the structural diversity of vaults across domains of life.

papers.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Translatomic Profiling Reveals Noncanonical RNA Junctions and Hidden Coding Potential in Porcine Epidemic Diarrhea Virus
papers.abstract: Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) poses a major threat to the global swine industry. Although coronavirus discontinuous transcription is well characterized, the classical model cannot fully explain the diversity of viral RNA junctions, while conventional genome annotations may underestimate viral protein-coding capacity. To address these gaps, we integrated time-resolved RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), cycloheximide (CHX)- and harringtonine (HAR)-treated ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq), comparative genomics, and peptide mass spectrometry to investigate PEDV RNA expression and hidden coding potential. RNA-seq revealed that, at 3 hours post-infection (hpi), the 3 genomic region exhibited strong relative coverage enrichment, whereas the relative contribution of the 5 replicase-coding region increased rapidly between 3 and 5 hpi, suggesting a possible transition from sgRNA-dominated RNA accumulation toward enhanced genomic RNA replication. Genome-wide junction analysis identified 43,635 distinct noncanonical RNA junctions, although canonical sgRNA junctions accounted for 95.5% of all junction-supporting reads. Several abundant noncanonical sgRNAs were predicted to generate novel coding products, including N-x4, N-x2, M-x3, and M-x2, short peptides encoded within the 3 untranslated region (UTR), and two distinct N-terminally truncated S proteins, thereby expanding the potential coding repertoire of PEDV. Genome-wide reading-frame analysis uncovered a pronounced asymmetry in hidden coding potential, identifying 68 overlapping open reading frames (ORFs) longer than 40 amino acids in the +1 reading frame, compared with only three in the +2 frame. Ribo-seq further revealed a progressive redistribution of viral ribosome occupancy toward structural protein-coding regions during the later stages of infection. By integrating HAR-associated translation initiation-site enrichment with CHX-based ORF-level translation analysis, we identified several noncanonical ORFs with strong translation-associated evidence, including N-x1, N-x2, S-x1, and ORF1b-x13. Moreover, peptide mass spectrometry detected a characteristic peptide corresponding to N-x1 in infected samples, providing independent proteomic evidence for the expression of this previously unannotated viral protein. Together, these findings uncover extensive noncanonical RNA synthesis and hidden protein-coding capacity in PEDV, establishing a foundation for understanding novel viral gene expression strategies and their potential evolutionary and pathogenic significance.

papers.title: Signals beneath the ectoderm: Mesodermal FGF signaling keeps the dorsally closing epithelium in shape
papers.abstract: Morphogenesis requires coordinated biochemical signaling, actomyosin contractility and dynamic adhesion within and between tissues. During Drosophila development, ectodermal fibroblast growth factor (FGF) ligands regulate mesoderm morphogenesis through the FGF receptor (FGFR) Heartless. We find that the mesoderm reciprocally influences ectodermal morphogenesis. We show that loss of the FGF ligands Pyramus or Thisbe, Heartless, or its adaptor Stumps transforms normally straight dorsal seams and the formed dorsal epidermis into highly distorted, dynamically changing zigzags during dorsal closure. In these mutants, mesoderm is specified but defective. Mesodermal expression of Heartless restores epithelial stability in heartless mutants, whereas ectodermal expression does not. Genetic ablation of mesoderm produces more extensive seam distortions that persist beyond the end of closure, thereby displacing the dorsal midline. Despite these striking deformations, closure continues to completion. Together, our findings reveal a non-cell-autonomous requirement for mesodermal FGFR signaling in stabilizing the closing ectoderm and its newly formed seams. They identify a reciprocal influence of mesoderm on the ectoderm that patterns it and show that stable tissue geometry can be uncoupled from successful completion of a morphogenetic movement.

papers.title: Systematic comparison of gliflozins identifies a selective anti-calcifying effect of canagliflozin beyond canonical SGLT2 inhibition
papers.abstract: Background: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) provide important cardiorenal benefits in chronic kidney disease (CKD), but their effects on vascular calcification remain conflicting. Whether potential anti-calcifying effects are shared across gliflozins or involve mechanisms beyond canonical SGLT2 inhibition is unknown. Methods: We systematically compared canagliflozin, dapagliflozin and empagliflozin in a high-phosphate diet-induced mouse model of vascular calcification and complementary ex vivo and in vitro models, including rodent and human vascular tissues and vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). Aortic transcriptional response was investigated by RNA sequencing. VSMC calcification, proliferation, migration, viability, glucose uptake and bioenergetics were investigated using complementary cellular assays, including OsteoSense staining, Annexin V/propidium iodide staining, radiolabeled 2-deoxyglucose uptake and Seahorse ATP rate analysis. SGLT2/1 expression was examined by RT-qPCR, Western blotting and immunofluorescence. We also evaluated sotagliflozin, a dual SGLT1/2 inhibitor, and mizagliflozin, a selective SGLT1 inhibitor. Results: Among the three gliflozins, only canagliflozin significantly reduced aortic calcification in vivo. Its anti-calcifying effect was also observed in rodent aortic rings, human vascular explants, cultured VSMCs and aortic rings from diabetic db/db mice. Aortic RNA-seq revealed that canagliflozin partially reversed HPD-induced transcriptional alterations, including changes in pro-calcific signaling and cellular metabolism, while some endothelial and inflammatory responses were shared among gliflozins. In mouse VSMCs, canagliflozin reduced calcification across all tested concentrations, dose-dependently decreased osteogenic marker expression, and reduced proliferation and migration. Increased apoptotic and damaged cell fractions were observed at higher concentrations, but not at lower concentrations. Canagliflozin also reduced glucose uptake and mitochondrial ATP production, without significantly affecting glycolytic ATP production. Neither dapagliflozin nor empagliflozin reproduced these cellular and metabolic effects at any of the concentrations tested. SGLT2 and SGLT1 expression was low or undetectable in vascular tissues and cells, and neither sotagliflozin nor mizagliflozin reproduced the anti-calcifying effect of canagliflozin in vivo or in vitro. Conclusions: Canagliflozin exhibits a selective anti-calcifying profile among the gliflozins tested, associated with changes in VSMC responses and cellular metabolism. These findings suggest that its vascular protective effects may involve mechanisms beyond canonical SGLT2 inhibition.

papers.title: Microbially conjugated bile acids differentially affect the lifecycle and pathogenesis of Clostridioides difficile
papers.abstract: Clostridioides difficile is a Gram-positive bacterium that causes C. difficile infection (CDI). In healthy adults, it has been proposed that the gut microbiota provides colonization resistance against C. difficile by competition through nutrient limitation and antagonism through secondary bile acid metabolism, the latter of which is mediated by the deconjugation of host-derived bile acids with bacterial bile salt hydrolases (BSH). Recently, BSHs have also shown an ability to reconjugate non-canonical (i.e., not glycine or taurine) amino acids to sterol cores, resulting in novel microbially conjugated bile acids (MCBAs). MCBAs have been associated with the resolution of recurrent CDI, though the mechanism underlying these effects are not well understood. To address this gap, we synthesized 36 MCBAs with nine amino acids (cysteine, isoleucine, leucine, phenylalanine, proline, serine, tryptophan, tyrosine, and valine) conjugated to the primary and secondary bile acids found in the human gut (CA, DCA, CDCA, and LCA) and tested their impact on various stages of C. difficiles lifecycle including bacterial outgrowth, membrane integrity, sporulation, and toxin activity. We show that BSH-mediated amidation of bile acid sterol cores can either increase or decrease inhibitory effects on C. difficile in an amino acid-dependent manner. For example, serine MCBAs enhanced C. difficiles ability to grow in otherwise inhibitory bile acid concentrations, increased spore production, and elevated toxin activity. Tryptophan MCBAs increased inhibition. By demonstrating these variable effects, our work clarifies the molecular determinants of MCBA activity and highlights specific MCBAs as promising targets for the development of C. difficile microbial-based therapeutics.

papers.title: Molecular and phytochemical investigation of medicinal Rhododendron spp. in the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau: the botanical sources of the traditional Tibetan medicine "Tale"
papers.abstract: The Qinghai-Xizang Plateau in China is a hotspot for Rhododendron species, with approximately 400 species distributed across the region. Various Rhododendron species in this area have been used medicinally in traditional Tibetan medicine for a long time and are collectively referred to as "Tale." Furthermore, "Tale" is classified as "Talegabao" or "Talenabao," depending on the species. These two types of medicine have similar but distinct properties, and "Talenabao" is usually used as an alternative to "Talegabao." However, differences in their phytochemical compositions and methods for discriminating between them have not been examined. To solve these problems limited the use of "Tale" medicines, 46 plant specimens belonging to nine Rhododendron species were collected from the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau. Molecular methods based on the internal transcribed spacer 2 (ITS2) region of nuclear DNA and psbA-trnH regions of chloroplast DNA were applied to these samples. In addition, 10 flavonoid compounds were quantitatively determined by HPLC. The results indicated psbA-trnH region successfully distinguished the species used as "Talegabao" or "Talenabao," whereas ITS2 failed to distinguish them because of its high degree of conservation. All 10 compounds were detected in all samples. However, the species used as "Talegabao" had more than twice the total content of the 10 flavonoid compounds observed in the species used as "Talenabao." Moreover, differences in the contents of certain compounds among species were detected, indicating potential chemical markers for the quality evaluation of "Tale" medicines. "Talegabao" is the first choice among "Tale" medicines. "Talenabao" can be used as an alternative to "Talegabao"; however, the appropriate dose requires further discussion in practical use. The psbA-trnH region is recommended as a DNA barcode for distinguishing between these two types of medicines.

papers.title: Higher stomatal density and smaller stomatal size associate with higher grain yield in winter wheat
papers.abstract: In wheat (Triticum aestivum L.), flag leaf is crucial in determining grain-filling rate and final grain yield. Stomata, microscopic pores on plant surfaces, balance CO2 uptake and evaporative water loss; their numbers and aperture sizes depend on environmental factors. Previous studies have reported associations between stomatal traits and grain yield; mostly under controlled conditions. Our study aimed to investigate flag leaf stomatal anatomical and physiological traits, and their relationships with winter wheat grain yield under field conditions. We measured stomatal density and size, and stomatal conductance on adaxial and abaxial flag leaf surfaces in a three-year field study with twenty-five winter wheat varieties. Stomatal density ratio remained constant despite different stomatal densities occurring in different years, indicating coordinated adjustments of stomatal numbers between leaf surfaces in response to environmental conditions. Stomatal conductance ratios varied widely, indicating leaf-surface specific stomatal responses to environmental conditions. Grain yield was positively associated with stomatal density and negatively with stomatal size. Flag leaf removal reduced grain weight per spike and did not affect grain numbers per spike, unlike in spring wheat. Our field study provides valuable insights into the relationships between winter wheat stomatal traits and grain yield that can be used in breeding.

papers.title: Highly prevalent cargo genes of F plasmids harbored in pathogenic Escherichia coli
papers.abstract: Analysis of prevalent orthogroups (OGs) in a collection of F plasmids from extraintestinal Escherichia coli ST131 isolates has led to the identification of two groups of previously uncharacterized cargo genes that may be widely distributed among F plasmids of pathogenic E. coli. Group 1 comprises four OGs whose encoded proteins are predicted to be involved in transport-related functions. The corresponding genes cluster with other genes associated with metabolism and are highly prevalent in extraintestinal ST131 isolates. Group 2 comprises several OGs whose encoded proteins currently have unknown functions. These OGs are present in a large proportion of F plasmids from both intestinal and extraintestinal E. coli isolates. The corresponding genes cluster within an F-plasmid region that also contains genes involved in DNA metabolism, suggesting that the proteins encoded by these newly identified OGs may likewise contribute to F-plasmid DNA biology. Characterizing the functions of these newly identified proteins may improve our understanding of the contribution of F plasmid to E. coli virulence and reveal novel targets for antimicrobial intervention, either by limiting F-plasmid dissemination among multidrug-resistant (MDR) E. coli strains or by directly targeting plasmid-carrying bacteria.

papers.title: Sex differences in cell type-specific transcriptional programs and GPCR signaling in the human subgenual anterior cingulate cortex
papers.abstract: Psychiatric conditions show marked sex differences in disease onset, symptom presentation, and response to treatments. Understanding how sex differences manifest across molecularly distinct neuronal populations in individuals without psychiatric conditions may help explain sex-dependent variation in neural circuit function and treatment response. Here, we examined molecularly distinct cell types within the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex (sgACC) of non-psychiatric subjects. Using RNA sequencing data previously generated from laser-capture microdissected neurons, we investigated sex differences in gene expression and co-expression networks in excitatory pyramidal neurons (layers 2/3 and 5/6) and somatostatin (SST)-, parvalbumin (PVALB)-, and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP)-expressing inhibitory interneurons (N=10 males, 9 females). We identified sex differences in transcriptomic profiles, biological pathways, and co-expression network connectivity. PVALB cells showed stronger overall female transcriptional enrichment, while SST cells exhibited male-enriched transcriptional signatures. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified PVALB and SST modules more connected in males and females, respectively, which included hub genes involved in immune, extracellular matrix, and bioenergetic processes. Since G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are viable therapeutic targets, we examined sex differences in GPCR transcripts. Across all GPCR-cell-type combinations, CHRM2 in PVALB cells showed the second strongest sex difference (enriched in females). To test the functional relevance of this difference, we used patch-clamp electrophysiology in mouse prefrontal cortex. M2 receptor activation increased maximal firing rates in PVALB cells from female but not male mice. Collectively, our findings demonstrate cell type-specific sex differences in the sgACC corresponding to functional differences in neuromodulator signaling, with potential implications for treatment response.

papers.title: Perturbation-induced gene programs map the hidden regulatory architecture of complex diseases
papers.abstract: Steady-state molecular profiles incompletely capture the regulatory programs through which genetic variation influences complex disease, particularly programs that emerge only when cells are perturbed. Here, we introduce Perturbscape, a computational framework that learns multiscale gene programs for individual perturbations in a CRISPR Perturb-seq screen using linear and nonlinear contrastive approaches alongside complementary program-learning methods, and integrates them with human genetics to prioritize disease-relevant genes, perturbations and downstream regulatory pathways. Across 15,859 perturbation-by-context profiles from 7 Perturb-seq systems and 53 complex diseases and traits (mean GWAS N=291K), perturbation-induced programs showed up to 4.3-fold higher heritability informativeness than analogous steady-state multi-tissue gene prioritization, and retained significant conditional heritability informativeness across all 34 matched cell system-trait comparisons after accounting for steady-state prioritization. Preserving perturbation-specific programs further yielded 2.5-5.3-fold higher trait relevance scores than programs derived from control cells, pooled perturbations or differential-expression summaries. In K562, Perturbscape-prioritized genes showed stronger enrichment for rare-variant burden genes than steady-state prioritization and were supported by orthogonal enhancer CRISPRi screens. In HepG2, LDL cholesterol-associated perturbation-induced programs specifically revealed statin-responsive pathways not significantly enriched by steady-state PoPS prioritization, supported by pharmacological transcriptional responses and population plasma proteomics. Perturbscape also recovered blood-related trait-conditioned trans-regulatory relationships that were specifically supported by population trans-eQTLs in IFN-gamma-stimulated monocytes (OR = 1.30, P=1.6e-05). Perturbscape further revealed developmental-stage-specific convergence between monogenic diabetes regulators and polygenic T2D risk during pancreatic islet differentiation, and neuronal-subclass-specific autism-associated regulatory programs in vivo. Together, these findings establish perturbation-induced gene programs as a complementary layer of disease-relevant regulatory information, revealing genetically informative pathways and context-specific regulatory relationships incompletely represented by steady-state molecular atlases.

papers.title: Comparative functional genomics reveals distributed SERPINE1 like characteristics among Drosophila serpins
papers.abstract: Serpins (serine protease inhibitors) regulate proteolytic activity through a suicide-substrate inhibitory mechanism, whereby the serpin covalently traps and inactivates their target protease. Serpins are broadly conserved across eukaryotes, but the evolutionary and functional relationships between human SERPINE1, and Drosophila Serpins in incompletely defined. To identify candidate Drosophila functional analogs of SERPINE1/PAI-1, a multi-omics framework was applied to thoroughly compare the serpins across species. The multi-level analysis integrated orthology prediction, protein sequence and structural characterization, phylogenetic reconstruction, bulk tissue transcriptomics, single-cell transcriptomics, and aging-associated expression analysis. Candidate serpins (Spn42Da, Spn42Db, Spn42Dc, Spn42Dd, Spn28B, and Spn28F) were evaluated using DIOPT, AlphaFold/ChimeraX structural comparisons, reactive center loop analyses, phylogenetic distances, GTEx, Human Protein Atlas, FlyAtlas2, Fly Cell Atlas, and Aging Fly Cell Atlas datasets. Comparative analyses demonstrated full-length sequence and reactive center loop (RCL) divergence despite preservation of the canonical serpin fold. Tissue, cell-type, and age-associated expression analysis revealed distinct candidate-specific patterns. Spn42Dd comparisons uncovered similarities to human SERPINE1 in sequence/structural and broad expression but did not represent the strongest overall cross-species expression correlations. Spn42Da and Spn42Db received the highest cross species integrated support. Quality check of the ranking confirmed that Spn42Da and Spn42Db were stable top candidates across orthology, sequence alignment, and expression domains. The multi-domain analysis was unable to identify a single definitive Drosophila serpin as the closest counterpart to human SERPINE1, indicating that cross-species similarity is distributed across multiple candidate serpins. This study therefore provides a quantitative method for prioritizing potential evolutionary and functional analogs across highly divergent species.

papers.title: The Reasoning Paradox in Scientific Sandboxes: Why Extended Reasoning Fails in Autonomous Bioinformatics and How to Fix It.
papers.abstract: Frontier large language models (LLMs) trained with extended reasoning, such as DeepSeek-R1 and OpenAI o1, have established state-of-the-art benchmarks in formal logic, competitive programming, and mathematics. In interactive, empirical scientific sandboxes, however, their efficacy remains counter-intuitive. In the Bioinformatics Benchmark (BixBench), extended reasoning models paradoxically degraded in multi-turn environments, leading benchmark authors to exclude them from primary agentic evaluations. In this paper, we conduct the first systematic forensic audit of the internal cognitive monologue (<think> ... </think>) of open-weight reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B) and matched instruction-tuned controls (Qwen2.5-Coder-14B) deployed inside containerized computational biology sandboxes on Nvidia H100 GPUs. Our forensic analysis uncovers two distinct systemic failure modes: (1) The PubMed Prior Trap, in which reasoning models engage in epistemic rationalization within their cognitive stream, falsely convincing themselves that empirical datasets are missing and substituting empirical computation with speculative literature recall (e.g., estimating adjusted p-values based on "typical experimental outcomes"); and (2) Tag Language Nesting Collisions, in which models conflate agent-level XML action tags with Python syntax, producing terminal interpreter syntax errors. To resolve this paradox, we introduce Dual Track Decoupled Reasoning (DTDR), an agent scaffolding architecture that evicts internal cognitive monologues from multi-turn history, injects strict empirical grounding guardrails, and dynamically intercepts runtime tool invocations. On a stratified diagnostic benchmark spanning single-cell RNA-seq, bulk differential expression (DESeq2), and genomic variant prioritization (n=22 per arm), DTDR rescues the 14B reasoning model from 0.0% to 9.09% accuracy (2/22), doubling the performance of the matched non-reasoning coder control (4.55%, 1/22) while slashing code execution errors by 81% (13.6% vs. 72.7%) and reducing average steps to solution by 66% (1.77 vs. 5.18 steps). All replication pipelines, prompts, and trajectory manifests are openly released.

papers.title: Hic sunt dracones: ancient DNA from the extinct palaeofauna of the tiny Mediterranean archipelago of Columbretes and its implications for human visitation
papers.abstract: The Columbretes archipelago in the Mediterranean is an example of deep isolation and sporadic human interaction during the Holocene. We recovered ancient DNA from 2,600-year-old microfauna and historical museum specimens to investigate the island's extinct fauna. Despite challenging preservation conditions, we successfully recovered mitogenomes from historical Vipera latastei specimens, and partial mitogenomes from snake, skink, and lizard subfossils. Phylogenetic analyses confirm the extinct Columbretes snake as Vipera latastei, sharing a haplotype with the historical specimen and clustering with modern populations from northeastern Iberia, validating its provenance and suggesting a single mitochondrial lineage since isolation. The extinct skink, Chalcides bedriagai, also shows affinities with eastern Iberia. These results point to a vicariant origin for the herpetofauna, likely isolated on the island following sea level rise after the Last Glacial Maximum. Conversely, a 2,600-year-old mouse incisor yielded a Mus musculus mitogenome, indicating Iron Age human-mediated introduction. Additionally, genomic analysis of a 11th-century CE human burial revealed an individual with genetic affinities to the Central Mediterranean and Balkans, highlighting medieval maritime mobility. This study resolves the long-debated Columbretes snake identity, traces biogeographic origins and illustrates the interplay of natural isolation and anthropogenic influence on the island biodiversity.

papers.title: Neural transformation from image realism to perceived realness
papers.abstract: Humans readily perceive whether a visual stimulus depicts something that could exist in the real world, yet the neural basis of perceived realness remains unclear. Because differences between real and unreal stimuli are ultimately expressed through visual features, realness might be expected to emerge along the ventral visual stream. Contrary to this prediction, we show that perceived-realness representations emerge in higher dorsal visual areas through a transformation of image-realism-related image-feature representations in early visual and early dorsal visual areas. fMRI revealed this representational shift toward intraparietal sulcus (IPS), with IPS patterns predicting perceived realness beyond image features and decision difficulty; source-localized MEG showed that realness coding in IPS peaked later than feature coding in early visual and dorsal visual areas. Together, these findings reveal a transformation from visual features to perceived realness along the dorsal visual stream. This representation may help guide subsequent actions and interactions with the real world.

papers.title: A Double Challenge: Cerebral Blood Flow During Concurrent Breath-Hold and Motor Task
papers.abstract: Motor activation and breath-holding probe complementary aspects of cerebrovascular function: the response to local neuronal demand and to a global vascular challenge. Combining them tests whether local perfusion responses remain supported when the cerebral circulation must also accommodate a systemic perturbation, potentially revealing constraints that either challenge alone would miss. We used arterial spin labelling (ASL) MRI to investigate whether concurrent breath-holding modifies the regional cerebral blood flow (CBF) response to motor activation. Fourteen healthy volunteers underwent pseudo-continuous ASL at 3T during sequential finger tapping with normal breathing, finger tapping during breath-holding, and breath-holding alone. Each condition included a resting baseline followed by eight 25-second task blocks interleaved with recovery. CBF responses were assessed using whole-brain voxelwise analyses and participant-specific primary motor cortex (M1) and supplementary motor area (SMA) regions. Baseline CBF was equivalent across conditions within predefined bounds of 10% either side. Motor-related perfusion increases remained detectable during concurrent breath-holding, but the mean M1 CBF increase was 26.5%, compared with 51.3% during normal breathing - a difference of 24.8 percentage points (p < 0.001). Corresponding SMA responses were 23.2% and 41.2%, although this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.092). Breath-holding alone produced spatially heterogeneous responses, including regional CBF reductions. No significant global grey- or white-matter CBF changes from baseline were detected after correction for multiple comparisons. These findings demonstrate that a detectable motor perfusion response can coexist with substantial attenuation during a concurrent respiratory challenge, despite comparable resting perfusion. Combining global vascular and local neuronal challenges may reveal constraints on regional perfusion responses that are not apparent from either challenge alone, providing a framework for investigating cerebrovascular adaptability and its potential impairment in disease.

papers.title: Functional Performance of Electrospun Tissue-Engineered Heart Valve Scaffolds Across Geometries Under Aortic Conditions
papers.abstract: Electrospun, bioresorbable polymer scaffolds are a promising platform for tissue-engineered heart valves (TEHVs) owing to their fibrous microstructure, tunable mechanics and capacity to support host-cell infiltration and remodeling. Recent in-vitro parametric studies of bioprosthetic heart valve (BHV) geometry have used silicone cast valves to link design parameters to hemodynamic performance and leaflet strain, but the functional behavior of electrospun whole-valve TEHV scaffolds across distinct leaflet geometries and clinically relevant aortic conditions remains poorly characterized. Here, we present an end-to-end workflow in which polycaprolactone (PCL) is electrospun directly onto parametrized, 3D-printed mandrels derived from two established analytical leaflet geometry models, yielding 21 whole-valve scaffolds across four geometries without cutting and assembling flat fiber sheets or suturing of flat fiber sheets. Fiber diameter, orientation and pore area were assessed by scanning electron microscopy and found to be consistent across scaffolds and geometries. Two scaffolds of each of four geometries were tested in a pulse duplicator under hypotensive, normotensive and hypertensive aortic conditions. All scaffolds opened and closed physiologically under all conditions, with a mean maximum geometric orifice area (GOA) of 44.5% of the valve area and a mean peak transvalvular pressure gradient of 10mmHg. Leaflet geometry had no apparent systematic effect on flow and pressure waveforms or on GOA. The mean regurgitant fraction was 82%, most likely due to leakage through the porous fiber network rather than incomplete leaflet closure. Electrospun whole-valve scaffolds thus achieve favorable leaflet kinematics at clinically relevant aortic conditions and the presented workflow provides a reproducible, parametric framework for their fabrication and translation toward regenerative heart valve replacement.

papers.title: Repurposing clofarabine against enteric pathogens via metabolic starvation
papers.abstract: Enteropathogenic and enterohaemorrhagic Escherichia coli (EPEC/EHEC) cause severe global diarrhoeal disease, exacerbated by rising antimicrobial resistance. Pathogenesis relies on "attaching and effacing" lesions, where bacteria generate actin pedestals to adhere, replicate, and destroy intestinal microvilli. To identify novel anti-virulence candidates targeting this process, we conducted a high-throughput phenotypic screen quantifying pedestal formation via high-content fluorescence microscopy. We identified the anticancer nucleotide analogue clofarabine as a potent inhibitor of EPEC growth and pathogenesis. Distinct from its oncology mechanism - inducing DNA chain termination and apoptosis - clofarabine competes with bacterial ATP-dependent processes to impede gene transcription, protein synthesis, and Type III Secretion System (T3SS) function. Remarkably, EPEC counteracts this inhibition by cleaving clofarabine, enabling restored protein synthesis and resumed growth. Furthermore, we report for the first time that clofarabine suppresses protein translation in human monocytes, suggesting an uncharacterised translational impact on mammalian cells. These findings reveal host and bacterial translation as interconnected vulnerabilities to purine antimetabolites, offering a novel strategy to disarm enteric pathogens while uncovering a bacterial enzymatic mechanism for neutralizing host-targeted therapeutics.

papers.title: Unsupervised Clustering Enables Cohort-Specific Variant Recalibration in Crops
papers.abstract: Trait discovery in crops require reliable marker datasets, yet variant discovery remains constrained by the lack of standardised, high-confidence reference resources. Publicly available plant genomic resources often rely on outdated reference genomes, heterogenous pipelines, and generic variant hard-filtering thresholds derived from human studies. Consequently, applying the Genome Analysis Toolkit (GATK) Best Practices framework, particularly machine learning-based variant quality score recalibration (VQSR), remains challenging in crops lacking suitable training resources. Here, we present an unsupervised approach for variant quality assessment and generating cohort-specific training resources, enabling integration of VQSR into established GATK workflows without predefined high-confidence training variant sets. Using Brassica napus as a model, we use the Illumina 60k Brassica SNP array to establish a reference-specific truth set for base quality score recalibration (BQSR) and independent benchmarking. Gaussian mixture model (GMM)-based clustering of multidimensional variant annotation profiles identifies high-, intermediate-, and low-quality variant classes, which provide flexible training resources without requiring labelled training data. We further validate the approach in diploid Brassica oleracea and hexaploid wheat (Triticum aestivum), representing contrasting population characteristics and genome architectures. Across all three species, GMM-based clustering consistently identifies informative quality classes and enables cohort-specific recalibration of both SNPs and insertion-deletions (INDELs). Comparison with conventional hard filtering reveals discordant pass/fail classifications for up to 46.4% of SNPs and 37.8% of INDELs across evaluated cohorts, demonstrating that the approaches capture distinct aspects of variant quality. Our results establish unsupervised variant classification as transferable strategy for generating cohort-specific VQSR resources, extending established GATK workflows to crops lacking comprehensive genomic resources.

papers.title: Combined HDAC and ATM inhibition with radiation in preclinical glioblastoma models
papers.abstract: Background: Brain-penetrant histone deacetylase inhibitors (HDACi) are promising radiosensitizing agents for glioblastoma (GBM). HDAC inhibitors can impair DNA damage response (DDR) pathways and promote persistent DNA damage. Here, we evaluated whether combined inhibition of HDAC and the DNA repair kinase, ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM), could synergize with radiation (IR) and improve therapeutic efficacy in GBM. Methods: In vitro dose-response assays were performed in patient-derived xenograft (PDX)-derived glioma stem cells (GSCs) with both inhibitors of HDAC (quisinostat, QST) and ATM (AZD1390) with or without IR treatment to assess synergy. Pharmacodynamic responses were evaluated by immunoblotting for histone acetylation, DDR signaling, and DNA damage markers. Transcriptomic analyses were performed to evaluate treatment-associated changes in DNA repair pathways. The combination of QST, AZD1390, and IR was further evaluated in an orthotopic GBM survival study. Results: Combined treatment with QST and AZD1390 produced synergistic radiosensitization in multiple GSC models in vitro. Furthermore, QST combined with IR suppressed transcription of homologous recombination (HR) pathway genes in GSCs, impairing double-strand break repair capacity through an epigenetic mechanism that does not directly inhibit ATM kinase activity. Pharmacodynamic analyses confirmed that QST increased histone acetylation while AZD1390 suppressed ATM signaling, together impairing complementary mechanisms to increase radiosensitivity of GSCs. In an orthotopic GBM model, QST combined with IR significantly prolonged survival compared with IR alone. However, the addition of AZD1390 did not provide a significant survival benefit beyond QST+IR, and AZD1390 combined with IR did not significantly improve survival relative to IR alone. Conclusions: Combined HDAC and ATM inhibition with QST and AZD1390 enhances radiosensitivity in patient-derived GBM cells, mechanistically underpinned by QST-mediated increase in DNA damage and dual disruption of DDR through complementary, non-overlapping mechanisms. However, this in vitro synergy did not confer additional survival benefit beyond QST+IR in an orthotopic GBM model under the dosing conditions tested, suggesting pharmacological limitations with the tumor microenvironment or suboptimal dosing schedules may have constrained in vivo efficacy.

papers.title: Interferon gamma-induced MX1 and IFITM1 inhibit Varicella-Zoster Virus Replication
papers.abstract: Interferon gamma (IFN-{gamma}) is a potent cytokine secreted following primary varicella-zoster virus (VZV) infection. Our previous studies demonstrated that pretreatment with IFN-{gamma} completely inhibited VZV replication in lung fibroblast MRC-5 and retinal epithelial ARPE-19 but not in melanoma MeWo cells, suggesting that IFN-{gamma}-stimulated protein(s) inhibit viral replication. Our microarray analysis revealed that 34 interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) were upregulated by greater than 2.5-fold at 8 h post-treatment in both ARPE-19 and MRC-5 cells compared to those of MeWo cells. The depletion of CTSS, GBP4, MX1, IFIT1, IFITM1 and IRF1 by siRNA in IFN-{gamma}-treated cells significantly increased VZV yields. Ectopic overexpression of interferon-induced myxovirus resistance 1 (MX1) or transmembrane protein 1 (IFITM1) significantly reduced VZV yield both in ARPE-19 and MeWo cells. IFITM1 abrogated viral major immediate-early IE62 protein-mediated trans-activation. IFITM1 reduced the level of VZV immediate-early IE62 protein, but not the IE62 mRNA, suggesting that IFITM1 expression reduces the expression level of IE62 by post-transcriptional regulation. Both human primary epidermal keratinocytes and calcium chloride-differentiated keratinocytes exhibit high levels of endogenous MX1 gene expression. Pharmacologic inhibition of JAK signaling reduced MX1 expression and enhanced VZV replication in calcium chloride-induced differentiated keratinocytes. Collectively, these findings identify MX1 and IFITM1 as key IFN-{gamma}-induced restriction factors that inhibit VZV replication and suggest that suppression of JAK-STAT signaling can promote VZV replication in differentiated keratinocytes.

papers.title: CheckAMG: Accurate Identification of Auxiliary Viral Genes with Genome Language Models
papers.abstract: Viruses shape microbial metabolism through auxiliary viral genes (AVGs) that reprogram host metabolism, physiology, and gene regulation during infection. Identifying AVGs is complicated by ambiguous viral versus cellular assignment, inconsistent curation, and reliance on sequence homology that misses divergent functions. Here we present CheckAMG, which pairs annotation-based AVG prediction, curated with a per-gene viral scoring system and ontological mapping of metabolic function, with a finetuned genome-language model for annotation-independent discovery. Benchmarked against DRAM-V and VIBRANT across three ecosystems, CheckAMG produced more strongly supported auxiliary metabolic gene (AMG) calls, and uniquely among AMG tools reports auxiliary physiological (APGs) and regulatory (AReGs) genes. Applied to 1,005,980 fragmented or complete soil and human-gut viral genomes, CheckAMG identified 541,199 AVGs tracking biome-specific protein clusters and functions, including 109,107 with no detectable sequence similarity to any reference database. CheckAMG thus provides a reproducible, scalable framework for identifying the genes through which viruses reprogram host biology.

papers.title: Adult corals enhance juvenile recruitment through cumulative ecological niche construction
papers.abstract: Ecosystem engineers are ecological niche constructors: by modifying local environments, they alter the conditions under which organisms establish, persist and interact. Although niche construction is often framed as a population-level evolutionary feedback, it could also operate at the assemblage level when communities collectively shape their environments and filter future trajectories, such as recruitment patterns. Reef-building corals offer an ideal setting to test this idea because adult colonies form three-dimensional carbonate structures that can persist after colony death, creating an inherited habitat for subsequent coral generations. Here, we tested whether coral recruitment to the juvenile stage was associated with local adult coral abundance, reef structure, and larval settlement supply. Combining spatially explicit coral censuses across >1300 quadrats, photogrammetric reef digital elevation models and data from settlement tiles across 15 reef sites at two time points at Jiigurru, Great Barrier Reef, we found that juvenile abundance increased additively on the log scale with adult abundance and with fractal dimension, a metric of fine-scale structural complexity. Surface rugosity had weaker effects, and interactions between adult abundance and habitat structure were limited, indicating largely additive, rather than synergistic or antagonistic, effects. Larval supply was negatively correlated with juvenile abundance. Our results show that both adult assemblages and the concurrent structural complexity, consistent with assemblage-level niche construction and ecological inheritance theory, shape coral recruitment.

papers.title: An interpretable open platform for sequence-based antibody developability prediction
papers.abstract: Antibody developability is increasingly predictable from sequence, yet software and trained models are rarely made available. We present DELPHI, open software for training developability predictors from labelled antibody assay data, together with ready-to-run, retrainable models. DELPHI compares 25 language-model and classifier combinations under CDR H3-cluster cross-validation that reduces sequence-similarity leakage, measures how performance changes with labelled training-set size, and reports residue-level model attributions. Applied to in-house polyreactivity and size-exclusion (SEC) data, it reaches mean AUC 0.959 and 0.933. Trained on those data alone, it transfers to a 246,293-antibody public library (AUC 0.950 with our deployed model) and ranks polyreactivity at a level similar to the best reported Ginkgo competition point estimate, without training on its data. Any laboratory can screen candidates before running assays, generate residue-level engineering hypotheses, and retrain DELPHI for a new assay.

papers.title: A novel vimentin-stabilizing urea compound MXC-017 ameliorates DSS-induced colitis and radiation enteropathy in mice
papers.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) and radiation enteropathy involve intestinal epithelial injury, barrier dysfunction, and inflammation, but effective treatments remain limited. This study evaluated MXC-017, a novel vimentin-targeting urea compound, in mouse models of dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis and radiation-induced enteropathy. Acute colitis was induced in C57BL/6 mice using 3.5% DSS for seven days, followed by regular water for seven days. Radiation enteropathy was induced by 13 Gy total abdominal irradiation. Mice received MXC-017 (150 mg/kg) or vehicle. Disease activity, intestinal permeability, inflammatory and epithelial markers, and histopathology were assessed. MXC-017's effects on cancer stem cell frequency, sphere formation, and migration were also examined in PC-3 and DU-145 prostate cancer cells. MXC-017 reduced DSS-induced colitis severity, accelerated weight recovery, lowered disease activity, partially preserved colon length, and restored barrier function. It also reduced proinflammatory cytokines, macrophage infiltration, epithelial injury, and goblet cell loss while preserving epithelial proliferation and markers of intestinal stem cell function and tight-junction integrity. Following irradiation, MXC-017 improved weight recovery, reduced intestinal permeability, preserved epithelial architecture, and partially mitigated villus shortening. Importantly, MXC-017 did not protect prostate cancer stem cells from radiation. Instead, it reduced stem cell frequency, sphere-forming capacity, and cancer cell migration. These findings support vimentin targeting with MXC-017 as a potential treatment for UC and radiation-induced intestinal toxicity and as an adjunct to radiotherapy for pelvic and abdominal malignancies.

papers.title: Time-Resolved Proteomics of a Polyglutamine-Expanded Huntingtin in vitro Cell Model Reveals Early RNA-Regulatory Compensation and Late Respiratory-Chain Remodeling
papers.abstract: Huntington disease (HD) is caused by a polyglutamine-expanded huntingtin protein that exerts progressive cellular toxicity. However, the temporal order of pathogenic events, and in particular which changes arise early and which emerge late, remains incompletely defined, despite their distinct therapeutic implications. To examine this trajectory, we profiled the proteome of a huntingtin-expressing cell model at early (72 h) and late (144 h) stages. Rather than a linear progression, the proteome changed in two distinct stages. At the early stage, cells showed increased abundance of RNA-processing, splicing, and protein-synthesis proteins, which may reflect an adaptive response to preserve gene-expression fidelity under stress. By the late stage, many of these proteins were depleted and mitochondrial energy-metabolism proteins dominated the response. Notably, 85% of proteins altered at both time points reversed direction between stages (95% at a false-discovery rate below 5%), and all reversals were supported by a significant genotype-by-time interaction, indicating that mutant huntingtin reorganizes the proteome rather than amplifying a fixed set of perturbations. Subunit-level analysis of the respiratory chain showed that Complex IV and ATP synthase subunits were reduced at 72 h, whereas at 144 h subunits of all five complexes were broadly increased, most strongly in Complex I and III, with a few distal subunits (COX5B, ATP5F1A, ATP5F1B) remaining reduced. Leveraging this proteomic map, we applied an AI-assisted, direction-aware drug repurposing strategy. Of 1,712 differentially abundant proteins, 498 were druggable, 109 had at least one agent whose mechanism was concordant with the required correction, and 89 of these 109 proteins mapped to at least one agent listed as approved in the source databases (56 to an agent with current regulatory approval). These included the approved Complex I inhibitor metformin, the investigational Complex I inhibitor ME-344, and pathway-level mitochondria-directed agents (elamipretide/SS-31, approved only for Barth syndrome; MitoQ, a dietary supplement), several of which have previously been evaluated in HD models. Collectively, these findings describe a two-stage proteomic response to mutant huntingtin in this cell model and suggest a putative early window for preclinical intervention testing, before late respiratory-chain remodeling is established.

papers.title: WHaloForce enables chemigenetic imaging of molecular tension in living cells and animals
papers.abstract: Piconewton forces borne by individual proteins within complex assemblies underlie cell adhesion, migration, and tissue morphogenesis, yet remain difficult to image in living systems. Here, we introduce WHaloForce, a chemigenetic HaloTag-based tension sensor that converts force-dependent relief of tryptophan-mediated dye quenching into a fluorescence lifetime change. Optical tweezers revealed a switch-like unquenching transition near 5 pN, and cellular measurements demonstrated dynamic responses to actomyosin activity. WHaloForce enabled quantitative tension imaging of diverse force-bearing proteins (vinculin, E-cadherin, -catenin, and laminin) in mammalian cells, mouse tissue, and C. elegans. Bright synthetic dyes made tension measurements possible at endogenous expression levels. In C. elegans, vinculin and laminin showed opposite tension patterns between tissues, highlighting tissue-specific force transmission through adhesions and the extracellular matrix. We also identified ovulation as a source of molecular loading within the spermathecal laminin network. WHaloForce thus offers a modular platform for imaging spatiotemporal tension patterns in living systems.

papers.title: Replicative and chronological epigenetic age track genome instability in opposite directions across cancers
papers.abstract: Epigenetic clocks are widely applied to tumor tissue, yet clocks trained to predict chronological age and clocks built to count cell divisions measure different quantities, and how either relates to the heterogeneity of methylation change within a tumor remains unclear. Here we compare four mitotic clocks with Horvath pan tissue clock in 506 matched tumor and normal pairs from 13 adult solid cancers and in 1,731 pediatric tumors. We show that mitotic age is higher in the tumor than in matched normal tissue in every adult cancer type, and that this advance is robust to tumor purity and cell type composition. The advance is explained chiefly by global methylation change and cell composition, with tumor proliferation contributing a small component that generalises across cancer types only for stemTOC; beyond proliferation, mitotic clock advance is associated with tumor grade, stage and genome instability, whereas Horvath clock is not, or is inversely so. Horvath clock, by contrast, reads older in renal clear cell and thyroid tumors and younger in endometrial, lung squamous, head and neck and prostate tumors, while in children 98.1% of tumors return a Horvath age above chronological age. Neither clock family is associated, patient by patient, with the heterogeneity of methylation change once its global magnitude and purity are accounted for, and neither changes consistently between primary and relapse. Methylation change is enriched on the X chromosome in female tumors only, independently of X copy number. Our data indicate that replicative epigenetic age is near uniformly advanced in cancer and records tissue remodelling more than current proliferation, whereas chronological clock readings of tumors are specific to cancer type and do not report clonal diversification in bulk tissue.

papers.title: TriMic: a Triticum aestivum microbial culture collection and synthetic community for dissecting wheat-microbe interactions
papers.abstract: Microbial culture collections and synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) are essential experimental resources for investigating underlying mechanisms of plant-microbe interactions. However, such resources remain scarce for agriculturally relevant crops. Here, we address this gap by developing TriMic, a community resource to investigate plant-microbe interactions in wheat. We employed a host-mediated isolation approach to obtain a bacterial collection from wheat roots and characterized its taxonomic representation and functional potential through whole-genome sequencing. We further evaluated the community dynamics of a consortium derived from this collection across time and wheat genotypes to inform the selection of a simplified community. TriMic includes core and keystone taxa reported in previous wheat microbiomes studies. Moreover, genomic analysis revealed genetic potential for diverse genes associated with plant colonization, nutrient cycling, plant growth promotion, and biosynthetic gene clusters with taxa exhibiting metabolic patterns associated with both generalist and specialist strategies. The proposed 15-member SynCom reflects the taxonomic and functional relevance of the full collection. By integrating publicly accessible bacterial isolates, whole-genome sequences, and an ecologically informed SynCom, TriMic provides a foundation for translating ecological and genomic observations into testable hypotheses, advancing mechanistic investigations of microbial community assembly and plant-microbiome interactions.

papers.title: Detection of bifidobacterial lipoproteins with anti-viral potential in donor human milk
papers.abstract: Background: Group B coxsackieviruses (CVBs) are involved in triggering type 1 diabetes. Free bifidobacterial lipoproteins (BLps) prevent CVBs cell infection. Our objective is to isolate free BLps potentially released by bifidobacteria in breastmilk and document their bioavailability. Methods: Bifidobacterium breve and B. longum were quantified by qPCR in samples donated to the hospitals biobank (DHM) within two weeks following delivery. BLps were captured onto CV B4, analyzed by SDS-PAGE and competitive ELISA. BLps transport through Caco-2 monolayers was monitored after DHM contact. Titration of anti-CV B IgA was carried out by ELISA. Results: Among the 90 enrolled donors, seven were excluded, 68 donated a unique sample and 15 donated multiple specimens (2 to 12). B. breve and B.longum were detected in 93.0 % and 32.8% unique DHM samples, respectively. The two species showed unstable counts in the multiple donation group. Although at highly variable amounts, BLps were readily detected. Free B.longum Lps were found in absence of B.longum itself. The BLps crossed the cell layer within 4h still binding CV B4. Conclusion: DHM contained BLps able to cross a cell layer mimicking the intestine still retaining their capacity to bind CV B. It suggested a possible newborns systemic protection against CV B4 infection that needs further investigation.

papers.title: Branch-Partitioned Selection Tests Reject Random Labels on Real Genes, Even Against a Null Simulated at the Depth of the Data
papers.abstract: Comparative genomics often turns a trait into a hypothesis about selection by labelling the branches that carry it and testing them against the rest. We asked how such a test behaves when the labels carry no trait. In three panels of about 50 species, fungi, yeasts and lactobacilli, two of them registered in advance, randomly placed terminal labels on presumed-null single-copy genes were rejected by PAML's two-ratio branch model in 65.9, 68.8 and 88.8% of genes, against a nominal 5%. Referring each real gene to replicates simulated under its own fitted null model did not remove the excess: with a generator matched to the depth of the real alignments, 65.0% (95% CI 53.5-75.3) and 83.8% (73.8-91.1) of 80 genes were still rejected. On the same genes the branch-site test, which asks only for positive selection on the labelled branches, rejected none after refitting, though on alignments simulated from its own fitted model it detected positive selection placed on all those branches in 95-100% of replicates, and replicates simulated under each gene's fitted per-branch {omega} rejected 1 of 40 genes against 28 of 40 for a control carrying only the noise of that fit: {omega} plausibly varies among branches on real genes, so that a randomly chosen set of branches does differ from the rest, though the fitted pattern is an upper bound. Under correct specification at the depth of the data the same test rejected random terminal labels in 5.4 and 6.8% of replicates, and internal labels of matched summed length differed from them by +0.2 and -1.2 percentage points. On earlier simulations from a site-mixture model, moving the labels from terminal to internal branches raised the rejection rate 1.3-fold on genes with a moderate fitted {omega} and 6.2-fold where a fitted class reached {omega} [≥] 100, in interaction with the fitted model. A trait label should therefore be read against random labels of the same size rather than against {chi}^2, and a reference simulated from the fitted model is not enough. The count question asked of the fungal panel is answerable: the within-genome ratio of plant-cell-wall-degrading enzymes to other carbohydrate-active enzymes is 0.473 times as large in ectomycorrhizal genomes as in free-living decomposers.

papers.title: Multi-omics profiling links epigenetic and lncRNA changes to early human endochondral ossification priming
papers.abstract: Differentiation programs remain incompletely understood across stem cell types, including for human bone marrow mesenchymal stromal/stem (BM-MSCs) cells, a heterogenous population orchestrating bone formation and establishing a functional hematopoietic niche in the bone marrow. BM-MSCs form and repair bone through the evolutionarily conserved process of endochondral ossification (EO), initiated by deposition of a transient cartilage template subsequently remodeled into bone and bone marrow tissues. Despite their considerable potential for skeletal regeneration, the early molecular and cellular events underlying BM-MSCs commitment to EO remain elusive. To overcome donor dependent variability in chondrogenic potential that limits mechanistic studies, we here exploit OssiGel as a potent chondro-inductive extracellular matrix offering robust recapitulation of EO by BMMSCs. Through multi-omics profiling of OssiGel-primed BM-MSCs, we identify rapid chromatin remodeling at chondrogenic loci as concomitant for lineage commitment. The emergence of a chondro-progenitor population is detected as early as 3 days in vivo and correlates with successful EO recapitulation. Mechanistically, we identify LINC02511 as novel enhancer-associated element involved in the onset of EO. We confirm presence of LINC02511 in human skeletal atlases, and its CRISPR-mediated silencing significantly impaired EO. By integrating human tissue engineering strategies with single cell multi-omics profiling, our study provides a framework for deciphering BM-MSCs fate decisions, highlighting the role of enhancer and non-coding elements as key determinants of early lineage specification. These findings advance our understanding of BM-MSCs biology and will prompt their translational exploitation in regenerative medicine.

papers.title: Toward pathology-guided illumination optimization for neuromodulation with a foundation-model-encoded light transport surrogate
papers.abstract: Clinical treatment planning for near-infrared (NIR) light neuromodulation requires patient-specific dosimetry to optimize light fluence (LF) delivery to cortical targets. The gold-standard Monte Carlo photon-transport forward solver is accurate but computationally expensive and non-differentiable for personalized inverse design across subjects. Here, we present PhomiNeuro, a foundation-model-encoded differentiable surrogate for time-resolved LF modeling and pathology-guided inverse design. A pretrained 3D medical imaging foundation model (VISTA3D) was domain-adapted to 285 training head models annotated with optical properties, and then coupled to an implicit neural representation (INR) that predicts LF at arbitrary spatiotemporal coordinates. Regularized by a time-dependent diffusion-equation residual, it demonstrated superior fidelity in 84 held-out participants, and ablations identified VISTA3D-derived anatomical priors as dominant and physics regularization as complementary. PhomiNeuro enables fast and robust queries of LF and its gradients with respect to illumination parameters for targets guided by individual structural magnetic resonance imaging and amyloid positron emission tomography, achieving 466-fold per-iteration speedup and 167-fold end-to-end optimization speedup. Explanatory analyses of LF delivery variability, including sex differences and amyloid status, identified structural variations as the primary drivers. These results position PhomiNeuro as a highly extensible translational framework toward personalized treatment planning and digital twin development in precision neuromodulation.

papers.title: zsasa: a Zig-based engine for high-throughput solvent accessible surface area at proteome scale
papers.abstract: Advances in structural and computational biology now yield structures by the hundreds of thousands, from predicted-structure databases to molecular-dynamics trajectories. Solvent accessible surface area (SASA), a long-established descriptor of protein stability, binding, and interfaces, remains central to their analysis. Established SASA tools are still widely used, but each covers only part of what such data now demand in input formats, outputs, and speed. We present zsasa, a fast, full-featured, open-source SASA engine for single structures, proteome-scale collections, and trajectories, usable from the command line or Python. It uses the same algorithms as established tools and owes its speed to the implementation, which makes full use of multicore processors and SIMD instructions while keeping memory use low. On a single laptop, zsasa reproduced FreeSASA, a widely used SASA library, down to individual atom areas on 4,370 Escherichia coli AlphaFold models. On the 23,586 structures of the human AlphaFold proteome, it was 3.3-fold faster than FreeSASA run in parallel while using a third or less of the peak memory of the other tools tested, and an optional approximate mode was 10-fold faster, with total SASA within 0.7% of the default results on average. On molecular-dynamics trajectories, it was 12- to 52-fold faster than MDTraj. As a demonstration, we computed interface burial for more than 600,000 predicted human protein dimers in under half an hour and found that a large buried area did not imply a confident predicted interface. zsasa is available under the MIT license at https://github.com/N283T/zsasa.

papers.title: Extending the least-cost theory of stomatal regulation to include soil moisture stress
papers.abstract: Terrestrial biosphere models commonly use empirical scaling factors to represent soil moisture constraints on carbon and water fluxes, but these lack mechanistic grounding and produce inconsistent estimates of soil moisture limitations on primary production and transpiration across models. Here we extended the least-cost hypothesis for optimal stomatal conductance to account for soil moisture limitations by allowing soil water availability to modulate the carbon cost of water transport, drawing on the observed temperature dependence of stem respiration, and derived a simple empirical approximation to the theory using global {delta}13C and eddy covariance data. The empirical analysis shows moderated thermal acclimation of stem respiration and a weak increase in water transport costs with aridity, supporting the interpretation that the decline in light-use efficiency (LUE) under arid conditions is primarily attributable to non-stomatal limitations. Validation against an independent global dataset of sapflow-derived canopy conductance and transpiration shows that the revised scheme significantly improves the predictive power of the least-cost hypothesis, offering a more mechanistically coherent alternative to existing soil moisture parameterisations.

papers.title: RNAquarium: an archive-scale atlas of zebrafish gene expression coupled with pan-taxonomic profiling reveals diverse viral drivers of transcriptomic states
papers.abstract: Zebrafish RNA-seq studies span diverse developmental, physiological, and disease contexts, yet most analyses remain confined to individual experiments and disregard the non-zebrafish component of the data. We present RNAquarium, a scalable framework for joint transcriptomic and metatranscriptomic analysis of RNA-seq data and apply it to all publicly available zebrafish RNA-seq datasets in the Sequence Read Archive. RNAquarium captures transcriptomic structure across development and tissues, reveals diverse microbial and viral associations, and identifies previously undescribed zebrafish viruses including a close relative of human influenza B virus linked to distinct host transcriptional states. We further demonstrate that archive-scale transcriptomes can support foundation-model training and prediction of infection-associated transcriptomic signatures. RNAquarium provides an open framework and interactive portal for exploring the breadth of zebrafish gene expression patterns and associated taxa profiled across a large research community. Moreover, our framework establishes a generalizable strategy for integrating transcriptomic and metatranscriptomic analyses across the diversity of life represented in public sequencing archives.

papers.title: Acoustic Characteristics of Low-Frequency Vocalizations of Bryde's Whales (Balaenoptera edeni edeni) in the Weizhou Island Waters of the Beibu Gulf, China
papers.abstract: Bryde's whales (Balaenoptera edeni edeni) are a first-class nationally protected species in China, and the waters around Weizhou Island in the Beibu Gulf support one of the country's few regularly observed coastal groups. Acoustic data for this population remain limited, and the effects of local vessel noise are poorly described. We conducted 16 vessel-based surveys around Weizhou Island between 11 and 31 January 2024 from a low-disturbance sailboat platform, with concurrent visual observation, and measured 729 low-frequency signals attributed to Bryde's whales. All signals were pulsed, with a repetition rate of 20~56 pulses per second, and their energy (400~1100 Hz) places them among the highest-frequency Bryde's whale calls reported. Signal duration was negatively correlated with maximum and center frequency in linear mixed-effects models that accounted for the non-independence of signals recorded within a session, but was unrelated to minimum frequency or bandwidth. Clustering of six standardized parameters, supported by bootstrap resampling (mean adjusted Rand index 0.87) and a Gaussian mixture model (minimum BIC at three components), resolved three call types differing in onset frequency, bandwidth and duration that co-occurred across sessions. In structure and frequency range these calls most closely resemble the pulsed moans and discrete pulse series described from juvenile Bryde's whales and mother-calf pairs, and they are distinct from the lower-frequency tonal calls (25~270 Hz) reported from the same region. Speedboat passage raised levels by 12.5 dB over the 20 Hz~20 kHz band and by 8.0 dB within the 400~1100 Hz band, cutting the detection margin of the calls from 10 dB to about 2 dB. The implied source levels match small high-speed craft elsewhere, so the masking risk is regional rather than local.

papers.title: Prenatal Alcohol Exposure Disrupts γ-Secretase Activity and Impairs Learning and Memory in Wild-Type and 3xTg-AD Mice
papers.abstract: Although prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) has been proposed as an early- life risk factor for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (AD/ADRD), the mechanistic underpinnings are underexplored. Mutations in the Presenilin genes contribute to AD/ADRD, with Presenilin 1 acting as the catalytic subunit of the gamma-secretase complex responsible for cleaving Notch and amyloid precursor protein (APP). We hypothesized that PAE disrupts gamma-secretase activity during brain development, which persists and is associated with behavioral deficits later in life. Pregnant wild-type B6129 and 3xTg-AD mice were fed an ethanol-containing liquid diet during gestational days 13-15. From birth to adulthood, PAE increased APP C-terminal fragments and Notch intracellular domain (NICD) levels in cortical lysates. These changes were accompanied by impaired hippocampal-dependent learning and memory in wild-type mice at 3 and 6 months of age and exacerbated behavioral deficits in 4-month-old 3xTg-AD mice. Our findings provide the first mechanistic insight linking PAE to AD/ADRD vulnerability.

papers.title: Behavioral flexibility, gut microbiome composition, and individual variability in oral oxycodone self-administration
papers.abstract: Prescription opioids such as oxycodone have been widely used in the United States and have contributed to the ongoing opioid epidemic. Although many individuals limit their use to prescribed contexts, a subset transitions to misuse and, in some cases, illicit opioid use. Identifying factors associated with variability in opioid intake may improve our understanding of vulnerability to opioid misuse. Here, we examined relationships among behavioral flexibility, gut microbiome composition, and subsequent oxycodone intake using an oral oxycodone self-administration model in male and female Long-Evans rats. Principal component analysis identified patterns of self-administration behavior that differentiated oxycodone-exposed animals from water controls. Among oxycodone-exposed animals, the principal component that contained variables of reinforced behaviors (i.e., active hole responding, reinforcers earned) was positively associated with oxycodone consumption, and hierarchical clustering identified three behavioral profiles distributed along this relationship. Behavioral flexibility, assessed before drug exposure using a contingency degradation task, was negatively associated with subsequent oxycodone intake, although it was not associated with the principal component measure of self-administration behavior. Oral oxycodone exposure was also associated with changes in gut microbiome composition, and analyses identified microbiome features associated with behavioral flexibility and oxycodone intake. Together, these findings demonstrate individual variability in oral oxycodone self-administration and identify behavioral and microbiome measures associated with subsequent drug-taking behavior. These results provide a foundation for future studies examining whether these measures prospectively contribute to vulnerability to opioid misuse.

papers.title: A nanoscale atlas of extracellular vesicles and particles in Drosophila olfactory sensilla
papers.abstract: Extracellular particles, including non-vesicular extracellular particles (NVEPs) and extracellular vesicles (EVs), are emerging as key contributors to sensory signaling, yet their ultrastructural organization within native tissues remains underexplored. Native tissues preserve extracellular particle organization and heterogeneity that are often lost during dissociation. Using cryofixation-based serial block-face scanning electron microscopy, we generated a nanoscale atlas of NVEPs and EVs across 352 Drosophila antennal olfactory sensilla ([~]70% coverage). Segmentation of more than 7,800 extracellular particles revealed distinct populations differing in morphology, size, electron density, and sensillum-class distribution. Analyses of EV biogenesis identified multivesicular bodies and membrane budding in auxiliary cells. Furthermore, sensilla housing degenerating neurons exhibited marked accumulation of EVs and NVEPs, accompanied by increased auxiliary-cell EV biogenesis. Together, these findings provide a large-scale ultrastructural characterization of extracellular particles in native sensory tissues and establish a foundation for understanding how extracellular particles are distributed, generated, and function during sensory signaling and degeneration.

papers.title: Comparative connectomics reveals stage-specific gap junction rewiring that reshapes avoidance behavior
papers.abstract: Environmental stress can remodel neural circuits, yet how such rewiring generates behavioral adaptation remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how dauer-specific circuit remodeling alters nociceptive behavior. We discovered that dauers exhibit significantly shorter avoidance durations than adults. Through comparative connectomics, we observed a substantial expansion of gap junctions within the dauer nociceptive circuit and found that dauer neurons exhibit more transient activity dynamics as a result of this rewiring. Modeling neuronal activity demonstrated that removing dauer-specific connectivity constraints failed to reproduce transient characteristics, validating the functional role of dauer-specific gap junctions. Furthermore, introducing synthetic dauer-specific gap junctions into adults was sufficient to recapitulate dauer-like activity patterns and shorten avoidance duration. Despite extensive rewiring, avoidance initiation remained preserved across developmental stages. Our findings show that the dauer neural circuit is selectively rewired through gap junction remodeling to balance flexibility and stability for survival under stress.

papers.title: Cross-cohort optimal transport maps macrophage plasticity and routes to inflammation and fibrosis in human atherosclerosis
papers.abstract: Single-cell transcriptomics has revealed extensive macrophage heterogeneity in atherosclerotic plaques, but how disease-associated programs reshape cellular identity remains unclear. Connecting macrophage states to these molecular changes could help identify candidate routes through which macrophages contribute to inflammation and fibrosis.
