papers.abstract: Nanopore sequencers produce reads within minutes, but metagenomic analysis remains challenging where internet access is limited, data are sensitive or computing resources are modest. EMtrace is an offline pipeline that runs on a laptop during sequencing: it classifies MinKNOW reads, estimates taxon abundance by expectation-maximization (EM) and assembles reference-based consensus genomes. We benchmarked it against five virome and four 16S rRNA tools on simulated, mock-community and clinical data. On field isolates and 16 SARS-CoV-2 clinical samples, EMtrace had the highest species-level F1 score (1.00 and 0.97) and one false-positive species, against 3-7 for the comparators. It recovered divergent viruses as completely as ViMOP, and low-titre field libraries more completely, at [≥]99.7% identity. In replayed runs, it identified the target virus in the first 4,000-read batch (5-13 min). With a shared 16S reference, EMtrace reported two to three times fewer false-positive species than Emu.

papers.title: Brain Network Dynamics from Neuronal Avalanches for Longitudinal Motor-Imagery Decoding
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) offer opportunities for personalized neurorehabilitation, but inter-session variability, repeated calibration, and the need for expert supervision limit their use beyond supervised settings. We propose a longitudinal BCI framework that integrates neuronal avalanches dynamics, reflecting cascades of propagation neural activity, with graph-theory and data-driven region of interest analysis to extract computationally efficient and neuro-physiological interpretable features. Source-reconstructed EEG from 20 BCI-naive participants performing right-hand motor imagery (MI) and rest across four training sessions was represented by a directed weighted connectivity network based on neuronal avalanches. Local, mesoscopic, and global network measures revealed task-related changes predominantly in contralateral sensorimotor regions and distributed reorganisation across training. We modelled here the learning-related evolution of feature distributions across previous sessions and used this trajectory to predict class-conditional distributions in an unseen fourth session, anticipating future brain states before new session calibration. PageRank-based ROI selection achieved an AUC of 73.5 +/- 7.9%, compared with 64.5 +/- 10.6% using all ROIs, while reducing computational time by approximately 39% relative to performance-driven selection. The proposed framework provides interpretable, compact descriptions of avalanche propagation and exploits training-related changes for prospective decoding. Moving spatial selection and model optimization to an initial offline phase may reduce subsequent calibration demands and facilitate more autonomous BCI use.

papers.title: Identification and localization of bone marrow ILC2s using Id2/Cxcr6 dual-reporter mice
papers.abstract: Type 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) are present in the bone marrow, where their identification and spatial localization remain challenging because of their low abundance and the expression of shared markers by other lymphoid populations. Here, we evaluated the use of Id2YFP/+ Cxcr6GFP/+ dual-reporter mice to identify and visualize bone marrow ILC2s. Using spectral flow cytometry, we showed that both ST2- and ST2 ILC2s expressed high levels of ID2, whereas CXCR6 expression differed between these subsets. However, the ID2 expressing compartments also contained NK cells, NKT cells, conventional T cells and ILC progenitors. Surface marker profiling identified CD25 and ICOS as useful markers for enriching ILC2 populations, with ST2 enabling the segregation of the ST2- and ST2 subsets. Single-cell RNA sequencing further characterized the diversity of Id2 and Cxcr6 expressing lymphoid populations and supported the use of CD5 and NKp46 as exclusion markers. Combining these markers with the dual-reporter system, confocal microscopy revealed YFPGFPCD5-NKp46- cells compatible with an ILC2 phenotype, distributed throughout the bone marrow as isolated cells or within multicellular clusters. Complementary flow cytometric analyses demonstrated that ILC2s accounted for more than 90% of a phenotypically related reporter-positive population after exclusion of major T and NK cell populations, providing additional support for the identification of the cells visualized in situ as putative ILC2s. Together, these findings establish a strategy combining dual-reporter mice, flow cytometry, transcriptomic profiling and confocal imaging to investigate the localization and spatial organization of putative bone marrow ILC2s.

papers.title: Beyond Exploration: Heightened Recent Reward Reliance and Midfrontal Sensitivity to Outcome Differences in ADHD
papers.abstract: Adaptive decision-making requires balancing the exploitation of known rewards with the exploration of alternative options, yet how attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) shapes this trade-off remains unclear. Using a restless four-armed bandit task and electroencephalography (EEG), we investigated the neural correlates of exploratory decisions and how recent rewards shape choice behavior and feedback processing in 23 adults with self-reported clinical ADHD diagnoses and 27 controls. Across 450 trials with dynamically changing payoffs, choices were classified against the highest last-observed payoff, and behavioral modeling quantified the influence of reward history on subsequent decisions. Contrary to our predictions, exploration rates, task performance, and neural differentiation between exploration and exploitation did not differ significantly between groups. However, adults with ADHD were more likely to repeat an option after high reward feedback and switch after low rewards, driven primarily by the immediately preceding outcome. At neural level, ADHD participants also showed greater midfrontal sensitivity to unsigned changes between consecutive payoffs, expressed in a feedback-evoked response spanning 280 to 568 ms and carried by slow activity below 2 Hz. Together, these findings dissociate the raw frequency of exploration from the dynamic weighting of recent outcomes in ADHD. Rather than reflecting an indiscriminate drive for novelty, behavior was characterized by heightened recent reward reliance paired with amplified slow-wave midfrontal sensitivity to outcome shifts. Crucially, this profile emerged without compromising overall performance, suggesting that, in this volatile environment, ADHD was associated with an increased weighting of recent outcomes rather than with a performance deficit.

papers.title: Neural Encoding Geometry of Human Voluntary Visual Selection
papers.abstract: Selecting relevant targets from competing alternatives is a core cognitive function. While human visual selection can be tracked with high spatiotemporal precision, it remains unsolved how selected targets and non-selected alternatives are neurally encoded to effectively separate them. Building on recent work revealing the neural encoding geometry underlying target selection in animals, we here examined how the representational format of selected targets and non-selected alternatives evolve over time during human voluntary selection. Initially, selected and non-selected objects showed equal spatially selective neural activity, yet the selected target was represented more strongly after 300-350 ms. Using cross-decoding, we found that selected and non-selected objects are encoded along a shared sensory axis, whereas selected targets are encoded along an additional spatially selective axis. This encoding geometry effectively separates selected targets from non-selected alternatives in neural space. Our results generalized across selection conditions: we found comparable results in instructed and free-choice selection, as well as in delayed oculomotor and covert visual selection. Together, we demonstrate that the human brain selectively encodes targets, but not distractors, along an additional axis, revealing a neural mechanism through which voluntary selection prioritizes behaviorally relevant information.

papers.title: LIGR-Nue for the global mapping of the bacterial sRNA targetome in vivo
papers.abstract: Interactions between regulatory small RNAs (sRNAs) and their target transcripts are central for post-transcriptional regulation in bacteria. Based on RNA-seq analysis, we determined the relative abundance of several sRNAs in the photosynthetic cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 under photoautotrophic growth conditions and after transfer to darkness. We observed an increase in the abundance of the sRNAs DsiR1 to 58.6% and of CsiR1 to 19% of the sRNA transcriptome after transfer to darkness. We then developed a duplex-directed, transcriptome-wide mapping strategy of RNA-RNA interactions in vivo, called LIGR-Nue, which involves aminomethyltrioxsalen-mediated UV cross-linking, proximity ligation, crosslink reversal, reverse transcription and sequencing. The data were analysed using the RNANUE pipeline for the detection of chimeric reads and mapping, and benchmarked against known targetome data for the sRNAs PsrR1 and NsiR4. Using this methodology, we identified RNA-RNA interactions, such as PsrR1 as a regulator of carbon assimilation, and DsiR1 as a global silencing factor of photosynthesis-associated mRNAs in the dark. This data enables the comprehensive analysis of sRNA functions in post-transcriptional gene regulation. LIGR-Nue is broadly applicable to map RNA-RNA interactions in bacteria.

papers.title: Mechanism and subunit-dependence of disease-associated lurcher mutation in AMPA-type glutamate receptors
papers.abstract: AMPA receptors are glutamate-activated neuroreceptors responsible for the majority of fast excitatory neurotransmission in vertebrate brains. Activity-dependent changes in their functional and trafficking properties underpin cognitive processes such as learning and memory formation. In the past 15 years, a number of mutations within AMPA receptor genes have been identified as disease-causing leading to some form of neurodevelopmental delay. Here, we focused on one such mutation called lurcher, resulting from a change of the third Ala in the highly conserved SYTANLAAF motif to Thr. We determined functional consequences of lurcher mutation in homomeric AMPA receptors composed of subunits GluA1 or GluA2. In GluA1 subunit, lurcher mutation has been identified as a hotspot in a large cohort of patients with neurodevelopmental disorders. We confirm previously established lurcher phenotype characterised by slower deactivation and desensitization kinetics as well as more profound block of desensitization compared to the wild-type (WT) homomers. We show that these effects are more pronounced in GluA2 than GluA1 homomers. Lurcher phenotypes are attenuated, but still present, in more physiologically abundant heteromeric AMPA receptors composed of two GluA1 lurcher and two GluA2 WT subunits (GluA1 lc/GluA2 WT). Schild analysis indicates lurcher enhances activity of AMPA receptors by primarily changing the efficiency with which they open their ion channel upon glutamate binding rather than by changing affinity for glutamate. Perampanel, the only widely licensed drug that targets AMPA receptors, is an anti-convulsant that acts as a non-competitive inhibitor. We show it continues to inhibit GluA1 lc/GluA2 WT heteromeric receptors and that its IC50 depends on the auxiliary subunits associated with the heteromers. Specifically, stargazin (TARP {gamma}-2) brings the IC50 for perampanel into the submicromolar range, just like in the WT receptors.

papers.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Quizartinib Resistance in FLT3 Mutants
papers.abstract: Quizartinib, a type II FLT3 inhibitor approved for FLT3-ITD-positive acute myeloid leukemia (AML), is frequently limited by acquired resistance, which arises in up to 40% of patients with disease progression and is driven largely by the D835Y and F691L kinase-domain mutations. To define the underlying mechanisms, we performed triplicate 200-ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulations of wild-type FLT3, FLT3-D835Y, and FLT3-F691L in complex with Quizartinib, combining conformational analysis, MM-GBSA binding free-energy calculations, and binding-pocket characterization. Both mutations destabilized the inactive DFG-out conformation required for type II inhibitor binding, with mean binding free-energy reductions of 5 kcal/mol for D835Y and 10 kcal/mol for F691L relative to wild-type. D835Y disrupted the activation-loop electrostatic network and reduced Cys694 hydrogen-bond occupancy from 85% to 45%, whereas F691L abolished key van der Waals contacts and opened a 120 cubic Angstrom hydrophobic void at the gatekeeper position. Both mutants sampled a wider range of conformations and lost 14-17% of binding-pocket volume. These predictions were corroborated by CCK-8 viability assays and Western blotting of p-FLT3 (Y591) in Ba/F3 cells, which reproduced the predicted resistance hierarchy (F691L > D835Y > WT) at the cellular level. Together, these results indicate that D835Y and F691L confer resistance through distinct electrostatic and hydrophobic mechanisms that converge on destabilization of the inactive kinase conformation, providing a structural basis for the design of next-generation FLT3 inhibitors.

papers.title: A trio of brain networks dynamically orchestrates music recognition
papers.abstract: Recognition memory continuously integrates internal representations with sensory information to guide adaptive behavior. Yet most theoretical models conceptualize recognition as the retrieval of an isolated stimulus through a discrete sequence of steps including sensory processing, hippocampal retrieval, and cortical reinstatement. However, in natural settings, perception, memory, and predictions interact continuously within an evolving context to guide adaptive responses. It is unclear how brain networks coordinate the integration of internal and external information during dynamic recognition. Here, we combined intracranial recordings (N = 30) of high-frequency activity (70-160 Hz) and dimensionality reduction to characterize distributed network dynamics during music recognition. We identified three interacting functional networks supporting sensory processing, sensory-memory integration, and decision formation, whose temporal dynamics predicted the timing of behavior. During recognition of memorized sequences, sensory activity progressively attenuated, sensory inputs were combined with mnemonic and contextual information, and decision-related activity evolved toward sensorimotor engagement. Novel sequences disrupted this organization by sustaining sensory responses and accelerating decision-related activity. Sensory and integrative networks communicated bidirectionally. Our findings reveal recognition as a distributed, context-dependent, and goal-directed process emerging from the continuous and bidirectional coordination of large-scale brain networks.

papers.title: Northern palsa and peat ecosystem microbiomes are potentially supported by hydrogen and carbon monoxide metabolism
papers.abstract: Northern peatland and permafrost ecosystems are facing rapid changes, with increasing temperatures, permafrost thaw and shifts in hydrology. Characterizing microbial communities and metabolic potential from the soils and associated water bodies is crucial to understanding the changes in biogeochemical cycling in these ecosystems. For this, samples were collected and sequenced from subarctic palsa and peat soils, along with samples from associated thaw ponds and streams. Metagenomics was utilized in describing the microbiome and its metabolic potential in these environments. Palsa soils hosted microbial communities that were distinct from the peatland soils, ponds and stream waters. Soils and their adjacent ponds shared taxa, and peat soils and ponds also shared taxa with the streams, unlike palsa soils which were likely more hydrologically isolated. Based on metabolic marker gene ratio for denitrification [(nirS+nirK)/nosZ], palsa soils had the strongest potential to be a source of nitrous oxide (N2O) out of all the sample types. Marker genes for hydrogen gas (H2) and carbon monoxide (CO) utilization were abundant across soil environments and metagenome assembled genomes, suggesting that trace gas oxidation is likely one of the key energy sources for microbiomes. In the palsa ponds and peat soils pmoA, marker gene for methanotrophy, was the most abundant compared to the other sample types.

papers.title: CD8+ T-cells protect against experimental atherosclerosis through antigen specific interactions in the plaque
authors: van de Sluis, B. A. J. A.
papers.abstract: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease with a significant adaptive immune component. CD8+ T cells accumulate in plaques and display signatures of antigen-specific activation. However, whether this accumulation is driven by local antigen recognition and what functional consequences follow, remains poorly understood. Here we address this gap of knowledge using loss- and gain-of-function experiments. Atherosclerotic Rag-/-Ldlr-/- mice received adoptively transferred wildtype or antigen-restricted CD8+ T cells alongside CD4+ T cells to distinguish antigen-specific from antigen-independent responses. In a complementary model, ApobOVA-TGxLdlr-/- mice, expressing an ovalbumin-tagged variant of the atherosclerosis-associated ApoB100 protein, enabled OT-I CD8+ T cells to function as atherosclerosis-antigen-specific CD8+ T cells. T-cell distribution, activation and phenotype were assessed systemically and within lesions, plaque burden and composition were quantified histologically. Wildtype CD8+ T cells accumulated significantly more in aortic lesions compared to antigen-restricted CD8+ T cells, and exhibited increased activation, exhaustion and cytokine secretion, indicating that plaque-infiltrating T cells are predominantly antigen-specific. Perturbing antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell interactions significantly decreased plaque stability index, suggesting a protective role for antigen-specific CD8+ T cells. In ApobOVA-TGxLdlr-/- mice, OT-I T cells accumulated at high frequency in the liver, consistent with hepatic ApoB100-expression, and were found in circulation and aorta. Histological analysis revealed reduced plaque burden in OT-I recipients, reproducing an atheroprotective effect of antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell responses. Plaque reduction coincided with reduced TUNEL, but similar Caspase 3 staining, suggesting OT-I transfer results in reduced secondary necrosis. In line with this, CD47 expression in OT-I recipient mice was reduced and in vitro, OT-I but not antigen non-specific CD8+ T cells reduced expression of CD47 on OVA-presenting foam cells. CD8+ T-cell accumulation in experimental atherosclerosis is driven primarily by antigen-specific interactions and such responses are associated with plaque stabilization and reduced lesion formation, potentially through induction of apoptosis and prevention of secondary necrosis

papers.title: Women's health outreach using a rapid and fieldable Nanopore-based microbiome profiling workflow.
authors: van den Braak, N. P. W. C. J.
papers.abstract: Background In recent years, scientific interest in the vaginal microbiome has increased due to its impact on women's health. Colonization of the Lactobacillus species in the vagina may contribute to protection against vaginal infectious diseases. In order to create public awareness regarding vaginal health and to provide insights into the vaginal microbiome, a rapid field microbiome analysis using Nanopore sequencing was evaluated at Lowlands, a three-day music festival in the Netherlands. This study aimed not only to evaluate a rapid sequencing workflow, but also to explore citizen science as a tool for health promotion and public engagement in women's health. Methods The workflow at Lowlands contained the following steps; (i) Dialogue concerning vaginal health, with invitation to participate. (ii) Informed consent and questionnaire to investigate knowledge on vaginal health, life-style and contraceptive usage; (iii) self-collection of a vaginal swab; (iv) DNA isolation using QuickExtract DNA extraction solution; (v) Ultrafast amplification of the 16S rRNA gene using NextGenPCR thermal cycling using 16S Barcoding kit 24 V14; (vi) Library preparation and sequencing was performed according to the manufacturers protocol using R10 chemistry; (vii) For data-analysis, MABA16S was used, with slight modifications. This workflow was established within 4 hours and results were communicated with interested participants.

papers.title: Somatic symptom burden is associated with anger internalization measured as reduced reactive aggression
papers.abstract: Difficulties in emotion regulation, including anger suppression, have been linked to more severe somatic symptoms in patients with chronic pain. Because this evidence comes mainly from clinical samples, it remains unclear whether such difficulties precede or follow symptom chronification. We examined whether somatic symptom burden is associated with reduced reactive aggression, as a behavioral marker of anger internalization. Forty-four healthy adults (25 females) completed the Taylor Aggression Paradigm, a competitive reaction-time task in which they selected noise intensity delivered to a fictitious opponent across three provocation conditions (low, moderate, and high). somatic symptom burden was evaluated using the Somatic Symptom Scale-8 (SSS-8) and Patient Health Questionnaire-15 (PHQ-15). Alexithymia was evaluated using the Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20). Participants with higher somatic symptom burden selected lower noise intensities overall, with significant differences at low and moderate provocation levels. Difficulty identifying feelings tended to be positively associated with somatic symptom burden, whereas alexithymia was not associated with reactive aggression. These findings suggest that inhibited retaliation, previously reported in chronic pain patients, may already be present in healthy individuals with higher somatic symptom burden, potentially aiding early identification of chronic pain risk. Difficulty distinguishing emotions from bodily sensations may also contribute to somatic symptom expression.

papers.title: Heterotopic expression of respiratory-associated genes suggests a developmental basis for pleopodal gill evolution in isopod crustaceans
papers.abstract: Background The evolution of organs in new anatomical positions contributes to morphological diversity and offers opportunities to examine developmental evolution. Crustacean gills provide a useful comparison: isopods bear pleopodal gills on abdominal appendages, whereas many other crustaceans possess thoracic epipodal gills. Here, we combined comparative anatomy and multiplex in situ hybridization chain reaction to examine embryonic expression of the respiratory-associated genes trachealess (trh) and ventral veins lacking (vvl) in the aquatic isopod Gnorimosphaeroma cf. hoestlandti and the terrestrial isopod Porcellio scaber. We also examined the posterior Hox genes abdominal-A and Abdominal-B (AbdB) to assess regional pleonal patterning. Results In both species, trh and vvl expression occurred in developing pleopodal regions corresponding to gill-bearing tissues. In G. cf. hoestlandti, prominent expression extended into both endopodal and exopodal regions of pleopods 4-5, whereas in P. scaber, it was concentrated in the endopods of pleopods 3-5. In both species, trh showed more restricted posterior pleopodal expression than vvl, and posterior expression domains overlapped spatially with AbdB-expressing regions. Conclusions Compared with thoracic epipodal expression reported in other crustaceans, these patterns differ at two anatomical levels: along the body axis (thorax versus pleon) and among appendage structures (epipods versus endopods/exopods). These differences suggest that the acquisition of heterotopic trh and vvl expression in isopod pleopods may have contributed to the evolution of pleopodal gills. Moreover, the different expression patterns in the two isopods suggest subsequent evolutionary changes in the spatial distribution of these genes, potentially associated with the diversification of pleopodal gills.

papers.title: Membrane Geometry Reveals Strengths and Limitations of AlphaFold-Predicted Transmembrane Protein Complexes
papers.abstract: High-confidence protein complex predictions do not necessarily represent physically or biologically plausible assemblies. This limitation is particularly relevant for transmembrane (TM) proteins, whose interactions are constrained by the lipid bilayer. Here, we systematically evaluated membrane compatibility in the recently expanded AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, analysing 189,469 high-confidence AlphaFold-Multimer TM-TM complexes and additional TM-soluble assemblies. Most predictions exhibited plausible membrane geometry: among 125,657 evaluable complexes with TM proteins possessing more than two TM helices, 95.4% had joint hydrophobic thicknesses within the expected range of 15-35 angstroms. Nevertheless, some complexes displayed substantial inconsistencies in membrane positioning or protomer orientation despite favourable prediction confidence. Interactions between TM proteins, particularly those containing only one or two TM helices, were frequently dominated by extramembrane contacts. Among TM-soluble complexes, 77.4% showed no penetration of the soluble partner into the hydrophobic membrane core. We further investigated whether AlphaFold3 (AF3) could overcome limitations of AlphaFold-Multimer. Although AF3 recovered an experimentally supported SERCA-phospholamban interaction, it failed to reproduce the cholesterol-mediated norepinephrine transporter homodimer. A benchmark of 173 cholesterol-containing membrane protein targets further revealed limited accuracy in predicting cholesterol-binding poses, particularly for structures released after the AF3 training cutoff. Together, these findings demonstrate that membrane-specific geometric constraints provide a valuable complement to conventional confidence metrics and highlight the persistent challenges of predicting assemblies involving lipids.

papers.title: spSheaf: sheaf-theoretic spatial domain inference from raw molecules without cell segmentation
papers.abstract: Spatial-transcriptomics pipelines usually require cell segmentation and discard 20-60% of transcripts. We introduce spSheaf, a segmentation-free spatial domain inference method built on cellular sheaf theory. Within a domain, neighbouring regions have compatible local expression structure; across a transition between programs they remain discordant after alignment of their local subspaces. spSheaf quantifies this alignment-adjusted disagreement and attenuates transitions during clustering. On the MERFISH hypothalamus benchmark it attains mean ARI 0.571 and NMI 0.655, ranks first of twelve on NMI, and leads SSAM, Points2Regions and FICTURE by 0.16 ARI on held-out slices. On three further annotated sections, every method tuned, it leads on one, ties on one and trails SSAM by 0.06 ARI. The sheaf weighting adds +0.102 ARI where domains are distinct programs and is neutral on laminar cortex. One domain above the annotated count, it divides the BST into the territories of two atlas neuronal populations on both adjacent sections.

papers.title: Unavoidable Disasters: the Hsp70 Chaperone Can Only Prevent Aggregation Over a Limited Time Span
papers.abstract: Cells must attain and maintain proper protein folding and avoid aggregation: this is a pervasive challenge across all domains of life. Molecular chaperones are central to this process, acting through mechanisms shaped by the free-energy landscapes of their client proteins. The impact of chaperones on client-specific kinetic and thermodynamic characteristics, however, remains poorly characterized. Here, we develop the CHAMPION70 computational model to perform kinetic simulations on the E. Coli Hsp70 chaperone system in the presence of client-protein folding and aggregation. Experimentally determined folding/unfolding/aggregation rate constants are taken into account. In the case of weakly aggregation-prone clients, CHAMPION70 predicts that Hsp70 prevents aggregation only over timescales approaching the average human lifespan (79 years). For strongly aggregation-prone clients, however, aggregation inevitably occurs starting from a few minutes, even at higher-than-physiological Hsp70 concentrations. Thus, the Hsp70 chaperone system merely delays, yet surprisingly does not eliminate, the onset of aggregation. Further, CHAMPION70 predicts that Hsp70 most effectively retards the aggregation of slow-folding, thermodynamically stable clients. In contrast, thermodynamically unstable clients remain engaged with Hsp70 for prolonged periods even when aggregation propensity is low, thereby consuming chaperone capacity and reducing the extent of productive folding. This outcome suggests that condensate formation by proteins containing disordered regions may serve to mitigate unnecessary Hsp70 engagement. In all, our results provide a quantitative framework for understanding how client-specific kinetic and thermodynamic properties shape chaperone activity and show that the Hsp70 chaperone system does not altogether prevent aggregation: it merely retards it.

papers.title: Cross-state representation learning enables prospective discovery of dynamic protein allosteric sites
papers.abstract: Allosteric regulation offers multifunctional induction in therapeutic interventions, yet conformational plasticity hinders computational identification of allosteric sites. Machine learning models rely on static holo (ligand-bound) structures, generalizing poorly to apo or substrate-bound states where binding pockets are transient or cryptic. We present AsBench2, a cross-state site-recognition benchmark, and AllositeUltra, a deep learning framework integrating multimodal protein representations (combining structure-aware language models with physical dynamics) and residue-guided candidate supplementation, effectively decoupling site detection from static pocket geometry. AllositeUltra demonstrates superior generalization, achieving Top-3 site recovery rates of 65.2% and 70.6% on apo and substrate-bound structures, respectively, representing relative improvements of 36.4% and approximately 50% over the best-performing baselines. Prospective application to MAGI2 identifies a previously unrecognized interdomain allosteric pocket, validated at atomic resolution through small-molecule screening and X-ray crystallography. Proteome-wide application yields a high-confidence atlas of targetable allosteric sites, bridging the gap between structural representation learning and prospective AI-driven drug discovery.

papers.title: IL13 critically contributes to the antitumor activity of polyfunctional CD4+ T cells driven by constitutively active Stat5
papers.abstract: The presence of polyfunctional T cells capable of concurrently producing multiple cytokines correlates with favorable clinical outcomes in patients with cancer. We previously reported that overexpression of constitutively active Stat5a (CASTAT5) confers polyfunctionality on tumor-specific CD4 T cells, enabling durable antitumor immunity following adoptive cell therapy. However, the mechanisms underlying the enhanced antitumor effects of CASTAT5-modified T cells remain unclear. Here, we identify interleukin-13 (IL13) as a critical effector cytokine contributing to the multifaceted antitumor activity of CASTAT5-conditioned polyfunctional CD4 T cells (C5-CD4). C5-CD4 T cells exhibit a prominent T helper 2 (Th2) cytokine profile, accompanied by extensive epigenomic remodeling at the Th2 cytokine loci, as revealed by Hi-C and histone-modification CUT&Tag assays. Neutralization of IL13 diminished the antitumor efficacy of C5-CD4 T cells. Furthermore, targeted Il13 disruption substantially impaired tumor control and was associated with reduced donor T cell expansion and persistence, diminished systemic cytokine and chemokine responses, and attenuated activation of endogenous tumor-reactive CD8 T cells. Nonetheless, IL13 overexpression alone in donor CD4 T cells failed to fully recapitulate the therapeutic activity of C5-CD4 T cells, indicating that IL13 is a critical contributor but is insufficient to account for the full antitumor activity conferred by CASTAT5. Single-cell RNA sequencing associated donor-derived IL13 with increased representation of tumor-infiltrating myeloid cells and IL13-signaling in monocytes and macrophages exhibiting tissue-repair-associated transcriptional programs. Moreover, Il13 disruption diminished the therapeutic efficacy of CASTAT5-expressing CD19-targeted CAR-T cells in a mouse B-cell lymphoma model. Reanalysis of a human CD19CAR-T infusion-product dataset further revealed an association between IL13 expression and type 2 cytokine signatures linked to prolonged clinical response, suggesting a potential contribution of IL13 to the efficacy of human CD19CAR-T therapy. Together, these findings uncover an unexpected antitumor role for IL13 and establish it as a critical node linking polyfunctional donor T cells with endogenous immune cells to promote sustained tumor immunity.

papers.title: Functional Conservation Amid Extreme Divergence in Freshwater SAR11 Hypervariable Region 2
papers.abstract: The Ca. Pelagibacterales order (SAR11) is a ubiquitous bacterioplankton in aquatic ecosystems. The genomes of SAR11 bacteria contain hypervariable region 2 (HVR2), the largest HVR with extreme diversity. Previous studies collectively indicated the enrichment of cell-surface modification genes on HVR2, which have been hypothesized to facilitate phage evasion. However, characterisation of HVR2 has primarily targeted marine clades and been limited for freshwater SAR11 (aka. Fontibacterium). Here, we employed single-cell genomics and recovered 176 Fontibacterium HVR2 sequences from Lake Biwa (Japan) and Lake Zurich (Switzerland), across multiple sampling years for Lake Biwa. Comparative sequence analyses revealed that freshwater HVR2 showed high intra-population diversity and appears to evolve independently of the rest of the genome, mirroring patterns observed in marine counterparts. Nevertheless, highly conserved HVR2 sequence pairs were observed for distinct Fontibacterium species from the two intercontinental habitats, suggesting horizontal transfers of HVR2 with conserved functional configurations across divergent lineages and large spatial scales. Further comparison with 145 marine HVR2 sequences revealed HVR2 sequences displaying synteny between Fontibacterium and marine SAR11, and 209 gene families conserved across habitats, including three near-universally conserved families. All examined freshwater HVR2s contained initiator methionine tRNA genes concentrated near the boundaries of the 5S region, suggesting a tDNA-anchored integration mechanism. These results suggest the functional equivalence of HVR2 across marine and freshwater SAR11 clades, and the existence of a shared pool of HVR2 sequences that evolve reticulately through mutual genetic exchange, independent of the vertical inheritance of the rest of the genome.

papers.title: Long-range regulatory sequence models reveal a phylogenetic boundary in vertebrate genome evolution
papers.abstract: Regulatory activity at a locus depends on local sequence and on long-range interactions with sequence further away, but how long each kind of information stays shared between genomes over evolution is unknown. Here we use sequence-to-function models as a comparative assay, training FunFormer, a long-context binary classifier that reads 20 kb, together with an architecture- and parameter-matched control that reads only the central 1 kb, in six vertebrates spanning 435 million years, and measuring what each retains when applied to another genome. Within species, the long-context model outperformed three published 1 kb classifiers by 1.0 to 3.8 percentage points in every genome, a gain that came from context rather than architecture. Across species, its contribution decayed with divergence, was near zero at the amniote split and reversed between 320 and 435 Mya, while local sequence still transferred into fish. Zebrafish and Atlantic salmon, which share their divergence from tetrapods but differ by the salmonid genome duplication, behaved alike, so the reversal is not explained by the salmonid duplication. An in silico flank intervention showed that replacing the flank with GC-matched sequence from the target genome cost 8 percentage points among mammals. When a mammalian model was applied to fish, a flank drawn from the source genome on average performed as well as the target's own flank, so the model drew nothing from the fish flank that an arbitrary source-genome flank did not provide. The long-range information that these models learn therefore stops being shared between vertebrate genomes well before the local information does. The same boundary sets a practical rule for reusing models in species without their own data, where long context helps among close relatives but is a liability across deep splits, and in variant scoring most foreign models matched a native model in data-limited pig but none did in human.

papers.title: Competing routes back to firing shape population hyperexcitability and its selective suppression
papers.abstract: Whether a neuron will fire again is fundamentally a different question from whether a quiescent neuron will activate. Even within the same neuron, successive spikes can follow distinct post-spike trajectories, with after-depolarization permitting early return to firing and depolarization block prolonging inactivity. Therefore, we propose that hyperexcitability involves changes in the opportunities to fire again across the spike cycle, and not just from quiescence. The firing hazard makes these opportunities measurable: in whole-cell recordings of midbrain dopamine neurons, the subthreshold voltage trough resolves a non-monotone aggregate firing hazard into physiologically distinguishable components. We represent these components as competing return pathways within a population renewal model and show that they lead to heterogeneous firing patterns within a single neuronal population subject to a common drive. An immediate-return pathway provides an early opportunity to fire by skipping some stages of recovery, and promotes population hyperexcitability independent of quiescent activation. Conversely, a sequestration pathway diverts recently active neurons into a prolonged non-recruitable state, representing depolarization block or use-dependent blockade. Pharmacological selectivity of anti-seizure medications such as phenytoin and carbamazepine arises from the redistribution of neurons among return pathways at every renewal, with fast-cycling pathological regimes providing more opportunities for renewal and eventual sequestration.

papers.title: Historical adaptation to transposable element invasions in Drosophila is primarily due to insertions in existing piRNA clusters
papers.abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) are genomic parasites that shift between host species, which may allow them to escape sequence-specific host silencing mechanisms. One such silencing mechanism, the piRNA pathway, is the main line of defense in the germline of animals, and acts through small RNAs targeting specific TE sequences. Though many mechanistic details of this pathway are known, how it evolves to respond to a new transposable element invasion is not. Here, we examine the piRNA-based response to three recently invading TEs in Drosophila simulans, the P-element, Shellder and Spoink. To this end, we assembled genomes of 22 strains, annotated piRNA-producing loci (piRNA clusters) in each strain, and located insertions of the new TEs within these loci. We find that piRNA clusters are highly polymorphic among strains and piRNAs targeting the new TEs come mostly from clusters that likely pre-date the invasions, though there is also some evidence of piRNAs generated de novo, particularly for the long-terminal repeat (LTR) elements. Moreover, resistance to each TE appears to have evolved mostly independently in the different strains through distinct insertions, often in different clusters, although some loci, such as flamenco for Shellder, are recurrent targets.

papers.title: Effect of Lactobacillus postbiotic supplementation on intestinal permeability, nutrient digestibility, and gut microbial and metabolic profiles in aging cats
papers.abstract: Aging in cats is associated with declining nutrient digestibility and increased intestinal permeability, but evidence supporting microbiome-targeted interventions in older cats remains limited. We investigated whether daily supplementation with the Lactobacillus-derived postbiotic LB fermentate HF (LBHF) affected intestinal permeability, apparent total tract digestibility, gut microbiome composition, and fecal and plasma metabolomic profiles in older cats. Twenty cats aged 7.7-13.8 years were enrolled in a blinded, placebo-controlled crossover trial comprising two 29-day treatment periods separated by a 28-day washout; 18 cats completed both periods. Intestinal permeability was the primary endpoint, while nutrient digestibility, microbiome composition, and metabolomic profiles were secondary endpoints. LBHF did not affect intestinal permeability or absorptive capacity relative to placebo, although intestinal permeability was positively associated with age. Overall nutrient digestibility was higher during LBHF treatment, with the clearest endpoint-specific evidence observed for protein digestibility. LBHF was associated with a non-significant overall increase in Shannon diversity and a reduction in the relative abundance of Streptococcus lutetiensis. The increase in Shannon diversity was significant only in cats receiving placebo followed by LBHF, indicating a treatment-sequence-dependent response. Thirty-three plasma and 29 fecal metabolites showed significantly different changes during LBHF treatment compared with placebo. Plasma metabolites generally showed more positive changes during LBHF treatment, whereas most associated fecal metabolites showed more negative changes. Sequence-stratified microbiome and metabolome responses differed substantially, suggesting possible period, treatment-order, or carryover effects. Overall, LBHF did not improve intestinal permeability but was well tolerated and improved nutrient digestibility, particularly protein digestibility, while producing modest and sequence-dependent microbiome and metabolome responses. These findings suggest that the effects of LBHF in healthy older cats may relate more strongly to digestive efficiency and host metabolic responses than to intestinal permeability.

papers.title: Deep CyTOF immune profiles of ex vivo granulomatous responses to Mycobacterium tuberculosis differ with European and African geographical origin
papers.abstract: Genetic and environmental factors influence human immunity and modulate responses to infection. Accounting for immune heterogeneity across human populations is critical to the design of novel vaccines and host-directed interventions that would optimally benefit populations experiencing the highest disease burden. Tuberculosis (TB) burden is unevenly distributed across geographical regions and our understanding of the differential immune response to Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) across human populations remains limited. Here, we sought to evaluate the impact of geographical origin on ex vivo granulomatous responses to Mtbinfection. We found that peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy African donors exhibited greater control of Mtbgrowth ex vivo than those isolated from European individuals. High-dimensional single-cell profiling of the granulomatous responses by cytometry by time-of-flight (CyTOF) revealed divergent profiles based on the specimens' geographical origin. Monocytes from European donors displayed a pro-inflammatory phenotype - correlating with Mtbgrowth -, whereas PBMCs of African individuals were enriched in activated, cytotoxic T cells - correlating with Mtbcontrol. Reduced inflammatory response in African monocytes following various microbial stimulations was confirmed. Taken together, our comprehensive immune profiling indicates that environmental and genetic factors shape a cytotoxic-regulatory response that promotes bacterial control. Against the current "one-treatment-fits-all" approach, our findings support the use of specimens from intervention-relevant settings to inform the targeted design of TB vaccines and host-directed interventions.

papers.title: Multiple adaptive trajectories shape antimalarial resistance evolution in Ethiopian Plasmodium falciparum
papers.abstract: Plasmodium falciparum malaria continues to impose a substantial public health burden across sub-Saharan Africa, with Ethiopia experiencing a recent resurgence in malaria cases. We analysed whole genome data from 120 P. falciparum isolates collected in 2024 across five ecologically and epidemiologically diverse transmission settings in Ethiopia and placed these in the context of 1,220 publicly available genomes. Parasite populations were highly structured within Ethiopia, while Horn of Africa isolates formed a genetically distinct regional cluster relative to East and West African populations. We identified evidence of recent positive selection surrounding the artemisinin resistance associated PfK13 R622I variant and detected co-occurrence with Pfcrt mutations together with recurrent selection signals at genes within the PfK13-associated haemoglobin endocytosis pathway, including Pfmca2, Pfkic7, Pfkic8 and Pfkic9. We further observed the emergence of the PfPX1 D384A-PIN haplotype, with shared identity-by-descent linking Ethiopian and Ugandan carriers, supporting a recent introduction followed by local selection. Widespread Pfhrp2/3 deletions occurred on diverse genetic backgrounds. Together, these findings reveal a complex adaptive landscape shaped by antimalarial and diagnostic selection pressures and suggest that parasite evolution in the Horn of Africa proceeds through multiple adaptive trajectories, rather than through the spread of a single dominant lineage.

papers.title: The structure and evolution of sex chromosomes in an androdioecious species with two mating types.
papers.abstract: Though flowering plants are ancestrally hermaphroditic, some species have evolved sexual specialization and are now composed of individuals expressing just one of their two reproductive functions (either male or female) together with co-sexual individuals. Androdioecy, the co-existence of males with hermaphrodites, is rare across the living world, but unusually common in species of the Oleaceae plant family. The mediterranean shrub Phillyrea angustifolia has a simple mendelian XY sex-determination system for androdioecy, but the underlying molecular determinants and the evolutionary history of the X and Y chromosomes remain unknown. The ability of males to by-pass the self-incompatibility phenotype expressed in hermaphrodites is essential to explain their high frequency in natural populations, but how the loci governing sex and self-incompatibility epistatically interact also remains unknown. To address these questions, we obtained full haplotype-resolved de novo chromosomal assemblies of P. angustifolia and its sister species P. latifolia. The sex-determining region in P. angustifolia spanned a fifth of chromosome 12, and was strikingly larger and more rearranged than that in P. latifolia. The male-specific region contains two putative sex-determining genes, ANDY1 and ANDY2, a tandem encoding two flowering-related transcription factors that arose by translocation followed by duplication of an autosomal gene before the two species diverged. Strikingly, this sex-determining region also contains a recent duplicate of the pollen allergen gene Ole-e1, which shows the strongest differential expression between the two self-incompatibility groups of hermaphrodites, hence establishing a direct molecular link between sex and self-incompatibility. Overall, our results provide novel insight on sex determination and the evolution of sex chromosomes in a plant lineage where the separation between sexes is still incomplete, and offer a possible mechanistic basis for the strong epistatic interaction between the sex and self-incompatibility determinants, with direct implication for how sex-ratios are established in nature.

papers.title: Gene-resolved metagenomics reveals partitioned nitrogen transformation potential in a landfill leachate sequencing batch reactor microbiome
papers.abstract: Landfill leachate can contain high concentrations of ammonia and organic nitrogen requiring treatment before discharge. Sequencing batch reactors (SBRs) promote biological nitrogen removal through alternating aerobic and anoxic conditions, but taxonomic profiling alone cannot resolve how nitrogen transformation and competing retention pathways are distributed across microbial communities. This study applied gene-resolved metagenomics to a sludge sample collected from a UK landfill leachate SBR. Nitrogen-metabolism genes were linked to contig-level taxonomic assignments and metagenome-assembled genome bins to examine nitrification, denitrification, dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA), and assimilatory nitrate reduction (ANR). Nitrogen-transformation potential was partitioned across dominant and minor taxa. Nitrospirota and Pseudomonadota were the most abundant classified phyla, whereas Actinomycetota represented only 4% of the community but included Actinomycetes, which showed the highest within-taxon proportion of nitrogen metabolism associated genes. amoABC was assigned only to Nitrosomonas and Nitrososphaerota, whereas denitrification genes were more widely distributed but frequently occurred as partial pathways. nosZ was detected only in the minor phyla Chloroflexota, Acidobacteriota and Myxococcota. DNRA and ANR-associated genes occurred across multiple lineages; nirA in Nitrospira and DNRA-associated nirBD elsewhere within Nitrospirota suggested nitrifier-associated lineages may also encode nitrogen retention potential. Gene-resolved metagenomics identified candidate low-abundance contributors, restricted distributions of genes associated with ammonia oxidation and nitrous oxide reduction, and nitrogen-retention potential not apparent from taxonomic composition alone. Because the study examined DNA-level potential in a single sludge sample, expression, reactor chemistry and longitudinal data are needed to establish pathway activity and operational relevance.

papers.title: Formation of perinuclear actin structures is driven by mechanosensitivity of actin polymerization
papers.abstract: Actin filaments are one of the most dynamic components of the cytoskeleton. Their fast polymerization, particularly in regions around the nucleus, allows the cell to react quickly and efficiently to external mechanical stimuli by controling nucleus morphology and position, thereby influencing the chromatin organization and gene transcription. While the biochemical mechanisms of actin polymerization are well known, the question why polymerization happens most prominently in the perinuclear region has so far remained elusive. Here, we develop a computational model for actin network formation whose key ingredients are: (i) a fully resolved orientational distribution of the local filaments, (ii) a strain-dependent depolymerization rate and (iii) active stress generation by actomyosin motors. With only these ingredients and without any ad-hoc assumptions on the spatial distribution of signaling molecules, our physics-based model explains the formation of perinuclear actin structures after mechanical stimulation as observed experimentally. In addition, our model also provides some insight into the role actin plays in positioning the nucleus, as it predicts the occurrence of a re-centering force when the cell nucleus is displaced, in quantitative agreement with experimental observations.

papers.title: Computational model of developmental self-assembly of a cortical microcircuit
papers.abstract: Cortical microcircuits emerge from local developmental interactions, yet large-scale computational models typically prescribe connectivity rather than explain its formation. Here we use BioDynaMo to simulate the self-assembly of ~70,000 cortical neurons from 1,200 progenitors in 3D physical space through migration, neurite growth and contact-based synapse formation. With one calibrated filling fraction per connection type, the locally formed synapses reproduce experimentally measured connectivity across 64 connection types (mean absolute error 0.0062) without prescribing individual connections. The grown spiking networks sustain stable, inhibition-dominated activity, and the same developmental rules, given different targets, generate both a canonical cortical microcircuit and a visual-cortex variant. Inverting the migration programme produces a reeler-like column whose aberrant connectivity destabilises network activity. Together, these findings provide a mechanistic link between local developmental processes and the emergence of cortical anatomy, connectivity and function.

papers.title: Comparative larval single-cell transcriptomics provides insights into the evolutionary origins of sensory-neural programmes in Porifera and Cnidaria
papers.abstract: Understanding how specialised cell types emerged and diversified is fundamental to reconstructing animal evolution. The origins of neural and sensory-secretory cell types are particularly intriguing, and early diverging non-neuronal metazoans, such as sponges, provide critical insights into pre-neural molecular toolkits. Free-swimming larval stages of sponges and cnidarians provide an unique context for investigating these questions, as these larvae rely on specialised sensory and signalling systems to detect environmental cues and coordinate behaviour during dispersal and settlement. Here, we integrated larval single-cell transcriptomic datasets from the demosponge Amphimedon queenslandica and four cnidarian species (Nematostella vectensis, Astroides calycularis, Pocillopora acuta and Clytia hemisphaerica). Cross-species mapping using Self-Assembling Manifold mapping (SAMap) recovered broad conservation of major cell-type identities among cnidarians, including neural, secretory, cnidocyte, epithelial, gastrodermal and apical populations. Extending these comparisons to A. queenslandica displayed transcriptional similarities between several sponge larval cell populations and cnidarian neural, sensory and progenitor-associated cell types. Within-species analyses showed that these cell populations remained transcriptionally integrated within the broader epithelial and sensory cell type of the sponge larva. Neural-associated gene modules, including conserved families associated with photoreception, neural fate specification and postsynaptic scaffolding, were distributed across distinct epithelial and sensory-like sponge larval cell populations rather than being restricted to a single proto-neural cell type. Our findings suggest that molecular components subsequently incorporated into neural systems were already deployed across diverse cell types in a common ancestor of sponges & cnidarians. Our work supports an evolutionary scenario in which extant neural and sensory-secretory cell types arose through the diversification and reorganisation of molecular programmes distributed across multiple ancestral sensory-secretory cell types.

papers.title: Early visual experience redistributes cFos-tagged neurons toward the cortex while preserving presynaptic spatial stereotypy
papers.abstract: The macroscale functional organization of the brain is spatially stereotyped across individuals, but whether this extends to finer spatial scales is not known. Furthermore, how experience shapes this organization across the brain remains unclear. To address this, we developed cFos promoter-driven reporter mouse lines that permanently label either the cell bodies or presynaptic terminals of neurons during defined temporal windows. Using serial two-photon tomography and voxel-wise statistics, we mapped brain-wide distributions of cFos-tagged somata or their presynaptic terminals during the first week of visual experience or its deprivation. We found that midbrain and subcortical regions show greater stereotypy for cFos-tagged neurons and their presynaptic terminals compared to cortical regions. This fine-scale spatial stereotypy remained largely preserved despite visual deprivation, which shifted the relative recruitment of cFos-tagged neurons from cortical toward the highly stereotyped midbrain and subcortical regions. Our findings identify heterogeneous, spatially constrained functional organization across the brain that is conserved across subjects yet accommodates experience-dependent reorganization of neuronal recruitment.

papers.title: Geometry-Conditioned Hyperalignment for Generalizable EEG Decoding Across Datasets and Paradigms
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) supports promising applications, but daily use remains limited by poor cross-subject and cross-dataset generalisation. That is because EEG recordings made with different electrode montages do not even share an observation space, and each subjects's leadfield projects the same neural sources onto the scalp differently. We present hTSMNet, which combines a novel geometry-conditioned hyperalignment frontend with a Riemannian symmetric positive-definite (SPD) manifold backbone that reduces the residual cross-subject distribution shift. From electrode coordinates alone, the frontend builds a linear map from any montage onto a fixed set of scalp anchors, placing every recording in one shared space. Because this map has no subjectspecific parameters, an unseen subject, dataset, or montage is aligned from its geometry alone, so transfer is zero-shot by construction. On a leave-one-dataset-out left-/right-hand motor-imagery (MI) benchmark across three datasets (172 subjects) and eight comparators, hTSMNet matches the strongest comparator at strict zero-shot, and attains the highest accuracy on every dataset once a few calibration trials for adjusting only final-layer classifier are available. We show that it orients the binary decision the same way in every dataset, so that a single linear rule learned on the source data is already correctly oriented on a held-out one. The same frozen MI-pretrained model also transfers across paradigms: with only a re-fit final-layer classifier, hTSMNet decodes mental workload and steady-state visual evoked potentials (SSVEP) well above chance, yet remains at chance on stimulus-locked event-related potentials (ERP). This dissociation follows from the architecture: covariance pooling reads oscillatory band power and is largely insensitive to the phase-locked potentials that ERP tasks depend on. What the representation generalizes is a signal family (band-limited oscillatory activity), not the named task. Geometry-conditioned hyperalignment thus yields an inspectable representation, which is generalizable across datasets and, within the oscillatory regime, across paradigms.

papers.title: Structure-based discovery of new GPR119 ligands from on-demand tera-scale chemical space
papers.abstract: The orphan G protein-coupled receptor GPR119 is involved in glucose homeostasis and is considered a promising target for the treatment of diabetes and other metabolic diseases. The recently solved structures of GPR119 in complex with potential endogenous lipid agonists, including oleoylethanolamide (OEA), provide a solid platform for 3D pharmacology analysis and structure-based ligand discovery. Here, we employed the V-SYNTHES2 approach to screen ~3 trillion on-demand compounds from Enamine xREAL chemical space to identify several new chemotypes of GPR119 agonists and antagonists. Structure-guided analog-by-catalog hit expansion of new chemotypes and stereoselective synthesis resulted in a series of full and partial agonists with low-micromolar potencies in functional assays. Cryo-EM structures of active GPR119-Gs complexes bound to three of the hits validated the docking predictions and established further SAR insights into ligand-receptor interactions, enabling the discovery of BRI-17403 and BRI-17409 agonists with EC50 values of 1.6 M and 1.3 M, respectively. These results demonstrate the utility of structure-based screening of tera-scale on-demand chemical spaces in accelerating drug discovery for therapeutically relevant orphan GPCRs.

papers.title: HV-MultiScaleGNN: A Multi-Scale Graph Neural Network Framework for Host-Virus Protein-Protein Interactions Prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of HV-PPIs is essential for understanding viral infection mechanisms and for developing antiviral therapeutic discovery. However, the experimental identification process is often time-consuming and expensive, while many computational approaches depend on incomplete protein sequences, structural and interaction information. Here, we present HV-MultiScaleGNN, a topology-driven multi-scale GNN framework for HV-PPIs prediction that operates exclusively on the topology of a heterogeneous interaction network. The framework formulates HV-PPIs prediction as a heterogeneous link prediction problem by integrating the human interactome with experimentally validated HV-PPIs. HV-MultiScaleGNN systematically investigates three complementary graph representation strategies, viz. Local view, Global view and an integrated Local+Global view. The Local view employs one-hop relation-aware graph attention to model fine-grained neighbourhood interactions. The Global view captures higher-order structural dependencies through propagation-based neighbourhood aggregation. The integrated representation combines both views to jointly encode local connectivity and global topological context within a unified embedding space, enabling relation-specific link prediction without relying on sequence- or structure-derived features. Experiments on large-scale HV-PPIs datasets evaluate all three strategies using discrimination, calibration, and ranking metrics. The Local view achieved the best discriminative performance (AUROC = 0.9444, AUPRC = 0.9422), whereas the Global view exhibited the lowest ECE (0.0379). The integrated Local+Global view provided consistently strong predictive performance (AUROC = 0.9378, AUPRC = 0.9356). Comparative evaluation against representative graph representation learning methods showed competitive predictive performance. Furthermore, interfacial interactions were identified using protein-protein docking and atomistic-level understanding was explored. Moreover, GO and KEGG enrichment provided additional functional insights into the selected host proteins. The proposed framework enables systematic evaluation of complementary graph representation strategies for heterogeneous biological link prediction and helps experimental researchers to delineate novel HV-PPIs.

papers.title: Nuclear retention and RNA editing safeguard self-tolerance to immunogenic intron lariats
papers.abstract: Introns are excised as lariats and rapidly degraded upon linearization, leaving their post-splicing role unclear. Here, we investigate their immunoregulatory potential by analyzing the intron lariat landscape upon inhibition of the debranching enzyme DBR1. We find that lariats harboring transposable elements (TEs), especially inverted Alu repeats (IRAlus), elicit cell cycle-dependent activation of protein kinase R (PKR), but only in cells harboring a high burden, such as breast cancer. These immunogenic lariats are initially retained in the nucleus, but upon cytosolic release, they drive PKR activation and apoptosis. Exploiting this, we combine DBR1 depletion with anti-mitotic chemotherapy to enhance lariat-PKR interactions and promote cancer cell death in vitro and in vivo. We further show that A-to-I editing of IRAlus-containing lariats weakens their interaction with PKR and suppresses PKR activation. Our findings highlight two parallel molecular mechanisms to sustain self-tolerance to repeat-rich introns, revealing a vulnerability exploitable for anti-tumor therapy.

papers.title: Spatial proteomics on repurposed sequencers reveals early astrocytic remodeling in an ALS mouse model
papers.abstract: Spatial proteomics can reveal how disease reshapes cells and their local environments, but extending these measurements across replicated tissue cohorts requires validated antibodies, consistent sample processing and integrated analysis. These requirements are particularly pressing in studies of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), where pathology evolves unevenly across spinal-cord regions and disease stages. Here, we established an end-to-end spatial proteomics workflow linking a validated 28-antibody panel to automated fluorescence decoding and imaging on repurposed high-throughput sequencers, followed by multicycle image processing, cellular profiling and probabilistic spatial-neighborhood analysis. We applied it to 70 lumbar spinal-cord sections from nine SOD1-G93A and nine wild-type mice at presymptomatic, disease-onset and symptomatic stages. Spatial neighborhood analysis revealed that the environments surrounding motor neurons were already remodeled at disease onset. GFAP-high neighborhoods expanded in the ventral gray matter, with 43% of motor neurons embedded in these environments in SOD1-G93A mice, compared with 15% in wild-type mice. This early expansion preceded the later decline of non-reactive gray matter and detectable motor-neuron loss. The regional organization of the protein-defined changes shared features with neuronal and astrocytic patterns mapped by spatial transcriptomics in mouse and human ALS. This work enables spatial proteomics across replicated tissue cohorts and identifies localized remodeling of the environments around surviving motor neurons as an early feature of disease in the SOD1-G93A model.

papers.title: Viral replication and host response in airway epithelial cells predicts coronavirus pathogenicity and identifies HCoV-229E as an atypical seasonal coronavirus
papers.abstract: Human coronaviruses (HCoVs) range from mild seasonal strains to pathogenic viruses that cause severe pneumonia. The virological and host determinants that distinguish pathogenic coronaviruses (MERS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2) from seasonal strains (HCoV-229E, HCoV-NL63 and HCoV-OC43) remain poorly defined. To identify determinants of pathogenicity, we systematically compared replication, cellular tropism, innate responses and cytopathogenicity of pathogenic compared with seasonal HCoVs across nasal, bronchial, small airway and embryonic stem cell derived alveolar type II (AT2) epithelial cell cultures. All HCoVs preferentially infected ciliated cells in the upper airway, but only pathogenic viruses replicated to high titres in AT2 cells. Pathogenic HCoVs reprogrammed AT2 function and suppressed key innate immune signatures, consistent with distal lung epithelial dysfunction. In contrast, seasonal HCoVs were associated with limited alveolar replication and milder disruption of AT2 homeostasis. Strikingly, despite modest replication in all cell types, HCoV-229E induced pronounced epithelial injury, cilia loss and strong interferon stimulated gene expression, as well as induction of cellular stress/death programmes resembling those induced by MERS-CoV. These findings highlight the striking differences in cellular responses throughout the airways and between distinct HCoV strains and emphasizes the importance of assessing distal lung tropism and epithelial host responses to evaluate emergent coronaviruses to inform pandemic preparedness strategies.

papers.title: Structural basis of virion assembly in the Mycobacterium tuberculosis-infecting mycobacteriophage SWU1
papers.abstract: The rising threat of drug-resistant tuberculosis has renewed interest in bacteriophage therapy as an urgently needed alternative. Rational engineering of these viruses, however, requires an atomic-level understanding of virion architecture. Mycobacteriophage SWU1 belongs to subcluster A2, one of the few mycobacteriophage lineages known to infect Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M. tuberculosis). Using single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM), we resolved essentially the entire SWU1 virion architecture by localized reconstruction of four modules, the capsid, portal vertex, tail and baseplate, at resolutions of 3.62 [A], 3.51 [A], 3.70 [A] and 3.22 [A], respectively. The T=7 capsid comprises 415 copies of an HK97-fold major capsid protein and lacks any decoration protein in density. The 12-fold portal reconciles its C5-C12 mismatch with the capsid vertex through defined, non-equivalent subunit contacts. The baseplate carries a 13-fold tail-fiber ring on a 6-fold hub, a geometry without precedent among characterized phages, established here by symmetry-free reconstruction. These findings provide the critical insights into the assembly and infection of SWU1, laying a structural foundation for the future optimization of phage-based anti-TB therapeutics.

papers.title: A distinct chondrogenic progenitor population from human umbilical cord derived mesenchymal stromal cells for osteoarthritis therapy
papers.abstract: Stem cell-based cartilage regeneration remains constrained by functional heterogeneity and phenotypic drift in conventional cell sources, compromising durable structural repair. Human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (UC-MSCs) represent an accessible, off-the-shelf cell source; however, their broad clinical utility is hampered by cellular heterogeneity, leaving the key chondrogenic subpopulation responsible for cartilage repair unresolved. By integrating single-cell transcriptomics with functional assays, we identified and prospectively isolated a distinct, highly expandable subpopulation of skeletal stem cell-like progenitors (U-CPCs) from the human umbilical cord, establishing an extra-skeletal cell source uniquely primed for joint restoration. Single-cell transcriptomics reveal their inherent regulatory landscape, uncovering a distinct transcriptional state uniquely primed for chondrogenesis. In comparison with conventional stem cells and other tissue-derived SSC-like populations (from umbilical cord, bone marrow, adipose tissue, and dental pulp), U-CPCs exhibit a markedly enhanced chondrogenic capacity. In both a mouse cartilage injury model and a rat osteoarthritis model, the administration of U-CPCs effectively mitigates joint degeneration and drives the restoration of a structurally sound, hyaline-like matrix. Mechanistically, U-CPCs secrete extracellular vesicles enriched with microRNA Let-7a-5p, which specifically modulates DUSP7/MAPK/ERK signaling in recipient chondrocytes, thereby restoring extracellular matrix homeostasis and promoting cartilage repair. By characterizing these specialized extra-skeletal progenitors and elucidating both their intrinsic chondrogenic priming and paracrine regulation of host tissue, this study establishes U-CPCs as a robust, lineage-restricted cellular source for osteoarthritis therapy.

papers.title: Reticulation-Aware Dissimilarities for Phylogenetic Networks
papers.abstract: Dissimilarity measures play a critical role in phylogenetics. They help quantify the accuracy of inferences when the ground truth is known, allow comparisons of inferences obtained using different methods, and provide a tool for summarizing sets of phylogenies. A wide array of dissimilarity measures has been introduced for phylogenetic trees over the past half-century, and they vary in their mathematical properties, empirical behavior, and computational complexity. When the evolutionary history involves reticulate processes, such as hybridization and horizontal gene transfer, it is represented by phylogenetic networks. Although the study of phylogenetic network dissimilarity is less established than its tree counterpart, the past two decades have seen an increasing number of measures developed for phylogenetic networks. However, while some have established mathematical properties---for example, metricity on certain classes of phylogenetic networks---none properly separates reticulation disagreement from tree-like disagreement. This is the rationale behind the introduction of the hybrid ancestry error (HAE) measure by Dai and Molloy. The HAE measure, however, is too simplistic to distinguish different reticulation scenarios. In this work, we propose a novel family of network dissimilarity measures that explicitly account for reticulation differences while being more informative than HAE. We prove that our measures are pseudometrics on rooted binary phylogenetic networks on a fixed taxon set, with two instantiations yielding metrics on binary level-1 networks. Empirically, the measures remain sensitive to reticulation errors as network size grows and respond to changes in hybrid identity and parental placement. Calibration experiments further characterize the measures' behavior under network edits of various magnitudes. Data Availability: The dissimilarities are implemented in the PhyNetPy library, available at https://github.com/NakhlehLab/PhyNetPy. All the data simulated for the study is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23933421. Funding: This work was supported in part by the NSF grants DMS/NIGMS-2153704 and DBI-2420499. Declaration of AI-assisted technologies: During the preparation of this work, the authors used OpenAI's Codex (GPT-6 Astra) and Anthropic's Claude (Fable 5) to assist with editing manuscript text, developing proofs and analysis code, and preparing figures. The authors reviewed and edited the resulting material, verified the analyses, and take full responsibility for the content of this article.

papers.title: Evidence-based re-identification: Leveraging appearance cues to correct tracking mistakes rather than trying to prevent them
papers.abstract: Naturalistic behavioral neuroscience experiments, in which groups of animals interact in enriched environments over prolonged periods, require each animal's identity to remain correct throughout the recording. Current multi-animal tracking tools assign identities frame by frame without revisiting past assignment decisions. A single, even sporadic, identity swap is therefore likely to persist until the end of the recording. Consequently, error-free tracking results become progressively less likely as recordings lengthen and cohorts grow. Even state-of-the-art multi-object tracking (MOT) methods that leverage appearance cues do so only to make each assignment more robust. This robustness, however, only delays the inevitable as even the most robust assignment process will eventually make a mistake over prolonged recordings. A mistake that will then persist just as it otherwise would have. Here, we introduce evidence-based re-identification, which uses appearance cues to correct tracking mistakes rather than prevent them. This fundamental shift allows the algorithm to build and progressively enrich appearance representations for each tracked subject. Tracking mistakes are then detected by continuously monitoring the evolution of these representations, triggering a correction whenever two representations drift toward one another in a sustained way. On two distinct, minutes-long benchmarks of mice interacting in enriched environments, motion-only trackers (DeepLabCut, SLEAP, ByteTrack) and the appearance-based BoT-SORT-ReID began accumulating identity errors within seconds, whereas ByteTrack paired with evidence-based re-identification remained reliable, outperforming even ByteTrack paired with the marker-based Tailtag system. This reliability was also positively correlated with the accuracy of the appearance extractor, but only when it was used through evidence-based re-identification. Foundation image encoders (CLIP, MegaDescriptor, DINOv3) showed promising out-of-the-box performance yet still required fine-tuning to be effective. Together, these results show that multi-animal tracking algorithms can remain reliable over prolonged periods only if they can reliably recover from tracking mistakes, and that fine-tuning appearance extractors remains essential to doing so.

papers.title: Genomes2Genes: A Progressive Cactus Gene Analysis Pipeline
papers.abstract: Whole-genome alignments are fundamental resources in comparative genomics, because they place genes and their surrounding sequences in a shared evolutionary context. Progressive Cactus aligns large numbers of genomes without a reference genome and reconstructs ancestral sequences along the input phylogeny. However, its Hierarchical Alignment Format output has mainly been used for visualization, phylogenomics, and pangenome studies, and gene-level analyses of these alignments remain difficult. Here, we present Genomes2Genes, a pipeline that converts Progressive Cactus graph-based alignments into validated coding sequence alignments of extant species and their reconstructed ancestors. The pipeline extracts exon alignment blocks, handles atypical genomic jumps, stitches exons into transcripts, and reports start codons, stop codons, and frameshifting indels across species, with validation steps throughout and a base-by-base audit of the final alignments. It catches both biological and technical artifacts and can be run on any part of the genome. We anticipate that this pipeline will be useful in identifying and removing problematic regions used in the potential reconstruction of species or gene phylogenies. We developed and tested the pipeline on a whole-genome alignment of 21 Brassicaceae species and 2 outgroups and found that, among 45,491 lineage-specific genes, the pipeline supported 22,376 candidate de novo genes, of which 1,811 had complete evidence of enabler mutations. Genomes2Genes is publicly available and extends whole-genome alignments to gene-level questions in comparative genomics and evolutionary biology.

papers.title: Working memory capacity is linked to directed exploration: behavioral, computational, and electrophysiological evidence
papers.abstract: Balancing the exploitation of known rewards against the exploration of uncertain options is central to adaptive decision making, yet the cognitive limits on strategic exploration are poorly understood. Directed exploration, the deliberate sampling of uncertain options for information, may depend on working memory (WM), but whether WM capacity (WMC) is selectively related to it, and through which processes, is unknown. 52 participants from the upper and lower tails of an operation-span distribution (26 high-WMC, 26 low-WMC) performed an adapted Horizon Task during EEG recording. We combined behavioral strategy classification, hierarchical Bayesian reinforcement learning, stimulus-locked event-related potentials (ERPs), and an exploratory Bayesian mediation analysis. High-WMC participants showed more directed exploration and less exploitation, with no group difference in random exploration.
