A model in which accumulated sampling history discounts option value best explained choices in both groups, and the discounting parameter {omega} was larger in the high-WMC group. Statistically, {omega} accounted for the association between WMC and directed exploration (indirect effect ab = 0.64, 95% CrI [0.28, 1.05]). Frontocentral P2 amplitude (180 to 280 ms) during directed exploration was larger in the high-WMC group, and the P2 difference between directed exploration and exploitation correlated with behavioral preference for directed exploration (r = .29, p = .040). These findings suggest that individual differences in exploration may reflect not only the willingness to seek information but also the capacity to use what has been sampled. The WMC-related difference lay in information use rather than choice noise and was already visible in early option evaluation.

papers.title: Lateral Membrane Heterogeneity Shapes Antimicrobial Association and Convergent Mechanical Responses
papers.abstract: Bacterial membranes are laterally heterogeneous, creating local physicochemical environments that can shape interactions with membrane-active antimicrobials. However, whether this spatial organization only affects local drug association or propagates into collective membrane responses remains unclear. Here we show that lateral membrane heterogeneity shapes antimicrobial association while distinct molecular responses converge on a common loss of membrane mechanical stability. Combining coarse-grained molecular dynamics, giant unilamellar vesicle fluctuation spectroscopy and microfluidic trapping, we follow octenidine, chlorhexidine and polymyxin B from molecular association to vesicle-scale behaviour. All three compounds preferentially associate with domain-associated membrane environments, but differ in how this preference changes with loading and in their effects on lipid mobility. Despite these differences, all three shift the membrane toward a mechanically softer state, while increasing exposure accelerates loss of vesicle stability under flow. These findings identify lateral membrane heterogeneity as an active determinant of antimicrobial response and provide a physical framework for understanding membrane-targeting activity beyond bulk composition and membrane-averaged charge.

papers.title: Inductive bias anchors a scaling law for biological learning
papers.abstract: The speed of animal learning varies substantially across individuals and task domains, and does not always track intuitive notions of task complexity. A nominally simple binary decision task can take thousands of rewards to reach proficiency, whereas seemingly complex naturalistic tasks can be learned within dozens. A long-standing explanation is that learning speed reflects the alignment between an animal's inductive biases and the task at hand. However, without a precise notion of alignment, it is difficult to translate this idea into quantitative predictions. Here, modeling an animal as a Bayesian learner that improves through iterative reward feedback, we use statistical learning theory to derive a scaling law for biological learning. The law makes two predictions. First, inductive bias multiplicatively sets the speed of learning through a single quantity, the effective complexity. This quantity measures how well the task aligns with the animal's prior, and corresponds to the number of bits required to represent the task solution under that prior. We demonstrate this multiplicative scaling in a human motor learning dataset, where behavioral measurements before learning can precisely predict subsequent learning speed. Second, task performance improves as a power law in experience. We validate this power law in a large-scale mouse learning dataset and show that a two-parameter rescaling collapses individual learning curves onto a universal function predicted by the theory. These results suggest that behavioral measurements before learning can be used to predict task-dependent learning speeds, and they explain why learning speed reflects alignment with prior knowledge rather than nominal task complexity.

papers.title: In situ single-cell CRISPR screens uncover context-dependent rewiring of glioma states and immune recruitment
papers.abstract: In vivo single-cell CRISPR screens can resolve perturbation effects in native tissues, but few combine cell-type-restricted delivery, somatic tumor initiation, and combinatorial perturbation. Here we developed an RCAS-TVA-based single-cell CRISPR screening approach coupling oncogenic transformation with single- or dual-guide perturbation in defined neural progenitors. In glioma, tumor suppressor loss produced distinct genotype-dependent transcriptional states, including an NF1-loss-associated increase in mesenchymal programs. Introducing a fixed Cdkn2a(ARF) perturbation altered malignant-cell state composition, immune-cell abundance, and the effects of additional tumor-suppressor perturbations, including increased representation of Pten- and Rb1-deficient cells, suggestive of the relief of an ARF-dependent genetic barrier. These perturbations converged on transcriptional states resembling pharmacologic p53 activation in human glioblastoma. Across mouse tumors and human glioblastoma models, this response was associated with increased astrocyte-like state representation. These findings establish a framework for single-cell analysis of context-dependent somatic perturbations during tumor initiation in vivo.

papers.title: Capturing continuous spectrotemporal pupil--brain coupling with simultaneous wearable EEG/Eye tracking
papers.abstract: Spontaneous fluctuations in pupil diameter are closely linked to neural dynamics, yet most evidence for pupil--brain coupling has been obtained in conventional laboratory settings. We therefore asked whether the spectrotemporal and directional organization of such coupling can be captured with wearable systems to test their use in naturalistic settings. Using combined lightweight mobile EEG (MUSE) and eye tracking (Tobii Pro Glasses 3) devices, we investigated resting-state pupil--brain coupling and explored interoceptive attention to determine whether the core organizational principles observed with stationary equipment are detectable within and preserved across continuous recording states. Cross-correlation, mutual information, and Granger causality analyses revealed that pupil--brain coupling displayed clear frequency-dependent organization. Lower EEG frequencies (2-12Hz) preceded pupil dynamics by roughly 764ms, while higher frequencies showed a distinct coupling range. Granger-causality analysis further indicated predominantly EEG-to-pupil directional coupling. Similar observations were made during interoception. Overall, these findings align well and extend previous evidence on spontaneous pupil--brain coupling, demonstrating that lightweight and movable wearable devices are suitable to characterize spectrotemporal and directional pupil--brain interactions. In turn, these results encourage future fundamental and translational research in naturalistic environments.

papers.title: Large seed size accompanying GmSDP1 suppression is linked to cellular remodeling and phytohormone regulation
papers.abstract: Soybean (Glycine max) seeds contain approximately 20% oil and 40% protein and are important for food, feed, and biofuel. Improving soybean productivity and seed quality requires optimizing carbon partitioning during seed development. Previously, seed-specific suppression of the lipase-encoding gene Sugar-Dependent 1 (SDP1) increased seed oil content by approximately 5% while slightly reducing raffinose family oligosaccharides without compromising protein content. Seed-specific SDP1 suppression also increased seed size by 18-25% without affecting seed number, resulting in greater seed biomass per plant. To determine the developmental basis of the increased seed size, we investigated the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying this phenotype. Microscopy and biochemical analyses showed that larger seeds were associated with increased seed cell size and enhanced lignocellulosic cell wall accumulation. Temporal biochemical and transcriptomic analyses further revealed coordinated changes in hormone homeostasis, including altered levels of abscisic acid, 12-oxo-phytodienoic acid, and jasmonoyl-isoleucine, together with differential expression of F-box and RING/U-box family genes. The results indicate that the enhanced seed size resulting from SDP1 suppression is associated with coordinated changes in cellular development, cell wall accumulation, hormone homeostasis, and regulation of gene expression during seed development. Developmental and metabolic changes associated with the increased seed size phenotype support SDP1 manipulation as a potential strategy for improving soybean seed yield and quality.

papers.title: OmniT2I: a unified table-to-image framework for survival prediction and cross-modal inference with incomplete multimodal cancer data
papers.abstract: Molecular profiles and histopathology provide complementary information about cancer prognosis, but these data are often incomplete for individual patients. Here we present OmniT2I, a table-to-image framework for survival prediction and cross-modal inference from incomplete multimodal cancer data. Each molecular profile was converted into a three-channel image representation with correlation-based feature placement. OmniT2I combines available molecular and histopathology embeddings through availability-aware fusion and predicts missing modalities from those observed. Across 10,373 patients with 32 cancer types, the C-index was 0.631 within cancer types and 0.783 with all cancers pooled (0.660 and 0.787 in 5,605 patients with all five modalities). A single model handled all 31 modality combinations and, compared with nine survival methods trained separately for each, achieved higher C-indices in 240 of 279 pooled and 226 of 279 within-cancer comparisons. Adding predictions of withheld modalities to observed inputs improved pooled C-indices in all 180 pairings of observed and withheld modality sets and within-cancer C-indices in 164. Adding measured histopathology to RNA produced the largest within-cancer C-index gain among the four additional modalities evaluated, whereas adding copy number variation reduced it. In seven external cohorts, frozen RNA-only C-indices differed from test performance in the corresponding cancer type in TCGA by a median of -0.003 (range, -0.092 to +0.079). OmniT2I enables prognostic modeling with incomplete multimodal data.

papers.title: LingoCell interprets gene perturbations through natural language and tissue niches
papers.abstract: Single-cell foundation models are general tools for resolving cell identities and disease states, but struggle to interpret changes in expression magnitude in biological language, to transfer to sparse spatial measurements, and to explain cellular niches. We introduce LingoCell, a foundation model connecting single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. It aligns cell representations with language while keeping gene expression editable, supporting cell annotation, cross-batch integration, description generation, and disease-language readouts of single-gene and combinatorial in silico perturbations. Extended to tissues, it annotates cells without single-cell references, learns identity-conditioned niche embeddings, and performs spatial in silico perturbation by replacing and editing neighbor expression. In lung adenocarcinoma, LingoCell revealed synergistic disease responses to jointly weakening alveolar differentiation programs and strengthening malignant programs. In colorectal cancer, it revealed different programs conveyed by the same fibroblast state to T cells, macrophages, and tumor cells. LingoCell provides a unified framework for prioritizing target combinations and stromal intervention programs.

papers.title: Pupil size reflects effort but not motor fatigability during a sustained motor task
papers.abstract: Pupil size has been shown to reflect physical effort during brief, discrete motor tasks. It remains unknown whether pupil size similarly scales with effort during sustained repetitive movement, or whether it also reflects the accumulation of motor fatigability, a reduction in motor performance during prolonged movements. In our previous work, sustained maximal tapping induced motor slowing, a subtype of motor fatigability, characterized by decreasing movement speed and associated with increased antagonistic muscle coactivation. Next to these behavioural effects, pupil initially dilated and then gradually decreased over time. Whether this temporal change in pupil size is shaped by physical effort alone or also by motor fatigability remains unclear. Here, we combined a repetitive wrist tapping paradigm with force measurement, electromyography, and pupillometry, and paced participants at three different tapping speeds to dissociate physical effort from motor slowing, which has been shown to be speed-dependent. Fatigability-related motor slowing emerged selectively at the fastest speed. Moreover, we showed that antagonistic muscle coactivation increased more steeply at faster speeds, even in the absence of motor slowing, suggesting it may reflect an early change in motor control. While we found clear evidence that pupil size scaled with overall tapping speed, we did not find evidence that the temporal change of the pupil was pacing-dependent. These findings extend the pupil effort relationship to sustained, dynamic motor tasks and suggest that pupil size is a marker of physical effort but not motor fatigability during sustained repetitive movement.

papers.title: Replication-stress response shapes Leishmania genome plasticity through non-equivalent RAD9 and HUS1 functions.
papers.abstract: Genome plasticity, manifested as gene copy-number variation and mosaic aneuploidy, enables adaptation in Leishmania , yet how genome-surveillance pathways shape this variation remains unclear. Here we show that partial depletion of HUS1 or RAD9, subunits of the conserved 9-1-1 checkpoint clamp, produces opposing replication-stress responses and contrasting patterns of genome remodelling in Leishmania major . During methotrexate selection HUS1 deficiency restricted DHFR-TS amplification and favoured linear amplicons, whereas RAD9 deficiency was associated with extensive circular amplification. This divergence extended to genome-wide scale: HUS1-deficient cells carried fewer but larger candidate rearrangements, whereas RAD9-deficient cells retained a largely wild-type rearrangement burden. These differences were accompanied by distinct HUS1 and RAD9 occupancy profiles around repetitive DNA implicated in gene amplification. Deficiency of either of these factors also resulted in differing effects on aneuploidy. While HUS1-deficient cells showed limited shifts towards chromosome disomy, RAD9-deficient cells exhibited broader chromosome copy-number gains and losses. Together, these findings identify replication-stress surveillance as a determinant of parasite genome plasticity, revealing that perturbing individual subunits of the same checkpoint complex can produce opposing genome-remodelling outcomes and reshape the variation available for adaptation.

papers.title: Preclinical Evaluation of a Novel BOC-Modified Triazoloacridinone (TRA-01AR) in Combination with 5-Fluorouracil in Colorectal Cancer
papers.abstract: 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) remains a cornerstone of colorectal cancer (CRC) therapy, yet its clinical efficacy is limited by resistance, systemic toxicity, and unfavorable pharmacokinetics. Strategies that enhance tumor sensitivity while maintaining tolerability are therefore of considerable interest. Here, we evaluated 5-FU in combination with two triazoloacridinones, C-1305 and a novel BOC-modified derivative, TRA-01AR, using integrated cellular, transcriptomic, bioenergetic, and in vivo approaches. Both compounds induced cytotoxic effects across cancer cell models and produced overlapping but distinct transcriptional responses, primarily affecting DNA replication and cell cycle pathways. Bioenergetic profiling revealed a shift toward oxidative phosphorylation accompanied by reduced glycolysis, indicating modulation of cellular metabolism relevant to chemotherapy response. Interestingly, TRA-01AR exhibited delayed cytotoxicity relative to C-1305, although the underlying mechanism remains to be defined. In vivo, the combination of 5-FU with C-1305 significantly reduced tumor weight in HT-29 xenografts, whereas 5-FU combined with TRA-01AR did not result in a statistically significant reduction compared to 5-FU alone. TRA-01AR was associated with a more favorable systemic profile and increased intratumoral blood flow compared with C-1305. Collectively, these findings indicate that triazoloacridinones modulate transcriptional and metabolic programs relevant to the 5-FU response. While C-1305 demonstrated greater antitumor activity under the tested conditions, TRA-01AR exhibited distinct biological effects, including improved tolerability and vascular modulation. Further studies are required to clarify TRA-01AR's mechanism of action and assess its potential relevance in CRC-specific therapies.

papers.title: Mechanical Fidelity of Fixed-Cell Traction Force Microscopy
papers.abstract: Cellular traction forces contribute to biological processes including cell migration and tissue morphogenesis. Traction force microscopy (TFM) is widely used to quantify these forces in living cells, but it remains unclear how well measurements after fixation reproduce the live-cell state. Here, we systematically evaluated fixation-induced changes by paired comparison of the same cells before and after fixation using different fixation protocols and substrate stiffnesses. Fixation largely preserved the spatial organization and direction of substrate displacements and reconstructed traction fields, whereas displacement, traction, and strain-energy magnitudes showed fixation-dependent changes. Among the protocols tested, glutaraldehyde (GA) provided the closest agreement with live-cell measurements, retaining up to 99% of displacement and traction magnitudes and strain energy. Paraformaldehyde-based protocols caused larger reductions in these quantities while largely preserving their spatial organization. These results show that fixed-cell TFM, particularly with GA fixation under the conditions tested here, can provide measurements close to the live-cell state and offers a practical approach for combining TFM with post-fixation fluorescence imaging in a multi-well workflow.

papers.title: Maternal separation remodels Purkinje cell circuits and impairs cerebellar synaptic plasticity
papers.abstract: Introduction: Early-life adversity has been associated with cerebellar abnormalities, but the cellular and circuit-level changes involved and their persistence across development remain poorly understood. We examined whether maternal separation (MS) disrupts cerebellar circuit maturation and whether these changes are accompanied by alterations in synaptic function and behavior. Methods: CD1 mice underwent daily maternal separation from postnatal day 2 to 18, whereas control litters remained undisturbed. Cerebellar alterations were assessed using transcriptomic and DNA methylation profiling, RT-qPCR, immunoblotting, Purkinje-cell morphometric analysis, and VGLUT1/VGLUT2 immunofluorescence. Patch-clamp electrophysiology was used to examine synaptic transmission and plasticity. Motor coordination, spontaneous locomotion, social approach, and stress-coping behavior were also evaluated. Results: RNA sequencing of whole cerebellar tissue revealed early transcriptional remodeling, involving synaptic transmission, neuronal architecture, and plasticity-related pathways. Consistent with this profile, we found that MS altered Purkinje cell dendritic arborization and excitatory input remodeling, together with deficits in cerebellar long-term synaptic plasticity and reduced BDNF-related signaling. In parallel, methylation analysis revealed hypermethylation of the glucocorticoid receptor promoter and reduced cerebellar receptor expression, indicating that early-life stress also engages stress-related epigenetic mechanisms in this region. Importantly, these neurobiological changes were associated with motor coordination deficits, altered stress-coping behavior, and impaired social interaction. Discussion: These findings identify the developing cerebellum as a target of early-life adversity and suggest that disrupted cerebellar maturation may contribute to lasting functional consequences. This study extends our understanding of the effects of maternal separation beyond the brain regions traditionally associated with stress responses.

papers.title: Gene-level structure of prior knowledge and perturbation responses informs target-level predictability in prior-informed models
papers.abstract: Background: Predictive models of transcriptional responses to unseen genetic perturbations increasingly incorporate biological prior knowledge. However, it remains unclear how well prior knowledge reflects each target's perturbation-response relationships and how closely prior-derived measures track target-level predictive performance. Here, we develop a gene-similarity framework to quantify agreement among eight sources of biological prior knowledge and between prior knowledge and co-function or co-regulation relationships derived from six Perturb-seq datasets. Results: In genome-wide and essential-gene screens, prior agreement accounted for 30-47% of the variance in co-function agreement and 35-43% in co-regulation agreement. Agreement with Perturb-seq responses was higher for essential genes, lower for transcription factor and signaling genes, and varied with gene expression characteristics and cellular context. We compared prior agreement and prior-derived train-test similarity with measures based on the observed test response in tracking target-level predictive performance. Across three prior-informed models, predictions were more accurate for targets whose observed perturbation-response relationships better matched prior knowledge and that were more similar to training perturbations. Notably, prior agreement and prior-derived train-test similarity, calculated without the test response, tracked relative differences in target-level predictive performance. The strength of these associations varied across models and datasets and, for train-test similarity, across prior sources. Conclusion: Our framework reveals gene- and context-level heterogeneity in how biological knowledge aligns with perturbation responses, and provides an a priori basis for assessing relative perturbation predictability before perturbation responses are measured.

papers.title: Expansion and Comprehensive Evaluation of the Peacock Eye Disease Management (PedMan) System across Olive Cultivars Differing in Susceptibility to Venturia oleaginea
papers.abstract: Peacock eye disease, caused by Venturia oleaginea , is an important foliar disease of olive that is primarily managed through fungicide applications. Integrating host resistance into disease-warning systems could improve spray timing and reduce unnecessary fungicide use. PedMan (Peacock eye disease Manager) was previously developed and validated for highly susceptible olive cultivars. The objectives of the present study were to expand PedMan to cultivars differing in susceptibility to V. oleaginea and to evaluate the expanded system under commercial grove conditions. A sensitivity analysis of the rainfall and temperature criteria used for highly susceptible cultivars was conducted to establish criteria for moderately susceptible and moderately resistant cultivars. The rainfall threshold of [≥]15 mm was retained, whereas the temperature range triggering an infection alert was narrowed from 12-18 {degrees}C for highly susceptible cultivars to 13-17 {degrees}C for moderately susceptible and 14-16 {degrees}C for moderately resistant cultivars. The expanded system was subsequently evaluated in 33 field trials and observations under natural infection conditions. PedMan recommendations were classified as correct or incorrect based on statistical comparisons of leaf abscission between fungicide-treated and untreated trees. Overall, 30 of 33 recommendations were correct, resulting in an accuracy of 90.9%. Sensitivity was 87.0%, while specificity and positive predictive value were both 100%. These results demonstrate that incorporating cultivar susceptibility into PedMan broadens its applicability and provides reliable cultivar-specific fungicide recommendations. The system has potential to reduce unnecessary fungicide applications while maintaining effective management of peacock eye disease across olive cultivars differing in susceptibility.

papers.title: Multiplexed mapping of long-range projections with FluoCode, a combinatorial fluorescent barcoding system
papers.abstract: Comprehensive mapping of long-range projections remains a major challenge in neuroscience. Conventional virus tracing labels only one or a few pathways per animal, and inter-individual comparison requires registering whole-brain images to a standard atlas. However, inter-individual variability in morphology and wiring limits fine-scale mapping. Here we report "FluoCode", a combinatorial fluorescent barcoding system for multiplexed projection mapping within single animals. We developed adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors that express two of seven different fluorescent proteins, yielding 21 distinct color codes, and a "FluoCode Reader" that automatically classifies neurite signals by color combinations and morphology. Using FluoCode, we mapped projections from up to 21 cortical areas to subcortical regions in individual mice, revealing fine-scale topographic maps in small subcortical nuclei. In the marmoset, mapping from the primary visual cortex demonstrated topographic projections in higher visual areas and thalamic nuclei. FluoCode thus enables fine-scale, within-animal comparison of long-range projections in rodents and primates.

papers.title: The co-evolution of adhesion and F-actin gives rise to hierarchical cellular force generation
papers.abstract: Cells --- the basic units of life --- dynamically adhere to their micro-environment, build their F-actin cytoskeleton, and apply molecular-motor generated contractile forces to it in a remarkably broad range of biological processes and physiological functions, in both health and disease. Yet, how these processes are orchestrated over multiple spatiotemporal scales is not fully understood. Using several experimental approaches and a theoretical framework, we show that adhesion assembly, on-adhesion F-actin accumulation and the contractile force itself all follow the same time evolution over tens of minutes, the cellular force timescale, at well-defined adhesion sites. We also show that the F-actin distribution away from the adhesion site features a multiplicative space-time decomposition. Finally, we show that F-actin retrograde flow --- central in the so-called molecular motor-clutch models --- is markedly faster than force generation rates, that it does not slow down over maturing adhesions and that its density drops at adhesion sites. These findings suggest a hierarchical, multi- scale force generation process that is controlled by slow adhesion recruitment, which is accompanied by rapid, bursty linear actin polymerization. The linear F-actin slowly accumulates with adhesion recruitment to form an extended near-adhesion F-actin network to which molecular motors attach and apply elastic-like contraction.

papers.title: Novel viral diversity and geographic structuring in the New Zealand West Coast blackfly (Austrosimulium ungulatum)
papers.abstract: Background Vector-borne diseases represent a major global public health burden, with climate change, land-use change and increasing human activity altering arthropod vector distributions and creating opportunities for infectious disease emergence. In Aotearoa New Zealand, insects commonly referred to as "sandflies" are blackflies belonging to the family Simuliidae. The West Coast blackfly, Austrosimulium ungulatum, is an endemic, human-biting species abundant throughout the South Island, yet its associated viral diversity remains largely unexplored. Methods Here, we used metatranscriptomic sequencing to characterise the virome of the West Coast blackfly and investigate patterns of viral diversity and community composition across geographical and environmental gradients. A total of 425 blackflies were collected from 19 locations spanning approximately 187 km. Results We identified 94 viral sequences across 16 orders and six phyla, all of which were putatively novel viruses. These included divergent lineages within families containing recognised vertebrate and arthropod pathogens, such as the Rhabdoviridae and Orthomyxoviridae. Viral community composition varied among sampling locations, but no significant associations were detected between land-use categories and viral diversity or community composition. In contrast, we revealed a weak but significant positive correlation between geographical distance and viral community dissimilarity, suggesting some degree of spatial structuring across the sampling range. Conclusions This study provides the first metatranscriptomic characterisation of the virome associated with the endemic West Coast blackfly, revealing substantial previously undescribed viral diversity and providing insights into the geographical distribution of arthropod-associated viral communities.

papers.title: Alveolar and airway progenitors converge on an epigenetically encoded profibrotic state
papers.abstract: During organ regeneration, epithelial transitional states arise from progenitors and instruct the mesenchyme to remodel the extracellular matrix. However, the identity of the progenitors, the mechanisms underlying this transition, and why these states persist in tissue fibrosis often remain elusive. Here, using lineage tracing in mice, we show that the profibrotic KRT5-/KRT17+ state in pulmonary fibrosis arises convergently from alveolar type (AT) 2 and airway secretory cells. AT1 cells generate neither KRT5-/KRT17+ nor AT2 cells. TGF-{beta}/SMAD3 acts through KMT2A and p300 to epigenetically reprogram human AT2 cells into the KRT5-/KRT17+ state. In human pulmonary fibrosis, KRT5-/KRT17+ cells slough off, and transitional cells re-epithelialize the denuded basement membrane. Transcriptionally convergent states arise in injured kidney, skin, and intestine. This work reframes fibrogenesis as the accumulation of a conserved profibrotic transitional state via ongoing turnover, not persistence alone, and nominates the state transition and its epigenetic regulators as therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Maternal deprivation impairs social recognition by diminishing the number of adult-born granule cells in the dentate gyrus
papers.abstract: Childhood neglect increases the likelihood of developing neuropsychiatric disease in adulthood. Maternal separation and early weaning (MSEW), a rodent model of maternal deprivation, was used to investigate effects on social recognition, a commonly impaired function in neuropsychiatric disorders in humans. We found that in adulthood, MSEW male mice showed social recognition impairments, and that MSEW female mice showed greater preference fo social novelty. MSEW male, but not female, mice had diminished numbers of adult-born granule cells (abGCs) in the dentate gyrus, as well as a lower density of abGC axons in the CA2 region compared to controls. MSEW males also showed a reduced rate of sharp wave ripples (SWRs) in the CA2 region in response to novel mouse exposure, as well as a reduction in differential SWR rates in response to novel and familiar mouse exposure. Living in an enriched environment restored the number of abGCs in the dentate gyrus of MSEW males to control levels and improved social recognition. Furthermore, chemogenetic activation of 4-6 week old, but not older, abGCs in a double transgenic model improved social recognition and partially restored CA2 SWR patterns in MSEW mice. These findings suggest that MSEW impairs social recognition through diminished adult neurogenesis, which can be restored in adulthood by living in a proneurogenic environment or by increasing the activity of existing abGCs.

papers.title: Protecting host mitochondria with vitamin B3 preserves bioenergetics and thermogenesis during antibiotic treatment
papers.abstract: Antibiotics that target bacterial translation can also impair mitochondrial function because mitochondria retain bacterial-like ribosomes. As antibiotic resistance continues to increase and the use of several broad-spectrum antibiotics has been limited by their mitochondrial toxicity, there is a growing need to understand their off-target effects in host physiology, and to identify strategies that can mitigate antibiotic-induced mitochondrial dysfunction. We demonstrate that antibiotic chloramphenicol (CA) induces a dose-dependent reduction in mitochondrial respiration and mitochondrial thermogenesis in Drosophila S2 cells, human HEK293T cells and in developing Drosophila larvae. In vivo, CA exposure triggers female-biased aberrant innate immune activation of hosts carrying naturally occurring mitochondrial rRNA variants. Metabolomic profiling revealed alterations in vitamin B3 metabolism in Drosophila during and following CA exposure. Among the vitamin B3 vitamers examined, nicotinamide (NAM) exhibited the strongest protective effect, mitigating the CA-induced impairments in mitochondrial respiration and thermogenesis, as well as aberrant immune activation. We identify mitochondrial thermogenesis as a previously unrecognized target of antibiotic-induced mitochondrial perturbation and a sensitive marker of mitochondrial stress. Furthermore, we demonstrate that co-supplementation of CA with NAM mitigates antibiotic-induced mitochondrial toxicity through evolutionarily conserved mitochondrial pathways. Finally, we establish Drosophila as a powerful model for investigating antibiotic-induced mitochondrial dysfunction and for developing therapeutic strategies to protect host mitochondria during antibiotic treatment.

papers.title: NeuroDisco: Interfacing neuronal populations - cell by cell, millisecond by millisecond, day by day
papers.abstract: Neuronal cultures offer comprehensive access to living networks, but their value as functional models is limited by synchronized bursts that drive pathologically strong neuronal depolarization. Theory attributes such bursting to a lack of external input. Here we present NeuroDiscos, compact {micro}LED and OLED projectors that operate inside standard incubators and deliver patterned, long-term optogenetic stimulation, synchronized with submillisecond precision to multi-electrode array recordings. Weak, uncorrelated NeuroDisco stimulation dispersed the bursts but left the population firing rate largely unchanged. In this asynchronous regime, neuronal activity reproducibly follows the weak stimulation, and stimulus-response relations characterize receptive fields and putative functional connections. At hardware costs of {euro}500-1,000, NeuroDiscos offer a scalable route to functional characterization of primary and patient-derived cultures.

papers.title: ProClust provides reliable statistical significance of clusters for single-cell transcriptomic data
papers.abstract: Clustering of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data is widely used to identify cell populations. However, overclustering can partition a single cell population into multiple clusters, potentially leading to spurious identification of cell subpopulations. Assessing the statistical significance of clusters is therefore needed to support their biological interpretation. We propose ProClust, a statistical test for clustering significance in scRNA-seq data. ProClust defines a single cluster as a log-concave distribution and adopts a projection-based approach to quantify clustering uncertainty through p-values. These projections can also provide interpretable visual evidence for individual clusterings. ProClust merges clusters when there is insufficient evidence to reject the single-cluster null hypothesis, refining an initial overclustering without prespecifying the final number of clusters. Across parametric and PBMC-based semi-synthetic simulations, ProClust avoided false subdivisions under single-population null settings while consistently recovering the underlying population structure across different numbers of true populations. In real scRNA-seq datasets from the Human Lung Cell Atlas, Tabula Muris, and Hydra, ProClust produced clustering solutions that showed overall agreement with reference annotations while retaining supported substructure and merging groups with insufficient evidence for separation. Together, these results demonstrate that ProClust provides a statistically principled and interpretable framework for refining an initial overclustering and distinguishing supported cellular heterogeneity. The ProClust R package is available at https://github.com/Anonym027/ProClust.

papers.title: Ultra-low-dose same-target combinations control drug resistance across stages
papers.abstract: The emergence of drug resistance continues to limit the long term effectiveness of cancer therapies [1], as tumour cells adapt to therapeutic selective pressure through diverse genetic and non-genetic routes [2,3]. Despite advances in more potent and next generation inhibitors and mechanism based combination therapies [4,5], durable disease control remains difficult to achieve. Here we tested an alternative strategy: combining multiple inhibitors directed against the same oncogenic driver, each at ultra low doses with minimal individual activity, to delay resistance emergence. In epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) driven cancer models, such ultra low dose same target combinations (ULDCs) distributed individually weak perturbations across multiple inhibitors directed against the same target and achieved substantial growth inhibition in vitro and antitumour activity in vivo despite weak effects of the corresponding single agents. Under similar levels of growth inhibition (~50%), single-agent EGFR inhibitors generated resistant outgrowth, whereas a five drug ULDC delayed resistance emergence. Increasing the number of inhibitors further delayed resistance emergence, with no detectable resistant outgrowth observed for combinations containing 8 to 14 inhibitors within the experimental timeframe. The five drug ULDC also retained measurable growth inhibitory activity against gefitinib resistant PC-9/GR cells, and resistant cells arising under five drug ULDC treatment exhibited markedly greater reversibility following drug withdrawal than those arising under single agent treatment. Although pharmacological additivity or synergy may contribute to the collective growth inhibitory effects of ULDCs, the divergent long term resistance outcomes observed under similar levels of growth inhibition indicate that resistance behaviour is not determined by inhibitory strength alone. Instead, our findings support a model in which increasing same target inhibitor diversity progressively constrains the adaptive trajectories available during resistance evolution, while therapeutic perturbation architecture may also influence the stability of resistant states that emerge. More broadly, these findings support the concept of same target collective suppression, in which multiple individually weak perturbations directed against the same target can collectively produce substantial antitumour activity and constrain resistance evolution across multiple stages. We propose that increasing same target inhibitor diversity may restrict accessible adaptive trajectories, while therapeutic perturbation architecture may also influence the stability of resistant states.

papers.title: FLASH radiotherapy drives intestinal regeneration via macrophage-derived WNT4 signaling and attenuated T-cell inflammation
papers.abstract: Ultra-high dose rate radiotherapy (FLASH-RT) reduces normal-tissue toxicity, yet how elevated dose rate improves tissue repair remains unclear. Here we combined whole-abdominal FLASH-RT and conventional radiotherapy (CONV-RT) in mice with single-cell transcriptomics, trajectory analysis, cell-cell communication inference, and in vivo perturbation experiments to define the intestinal repair ecosystem. Compared with CONV-RT, FLASH preserved Lgr5+ intestinal stem cells and Fabp1+ absorptive epithelial cells. Trajectory analysis showed that FLASH maintained stem-cell differentiation toward mature epithelial states enriched for fatty-acid metabolism. During a day-3 repair window, FLASH was accompanied by enrichment of Mrc1 macrophages, increased WNT4-associated signaling involving Fzd5Lrp5/6-expressing stem cells, and early transient {beta}-catenin activation. In vivo augmentation of Wnt4 signaling promoted crypt regeneration after CONV-RT. FLASH also reduced Tcf7 and Tbx21 CD4 T-cell populations and TNF- levels, consistent with attenuation of the pro-inflammatory CD4 T-cell response during intestinal recovery. Together, these findings indicate that FLASH-associated tissue sparing involves coordinated remodeling of regenerative and inflammatory immune states, suggesting that radiation dose rate influences not only initial tissue injury but also the immune microenvironment of subsequent recovery. Targeting this immune-stem cell crosstalk may provide a strategy to mimic FLASH-like radioprotection.

papers.title: Bacterial-Mimetic Membranes Reveal Hopanoid-Associated Domain-Like Lateral Heterogeneity
papers.abstract: Bacterial membranes are increasingly recognized as laterally heterogeneous assemblies whose local organization can regulate transport, stress adaptation, and interactions with membrane-active compounds. However, the physical principles by which bacterial lipid composition generates spatially distinct membrane environments remain poorly understood, partly because experimentally tractable models that reproducibly exhibit lateral segregation and permit quantitative characterization are limited. Here, we show that a multicomponent, hopanoid-containing bacterial-inspired membrane spontaneously self-organizes into laterally distinct physical environments that are consistently resolved in experiments and molecular simulations. Giant unilamellar vesicles prepared from a lipid mixture inspired by lipid classes found in hopanoid-producing bacteria, including Methylorubrum extorquens, exhibit stable micron-scale lateral segregation, which is independently reproduced in compositionally matched coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations. The resulting membrane environments differ in composition, packing, order, mobility, and mechanical properties. Hopanoid-associated domain-like regions are more condensed, more ordered, and less mobile, whereas PE-rich non-domain regions remain more laterally expanded and exhibit faster lipid diffusion. At the global level, the bacterial-inspired membrane displays greater bending rigidity than a fluid phosphatidylcholine reference, while ATR-FTIR measurements independently support increased lipid-chain ordering and denser membrane packing. Together, these findings establish that hopanoid-containing bacterial-inspired membranes can spontaneously generate coexisting physical environments whose distinct local properties collectively determine global membrane behavior. The resulting experimental-computational framework provides a quantitative basis for investigating bacterial-like membrane heterogeneity and how local composition, dynamics, and mechanics govern responses to membrane-targeting perturbations.

papers.title: DecoyOpt: A two-stage pipeline for decoy-aware enzyme discrimination and EC number prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate and efficient EC number prediction is essential for elucidating the catalytic roles of enzymes. Although similarity-based and deep learning-based approaches have advanced this task, they often fail to distinguish active enzymes from closely related decoys inactivated by local functional-site mutations, leading to high false-positive rates (FPRs). We propose DecoyOpt, a two-stage pipeline for decoy-aware enzyme discrimination and EC number prediction. Specifically, we generated putatively inactive functional-site decoys using ESM3 and evaluated 16 protein language models across three splits. An MLP trained with classification and ranking losses distinguishes enzymes from unannotated proteins and decoys before a contrastive learning model assigns EC numbers to predicted enzymes. On the most stringent GraphPart 40% split, DecoyOpt achieves an MCC of 0.899 and a D0 decoy FPR of 6.17%, outperforming retrained baselines. Across all splits, it outperforms these baselines in EC number prediction on the full test set while maintaining performance close to CLEAN on the enzyme subset. It also correctly annotates all four wild-type enzymes and rejects all eight inactive or nearly inactive variants. We believe that DecoyOpt has potential for annotating uncharacterized proteins and their variants, with applications in genomics, synthetic biology, and biocatalysis.

papers.title: Dual CD40/CD28 co-stimulation reprograms the solid-tumor microenvironment to unleash CAR-T and endogenous anti-tumor immunity
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has shown limited efficacy against solid tumors, owing to poor T-cell persistence, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) and cancer immune evasion. Here we describe LACO-Stim (lymphocytes-APC co-stimulator), a chimeric co-stimulatory molecule composed of an agonistic anti-CD40 single-chain variable fragment (scFv) and the CD28 intracellular signaling domain, such that a single molecule activates CD40-expressing antigen-presenting cells while delivering CD28 co-stimulation to the T cell that bears it. Co-expressed with a 4-1BB-based CAR (LACO-CAR-T), it enhanced anti-tumor activity in vitro and achieved durable, complete in most mice, tumor regression rather than transient control in xenograft and immunocompetent models. In immunocompetent hosts, LACO-CAR-T activated dendritic cells, reprogrammed tumor macrophages toward M1-like, antigen-presenting states, and induced epitope spreading with endogenous CD8 T-cell responses against tumor neoantigens. Single-cell transcriptomics and RNA-velocity analysis revealed coordinated immune remodeling: T cells shifted toward a more stem-like, less terminally exhausted state, regulatory T cells declined in frequency and suppressive function, and myeloid cells acquired antigen-presentation programs while excessive inflammatory and suppressive signaling was restrained. LACO-Stim further synergized with anti-PD-1 blockade to control tumor growth. LACO-Stim thus enables CAR-T cells to coordinate intrinsic T-cell reinforcement with extrinsic immune reprogramming, converting an immunosuppressive TME into a de-inflamed (reduced inflammatory signaling), de-suppressed rather than merely armed niche that supports endogenous anti-tumor immunity.

papers.title: Peptide Sequence Determines the Efficacy of Single-Dose AAV-Vectorized GLP-1R Agonists in Diet-Induced Obese Mice
papers.abstract: Background: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonists such as semaglutide produce substantial weight loss and glycemic improvement, but their long-term efficacy depends on sustained adherence to chronic dosing. Adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapy could, in principle, provide durable GLP-1R agonist (GLP-1RA) exposure from a single administration, but the degree of peptide engineering required for a vectorized GLP-1RA transgene to be efficacious in vivo is unknown. Methods: We generated four self-complementary AAV (scAAV) constructs encoding: native human GLP-1(7-36) (GLP-1), a DPP-IV-resistant Gly8-GLP-1(7-36) variant (Gly8), Exendin-4 (Ex4), or an Exendin-4 human IgG4 Fc fusion protein (Ex4-Fc). All four constructs were validated to secrete functional GLP-1R agonists in vitro using a conditioned-media potency assay. Subsequently, these constructs were packaged into PHP.eB capsids and administered as a single intravenous dose (5x1012 vg/kg) to diet-induced obese (DIO) mice alongside a vehicle control. Body weight, body composition, food intake, fasting plasma insulin, and oral glucose tolerance were assessed over a 3-week period. At the end of the study, tissues were harvested for assessments of plasma/liver lipids, tissue transgene transcript and peptide levels. Results: HEK293 cells transfected with the four AAV constructs all secreted active peptides/proteins as assessed by a cell-based GLP-1R activation assay, although the effective concentration of the GLP-1 constructs in the media spanned nearly four orders of magnitude 72 hours after transfection. In diet-induced obese (DIO) mice, Ex4 and Ex4-Fc vectors, but not GLP-1 or Gly8 vectors, produced significant reductions in body weight of up to 22.6% of starting body weight out to 21 days after a single dose. In addition, reductions in food intake, fat mass, and fasting insulin relative to vehicle were also observed for Ex4 and Ex4-Fc. Furthermore, Ex4-Fc improved oral glucose tolerance while reducing plasma cholesterol and liver triglycerides relative to vehicle. Although transcript levels did not differ appreciably among the four constructs in either brain or liver, measurable peptide product in plasma and brain lysate tracked the rank order of the in vitro supernatant screen, with GLP-1 and Gly8 groups indistinguishable from endogenous background. Conclusions: PHP.eB scAAV Ex4 and Ex4-Fc showed robust efficacy on multiple metabolic endpoints including weight loss and glucose tolerance. In contrast, vectorized GLP-1 and Gly8 showed no in vivo efficacy despite comparable levels of viral transcript in the brain and the liver. Vectorized GLP-1 and Gly8 also performed poorly compared to exendin-4-based constructs in vitro, suggesting that conditioned-media potency screening is a valid early filter for construct selection in vectorized-peptide AAV development. Engineering peptides to improve translation and secretion efficiency, in addition to circulating plasma stability, could further optimize vectorized GLP-1RA therapeutics.

papers.title: CPDD: Adapting an autoregressive DNA language model for bidirectional phage genome modeling
papers.abstract: Autoregressive DNA language models generate sequences ef[fi]ciently from left to right, but many genome-analysis and sequence-editing problems are naturally conditioned on both [fl]anks. We introduce CreatiPhage, a 144.5M-parameter autoregressive DNA language model for bacteriophages, and its diffusion extension, CreatiPhage Diffusion DNA-LM (CPDD). CPDD is a 147.5M-parameter bidirectional discrete diffusion model initialized from the six-epoch CreatiPhage checkpoint. CPDD retains the pretrained Transformer, block attention residuals, and Engram conditional memory, while introducing non-causal attention, a MASK-aware base-5 Engram, centered depthwise convolution, and position-aligned nucleotide readout. Training combines masked and GIDD-style uniformly substituted bases with nucleotide- and amino-acid-level losses over a 10 kb, 32 kb, and whole-source context curriculum. On a screened panel of 522 phage CDSs, CPDD achieves higher random-mask restoration accuracy than a comparable diffusion model and performs well above codon-level references. In a mixed-corruption test, it restores 42.4% of visible incorrect bases. Frozen CPDD representations also support infA [fi]tness prediction and seven-class phage virion protein subtype classi[fi]cation. Controlled evaluations further characterize how restoration depends on visible context and identify opportunities to improve longer-range sequence recovery. Together, these results support scaffold-conditioned sequence modeling as a step towards modular design of phage genomes.

papers.title: KLONE: An Imbalance-Robust k-NN Ensemble for Cross-Modal Single-Cell Clone Assignment
papers.abstract: Single-cell DNA sequencing (scDNA-seq) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enable the inference of copy number clones and transcriptional states in tumor studies. However, these two assays usually profile different cells of the same tumor, requiring computational assignment of unpaired scRNA-seq cells to clones identified by scDNA-seq to link clonal genotypes with transcriptional profiles. This task is challenging because the only connection between the two modalities is a weak, gene-dependent dosage effect, and the absence of clone labels for RNA cells precludes supervised learning of this relationship. Moreover, clonal distributions may differ between the two modalities because the cells are profiled independently, while the inherent clonal imbalance of real tumors can leave minority subclones underrepresented, further compromising assignment accuracy. To address these challenges, we present KLONE, a per-clone $k$-nearest-neighbor ($k$-NN) ensemble that assigns RNA cells directly to copy-number clones based on cross-modal Pearson similarity, without the need for a parametric model or clone labels for RNA cells. To ensure a fair assessment of each clone's compatibility with a given RNA cell, KLONE allocates an identical neighborhood budget to every clone, preventing majority clones from dominating the affinity assessment solely through their greater abundance. We compare KLONE with six existing methods on three colorectal cancer patients, using cells profiled in both modalities as ground truth. KLONE is the most accurate method and recalls minority clones at 100\%. Despite discrepancies in clonal distribution between the two modalities, KLONE recovers the clonal distribution of RNA cells almost perfectly ($\rho = 0.99$).

papers.title: The neural circuit implementation of distributional reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: Distributional reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms outperform traditional RL by representing the full probability distribution of future outcomes rather than its mean. Neural signatures consistent with distributional coding have been observed in dopamine neurons and in striatal value representations. However, how distributional RL is implemented within the anatomical circuit organization of the basal ganglia remains unknown. Uncovering how representations of outcome distributions are organized across brain circuits has broad implications for both fundamental and clinical neuroscience, providing new insights into how the brain represents uncertainty and how these representations shape risk-sensitive learning and decision-making. Here, we investigated how representations of outcome distributions are organized across dopamine projections to the striatum by combining striatum-wide fiber photometry of dopamine axonal activity with Neuropixels recordings from projection-defined dopamine neurons. We found that distributional reward prediction error signals are preferentially encoded in lateral ventral striatum-projecting dopamine neurons, but that reward distribution information is shared between the ventral and the dorsal striatum. Additionally, an anatomical gradient of optimism in the midbrain supports the diversity of value predictions required for distributional RL. Our findings extend the actor-critic framework proposed for the basal ganglia by revealing distributional prediction errors in a subpopulation of mesolimbic dopamine neurons capable of training parallel striatal regions thought to implement different types of behavioral control.

papers.title: Open-BEATBox: an open-source autonomous operant chamber for high-throughput data acquisition of complex behaviour
papers.abstract: Behavioural neuroscience increasingly relies on rodent models to investigate the neural mechanisms underlying cognition in health and disease. However, conventional operant testing is typically restricted to short daily sessions that require frequent experimenter intervention and often rely on food or water restriction. These constraints limit behavioural sampling, disrupt natural activity patterns, and introduce variability associated with handling and experimental schedules.Here, we present the Open Platform for Experimental Neuroscience Behavioural and Autonomous Box (Open-BEATBox), an open-source, autonomous home-cage platform that enables continuous, self-paced assessment of complex cognitive behaviour in mice. By allowing animals to live in the testing environment throughout the experiment, Open-BEATBox supports longitudinal behavioural assessment across different cognitive tasks while minimizing experimenter intervention and preserving natural circadian activity. The platform is modular, customizable, and designed to accommodate a broad range of operant paradigms and integration with chronic neural recording and neuromodulation technologies.Using a visual reversal-learning task, we show that continuous autonomous testing generates approximately ten times more completed trials during reversal learning than conventional session-based protocols while reducing experimenter workload without evidence of major adverse effects on the welfare measures assessed. The flexibility of the platform further enables implementation of additional cognitive paradigms, including uncertainty-based decision-making tasks.Together, Open-BEATBox provides an accessible open platform for longitudinal cognitive phenotyping, facilitating the collection of large longitudinal behavioural datasets and creating new opportunities to combine continuous behavioural assessment with modern systems neuroscience approaches.

papers.title: Elucidation of Sequence Constraints for Protein Folding on the Ribosome
papers.abstract: The pioneering round of protein folding on the ribosome is critical for the proper assembly and function of many proteins. Emerging evidence suggests some proteins sample distinct conformational intermediates during translation, which implies the mechanisms of cotranslational folding may impose specific constraints on protein sequence. To assess how folding on ribosome may shape mutational tolerance, we paired a fluorogenic arrest peptide sensor with deep mutational scanning to survey how 9,480 mutations modulate E. coli dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) folding on the ribosome in live cells. By controlling for differences in variant abundance, we assess how these mutations specifically impact the efficiency of DHFR folding on stalled ribosomes. Mutagenic trends are broadly correlated with computational estimates for the change in the free energy of the native fold, suggesting that the sequence constraints associated with late-stage folding on the ribosome are broadly similar to those of post-translational folding. However, a close inspection of mutagenic trends reveals that folding on the ribosome is vulnerable to perturbations of specific contacts within a central portion of the adenosine binding domain and the C-terminal {beta}-strands of the discontinuous loop domain. Some of these regions are known to retain structure in the context of conformational intermediates that form on and off the ribosome, while others appear to be specific to cotranslational interactions. Together, our findings highlight how the constraints of folding on the ribosome may constrain evolutionary sequence space.

papers.title: Telotrons: spliceosomal introns composed of telomeric repeats
papers.abstract: Spliceosomal intron numbers vary widely across eukaryotes, but the only established mechanism for large bursts of intron gain is the spread of transposable introner elements. We describe telotrons, spliceosomal introns composed predominantly of telomeric repeats. In a survey of 10,310 eukaryotic genome assemblies, we identified 7,008 introns with >85% telomeric repeat coverage and an additional 44,423 with >50% to [≤]85% coverage, in 25 genomes spanning haptophytes, dinoflagellates, a cryptophyte, stramenopiles, the apicomplexan Eimeria, and the nematode Mesorhabditis. Most telotrons carry GT-AG or GC-AG splice boundaries, and RNA-seq supports their splicing. Their repeat orientations are consistent with telomerase extension of broken DNA ends, and intron absence at corresponding positions in orthologs supports widespread de novo gain. In Eimeria and Mesorhabditis, telotrons instead occupy positions where orthologs carry ordinary introns, suggesting modification of existing introns. Telotrons thus point to telomerase as an endogenous driver of structural innovation through intron creation and remodeling.

papers.title: An elongated lifespan is associated with higher oxidative protection of flight tissue in Heliconiini butterflies
papers.abstract: Evolutionary theories of ageing often invoke trade-offs in resource allocation between somatic maintenance and other important physiological functions. One proposed mechanistic mediator of these trade-offs is oxidative stress, which arises from an imbalance between an organism's production of reactive oxygen species and its ability to detoxify them. Accordingly, many long-lived species across the animal kingdom show evidence for resistance to oxidative stress. However, it can be difficult to associate lifespan differences with oxidative phenotypes when comparing species across wide taxonomic distances, which may also show large differences in physiology. Butterflies in the long-lived Heliconius genus show a 3-fold lifespan extension and slowed ageing in comparison with their close relatives in the Heliconiini tribe, to whom they are phylogenetically, ecologically, and physiologically similar. However, proximate explanations for this extended longevity are currently lacking. Here, we leverage the neat comparative framework between Heliconius hecale and Dryas iulia, a shorter-lived Heliconiini outgroup, to test whether the observed lifespan differences between the two species are associated with differences in oxidative physiology. Our findings suggest superior oxidative protection of thoracic tissue in the longer-lived H. hecale compared to D. iulia, as evidenced by increased superoxide dismutase activity, increased total antioxidant capacity, and a corresponding reduction in lipid peroxidation in this tissue. Considering the metabolic demands of insect flight, we suggest that this oxidative phenotype may contribute to the extended longevity of Heliconius by enhancing protection of thoracic tissues against oxidative damage, representing a plausible proximate pro-longevity mechanism in this genus.

papers.title: Homogeneous network inference for subtype-stratified master regulator analysis in cancer
papers.abstract: Master-regulator analysis of 34 TCGA tumour cohorts (cancer x molecular subtype; n between 27 and 562 tumours) requires one regulatory network per cohort. Mutual-information (MI) networks inferred with ARACNe3 are the usual choice, but they are not available for the smallest cohorts; filling the gap with correlation networks would mix two methods inside the very comparison between subtypes that the analysis is meant to make. We therefore infer every network with a single procedure, fixed-size Spearman regulons (FSR): rank correlation between regulator and target, a fixed effect-size threshold rho >= 0.2, the per-target data-processing-inequality (DPI) pruning implemented in corto, bootstrap support, and truncation to the 100 best-supported targets per regulator. We quantify what this choice concedes and what it provides, labelling each claim as a standard result, a heuristic, or an empirical result. Rank correlation is more powerful than the MI estimators we simulated for n < 200 but cannot see non-monotone dependence, which in a synthetic worst case costs at most about 0.05-0.10 of the master regulators recovered; the per-target DPI is a heuristic with a measurable disagreement rate with the MI-based one; and pairwise dependence is not direct interaction, for MI and correlation alike. Where both methods are feasible (n >= 95) they overlap in 0.7 of the top-20 regulators, the same as two filterings of the same ARACNe3 network, although the rank correlation of the full score vector shows a measurable method effect in the tail. Subsampling large real cohorts indicates that networks inferred from fewer than 60 tumours do not reliably reproduce their own cohort's master regulators, that 60-100 is a grey zone, and that a cancer-wide network does not rescue small subtypes. We present FSR as an adequate and uniform choice for multi-cohort analysis, not as a statistically superior one.

papers.title: Multi-material delivery strategies to create deferoxamine-functionalized collagen scaffolds for craniofacial bone repair
papers.abstract: Craniomaxillofacial (CMF) bone injuries are common and can occur secondary to trauma, bone resection, and congenital abnormalities. While the current standard of care remains allograft or autograft, tissue engineering approaches offer the opportunity for alternative regenerative solutions. Biomaterial design has been central in this effort, with a primary consideration being the incorporation of motifs into biomaterials that accelerate osteogenic differentiation of progenitor cells and subsequent mineral synthesis. However, angiogenic potency, and subsequent angiogenic-osteogenic coupling, represent a critical challenge, as poor angiogenic activity can impair regenerative healing. Deferoxamine (DFO) can mimic cellular hypoxia via iron chelation and has been used as an angiogenic factor. However, its size (<1 kDa) severely limits its retention in the wound area. Here, we report a multi-material approach to improve angiogenic coupling in an osteogenic biomaterial. We report methods to retain DFO in mineralized collagen scaffold via its binding to a second polymer, gelatin, that can be incorporated into the scaffold to boost angiogenic potency while maintaining its osteo-regenerative properties. We employed carbodiimide chemistry to attach DFO to a gelatin backbone and retained 79.6% of the drug over a 7-day culture. Using a composite drug-delivery approach that combines freely soluble DFO with gelatin-bound DFO into the mineralized collagen scaffold, drove increased mesenchymal stem cell metabolic activity and enhanced expression of angiogenic genes in culture over 14 days. This work provides a novel approach to advance acellular regenerative biomaterials for osteogenic-angiogenic coupling processes.

papers.title: Nucleobase-Specific Recognition of DNA by Protamine
papers.abstract: Protamines--arginine (Arg)-rich, intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs)--replace histones to compact DNA in the sperm nucleus. While folded domains can bind DNA site-specifically, whether IDPs exhibit DNA-sequence specificity remains open. Here, we used all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to characterize protamine-DNA binding. Eight copies of salmon protamine (33 residues with 21 Arg) rapidly wrap around a 35-bp DNA molecule. In addition to salt bridges with DNA phosphates, Arg hydrogen-bonds with multiple nucleobases on both strands or the same strand. At the major groove, protamine prefers GC over AT by a 2.6-to-1 ratio, with guanine's O6 and N7 atoms as hydrogen-bond acceptors; the preference is especially strong at G-tracts. This selectivity reverses at the minor groove, where AT overtakes GC by a 2.1-to-1 margin. The net effect is a moderate bias for GC over AT in protamine-base interactions. Additional simulations with 20-bp DNA molecules and free-energy calculations reinforce these observations. For experimental validation, we designed DNA sequences with 0-40% GC content. Protamine-DNA mixtures form aggregates, with an increasing propensity at higher GC content and upon shuffling into G-tracts. This work demonstrates that IDPs can bind DNA in a nucleobase-specific manner, with implications for protamine-mediated transcription silencing and remodeling of paternal chromatin.

papers.title: Systemic TLR7 agonism moderates disease severity in acute DSS-induced colitis in mice
papers.abstract: Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7) is an endosomal sensor of single-stranded RNA, studied for its antiviral and pro-inflammatory functions. Its role in intestinal inflammation is undefined, and no approved or clinical-stage therapy for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) engages this pathway. Here we report that systemic administration of the reference TLR7 agonist GS-9620 (vesatolimod) moderates disease severity in acute dextran sodium sulfate (DSS)-induced colitis in mice. GS-9620-treated mice lost less weight, had lower Disease Activity Index scores, and were protected from DSS-induced colon shortening. Immunophenotyping of the spleen showed reduced Th17 and Tr17 populations and an increased proportion of regulatory T cells. These findings indicate that pharmacological TLR7 agonism is not merely tolerated in the inflamed intestine but is associated with a shift of the systemic immune compartment toward a regulatory phenotype. The results identify TLR7 as a candidate disease-moderating target in IBD and motivate direct tests of causality, route and chronic-disease relevance.

papers.title: Disentangled generative modeling of single-cell perturbation responses across dynamic cellular states
papers.abstract: Single-cell perturbation studies are increasingly conducted across complex, multi-condition biolog-ical systems, offering a powerful lens into how interventions reshape cell states and molecular pro-grams. However, standard computational models compress single-cell profiles into unified repre-sentations where treatment effects are obscured by cell division, lineage progression, donor varia-tion, and cellular stress. Here, we present Disentangled Variational Inference for Perturbation Re-sponse (PertVI), a deep generative model that separates baseline mitotic phase, cellular state, and batch effects from treatment-induced shifts while isolating aberrant off-manifold responses in or-thogonal anomaly space. This structured design tackles two intertwined tasks: (1) quantifying treatment-induced changes in cell-state composition, and (2) inferring state-gated transcriptional changes in response to treatment. Across simulated benchmarks, PertVI accurately disentangles coupled biological axes and recovers weak treatment signatures. In conditional chemical and genet-ic screens of primary human CD8+ and CD4+ T cells, PertVI separates memory-precursor adju-vants from toxic phenocopies, resolves co-clustered regulators into directional kinetic trajectories and biphasic rebounders obscured by standard workflows, and reveals that treatment-induced phe-notypic shifting is decoupled from broad transcriptional perturbation responses and instead gov-erned by state-specific impulses. Altogether, PertVI brings unique mechanistic granularity to sin-gle-cell perturbation response modeling, serving as a proof of principle for biology-informed, struc-ture-guided variance disentanglement in dynamic cellular systems.

papers.title: ASD Neuro Agentic (ANA): An Agentic Framework for Feature Discovery and Cross Site Generalization in Autism fMRI Classification
papers.abstract: Classifiers of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) from resting state functional MRI rarely generalize across sites, and many reported accuracies are inflated by data leakage.We show that an agentic artificial intelligence framework, ASD Neuro Agentic (ANA), whose language model agents propose features from the literature and researcher input while fixed tools perform every calculation, can search auditably for site independent classifiers while controlling the leakage. In 1,028 participants from 17 ABIDE I centers, ANA tested 71 pipelines and selected a ComBat harmonized ensemble of tangent space connectivity models from six parcellations and 98 public connectivity derivatives. In leave one center out testing, the ensemble reached an area under the curve of 0.814 (95% CI, 0.773 to 0.841), outperforming ASD DiagNet and ASD SAENet. Predictive connectivity was mainly reduced in ASD. Agentic AI offers a systematic and efficient approach to exploring, evaluating, and identifying pipelines as model selection grows complex.

papers.title: Statistical significance testing for spatial domain detection in spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: In spatial transcriptomics, domain-detection methods group platform-specific spatial measurement units--cells, bins or multicellular spots--into spatial domains for comparing molecular programs, cellular composition and interactions among tissue regions. However, the number of candidate domains detected in the same tissue can vary with user-specified parameters or model-selection criteria. Whether candidate domains should be merged can be framed as a test of a single-domain null hypothesis, under which each gene has constant mean expression across all spatial units in the combined region. However, testing candidate domains on the same gene-expression data used to detect them may induce post-selection bias and yield anti-conservative p-values, increasing the risk of oversegmentation. To address these challenges, we introduce SigDoTS (statistical Significance testing for Domain deTection in Spatial transcriptomics), a hypothesis-testing framework for spatial domain detection. SigDoTS uses hierarchical testing to determine which candidate domains to retain or merge, with adjustment for family-wise error control. It accounts for gene-gene covariance and spatial dependence and computes p-values by rerunning the upstream domain-detection pipeline on datasets simulated under the fitted single-domain null. In simulations, SigDoTS controlled the type I error rate at the root node under the single-domain null and improved recovery of the true spatial domains when multiple domains were present. In human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, SigDoTS retained superficial and deep Layer 6 domains but merged Layer 3 candidate domains across different initial numbers of candidate domains. In ovarian and colorectal cancers, SigDoTS retained epithelial domains with different gene-expression programs and local immune environments, together with immune, stromal and vascular domains.

papers.title: A LOV-domain photoreceptor mediates phototaxis in brown algae
papers.abstract: Phototaxis enables motile cells to navigate light environments and plays a critical role in survival and reproduction across diverse eukaryotic lineages. This ability has evolved independently through distinct photoreceptor systems. Yet, the molecular mechanisms underlying phototaxis remain poorly understood in many major eukaryotic lineages, including stramenopiles. Here, combining functional genetics, cell biology and evolutionary analyses, we identify Helmchrome (HELM), a LOV-domain protein required for phototaxis in the brown alga Ectocarpus. HELM localizes to the posterior flagellum and is responsible for the characteristic flavin-associated fluorescence of brown algal gametes. Loss of HELM abolishes phototactic accumulation and directional orientation without affecting basal motility or fertilization, demonstrating its specific requirement for light-directed movement. Phylogenetic analyses reveal that HELM-like proteins are distributed across diverse stramenopile lineages and that their domain architecture evolved through repeated duplication of an ancestral RGS-LOV module. Our findings identify HELM as a key component of the light-sensing machinery in brown algae, provide a molecular explanation for the long-standing observation of flagellar flavin fluorescence, and reveal a distinct phototaxis system that expands the known diversity of eukaryotic light-sensing mechanisms.

papers.title: Uncovering Viral Signals Across Cell Populations in Colorectal Cancer
papers.abstract: Viral sequences have been detected in colorectal cancer, but their cellular and anatomical distribution remains poorly resolved. We aimed to establish a cell-type-resolved map of viral reference-associated RNA signals across colorectal cancer, tumour-adjacent normal tissue, and healthy colon. We repurposed human-unmapped reads from single-cell RNA sequencing libraries generated in ten publicly available studies. We retained cell-barcode and unique molecular identifier information, removed duplicate molecules, and aligned reads to a curated human-associated viral reference using three aligners. Viral signals were analysed across cell types, tissue conditions, and colorectal segments. We used participant-grouped repeated cross-validation to evaluate tissue-condition classification and screened an independent paired colorectal cancer proteomics cohort for compatible peptide matches. The study included 547 libraries from 112 participants, including 49 with matched colorectal cancer and tumour-adjacent normal samples, and approximately 415,000 cells spanning ten major cell populations. Viral reference-associated RNA signals differed across epithelial, immune, stromal, and vascular compartments, tissue conditions, and anatomical regions of the colon. Of 318 independent healthy-reference viral-load comparisons, seven involving six virus-cell-type groups remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction, including plasma-cell HHV-7 and HHV-6B and mast-cell HCV-2. Cell-type-resolved viral features distinguished colorectal cancer, tumour-adjacent normal tissue, and healthy colon in participant-grouped validation; random forest achieved a macro-AUC of 0.957 (SD 0.028), with HERV-K113 as the leading quantitative feature. An independent proteomic screen identified peptide matches compatible with 20 candidate viral groups. We established a cell-type-resolved map of viral reference-associated RNA signals across colorectal tissue conditions and anatomical regions. By identifying candidate viral signals in epithelial and immune compartments, this map provides a basis for investigating virus-host pathways involved in tumour biology, immune regulation, and antigen-presentation states, and could help prioritise future combination strategies pairing virus-directed or virus-mimetic approaches with standard treatment or immune checkpoint blockade.

papers.title: Developing a Multimodal miR-15a Mimic to Overcome Gemcitabine and RAS(ON) Inhibitor Daraxonrasib Resistance in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
papers.abstract: Gemcitabine remains a mainstay of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) treatment, while the RAS(ON) inhibitor daraxonrasib has recently demonstrated improved survival in previously treated metastatic disease. However, acquired resistance to both therapies remains a major clinical challenge. Here, we developed MTX-5-FU-Gem-miR-15a, a multimodal microRNA (miRNA)-based therapeutic, by chemically modifying tumor-suppressive miR-15a with methotrexate (MTX), 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), and gemcitabine (Gem) to combine sequence-specific gene regulation with disruption of nucleotide metabolism. MTX-5-FU-Gem-miR-15a exhibited low-nanomolar potency across five PDAC cell lines and retained activity in gemcitabine- and daraxonrasib-resistant models under vehicle-free conditions, substantially exceeding that of stoichiometrically matched free antimetabolites. Treatment induced S-phase accumulation, increased DNA damage and apoptosis, and suppressed checkpoint and survival-associated proteins, including WEE1, CHK1, YAP1, and BCL-2.
