Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed increased DNA replication, replication-stress, and repair-associated programs, together with reduced oncogenic signaling. In gemcitabine-resistant cells, treatment restored the gemcitabine-activating enzyme dCK, reduced ABCC1 and ABCC3 expression, and suppressed resistance-associated signaling programs, indicating partial remodeling of resistance-associated pathways. MTX-5-FU-Gem-miR-15a also synergized with daraxonrasib (mean Bliss synergy score, 22.52) and activated tumor-cell-intrinsic STING-TBK1 signaling, accompanied by increased interferon stimulated gene expression and IFN-{beta} and CXCL10 secretion. Finally, MTX-5-FU-Gem-miR-15a retained low-nanomolar potency in three patient-derived PDAC organoids and significantly suppressed metastatic tumor growth in vivo at 4 mg/kg. Together, these findings support a multimodal miRNA therapeutic strategy that combines replication-associated DNA damage, checkpoint protein suppression, and innate immune activation-associated responses to target therapeutic resistance in PDAC.

papers.title: Accessing Mesoscale Functional Organization from Standard Functional MRI Leveraging AI-Based Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: Access to the fine-scale functional organization of the human brain is essential for understanding cognition and neurological disorders yet remains beyond the reach of conventional functional MRI (fMRI) because of its limited spatial resolution and contrast-to-noise ratio. To overcome this limitation, we developed f-LENNS (functional Localization Enhancement via Neural-Net-Sharpening), an artificial intelligence (AI)-based framework that enhances the effective spatial resolution of reconstructed fMRI magnitude images. The model was trained exclusively on high-resolution synthetic MRI data using extensive domain randomization and no adversarial or generative components. This approach enables robust out-of-the-box generalization (without retraining) to experimental datasets obtained with diverse acquisitions, while effectively curbing hallucination. Our experiments show that our publicly available model substantially improves the spatial fidelity of functional activation maps across multiple imaging paradigms and generalizes to a cohort of individuals with atypical brain function caused by amblyopia (lazy eye). F-LENNS consistently outperforms conventional resolution enhancement approaches, including interpolation-based upsampling and sharpening methods. These findings demonstrate that AI-driven super-resolution combined with domain randomization can overcome domain shifts arising from differences in MRI acquisition, enabling scalable, fine-scale functional brain mapping with widely available MRI hardware.

papers.title: Shared brain transcriptome signatures of social evolution and plasticity in shell-dwelling cichlid fishes
papers.abstract: Inter-individual variability in phenotypic traits is widespread in nature both across and within species, with similar patterns of variation often occurring between and within species. Given that these two types of variation are generated by evolutionary and plasticity processes respectively, it raises the question to what extent the causal mechanisms underlying such variability at these two different levels are shared or not. To address this question, we studied the variation in brain transcriptomes in Tanganyikan cichlids that exhibit both intra- and interspecific variation in social behavior. We compared two facultatively social cichlid species, each containing naturally occurring solitary and social-living individuals, with a closely related obligatory solitary resembling the ancestral state. Differential gene expression and Gene Set Enrichment Analyses were performed in the telencephalon and diencephalon transcriptomes to investigate the molecular basis of both behavioral plasticity and the evolution of sociality. Behavioral plasticity involved few differentially expressed genes but extensive changes in biological pathways, supporting a highly polygenic architecture of social behavior. Across both species, social-living individuals consistently upregulated pathways involved in translation, protein homeostasis, and energy metabolism, whereas solitary individuals showed enrichment of neuronal morphogenesis, cell adhesion, and structural plasticity. Remarkably, these same functional programs were associated with the independent evolution of sociality, revealing a strong overlap between evolutionary and plastic transcriptional responses. This convergence was largely restricted to the telencephalon, while the diencephalon showed limited and inconsistent functional signatures. Together, our results support the repeated recruitment of gene regulatory programs during the evolution of sociality and demonstrate that behavioral plasticity and evolutionary transitions share common neurogenomic responses, consistent with a conserved genetic toolkit for social behavior.

papers.title: Tendon-specific PIEZO1 activation enhances neural drive to muscle during ballistic movement
papers.abstract: Tendons are generally regarded as passive structures that transmit muscle force to bone, yet they contain the Golgi tendon organ (GTO), whose Ib afferents act on motor neurons either inhibitory or excitatory depending on movement context. Whether a change in tendon mechanical properties alters the neural drive to muscle during movement remains unknown. We therefore recorded electromyography (EMG) and ankle kinematics during jumping in male mice carrying a tendon-specific gain-of-function (GOF) mutation in the mechanosensitive channel PIEZO1, which renders the tendon more compliant. In wild-type (WT) mice, gastrocnemius EMG amplitude increased with jump distance but not tibialis anterior activity, identifying the gastrocnemius as the muscle that scales with jump demand. At their maximum jump distance, which was longer in GOF than in WT mice, GOF mice showed a larger gastrocnemius EMG amplitude with unchanged burst duration. No genotype difference was detected at a submaximal distance, indicating that this enhancement depends on load. Kinematics showed the same specificity: GOF mice reached a deeper peak dorsiflexion before takeoff only at maximum jump distance, and the EMG difference emerged only after maximal dorsiflexion, not at burst onset. Muscle mass and myogenic gene expression were unchanged, whereas tendon marker genes were elevated, indicating that the enhancement was not of muscular origin. These findings indicate that a change in tendon mechanical properties alters the neural drive to muscle in a load-dependent manner, most plausibly through positive force feedback from the GTO, and identify the tendon as a sensory organ whose mechanical properties shape motor output.

papers.title: Conserved RNA structural elements mediate WDR5 recognition of the long non-coding RNA UMLILO
papers.abstract: The long non-coding RNA (lncRNA), UMLILO (upstream master lncRNA of the inflammatory chemokine locus), regulates the epigenetic programming of innate immune genes. Although its basic mechanism was revealed in cells, the molecular basis by which UMLILO interacts with its partner, WD repeat-containing protein 5 (WDR5), remained unknown. To understand how UMLILO interacts with WDR5, we determined the secondary structure of UMLILO by chemical probing and performed binding assays, uncovering the multivalent nature of their interaction, involving multiple RNA stem-loops. Conservational analysis revealed a stem-loop structurally conserved across mammals. Furthermore, we found that UMLILO engages multiple sites on the surface of WDR5 as revealed by NMR chemical shift perturbation analysis, and that full-length UMLILO increases WDR5 recruitment into in vitro condensates. Our report provides a detailed characterization of the molecular basis of WDR5 recognition by an RNA and establishes a new paradigm for the role of IPLs in enhancing gene expression.

papers.title: Lifestyle-mediated shifts in the gut microbiome and host genetics modulate gene expression in intestinal organoids
papers.abstract: Industrialization-associated shifts in the gut microbiome have been linked to disease, but the mechanisms by which microbial communities influence host gene regulation remain poorly understood. We developed a live microbiome-colonic organoid (colonoid) co-culture system to investigate genotype-dependent host responses to gut microbial community variation. Colonoid 2D monolayers from healthy donors were co-cultured with live gut microbial communities from individuals living urban or rural lifestyles, followed by RNA-sequencing. Urban and rural microbiomes elicited largely shared transcriptional responses, however they induced distinct host genetic effects on gene expression. We identified 511 host genes with microbiome-dependent allele-specific expression (ASE) which were involved in epithelial architecture, cell-matrix interactions and structural integrity. Notably, 149 host genes had distinct allelic effects between Urban and Rural microbiomes (urban-rural condition specific ASE or cASE), revealing genotype-dependent host responses to lifestyle-associated microbiomes. Urban-rural cASE was associated with microbial community composition, predominantly involving Prevotella and Bacteroides species. Targeted Prevotella copri spike-in recapitulated Prevotella-associated allelic effects at specific loci, including one in the IBD-associated autophagy gene, ATG4B. Together, these findings establish an experimental framework to investigate genotype-by-microbiome interactions, and demonstrate that lifestyle-mediated shifts in the microbiome modify host cis-regulatory genetic effects on gene expression.

papers.title: Dissecting human embryonic patterning during organogenesis reveals a rostral midline progenitor population for mesoendoderm induction
papers.abstract: Understanding how human organogenesis is accomplished via intricate spatiotemporal patterning of organ primordia requires spatial atlases at cellular resolution. However, existing human embryo spatial atlases are built using sequencing-based platforms such as Stereo-seq, which have limited spatial resolution and blurred anatomical boundaries, leading to misclassification across adjacent cells. Here, we integrate in situ imaging-based transcriptomics (Xenium) with transcriptome-wide spatial profiling (Visium-HD) of Carnegie stages 9-12 embryos to delineate the patterning of core embryonic tissues at single-cell resolution, including the brain, spinal cord, somites, neural crest, notochord, heart, and gut tube. A new finding enabled by spatial single-cell resolution is the identification of rostral midline progenitors (RMPs), a cell population co-expressing SOX2, TBXT, and OTX2. Transcriptionally, RMPs are distinct from both neuromesodermal progenitors (NMPs) and prechordal mesoderm, and in vivo clonal barcoding in mice indicates that RMPs share a common developmental origin with rostral neural ectoderm. To interrogate their functional significance, we leveraged our spatial transcriptome data to recapitulate RMP-like cells from human pluripotent stem cells and showed that these cells can induce epiblast-like cells to acquire mesendodermal and endodermal fates, while themselves adopting an ectodermal fate consistent with their in vivo counterparts. This work provides a 3D, stage-resolved molecular cell atlas of tissue patterning in human embryo that serves as a reference for in vitro models.

papers.title: KAT6 and KAT7 actively maintain mitotic chromatin composition and acetylation to preserve developmental competence
papers.abstract: Mitotic bookmarking enables transmission of regulatory information across cell division, yet how active chromatin states are molecularly preserved during mitosis and how they contribute to postmitotic cell fate decisions remain unresolved. Here, we demonstrate that the acetyltransferases KAT6 and KAT7 remain chromatin-bound and catalytically active throughout mitosis in mouse and human pluripotent stem cells. Acute KAT6/7 depletion disrupts mitotic histone acetylation and the retention of multiple chromatin regulators with minimal effects on chromatin accessibility. Mechanistically, KAT6/7 bookmark both self renewal and developmental gene loci, where they are required for post-mitotic transcriptional reactivation and priming of lineage-specific programs. Consistently, genes impaired during postmitotic reactivation also fail to activate during neuronal differentiation upon continuous KAT6/7 perturbation, compromising the establishment of the neuronal program and identity. Altogether, our findings identify KAT6 and KAT7 as a cooperative mitotic chromatin maintenance system that couples active histone acetylation to preservation of chromatin composition, transcriptional memory, and developmental competence across cell division, extending the bookmarking function beyond transcriptional memory. These findings also provide a new framework for understanding KAT6/7 function in neurodevelopmental disorders and cancer.

papers.title: A population-scale isoform atlas enables isoform-based trait association and regulatory analysis in lettuce
papers.abstract: Genomic variation shapes phenotypic diversity, yet how genetic variation contributes to transcript isoform diversity remains poorly understood at the population scale. Here, we integrated transcriptomic data from 240 lettuce accessions with a lettuce pangenome to construct a comprehensive pan isoform atlas comprising 531,657 isoforms from 49,729 transcribed loci. Isoform presence absence variation (iPAV) captured extensive transcript diversification during domestication and horticultural differentiation, providing additional resolution beyond locus-level analyses, particularly within loci shared across the population. To facilitate the systematic analysis of isoform trait associations, we developed ISONET-GWAS, a computational framework that integrates isoform-based association mapping, functional annotation, and network-based candidate prioritization. ISONET-GWAS recovered the known chlorophyll regulator LsGLK, identified 455 metabolite isoform associations across 77 metabolites, and prioritized candidate regulators of chlorophyll metabolism supported by functional validation. Genome-wide splicing quantitative trait locus (sQTL) mapping identified 10,498 sQTL associations, revealing widespread distal genetic associations with alternative splicing and candidate trans-sQTL hotspots. Notably, we identified a trans-sQTL hotspot overlapping LsPPR, which encodes a pentatricopeptide repeat RNA-binding protein. Perturbation of LsPPR resulted in widespread changes in alternative splicing of floweing-related genes, accompanied by delayed bolting and flowering and altered splicing of flowering-related genes. Together, our study establishes a population-scale pan-isoform resource and a broadly applicable analytical strategy for isoform-level trait association, candidate prioritization, and complementary analysis of the genetic regulation of alternative splicing in crops.

papers.title: LuCEMe: An accessible luciferase-based method to functionally assess cellular metabolism across model systems
papers.abstract: Metabolic profiling approaches such as extracellular flux analysis, metabolomics, stable isotope tracing and cytometry-based assays have transformed our understanding of cellular metabolism in physiological and pathological contexts. However, most techniques require specialized equipment or reagents, and do not allow differential metabolic analysis in intact multicellular systems. Here, we present LuCEMe, a luciferase-based metabolic phenotyping approach that combines acute metabolic perturbations with quantitative ATP measurements to resolve glycolytic and mitochondrial dependencies and capacities under native culture conditions, including in complex coculture and ex vivo systems without prior cell separation. The assay can also be adapted to increase metabolic resolution and distinguish between glycolytic activity, glucose oxidation and fatty acid/amino acid-driven mitochondrial ATP production. We use LuCEMe to reveal profound metabolic differences between leukemia cells cocultured with macrophages, stromal cells or adipocytes, and demonstrate distinct metabolic rewiring during macrophage polarization, osteogenic and adipogenic differentiation, and T cell activation. Ex vivo LuCEMe analysis identified a particular metabolic adaptation associated with chemotherapy response in acute myeloid leukemia that was not evident from conventional analyses. LuCEMe thus provides an accessible, robust and versatile framework for direct functional metabolic phenotyping across in vitro, ex vivo, and multicellular systems that complements existing metabolic profiling technologies.

papers.title: Miniaturized Traceless Staudinger Ligation Enables Direct-to-Biology Screening of Potent BRD4 PROTACs
papers.abstract: Direct-to-biology (D2B) approaches accelerate PROTAC discovery by enabling biological screening of crude reaction mixtures without intermediate purification. However, the range of chemical transformations compatible with these workflows remains limited. Herein, we establish a miniaturized, base-free traceless Staudinger ligation platform diversifying linker chemistry for a preexisting library of E3-ligand-linker adducts bearing azide moieties. As a proof-of-concept target, BRD4 was chosen, yielding amide-linked BRD4-targeting PROTACs. By combining phosphine-functionalized JQ1 derivatives with 72 selected azide building blocks, reactions were performed on a 5 L scale in 384-well plates, achieving a mean LC-MS conversion of approximately 65%. Spiking experiments confirmed that the phosphine starting materials had no significant impact on BRD4 degradation, supporting the direct biological evaluation of crude reaction mixtures in the presence of residual starting material. Cellular screening identified 23 hits at 250 nM screening concentration, reducing BRD4 levels below 40%. Two resynthesized and purified PROTACs were subsequently validated, displaying pDC50 values of 8.2 and 7.0 and a Dmax of 90% and 96%, respectively. This work establishes traceless Staudinger ligation as a complementary D2B strategy for the rapid discovery of amide-linked PROTACs.

papers.title: Matrix Gla Protein deficiency reveals a previously unrecognized mucosal calcification in the mouse airways
papers.abstract: Tracheal calcification is a common finding that is considered to have limited clinical significance when detected most often in elderly individuals. Despite its frequent occurrence, the cellular and molecular mechanisms at the origin of tracheal calcification remain largely unexplored. In this context, we aimed to characterize the development of tracheal calcification, and to determine the role of matrix Gla protein (MGP), a major inhibitor of ectopic calcification whose genetic or pharmacologic deficiency is associated with premature tracheal calcification in humans. We found that wild-type mice undergo an unexpected early physiologic calcification of the tracheal cartilage rings beginning around one month after birth. This calcification progresses in a dynamic rostro-caudal sequence through a process involving terminal differentiation of tracheal chondrocytes. These findings challenge the prevailing view that tracheal cartilage is a permanent hyaline cartilage and instead reveals an early and highly organized physiologic calcification process. Furthermore, our findings further identify MGP as a key regulator of calcification within the respiratory tract. Indeed, MGP deficiency not only markedly accelerates tracheal cartilage calcification through a similar pattern and mechanism but also induces a previously unrecognized calcification of the tracheal mucosa, a lesion absent in wild-type mice. These alterations could partly explain the respiratory manifestations observed in MGP-deficient patients having Keutel syndrome, which include dyspnea, cough, stridor, and recurrent infections, symptoms previously being mainly attributed to calcification of the tracheal cartilage rings.

papers.title: Melanoidins Suppress Cucumber and Tomato Diseases Incited by Pathogens that are Oomycetes, Bacteria and a Virus
papers.abstract: We recently reported that solutions of the nitrogenous compounds melanoidins (M), that are formed during the final stages of the Maillard Reaction, are inducers of plant resistance (Elad et al. 2026). M promoted immunity and induced disease resistance through an effect on the transcriptome, primarily through the salicylic acid pathway. Here we tested the effect of M on plant diseases that are caused by Oomycetes, bacteria and a tobamovirus. Drench and spray of M suppressed Pythium aphanidermatum damping off in cucumber, cucumber downy mildew (Pseudoperonospera cubensis), tomato late blight (Phytophthora infestans), bacterial speck (Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato), bacterial canker (Clavibacter michiganensis subsp. michiganensis) and the Tobamovirus Tomato brown rugose fruit virus (ToBRFV) in tomato. In various experiments control was achieved by concentrations of 0.03 and 0.1% and on older and younger leaves and even in long term experiments where the M was applied for ca 11 weeks. It can be concluded that the disease resistance inducer M can suppress soilborne and foliar diseases that are caused by Oomycetes, bacteria and a virus of the genus Tobamovirus, in addition to the fungal pathogen Botrytis cinerea reported earlier.

papers.title: Distinct Roles of ADP and Magnesium in the Structural Remodeling and Higher-Order Assembly of Peroxiredoxin 2
papers.abstract: 2-Cys peroxiredoxins (Prxs) undergo oligomeric transitions linked to peroxidase and chaperone activities, but the contributions of nucleotides and cations to lipid-dependent assembly remain unclear. We examined phosphatidylserine (PS)-induced Prx2 oligomers using biochemical assays and high-speed atomic force microscopy (HS-AFM). Both wild-type (WT) and P44A/S76A mutant (MT) Prx2 formed chaperone-active oligomers, although MT assembled more slowly and exhibited a more compact lateral geometry. Mg disassembled both oligomers, whereas ADP alone predominantly disassembled WT. Under combined Mg-ADP conditions, HS-AFM directly captured oligomer disassembly in both proteins, and separate experiments demonstrated higher-molecular-weight (HMW) assembly. WT HMW assemblies exhibited greater heights and stronger Mant-ADP co-elution than MT. Structural predictions suggested altered local Ser76-mediated contacts without major backbone changes. These results distinguish PS-induced functional switching from Mg- and ADP-dependent remodeling and support, without directly proving, a disassembly-reassembly route to HMW formation.

papers.title: Decoupled Surface Engineering Enables Cell-Interactive Edible Microcarriers across Food-Grade Polysaccharides
papers.abstract: Edible microcarriers for cultivated meat must support cell expansion while also contributing appropriately to the properties of the final food product. Food-grade polysaccharides exemplify this design challenge: despite their desirable food-related functions, they generally provide limited support for cell adhesion. This limitation calls for a strategy that introduces cell-interactive functionality without constraining bulk material selection. Here, we developed a decoupled surface-engineering strategy in which a poly-L-lysine/tannic acid (PLL/TA) interface is constructed on preformed polysaccharide microcarriers to enable cell-supportive functionality to emerge through interactions with the culture environment. On alginate microcarriers, PLL/TA modification markedly enhanced initial cell attachment, with 83% of modified microcarriers supporting attached cells compared with no detectable attachment on bare alginate. Cell-covered area subsequently reached 63.74% by Day 6, compared with 9.64% on PLL-coated microcarriers and negligible coverage on bare alginate. The PLL/TA interface promoted the recruitment of culture-medium proteins, including fibronectin, supporting an adaptive mechanism in which a cell-supportive interface develops through protein recruitment rather than predefined protein presentation. Importantly, the same surface modification enhanced early cell attachment when extended to pectin and carrageenan microcarriers and to Hanwoo bovine and Handon porcine muscle cells. On carrageenan microcarriers, the proportion of cell-bearing microcarriers increased from 30% to 100% for Hanwoo bovine cells and from 10% to 100% for Handon porcine cells following PLL/TA modification. These findings establish an adaptive and transferable surface-engineering strategy that enables cell-interactive functionality to be engineered separately from bulk material selection, expanding the design space for edible microcarriers in cultivated meat production.

papers.title: Development of a Thyroid Cancer to Lung Metastasis-on-a-Chip Model
papers.abstract: Background: Study of the metastatic cascade in differentiated non-medullary thyroid cancer (NMTC) is hampered by the relative lack of preclinical models that metastasize from primary tumors to other organs. We previously identified regulator of calcineurin 1 isoform 4 (RCAN1.4) as a suppressor of NMTC cell growth, invasion, and metastasis using in vitro systems and tail vein injections in immunocompromised mice. We then reported a microfluidic device mimicking the mouse tail vein injection where cancer cells were allowed to flow directly to lung organoid constructs. We now report the development of a full primary tumor to lung metastasis-on-a-chip (MOC) model for TC. Methods: Resin molds for primary and secondary sites connected by a channel were 3D printed and filled with polydimethylsiloxane to create a molded silicone elastomer. The primary site was seeded with an organoid composed of a hyaluronic acid and collagen-based hydrogel into which FTC236 and HTh74 NMTC cells with and without knockdown of RCAN1.4 were engrafted. The secondary site consisted of a hydrogel organoid into which bronchial epithelial cells and lung fibroblasts were seeded. Culture media was circulated and movement of NMTC cells to the secondary site was assessed. Results: Both cell lines that expressed RCAN 1.4 metastasized to the secondary lung site. RCAN1.4-reduced FTC236 cells had increased metastatic behavior vs controls while HTh74 was less affected by RCAN1.4 loss, similar to prior studies. To determine if the MOC could be used for incorporation of immune components and therapeutic modeling, NK-92 cells were added and were shown to be reduce metastases for both cell lines in the presence or absence of RCAN1.4. Analysis of MOC circulating fluid revealed elevated levels of granzyme B, consistent with NK-92 cell activation. Cytokine profiling identified elevated probable NMTC and NK-92-derived factors. Conclusions: These results indicate that NMTC metastatic behavior can be modeled using a novel MOC system for mechanistic and preclinical therapeutic studies.

papers.title: Parsimonious Creatures: Building Gene Regulatory Networks Robust to Somatic Evolution
papers.abstract: For early multicellular life to have formed and maintained cellular organization, preventing loss of controlled cell replication due to somatic evolution was of critical importance, and remains important to this day for control of cancer. We study how gene regulatory networks (GRNs) can be designed to slow the divergence of somatic clonal lineages in the context of early multicellular life. We model the mutation of GRNs within simplified 12-celled organisms we term "parsimonious creatures", who must replicate from a single cell to 12 cells and then prevent replication past 12 cells to maximize fitness. We found two minimal motifs can achieve these goals, but both are prone to breakdown through somatic evolution: The feedforward motif, which is loosely regulating but relatively robust, and the simple step motif, which uses strong interactions and feedback to form memoryless ultrasensitivity, but is fragile. These simple motifs may be duplicated to form redundant networks via one of two structures: averaging redundancy, which averages multiple sources of information, and min redundancy, which adopts the most conservative source. Averaging redundancy uniformly slows somatic evolution, while min redundancy stalls somatic evolution until neutral mutations accumulate. Either may be superior dependent on life history. However, averaging redundancy slowly increases fitness as the network becomes larger, but large min redundancy networks eventually become "paralyzed", increasing the probability of senescence and reducing fitness. These GRN designs are idealized, yet provide imperfect solutions with fundamental tradeoffs, offering insight as to why somatic evolution remains an incompletely solved problem for multicellular life.

papers.title: Relative expression of THY1 and PDGFRA in equine endometrosis in relation to severity, histopathological features and endometrial transcripts
papers.abstract: Equine endometrosis is a degenerative uterine disease characterized by periglandular fibrosis and represents a major cause of subfertility in mares. While stromal cell activation results in pathological tissue remodeling, the involvement of cell-surface integrators (THY1) and growth factor receptors (PDGFRA) was not researched. This study evaluated the relative mRNA expression of THY1 and PDGFRA across Kenney and Doig (KD) endometrosis categories and specific histopathological features. Additionally, transcriptomic correlation profiles between target genes and markers of myofibroblast differentiation (ACTA2), cellular proliferation (MKI67), and steroid hormone receptors (ESR1, PGR) were analyzed. Endometrial samples (n = 47) were quantified using RT-qPCR. Relative mRNA expression of THY1 differed significantly across KD categories (p = 0.014), exhibiting a transient upregulation in category IIA compared with category I (p = 0.009) and category IIB (p = 0.002). Furthermore, THY1 relative mRNA expression was significantly elevated in tissues with glandular basal lamina disruption (p = 0.022). Conversely, PDGFRA relative mRNA expression remained stable across disease categories (p > 0.05). THY1 relative mRNA expression correlated very strongly with ACTA2 ({rho} = 0.875, p < 0.001) and strongly with ESR1 ({rho} = 0.652, p < 0.001). PDGFRA relative mRNA expression exhibited a very strong positive correlation with ESR1 ({rho} = 0.864, p < 0.001) and a strong positive correlation with MKI67 ({rho} = 0.674, p < 0.001). These results indicate that THY1 transcription is transiently induced during early stromal remodeling and basal lamina loss, whereas PDGFRA maintains constitutive transcript stability. Observed co-expression profiles reflect statistical co-variation among stromal remodeling, proliferative, and steroid-responsive cell populations in bulk tissue.

papers.title: A shared wireless acquisition core for cortical and peripheral recordings in freely moving mice
papers.abstract: Experiments in freely moving mice often require simultaneous recording of cortical, muscle and movement signals, but adding channels and peripheral sensors increases headstage burden and acquisition complexity. We developed an eight-channel wireless headstage that records six cortical channels and two neck-electrode channels, together with synchronized acceleration. Reassigning electrodes enables cardiac recording with the same electronics. The 13*11*3 mm board forms part of an approximately 1.2-g head-mounted assembly, with the battery carried separately on the back. With inputs internally shorted, root-mean-square noise was 0.176V over 0.5-100 Hz. In four mice with chemically induced seizures, recordings resolved distributed cortical activity and animal-level spectral changes. Subject-dependent evaluation of the seizure detector yielded an overlap-based event F1 of 0.893 +/- 0.022. During pseudo-online replay, inference-software processing took 46.394 +/- 0.363 ms per update. In a separate cohort, recordings revealed distinct coherence patterns associated with movement and social behavior, highlighting potential as biomarkers of behavior-related neural activity. Together, these results demonstrate concurrent cortical, muscle, and movement recording through a common acquisition chain, with electrode reassignment extending the same hardware to cardiac recording.

papers.title: Measuring the strength of selection and pollen limitation on flower colour along an urban rural cline in Hesperis matronalis
papers.abstract: Closely located urban and rural environments can differ in temperature, water availability, species diversity, and more. As a result, organisms in urban environments may experience different selection than those in rural environments. We investigated whether differences in selection might explain a previously identified urban-rural cline in the flower colour of Hesperis matronalis (dame's rocket). To explore whether plants in urban and rural environments are impacted by possible differences in pollinator availability or behavior, we performed a pollen supplementation experiment. We did not detect an effect of pollen supplementation on seed production in either setting (urban or rural), indicating that there is limited opportunity for any differences in pollinator availability or visitation to explain the cline in flower colour. We also measured the strength of selection acting on flower colour to investigate if it differed between urban and rural populations. In all but one population, we failed to detect significant linear or non-linear selection on flower colour, suggesting that selection on flower colour does not differ between urban and rural populations. Our results suggest that the urban-rural flower colour cline is likely not caused by differences in selection or pollen-limitation and may be due to stochastic forces.

papers.title: Widespread oscillatory suppression in autism persists in the absence of psychotropic medication.
papers.abstract: Purpose: Investigate the neural oscillatory activity associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) using electroencephalographic (EEG) recordings in children and adolescents. Compare the corresponding oscillatory power between ASD patients taking psychotropic medication with a drug-naive group. Methods: ASD diagnosis was done using DSM-IV and CARS (Childhood Autism Rating Scale). EEG recordings employed 22 scalp electrodes (10/20 system). ASD vs. neurotypical groups were matched for sex and age (5 females; average age: ~10 years old). We analyzed the resting state (eyes open) EEG power spectrum during ~2-minute recordings. The multitaper FFT method was used to estimate spectral power for the delta, theta, alpha, beta and gamma frequency bands. We pooled together data from several electrodes to compute comprehensive power spectra and assess the oscillatory behavior of macro brain regions. Results: We observed widespread (~4Hz - 20Hz) oscillatory suppression comprising the theta, alpha and beta frequency bands. The most widespread and robust ASD-associated power suppression was in the high theta and alpha bands. Delta and gamma bands showed no significant power change for any of the brain regions studied. Results from a subgroup of patients (N = 9) who never used psychotropics confirmed these findings, indicating that they are not an artifact of medication. Conclusion: Suppression in theta, alpha and beta oscillations may offer insights into the neurophysiological underpinnings of autism and could be used as an accessible and comprehensive tool in ASD diagnosis, regardless of the patients being or not on medication.

papers.title: Learning from Hi-C reveals nuclear dynamical reorganization in budding yeast across the cell cycle
papers.abstract: Hi-C contact maps provide population-averaged measurements of chromosomal contacts. Converting these measurements, however, into three-dimensional structures and associated dynamics remains an underdetermined problem. Existing approaches broadly fall into two classes. Data-driven reconstruction methods that infer either a consensus structure or an ensemble of conformations, but do not inform on chromosome dynamics. Physics-based models, which generate dynamical trajectories, but require prior assumptions about nuclear geometry, chromatin mechanics, tethering, or molecular interactions. Here, we bridge these approaches using the Full-Inversion Chromatin model, a data-driven whole-genome polymer framework that learns an effective force field directly from Hi-C contact probabilities, integrated with Serpentine, a tool to quantify contact-map discrepancies while accounting for differences in sequencing coverage and sparsity. This generates structural ensembles of chromosomes and effective chromatin dynamics. We apply this method at 5-kb resolution to Saccharomyces cerevisiae in G1, mid-S, S/G2, G2/M, anaphase, and quiescence. Without explicitly imposing the spindle pole body, centromere or telomere tethering, predefined chromatin states, or nuclear-envelope interactions, the inferred ensembles recover these major features of yeast nuclear organization. Importantly, although dynamical information is not used during model training, the resulting polymer trajectories reproduce the subdiffusive scaling and chromosomal variations of independently measured chromatin motion. The model further predicts heterogeneous mobility along chromosomes and a distinctive telomere-dependent dynamical organization. Thus, population-averaged Hi-C contacts contain sufficient information to infer not only three-dimensional genome organization, but also effective, locus-dependent chromatin dynamics.

papers.title: A global post-transcriptional regulator directs Acinetobacter baumannii carbon preference and gut colonization
papers.abstract: Acinetobacter baumannii is a multidrug-resistant pathogen that colonizes the gut, increasing the risk of subsequent infection and transmission. Recent work showed that A. baumannii catabolizes ornithine, a non-preferred carbon source, to colonize the gut. However, the mechanisms of carbon preference were unknown in A. baumannii. Here, experimental evolution identified the conserved RNA-binding protein CsrA as a regulator of carbon preference in A. baumannii, a previously unreported CsrA function. RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing (RIP-Seq) revealed hundreds of CsrA-associated transcripts. A. baumannii CsrA directly bound and repressed expression of the ast arginine/ornithine catabolic operons. The Pseudomonas aeruginosa CsrA homolog RsmA repressed arginine/ornithine catabolic operon expression, suggesting this CsrA function extends to other bacterial taxa. Finally, CsrA was required for competitive fitness during A. baumannii gut colonization. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized role for a global regulator in A. baumannii carbon preference and persistence in the gut, a critical reservoir for multidrug-resistant pathogens.

papers.title: High-content screening identifies FDA-approved activators of mitophagy
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial diseases are highly heterogeneous disorders caused by defects in oxidative phosphorylation, for which only limited therapeutic options are available. The elimination of dysfunctional mitochondria via mitophagy activation is an attractive strategy to treat several mitochondrial diseases, irrespective of the underlying genetic defect. To identify pharmacological activators of this pathway, we performed a high-content screening of 1,971 FDA-approved compounds using cellular reporters of TFEB nuclear translocation and mitophagy. This screening identified 294 compounds that promoted TFEB translocation, nine of which increased the number of mitolysosomes without compromising cell viability or damaging mitochondria. Among the selected compounds, Meptazinol and Ponatinib emerged as the top-ranked mitophagy inducers in fibroblasts from patients with complex I and IV deficiency, respectively, and were prioritised for further characterisation. However, they did not rescue the bioenergetic defect, suggesting that the stimulation of mitophagy per se is not sufficient to ameliorate the OXPHOS defect in mitochondrial diseases. Overall, our findings establish a scalable platform for the identification of pharmacological activators of TFEB and identify candidate compounds for therapeutic modulation of mitophagy.

papers.title: Sex-linked genomic variation reveals reproductive skew and male-biased dispersal in polygynous sea lions
papers.abstract: Sex-biased dispersal and the resulting asymmetry in gene flow are important factors in evolution. However, their quantification in natural populations remains challenging, not least because sex-specific reproductive skew, as reflected in the mating system, further influences the relative contributions of males and females to the genetic pool of subsequent generations. Incorporating information from mitochondria (MT) and sex chromosomes (X, Y) alongside the more commonly used autosomal markers (AUT) provides a promising framework to partly disentangle confounding processes. Here, we exemplify this approach in two closely related, polygynous species with observational evidence for male-biased dispersal, the Galapagos sea lion (GSL) and the Steller sea lion (SSL). Using whole-genome resequencing data, we leveraged genetic variation among all four genomic compartments, representing genetic variation with female-only (MT), mixed (X, AUT) and male-only (Y) inheritance, to obtain information on the mating system and test for sex-specific migration across geographic and environmental boundaries. For GSL, genomic signatures were consistent with mild polygyny and a moderately elevated rate of male migration, particularly across habitat boundaries. In SSL, male reproductive skew was substantially greater, and male-biased migration was more pronounced and less habitat-dependent. Our results align with the species' life history and support a link between mating system and dispersal, but were also impacted by confounding biological processes and bioinformatic choices. This study highlights the value and challenges of population genomic approaches integrating multiple genomic compartments to infer variation in individual behaviours.

papers.title: EWSR1::ATF1 hyperactivation via TRIM11 depletion triggers lethal metabolic rewiring in clear cell sarcoma
papers.abstract: Clear cell sarcoma (CCS) is an ultra-rare and aggressive soft tissue sarcoma driven by the EWSR1::ATF1 fusion oncoprotein. Currently, no effective and well-tolerated treatment options are available to CCS patients. Direct inhibition of fusion transcription factors is precluded by the absence of defined ligand-binding pockets, whereas their abundance is under the control of the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), offering an alternative avenue for biology-guided treatment. Here we show the abundance of EWSR1::ATF1 is tightly regulated by the UPS, and that release of this constraint is lethal to CCS cells. A reporter-based CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screen of UPS components identified TRIM11 as an E3 ligase that regulates turnover of EWSR1::ATF1, which it recognises as a neosubstrate without altering wild-type EWSR1 or ATF1. Depletion of TRIM11 increased nuclear fusion protein abundance, amplified the fusion-driven transcriptional programs and reduced viability. Proteomic analysis identified the cataplerotic enzyme phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase 1 (PCK1), a direct EWSR1::ATF1 target, as the key mediator of lethal effects of fusion hyperactivation. Extracellular flux analysis, isotope tracing and quantitative metabolomics revealed excessive cataplerotic carbon withdrawal and impaired oxidative phosphorylation as the underlying mechanism. In patient tumors, high PCK1 expression associated with metastatic transcriptome programs and disease presentation, as well as shorter survival. Taken together, we report that hyperactivation of EWSR1::ATF1 opens a metabolic vulnerability, establishing TRIM11 as an actionable dependency and PCK1 as a candidate prognostic biomarker in CCS.

papers.title: A TMEM175 Mutation Disrupts the Lysosomal-Mitochondrial Axis Causing Short QT Syndrome and Sudden Cardiac Death
papers.abstract: Short QT Syndrome (SQTS) is a rare cardiac channelopathy characterized by abnormally short QTc intervals and increased sudden cardiac death (SCD) risk. Only 20-30% of SQTS cases have been linked to genetic mutations, typi-cally in surface membrane ion channels. We identified a novel lysosomal TMEM175 gene mutation (p.Arg377His) in 7 patients in a family with SQTS and SCD. Genetic analyses, including whole exome sequencing in the family and rare-variant burden testing in [~]118,000 UK Biobank participants, sug-gested an association between TMEM175 rare variants and QT interval short-ening. Functional studies in CRISPR-engineered mice and patient-specific induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) revealed that TMEM175R377H causes shortened QT intervals and hastened repolariza-tion, respectively, as well an increased arrhythmia susceptibility. Isolated TMEM175R377H cardiomyocytes showed action potential duration (APD) abbre-viation, confirmed in whole TMEM175R377H mouse hearts and patient-specific iPSC-CM monolayers. In silico and electron microscopy studies showed that TMEM175R377H disrupts lysosomal-mitochondrial interactions, leading to mito-chondrial dysfunction, as evidenced by the reduced maximal respiration and spare respiratory capacity, with reduced ATP production, IKATP activation, and APD shortening. This mutation represents the first non-sarcolemmal ion chan-nel defect associated with SQTS and high SCD risk, potentially expanding the genetic landscape of the disease.

papers.title: Homeostatic fibroblast niche collapse in clinically uninvolved skin marks a pre-fibrotic stage of systemic sclerosis
papers.abstract: Systemic sclerosis, or scleroderma, is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by vasculopathy, immune dysregulation, and progressive fibrosis of the skin and internal organs. Heterogeneous clinical presentation and polygenic risk complicate our understanding of disease mechanisms and the path to effective therapy. Single-cell analyses have revealed substantial transcriptional diversity in skin, but disease-associated reprogramming remains poorly defined. To address this, we performed high-resolution spatial transcriptomic profiling of paired clinically uninvolved and clinically affected scleroderma donor skin alongside healthy controls. We identified a continuum of cellular, molecular, and spatial changes to the stroma that were already evident in clinically uninvolved tissue yet remained distinct from the broader and more advanced changes in paired fibrotic biopsies. Uninvolved skin was comparable to healthy tissue by clinical and histopathological assessment, but distinguishable by the numerical reduction, transcriptional reprogramming, and spatial isolation of LGR5+SCARA5+PI16+ progenitor fibroblasts. In parallel, the dermal vascular smooth muscle compartment shifted from a contractile to a synthetic, activated state, suggesting reprogramming that begins before overt fibrosis. Cell neighborhood analysis revealed that progenitor fibroblasts occupy dense stromal niches in healthy skin that collapse in clinically uninvolved tissue, replaced by isolated, disease-associated fibroblast populations. These data indicate that clinically uninvolved skin occupies an intermediate stage along the pathologic continuum of scleroderma, establishing a framework for strategies to allow early diagnosis and preserve homeostatic fibroblast niches before irreversible tissue remodeling and fibrotic commitment.

papers.title: spearfish: ultrafast Δ-mapping of long reads to redundant transcriptomes
papers.abstract: In a transcriptome, isoforms share most of their sequence, and gene families add further near-copies. Yet most long-read mappers treat each isoform as a separate target and repeat seeding, chaining and alignment for each. We introduce spearfish, a long-read mapper built for this redundancy. Its delta mapping ({Delta}-mapping) computes each target's alignment-score difference from the best candidate. It skips sequence that all candidates share, which cannot change the difference, and aligns where they differ once per distinct sequence rather than once per target. Seeds come from locally consistent parsing (LCP), so every isoform that contains an exon receives the same seeds in its interior. Collapsing them gives a core graph, a de Bruijn-like graph whose size is bounded by the distinct exonic sequence plus a small term per splice junction, independent of the number of isoforms. Over this graph, spearfish computes the exact colinear chaining score of every candidate transcript, sharing dynamic-programming state among transcripts via a procedure which we prove is equivalent to chaining on each transcript separately. Across RNA-seq experiments, using 32 threads, spearfish maps reads 26-83x faster than minimap2 in at most a seventh of the memory, and 2.6-11.3x faster than lr-kallisto's pseudoalignment. On simulated reads it ranks the true transcript first more often than minimap2 on HiFi reads and within 0.5 percentage points of it on ONT reads at 95% accuracy. When using spearfish's {Delta}-mapping with oarfish for abundance estimation, the abundance estimates match or improve on those that make use of minimap2's alignments on both simulated reads (especially when they are untrimmed) and on seven SG-NEx runs with spike-ins, and quantification is 3.0-8.8x faster than lr-kallisto in going from reads to abundances.

papers.title: Subcellular Spatial Profiling Unveils Links Between Neuritic Plaques with Selective Tau Vulnerability in Alzheimer's Disease
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) features widespread extracellular amyloid-{beta} plaques but selective intraneuronal tau accumulation in cortical layers II/III and V, while layer IV remains relatively resistant. Here, we combined subcellular spatial transcriptomics with co-registered A{beta} and pTau immunohistochemistry to determine why neurons exposed to comparable plaque-associated pathology differ in somatic pTau accumulation. Plaque-associated neuritic stress occurred similarly across layers, but layer IV neurons showed attenuated pTau accumulation and reduced somatic expression of a shared neurite-soma stress program involving DCTN1, CALM3, NORAD, and PIN1. Trajectory analysis within layers identified tau-vulnerable and resistant neuronal states implicating calcium signaling, retrograde transport, and lysosomal function. Notably, astrocytic APOE-neuronal LRP1 co-expression increased significantly along the pTau-vulnerable trajectory, and APOE {epsilon}4 was associated with stronger coupling of local plaque pathology to pTau-associated molecular programs. These findings reveal neuronal programs and neuron-glia interactions underlying selective tau vulnerability and resistance in AD, highlighting potential tau-targeting therapeutics.

papers.title: Measuring neuronal input-output operations in vivo with random access projection microscopy
papers.abstract: Neurons transform thousands of synaptic inputs into spiking output, and understanding this transformation requires measuring many submicron synapses at millisecond timescales in vivo. Here we present SLAP2, a two-photon random access projection microscope with no per-target access time cost, yielding over 5-fold faster imaging than existing methods, and performant real-time hardware motion correction. Flexible scanning modes enable measurement of hundreds of synapses at ~200 Hz, >800 synapses volumetrically at 50-100 Hz, and compartment-resolved dendritic voltage at 2-10 kHz in behaving mice. Simultaneous dendritic glutamate and somatic calcium imaging in visual cortex pyramidal neurons revealed nonlinear input-output amplification of stimulus onset and preferred stimulus orientation responses. Amplified features are associated with spatially organized inputs and stronger trial-to-trial coupling between synaptic activity and somatic output. These measurements establish SLAP2 as a powerful tool for recording intricate patterns of subcellular fluorescence dynamics in behaving animals.

papers.title: Host availability, climate and pupal-stage ecology shape the predicted environmental suitability of the New World screwworm across Central and South America
papers.abstract: Background: The New World screwworm, Cochliomyia hominivorax, causes primary myiasis in warm-blooded vertebrates. Its recent resurgence in Central America has renewed the need for spatial tools that identify environmentally suitable areas and surveillance gaps. Most previous distribution models have emphasized climate and livestock, whereas ecological constraints acting during the free-living pupal stage have rarely been incorporated. Methods: We compiled 2,461 georeferenced occurrence reports from the literature across Central and South America and linked them to climate, livestock density, forest cover and superficial soil predictors. Four sequential (nested) logistic models quantified the incremental contribution of predictor blocks, compared using likelihood-ratio tests, AIC and discrimination metrics. Logistic regression and Random Forest were then compared using five-fold spatial block cross-validation, which we treat as the primary measure of generalisation, and an independent municipality-level 70:30 train-test split. Variable importance was assessed using Random Forest Mean Decrease Accuracy together with partial-dependence profiles. Because presence and pseudo-absence classes were balanced before fitting, model outputs are interpreted as relative environmental suitability rather than absolute probability of occurrence. Results: The literature database represented 2,589 infected hosts, dominated by cattle, pigs, dogs and humans. Across the sequential models, AUC increased from 0.780 for climate alone to 0.898 with livestock density, 0.908 with forest cover and 0.918 with superficial soil properties; the increment attributable to the soil block ({Delta}AUC = 0.010) was smaller than the between-fold variability observed under spatial cross-validation (SD 0.049) and is therefore reported as suggestive rather than established. Sheep and horse density and cold-quarter soil temperature showed the highest Mean Decrease Accuracy values, while silt texture ranked above cattle density and forest cover. Under spatial block cross-validation Random Forest was markedly more stable than the GLM (mean AUC 0.926 {+/-} 0.049 versus 0.814 {+/-} 0.157) and was retained as the final model. On the independent municipality-level test set it achieved AUC 0.981, TSS 0.824, sensitivity 0.850 and specificity 0.972, values we regard as optimistic relative to the spatially blocked estimates. Predicted suitability was highest across Central America and parts of northern and tropical South America. Conclusions: C. hominivorax occurrence was associated with interacting climatic, host and landscape conditions. Superficial soil variables added a small, biologically interpretable signal consistent with constraints acting during pupation, but one that lies within the uncertainty of our spatial validation and requires confirmation with independent data. The maps estimate relative environmental suitability rather than infection incidence, and are intended to identify areas where surveillance could be strengthened rather than to guide control operations directly.

papers.title: Hybrid RY-mers increase aDNA alignment sensitivity
papers.abstract: One of the key steps in ancient DNA data analysis is the accurate identification of endogenous short reads that originate from the ancient genome. Currently, this step is performed using general-purpose sequence aligners, such as BWA-aln, with parameter settings optimized for sensitivity. This approach results in increased runtime, even relative to standard DNA alignment workflows, and is not sufficient for aligning samples that are highly divergent from a reference database. We introduce hybrid RY-mers, a seed construct designed to incorporate aDNA-specific sequence damage. We adapt hybrid RY-mers to the existing concept of multi-context seeds and implement them in the read aligner strobealign. On simulated genomic and metagenomic datasets, we show that hybrid RY-mers result in higher mapping accuracy, while also reducing runtime by 4-6 times compared to the state-of-the-art aDNA alignment method BWA-aln. Furthermore, substituting aDNA aligner MALT in the metagenomic tool-suite aMeta with our new alignment approach demonstrated that aMeta gave a faster and less memory consuming detection of ancient taxa present in the samples.

papers.title: pLM-bVAE: protein language model-enhanced binary representation improves quantum annealing-based protein sequence design
papers.abstract: Quantum annealing (QA) has been explored as an approach for protein design in vast combinatorial sequence spaces. Applying QA to protein sequence design requires amino acid sequences to be encoded as binary vectors, and optimized vectors to be decoded back into amino acid sequences. Thus, both the quality of binary encoding and sequence reconstruction accuracy are important for effective QA-based optimization. Binary variational autoencoder (bVAE) has been used to map protein sequences to binary representations in QA-based protein sequence design. However, bVAE was originally developed for natural language modeling, and its suitability for proteins has not been systematically evaluated. Here, we present pLM-bVAE, which incorporates protein representations derived from a pretrained protein language model (pLM) into the original bVAE model. In computational experiments on three public protein variant datasets, pLM-bVAE showed higher sequence reconstruction accuracy and binary encoding performance than bVAE. Moreover, we incorporated pLM-bVAE into a QA-based protein sequence design framework. Across all three datasets, pLM-bVAE generated more high-scoring sequences with greater sequence dissimilarity from the training and validation data than bVAE. Our results demonstrate that pLM-bVAE provides an effective binary representation for improving QA-based protein sequence design. Availability The source code used in this manuscript is available at https://github.com/hueda8/pLM-bVAE.

papers.title: Joint protein-DNA language modeling enables prediction and engineering of DNA recognition specificity
papers.abstract: Protein-DNA recognition specificity underlies transcriptional regulation, DNA replication, chromatin remodeling and genome editing. Protein-DNA recognition depends on both interacting sequences, yet language models that learn this cross-molecular dependence explicitly during pretraining remain limited. Here, we developed the Protein-DNA Language Models (PDLMs), interaction-aware language models that jointly represent protein and DNA sequences. PDLMs were built by continued pretraining from ESM2 with masked language modeling on paired protein-DNA sequences. A shared encoder places amino acids and nucleotides in the same molecular context, enabling conditional sequence scoring and transferable pair representations. We further introduced a domain-aware masking strategy that increased masking probability within DNA-binding domains to strengthen learning of interaction-relevant regions. Across downstream tasks, PDLMs improved protein-DNA pair classification relative to independent-encoder baselines and supported prediction of mutation-associated binding changes. Zero-shot scoring recovered known changes in DNA-recognition specificity and prioritized variants with higher editing activity. Learned representations also supported cross-study prediction of base editor activity. After fine-tuning on transcription factor binding data, PDLMs predicted DNA motifs directly from protein sequences. Together, PDLMs provide a framework for interaction-aware biomolecular language modeling, with potential applications in protein engineering and genome editing.

papers.title: Rates of molecular and morphological evolution are uncoupled across the eukaryote Tree of Life
papers.abstract: A vast degree of phenotypic variation can be seen across lineages of eukaryotes. Although at least part of this diversity has a genomic basis, it is unclear whether there are broad-scale links that can be detected between rates of genomic and phenotypic evolution. The presence of a correlation would imply the action of shared drivers, such as mutational or adaptive processes that occur on a genome- and organism-wide scale. We investigated this question by using a phylogenetic approach to test for correlations between molecular and morphological evolutionary rates. We analysed 60 data sets of combined nucleotide sequences and discrete morphological characters, representing a diverse range of eukaryotes. Using a maximum-likelihood phylogenetic approach based on sister-pair contrasts, we found very little evidence of any link between rates of molecular and morphological evolution, a striking result given the scale and taxonomic breadth of our analyses. Our results point to contrasting evolutionary dynamics underlying genomes and phenotypic traits; these have led to greater variation in morphological evolutionary rates across lineages, whereas molecular evolution is more clocklike. Our study reveals the discrepancies in evolutionary drivers that act at the genomic and phenotypic levels across the eukaryotic Tree of Life.

papers.title: Language-guided domain adaptation improves protein sequence representations for antimicrobial resistance analysis
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR), particularly antibiotic resistance in bacterial pathogens, complicates infectious disease management. Because bacterial resistance is often mediated by protein functions, including antibiotic inactivation and efflux, protein sequence analysis provides a molecular basis for digital AMR surveillance and therapeutic intervention. We developed BacLLM, a language guided protein representation framework that integrates annotation-derived functional knowledge into protein language model representations for AMR analysis in WHO priority bacterial pathogens. Through sequence enhancement, semantic enrichment of UniProt annotations, and cross modal contrastive learning, BacLLM transfers LLM encoded annotation priors into the sequence encoder. Compared with baselines, BacLLM provided more informative representations for resistance-gene identification and mechanism prediction, captured resistance associated mutational signals at single-residue resolution, and preserved taxonomic relationships not reflected by phenotype based clinical groupings. Moreover, BacLLM recovered resistance associated functional organization within a TolC-centered protein association network, prioritizing proteins with low sequence identity to TolC but predicted structural similarity to TolC. Extending from AMR characterization to therapeutic prioritization, BacLLM also improved strain-level phage host matching for phage therapy candidate prioritization. Together, these findings establish BacLLM as a protein representation framework supporting AMR surveillance, functional characterization, and therapeutic candidate prioritization.

papers.title: Rab10 and Arhgef7 interact to promote axon extension by linking vesicle supply and exocytosis
papers.abstract: The formation of functional neural circuits begins with the extension of a single axon by immature neurons. Axon elongation requires an expansion of the plasma membrane that depends on the polarization of vesicle trafficking and exocytosis. It is not completely understood how the increased transport of vesicles into the growing axon is linked to their subsequent insertion into the plasma membrane. An analysis of early stages of neuronal differentiation indicates that an asymmetry in neurite length precedes axon specification and the accumulation of PPVs in the nascent axon. We show that increasing the transport of vesicles in unpolarized neurons is sufficient to promote the extension of additional axons. This effect indicates that an increased supply of vesicles stimulates their subsequent insertion into the membrane to allow neurite growth. The link between vesicle transport and exocytosis is mediated by the interaction of Rab10 with Arhgef7. Rab10 stimulates Arhgef7 activity on PPVs as a GEF for Cdc42b to promote axon extension through exocyst-dependent exocytosis, suggesting that their interaction links the increased supply of PPVs to their exocytosis.

papers.title: Harnessing catalytic knowledge to guide enzyme discovery and evolution with AlphaEnzyme
papers.abstract: Retrieving an enzyme for a target reaction provides a starting point for evolution, but predicting how to improve it remains difficult. This requires connecting evolutionary information with the structural and chemical context of catalysis. Here we present AlphaEnzyme, an enzyme foundation model built on a structure-grounded representation of an enzyme paired with its reaction, from which catalytic compatibility, kinetics and mutational response are read out together. On a time-separated benchmark, AlphaEnzyme achieves a top-1 catalyst retrieval success rate of 30.1%, against 17.2% for the strongest baseline. Michaelis constant predictions achieve the highest rank correlations among the compared methods, reaching 0.64 for enzymes sharing at most 40% identity with the kinetic training set. The model also enriches high-fitness TrpB variants at a budget of 16 candidates without target-specific fitness training. In prospective transaminase engineering, several prioritized variants exceed the parent, with the best design yielding a 30.4-fold increase in product signal in a lysate-based assay while retaining (R)-selectivity. Together, AlphaEnzyme provides a common molecular basis for selecting starting enzymes and prioritizing sequence changes for their improvement.

papers.title: Metagenomic Insights into the Fecal Microbiome, Resistome, and Mobilome of Beef Cattle in Cow-Calf Operations in Florida, United States
papers.abstract: Food-producing animals are a focus of One Health approaches to antimicrobial resistance (AMR) as reservoirs of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria (ARB) and antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). We hypothesized that microbial composition, ARGs profiles, and mobile genetic element (MGE) profiles would differ by operation size and animal age group. Fecal samples from 162 cows and calves were combined into 54 composite samples, each comprising three animals of the same age group. Across operation sizes, Bacillota (51.4-64.9%), Bacteroidota (12.0-17.3%), Pseudomonadota (10.3-16.5%), and Actinomycetota (3.3-10.9%) were predominant phyla. Alpha diversity did not differ among operation sizes; however, cows exhibited greater observed richness, Shannon diversity, and Simpson diversity than calves (all P < 0.001). Microbial composition did not differ significantly among operation sizes (PERMANOVA, R{superscript 2} = 0.065, P = 0.609) but differed significantly between cows and calves (R{superscript 2} = 0.200, P < 0.001). Seventy-five ARGs representing 14 resistance classes were identified. Normalized ARG hit rates were higher in small operations (0.444) than in medium (0.278) and large operations (0.222; P = 0.088), whereas calves exhibited a higher estimated marginal mean normalized ARG hit rate than cows (0.383 vs. 0.247 hits/million reads; P < 0.001). Of 1,054 curated ARG hits, 23.9% occurred on predicted plasmid contigs, 0.9% on predicted viral contigs, and 7.1% on contigs containing insertion sequences. Overall findings demonstrate differences in fecal microbiome diversity and ARG abundance between cows and calves and indicate that predicted plasmids are associated with a notable proportion of ARG hits in Florida beef cow-calf operations.

papers.title: Characterization of Lactobacillus rhamnosus-Derived Extracellular Vesicles and Their Cellular Cytoprotective Effects Against Trimethylamine-Induced Oxidative Stress in Caco-2 Cells
papers.abstract: Dietary trimethylamine (TMA) underwent gut microbiota-mediated catabolism and subsequent hepatic oxidation to generate trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a key metabolic factor linked to vascular and colorectal diseases. While the systemic effects of circulating TMAO were heavily investigated, the direct localized cellular interactions of its precursor, TMA, at the intestinal epithelial level required further elucidation. This study characterized extracellular vesicles isolated from Lactobacillus rhamnosus (Lr-EVs) and evaluated their cytoprotective potential in an in vitro human intestinal Caco-2 cell model under TMA-induced stress. Exposure to a high concentration of TMA (20 mM) significantly reduced Caco-2 viability to 78.8%, triggered intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, and compromised tight junction integrity as observed via the disruption of Zonula Occludens-1 (ZO-1) alignment. Co-treatment with Lr-EVs (100-300 g/mL) counteracted this cellular toxicity, enhancing cell survival up to 172%. Quantitative PCR analysis revealed that Lr-EVs suppressed the transcriptional upregulation of the pro-inflammatory gene IL-1{beta}, restored the expression of the metabolic regulator SIRT1, and stabilized transcript levels of key mitochondrial-encoded electron transport chain genes (ND6, CYTB, CO1, and ATP6). Additionally, Lr-EVs exhibited intrinsic radical scavenging activities in cell-free ABTS and DPPH assays. These preliminary in vitro findings demonstrated that Lr-EVs mitigated TMA-induced cellular injury, oxidative stress, and junctional disruption at the transcriptomic level, supporting further investigation of probiotic-derived EVs as prospective cell-free functional ingredients.

papers.title: LOca-1: A minimal calcium-activated arginyl-specific orthocaspase from the Loki's Castle hydrothermal vent field
papers.abstract: Orthocaspases are prokaryotic homologs of metacaspases within the C14 family of cysteine proteases, yet their biochemical properties and cellular roles remain poorly understood. Here, we report the discovery and comprehensive characterization of LOca-1, a metagenome-derived orthocaspase from the Loki's Castle hydrothermal vent field. LOca-1 consists primarily of a single, conserved p20 catalytic domain and undergoes calcium-dependent activation through cleavage at a conserved arginine residue. Once activated, LOca-1 displays strict arginyl-specific proteolytic activity and strong selectivity for residues surrounding the cleavage site. The enzyme is both thermoactive and thermostable, exhibiting maximal activity at 65 {degrees}C and a melting temperature of approximately 72 {degrees}C. Structural modelling revealed conservation of the catalytic core relative to plant metacaspases despite substantial sequence divergence. To our knowledge, LOca-1 is only the second biochemically characterized orthocaspase and the first reported from a deep-sea hydrothermal vent environment. LOca-1 expands the known biochemical diversity of prokaryotic metacaspase homologs and provides insights into the properties of a minimal p20-domain orthocaspase. Together, our findings establish LOca-1 as a thermostable, calcium-activated arginyl-specific orthocaspase and provide a foundation for future studies of orthocaspase function in prokaryotes.

papers.title: EngA adopts multiple distinct conformational states during ribosome assembly
papers.abstract: Ribosome assembly, a highly coordinated and crucial cellular process, is assisted by various assembly factors, including GTPases. EngA, an essential P-loop GTPase, is involved in late-stage assembly of the 50S ribosomal subunit. The structures of 50S ribosome in complex with EngA-bound GMPPNP, and EngA-bound GDP alone, without 50S subunit, have been reported previously. However, the molecular mechanism of EngA GTP hydrolysis-assisted 50S maturation remains poorly understood, and structures of the 50S ribosome in complex with EngA-bound GDP have yet to be deciphered. We have reported cryo- EM structures of the Mycobacterium smegmatis 50S ribosome in complex with EngA-bound GTP{gamma}S or GDP at 2.8 - 3.5 [A] resolution. Structural analysis revealed that EngA and 50S subunit undergo a coordinated structural rearrangement, and an assembly intermediate is formed in which the stem-loop of H80 makes base-pair interactions with the junction of H89 and H90, forming a unique stem-loop-junction (SLJ) motif. EngA-bound GDP adopts distinctly different conformations in its ribosome-bound and unbound states. In summary, this study proposed a multi-state conformational model for EngA-assisted ribosome assembly.

papers.title: A Y-specific translocated gsdf copy is a candidate master sex-determining gene in common dab (Limanda limanda)
papers.abstract: Sex-determining systems in flatfishes are highly diverse, and even closely related species can differ in both sex-determining loci and heterogametic systems. In common dab (Limanda limanda), the genetic basis of sex determination has not yet been established. Here, we investigated sex determination using pooled whole-genome sequencing combined with long-read genome sequencing of females and males from Iceland and Norway. Genome-wide allele-frequency analyses identified sex-associated regions consistent with male heterogamety (XX/XY), with the strongest signal on chromosome 16. Comparison of the existing reference assembly, which represents an X haplotype at this locus, with a haplotype-resolved male PacBio HiFi assembly revealed a [~]21.5 kb Y-specific insertion on chromosome 16. The insertion showed complete coverage in male pools but little or no coverage in female pools from either population. It contained a translocated genomic segment including a copy of gonadal soma-derived factor (gsdf) and a predicted gene of unknown function. Comparative genomic analyses were consistent with this segment originating from an autosomal gsdf-containing region on chromosome 1. Given the recurrent recruitment of gsdf as a sex-determining factor in teleosts, we designate the Y-linked copy gsdfY and identify it as the strongest candidate for the master sex-determining gene in common dab. Additional broad sex-associated differentiation on chromosome 19 was restricted to the Icelandic samples and may reflect population-specific expansion of the sex-linked region, although its structural basis remains unresolved. Together, these findings provide the first genomic characterization of sex determination in common dab and demonstrate how gene duplication and translocation can contribute to the evolution of novel sex-determining systems in flatfishes.

papers.title: Receptor-proximal phosphoform organization precedes β2 integrin activation
papers.abstract: Receptor signaling is often framed as protein recruitment after stimulation, but whether receptor-proximal environments are organized in composition and phosphorylation state beforehand remains unclear. We used CD18-APEX2 proximity labeling and a spatial membrane reference to quantify proteins and phosphosites near leukocyte {beta}2 integrins. At rest, receptors, adaptors and Rap GTPases were preferentially represented relative to several catalytic classes. Parent-protein correction revealed spatial phosphoform organization, with 32% of 4,564 phosphosites deviating significantly from the distribution center and 56% of proteins with multiple quantified sites showing divergence beyond measurement error. Sustained activation altered 31% of phosphosites while 95.9% of proteins remained equivalent within {+/-}0.5 log2 and spatial phosphoform organization largely persisted. Most phosphorylation responses were shared across both labeling environments, whereas receptor-preferential changes were dominated by phosphosites. These findings suggest that receptor signaling can regulate pre-existing molecular states without extensive protein redistribution.

papers.title: Broad-spectrum in situ genetic reprogramming of native microbiomes
papers.abstract: Complex microbial communities are found throughout terrestrial, aquatic, and animal-associated ecosystems. Genetic modification of discrete microbial taxa within native communities represents a powerful tool to study and augment microbiome functions. Herein, we develop Synthetic Phage Assisted Reprogrammable and Targetable Addition (SPARTA) as a one-step strategy for packaging, delivering, and integrating large synthetic DNA into a broad range of native microbiomes. SPARTA leverages a broad-spectrum synthetic phage particle for in situ genome engineering within complex soil, freshwater, and mammalian fecal microbiomes, reprogramming 59 native species across 16 families. By modulating SPARTA components, we further demonstrated tunability of SPARTA towards targeted microbiome population. Additionally, we built a novel companion tool to quantitatively identify engineered taxa, named 16S crRNA-guided inference of bacterial engineering sequencing or ScRibe-seq. The SPARTA-ScRibe-seq pipeline delivered and validated functional synthetic gene clusters in diverse native microbiomes while preserving the original microbial community structure. Together, this novel genome engineering framework constitutes an end-to-end programmable platform for rational and customizable reprogramming of native microbiomes.

papers.title: Time-resolved single-cell screening reveals the dynamic regulatory architecture of human cardiogenesis
papers.abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) originates during early embryogenesis, yet when disease genes act cannot be determined from existing data. Human fetal heart atlases lack critical time points, and perturbation screens that systematically assess gene function currently profile at most a few time points. Here we combined single-cell CRISPR screening of 400 disease-relevant genes in cardioids, sampled daily over seven developmental days (~975,000 cells), with a matched multiome atlas. Perturbation phenotypes were strongly dependent on developmental stage. Perturbations that reshaped cell-fate allocation or gene expression were enriched for CHD-linked genes, and most acted already during progenitor stages. Timing was largely independent of the target gene's own expression, marking instead when a cell state became functionally dependent on it, and some effects persisted after expression declined. Consensus gene regulatory networks integrating perturbation and multiome data recovered stage-specific regulators and nominated HOXB2 and HOXB3 as candidate cardiac regulators. Many perturbations converged on shared downstream programmes, which were reorganised through differentiation. Effects correlated in progenitors were maintained in differentiated cells, split into distinct programmes, converged with other perturbations or disappeared entirely, indicating that gene function is highly context dependent. Beyond advancing our understanding of the developmental regulatory logic underlying CHD, our work provides a resource for developing context-dependent models for in silico prediction of perturbation effects.

papers.title: Where single-cell foundation models help: a benchmark of annotation, perturbation and regulatory inference against simple baselines
papers.abstract: Single-cell foundation models (FMs) are proposed as general tools for cell-type annotation, in silico perturbation and gene-regulatory-network (GRN) inference.
