To identify where they add value, we benchmarked five FMs (scGPT, Geneformer V1 and V2, Nicheformer, scFoundation), CellOracle, supervised perturbation models including STATE, and task-matched simple baselines on the same data, from K562 Perturb-seq screens and primary cells to healthy-donor and isogenic leukodystrophy brain organoids, a public organoid CRISPR screen and lung cancer biopsies. FMs were most useful when labels had to be transferred across species: from human to mouse lung, Nicheformer reached 0.98 accuracy and Geneformer V2 and scFoundation about 0.90, against 0.68 for the best baseline. Zero-shot in silico perturbations captured the direction of real responses in K562, with up to 75% of perturbations shifted in the expected direction (scFoundation, p < 1e-8), and Geneformer V2 networks recovered patient-level tumour differential expression better than co-expression (fold enrichment 2.9 versus 2.0). Within a species, FM embeddings annotated cells as accurately as principal components. In organoids, predicted knockout effects were largely explained by where the target is expressed, and an expression-matched control test isolated the gene-specific part, 12 to 35% of the effects. Isogenic Canavan and Krabbe organoids and 4H patient organoids, with one library per line and time point, did not yet separate methods from differences between clones and donors, which defines the replication needed for future validation. Fine-tuning changed classification accuracy but not knockout rankings. We release the benchmark, baselines, pipeline checks and the isogenic reference task as the fmaudit package, so that new models can be evaluated on the tasks where FMs already help.

papers.title: Contig-Resolved Genetic Context of Antimicrobial Resistome in Sediments of Two Contrasting Wastewater-Impacted Rivers
papers.abstract: River sediments harbor diverse antimicrobial resistance (AMR) determinants; however, gene abundance alone provides limited insight into their genomic context, mobility potential, and associated bacterial hosts. This study employed an assembly- and read-mapping metagenomic framework to surface-sediment metagenomes (40.78 Gb clean data) from two contrasting wastewater-impacted Indian rivers, Adyar (Chennai) and Musi (Hyderabad), retaining sample-, contig- and open reading frame level provenance. ARG-carrying contigs (ACCs; n = 2,402) were annotated for mobile genetic elements (MGEs), biocide/metal resistance genes (BMRGs), virulence factor genes (VFGs), nitrogen-cycling genes (NCycGs), and putative host taxonomy. The resistomes exhibited substantial diversity (264 ARG subtypes) and spatial heterogeneity, with subtype richness in the Adyar (up to 171 subtypes) than in the Musi, where richness progressively declined downstream. Rank IV determinants dominated ARG abundance (77.82%), whereas Rank I determinants accounted for only 9.89%. MGEs were detected on just 3.12% (75/2,402) of ACCs, predominantly comprising plasmid-like contigs and proximal ARG-MGE associations. Co-occurrence with BMRGs was observed on 386 ACCs, whereas VFGs were uncommon (26 ACCs) and primarily represented dual-annotated efflux and envelope-integrity determinants rather than independent virulence loci. NCyc annotations were sparse (12 ACCs), with no evidence of complete nitrification or denitrification pathways. Taxonomic classification resolved 217 ACCs to the species level, with no matches to curated human pathogenic bacteria. Only two Acinetobacter-assigned ACCs exhibited both genus-level pathogenicity and mobility evidence. These findings highlight the importance of integrating mobility and host-taxonomic information to distinguish baseline environmental resistance from potential priorities for AMR surveillance.

papers.title: Uncovering cross-signal interactions in single-cell and spatial omics
papers.abstract: Individual cells simultaneously encode multiple biological signals in their gene expression profiles, including spatial position, circadian phase, and disease state. These signals can be entangled in complex ways, including circadian patterns that vary along disease progression and cell cycle dynamics that shift along developmental trajectories. While methods to disentangle such signals have been recently developed, characterizing the interaction itself between multicellular signals along with its effects on tissue function, localizing cellular subpopulations which exhibit signal interactions, and identifying potential candidate genes which drive such interactions, all remain major challenges. We present CRISP which characterizes signal interactions in single-cell gene expression data based on the correspondence between the multiple, probabilistic signal-specific projections of the data. Across simulations with tunable couplings and four single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets, CRISP recovers diverse biological signal interactions and localizes them to informative cellular subpopulations and groups of associated genes; CRISP distinguishes healthy from fibrotic liver samples and localizes the loss of zonation-position coupling to individual fibrotic hepatocytes, resolves the asymmetric coupling of TGF-{beta} response, EMT, and cell-cycle phase to specific cell subpopulations, and flags transcriptionally delayed hepatocytes in Plasmodium liver infection. Beyond quantifying and localizing signal interactions, CRISP can refine existing labels, uncover continuous cellular transitions and reveal condition-associated genes.

papers.title: A Fibrous Optofluidic Probe for Endovascular Sensing of Blood Oxygenation and Flow Velocity
papers.abstract: Local hemodynamic information including blood oxygenation and flow velocity could guide vascular interventions, yet obtaining these parameters in deep, narrow vessels remains challenging. Here, we report a flexible, submillimeter-scale fibrous optofluidic probe for endovascular sensing of blood oxygenation and flow velocity. The probe integrates a polymer optical fiber for light transmission with a microfluidic tube for dye injection, enabling spectroscopic oximetry and fluorescence dilution-based velocimetry through a single device. Via vascular intervention, we demonstrate local hemodynamic sensing in rabbit arteries and angiography-guided deployment in canine carotid arteries. The probe captures local changes in blood oxygenation and flow velocity during vascular occlusion and reperfusion, revealing hemodynamic disturbances that are not reflected in peripheral monitors. These results illustrate the complementary information provided by local oximetry and velocimetry and establish a compact optofluidic platform for quantitative hemodynamic monitoring during vascular interventions.

papers.title: Urban enrichment of molestus ancestry and opposing temperature clines in a metropolitan Culex pipiens hybrid zone
papers.abstract: Hybridization between ecologically distinct lineages can fuel rapid adaptation when introgressed alleles are locally favored. The North American Culex pipiens assemblage, a principal West Nile virus vector east of the Mississippi, comprises three lineages---temperate Cx. pipiens f. pipiens, urban-specialist Cx. pipiens f. molestus, and subtropical Cx. quinquefasciatus---that meet in a mid-Atlantic hybrid zone where temperature and urbanization gradients intersect. Using whole-genome Pool-seq of 24 field populations and three lineage-reference pools across the Baltimore--Washington corridor, we find a weakly differentiated, Cx. pipiens f. pipiens-like background, richer in molestus- and quinquefasciatus-like ancestry toward the warmer end of the corridor. Urbanization impacts allele frequencies across the genome: molestus-like ancestry rises with impervious surface, independently of temperature and position, while Cx. quinquefasciatus-like ancestry does not. An 11.6 Mb chromosome 3 inversion is molestus-like in every population, most of all in urban ones, and tracks genome-wide molestus-like ancestry. Temperature acts locus by locus. On chromosome 1, a cluster of six CYP6 paralogs, a family implicated in insecticide resistance and thermal-stress response, shows rising Cx. quinquefasciatus-like ancestry and read depth with temperature. A chromosome 2 interval centered on a Yan ortholog, a repressor of cell differentiation, shows non-quinquefasciatus ancestry increasing with temperature, consistent with selection against Cx. quinquefasciatus-like introgression. Urban populations therefore carry more ancestry from the human-commensal lineage, while temperature moves Cx. quinquefasciatus ancestry both ways at individual loci. Both molestus and Cx. quinquefasciatus donors carry human-contact traits, so these patterns bear on how warming and urbanization will reshape arboviral risk.

papers.title: LIMBER: A Hybrid RNA Foundation Model for Predicting and Understanding RNA Structure and Function
papers.abstract: RNA foundation models offer a promising route to decoding the relationships between RNA sequence, structure and function, yet how model architecture shapes the acquisition and organization of biological information remains poorly understood. Here we introduce Layer-Interleaved Mamba-Bidirectional Encoder for RNA (LIMBER), a hybrid foundation model integrating bidirectional self-attention with selective state-space modeling, pre-trained on 40.5 million non-coding RNA sequences. With task-specific fine-tuning, LIMBER achieves leading performance on secondary-structure prediction and non-coding RNA classification benchmarks, while demonstrating strong transferability to translation-related tasks and RNA--small-molecule interaction prediction. Beyond model development, we establish a unified, task-agnostic framework to systematically evaluate and interpret the biological knowledge intrinsically acquired by RNA foundation models. This framework validates LIMBER's strong capabilities in recovering RNA structures and predicting mutational effects, while uncovering a hierarchical, task-dependent organization of biological information across model layers. In addition, we demonstrate distinct scaling behaviors across structural, evolutionary, and functional capabilities by training and evaluating a broad panel of model variants spanning model capacity, training duration, and dataset size. Taken together, these findings establish LIMBER as a versatile RNA foundation model and provide insight into how architectural design, internal representations and scaling shape the learning of RNA sequence-structure-function relationships.

papers.title: Evaluation design shapes estimates of cross-donor generalization in single-cell classification of cell-type
papers.abstract: Motivation: Single-cell cell-type classifiers are often evaluated using random cell-level splits, although cells from the same donor are not independent. We asked how evaluation design affects estimates of cross-donor generalization. Results: Across PBMC and lung datasets, random cell-level splitting consistently yielded higher macro F1 than donor-held-out evaluation across multiple expression representations. This gap persisted after batch covariate adjustment and donor-level mixed-effects modeling. In contrast, evaluation gaps were generally minimal in highly separable, trivially easy kidney, pancreas, and blood classification settings and in a randomized-label setting with no meaningful predictive signal. These results show that evaluation bias depends on the underlying classification difficulty and that donor-held-out evaluation is necessary when claims concern generalization to unseen individuals. Availability and Implementation: Code and analyses are available on GitHub at https://github.com/danielchen05/scRNA-cross-donor-generalization/. Processed data are archived at Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19717558. Contact: ajbattle@jhu.edu

papers.title: Overcoming segmentation bottlenecks in brain tissue for spatial proteomic inference at population scale
papers.abstract: In spatial proteomics across large cohorts, downstream estimates from tens of thousands of images depend on accurate cell segmentation. Yet pretrained segmentation models struggle with morphologically complex cell bodies in human brain tissue, and how domain adaptation affects downstream discovery remains unclear. Here, we introduce SPInfer, a workflow for spatial proteomic inference developed using 5,832 manually annotated cell bodies from 120 immunofluorescence images of the human prefrontal cortex. After benchmarking eight segmentation methods spanning classical, convolutional, and foundation models, we adapted Cellpose-SAM, raising cell segmentation F1 from 0.37 to 0.84 and recovering cell compositions concordant with matched single-nucleus RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics. Across 14,765 images from 69 postmortem donors, identical Alzheimer's disease pathology models found no significant associations after false discovery rate correction using zero-shot masks, versus four using fine-tuned masks; three linked higher OLIG2-positive fractions to greater neurofibrillary tangle and plaque burden. Using the fine-tuned masks, a graph attention network over nuclear neighborhoods classified four cell types without marker information, and differential expression analysis linked cell morphology to gene expression. This provides a pipeline for fine-tuning foundation models to segment complex tissues, enabling biological discovery in spatial proteomics at the population scale.

papers.title: HaloPROTAC-mediated degradation reveals SOX10-dependent gene expression changes in melanoma cells
papers.abstract: The transcription factor SOX10 is required for melanoma cell proliferation. However, SOX10 expression in single cells is heterogeneous, and low SOX10-expressing melanoma cells exhibit a dormant-invasive phenotype associated with drug resistance and metastasis. Despite longstanding interest in SOX10 as a diagnostic marker and potential therapeutic target in melanoma, the function and targets of SOX10 remain incompletely understood. New tools for the study of SOX10 are needed to address these gaps in our knowledge. In this study, we engineered a patient-derived WW165 melanoma cell line for programmable SOX10 targeted proteolysis. We achieved this by replacing the endogenous copies of SOX10 with a SOX10-HaloTag transgene that supports cell growth, but can be rapidly degraded by the ubiquitin-proteasome system upon with a commercially available HaloPROTAC3 degrader molecule. We demonstrate that inducible degradation of SOX10-HaloTag faithfully recapitulates the known SOX10 transcriptional program, while also enabling discovery of NAV2 and NCKAP5 as novel SOX10 target genes. This study demonstrates that new biological insights into the function of SOX10 can be enabled by targeted degradation.

papers.title: P2K1 P2K2 are required for early, mechanical adaptation to osmotic and cell wall stress in Arabidopsis roots
papers.abstract: The cell wall and plasma membrane (PM) form the interface between a plant cell and its environment yet how their mechanical properties change in response to stress is poorly understood. Here we investigate how the mechanical properties of the cell wall, plasma membrane, and vacuole change in vivo in Arabidopsis thaliana roots in response to hyperosmotic stress and cell wall damage (CWD) using a solvatochromic dye, molecular rotors, and Brillouin microscopy. We observe initially dynamic changes in mechanical properties of the PM that are sensitive to both hyperosmotic stress and CWD, while the cell wall changes are limited and the vacuole adapts only after several hours. In the p2k1 p2k2 double mutant, lacking receptors for extracellular ATP perception, sorbitol-induced effects on PM mechanostasis and early isoxaben-induced increases in PM order are lost. Our results indicate that P2K1 and P2K2 are required to modulate adaptive changes in mechanical properties of the PM induced by hyperosmotic stress and CWD.

papers.title: Decoding plant x environment interactions through spatial gradients in leaf physiology and metabolism
papers.abstract: Succulent leaves are well known to combine photosynthesis, carbon storage and hydraulic buffering. However, their metabolic responses to heat and drought may differ along the same leaf axis. We investigated spatial and temporal changes in leaf tissue water content, photosynthetic performance and central carbon metabolism in the CAM plant Sansevieria cylindrica across three experimental phases: (i) heat, (ii) combined heat and drought, and (iii) rewatering under continued heat. Apical, middle and basal leaf sections were sampled at midday, and chlorophyll fluorescence was monitored near the leaf tip. Fresh-weight-to-dry-weight ratios declined significantly in basal tissues under drought, whereas apical tissues showed a significant decrease only during rewatering indicating a considerable delay in tissue water supply along the leaf axis. Apical photosystem II quantum yield decreased during combined heat and drought, and sucrose accumulated transiently during heat exposure, particularly in middle and basal sections. Glucose and fructose peaked under drought conditions and declined after rewatering. Citrate decreased during the experimental time course, while apical malate increased significantly during rewatering phase. Chlorophyll varied primarily with leaf position, whereas starch and fumarate showed no significant effects. Neural network classification identified citrate and sucrose as major contributors to the discrimination of treatment phases, while chlorophyll was most informative for distinguishing leaf positions. Together, these findings demonstrate that within leaf physiological and metabolic gradients capture complementary dimensions of plant x environment interactions, distinguishing spatially structured leaf characteristics from dynamic stress responses. Integrating spatially resolved metabolic and physiological profiles thus provides a promising approach for identifying biochemical signatures of environmental stress and recovery in CAM plants.

papers.title: A Multidimensional Arithmetical Ontology for High-Parameter Cytometry: Gaussian Primes and Cryptographic Hashing for Cell Population Standardization
papers.abstract: Background. The rapid expansion of high-dimensional single-cell technologies has outpaced the development of standardized metadata infrastructure. Current text-based ontology for cell populations and gating strategies lacks computational rigor, hindering process automation and cross-study reproducibility. Our previous frameworks, the Prime Population System (PPS) and the Unique Gating Identifier (UGI), proposed arithmetical solutions but were limited by biological fragility (no inherent link between a protein and its structural isoforms) and by computational bottlenecks caused by exponential integer growth. Objective. To develop a scalable, multidimensional arithmetical ontology that unambiguously identifies cell populations and hierarchical gating strategies. Methods. We transition the marker dictionary from the one-dimensional real axis (R) to the complex plane of Gaussian integers (a+bi). The reviewed human proteome of the UniProt Knowledgebase is paired with Gaussian primes satisfying a > b > 0. Each protein receives a contiguous reserved block of 64 primes: slot 0 addresses the protein with isoform unresolved, and slot k addresses UniProt isoform k, the slot index being read directly off the accession. Carbohydrate epitopes, which have no UniProt entry, are paired through the CD nomenclature instead: in a CD region beyond the 80,000 blocks reserved for the proteome, each CD number receives a block of 1,024 primes, with the slot read off the suffix of the designation. A bipartite encoding represents positive (a+bi) and negative (b+ai) expression states through Conjugate Pair Symmetry. To avoid the integer explosion of Godel exponentiation, hierarchical gating sequences are held as vectorized arrays of complex numbers and compressed by SHA-256 deterministic hashing. Results. Pairing against the human proteome assigns 53,296 identifiers, 20,431 protein-level and 32,865 isoform-level. Every isoform description resolves under a single rule, including the 329 descriptions whose accession prefix differs from the entry that cites them. The 19 carbohydrate designations of the CD list, CD57 among them, receive identifiers in the CD region. Localized vectorization with SHA-256 hashing yields immutable 64-character hexadecimal fingerprints for entire gating strategies, resolving the integer explosion problem. Conclusion. By combining Gaussian primes with hashing, Gaussian Prime Cytometry provides a scalable, computationally lightweight and biologically accurate identifier system. The system eliminates nomenclature ambiguity and facilitates machine learning applications and centralized global cytometry databases.

papers.title: High-throughput light-sheet 3D microscopy of whole rodent brain microstructure for integration with MRI
papers.abstract: Whole-brain cellular mapping is essential for understanding how cellular architecture shapes brain organisation and function. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) provides whole-brain coverage but is only indirectly sensitive to cellular features, motivating integration with microscopy to improve the interpretation and specificity of microstructural MRI. Here, we present a scalable cross-resolution framework integrating 3D light-sheet microscopy (LSM) of intact rodent brains with diffusion MRI (dMRI) to bridge cellular and macroscopic brain imaging. By combining active tissue clearing and immunolabelling with accelerated LSM acquisition, we achieve multiplexed mapping of neuronal and glial populations across the whole brain on timescales comparable to conventional histology. We apply this framework across eight genetically diverse mouse strains to develop predictive models of microscopy-derived cellular features from multi-shell dMRI contrasts. Data-driven combinations of dMRI contrasts predicted neuronal and astrocytic features better than individual contrasts across animals. This framework enables scalable integration of MRI and 3D LSM, providing a means to identify cellular determinants of MRI contrast and guide the development and interpretation of microstructural MRI measures ultimately translatable to the living human brain.

papers.title: Shared experimental materials inflate and reorder cross-participant decoding benchmarks
papers.abstract: Decoding mental states from brain activity underpins brain-computer interfaces and cognitive neuroscience. Decoders are judged by how well they generalize to people left out of training, taken as evidence that they capture what transfers between brains. However, most benchmarks present the same experimental materials to every participant, so held-out participants are tested on materials the model has already seen. Here we show, across 15 EEG, fMRI and eye-tracking datasets and 318 matched comparisons, that shared materials inflate cross-participant accuracy by up to 46 percentage points. They also reorder methods, reversing the advantage of foundation models over handcrafted features on the largest emotion EEG benchmark. The inflation tracks cross-participant item identifiability and, in sealed prospective tests, vanished where items could not be identified. Adding training items improved new-material accuracy more reliably than adding participants. These findings call for reporting new-material accuracy alongside conventional scores and for measuring item identifiability first.

papers.title: Reinterpreting Keratoconus Gene Expression in Light of Inherited Stromal Weakness
papers.abstract: Purpose. To reinterpret keratoconus (KC) gene expression in light of inherited stromal weakness, and to define how expression should guide model and target selection. Methods. We combined genetic and chromatin data with expression from eight studies (182 donors). We compared the same KC samples with normal and pathological controls, built references matched to control source and tissue layer and tested them in independent tissues, and indexed published intervention-outcome records. Stimulated cells and genetic analyses assessed repair capacity and inherited risk. Results. Changing only the control reversed expression directions, flipping KC-like classification in 21-27 of 42 models and supplement-or-inhibit direction in 361-385 of 1,090 targets. Our references addressed this, predicting direction more accurately than published methods in independent spatial stroma and two bulk comparisons. Against these references, 41 of 46 target nominations required a different comparison, measurement, or use. A correct direction described only the stromal state: across control types, KC stroma showed lower inflammatory, immediate-early (stress-response), and transforming growth factor-{beta} (TGF-{beta}) programs, which signaled neither lost repair capacity (stimulated KC cells increased matrix production) nor disease cause (no genetic enrichment). Inherited risk converged on the matrix: collagen assembly was the only replicated pathway family, and genetically predicted higher corneal resistance lowered disease odds independently of thickness. Because these expression changes do not drive disease, reversing them does not ensure functional benefit: among 2,769 intervention-outcome records, the two were separate outcomes. Conclusions. Expression direction therefore reflects the choice of control and the stromal state, and does not indicate how to intervene. Because inherited risk lies in matrix structure and resistance to deformation, repair should restore organized, load-bearing matrix rather than reverse expression changes. Models should therefore be judged against matched references, and targets by measured functional outcomes.

papers.title: DECONVersation: Single Cell Foundation Model-Derived Embeddings for Robust Cell Type Deconvolution of Bulk RNA-seq
papers.abstract: Motivation: Bulk RNA-seq deconvolution uses single-cell references to estimate cell type proportions in bulk tissue. Existing methods face challenges with batch effects, subject-level variation, and marker gene selection. We propose a new approach leveraging general-purpose single-cell foundation models. Results: DECONVersation combines pretrained or fine-tuned single-cell foundation model embeddings with non-negative least squares for deconvolution. The embeddings eliminate the need for explicit marker selection, and reduce batch effects. Compared against MuSiC, DWLS, and BayesPrism, DECONVersation with Geneformer or Cell2Sentence-2B achieved competitive performance across six bulk datasets with ground truth, with performance improvements after reference-specific fine-tuning. Availability and Implementation: DECONVersation is available through the Python Package Index. The source code is available at https://github.com/nygenome/DECONVersation, and the datasets and Apptainer/Singularity images are archived on https://zenodo.org/records/22949405.

papers.title: Deep Vein Thrombosis-primed neutrophils reshape the brain microenvironment to promote brain metastasis
papers.abstract: Brain metastasis (BrM) is a devastating complication of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), yet how host macroenvironmental conditions influence brain metastatic susceptibility remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the impact of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), a common complication in patients with cancer, on TNBC brain metastasis. Analysis of a large clinical cohort identified DVT as an independent risk factor for BrM in patients with metastatic breast cancer. Using two syngeneic TNBC models, we demonstrated that DVT selectively enhanced brain metastasis without significantly affecting primary tumor growth or lung metastasis. Mechanistically, DVT increased neutrophil accumulation in the brain metastatic microenvironment, and neutrophil depletion completely abrogated the metastasis-promoting effect of DVT. Single-cell RNA sequencing of CD45+ cells in peripheral blood revealed that DVT reprogrammed circulating neutrophils toward migratory and inflammatory transcriptomic profiles characterized by neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation. DVT increased CXCR2 expression on circulating neutrophils and enhanced neutrophil recruitment in brain. Moreover, DVT significantly increased circulating NETs. Collectively, our findings identify DVT as a systemic driver of TNBC brain metastasis and reveal that DVT primes circulating neutrophils toward enhanced vascular recruitment and NET formation, providing a mechanistic link between cancer-associated thrombosis and brain metastatic susceptibility.

papers.title: Red-light-catalyzed photolipid switching enables leaflet-selective control of membrane mechanics
papers.abstract: Azobenzene photolipids are versatile actuators of membrane mechanics and protein function, yet long-wavelength control and leaflet-selective perturbations remain difficult to impose. Here, we address both limitations. First, we confirm that red-light excitation of a lipidated Nile Blue derivative (NB-lipid) catalyzes rapid cis[->]trans photoisomerization of co-localized azobenzene photolipids in planar bilayers without requiring covalent conjugation. Second, we demonstrate that photocatalysis is predominantly intraleaflet, enabling leaflet-selective actuation by incorporating the membrane-targeted chromophore into only one bilayer leaflet. This enables on-demand and rapid writing of transbilayer mechanical asymmetry, which we track via lock-in capacitance signatures. Critically, symmetric and asymmetric leaflet mechanical perturbations can be evoked within the same membrane by illuminating with blue or red light, respectively. For electron-rich azobenzenes, the anticipated singlet-state photoredox pathway is expected to limit triplet-associated photodamage. Repeated, reversible modulation of gramicidin A, a mechanosensitive peptide ion channel susceptible to reactive oxygen species, supports the compatibility of photocatalysis with membrane protein function. Our results establish a novel tool for dissecting the role of dynamic leaflet-specific mechanical changes in membrane remodeling and protein function.

papers.title: Genome-wide interrogation of genetic requirements for root colonization by CRISPRi-seq in Bacillus subtilis
papers.abstract: Bacillus subtilis is a known plant growth promoting rhizobacterium. Yet, the genetic basis for effective B. subtilis root colonization remains unclear. Here, we applied genome-wide CRISPR interference sequencing (CRISPRi-seq) to systematically identify bacterial genes required for early Arabidopsis thaliana root colonization by the undomesticated B. subtilis strain NCIB3610. Complementary bacterial RNA-seq experiments in the same conditions further revealed a distinct transcriptional state of root-associated cells. Together, we identified 249 B. subtilis genes impacting root colonization. We reveal a critical, biofilm-independent, role of cell envelope remodeling during early root association, specifically wall teichoic acid synthesis and D-alanylation. Moreover, we observed a metabolic shift toward TCA-cycle-driven aerobic growth and utilization of fructose, induction of secondary metabolite biosynthesis, as well as active repression of sporulation, competence and prophage programs. Our work establishes CRISPRi-seq as a powerful tool for dissecting bacterial-plant interactions relevant to sustainable agriculture.

papers.title: Talking Brains: Neonatal Aperiodic Activity in Resting State EEG Relates to Later Communicative Abilities
papers.abstract: Communicative abilities acquired over the first year of life are foundational for language development. Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying these abilities can explain individual differences and improve predictions of later language outcomes. While prior research on neural markers of language development has focused predominantly on oscillatory neural activity, the underlying aperiodic component of the neural signal may provide further insights into cortical maturation by indirectly reflecting variation in neural excitation/inhibition (E/I) balance. In neurodevelopmental conditions, both reduced and elevated aperiodic activity are linked to atypical development, and initial evidence from at-risk cohorts also relates aperiodic activity to language outcome. Moving beyond clinical populations, the present study examined whether aperiodic activity during neonatal resting-state EEG relates to 12-month communicative abilities in typically developing infants. Aperiodic offset and exponent were extracted from resting-state EEG recorded two weeks after birth in n = 50 neonates using the FOOOF algorithm. At 12 months, communicative abilities were assessed with the parent-report CSBS-DP Infant-Toddler Checklist. Quadratic regression analyses showed an inverted U-shaped relationship between the neonatal aperiodic exponent and communicative abilities: both lower and higher exponent values were associated with poorer outcomes, with intermediate values linked to better abilities. No robust association was found for the offset. These findings suggest that aperiodic activity captures variability in early communicative development, with an optimum at intermediate levels, consistent with a balanced E/I state. The scope of aperiodic brain activity as a developmental marker may thus extend beyond clinical populations to predicting communicative development in healthy infants.

papers.title: Preserved cortical hierarchy characterizes vision without awareness after visual cortex damage
papers.abstract: After primary visual cortex (V1) damage, some patients successfully detect stimuli yet deny seeing them, a rare condition known as "blindsight". Blindsight provides a unique natural experiment in consciousness research: visual information guides behavior without entering awareness. Why only some patients with comparable lesions show blindsight is unknown, and current accounts have focused on spared, V1-bypassing pathways. One extant question concerns how the functional organization of the remaining brain helps explain the divergent behavioral outcomes of V1 damage. Using resting-state fMRI, we quantified regional coupling as mutual information in the largest available cohort of psychophysically defined blindsight-positive and negative patients with age-matched controls. Despite overlapping lesions and field defects, blindsight-positive patients retained a control-like sensory-association coupling pattern, whereas blindsight-negative patients showed reduced unimodal-transmodal differentiation, reflecting lower coupling of unimodal cortex. This differentiation tracked blind-field stimulus detection and predicted performance across the patient cohort. The ipsilesional posterior thalamus, in a location consistent with the pulvinar, showed the same group difference and stronger coupling with contralesional visual and frontal pre-motor regions in blindsight-positive patients. Together, our findings outline the complementary contribution of the local and global functional organization through which V1 bypassing visual signals can influence behavior. An intrinsic cortico-subcortical functional architecture previously implicated in conscious states also bears on visual behavior without awareness.

papers.title: SPOUT: An open-source hardware and software platform to study decision making while manipulating and recording from neural activity
authors: van den Boom, B. J. G.
papers.abstract: Recording and manipulating brain activity during behavior is critical to understanding the underlying mechanisms of decision-making. Linking neural activity to behavior requires behavioral hardware and software tightly integrated with recording and perturbation systems on a shared clock. We built SPOUT (State-machine Platform for Operant Uni/dual-spout Tasks), an open-source, Teensy-driven state-machine platform with a MATLAB interface that runs 10 unique decision-making tasks (with dozens of variations available through user-friendly settings) to study behavior in head-restrained mice. The platform is built on several custom hardware devices: a dual-lick detector, headplate designs for optogenetics and two-photon calcium imaging, a three-axis motorized spout manipulator, and an optogenetics power modulator. The firmware differentiates between one and two lick spout tasks and can be controlled by a user-friendly interface. Task settings can be selected through the interface or by loading predefined settings files. We validated the clock speed and lick detection against an independent, external acquisition system and identified highly precise, sub-millisecond detection of single licks. Using a pseudo-random synchronization pulse generated by SPOUT, we corrected for missing data due to glitches in the acquisition system and clock drift. We showcase the versatility of SPOUT by training mice on an uninstructed lick-left/lick-right task in which the rewarded side switches unexpectedly and found that mice use history-dependent action-outcome associations to guide future behavior. Transiently inhibiting the anterior lateral motor cortex (ALM) during cue presentation induced contralateral deficits, without affecting ipsilateral trials. Finally, two-photon imaging of ALM neurons revealed stronger population responses during contralateral choice licks compared to ipsilateral ones. Together, SPOUT offers an open-source, affordable platform to study decision-making in head-restrained mice while combining neural recordings and manipulations.

papers.title: Implicit Hierarchical Tensor Decomposition of Single-Cell Four-Omics Data Reveals Cell-Type-Linked Candidate Enhancer--Promoter-Associated Programs
papers.abstract: Single-cell multi-omics provides complementary views of gene regulation, but integrating modalities with natural features comprising enhancers, genes, and three-dimensional (3D) genomic loci remains challenging. This study developed an implicit hierarchical tensor decomposition framework and applied it to the CHARM single-cell four-omics mouse brain data (GSE303006) by jointly analyzing ATAC, H3K27ac, RNA, and reconstructed 3D enhancer--promoter (E--P) distances. After quality control, 730,969 E--P pairs, 42,669 enhancers, 16,239 genes, 391,435 20-kb bin pairs, and 4,258 cells were retained. Each modality was independently reduced to 20 components and mapped to an implicit 730,969x4{,}258x20x4 tensor, which was decomposed without materializing the full array. In a joint model, cell type explained more variance than biological replicate for all 12 distinct cell components represented among the 100 largest Tucker core elements. A representative core linked the Inh_Ndnf/Lamp5--Ex_L3/4_IT cell axis to contrasting presynaptic-transmission and developmental/morphogenetic candidate E--P-associated programs. Its E--P and cell factors were recovered when the whole analysis was repeated independently on each pair of replicates, and the E--P pairs it prioritized agreed in direction with the cell-type-resolved enhancer--gene links of the original CHARM study. No single modality reproduced the program, which required the combination of accessibility, chromatin contact, and expression. Backprojection showed reproducible ATAC, H3K27ac, and 3D effects across three biological replicates; RNA differed clearly for the developmental module but not for the presynaptic module. The framework thus identifies regulatory structure that is shared across molecular modalities and is not recoverable from any single modality.

papers.title: Searching for patterns in rate of molecular evolution using phylogenetic pairwise contrasts
papers.abstract: Understanding variation in molecular evolutionary rates among species offers insight into the forces shaping evolution, and can inform phylogenetic models and molecular dating. Explaining this variation is challenging, however. Analyses must account for phylogenetic relationships, correlated species traits, and features of substitution rate estimates that standard approaches like phylogenetic generalised least squares (PGLS) do not address. Notably, substitution rates describe change accumulated over time along the lineages of a phylogeny, where shorter branches have higher variance in substitution rate estimation. Traits like body mass, by contrast, are instantaneous measurements and are therefore properties of nodes or tips, rather than branches. Here, we formalise an approach that overcomes these problems using phylogenetic pairwise contrasts (PPC). By comparing differences between pairs of taxa, we avoid estimating traits at internal nodes. Pairs are sampled from a phylogeny so that the edges connecting them do not overlap with any other pairs, generating comparisons that can be analysed using a linear regression. Simulations show that PPC tolerates measurement error in both traits and substitution rates while keeping its false positive rate close to nominal. PGLS, by contrast, is poorly calibrated for finding covariates of substitution rate, with up to 35% of replicates yielding p<0.01 when no true association exists. We "ground-truth" PPC using empirical datasets, corroborating the well-established negative correlation between body size and substitution rate in flowering plants and mammals. This work offers a straightforward, reliable method for linking substitution rates to biological traits, implemented in the R package phylowise.

papers.title: Mitochondrial Signaling: Nitric Oxide Synthesis by Cytochrome c Oxidase and Its Oxygen Sensitivity Are Modulated by Adenine Nucleotides
papers.abstract: Nitrite can be reduced to nitric oxide (NO) by several heme- and molybdenum-containing proteins, including mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase (Cco). This activity, designated Cco/NO, has been implicated in hypoxic signaling, but its regulation and quantitative significance relative to other NO-producing systems remain uncertain. We examined its modulation by adenine nucleotides using detergent-solubilized yeast and mouse brain mitochondria supplied with 1 mM nitrite and an ascorbate/TMPD/cytochrome c electron-donor system. ADP and ATP differentially modulated Cco/NO activity, and ADP shifted the apparent oxygen sensitivity of Cco/NO toward lower O2, with significant stimulation at 10 uM O2 and below. Nucleotide regulation was also isoform-dependent: ATP slightly inhibited Va-containing Cco but strongly stimulated Vb-containing Cco under anoxic conditions. Rates normalized to cytochrome aa3 demonstrate multi-turnover nitrite-reductase capacity under these substrate-driven assay conditions. Both the cellular ADP/ATP ratio and subsequently assayed Cco/NO activity increased transiently following a hypoxic shift. These findings establish metabolic and isoform-dependent gating of the catalytic capacity of Cco/NO; they do not establish its fractional contribution to total cellular NO or its operation at physiological nitrite concentrations in intact, coupled mitochondria.

papers.title: Macroscale dynamics of EEG microstates constitute the periodic and aperiodic features of the neural power spectrum
papers.abstract: The global signal characteristics of scalp-recorded electroencephalography (EEG) are composed of periodic oscillatory rhythms and aperiodic broadband fluctuations that together comprise the neural power spectrum. Spectral decomposition of these features has long served as the primary window into the macroscale characteristics of human brain activity. Here, we propose that the primary periodic rhythms and majority share of broadband spectral power within the brain's dominant frequencies are the frequency-domain representations of the dynamics of EEG microstates. Microstates are characterized by a small repertoire of topographic voltage configurations that each reflect the momentary functional state of the cortex, and it is their time-domain dynamics that mathematically constitute periodic and aperiodic spectral features. We isolated and removed the spatial projections of distinct microstate configurations from high-density EEG using orthogonal subspace projection applied to both the surface scalp recordings and their modeled cortical generators to computationally test this dependency. Spectral parameterization of the residual power spectral density revealed that removing these spatial projections strongly attenuated alpha and theta rhythms and features of the aperiodic 1/f background. Selectively removing specific microstate configurations also demonstrated that each configuration aligned with spatially specific oscillatory and aperiodic 1/f components. Furthermore, correlational analyses of microstate temporal dynamics demonstrated that the average duration and temporal persistence of microstates strongly correlate with periodic alpha power, theta power, and the aperiodic 1/f background. Our findings suggest that dominant periodic and aperiodic spectral features are more accurately understood as the frequency-domain expressions of the dynamics of EEG microstates.

papers.title: A Conformational Switch in the Catalytic Lysine Governs the Stereochemical Outcome of DERA-Catalyzed Aldol Addition
papers.abstract: 2-Deoxyribose-5-Phosphate Aldolase (DERA) is a key enzyme in the pentose phosphate pathway. Due to its C-C bond formation and stereoselective capabilities, DERA has been widely used for biocatalytic applications including the synthesis of chiral intermediates for antiviral and anticancer drugs. Protein engineering has expanded its substrate-scope, improved yield, and enhanced S-stereoselectivity. Recently, rational mutagenesis of DERA from Geobacillus sp. (DERAGs) resulted in two enantiocomplementary variants, T12I/S185A and S185G. In particular, the single mutation at Ser185 to Gly inverts the natural S-selectivity to R-selectivity. However, the molecular basis of enantioselectivity remains unclear. Here, we determined high-resolution crystal structures of wild-type DERAGs and two enantiocomplementary variants in the apo form. Using a combination of structural biology, biochemistry, biocatalysis and molecular dynamic simulations, we show that the catalytic lysine adopts two conformations, a finding that relates to the enantioselectivity of DERA. We further identified a mechanism of regulating enantioselectivity via a key conserved amino acid. Using DERA from E. coli, we show that these findings are conserved across bacterial species.

papers.title: Chromosome-scale CRISPR screening reveals secretory pathway genes as drivers of aneuploidy-mediated antifungal tolerance
papers.abstract: The gain or loss of chromosomes in eukaryotes often drives aberrant phenotypes by altering the expression levels of hundreds or thousands of genes. In the case of beneficial aneuploidies, the genetic basis of fitness improvement has rarely been pinpointed, and identifying the causal genes remains a major challenge in engineering biology. The leading cause of human fungal infections, Candida albicans, frequently acquires extra copies of chromosome R (ChrR) following exposure to azole antifungal drugs, resulting in heightened antifungal tolerance. Despite this, why this aneuploidy frequently emerges following azole exposure and how it promotes antifungal tolerance remain unknown. Here, we combine RNA-seq with parallel chromosome-wide CRISPR activation (CRISPRa) and CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) screens to systematically profile the ChrR genes contributing to azole tolerance. Using multiplexed CRISPR-dCas12a tools, we further characterize the combinatorial effects of candidate genes and uncover a central role for post-Golgi secretory trafficking in antifungal tolerance. Specifically, we demonstrate that the secretory pathway regulators SEC4 and YPT31 are both necessary and sufficient for ChrR-mediated azole tolerance, and drive increased ergosterol content in the cell membrane. By leveraging a large-scale CRISPRa screen in a fungal pathogen, our work functionally dissects one of the most common aneuploidies observed in C. albicans, provides mechanistic insight into the molecular basis of antifungal tolerance, and establishes a generalizable framework for studying aneuploidy-mediated phenotypes across eukaryotic organisms.

papers.title: Interconnected reservoirs of multidrug-resistant bacteria and plasmids within hospital plumbing infrastructure
papers.abstract: Hospital sinks and wastewater streams are hotspots for contamination and colonization with multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria (MDR-GNB). While hospital water systems may facilitate MDR-GNB transmission during outbreaks, longitudinal population dynamics of environmental MDR-GNB and their long-term relationship with patient isolates remain unclear. Here we aimed to characterize the diversity and abundance of MDR-GNB within the hospital built environment and evaluate their relationship with clinical isolates. We performed nanopore sequencing on MDR-GNB cultured from sink drains (n=523) and wastewater (n=146) at a New York City hospital between March-August 2023. We assessed spatial and longitudinal genomic strain and plasmid dynamics and quantified relatedness to historical clinical isolates from the same hospital (n=602). Sink drains (54-73%) and wastewater (100%) demonstrated widespread, longitudinal colonization with MDR-GNB, driven primarily by carbapenem-resistant GNB including opportunistic organisms and Enterobacterales encoding blaKPC. While bacterial colonization differed across environmental niches, we identified both MDR-GNB strains and resistance plasmids that were shared between clinical and environmental sources, as well a distinct interplay between clinical and wastewater versus sink drain samples. This study supports the role of hospital plumbing as an important reservoir for clinically relevant MDR-GNB, but highlights differences across environmental sources, which may impact surveillance approaches.

papers.title: Multimodal temporal modeling of behavioral reorganization across threat learning and extinction in rats
papers.abstract: After threat disrupts a learned activity, does engagement return as defensive responding later declines? Tri-reference-point theory describes decisions under risk relative to a minimum requirement, the status quo and a goal; we extended this logic to defense and engagement. We followed freezing, 22-kHz and 50-kHz calls, and food-reinforced lever responses across conditioning, extinction, delayed retesting and context changes in 29 male rats (45,300 five-second windows). A hidden Markov model described recurring response combinations, or configurations, and their persistence. For every animal, it predicted behavioral sequences excluded from fitting better than a matched model that ignored temporal order. Among models with two to eight configurations, eight predicted best; four provided a coarser description. This coarser model separated relatively brief press-active patterns from more persistent vocal-active and low-output patterns. Low-output patterns contained few calls and lever responses, but could involve either little or substantial freezing. In the repeated-session comparison, the estimated share of time in press-active patterns increased on average in the full extinction group (n=9) and decreased in cue-free context controls (n=8), from different first-session levels. These descriptive trajectories included renewed instrumental engagement alongside continued defensive immobility. We separately tested whether configuration summaries added predictive value beyond the measured behaviors for later responding or whole-recording fecal-pellet counts, finding no consistent benefit. Tracking how behavioral combinations change and persist provides a computational framework for evaluating functional adaptation beyond defensive decline.

papers.title: Kinetochore-microtubule attachments are strengthened by Cnn1 stabilization of Stu2
papers.abstract: Accurate chromosome segregation requires kinetochores to form robust, load-bearing attachments to dynamic spindle microtubules, mediated primarily by the Ndc80 complex. Two receptors, Dsn1 and Cnn1 (CENP-T), recruit multiple copies of Ndc80c to the kinetochore. We previously demonstrated that kinetochore components co-purifying with the yeast Dsn1 protein can maintain persistent load-bearing attachments that track with microtubule tip growth and shortening, but the properties of the Cnn1 receptor have not been explored. Using an optical trapping-based assay, we show here that Cnn1 purifications also sustain dynamic microtubule attachments under load. Mutation of a conserved region within the disordered N-terminal tail of Cnn1 weakened attachment strength in vitro and caused a growth defect when Dsn1 function was impaired. The Cnn1 mutation reduced Stu2 kinetochore levels without altering other kinetochore proteins. Restoring Stu2, either by direct addition in vitro or by tethering it to Ndc80c in vivo, rescued both attachment strength and cellular viability. These findings reveal a biophysical role for Cnn1 in enabling Stu2-dependent stabilization of kinetochore-microtubule attachments.

papers.title: Inherited proliferation states organize plant transcriptomes
papers.abstract: Expression variation in natural plant populations is usually read gene by gene, as a response to the environment. Whether a leading axis of that variation is more strongly associated with ancestry than with home-site environment, and whether it is heritable, remain unresolved. We integrated transcriptomes, genotypes, environmental records and phenotypes from 665 Arabidopsis thaliana accessions grown under one condition. Genomic ancestry uniquely explained 5.0% of the dominant expression axis, compared with 2.6% for home-site environment, and exceeded environment under all four allocations of geography and the circadian covariate (1.9- to 6.2-fold). This axis was associated with a heritable cell-cycle- and ribosome-enriched module (prolifME; h^2 = 0.19), linked to four loci with widespread trans-expression associations and associated with smaller plants in two independent experiments and with slower growth under controlled conditions. The advantage is concentrated on the leading expression axes and narrows across the full transcriptome. The gene weights defining the Arabidopsis axis were correlated with independently derived profiles in rice and maize, with the correspondence carried mainly by photosynthesis-associated genes. Ancestry therefore predicts the leading expression axes, and the heritable proliferation module that carries the first axis tracks growth phenotypes independently of ancestry.

papers.title: One Health genomic epidemiology reveals cryptic transmission and surveillance gaps in a decade-long urban rabies epidemic in Arequipa, Peru
papers.abstract: Persistent local foci remain a major barrier to eliminating dog-mediated rabies, yet the processes sustaining transmission at micro-scales, particularly within complex urban systems, remain poorly understood. We apply an integrated One Health genomic epidemiology framework to reconstruct a decade-long rabies virus (RABV) epidemic in Arequipa, Peru. Combining 133 newly generated whole genomes with existing data, we assembled the most comprehensive canine RABV dataset in Latin America and used whole-genome-informed phylogenetic, phylodynamic and landscape analyses to trace the epidemic from its first detection in 2015. Transmission was dominated by a single lineage, estimated to have been introduced around 2012, which circulated for approximately three years before detection. We estimate that only 1-2% of infections are routinely detected, revealing extensive cryptic transmission and highlighting the limitations of case-based metrics for verifying disease freedom. Although additional regional and transboundary introductions were identified, only one resulted in sustained transmission. Within Arequipa city, transmission was highly structured, concentrated in densely populated and socioeconomically deprived areas, and shaped by urban connectivity. Roads and dry water channels facilitated spread, while rivers acted as partial barriers. Our findings demonstrate that rabies persistence reflects interacting processes across spatial scales, from regional introductions to highly structured urban transmission. They highlight the importance of genomic-informed, spatially targeted surveillance and control strategies to identify and address persistent transmission foci and accelerate progress towards elimination.

papers.title: RICO enables integrated analysis of ribosomal DNA copy number and methylation from nanopore long-read sequencing
papers.abstract: Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) provides the structural and catalytic core of ribosomes and is encoded by ribosomal RNA genes (rDNA) arranged in tandem repeat arrays. rDNA copy number (CN) is highly dynamic, representing a clinically relevant form of structural variation, but its accurate quantification has been challenging due to its highly repetitive and GC-rich nature. Here, we present RICO (RIbosomal dna Integrated COpy number and methylation analysis), a novel computational pipeline for integrated estimation of rDNA CN and methylation using Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing. RICO leverages long sequencing reads that span entire rDNA repeats, mapped to an rDNA-augmented reference genome, and normalizes coverage using a single-copy gene panel. We demonstrate that RICO provides accurate rDNA CN estimates in simulated datasets and reproducible measurements across human samples, with strong agreement to short-read sequencing and PCR-based methods. Furthermore, RICO reproduces a ~40% reduction in rDNA CN in Atrx-knockout mouse embryonic stem cells, consistent with established effects of ATRX loss on rDNA CN. RICO also captures an increased total and active rDNA CN in malignant cells from a MYC-driven B-cell lymphoma mouse model, in agreement with prior studies. Applying RICO to independent human cohorts, we uncover that individuals with higher total rDNA CN consistently exhibit higher fractions of highly methylated rDNA copies, suggesting a dosage compensation mechanism that potentially maintains a similar number of active rDNA copies across individuals. Together, RICO enables integrated analysis of rDNA CN and methylation state, providing a scalable framework for investigating rDNA regulation across population and disease studies. RICO is available at https://github.com/comprna/RICO.

papers.title: Replication stress links Geminin depletion to centrosome amplification
papers.abstract: The timing of DNA replication and centrosome duplication is tightly regulated with cell cycle progression to ensure the faithful duplication of the genome during cell division. Both DNA and centrosomes are licensed for replication in late telophase/early G1, replicated in S phase and segregated during mitosis; yet how defects in DNA replication licensing are coupled to centrosome homeostasis remains poorly understood. Here, we show that depletion of the replication licensing inhibitor Geminin in proliferating mouse embryonic fibroblasts induces robust centrosome amplification together with impaired primary cilium assembly. Rather than promoting whole-genome reduplication, knockdown of Geminin triggers a replication stress response, characterized by DNA damage accumulation throughout the cycle, and activation of an ATR-dependent DNA damage response. Mechanistically, Geminin depletion-induced replication stress activates the ATR-Chk1-Wee1 checkpoint axis prolonging G2 and leading to premature centriole disengagement and centrosome amplification. These findings identify replication stress as the signaling module that couples defective DNA replication licensing to centrosome amplification.

papers.title: LOESS and DE-SWAN can induce artifactual "waves" of molecular aging
papers.abstract: A growing body of literature has investigated the relationship between age and biomolecular changes, leading to conclusions that aging occurs in discrete molecular ``waves.'' Data summary tools such as LOESS and sliding window analyses like DE-SWAN are common approaches that have gained acceptance in recent years. We demonstrate via simple simulations that these tools can identify non-linear patterns of aging where they do not exist. Specifically, we show that (i) clustering of molecular trajectories using LOESS can lead to artifactual characteristic patterns of molecular aging, (ii) ``waves'' of aging identified using the combination of LOESS and DE-SWAN in real data are not robust to changes in the underlying age distribution and are not supported by valid permutation testing, and (iii) DE-SWAN alone can generate pronounced "waves'" of nonlinear molecular aging in linear data due to differences in statistical power along the age continuum. Our results specifically challenge the statistical support for discrete aging crests inferred in the literature, but do not rule out nonlinear molecular aging or age-associated transitions that may be detectable using other cohorts and statistical models.

papers.title: Post-attack bioluminescence is an aposematic signal in cypridinid ostracods
papers.abstract: Aposematic signals convey information about prey unpalatability to potential predators. Such signals are defined as advertisements, with prey usually signalling unpalatability before an attack. Overlooked, however, is whether signals presented after an attack can function as aposematic warnings and improve survival. Here, we test if post-attack signals can be aposematic by observing fish predators responding to prey (Ostracoda, Cypridinidae) that produce bioluminescence following an attack. By manipulating potential chemical defences of prey, and by comparing feeding responses to both bioluminescent and nonluminescent prey, we provide multiple lines of evidence to show bioluminescent prey are unpalatable and use post-attack bioluminescence as an aposematic signal. First, live, bioluminescent prey secrete bioluminescence only after being attacked. Second, predatory fishes rarely consumed bioluminescent prey, especially compared to nonluminescent alternatives. Third, because fishes readily ate bioluminescent prey that had been treated (frozen or boiled), which should remove chemical defences, bioluminescent species likely possess some unidentified defence over nonluminescent relatives. Finally, over the course of four experimental trials, predators were less likely to consume bioluminescent prey as their cumulative exposure to bioluminescent displays increased, indicative of learning. Post-attack aposematic signals, as found with bioluminescence, may be as common and effective a defensive strategy as pre-attack signals.

papers.title: Metabolism of bilirubin to urobilinogen by human gut bacteria occurs by a branched, multi-enzyme pathway
papers.abstract: Bilirubin, the predominant product of heme catabolism in mammals, enters the intestine via the hepatobiliary system and subsequently is metabolized by the gut microbiome into multiple downstream derivatives, such as urobilinogen and stercobilinogen. Variation in levels of bilirubin and its derivatives are associated with inflammatory and metabolic disorders, but the microbial species and enzymes that metabolize bilirubin have remained largely unknown, which has precluded causal and mechanistic studies. Here, we demonstrate that metabolism of bilirubin to urobilinogen requires multiple distinct reactions carried out by separate enzymes. We find that bilirubin reductase (BilR), an enzyme that was recently discovered and proposed to convert bilirubin to urobilinogen, is specific for reducing the methine bridges of bilinoids, converting bilirubin to the previously uncharacterized intermediate divinylurobilinogen and mesobilirubin to urobilinogen. We identify bilinoid vinyl reductase (BilV), a flavin-dependent oxidoreductase of the Old Yellow Enzyme (OYE) superfamily, as the enzyme responsible for reducing the vinyl groups of bilirubin and divinylurobilinogen. Both BilR and BilV are capable of acting on multiple bilinoids, such that the reductions required to convert bilirubin to urobilinogen can proceed in multiple orders through a branched network of intermediates. BilV is widespread in human gut metagenomes and is broadly distributed across gut bacteria in a manner that overlaps with but does not mirror the distribution of BilR. These findings establish the identities of novel factors in bacterial bilirubin metabolism, delineate the branched architecture of the pathway, and enable defined studies to interrogate how such branched metabolism contributes to human health and disease.

papers.title: BenchRep-T: A Systematic Evaluation of T-Cell Repertoire-Based Disease Diagnostics
papers.abstract: Adaptive immune receptor repertoire sequencing data has emerged as a promising potential modality for disease diagnosis, relying on computational methods to analyze T-cell receptor (TCR) sequences from an individual's blood sample. Published methods rely on different cohorts, data preprocessing pipelines, and evaluation metrics, making direct comparison across methods challenging. We present BenchRep-T, a unified benchmark that standardizes multiple publicly available TCR repertoire datasets and evaluates nine computational approaches, spanning statistical enrichment of shared sequences, feature-engineered ensembles, deep learning, and sequence clustering. BenchRep-T evaluates methods on four tasks: disease classification across conditions, performance scaling under restricted sequence-sampling depth, recovery of known antigen-specific driver sequences, and evaluation of sensitivity to demographic confounding. Under controlled evaluation, simple baselines prove competitive, with tree-based models trained on V- and J-gene usage and short sequence motifs approaching the classification performance of more complex methods. Our findings underscore the complexity of modeling TCR repertoire data, and show that no single method dominates across all tasks. BenchRep-T provides a framework for rigorous and reproducible evaluation of TCR repertoire classification methods to accelerate the development of immune repertoire-based diagnostics.

papers.title: Butyrate supplementation reshapes systemic metabolism and attenuates cardiac aging
papers.abstract: Identifying interventions that improve health and cardiac function is important for extending healthspan. We show that supplementation with the SCFA butyrate beginning at 18 months (late life) extends survival in male and female mice and improves systemic metabolic and physical-performance measures. Treatment reduces adiposity and fasting glucose and attenuates age-associated cardiac hypertrophy, fibrosis, and systolic and diastolic dysfunction. Integrated plasma and myocardial metabolomics and lipidomics reveal compartment-dependent metabolic remodeling, while cardiac proteomics and full-length RNA sequencing identify coordinated changes in extracellular-matrix, RNA-processing, lipid-metabolism, and autophagy-associated programs. These molecular responses are accompanied by improved mitochondrial ultrastructural organization and respiratory function. Butyrate supplementation also enhanced cardiac autophagy and mitophagy, and its beneficial effects on LV hypertrophy and diastolic indices required ATG7. These findings demonstrate that butyrate supplementation initiated at an advanced age modifies systemic and cardiac aging phenotypes and implicate metabolic remodeling and mitochondrial quality control pathways as contributing to these benefits.

papers.title: Evaluation of the Peacock Eye Disease Management (PedMan) System in Highly Susceptible Olive Cultivar and Using the System for Addressing Key Biological Questions
papers.abstract: Peacock eye disease, caused by Venturia oleaginea, is a major foliar disease of olive (Olea europaea) in Mediterranean regions, resulting in defoliation, reduced tree vigor, and yield losses. Effective disease management relies on precise fungicide timing. In this study, we evaluated a decision support system (DSS) named PedMan (Peacock eye disease Manager), designed to predict infection events and optimize fungicide application timing in highly susceptible olive cultivars based on rainfall and temperature conditions. PedMan recommendations were examined in seven independent grove experiments conducted during the 2023/24 and 2024/25 growing seasons in commercial olive orchards in Israel. In addition, simulation analyses were performed using weather data from 11 meteorological stations representing diverse climatic regions. Field evaluation showed that fungicide applications timed according to PedMan recommendation significantly reduced leaf abscission by approximately 60% compared with untreated controls. Applications made contrary to system recommendations did not improve disease control, confirming the reliability of both positive and negative recommendations. Multi-season analyses indicated cumulative disease suppression, with up to 85% reduction in leaf abscission after three consecutive years of correctly timed applications. The system was implemented by olive growers in 2025/6 with applicable success. Simulation results showed that most infection alerts occurred in autumn and early winter. Across all regions and seasons, PedMan recommended 0-3 fungicide applications per season, comparable to or fewer than conventional spray programs. These findings demonstrate that PedMan is a robust, field-validated DSS that improves fungicide timing, enhances disease control efficiency, and supports sustainable management of peacock eye disease without increasing spray instances under Mediterranean conditions.

papers.title: A dynamic encoder-like protein hub reconciles specialization and plasticity through subcellular mobility
papers.abstract: How does a conserved regulatory network produce locally specific outcomes across many developmental contexts? Flexible subcellular compartmentalization of proteins can be a powerful source of dynamic modularity, in which proteins mobility links parts of a network, opening alternative regulatory states. Using a comprehensive protein-expression atlas of avian beak morphogenesis, we show that a craniofacial network resolves into a stable core and a hub of multivalent proteins whose links to the core depend on where in the cell they colocalize. We show that this bow-tie architecture doubles the number of regulatory states the network can express at any given stage and, across development, allows nearly complete exploration of its regulatory potential without adding or removing elements. These proteins behave as dynamic encoder-like hubs whose localization-dependent interactions convert diverse mechanical and biochemical inputs into specific outputs, such that specialization and changeability increase together rather than trade off as is commonly assumed. This organization lets a compact, conserved network sustain continuous and diversifying development, exemplifying a mechanistic reconciliation of ecological precision and the evolutionary lability of avian beaks.

papers.title: Diploidy alters the path of fluconazole adaptation in Candida glabrata
papers.abstract: Candida glabrata (syn. Nakaseomyces glabratus) is a major fungal pathogen, typically isolated as a haploid. We isolated a spontaneous diploid variant of the type strain CBS138 and performed experimental evolution under fluconazole. At physiologically relevant concentrations of fluconazole, we found that haploids and diploids both acquired PDR1 mutations, as is commonly observed in C. glabrata; diploids additionally acquired heterozygous ERG11 and ERG25 mutations and were more likely to acquire aneuploidies. Despite an ancestral fitness advantage for haploids, after ~200 generations the highest-fitness clones, as measured in competitive assays with and without fluconazole, were diploid double heterozygotes having nonsynonymous mutations to PDR1 and ERG11 or PDR1 and ERG25. Diploid clones also had higher minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) to fluconazole. These results suggest, in this particular context, an evolvability advantage for diploids. In a follow-up experiment in which we rapidly increased the fluconazole concentration to a very high concentration, haploids and diploids adapted via entirely distinct routes: haploids via co-mutation in ERG3 and CgOSH3, a previously unreported path to fluconazole resistance, and diploids via heterozygous mutation in ERG25 coupled with trisomies of chrF, chrG, and chrI in all sampled clones, and chrC in most sampled clones.

papers.title: Strand inequality in terms of expression-dependent synonymous single-nucleotide polymorphism in the Escherichia coli chromosome
papers.abstract: Mutations in genomes are mainly attributed to replication, though transcription, which is a more frequent event than replication, is also known to be mutagenic in an organism. However, a distinct demonstration of specific mutations being replication-dependent and/or expression-dependent in genomes is yet to be established. Here, we studied synonymous single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in 2091 individual coding sequences (CDS) in the leading strand (LeS) and the lagging strand (LaS) of the Escherichia coli chromosome by comparing across 157 strains. The frequencies of complementary transitions (ti) and complementary transversions (tv) were compared in each CDS to assess parity violation in the context of strand location and gene expression using codon adaptation index (CAI) as a proxy. The C[->]T and G[->]A tiexhibited the maximum frequency as well as the most prominent strand inequality, as these ti were influenced both by the strand asymmetry and gene expression, especially in the LeS. Surprisingly, the inequality between T[->]C and A[->]G was found to be gene expression dependent. In addition to CAI-based analysis, we performed the above analysis in CDS based on protein expression data and obtained similar results. A[->]T and G[->]Ttv were more frequent than their complementary T[->]A and C[->]A, respectively, in a strand-independent manner. The strand-independent but expression-dependent synonymous SNP inequality in CDS supports the role of transcription-induced mutagenesis contributing to strand inequality in the E. coli chromosome.

papers.title: Alternative splicing switches human Musashi-2 between cytoplasmic and nuclear regulatory functions
papers.abstract: Musashi-2 (MSI2) is an RNA-binding protein that controls self-renewal and differentiation in the hematopoietic and nervous systems and sustains myeloid leukemia. It both activates and represses translation of its target mRNAs, outcomes usually attributed to cellular context. We find instead that the capacity to activate translation is determined by an alternative 3' splice acceptor in exon 12, which splits full-length MSI2 into isoforms that carry or lack an 18-amino-acid insertion in the C-terminal disordered region. MSI2-328 is cytoplasmic and the insertion-containing MSI2-324 is nuclear. The insertion is necessary and sufficient for nuclear localization. Tethering MSI2-328 to a reporter mRNA promotes translation, whereas tethering MSI2-324 does not, and removing the insertion restores activation. Consistent with their localization, MSI2-328 binds translation factors and 3' UTRs, while MSI2-324 binds splicing factors and introns. Use of the insertion-generating acceptor ranges from 19% in skeletal muscle to 51% in the brain and increases in several tumor types. Altogether, one splicing event toggles MSI2 between the cytoplasm and the nucleus, so localization, rather than cellular context, determines its regulatory function.

papers.title: Decomposing the modulation of interactions between neuronal populations
papers.abstract: Identifying, through analysis of large-scale neural recordings, subpopulations of neurons interacting across brain areas is key for understanding across-brain communication with cellular resolution. The communication subspace (CS) framework addresses this need by capturing additive interactions between subspaces of source and target neural populations. However, no current method identifies interpretable components of how a measured, multivariate modulator - such as behavioral state or the activity of another population - reshapes these interactions. Here we extend the CS framework by using a bilinear perturbation of reduced-rank regression to parameterize modulation as a low-rank tensor. We derive MICs - multiplicative interaction channels - a method to identify triplets made of a source and a target activity pattern and a modulator of their interaction. We develop a hierarchical fitting pipeline and provide a closed-form decomposition that quantifies whether modulation reshapes the modulator-averaged baseline interaction, recruits private dimensions of one population, or opens new interactions. In simulations, MICs reliably recovers the presence and geometry of ground-truth modulation even in the high-dimensional, low-sample regime. Applied to a benchmark macaque dataset, MICs recovers the geometry and functional form of the stimulus modulation of interactions between primary and secondary visual cortices. Applied to simultaneous calcium imaging of prefrontal axons and interneurons in mouse visual cortex, MICs reveals that behavioral state asymmetrically modulates top-down interactions, reconfiguring the prefrontal projection patterns that interact with a stable set of visual interneurons. MICs provides a data-efficient, interpretable account of how measured modulators reshape the interactions between neural populations. Code is available at https://github.com/mcelotto/multiplicative_interaction_channels.

papers.title: Electrophilic Multi-Kinase Probes Identify Degradation and Aspartate Conjugation of ULK1
papers.abstract: Kinases have proven to be one of the most fertile target classes for new drug approvals, however, classical reversible inhibitors may not be capable of the levels of specificity or target modulation required across a broad spectrum of disease areas. Approaches that chemically modify kinase inhibitors in solvent exposed regions are unveiling a swathe of mechanisms to address kinase function in new ways. For example, by either covalently recruiting nucleophilic residues outside of the ATP-binding pocket to inhibit, or by recruiting secondary effector proteins to degrade. Here, we established a systematic workflow to assess the cellular impact of minimal electrophilic modifications to ATP-site binding scaffolds. Amongst multiple potential starting points for monovalent kinase degradation that were revealed, we identified that one of our scout molecules was able to control the abundance of the master regulator of autophagy, Unc-51-like autophagy activating kinase 1 (ULK1) and that a scaffold-hop could be performed to generate a targeted monovalent ULK1 degrader chemical tool, we named ALP-1. Remarkably, further investigation of how ALP-1 engages ULK1 unveiled an atypical conjugation event between the chloroacetamide warhead of ALP1 and an aspartate residue on the lip of the ULK1 ATP-binding site. These discoveries reveal new understanding of the potential for non-cysteine reactivity of the commonly employed chloroacetamide warhead, as well as new opportunities for the targeting and covalent engagement of kinases.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses identify novel biomarkers of bladder outlet obstruction
