Nevertheless, the remaining surviving population maintained required active chemotactic capabilities, while the lysed bacterial matrix provided a natural protein capping layer that prevented nanoparticle aggregation. Under 5 minutes of continuous NIR laser irradiation, the EcN::AuNPs platform exhibited exceptional concentration-dependent hyperthermia kinetics, triggering a drastic thermal escalation from 20 C to an absolute peak of 75.4 C, vastly outperforming all baseline control groups (pure EcN, bare HAuCl4, and standalone ascorbic acid). Conclusion: The engineered EcN::AuNPs bio-hybrid platform represents a highly efficient and biosafe "bacteriobot" paradigm. By shifting the SPR footprint and leveraging the native bacterial cell envelope for colloidal stability, this system achieves an optimal equilibrium between active biological tumor targeting and rapid, localized photothermal ablation, offering a promising alternative for targeted oncological interventions.

papers.title: Agile manufacturing of PDMS microfluidic devices for cell culture without a clean room
papers.abstract: Microfluidic devices control fluid flow and the cellular microenvironment, and their fabrication usually relies on photolithography in a clean room. For devices with features of hundreds of micrometers to millimeters, this route is slow and costly, especially during prototyping, when the design changes after each test. Here, we describe and benchmark a workflow to fabricate polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) devices from laser-cut master molds, with equipment accessible to most biology laboratories. We cut three inexpensive materials, poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA), polystyrene and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) tape, over a grid of laser power and speed and measured each cut by scanning electron microscopy. Cut depth and width increased line-arly with the laser energy delivered per unit length, which gives a simple rule to choose the settings for each material. We then bonded the PDMS replicas to glass without a plasma cleaner, by stopping curing early, once the replica could be demolded, and completing it in contact with the glass. Without any surface treatment, these devices held up to about 400 mbar; activating the glass with a handheld corona device raised this to about 900 mbar, enough for perfusion. The master material set the surface of the device: PMMA gave smooth replicas, whereas PVC tape gave rough walls. A three-channel device molded on PMMA held two cell-laden gels in place with phase guides and supported the co-culture of cancer cells and fibroblasts under perfusion. Further analysis of flow laminarity and different mixer designs confirmed the robustness of this method. This workflow takes a digital design to a working de-vice within a day and lets biology laboratories adapt microfluidic devices to their experiments without the need of a clean room.

papers.title: BioMeme: biological response memory for virtual cells
papers.abstract: Virtual cells predict responses to unmeasured perturbations, but neural models absorb measurements into weights, require retraining and cannot cite supporting experiments. Here we introduce biological response memory, replacing a learned state-to-response layer with a memory of measured experiments. BioMeme predicts next-dose responses in a new cell type from measured lower-dose states, recalling similarly responding compounds in that cell and the same compound in a reference cell line. Each prediction is an exact weighted sum of named measurements, and memory updates with one linear solve. In all nine preregistered comparisons across three screens, memory predicted response direction better than the learners it replaced. In U2OS, BioMeme outperformed input-matched ridge, adapted chemCPA and a neural layer in memory's place, and matched a full-panel network reading reference responses directly (error within 3.4%). Transfer was compound-specific, lowering error by 21.2% against at most 1.8% for wrong compounds, and replicated in reserved MCF7 data. With 20 references, fitting took seconds on one CPU thread, at least 420 times faster than neural tuning and fitting. Adding its prediction to one measured well cut that well's error by 27-31%. Biological response memory establishes a design principle for virtual cells any laboratory can update, inspect and run.

papers.title: PRISM: probabilistic cell-type resolution with integrated spatial modelling for simultaneous ambient RNA decontamination and doublet correction in spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics count matrices are confounded by ambient RNA contamination and cell-segmentation doublets, two artifacts that co-occur but are rarely modelled jointly. We present PRISM, an Expectation-Maximization framework that simultaneously (i) assigns each cell a probabilistic cell-type identity, (ii) detects doublets via log-likelihood ratio testing of two-component mixtures, and (iii) estimates a per-cell contamination fraction anchored to a spatially resolved ambient profile. In an in silico benchmark of 40,800 simulated cells, PRISM recovers with Pearson r=1.000 across all contamination levels (0.05 to 0.50) and UMI depths (500 to 5,000), with zero doublet false positives and 100% singlet accuracy. Applied to a Visium HD mouse cerebellum dataset (four samples, 125,289 cells, 17 reference types) from a metachromatic leukodystrophy (MLD) model, PRISM identifies a median =0.60, flags 67.4% doublets (driven by the densely packed cerebellar granule layer), eliminates spurious myelin signal from microglia (0.82% to 0.00%), and doubles oligodendrocyte myelin purity (2.8% to 5.6%). PRISM runs on commodity CPUs in under 15 minutes and returns decontaminated integer count matrices for every measured gene.

papers.title: Divergence in sleep architecture associated with interspecific shifts in memory investment
papers.abstract: Sleep plays a critical role in stabilising memory. However, whether the architecture of sleep co-evolves with investment in learning and memory is unknown. To address this, we exploit the extreme levels of neural and behavioural divergence among Heliconiini butterflies. Compared to other Heliconiini, Heliconius have massively expanded mushroom bodies, the insect centres of learning and memory, which are associated with specific enhancements in visual learning and memory. Using a purpose-built video system, machine learning-facilitated behavioural tracking, and in-depth analysis of micro-behaviours during nighttime quiescence, we describe multi-state sleep in Heliconius melpomene and an outgroup Heliconiini, Dryas iulia. In both species, sleep is predominantly composed of quiet sleep, however, Heliconius and Dryas deviate in specific features. In Dryas iulia, quiet sleep is characterised by highly stereotyped, rhythmic antennal oscillations. Conversely, the antennae of Heliconius melpomene remain largely motionless but occasionally perform large movements which interrupt quiet sleep. These antennal deflections are associated with bouts of activity that include increased overall antennal displacement, isolated head twitching, proboscis movements and less frequently, wing movements. While these episodes were also seen in Dryas iulia, they were considerably less frequent. We further demonstrate that the behavioural profile of these active sleep bouts is constituently different from bouts of induced wakefulness, providing experimental support for multi-state sleep in Lepidoptera. This work shows that Heliconius melpomene, a species distinguished by its expanded mushroom bodies, exhibits more frequent bouts of active sleep than the outgroup species Dryas iulia. These findings raise the possibility that increased investment in learning and memory, as well as the structures that support it, may be associated with changes in sleep architecture.

papers.title: Natural regeneration in tree islands drives long-term recovery of native forest-associated woody species in oil palm landscapes
papers.abstract: 1. Large-scale conversion of tropical rainforests to oil palm plantations is a major driver of biodiversity loss in Southeast Asia, particularly threatening native forest-associated plant species and their associated biota. Integrating tree islands within monocultural oil palm landscapes has emerged as a promising approach to mitigate biodiversity loss. However, their effectiveness in sustaining natural regeneration and long-term recovery of native forest-associated plant species remains unclear. 2. We analyzed temporal trajectories of diversity, abundance, and composition of naturally recruiting woody species in tree islands embedded in a monoculture-dominated landscape. We used a large-scale biodiversity enrichment experiment with 52 tree islands, varying in area (25 - 1600 m2) and planted tree diversity (0, 1, 2, 3, or 6 species), established in a conventional oil palm plantation in Sumatra, Indonesia, in 2013. 3. Across four censuses conducted between 2 and 8 years after the onset of natural regeneration, we found 82 species of recruiting woody plants (trees and shrubs) belonging to 64 genera and 34 families. At the landscape (gamma) scale, species richness and abundance increased by ~42% and ~69%, respectively, from 2018 to 2024, with shifts in community evenness and continued species arrival. After 8 years, neither richness nor abundance saturated, indicating continued accumulation of recruiting plant species. 4. Tree islands promoted natural regeneration of native diversity, with 90% of species and individuals being native. Native forest-associated species (N = 35) increased steadily at the landscape scale, while localized dominance of alien species did not indicate arrested succession. 5. At the local (alpha) scale, larger island area exerted a sustained positive effect on recruiting diversity. Higher initial planted tree diversity promoted native recruitment, particularly of forest-associated species, at earlier stages, an effect that diminished over time. 6. Synthesis and applications. Tree islands promote natural regeneration and accelerate recovery of native forest-associated diversity over extended periods, providing an effective strategy to enhance forest-associated biodiversity within oil palm landscapes. Preserving the last remaining lowland rainforests, irreplaceable reservoirs of native forest-associated species, remains essential to support continued recruitment into tree islands that can create stepping-stone habitats and a more wildlife-friendly agricultural matrix.

papers.title: A Three-View System for CRISPR-Cas12a crRNA Activity Ranking: When to Ensemble, When Context Matters More
papers.abstract: CRISPR-Cas12a assays require effective crRNA selection, but experimentally screening all possible candidates is costly. We developed TriCasRank, a ranking model that combines sequence features with EasyDesign reference mapping and activity summaries from related training records. Historical summaries were calculated within each training fold to avoid information leakage. In five-fold target-grouped cross-validation using out-of-fold predictions, TriCasRank improved the Spearman correlation from 0.741 for the sequence-only ensemble to 0.821 (paired difference, 0.080; 95% target-group bootstrap interval, 0.072 to 0.090). However, its performance was comparable to that of a strong sequence-plus-mapping XGBoost model (SCC, 0.822; paired difference, -0.001; 95% interval, -0.007 to 0.005). Separate perturbation analyses supported the predictive value of mapping and historical features, although their effect sizes were not directly comparable because they were evaluated using different model configurations. Prediction errors remained larger at the extremes of the activity distribution. Performance also became less stable when template identities were separated between training and evaluation. TriCasRank may therefore be useful for ranking candidates represented within the EasyDesign-derived domain, but evaluation on an independent experimental cohort is still needed.

papers.title: Microenvironmental Fingerprint of Maturing Tau Condensates from Spectral and Lifetime Phasor Analysis of a Solvatochromic Dye
papers.abstract: Solvatochromic dyes respond to changes in their local environment through variations in both spectral properties and fluorescence lifetime. These responses arise from the excited-state behavior of the probe, but the sensitivity of each response to a given environment can differ. In this work, we developed a multimodal phasor-based framework for two-photon spectral and fluorescence lifetime imaging analysis. To validate the framework, we imaged the solvatochromic dye ACDAN in water, glycerol, and ethanol. ACDAN showed clear spectral differences among the three solvents, whereas its fluorescence lifetime separated water from both organic solvents but not glycerol from ethanol, indicating that the two observables respond differently to the same environmental change. We then applied ACDAN to a well-described model system, the maturation of liquid-liquid phase-separated condensates of the microtubule-binding, neurodegeneration-related protein Tau into later-stage assemblies. Across Tau samples incubated for 1, 4, and 48 h, a progressive decrease in the ACDAN spectral phasor angle {theta} and increase in its phase-derived lifetime {tau}P suggested increasingly restricted dipolar relaxation in the probe environment. Differences among condensates were apparent by 4 h, whereas pronounced spatial heterogeneity within assemblies was observed at 48 h. Lastly, we evaluated the multimodal framework on Tau assemblies labeled with the fluorogenic probe Thioflavin T. As expected, this dye predominantly sensed its environment through its fluorescence lifetime, with comparatively limited spectral changes, whereas ACDAN reported microenvironmental changes in both coordinates. Together, this framework combines spectral and lifetime descriptors to characterize changes in the fluorescence response across Tau assembly maturation while retaining their spatial distribution.

papers.title: SeekNSee: A Rule-Based Framework for Prioritizing Proteotypic Peptides
papers.abstract: Selecting peptides candidates for target proteomics requires integrating a multicriteria problem, particularly when users lack prior experimental data, programming expertise, or stable access to external repositories. We development SeekNSee, a locally executed R/Shiny application designed to improve the reproducibility and auditability of peptide-candidate screening through enzyme-aware in silico digestion, configurable and traceable rule-level decision tracking. Starting from a user provided reference proteome and target sequences, SeekNSee generates peptides-candidates using nine digestion configurations and evaluates them with 12 rules configured as ignore, apply, or block. Numerical score and retained/blocking status are stored independently, and every candidate-rule outcome is preserved in a rule-level trace. Computational validation confirmed the specified behavior in controlled cases through 198 passing automated assertions, complemented by successful operational and processing tests on Windows and Ubuntu. Proteome-wide application covered all 20,416 reviewed human proteins, generating 733,864 peptide-candidate and 581,026 unique peptides sequences while preserving data integrity, decision traceability, and candidate-specific context. DIA, DDA, and deep-fractionated proteomics benchmarking showed strong associations between SeekNSee scores categories, peptide observation, and multiple analytical measurements. Together, these results support that SeekNSee provides a transparent and traceable screening layer for generating peptide-candidates for subsequent assay and experimental validation.

papers.title: 41% of Gram-negative bacteria encode a Type Six Secretion System
papers.abstract: The type six secretion system (T6SS) is a highly studied, versatile bacterial nanoweapon that is important in bacterial pathogenesis and evolution. Despite extensive study, its prevalence remains poorly quantified. Analyzing 35,467 representative genomes, we find that approximately 41% of genomes in the average well-sampled Gram-negative genus (more than 30 sampled genomes) encode a T6SS. Further, we show that the distribution of the T6SS is patchy at all taxonomic levels. The uneven distribution we found is consistent with context-dependent selection, repeated evolutionary loss, or greater evolutionary lability. Our dataset provides a foundation for studying the drivers of T6SS distribution, and our pipeline enables similar surveys of other secretion systems, gene clusters, and multi-protein complexes across bacteria.

papers.title: EGF and EREG regulate early oncoprotein-mediated tissue transformation in intestinal organoids.
papers.abstract: Somatic mutations, coupled with abnormal extracellular signaling cues, promote tumor development. The abundance and affinity of EGF-family ligands for EGFR influence tissue development and play a central role in organoid culture by differentially regulating the balance between crypt proliferation and villus differentiation in mouse small intestinal organoids (mSIOs). To test how medium ligand composition affects early oncogenic transformation, we generated a Ptprg KO organoid line by CRISPR/Cas9 and two previously described organoid lines harboring synthetic bio-orthogonal expression systems for KRASG12V and {beta}-Ctn4A, activated by the membrane-diffusible ligands TMP or TMP-Cl. Measurements of crypt and villus region area showed that acute oncogenic activity did not alter organoid growth in media containing 50 ng/mL EGF; however, organoids grown without EGF consistently showed differential growth of the crypt region. Furthermore, EREG and sub-saturating EGF (0.5-5 ng/mL) treatments differentially affected crypt/villus development in each organoid line. Finally, we measured organoid morphology and found that crypt domain spatial distribution is independent of crypt area and requires EGF or EREG, highlighting the role of both proliferation and crypt organization in oncogenic tissue transformation.

papers.title: Symbiotic and commensal root microbes are key determinants of plant responses to rising CO2
papers.abstract: Rising atmospheric CO2 stimulates plant growth, but this effect is often constrained by nutrient availability. While beneficial soil-derived microbial symbionts such as nitrogen-fixing rhizobia and mycorrhizal fungi are known to mitigate this limitation, the role of plant commensal microbiota remains unclear. Here, using a gnotobiotic growth system and the model legume Lotus japonicus, we show that the magnitude of plant responses to elevated CO2 is largely explained by the composition of its root-associated microbial community. Axenic plants exhibited limited physiological responses to increasing CO2 but inoculation with symbiotic and commensal microbes significantly amplified this effect. Commensal bacteria alone, while not increasing overall biomass, shifted plant carbon allocation belowground. Microbial abundances in roots increased with atmospheric CO2, even when normalized to plant DNA. The strongest plant and microbial responses were observed when rhizobia, arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi, and the commensal bacterial community were all present. These findings indicate that multi-partner microbial associations will shape both plant growth and the allocation of carbon belowground as atmospheric CO2 concentrations continue to rise.

papers.title: Biocatalytic Asymmetric Radical Dearomatization of Electrophilic Heterocyclic and Non-Heterocyclic Arenes
papers.abstract: Catalytic asymmetric dearomatization provides a powerful strategy for converting readily available aromatic feedstocks into valuable three-dimensional molecular scaffolds. Despite substantial advances over the past several decades, general methods for catalytic asymmetric dearomatization of electrophilic arenes, particularly non-heterocyclic substrates with high aromatic stabilization energies, remain a challenging task. Here, we report the use of a hydrogen atom transfer mechanism for biocatalytic radical dearomatization of electron-deficient arenes. Repurposing and directed evolution of our previously developed P450 halogen atom transferases furnished hydrogen atom transfer dearomatases that catalyze the stereoselective dearomatization of a range of electrophilic arenes, including electron-deficient indoles, pyrroles, and simple benzene derivatives. These evolved biocatalysts facilitated both diastereodivergent and enantiodivergent radical dearomatization, providing access to fused and spirocyclic chiral scaffolds bearing challenging quaternary and/or contiguous stereocenters. Computational and experimental studies revealed that a strategically positioned active-site lysine residue enables enzyme-controlled proton transfer against the intrinsic thermodynamic stereopreference, allowing catalyst-controlled reversal of diastereoselectivity from a common radical intermediate. Importantly, the evolved dearomatases efficiently transformed challenging arene substrates that proved recalcitrant under previously optimized Fe, Mn and Co-based metal-hydride hydrogen atom transfer conditions. Collectively, these results establish new-to-nature metalloredox biocatalysis as a powerful strategy for overcoming longstanding challenges in asymmetric radical catalysis.

papers.title: Stathmin-2 regulates microtubule dynamics and axonal resilience in human motor neurons
papers.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is characterized by the selective degeneration of motor neurons, yet the mechanisms that either induce neurodegeneration or confer neuronal resilience remain poorly understood. Loss of the microtubule-associated protein Stathmin-2 (STMN2) is a downstream consequence of TDP-43 pathology present in nearly all cases of ALS and has emerged as a central feature of disease. However, the mechanisms by which STMN2 maintains homeostasis in motor neurons remain incompletely defined. Here, we investigated the role of STMN2 in regulating cytoskeletal organization and axonal function. Using TIRF microscopy, we quantified STMN2-dependent changes in microtubule growth and catastrophe at single-microtubule resolution. In human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived motor neurons, STMN2 depletion increased baseline rates of microtubule polymerization. However, STMN2 depletion impaired recovery of axonal microtubules following transient nocodazole-induced depolymerization, indicating that STMN2 is required for efficient cytoskeletal remodeling after stress. Consistent with these findings, STMN2-depleted neurons exhibited impaired microtubule recovery following acute depolymerization and reduced axonal recoil after optically induced local microtubule severing. Finally, STMN2 depletion disrupted the formation of neuromuscular junction-like contacts in human motor neuron-myocyte co-cultures, linking impaired cytoskeletal homeostasis to loss of distal neuronal connectivity. Together, these findings identify STMN2 as a key regulator of cytoskeletal resilience that coordinates microtubule remodeling, mitochondrial transport, and maintenance of neuromuscular junctions. We propose that impaired resilience of the axonal cytoskeleton represents a critical point of vulnerability in motor neurons in patients with ALS, establishing cytoskeletal resilience as a potential therapeutic target downstream of TDP-43 pathology.

papers.title: Inter-domain flexibility in F-Box proteins revealed by integrative modeling
papers.abstract: F-box proteins, the substrate-recognition modules of the SCF (Skp1-Cul1-F-box) ubiquitin ligase complex, play a central role in targeted protein degradation by enabling the selective recruitment of diverse substrates. F-box proteins share a common architecture with a conserved anchor domain linked to the substrate-binding domain. Despite extensive structural characterization of F-box proteins, their potential conformational dynamics remain poorly understood. Here, we employ an integrative modeling approach combining cryo-EM structures, cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS), and deep learning-based conformational ensemble prediction to profile the accessible conformations of F-box proteins. Our analyses reveal a significant inter-domain flexibility in FBXL2 and FBXL17 that enables sampling of a broad range of conformations within assembled SCF and CSN-SCF complexes. By contrast, other F-box proteins, including FBXL1 and FBXO22, exhibit intrinsic flexibility but are restricted to a considerably narrower conformational landscape. Together, our work highlights inter-domain plasticity as a tunable architectural feature of F-box proteins, which may shape their functional versatility within SCF complexes.

papers.title: Integrative Transcriptomic Analysis Reveals Differential Exon Usage and Virulence Gene Family Dynamics in Plasmodium falciparum during Severe Malaria
papers.abstract: Malaria remains a leading cause of child mortality in developing countries, with roughly 610,000 deaths per year. While the disease is caused by five human Plasmodium species, Plasmodium falciparum (Pf ) causes the most severe form. Progression from uncomplicated to severe malaria is characterized by high proliferation of the parasite, severely affecting children under five years old. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying disease progression remain an active area of research. Many multicopy genes have been implicated in Pf virulence. Some of these genes are implicated in cytoadherence, host-cell invasion, immune evasion, sequestration of infected erythrocytes, and antigenic variation. We employed an integrative transcriptomic analysis in this study to elucidate the molecular underpinnings of severe malaria and gene expression patterns, virulence gene dynamics, and the potential contribution of alternative splicing. Results show an overexpression of protein synthesis and ribosomal genes associated with severe malaria. About 86% (n=1865) of all differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were downregulated in severe malaria, and 226 genes exhibited both differential expression and differential exon usage (DEU). Pf virulence genes and antigenic genes such as var (pfEMP1), stevor, surfin, rif (rifin), ptm-2TM, and msp were upregulated in severe malaria compared with uncomplicated malaria, except for rifin. In severe malaria, there was evidence of co-expression and regulation within multigene families, as well as DEU and alternative splicing in virulence genes and antimalarial resistance-related proteins. Pf does not employ a single mechanism for disease progression but suppresses and deregulates nonessential pathways, processes, and genes, which are upregulated virulence genes, DNA replication, mRNA transcription, and protein synthesis. Multicopy genes are co-expressed and regulated to meet the molecular needs of the parasite. The parasite employs alternative splicing and DEU mechanisms for immune invasion and evasion, host-parasite interaction, as well as antimalarial resistance.

papers.title: FACT frees Ubp10 from nucleosome sequestration after rapid H2B deubiquitination
papers.abstract: Chromatin-modifying enzymes must engage their substrate, act on it and release it, but which step limits their turnover is unclear. Using three-color single-molecule fluorescence, we directly visualized the yeast deubiquitinase Ubp10 removing ubiquitin from H2B on individual nucleosomes. Ubp10 cleaved the mark within seconds of binding, without detectable DNA unwrapping, yet it did not let go: ~80% of nucleosomes remained bound after 45 minutes, and unmodified nucleosomes formed similarly long-lived complexes. Ubp10 turnover is therefore limited by release rather than catalysis. The histone chaperone FACT relieved this bottleneck by accelerating Ubp10-nucleosome dissociation. In living yeast, nuclear depletion of the FACT subunit Spt16 increased the slowly diffusing, chromatin-bound fraction of nucleoplasmic Ubp10. These findings identify FACT-dependent release as a likely mechanism for recycling Ubp10 on chromatin. More broadly, a nucleosome can sequester the enzyme acting on it, making enzyme release a step at which chromatin modification can be controlled.

papers.title: A tabular foundation model rivals established species distribution models from presence-only records
papers.abstract: Predicting where something occurs from records of where it has been observed, without reliable records of absence, is a common problem in science. Species distribution models (SDMs) such as MaxEnt address it in fields from biological conservation and climate-change assessment to the mapping of disease vectors and archaeological sites, but must be tuned for each dataset. Tabular foundation models, pre-trained on synthetic prediction tasks, predict new datasets without per-dataset training. Only one study has tested them as SDMs, and it fine-tuned on survey data from the evaluated regions. We evaluated tabular foundation models on the standard SDM benchmark (225 species in six regions, with independent presence-absence surveys), under the protocol used to compare 21 methods, and on 120 virtual species with known distributions. Without tuning, a tabular foundation model, TabPFN 3.5, equalled the best published approach, a five-model ensemble (mean AUC 0.732). Fine-tuned on presence-background tasks from other regions, it became the best single model on the benchmark (0.736), outperformed MaxEnt (0.728) and boosted regression trees after correction for multiple comparisons, and was better calibrated than MaxEnt, although six regions were too few to establish the advantage for new regions. Fine-tuning on presence-absence surveys of other species helped only when they came from the evaluated regions. On virtual species, it recovered simple additive relationships less well than regression-based methods but complex ones at least as well when records were unbiased, and was worse with environmentally biased records. Tabular foundation models are competitive SDMs without per-dataset tuning, but they are sensitive to environmentally biased records.

papers.title: ApoE isoforms establish distinct antioxidant trajectories across the aging brain
papers.abstract: APOE {varepsilon}4 is the strongest common genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimers disease, but how ApoE isoforms shape physiology before disease remains unclear. Across the ancestral-to-derived ApoE4[->]ApoE3[->]ApoE2 sequence, we examined antioxidant regulation during aging. Young humanized ApoE4 mice had lower antioxidant protein abundance and oxidized phospholipid reduction before detectable oxidative damage, yet accumulated lipid peroxidation products with age despite antioxidant remodeling. ApoE4 cells mounted the strongest antioxidant transcriptional response to sulforaphane but accumulated less protein from targets supporting proteostasis, glutathione synthesis and ferroptosis suppression, alongside altered eIF2 signaling and translation kinetics. Antioxidant transcription shifted from an ApoE4 bias in youth toward ApoE2 with age, and adult APOE4-to-APOE2 switching redirected expression in astrocytes and microglia. Cognitively normal human brains showed regional reductions in nuclear Nrf2 and antioxidant proteins, with transcriptomic analyses supporting context-dependent organization. ApoE isoforms differentially couple stress-responsive transcription to protein output, linking age-dependent antioxidant adaptation to neurodegenerative vulnerability.

papers.title: Integrated genotyping, annotation and epigenetic characterization of transposable elements with GraffiTE
papers.abstract: Genotyping, annotating and characterizing TE variation leaped forward with long-read sequencing (LRS) and de novo assembly. LRS techniques also reveal CpG methylation, which enables measuring the impact of TEs on epigenomes and sheds light on the role of TEs as regulatory sequences. Yet, TE genotyping tools discard the valuable allele-specific epigenetic information. We introduce GraffiTE v1.1, the first Nextflow pipeline that genotypes SVs, annotates polymorphic mobile elements (MEI), and maps epigenetic data to TEs using pangenome graphs in one command. GraffiTE v1.1 is designed to map any epigenetic information that is based on LRS stencils, including Fiber-seq. We demonstrate the capabilities of GraffiTE v1.1 by analyzing genomes and methylomes obtained from 20 Quebec residents of French-Canadian descent. In these genomes, TE annotation yields 4,908 Alu, 704 LINE1, 112 SVA and 21 HERVK (HML-2) distinct polymorphic mobile elements (MEIs). We also identify 10 fixed HERVK insertions that vary between solo LTR and provirus, or in proviral copy number. We determine that these MEIs contribute 144,748 additional CpGs not present in the reference. From this, we identify 480 Alus, 67 LINE1s, 12 SVAs and 2 HERVKs in hypomethylated states. We note that Alus and SVAs are more methylated than other LINE1 and HERVK. Lastly, MEIs dating reported a mean of age 1.08 Mya (median: 640 kya) and beta regression identified a moderate demethylating effect of age on MEIs (effect: -0.069 log-odds per log10 years, P < 6.08 x 10-19). Our results show that the methylation level of a LINE1 MEI is expected to decrease from 86.4% to 80.8% in the first Mya. In conclusion, GraffiTE v1.1 genotypes SVs, annotates MEI, and characterizes their epigenetic state at the scale of populations by leveraging the full potential of LRS. While we showcase its application in human data, the pipeline can be deployed in any model for which a TE library is available.

papers.title: Receptor-guided engineering of oncolytic vaccinia creates a synthetic support niche for off-the-shelf NK cell therapy
papers.abstract: Combining adoptive cell therapy with oncolytic viruses offers a means to provide localized support within solid tumors, yet viral chassis and therapeutic payloads are often selected independently of the biological state of the manufactured cell product. Here, we establish an engineering framework that uses the phenotypic and functional features of an adoptive cell product as design inputs for a complementary oncolytic niche. Using off-the-shelf expanded, frozen, and thawed (EFT) natural killer (NK) cells as a model system, we identified manufacturing-associated reductions in chemokine responsiveness, dependence on extrinsic cytokine support, and loss of sustained function at limiting effector-to-target ratios. In a head-to-head evaluation under human NK-cell antiviral pressure, oncolytic vaccinia virus (VV) retained replication and spread, whereas HSV-1 was rapidly restricted, establishing VV as a compatible viral chassis. Mapping endogenous receptor expression and applying sequential functional screening under increasingly limiting effector densities then prioritized a five-factor program comprising CXCL11, IL-15, IL-27, IL-2, and IL-1{beta} that supported NK-cell migration, survival, cytotoxicity, and metabolic fitness at effector-to-target ratios as low as 1:10. Consolidating these signals into a single viral chassis increased antitumor activity but revealed a systemic inflammatory liability associated with constitutive IL-1{beta} expression. We therefore placed the IL-2/IL-1{beta} module under chemically inducible control, retaining in vivo antitumor activity while limiting systemic toxicity. Together, these findings establish a framework in which the post-manufacturing state of an adoptive cell product guides viral chassis selection, payload prioritization, and programmable control of a complementary oncolytic support niche.

papers.title: Sensory experience-induced plasticity of somatostatin interneurons occurs through two-pore potassium (K2P) channels
papers.abstract: GABAergic interneurons (INs) are powerful modulators of plasticity and learning in cortical networks, but plasticity of INs themselves is not well understood. We studied experience-dependent plasticity in somatostatin (SST) INs, which critically regulate dendritic integration, sensory tuning, and plasticity in pyramidal neurons in sensory cortex. Whether SST INs exhibit experience-dependent plasticity, and by what mechanisms, is unknown. We found that 3 days of whisker deprivation strongly downregulated intrinsic excitability of SST INs in L2/3 of somatosensory cortex, by reducing input resistance. Deprivation also increased mEPSCs onto SST INs. The reduction in intrinsic excitability was caused by an increase in leak potassium current through two-pore K+ (K2P) channels, without changes in HCN, KV1, or KV7 currents, which contribute to plasticity in other IN types and brain areas. Immunohistochemistry showed an increase in TRESK, but not other K2P channels, indicating a novel role for K2P channels in experience-dependent plasticity of interneuron excitability.

papers.title: The role of familiarity in grouping decisions of Trinidadian guppies
papers.abstract: Social grouping is widely observed in numerous taxa, providing individuals with a variety of benefits including efficient information exchange and predator protection. However, grouping can also carry costs such as increased competition for resources, which means that individuals must often make decisions regarding joining or leaving a group. These decisions to leave or stay might in turn depend on prior experience with potential groupmates. Past work has shown that many fish distinguish between familiar and unfamiliar conspecifics and use these distinctions in their grouping choices. Trinidadian guppies (Poecilia reticulata), well known for their diversity in shoaling preferences, are an excellent system in which to investigate the role of familiarity in grouping decisions. We examined preferences for familiar individuals following both a 15-day and 55-day cohabitation period in two different guppy populations. Utilizing two binary-choice designs, we found no evidence for a familiarity preference in either population, despite observing a high preference to group with conspecifics in both populations. These results suggest that various contextual- and population-level differences may impact familiarity preferences, in turn contributing to the growing body of work on the evolution of social organization and grouping decisions in teleost species and beyond.

papers.title: SPARK: Physiology-informed inference of latent cardiac autonomic dynamics from RR intervals
papers.abstract: Cardiac autonomic activity is observed only through beat-to-beat (RR) intervals, and separating it into parasympathetic-like and sympathetic-like components is an inverse problem that RR alone is not expected to solve uniquely. We introduce SPARK (Stochastic Phase-domain Autonomic Reconstruction Kinetics), a state-space model in which two independent, mean-reverting latent drives modulate heart rate through an integrate-and-fire pacemaker. The model is combined with exact continuous-time Kalman filtering and with an explicit physiological identification structure: time-scale priors, a kinetic ordering and a spectral partition of heart rate variability. SPARK offers a model-conditional description of autonomic trajectories that complements conventional heart rate variability; its latent states are reconstructions, not measurements of neural activity. Across recordings, fitting each recording from many different starting points gave a median of 23.5 distinct solutions without physiological information versus 1.0 with it, and one process absorbed essentially all the variability in 75% versus 4% of the fits; the fit diagnostics showed residual structure in most recordings. Reconstructions were then examined: in 10 tilt-table recordings, the vagal-like state decreased and the sympathetic-like state increased in 10 of 10; exploratory comparisons between 20 young and 20 older adults showed differences in reconstructed variability and faster-component kinetics, although several latent summaries were mathematically redundant; and in 263 exercise recordings, median recovery times, which are closely tied to the fitted time constants, were 42 s (vagal-like) and 341 s (sympathetic-like). How a stressor-induced change is split between the two drives remained sensitive to the spectral anchor.

papers.title: Linking Covariates to State Durations in Dynamic Brain Networks via Hidden Semi-Markov Models
papers.abstract: Hidden semi-Markov models (HSMMs) provide a flexible framework for studying dynamic functional connectivity because they represent brain activity as transitions between latent network states with explicit dwell time distributions. Although dwell times are often associated with behavioral and demographic variables, these associations are typically assessed only after model fitting using indirect group comparisons, limiting formal covariate modeling and the simultaneous inclusion of multiple predictors. In this work, we extend the HSMM framework by introducing covariate-dependent dwell time distributions through a regression-based formulation, allowing expected state duration to vary with subject-level covariates and enabling direct inference on how these factors relate to state persistence. Model parameters are estimated with an expectation-maximization algorithm, and uncertainty in the dwell-time regression coefficients is quantified using a subject-level nonparametric bootstrap. In simulations, the proposed model accurately recovered covariate effects under both shifted-Poisson and Gamma dwell time specifications, with low bias and variability. We applied the method to resting-state fMRI data from 1,000 UK Biobank participants and found that age and sex were associated with dwell times in a subset of brain states. Together, these results show that modeling dwell-time behavior directly provides a more flexible framework for studying individual differences in brain dynamics, revealing not only which states occur, but also how long individuals remain in them.

papers.title: Deep phenomics of African green monkey and Baboon PBMCs using a 30-marker spectral flow cytometry panel
papers.abstract: Vaccines are the best way to prevent and combat diseases. Non-human primate (NHP) models have proven to be the gold standard model for studying the efficacy of certain vaccine candidates prior to human trials. Cell-mediated immunity serves as a surrogate marker for predicting vaccine efficacy. Despite the availability of deep-immunophenotyping panels for T cells in the peripheral blood of humans, their application to NHPs, particularly African Green Monkeys (AGMs) and baboons, remains limited. Notably, AGMs are valuable for HIV and COVID-19 research, while baboons are utilized for pertussis research as a natural infection model and vaccine trial. To overcome such limitation, using spectral flow cytometry, we developed a 30-parameter panel to profile major immune cell subsets (B cells, NK cells, DCs, monocytes) either in AGM or baboon PBMCs. We also profiled T cells, memory phenotypes, functional cytokines by tracking established Th1 markers IFN{gamma}, TNF and IL-2; Th2 markers IL-4/5/13 and the Th17 marker, IL-17, activation-induced markers (AIMs) and FoxP3+ Tregs in both AGM and baboon PBMCs in steady state as well as in mitogen stimulated conditions. For AIMs, CD69, CD134 (OX40) and CD137 (4-1BB) are included and validated in both NHP species. This panel holds potential for exploratory analysis of the impact of these functional cytokines, AIMs, or Tregs on host immunity following infection or vaccination. The panels high level of customization empowers researchers to tailor it to their specific research needs.

papers.title: Electrophysiological Dynamics of Default Network Suppression
papers.abstract: Distributed brain networks compete with one another in the service of information processing. One dramatic example is antagonism between networks that support internally directed cognition, often collectively referred to as the default network, and networks that orient to external events and drive action. Here we combined within-individual precision functional neuroimaging and intracranial electrophysiology to investigate network competition at high spatiotemporal resolution. In six patients, robust antagonism between networks was established during a target detection task. Network-assigned electrophysiological recordings displayed concordant responses, including in single-neuron firing rates, and further revealed the temporal dynamics of network competition. Networks involved in salience detection and action planning showed early, transient responses that peaked near the participant response. Default network suppression occurred later, reflected in decreases in high-frequency broadband activity and in single-neuron firing rates in response to targets. Examining subcortical regions revealed rapid activity increases in the thalamus and posterior hippocampus aligned to the participant response. Critically, a late evolving, sustained suppression was observed throughout the hippocampus. These findings suggest that, across cortical and subcortical regions, network competition is temporally layered. Furthermore, the hippocampus can be dissociated along its long axis during competition. Such push-pull antagonism may be fundamental to advanced human cognition, and its disruption may underlie mental illness.

papers.title: TMEM11-Dependent Cristae Architecture Restrains Imiquimod-Induced NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation via Mitochondrial ROS
papers.abstract: Imiquimod (IMQ) is a clinically approved drug widely used to treat skin malignancies; however, its application frequently provokes severe inflammation through NLRP3 inflammasome activation. The mechanism underlying IMQ-induced activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome is not completely defined. While IMQ-induced inhibition of mitochondrial electron transport chain complex I is necessary for activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, it is not sufficient; suggesting presence of additional targets/triggers. The role of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) as the additional trigger to activate the inflammasome remains contentious based on conflicting reports. Using a unique genetic model lacking expression of mitochondrial membrane protein TMEM11 we reaffirm the role of mtROS in IMQ-induced NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Macrophages deficient in Tmem11, a mitochondrial contact site and cristae organizing system (MICOS)-associated membrane-protein, exhibit ultrastructural defects in cristae morphology without altering mitochondrial mass or mtDNA copy number. Loss of TMEM11 influences cristae length and density, reducing mitochondrial oxygen consumption. Tmem11-deficient macrophages exhibit normal NLRP3 inflammasome activation in response to canonical agonists (e.g., ATP, nigericin) but show caspase-1 hyperactivation and exaggerated IL-1{beta} and IL-18 secretion upon IMQ treatment. This exaggerated response is rescued by antioxidant treatment, confirming the role for mtROS. These findings demonstrate that cristae architecture restrains drug-induced mtROS to limit NLRP3 activation and that mtROS is a primary driver of IMQ-mediated NLRP3 inflammasome activation.

papers.title: Ergodic breakdown of brain dynamics under chronnectome complexity across cognitive states and age
papers.abstract: Chronnectome complexity, the extent to which time-varying functional connectivity follows a structured sequence of distinct configurations, contributes to shaping large-scale brain dynamics. However, it remains unclear how this complexity influences the encoding of information that distinguishes resting state and task conditions. In ergodic theory, time averages represent ensemble behavior under ergodicity, which breaks down when dynamics are non-stationary, as when activity moves sequentially between distinct regimes. We hypothesize that this information resides in time-averaged connectivity under lower-complexity conditions but in trajectory geometry under higher-complexity conditions, where brain activity traverses distinct configurations over time, consistent with ergodic breakdown, which we term the \textit{information migration principle}. We formulate this as dynamics-driven multi-class classification and introduce the Brain Dynamics Classifier (BDC), an interpretable data-driven mechanistic model in which a graph neural network embeds dynamic functional connectivity into a latent space and a neural ordinary differential equation learns the vector field governing trajectories through that space. The proposed model derives two complementary representations within a single learned dynamical system, capturing time-averaged connectivity, which is sufficient under ergodic dynamics, and trajectory geometry, which preserves the temporal organization obscured by averaging under non-ergodic dynamics. Our results show high classification accuracy, $97.4\%$ for eight conditions in the Human Connectome Project young adult cohort and $92.2\%$ for four in the aging cohort. To test the information migration principle, we ablated the time-averaged representation and found that trajectory contributions varied with chronnectome complexity, from high for Working Memory to absent for Relational Reasoning, consistent with ergodic breakdown. Including subcortical regions further increased trajectory contributions for affective conditions. In aging, the distinction between higher and lower complexity conditions was preserved, resting-state dynamics became less ergodic with advancing age, and higher fluid intelligence was associated with more ergodic resting-state dynamics.

papers.title: Structural evolution of Fcα/μR-mediated antibody recognition
papers.abstract: The Fc alpha-mu receptor (Fc/R) is an ancient Fc-receptor sharing common ancestry with the polymeric Ig receptor (pIgR) and binding polymeric IgM and IgA ligands. In several vertebrate lineages, including birds, Fc/R may serve as the sole IgM and IgA Fc receptor; yet its evolution and ligand-recognition mechanisms across vertebrates remain poorly understood. Here, we identify FCAMR expression in duck (Anas platyrhynchos, ap) lymphoid tissues and demonstrate that recombinantly expressed apFc/R ectodomain binds apIgM and apIgA ligands. apFc/R affinity was ~10-fold higher for apIgM versus apIgA and ~10-fold higher than mouse (mm) Fc/R. Cryo-EM structures of apFc/R in complex with pentameric apIgM (3.27 [A]) and tetrameric apIgA (3.57 [A]) showed three Ig-like domains (D1-D3) bound asymmetrically with 1:1 stoichiometry. Comparisons to avian pIgR, which contains four Ig-like domains (D1-D4), revealed overlapping contacts between apFc/R-D1 and pIgR-D1. apFc/R D2-D3 engaged sites similar to pIgR D3-D4, yet formed distinct contact networks. Parallel analysis of a mmFc/R-mmIgM structure (4.13 [A]) revealed mmFc/R's single Ig-domain bound analogous to apFc/R-D1 and to mammalian pIgR-D1, whereas downstream ectodomain regions were not observed. Collectively, the data elucidate PIGR-family mechanisms across vertebrates, providing a foundation for delineating common and divergent functions.

papers.title: Cholinergic modulation engages a CHRM1-IL-17 neuroimmune axis to promote diabetic wound repair
papers.abstract: Chronic non-healing wounds are a major complication of diabetes, where persistent inflammation fails to transition into effective tissue repair (1-3). Here we identify cholinergic modulation as a mechanism that promotes productive inflammation and diabetic wound healing. Using a healing-associated fibroblast signature derived from single-cell profiling of human diabetic foot ulcers (3), we identified the acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitor metrifonate as a candidate inducer of reparative wound programs. Topical delivery accelerated healing in diabetic mice and increased acetylcholine availability within the wound. Complementary receptor pharmacology identified muscarinic acetylcholine receptor 1 (CHRM1) as the principal receptor mediating the reparative response. Transcriptomic and cellular analyses revealed early induction of IL-17-associated inflammatory programs and enrichment of CHRM1NK1.1 innate lymphocytes. Depletion of NK1.1 cells or neutralization of IL-17A abolished the pro-healing effect, whereas spatial transcriptomics revealed treatment-associated organization of NK cells within vascular niches. Localized treatment further promoted repair in diabetic porcine wounds and human skin models. Together, these findings identify a CHRM1-IL-17 neuroimmune axis linking cholinergic modulation to diabetic wound repair and establish local AChE inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy for chronic wounds.

papers.title: Pre-synaptic facilitation of corticospinal output improves dexterity and finemotor control after stroke
papers.abstract: The corticospinal tract (CST) is a neural pathway that supports skilled use of the arm and hand. Lesions of corticospinal axons result in muscle weakness, deficits of gross motor function, and loss of proximal and distal dexterous control for which effective treatments are still lacking. Here we exploited excitatory connections from motor thalamus to primary motor cortex to potentiate surviving descending signals and restore volitional arm and hand control in three monkeys with corticospinal tract lesion, using deep brain stimulation. Stimulation targeted to thalamocortical projections facilitated upper-limb movements, enabling monkeys with arm and hand paralysis to perform unconstrained 3D reach and fine dexterous tasks. Stimulation improved strength, hand gross motor function, and digits control. Electrophysiology suggested that effects were mediated by and more effective when targeting fibers with monosynaptic connection to the corticospinal motoneurons. Stimulation was delivered in continuous with FDA-clinically approved parameters holding realistic promises of clinical translation.

papers.title: A caudate-centered network for alexithymia derived from patients with brain tumors
papers.abstract: Alexithymia is a trait characterized by impaired emotional awareness. Previous accounts examining the neurobiological underpinnings of this trait have centered on a variety of structures, and alexithymia-causing lesions occur in disparate locations. We use lesion network mapping to derive a neural circuit for alexithymia. In a neurosurgical cohort of 45 patients with gliomas (19 female; aged 18-75 years), we compute each lesion's connectivity to the rest of the brain using a normative connectome (n = 1,000) and relate these connectivity maps to preoperative Toronto Alexithymia Scale scores using permutation testing. Lesions associated with higher alexithymia are connected to a common network that includes the bilateral caudate heads (right greater than left) and the anterior cingulate cortex, peaking in the right caudate head (family-wise error-corrected p < 0.05). The network converges with coordinates from an independent meta-analysis of gray matter volume in alexithymia (13 of 14 coordinates positive; p = 0.0004). Of the three subscales, difficulty identifying feelings localized to this network. Within the striatum, the network spans the executive and limbic subdivisions. These findings suggest a caudate-centered circuit, at the interface of affective and executive systems, that unifies disparate lesion locations.

papers.title: Human medial frontal neurons represent integrated semantic content and sensory evidence to inform decision-making
papers.abstract: Humans can reconfigure how they act on the world from a single verbal instruction. Central to this capacity is the ability to represent what an instruction specifies and to bring that content to bear on incoming sensory evidence. However, little is known about where in the human brain instruction content is encoded, how it combines with sensory evidence to produce a choice, and how this integration relates to behavior. Here, we characterized single-neuron and population responses recorded in the ventral temporal cortex, medial temporal lobe, medial frontal cortex and ventromedial prefrontal cortex of neurosurgical patients performing a verbal instruction task. On each trial, a written instruction specified which stimulus feature was relevant and whether the correct response was to choose or to reject the stimulus that best matched it, so that the same image pair required opposite responses under different instructions. Only medial frontal populations jointly encoded the instructed task, and the target feature, whereas ventral temporal populations encoded stimulus features along axes that generalized across instruction conditions. Choice representation emerged first in ventromedial prefrontal and then in medial frontal cortex during stimulus presentation, before a motor response could be prepared. Shuffling instruction content selectively degraded prediction of medial frontal population activity, whereas shuffling stimulus identity selectively degraded ventral temporal activity. To ask how these representations could be computed, we trained a vision-language model with separable visual and linguistic streams converging on a recurrent decision module to perform the same task. Its visual embeddings predicted held-out ventral temporal activity and its recurrent activations revealed a task solution space that predicted medial frontal activity, and the strength of this alignment tracked behavioral accuracy. These results identify a cortical hierarchy in which medial frontal circuitry represents the content of verbal goals and acts on a ventral temporal substrate whose representational axes remain stable, and indicate that functional hierarchies discovered in artificial networks can serve as predictive models of human neural circuitry.

papers.title: Mucin promotes pneumococcal colonization via autolysis suppression and tryptophan-mediated immune modulation
papers.abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a leading human respiratory pathogen, yet its success depends not on disease but on its ability to persist as an asymptomatic colonizer of the nasopharynx. The nasopharyngeal mucosa is lined with mucus, whose heavily O-glycosylated mucin proteins are the most abundant macromolecules in the pneumococcal natural niche. While mucus is canonically viewed as a host defense barrier, we found that mucin actively reprograms pneumococcal physiology to promote colonization through two distinct mechanisms. First, mucin suppresses pneumococcal autolysis by specifically inhibiting the enzymatic activity of the major autolysin LytA, prolonging bacterial survival and restricting release of the cholesterol-dependent cytotoxin pneumolysin, thereby reducing host cell damage. Second, mucin induces de novo biosynthesis and extracellular release of tryptophan, an essential amino acid that humans cannot synthesize and that serves as a substrate for host immunomodulatory pathways. Tryptophan biosynthesis was critical for pneumococcal survival against macrophage killing, and its disruption abolished both colonization and invasive disease. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that tryptophan biosynthesis enables the pneumococcus to survive a bactericidal macrophage state while preventing macrophage transition to proliferative tissue repair. Together, these findings reveal that mucin is not merely a barrier but an active signal that reprograms the pneumococcus toward a persistent, host-tolerant state, identifying a distinctive repertoire of colonization mechanisms that allow a virulent respiratory pathogen to sustain long-term asymptomatic carriage in its human reservoir.

papers.title: Parallel Trajectories in the Evolution of C-class MADS-box Genes in Flowering Plants and Conifers
papers.abstract: Gene duplication events frequently underpin phenotypic diversity due to the increase in genetic material that can be shaped by evolution. AGAMOUS (AG) genes are members of the MADS-box gene family that show conserved function in specifying reproductive organ identity in seed plants. While the function, expression, and evolution of these genes have been extensively studied in flowering plants, they remain understudied in gymnosperms. Consequently, little is known about how AG has contributed to reproductive diversity and evolution outside of the flowering plants. Here, we report that AG genes underwent two duplication events within conifers prior to the split between Cupressaceae and its sister family, Taxaceae. Further, we characterize the in situ expression pattern for each resulting paralog (AG1, AG2, and AG3) in seed cones of three Cupressaceae species, Metasequoia glyptostroboides, Taxodium distichum, and Juniperus virginiana. We discover gene expression patterns consistent with subfunctionalization: AG1 specialized in seed and sporangial development, AG2 in seed cone and seed coat development, and AG3 in ovuliferous scale development. This study provides an evolutionary mechanism for the development of unique seed cone reproductive traits in Cupressaceae. More broadly, our results uncover convergent patterns in the evolution of AG gene lineages across conifers and angiosperms.

papers.title: Reversible decrease in swimming motility accompanies emergent β-lactam antibiotic resistance in Escherichia coli
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) threatens global health, food security, and development; however, the evolutionary and molecular pathways that drive AMR remain poorly understood, limiting our ability to advance diagnostics and rapidly detect newly emerging resistance. In this report, we employed laboratory evolution of an environmental Escherichia coli strain (NIST 0056) under B-lactam antibiotic pressure (ampicillin and cephalexin) to specifically investigate the relationship between resistance genotype and motility phenotype. Within 10 passages, populations evolved varying levels of B-lactam resistance (including high-level resistance > 32 ug/mL) and showed consistent, dose-dependent reductions in swimming motility. Whole-population genome sequencing revealed large deletions in marR, SNPs in efflux pump gene acrB and fumarate reductase gene frdD, and mutations with evidence of amplification in the chromosomal class C B-lactamase gene ampC, collectively linking these efflux-mediated, B-lactam resistance mechanisms to loss of motility. Notably, motility reductions were more pronounced in individual clones than in the mixed populations (p < 0.005, Mann-Whitney; two-tailed test). Following removal of antibiotic pressure, motility was restored and AMR-associated mutations decreased in frequency, suggesting fitness costs associated with resistance. In aggregate, our results demonstrate that reduced swimming motility accompanies specific efflux-driven, B-lactam resistance mechanisms. Further work will investigate if the behavior is generalizable across flagellated Enterobacteriaceae. Because these rapid changes are amenable to high-throughput measurement, swimming motility may offer a tractable physiological metric for AMR detection in environmental surveillance.

papers.title: Population dynamics in extreme environments: shared histories of strong selection lead to predictable patterns across separate high-elevation populations of small mammals
papers.abstract: Many frameworks exist to identify species that are vulnerable to environmental change, but we still generally lack the ability to anticipate species' responses when changes occur. Exploring patterns of trait evolution along environmental gradients could help this process: conditions become more predictable and less variable at the ends of gradients, with past studies hypothesizing that consistently harsh environments will result in predictable evolutionary patterns. To test this hypothesis, we characterized genetic and phenotypic variation, as well as selection on this variation, in deer mice (Peromyscus maniculatus) along two transects spanning from 2120-4200m in the Colorado Rocky Mountains, U.S.A. We found that both genetic and phenotypic variation declined with elevation, that high elevation populations had higher rates of survival, and that fewer traits influenced survival at high elevations. These results suggest extreme environments may lead to predictable consequences for populations and provide a basis for forecasting population vulnerability to environmental change.

papers.title: Overlapping enhancer activity robustly regulates rax expression during ocular development in zebrafish
papers.abstract: Vertebrate eye development relies on the tightly regulated yet highly dynamic spatiotemporal expression of eye field transcription factors that coordinate developmental programs required for the formation of a functional eye. The gene rax is among the earliest expressed eye field transcription factors and is specifically associated with ocular-fated tissue. It encodes a transcription factor that is essential for optic vesicle evagination, the precursor to the optic cup and retina. Although the developmental functions of rax are well characterized, the cis-regulatory elements that control its expression remain poorly understood. Using zebrafish (Danio rerio), I identified five novel ocular enhancers and demonstrate that they drive similar spatiotemporal expression patterns as rax at three key stages of eye development. Furthermore, I performed an in-depth characterization of two enhancers and demonstrate that they exhibit substantial transcript-level overlap with endogenous rax expression during development. Additionally, through the generation of enhancer deletion lines, I further demonstrate that the gene regulatory network (GRN) controlling rax expression is largely robust to individual and combinatorial enhancer perturbations. However, perturbation of this regulatory network can result in rax-associated ocular abnormalities, including microphthalmia and anophthalmia. Together, these findings highlight the importance of studying developmental ocular enhancers to better understand the functions of noncoding genomic regions and provide insight into potential causes of unexplained congenital eye disease.

papers.title: Stress-adapted endophytic Pseudomonas strains isolated from unmanaged lupin promote potato growth and suppress verticillium wilt through complementary biocontrol and plant growth-promoting mechanisms
papers.abstract: Verticillium wilt, primarily caused by Verticillium dahliae, is among the most destructive soil borne diseases impacting global potato production. Fungal propagules remain viable in soil for extended periods, and conventional control measures often show limited efficacy. These challenges underscore the necessity for sustainable disease management strategies. We evaluated two stress adapted endophytic Pseudomonas strains, B18 and B14, isolated from unmanaged wild Lupinus roots in Quebec, Canada, for their plant growth promoting and biocontrol potential against Verticillium wilt in potato. Both isolates exhibited multiple plant beneficial traits. B18 demonstrated strong phosphate solubilization, indole 3 acetic acid production, putative nitrogen fixation related activity, siderophore production, and hydrogen cyanide production. These traits correlated with enhanced plant growth promoting effects, including stimulation of seed germination and radicle growth. In contrast, B14 primarily exhibited antagonistic activity against Verticillium species through similar plant beneficial mechanisms, indicating complementary activities between the strains. The cell free supernatants of B18 further supported its biostimulant activity, suggesting a significant role for its extracellular metabolites. Greenhouse experiments using the Verticillium susceptible potato cultivar Russet Burbank, inoculated with either strain, showed enhanced plant growth and reduced disease severity compared with pathogen only controls. Under pathogen challenge, plants treated with plant growth promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) exhibited up to 62% greater shoot height and approximately double the leaf production. Additionally, these plants produced 4.2 times more tubers than pathogen only plants. Disease progression, measured as the area under the disease progress curve (AUDPC), was reduced by 84 to 92% following bacterial inoculation. While individual strains effectively suppressed disease, the combined B18 plus B14 strains resulted in the most substantial improvements in growth, biomass, root development, and tuber production. These findings demonstrate that stress adapted endophytic Pseudomonas strains from wild Lupinus can contribute to sustainable potato production. The B18 plus B14 consortium, when combined with two-strain inoculation, demonstrated the most significant effects. These findings emphasize the potential of functionally complementary microbial inoculants for the integrated management of Verticillium wilt and other persistent soil-borne diseases in potatoes.

papers.title: First-in-class -PET radiotracers for GPR39: A platform for noninvasive target engagement imaging in vivo
papers.abstract: Disrupted zinc homeostasis is a hallmark of Alzheimer's disease. As a key zinc-sensing receptor, GPR39, a G protein-coupled receptor implicated in neurodegeneration, vascular regulation, and neuropsychiatric disorders, represents an emerging target for molecular imaging. However, the lack of suitable positron emission tomography (PET) radiotracers has limited the in vivo characterization of GPR39. Quantitative assessment of GPR39 in vivo could improve our understanding of its role in physiology and disease and facilitate the development and evaluation of targeted therapeutics. Here, we introduce [18F]GPR39 2.1 as a PET radiotracer for specific imaging of GPR39. [18F]GPR39 2.1 exhibited excellent serum stability with negligible radiometabolite formation. In vitro cell uptake studies demonstrated a 55-70% reduction in tracer uptake following pharmacological blockade. PET imaging showed rapid brain uptake, efficient blood-brain barrier penetration, and gradual washout. Blockade studies in rats demonstrated significant reductions in brain uptake of up to approximately 90% (p<0.0001) across multiple brain regions. GPR39 specificity was further validated in GPR39 knockout mice, which showed 76% (p<0.002) and 90% (p<0.0002) reductions in brain uptake by PET imaging and biodistribution, respectively. Moreover, 5xFAD transgenic mice exhibited significantly lower brain uptake by PET imaging (40%, p<0.0002) and biodistribution (77%, p<0.002), indicating sensitivity of [18F]GPR39 2.1 to disease-associated alterations in GPR39. Biodistribution studies demonstrated favorable pharmacokinetics, while autoradiography further confirmed GPR39-specific binding, consistent with the PET and biodistribution findings. Collectively, these results establish [18F]GPR39 2.1 as a stable, brain-penetrant, and highly specific PET radiotracer for noninvasive imaging of GPR39 in vivo. This work provides a translational framework for investigating GPR39 biology and supports the development of GPR39 as an imaging and therapeutic target in neurological and systemic diseases associated with GPR39 dysregulation.

papers.title: BCAS3 regulates WIPI2b via a direct interaction in the ATG16L1-binding cleft
papers.abstract: De novo formation of the phagophore membrane is a fundamental step in autophagy and relies on recruitment of the E3-like ligase complex via an interaction between ATG16L1 and phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PtdIns3P)-effector protein, WIPI2b. Although WIPI2b can directly bind membranes, how its membrane association is regulated is still not fully understood. Here, we describe BCAS3 as a novel direct interactor of WIPI2b and demonstrate that a peptide of BCAS3 binds in the ATG16L1-binding cleft of WIPI2b with low micromolar affinity. We show that BCAS3 and its partner PHAF1 induce recruitment of WIPI2b to membranes via the interaction of BCAS3 with PtdIns3P. This not only challenges the current paradigm, whereby ATG16L1 is the only confirmed binder of WIPI2b in this region, but also offers a mechanism through which WIPI2b membrane association might be regulated.

papers.title: Variable errors suppress implicit motor adaptation among older adults
papers.abstract: Age-related changes in motor control networks manifest in a highly task-dependent manner. Although older adults can display enhanced implicit sensorimotor adaptation, this effect is inconsistent across perturbation types (e.g., visuomotor vs. force-field perturbations). Because these perturbations induce different errors to drive learning, their distinct effects on learning suggest that specific properties of the error signal modulate the extent of adaptation among older adults. Here, we investigated whether age-related hyper-adaptation is modulated by error variability. More specifically, we manipulated the consistency of error direction during an error-clamp visuomotor adaptation task in both younger and older adults. While consistent errors elicited enhanced implicit adaptation in older adults relative to younger controls, variable errors did not. These findings reveal that error consistency is a critical prerequisite for age-related enhancements in implicit motor learning. Rather than exhibiting unconstrained hyper-adaptation, older adults maintain an adaptive error-sensitivity mechanism that prevents hyper-recruitment of implicit systems in noisy motor environments.

papers.title: Amino acid clustering and epistasis guide sequence-based prediction of phenotype modulation
papers.abstract: Protein sequences encode the molecular information necessary for their biological function. As functional adaptation often emerges from combined effects of multiple positions, understanding how sequence variation gives rise to functional differences remains a central challenge. Here, we developed an improved strategy to identify phenotype modulating positions and use them to predict phenotypes, by relating amino acid identity to experimentally measured quantitative properties across families. Using family-specific sequence-phenotype datasets, our results show that epistasis plays a crucial role in phenotype modulation. Position specific amino acid clustering further improved performance indicating that key functional information is often captured by broad physicochemical amino acid classes, with hydrophobicity playing a crucial role in phenotype modulation. Our identified phenotype modulating positions involve both proximal and distal sites relative to functional sites. While the former is captured by individual positions, the latter is captured when epistasis is taken into account. Comparison with experimentally identified positions showed partial recovery of known functionally relevant residues, while at the same time revealing candidate positions that may contribute to phenotypic variation. Taken together, these results suggest that quantitative phenotypes are often governed by a network of interacting amino acid residues and may be engineered by a limited amount of sequence modifications. This finding highlights the potential of our framework to deepen our understanding of protein function, evolution, and adaptation, providing new targets for the rational modulation and engineering of protein phenotypes.

papers.title: Replicable Connectivity and Spectral Alterations of Functional Networks in Major Depression
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is usually characterized in functional MRI through connectivity alone, often in samples too small to resolve its modest effects. Here we applied multi-scale, template-guided independent component analysis to resting-state data from the multi-site MDD-DIRECT cohort and jointly examined the connectivity, spectral content and spatial composition of 105 intrinsic brain networks. Differences between patients and controls were widespread, small and structured: cerebello-subcortical coupling was reduced, subcortical--somatomotor coupling was increased, and spectral power shifted from lower to higher frequencies, most prominently in the thalamus, which also showed the most altered connectivity. Spatial composition differed in every network examined. In a smaller independent cohort, the direction of effect agreed for 95% of significant connections, 78% of significant spectral effects and 77% of the largest spatial-composition effects. Depression therefore alters several distinct properties of intrinsic networks, consistently across cohorts and most prominently in the thalamus.

papers.title: Allele-agnostic KCNH1 suppression rescues gain-of-function developmental epileptic encephalopathy
papers.abstract: Gain-of-function variants in KCNH1, which encodes the voltage-gated potassium channel Kv10.1, cause developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) characterized by seizures, developmental delay and intellectual disability. While pathogenic variants enhance channel activity, loss of KCNH1 is tolerated in humans and mice, suggesting that allele-agnostic gene suppression may represent a viable therapeutic strategy. Here, we developed a gapmer antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) targeting KCNH1 and evaluated its efficacy in human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived neurons and a knock-in mouse model of KCNH1-related disorder. Neurons carrying the pathogenic KCNH1 variants I494V or G375R exhibited a shared phenotype characterized by hyperpolarized resting membrane potential and abnormalities in neuronal network activity despite largely preserved intrinsic firing properties. ASOs efficiently reduced KCNH1 expression without disrupting network activity in control neurons. In contrast, ASO treatment normalized network dysfunction across both mutant genotypes, demonstrating that distinct KCNH1 gain-of-function variants converge on a reversible disease state. To assess the efficacy of ASOs in vivo, we generated a new Kcnh1-R357Q knock-in mouse model that exhibited profound seizures and early mortality. A single ASO treatment reduced seizure burden significantly and restored survival to near-normal levels. Together, these findings establish KCNH1 suppression as a precision therapeutic strategy for KCNH1-related DEEs and provide a framework for treating gain-of-function epilepsies in which partial gene reduction is clinically tolerated.

papers.title: Ok-k-mer: Selecting k-mer length ensembles for calculating genomic distance
papers.abstract: Current methods for computing sequence similarity across large groups of genome sequences tend to do so at the level of k-mers since this is far more efficient than base-by-base alignment. While these methods use default k-mer lengths, recent work shows that the particular choice of k-mer length greatly affects accuracy, and that using multiple values of k can boost accuracy relative to the best single choice of k, particularly when the goal is to estimate genomic distances that reflect true phylogenetic relationships. Here, we introduce Ok-k-mer, a tool to systematically select weighted k-mer length ensembles for pairwise genomic distance estimation, thereby increasing the accuracy of those estimates. Given a phylogenetic tree, Ok-k-mer ranks genome pairs by Jaccard distance across a range of k and uses a progressive search to maximize the Spearman correlation, {rho}, between weighted-average k-mer ranks and branch distances. Across eight Genome Taxonomy Database datasets, Ok-k-mer ensembles improved correlation over standard default k-mer lengths. In the Chlamydiales taxonomy, a three-length ensemble k=(9,17,22) achieved a 23.9% relative improvement over the best single length (k=20) and a 36.7% improvement over a commonly used default of 31-mers.
