papers.title: Realism and resolution: How AI-predicted protein structures differ from experimental structures
papers.abstract: Protein structure predictors can recover protein folds with remarkable accuracy, and their models are increasingly used as if they were experimental structures. Yet even for a confidently predicted fold, it remains difficult to judge how faithfully the model reproduces protein geometry. We introduce WhatRes, which assesses a structure from its coordinates on two complementary axes. Apparent resolution estimates the experimental resolution its local geometry most closely resembles. Realism measures how closely that geometry matches experimental structures at the same apparent resolution. Predicted models can score well on apparent resolution while showing systematically less variation in bond lengths and angles than is observed in high-resolution crystal structures. WhatRes reveals this over-idealisation even in high-confidence models.

papers.title: Quantifying and Visualizing the Invisible Hazard of Infant Rebreathing
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Rebreathing of expired gases during prone infant sleeping contributes to hypoxic and hypercapnic exposure, even without airway obstruction. We investigated how anatomical, physiological, and environmental factors influence aerodynamic rebreathing. METHODS: A dynamically scaled in vitro model simulated prone nasal breathing corresponding to infants weighing 2 to 5 kg, with nostril diameters of 3.2 to 6.0 mm and breathing frequencies of 25 to 40 breaths/min. Ambient temperature and sleep-surface characteristics were varied. Rebreathing was quantified using tracer measurements, while flow visualization revealed the underlying aerodynamic mechanisms. RESULTS: Rebreathing exceeded 60% despite unobstructed nasal openings. Increasing ambient temperature from 23 to 30 degrees C increased rebreathing by 68 to 77%, while reducing simulated infant mass from 5 to 2 kg increased rebreathing by 39 to 46%. Fibrous surfaces increased rebreathing, particularly near inclined nasal openings. A novel finding was that increasing nostril diameter from 3.2 to 6.0 mm increased rebreathing by up to 50%. Flow visualization revealed vortical structures that retained expired fluid near the nasal openings, facilitating re-inspiration. CONCLUSIONS: Aerodynamic rebreathing depends strongly on simulated infant characteristics and sleeping environments. These findings are consistent with established safe-sleep recommendations and identify nostril diameter, for the first time, as a potentially important anatomical factor warranting clinical investigation.

papers.title: BEHAV3D-Explorer enables natural language-assisted profiling of 3D cellular dynamics
papers.abstract: Obtaining quantitative measurements from live 3D microscopy remains difficult to implement across research settings, particularly without profound image-analysis expertise. We present BEHAV3D-Explorer, an interactive, user-friendly platform that uses natural-language guidance to help users select analysis strategies, tune parameters and configure workflows. BEHAV3D-Explorer enables time-resolved behavioral classification and integrates it with morphological, interaction and functional analyses, thereby connecting dynamic readouts to yield interpretable results across imaging applications.

papers.title: Genome-scale modelling and stable isotope tracing reveal dynamic metabolic reprogramming in a human cardiac hypertrophy model
papers.abstract: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is associated with metabolic remodelling; however the temporal dynamics of this remodelling remain poorly defined in human cardiomyocyte systems. Here, we combined transcriptomic profiling, genome-scale metabolic modelling and stable isotope-resolved metabolomics (SIRM) to map the metabolic consequences of endothelin-1 (ET-1) stimulation in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs). Integration of RNA sequencing data obtained after 8 and 48 hours of ET-1 treatment with the Human2.0 genome-scale metabolic model predicted time-dependent remodelling, characterised by progressive increases in glycolytic flux, enhanced glucose carbon entry into the TCA cycle, and a decrease in fatty acid {beta}-oxidation. Computational flux predictions were independently confirmed by extracellular flux analysis and 13C-substrate tracing, with concordance between modelled and measured fluxes. Extracellular flux analysis showed increased glycolytic capacity and mitochondrial respiration after 48 hours, with greater sensitivity to inhibition of mitochondrial pyruvate transport. Glucose tracing revealed increased 13C enrichment of glycolytic, pentose phosphate pathway, serine-glycine and TCA cycle metabolites, consistent with altered glucose-derived carbon allocation. Increased m+3 labelling of selected TCA-related metabolites was compatible with pyruvate anaplerosis, although pathway-specific fluxes were not resolved. In three-dimensional engineered heart tissue (EHTs) treated with ET-1 for 7 days, increased hypertrophic marker expression was accompanied by a blunted inotropic response, and metabolomics showed similar changes in metabolite abundance and glucose-derived labelling to 2D cultures. These findings support hiPSC-CMs and EHTs as complementary platforms for studying early metabolic remodelling in pathological cardiac hypertrophy and provide an integrated framework linking model predictions to functional and isotope-tracing measurements.

papers.title: scHiR learns joint cellular representations from paired single-cell transcriptome and 3D genome data
papers.abstract: Simultaneously sequenced scRNA-seq and scHi-C technologies provide matched measurements of gene expression and three-dimensional (3D) genome organization within individual cells, offering complementary insights into cellular state. However, integrative analysis remains challenging due to the heterogeneous structures and characteristics of these modalities. To realize the full potential of such data, we need effective computational methods to learn joint cellular representations. Here, we present scHiR, a framework based on a hyperspherical variational autoencoder (S-VAE) for learning co-embeddings from paired gene-expression profiles and chromatin contact maps. The framework facilitate downstream analyses such as cell clustering, fine-grained cell-state characterization, and developmental trajectory inference, while modality-specific decoders enable the signal recovery of input profiles. We evaluated scHiR across six paired datasets generated by HiRES, GAGE-seq, and LiMCA. scHiR captured cell-type-specific information and achieved improved clustering performance compared with representative single-omics methods. It was also capable of resolving fine-grained subclusters and revealed discordant and distinct cellular profiles. In developmental biological datasets, scHiR preserved trajectory-related structure and improved pseudotime in agreement with known developmental progression. Finally, scHiR generated reconstructed transcriptomic and chromatin contact profiles with reduced noise, enhanced cell-type-related signals, and improved recovery of held-out chromatin contacts. These results demonstrate that scHiR provides an effective method for learning joint cellular representations from paired scRNA-seq and scHi-C data.

papers.title: π-SPECFormer: A Mass Spectrometry-based Foundation Model for Decoding the Dark Proteome
papers.abstract: In mass-spectrometry-based proteomics, a substantial proportion of acquired spectra remain unidentified, concealing a vast reservoir of biological variations commonly termed the "dark proteome", potentially obscuring sequence mutations, non-canonical peptides and post-translational modifications. Existing deep-learning methods largely rely on supervised training with peptide-spectrum matches (PSMs), limiting their ability to learn from the much larger pool of unannotated spectra. Here we introduce {pi}-SPECFormer, a mass-spectrometry foundation model pre-trained on 291 million spectra through a two-stage framework that combines self-supervised and PSMs-guided representation learning. {pi}-SPECFormer transfers effectively to de novo peptide sequencing, spectrum clustering and modification detection, consistently outperforming task-specific baselines. When applied to proteomic profiles from 103 individuals with lung adenocarcinoma, the model identified nine high-confidence mutated peptides, including six that were absent from the reference databases. {pi}-SPECFormer thus enables unbiased decoding of molecular complexity beyond the boundaries of the canonical proteome.

papers.title: Engineered DNA materials shape microbial physiology and ecological selection
papers.abstract: Extracellular DNA (eDNA) is both a structural component of microbial biofilms and a potential reservoir of genetic information, yet its role as an ecological material remains largely unexplored. Here we establish engineered extracellular materials as determinants of microbial physiology and community assembly across increasing biological complexity. A three-dimensional DNA hydrogel altered bacterial stress-associated responses, elicited species-dependent phenotypes and transcriptional changes in a defined consortium, and shaped community succession in wastewater-derived microbiomes. Distinct responses to surface-bound oligonucleotides reveal that DNA presentation matters beyond its mere presence. Strikingly, metagenomic sequencing identified rare, hydrogel-specific candidate junctions linking material-derived DNA to microbial genomic sequences, suggesting a previously unexplored interface between extracellular DNA materials and microbial genetic information. These findings reveal a dual role for engineered DNA: its material organization shapes microbial physiology and ecological selection, while its encoded sequences may engage with microbial genomic processes.

papers.title: Integrating Microbial Ecology and Sustainability: Linking Agricultural Waste Gas Streams to Microbial Community Shifts in a Photobioreactor
papers.abstract: Photobioreactors (PBRs) coupled to animal housing offer potential for mitigating gaseous emissions such as CO2 and NH3 while simultaneously producing biomass. Here, we present a time-resolved characterization of microbial community dynamics, with a focus on the genetic potential for carbon and nitrogen metabolism. Using a cone-shaped, helical PBR cultivating Arthrospira platensis (Spirulina) and supplied with exhaust air from a chicken house, we characterized microbial communities over continuous exhaust-air exposure and periodic biomass harvesting. Microbiome and gene-centric profiling revealed temporal variation in community composition and in the representation of genes associated with carbon and nitrogen metabolism. Cycle-based dissolved inorganic nitrogen balances showed that the decrease in dissolved inorganic nitrogen was only partially recovered in harvested biomass, while ammonia-oxidizing microorganisms were associated with structured, low-light niches. These observations indicate ammonia-oxidizing potential but do not establish a quantitatively relevant nitrification flux. Structured carrier matrices provided attached-growth niches harboring microbial populations underrepresented in the circulating suspension, while pre-colonized carriers facilitated biomass development during re-inoculation. Overall, our results show that coupling PBRs to agricultural exhaust streams can support biomass production while sustaining spatially structured microbial communities with taxonomic and functional potential. These findings may inform their further development for emission mitigation and circular biomass production.

papers.title: LinearKnot: linear-time ensemble analysis of RNA density-2 pseudoknots under hierarchical folding
papers.abstract: Motivation: A pseudoknot is an arrangement of crossing base pairs. Pseudoknots complicate structure prediction and calculations over possible structures (an ensemble). CParty sums structure weights for hierarchical pseudoknots that keep a supplied pseudoknot-free structure (scaffold). Its time is cubic in sequence length. Results: LinearKnot approximates CParty with beam pruning. It combines at most two partial structures in each step and keeps the highest-ranked candidates. At fixed beam width, hairpin length limit, and scaffold search limit, partition functions, minimum-free-energy (MFE) predictions, and representative {gamma}-centroid structures from base-pairing probabilities take linear time in sequence length. Loop profiles give probabilities for pairing and six unpaired loop types, including gaps between crossing stems (PseudoLoop). Window accessibility is the probability that a window is unpaired. For each RNA, we compared each base's distributions over pairing partners (including the unpaired state) and structural contexts with exact probabilities and averaged their total variation (TV) distances over bases unpaired in the scaffold. At width 200, the 90th percentiles of these RNA averages among 300-399-base RNAs were 0.0015 for pairing and 0.0017 for contexts. At width 100, LinearKnot completed partition functions for all 107 real RNAs through 29 kilobases. Under our settings, CParty completed RNAs up to about 1 kilobase and was faster on them. For the RNAcentral long non-coding RNA URS00023A4DB9 (29,106 nt), partition-function, pairing-probability, and MFE calculations at width 100 took about 7 minutes and 3.22 GiB. We compared free energy and pairing probabilities before and after each increase in beam width and local limits. These changes generally became smaller at larger widths. At width 200, the calculations for URS00023A4DB9 took about 20 minutes and 5.68 GiB. In rat telomerase RNA, a four-base window next to a pseudoknot was mostly unpaired as part of a PseudoLoop. A pseudoknot-free calculation with the same scaffold gave lower accessibility and placed the window mainly in a hairpin when unpaired. Availability and implementation: LinearKnot provides the linearknot command at https://github.com/TakumiOtagaki/LinearKnot. Experiment scripts and data are at https://github.com/TakumiOtagaki/LinearKnotExperiments.

papers.title: Genomic signatures of long-term selection in the Langhill dairy herd: the power of a five-decade experiment for sustainable dairy cattle breeding
papers.abstract: Background Selective breeding has transformed dairy cattle productivity, but the genomic consequences of long-term directional selection - what it costs in diversity and where in the genome it acts - are hard to quantify because contemporaneous control populations are rare. The Langhill experiment, established in 1973, is one of the world's longest-running dairy cattle selection trials with a designed control line kept under common management. We used this resource population to ask what five decades of bull selection have cost in genetic diversity, where in the genome selection has acted, and whether complementary scans converge on the loci under selection. Results We genotyped archived blood samples from 1,126 cows of two genetic lines: a Select line sired by bulls in the top decile of UK genetic merit for milk fat-plus-protein yield, and a Control line sired by bulls of average merit. The Select line showed the expected gains in every yield trait. Inbreeding accumulated at the same annual rate in both lines, and effective population size, estimated from that rate, was approximately 33. Linkage disequilibrium was higher in the Select line at every marker distance from 2 to 300 kb. Autozygosity was 24.7% higher in the Select line than in the Control line (0.078 versus 0.063), a difference robust across four calling parameter sets and two independent callers. The excess was confined to runs of homozygosity longer than 2 Mb; shorter runs did not differ between lines, confirming a shared founder base and placing all divergence after the lines were split. It did not arise from a numerically narrower sire pool: the Select line used more sires (79 versus 72), each with fewer daughters, yet its cows were three times more related to one another. Twenty-eight regions across thirteen chromosomes showed strong differentiation; intersecting five scans identified a four-method signal on chromosome 21 spanning the SERPINA gene cluster and sixteen three-method regions, including chromosome 3, with haplotype and diversity statistics agreeing on the line carrying the signal in fourteen of seventeen. Autozygosity itself did not localise to any region. Conclusions Selection left two genomic footprints: diffuse, recent inbreeding accumulated through the narrow ancestry of the elite sire pool, and localised differentiation at specific loci. Runs of homozygosity index only the first process; the second is captured by frequency- and haplotype-based differentiation scans. Because the cost of inbreeding is incurred through ancestry rather than the number of bulls used, mating schemes that constrain the rate of co-ancestry would be preferable to simply managing the number of sires selected and used.

papers.title: Therapeutic anti-IgE antibodies generate distinct functional immune complex signatures
papers.abstract: Therapeutic IgG anti-IgE antibodies are benchmarked by their ability to interfere with IgE-Fc[epsilon]RI binding, but their activity within IgE and IgG-containing immune complexes remains poorly defined. Here we show that omalizumab and ligelizumab form binary IgE-IgG and ternary allergen-containing immune complexes with distinct functional properties. In primary human leukocytes, these complexes exhibited antibody- and composition-dependent patterns of cellular association and activation. Using multiplexed focal molography, we resolved Fc receptor engagement across free and complexed antibody states and identified distinct receptor-binding signatures for omalizumab- and ligelizumab-containing complexes. Notably, allergen incorporation reversed the relative ability of the two antibodies to neutralize IgE-Fc[epsilon]RI interactions and remodelled Fc[gamma]R binding. Thus, immune-complex composition is a determinant of therapeutic antibody function.

papers.title: TideCluster: clustering and classification of tandem repeats for comparative and pangenomic analysis
papers.abstract: Satellite DNA, composed of tandem arrays of relatively short repeated units, is a ubiquitous component of plant and animal genomes. Despite its biological importance, systematic investigation of satellite DNA remains challenging, in part because integrated bioinformatic tools for structured comparative analyses across individual arrays, chromosomes, and genomes are lacking. Here, we present TideCluster, a reference-independent pipeline that converts fragmented tandem repeat detections into genome-wide, interpretable repeat family catalogs. Starting from a genome assembly, TideCluster consolidates detected regions into arrays, clusters arrays by sequence similarity, reconstructs representative monomer consensus sequences, estimates locus-specific periodicity, identifies higher-order repeats, and generates GFF3 annotations. In addition to predefined visualizations, including the chromosomal distributions of satellite repeat families, TideCluster produces information-rich outputs that can be adapted for user-specific downstream analyses. We demonstrate its capabilities using the well-characterized genome of Arabidopsis thaliana and a set of Solanum species with highly diverse satellite repeat complements that vary markedly in abundance and have monomer lengths ranging from a few base pairs to more than 20 kb.

papers.title: Mapping the brain-web morphology to characterise ageing and cognitive impairment
papers.abstract: Ageing reshapes human brain anatomy across spatial scales, yet its geometrical organisation remains difficult to quantify. Here we introduce SHARP (Spectral Hierarchy Analysis, Reconstruction and Prediction), which transfers hierarchical cosmic-web classification to structural MRI, identifying knots, filaments, sheets and voids at four spectral levels and combining their morphology with higher-order spatial statistics and anatomical measurements. In CamCAN, selected filament- and sheet-associated features show opposing correlations with age and distinct associations with subcortical and ventricular volumes. To quantify their contribution, we compare SHARP with a neural-network baseline combining 36 regional anatomical measurements, total brain volume and sex. Adding cosmologically motivated descriptors reduces the mean absolute error of MRI-only age prediction from 6.04 to 4.71 years (22%) in CamCAN and from 4.57 to 4.07 years (11%) in OASIS-3 under participant-independent validation. Brain-web morphology with only brain volume and sex already achieves 5.12 years in CamCAN. For cognitive-status classification in OASIS-3, SHARP identifies 85% of Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR)-positive observations at 86% specificity, compared with 78% sensitivity for the anatomical baseline at matched empirical specificity. These results demonstrate that cosmological methods provide complementary geometrical information and measurable gains in characterising brain ageing and cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Anisotropic regulation of lateral surface tension directs invagination in C. elegans gastrulation
papers.abstract: Epithelial invagination is commonly attributed to actomyosin-driven apical constriction, but how the direction of tissue deformation is determined remains unclear. Here, we show that gastrulation in Caenorhabditis elegans involves anisotropic invagination, with preferential anterior-posterior convergence of neighboring cells. Laser ablation revealed no detectable directional bias in apical cortical recoil, suggesting that anisotropy in apical cortical tension is unlikely to be the primary determinant of the observed directional deformation. Instead, HMR-1/E-cadherin exhibited anisotropic accumulation preferentially at specific lateral cell-cell interfaces, where its enrichment is associated with junctional geometry consistent with reduced interfacial surface tension. Three-dimensional mechanical simulations showed that selectively reducing tension at these interfaces reproduces the observed anisotropic deformation and markedly enhances invagination, whereas uniform tension reduction does not. These findings reveal that spatially patterned lateral surface tension cooperates with apical constriction to control the direction and extent of invagination, uncovering a mechanical role for cell adhesion beyond force transmission.

papers.title: The role of Plasmodium falciparum acyl-coenzyme A synthetase 10 in fatty acid acquisition and lipid synthesis
papers.abstract: During the asexual blood stage, malaria parasites synthesize large quantities of lipids to support their rapid proliferation. Exogenous fatty acids obtained from host plasma are activated for lipid synthesis by parasite acyl-coenzyme A synthetases (ACSs). Of the twelve Plasmodium falciparum ACS homologs, ACS10 has emerged as a key blood-stage enzyme. Here, we sought to define the role of ACS10 in fatty acid acquisition and lipid synthesis during asexual development. To accomplish this, we have employed fatty acid alkyne probes of parasite lipid synthesis together with selective depletion of ACS10 in a conditional knockdown parasite line. This approach revealed that ACS10 is required for efficient incorporation of 16- to 20-carbon unsaturated fatty acid alkynes and a 20-carbon, saturated fatty acid alkyne into the major parasite phospholipids and neutral lipids. In contrast, shorter saturated fatty acid alkynes were either unaffected by ACS10 depletion or were hyper-incorporated into parasite lipids. ACS10 knockdown elicited a profound deformation of the food vacuole, which was likely caused by an imbalance of saturated and unsaturated fatty acids in parasite lipids. To promote the discovery and characterization of ACS inhibitors, we have established a fatty acid alkyne-based approach for identifying compounds that target ACS10 as their primary mode of action.

papers.title: Extracting and Updating Compact Colored k-mer Indexes
papers.abstract: Colored k-mer indexes record, for every k-mer of a collection of genomes, the genomes or species that contain it, and underpin pseudoalignment and sequence search against large collections. Construction of such an index is expensive, yet the collection it represents is rarely final: genomes are retracted or found to be contaminated, users need an index of a single species or clade, and new genomes keep arriving. Rebuilding the index after every such change requires the original sequences and repeats the costly construction. We show that colored indexes based on the spectral Burrows-Wheeler transform (SBWT) can instead be updated efficiently in batches, without the original sequences, and with a result equivalent to the index built from scratch. Given an SBWT and any subset of its k-mers, we first extract the SBWT of this subset directly from the input, in one linear pass and without building a new index. Removing genomes, intersection and difference all reduce to this operation. We then carry the colors through every operation, by finding from the inputs alone where the color sets of the result change, so that removing or extracting genomes, as well as the union, intersection and difference of two colored indexes, each directly yield a complete colored index. In our experiments, editing paid off for large results: removing a genome from an index of 3,682 E. coli genomes took 54 seconds instead of 13 minutes for a rebuild, and adding one took about a minute. On AllTheBacteria, with 192 billion k-mers and 12,733 species, extracting M. tuberculosis, with 180,094 genomes, took less than four hours, and set operations then traced contamination of its color, some of which the next release of AllTheBacteria still contains. Our work turns large colored k-mer indexes from static snapshots of a collection into resources that can be maintained as the collection evolves. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/LoreDepuydt/colored-sbwt-setops.

papers.title: PP271, a novel bacteriophage primase-polymerase, enables Primer-Free DNA Amplification
papers.abstract: Primases are essential enzymes that initiate DNA replication by synthesizing de novo primers for replicative DNA polymerases, which ensure accurate genome duplication owing to their high specificity, fidelity, and processivity. PrimPols have emerged as versatile DNA-initiating enzymes that are widely distributed across diverse replication systems, from bacteriophages to humans. In this work, a novel PrimPol enzyme, PP271, encoded by bacteriophage vB-EfaS-271, was characterized. PP271 belongs to the archaeal-eukaryotic primase (AEP) superfamily and contains the conserved catalytic core, together with a C-terminal PriCT domain. Enzymatic analysis demonstrated that PP271 functions as a bona fide PrimPol, i.e. a DNA primase capable of synthetizing short DNA primers. PP271 priming activity is strongly stimulated by ADP, which serves as the preferred initiating nucleotide. Additionally, PP271 exhibits relaxed specificity for selecting the priming site, compared to other PrimPols with more restricted template preferences. TruePrime amplification technology combines the Thermus thermophilus PrimPol and the highly processive Phi29 DNA polymerase to achieve primer-free DNA amplification. While highly efficient, further improvements in amplification yield, fidelity and product complexity remain possible. Here, we show that DNA primers synthesized by PP271 are efficiently extended by Phi29 DNA polymerase, enabling their coordinated action. Moreover, the short primers generated by PP271 are expected to minimize the contribution of primase-derived errors to the final amplification product while allowing efficient DNA synthesis across a broader range of sequence contexts. Altogether, these findings identify PP271 as a promising alternative for improving primase-dependent DNA amplification.

papers.title: SPARK: Systematic Profiling of Antibiotic-Phage Response Kinetics
papers.abstract: Phage therapy is, in practice, combination therapy: phage are almost always added to an ongoing antibiotic regimen, yet the combination is rarely designed to have a specific interaction pattern. Interactions can be antagonistic, additive or synergistic and cannot be inferred from either agent alone. Here we introduce SPARK, a method which quantifies phage antibiotic interaction from growth curves as the integrated deviation of observed growth from the growth expected under Bliss independence. We profiled 42 combinations spanning the ESKAPE pathogens and Escherichia coli with twelve antibiotics. We show that i) synergy and antagonism are resolvable within a single high-throughput assay, with the interaction determined by the phage antibiotic bacteria pairing; ii) 21 clinical Staphylococcus aureus isolates differ among themselves as widely as the seven species do; and, iii) interactions change between a few hours and two days, several reversing direction. Overall, SPARK needs only a plate reader and the analysis is performed with a specific openly available web tool.

papers.title: Effects of Overripe Banana Processing Techniques on the Chemical Composition and Attractancy to Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus
papers.abstract: The rising incidence of vector-borne diseases transmitted by mosquitoes has become a significant public health concern. The increasing resistance of mosquitoes to conventional insecticides has prompted the need for alternative control strategies such as Attractive Targeted Sugar Baits (ATSBs). While fruit-based attractants have shown promise, the impact of different production methods on their attractiveness remains underexplored. This study investigates the effect of three production techniques of overripe banana (Musa acuminata) extracts: liquid extraction, syrup concentration, and freeze-drying, on the chemical composition and their attractiveness to Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. Extracts were infused into hydrogel beads and tested in dual-choice olfactometer assays to mosquito vectors Ae. aegypti and Ae. albopictus. Chemical profiling was conducted through Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and enzymatic sugar analysis. Results showed that all banana extracts were significantly more attractive than the 10% sucrose control. Among the extracts, syrup concentrates showed the highest attraction (PI = 0.58 {+/-} 0.17 for Ae. aegypti; 0.58 {+/-} 0.14 for Ae. albopictus), followed by freeze-dried (PI = 0.52 {+/-} 0.20; 0.54 {+/-} 0.08) and liquid extracts (PI = -0.40 {+/-} 0.04; 0.49 {+/-} 0.18). GC-MS analysis revealed that freeze-dried powder retained the greatest diversity and abundance of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), especially esters like butyl ethanoate and isoamyl acetate, which are known to influence mosquito behaviour. Although syrup concentration resulted in VOCs degradation, it also generated Maillard reaction products, such as sulphur-containing volatiles, which may enhance olfactory cues. Sugar analysis indicated that both syrup and freeze-dried extracts contained higher levels of sucrose (0.35-0.57 g/100g), glucose (21.20-28.70 g/100g), fructose (14.64-17.89 g/100g), and maltose (9.28-15.56 g/100g), aligning with mosquito preferences. Overall, the findings demonstrate that production techniques significantly influence the chemical composition and attractant potential of overripe banana extracts, offering valuable insights for the development of fruit-based mosquito lures in vector surveillance and control strategies.

papers.title: Phosphorylation-dependent conformational change in the Keratin 19 head domain: Implications for filament assembly and binding to GSK3β and 14-3-3
papers.abstract: Keratins are intermediate filament (IF) proteins expressed in various cell types, playing a crucial role in mechanical support and signaling pathways. Keratin 19 (K19) is predominantly found in gut epithelia and early embryonic ectoderm. K19 interacts with signaling proteins such as GSK3{beta} and 14-3-3 to participate in cell signaling pathways. However, details on the binding sites of these proteins on K19, and specific molecular mechanisms governing these interactions, are lacking. Additionally, the N-terminal head domains of IFs including K19 are considered intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs), and their atomic-resolution structures are unavailable. Using NMR spectroscopy, we obtained the first solution structures of K19 head domain peptides. Structural models involving phosphomimetic peptides suggest a phosphorylation-dependent conformational change in the K19 head domain. The phosphomimetic S35E substitution alters the conformation of the head domain, affecting its association with keratin filaments and K19-binding partners. NMR spectral changes indicate that the S35E substitution affects the association of the K19 head domain to K8/K19 filaments and GSK3{beta}, whereas no significant binding changes were observed with 14-3-3{zeta} and 14-3-3{sigma}. Cell-based analyses further showed that the S35E mutation altered keratin filament organization and reduced the proximity between K19 and GSK3{beta} in 293T cells, whereas no significant change was observed in the proximity between K19 and 14-3-3{sigma}. Our findings provide insight into the structure-function relationship of the head domains in IF proteins with direct implications for the assembly of filaments and their role in signal modulation.

papers.title: SAMP1/TMEM201 protects alveolar type 2 cells from DNA damage-associated senescence and restrains pulmonary fibrosis
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive interstitial lung disease in which repetitive injury to the alveolar epithelium and senescence of alveolar type 2 (AT2) cells drive persistent myofibroblast activation and extracellular matrix deposition. Inner nuclear membrane (INM) proteins organise nuclear architecture and participate in the DNA damage response, but whether they influence epithelial senescence and fibrogenesis is unknown. Here we identify SAMP1/TMEM201, an INM protein that binds lamin A/C, emerin and LINC-complex components, as a compartment-selective protector of AT2 cells. In the bleomycin model of pulmonary fibrosis, SAMP1 was reduced in AT2 cells but unchanged in lung fibroblasts. AT2 cell-specific deletion of Samp1 (Sftpc-Cre^ERT2^; Samp1^flox/flox^) aggravated fibrosis at day 21, with higher Ashcroft scores and increased pulmonary Tnfa and Acta2 expression, whereas intratracheal delivery of AAV6-CAG-Samp1 before bleomycin attenuated both histological fibrosis and these transcriptional responses. In primary AT2 cells analysed immediately after isolation without in vitro stimulation, SAMP1 loss was accompanied by reduced 53BP1 protein, comparable gammaH2AX levels, and upregulation of the senescence-associated and profibrotic markers p16^INK4a^ and PAI-1. These findings define a SAMP1-AT2 senescence axis that constrains pulmonary fibrogenesis and suggest that preserving INM-dependent genome surveillance in the alveolar epithelium may offer an epithelium-directed therapeutic strategy for IPF. Because DNA damage signalling was assessed only under baseline conditions, the data establish an association with altered DNA damage signalling rather than a definitive defect in lesion repair.

papers.title: Decoupling Quantification and Identification for Label-Free Top-Down Proteomics Improves Proteome Coverage
papers.abstract: Quantifying proteoforms is essential for understanding biological processes. The most widely used quantification approach in top-down proteomics (TDP) is label-free quantification (LFQ), where quantification and identification compete for acquisition time. We identified missing values, insufficient fragmentation, and undersampling of low-abundance proteoforms as major factors limiting conventional TDP-LFQ workflows. Our proposed workflow decouples quantification and identification through MS1-only quantification followed by targeted data-dependent MS2 identification. The MS1-only acquisition more than doubled the number of mass features quantified reliably and improved quantification precision. Focusing targeted MS2 acquisition on significantly differentially abundant features enables optimization of MS2 parameters and increases identification coverage by 50%. The workflow was validated across different chromatographic conditions, MS acquisition setups, and sample preparation strategies. In Escherichia coli grown on glucose or acetate, the increased depth enabled by this workflow revealed biological insights inaccessible to a previously published bottom-up proteomics dataset. Overall, decoupling quantification and identification improves quantitative depth and proteoform coverage in TDP-LFQ and provides a flexible strategy for high-sensitivity and high-throughput proteoform quantification.

papers.title: Tardigrades survive reversible dormancy during spaceflight: In-orbit revival, post-flight recovery, and transcriptomic responses
papers.abstract: Long-duration space missions face substantial challenges, including limited resources and prolonged exposure to microgravity and radiation. Transporting organisms in a dormant state and reviving them at their destination could help overcome some of these limitations. However, the feasibility of this strategy has not been experimentally demonstrated in multicellular animals beyond Earth. Here, we investigated this possibility using tardigrades, microscopic invertebrates capable of entering a reversible state of dormancy. We demonstrate that dormant tardigrades can withstand near-absolute-zero temperatures (~12 mK), near-vacuum conditions (10-9 mbar), high doses of ionizing radiation (3000 Gy), and complete desiccation. We transported dormant tardigrades to the International Space Station (ISS). They were revived aboard the ISS, subsequently returned to a dormant state, and successfully revived again following their return to Earth. Approximately 45% of the space-flown tardigrades survived the 64-day experimental period. This included two dormancy-revival cycles, 18 days aboard the ISS, and prolonged periods without food or water. Importantly, surviving tardigrades retained their reproductive capacity. Transcriptomic analysis of ISS-exposed tardigrades revealed upregulation of genes associated with protein folding and stress responses, accompanied by downregulation of genes involved in energy metabolism and protein synthesis, providing insights into their molecular responses to the spaceflight environment. Together, these findings demonstrate the successful revival and re-induction of dormancy in a multicellular animal beyond Earth and establish an experimental foundation for exploring dormancy-based strategies for future long-duration space missions.

papers.title: Citrate-Based Hydrogels Promote Closure of Infected Diabetic Wounds
papers.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are a significant threat to the quality of life for individuals with diabetes, affecting approximately 1.6 million patients in the US, as of 2023. When these wounds do not heal and become chronic wounds, they can become infected and increase the risk of digit and/or lower limb amputation. Therefore, there is a critical need for therapies that promote wound closure in the presence and absence of infection. We have previously reported the potential benefits of the thermoresponsive citrate-based macromolecule poly(polyethylene glycol citrate-co-N-isopropylacrylamide) (PPCN) in diabetic rodent and swine models of non-infected full thickness dermal wounds. In this study, we compared four PPCN formulations (PPCN, PPCN-CMOF, A5G81-PPCN, and A5G81-PPCN-CMOF), which are functionalized with the laminin-derived cell adhesion peptide A5G81 and/or contain entrapped copper metal-organic framework nanoparticles (CMOF) designed to release Cu2+ slowly, in diabetic mice with wounds infected with S. aureus. In infected wounds, all four formulations significantly improved cumulative closure relative to saline (adjusted p = 0.002-0.021). In non-infected wounds, only PPCN-CMOF significantly improved cumulative closure relative to saline (p = 0.046), although all four formulations reached [≥]95% closure earlier than saline (adjusted p = 0.009-0.045). In vitro, the CMOF-containing formulations produced the highest bacterial killing (90% for A5G81-PPCN-CMOF and 84% for PPCN-CMOF), whereas A5G81-PPCN and PPCN reduced bacterial colonies by 76% and 59%. PPCN modification with A5G81 and/or CMOF increased endothelial mesh formation in vitro. In vivo, PPCN-based formulations increased granulation tissue thickness and, depending on formulation and infection status, vascular marker expression. These results suggest that PPCN and PPCN formulations containing CMOF and/or A5G81 are a potentially viable technology that can be added to the wound care toolbox to accelerate healing of diabetic foot ulcers in the presence of infection. These findings support further investigation of PPCN as an instructive pro-regenerative biomaterial in a preclinical large animal model.

papers.title: Both genetic and social inheritance influence female aggressive and submissive behavior in a wild primate
papers.abstract: Agonistic interactions are important determinants of resource access in wild animals, but their genetic basis remains poorly understood. Here we use a quantitative genetics approach to estimate the heritability of aggressive and submissive behavior of wild female baboons, considering relative rates of both individual and dyadic aggression and submission. To control for the social inheritance that creates kin-based dominance hierarchies, we implemented a multi-matrix model that included a social status similarity matrix alongside the additive genetic matrix. Despite a substantial contribution of social inheritance, especially for submissive behavior, we found heritable components for both aggressive and submissive behavior (h2=0.21 and h2=0.09-0.11, respectively). In dyadic models, aggressive behavior was primarily influenced by the aggressor's genotype (a direct genetic effect), while submissive behavior was primarily affected by the social partner's genotype (an indirect genetic effect). Finally, we found evidence for a negative genetic (but not phenotypic) correlation between aggressive and submissive behavior within dyads, and a negative genetic correlation between submissive behavior and eliciting submissive behavior. Together, our results highlight how direct genetic, indirect genetic, and social inheritance effects combine to influence primate social behavior.

papers.title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction is Part of a Novel Mechanism for Chemotherapy-Induced Neuropathic Pain
papers.abstract: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a common, persistent complication of cancer treatment, yet the mechanisms sustaining pain remain unclear. Mitochondrial dysfunction has been implicated in chronic pain, but its role in spinal cord dysfunction after chemotherapy, and whether it can be reversed, is unknown. Here, we show that paclitaxel-induced persistent mechanical allodynia was associated with spinal cord (L1-L6) mitochondrial dysfunction 18 days after the last injection, including reduced oxygen consumption and membrane potential ({Psi}m) in the non-phosphorylated state, ATP-linked respiration, maximal respiration, and electron transfer capacity. Paclitaxel also increased susceptibility to mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP)-induction, lowering calcium retention capacity at 3, 8, and 13 days after the last injection. Acute ex-vivo paclitaxel exposure had a similar effect, and cyclosporin A, an mPTP blocker, significantly reversed it. Consistent with a causal role for mitochondrial impairment, hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT), initiated after allodynia developed, improved oxygen consumption and {Psi}m and progressively enhanced mechanical thresholds. Likewise, intrathecal delivery of healthy mitochondria to the spinal cord attenuated established allodynia in paclitaxel-treated rats and reduced mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity in other pain models, sciatic nerve crush and capsaicin. These findings identify persistent spinal mitochondrial dysfunction and increased mPTP susceptibility as features of CIPN and support mitochondrial protection as a therapeutic strategy for CIPN and other pain conditions.

papers.title: Transcriptomic and Metabolomic Analysis of the Caudate and Putamen in ADHD
papers.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a highly heritable, heterogeneous neurodevelopmental disorder that typically manifests in childhood; however, transcriptomic studies have inadequately accounted for age of onset and subtype, with cohorts largely comprising of adults. To address this gap, we established a stringently phenotyped ADHD cohort (up to 19 years; clinically diagnosed combined and inattentive-type ADHD) and integrated postmortem caudate and putamen bulk RNA-seq, LC-MS metabolomics, MEGENA gene co-expression analysis, and cross-study comparison. We identified 279 up- and 35 downregulated DEGs in the caudate and 110 up- and 89 downregulated DEGs in the putamen. The combined caudate-putamen metabolomic analysis revealed dopamine dysregulation (1.68-fold reduction) and dysregulation of four additional metabolites. Enrichment analysis revealed shared molecular signatures involving immune responses, ATP metabolism and calcium ion-dependent signaling, with region-specific differences in the direction of alteration. Neuronal homeostasis, and protein stress showed suppression in the putamen, along with activation of neurotransmitter reuptake, whereas CSF circulation and ECM organization were activated in the caudate, with suppression in CNS myelination, and signs of ventricular perturbations. MEGENA identified 26 ADHD-associated caudate modules and 33 putamen modules. These modules captured canonical synaptic and neuronal-circuitry pathways alongside cellular differentiation, metabolism, and cell-survival processes. FGD1 emerged as a candidate caudate hub gene among the neuronal modules. Cross-study comparison analysis suggested that molecular alterations in ADHD may be age-dependent. Additionally, assessing levels of 76 potential risk genes identified by a large ADHD GWAS study one ARTN exhibited dysregulated levels in putamen and none in caudate. Together, these findings reveal brain-region-specific molecular dysregulation in ADHD across pathways extending beyond canonical neurotransmission to immune, differentiation, and energy-metabolic processes, along with novel evidence of perturbations in the understudied lateral ventricles.

papers.title: Allele-selective knockdown of mutant DNAJB6 improves molecular features in a primary mouse myotube model of LGMDD1
papers.abstract: Dominant variants in DNAJB6 cause limb-girdle muscular dystrophy D1 (LGMDD1), a progressive myopathy associated with disrupted protein homeostasis. Because complete loss of DNAJB6 is embryonic lethal in mice, we evaluated allele-selective knockdown as a strategy to reduce mutant DNAJB6 while preserving wild-type protein. We generated a knock-in mouse carrying an N-terminal 3xFLAG tag on the wild-type Dnajb6 allele, allowing endogenous wild-type and F90I DNAJB6, the murine equivalent of human F89I, to be measured within the same sample. Flag-LGMDD1 mice recapitulated the functional, myopathological, and biochemical features seen in other LGMDD1 models and in human disease. F90I DNAJB6 was more abundant and degraded more slowly than wild-type DNAJB6, and LGMDD1 muscle and primary myotubes showed altered protein handling at baseline and following proteostatic stress. Comparative proteomic analyses identified DNAJA4 as a candidate marker responsive to pathogenic DNAJB6 activity. A two-stage mismatch screen identified a lead candidate siRNA with 264-fold selectivity for F90I DNAJB6. In primary Flag-LGMDD1 myotubes, this siRNA selectively reduced F90I DNAJB6 and shifted several baseline and stress-dependent molecular abnormalities involving p62, HSP70, DNAJA4, and markers associated with unfolded protein response signaling toward control values. These findings establish cellular proof of concept for allele-selective knockdown in LGMDD1.

papers.title: Tissue-like Viscoelasticity Drives Muscle Stem Cell Expansion Through Mechanical Memory Formation
papers.abstract: Mechanical cues are potent regulators of stem cell fate, with even transient exposure to substrates with varied elastic stiffness driving persistent changes in cell fate. Such elastic mechanical memory contributes to the loss of regenerative potential in skeletal muscle stem cells (MuSCs) when cultured on rigid substrates, hampering the translation of myogenic cell replacement therapies. Beyond elastic mechanical properties, cells also respond to time-dependent, viscoelastic mechanical properties, such as stress relaxation. However, whether tissue-like viscoelasticity can impart a mechanical memory that directs stem cell fate remains an open question. Accordingly, dual-network hydrogel biomaterials with decoupled control of stiffness, stress relaxation, and adhesive ligand presentation were engineered to recapitulate the viscoelastic mechanical properties of native muscle. Muscle-like viscoelastic substrates promote in vitro MuSC activation and accelerate stem cell expansion, matching in vivo activation timescales. Mechanistically, physiological viscoelasticity promotes focal adhesion stabilization and enhances Rac-Akt signaling, establishing a viscoelastic mechanical memory that supports progenitor expansion and persistent maintenance of a stem-like phenotype. These findings identify matrix viscoelasticity as a potent and persistent regulator of MuSC fate and provide a framework for engineering biomaterials that preserve MuSC stemness and expansion ex vivo.

papers.title: Diverse bacteria exhibit superadditive growth on mixed classes of carbon sources
papers.abstract: Heterotrophic bacteria in nature encounter complex mixtures of functionally-distinct carbon sources, yet whether such diversity enhances growth yield across diverse taxa remains unknown. We grew dozens of strains from four phyla on defined mixtures representing five classes of carbon sources. Remarkably, many but not all strains exhibited superadditive growth on a dilute mixture of all 64 compounds--that is, yield exceeding the weighted sum of yields on more concentrated subsets of functionally-similar compounds. Using exometabolomics, pooled genetic screens, and proteomics, we find that superadditive growth is associated with enhanced carbon consumption in the mixed-class medium, combined with reduced dependence on amino acid and nucleotide biosynthesis. Moreover, superadditive growth was predictable from genomes within the tested strain panel and correlated with genomically encoded sugar-over-acid preference. These findings reveal a previously underrecognized axis of physiological variation among heterotrophs and open the door to understanding the biochemical and evolutionary basis of this divergence.

papers.title: Midbrain neurons regulate the production of courtship squeaks in female mice
papers.abstract: Animals produce different vocalization types (e.g., contact calls, mating calls) to communicate in different behavioral contexts, but how the brain is organized to enable the production of different vocalization types remains poorly understood. Recent work found that specialized neurons in the midbrain periaqueductal gray (PAG) regulate the production of ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) in female and male mice, but these PAG-USV neurons are not required for the production of broadband vocalizations (squeaks). To identify PAG neurons that may regulate the production of squeaks, we used an activity-dependent labeling strategy (TRAP2) to identify and manipulate PAG neurons that are active in association with the production of courtship squeaks in female mice. Optogenetic activation of courtship squeak-TRAPed PAG neurons elicits the production of squeaks, while ablation of TRAPed PAG neurons blocks the production of courtship squeaks without altering female non-vocal courtship behaviors. Surprisingly, ablation of courtship squeak-TRAPed PAG neurons did not affect the production of footshock-elicited squeaks. Moreover, non-selective PAG ablation, which blocked the production of courtship squeaks in females and USVs in both sexes, attenuated but did not block the production of footshock-elicited squeaks. Our results identify a population of PAG neurons that critically regulates the production of courtship squeaks in female mice and also suggest that a non-canonical, PAG-independent pathway regulates the production of pain-elicited vocalizations.

papers.title: Regulation of sociality and neuronal development by the translation initiation factor eIF4H1 in Drosophila
papers.abstract: Most animal species exhibit some level of sociality. However, whether sociality-related traits evolved independently, or are instead derived from common core mechanisms, remains controversial. Nevertheless, an emerging theoretical framework stipulates that key aspects of how animals interact with their social environments may be regulated by a phylogenetically conserved genetic toolkit. Therefore, we hypothesized that mutations that lead to social deficits in specific human disorders may implicate genes that play conserved roles in the regulation of core social traits across Animalia. Specifically, here we focus on genes associated with Williams syndrome (WS), a rare human multi-system disorder characterized in part by hypersocial cognitive traits. WS is caused by a hemizygous chromosomal microdeletion of 25-28 protein-coding genes. Consequently, it has been hypothesized that haploinsufficiency in at least one of these genes plays an important role in the development and/or function of social neural circuits in humans. Because the Drosophila genome encodes orthologs of 17 of the 28 genes deleted in WS, we reasoned that at least some of them may serve a conserved role in the regulation of social traits across flies and humans, as predicted by the genetic toolkit framework. Using a neuron-specific RNAi knockdown screen, we identified eIF4H1, an ortholog of a highly conserved subunit of the eukaryotic translation initiation complex eIF4F, as a candidate gene for neuronal regulation of sociality in the fly. We show that eIF4H1 expression is predominantly neuronal in the adult fly brain, and that its action plays a differential role in the organization of specific dopaminergic neuron subtypes that are associated with sociality and cognitive functions. These results indicate that eIF4H1 may serve a conserved function in regulating the development of the neuronal circuits that regulate social behaviors, thus supporting the idea of a conserved sociality genetic toolkit.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Personalised Gene Expression Prediction Improves Cell-Type-Specific Association Testing
papers.abstract: Linking genetic variation to disease requires accurate prediction of its effects on gene expression in relevant cell types. Sequence-to-function models offer a way to predict these effects and, with training on personal genomes, have begun to capture inter-individual expression differences. However, effect sign accuracy remains limited, and predictive uncertainty is unquantified. Here we introduce ATTICUS, which combines personalised sequence representations with uncertainty-aware expression prediction. ATTICUS transfers regulatory information learned in bulk expression pretraining to cell-type-specific expression prediction without requiring genotypes paired with single-cell expression data. Across blood and brain cell types in OneK1K and ROSMAP, ATTICUS approximately doubles expression prediction correlations relative to scPrediXcan and substantially improves sign accuracy. Moreover, ATTICUS enables uncertainty-aware transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS). Applied to systemic lupus erythematosus and Alzheimer's disease, ATTICUS identifies more associations, with greater cell-type specificity and stronger directional concordance, and reduced statistical inflation. Together, our results demonstrate that personalised training makes predictions more directionally consistent, and uncertainty propagation improves the calibration of TWAS and the prioritisation of disease genes. ATTICUS provides a framework for both, enabling the use of single-cell expression datasets without matched genotypes to inform uncertainty-aware TWAS, expanding their use in prioritising disease-associated genes and cell types.

papers.title: Circulating CD4 regulatory T cells are broadly preserved in Parkinson's disease despite altered HELIOS expression
papers.abstract: Background Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are an important component of adaptive immune regulation and have been implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD), with previous studies suggesting altered Treg proportions, phenotype and, in some cases, function. However, existing studies have been limited by variable phenotyping approaches and a lack of detailed functional assessment. Given the growing interest in Tregs as potential therapies in PD, better understanding of their phenotype and function in the disease is important. Methods Circulating FOXP3+ Tregs were characterised in individuals with PD and age-matched healthy controls (HC) using a 24-colour spectral flow cytometry panel. Treg suppressive function was assessed by their ability to inhibit proliferation and cytokine production by polyclonally stimulated autologous T effector cells in vitro. Treg lineage stability was assessed by analysis of FOXP3 TSDR demethylation. Results The proportions and phenotypic characteristics of circulating CD4 Tregs were broadly similar between individuals with PD and HCs, as were Treg suppressive function and FOXP3 TSDR demethylation. However, naive CD4 Tregs from individuals with PD showed reduced HELIOS expression, with a similar but non-significant trend in FOXP3 expression. Reduced HELIOS expression was also observed in the CD8 naive Treg compartment. Conclusions Major quantitative or functional abnormalities in circulating Tregs do not appear to be a dominant feature PD. However, reduced HELIOS expression in naive Tregs suggests more subtle phenotypic alterations that warrant further investigation. The broadly preserved suppressive function is reassuring for therapeutic approaches aimed at increasing Treg numbers, although it will be important to establish that expanded Tregs retain a stable phenotype and suppressive function in inflammatory and tissue environments.

papers.title: A PTN-Rich MSC Subtype Promotes Cartilage Repair in End-Stage Knee Osteoarthritis
papers.abstract: Mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapy for end-stage knee osteoarthritis (KOA) shows inconsistent efficacy, and whether MSCs retain cartilage repair capacity in the inflammatory joint remains unclear. Using single-cell RNA sequencing of human Kellgren-Lawrence grade (G ) and (G ) KOA joint tissues and exogenous MSCs, we found that pleiotrophin (PTN) signalling shifts from MSC-chondrocyte crosstalk to chondrocyte-dominated autocrine signalling, with PTN exhaustion and elevated cluster of differentiation 74 (CD74) in G cartilage. We therefore identified and sorted a PTN-rich CD74-low placenta-derived MSC subtype and evaluated it in a murine KOA model and in co-culture with patient-derived chondrocytes. This subtype enhanced cartilage repair, upregulated SOX9, and suppressed MMP13, CD74, IL-6, and IL-1{beta}, potentially through CD74 suppression and reduced NF-{kappa}B signaling. These findings provide a basis for functionally defined, stage-matched cell therapy tailored to the pathological microenvironment of end-stage KOA.

papers.title: Impact of iron-enriched diets on the nutritional composition and microbiome diversity of house crickets (Acheta domesticus)
papers.abstract: Iron deficiency (ID) and iron-deficiency anaemia (IDA) pose significant global health challenges. ID and IDA are particularly widespread in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asian countries, where reliance on plant-based foods is high. Edible insects provide an alternative nutritious food source, rich in both protein and essential minerals and trace elements. Little is known about how dietary iron manipulation affects the trace element bioaccumulation and microbiome community composition of edible insects. This study examined the impact of dietary iron supplementation on the growth, survival, nutrient profile, and microbiome of Acheta domesticus. Experimental diets were formulated using iron (II) sulphate heptahydrate, resulting in final iron concentrations ranging from 333.45 mg Fe/kg (control diet) to 6923.39 mg Fe/kg (100 mM Fe diet). Iron supplementation significantly altered the cricket trace element profile, with iron levels increasing fivefold from basal 21.38 mg/kg to 118.34 mg/kg in the highest iron treatment group. Concurrently, manganese levels showed a strong negative correlation with dietary iron, while zinc and cadmium displayed non-significant downward trends. High-iron diets statistically altered dry matter, chitin, and TBARS, whereas carbohydrates, protein, glycogen, and lipids remained stable. Amino acid profiles shifted progressively, with branched-chain, sulphur-containing, and aromatic amino acids peaking in the 25 mM Fe group. In contrast, the diversity and overall structure of the microbial community remained unaffected across all treatments. In conclusion, tailoring dietary iron can significantly boost the iron content of Acheta domesticus without compromising host survival or altering core microbial structures. To optimize insect rearing strategies aimed at alleviating human micronutrient deficiencies, a feeding dose of 10-25 mmol Fe/kg is recommended.

papers.title: Automatic orofacial behaviors remap within cortical substrates for voluntary motor control in freely moving primates
papers.abstract: Orofacial behaviors, like yawning and emotional facial expressions, involve phylogenetically conserved subcortical circuits. Yet, their context-dependent modulation in primates suggests overlooked cortical contributions. Here, we wirelessly recorded from 640 ventral motor and premotor sites in two freely moving macaques during spontaneous orofacial actions combining automatic and voluntary components to varying degrees (yawning, threat, bite, drink). We identified coupling between synaptic input (local field potential) and spiking output in 169 spatially distributed sites during yawning, while threat display was sparsely represented. Yawn-related sites exhibited an early beta-band suppression followed by high-gamma power enhancement. Of 401 isolated single neurons, 95 (predominantly putative medium-sized pyramidal cells) encoded yawning, mostly together with voluntary biting and drinking actions. No modulation was found during the observation of yawning by conspecifics. Yawn-related units either switched or maintained their mouth opening/closing tuning across yawning and more voluntary actions, suggesting counteracting and synergistic downstream influences on yawning motor control. In contrast, threat-related units predominantly preserved their opening/closing tuning during biting and drinking. Head-free intracortical microstimulation of sites hosting yawn-related units preferentially evoked localized mouth and face movements, supporting their causal role in orofacial motor control. Finally, projecting neural activity into a low-dimensional manifold showed that voluntarily controlled and largely automatic behaviors engaged distinct population dynamics while preserving the discriminability of individual orofacial displays. These findings reveal that cortical substrates of voluntary motor control can be recruited to shape otherwise automatic orofacial displays.

papers.title: A Deformulating Multi-Attribute SEC Method for Simultaneous Quantification of Total RNA, Conjugated Antibody, and Free Antibody in Targeted Lipid Nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Targeted lipid nanoparticles (tLNPs) hold promise for improving cell- and tissue-selective delivery of therapeutic payloads but introduce analytical challenges associated with characterizing both encapsulated cargo and surface-associated targeting ligands within the same formulation. Conventional nucleic acid and protein assays can be affected by nanoparticle scattering, matrix interference, or a limited ability to distinguish conjugated antibody from free antibody. Here, we report an online deformulating size-exclusion high-performance liquid chromatography (SE-HPLC) method that enables simultaneous quantification of total RNA, conjugated antibody, and free antibody from 5 L of tLNP sample. Following injection, exposure to a mobile phase containing sodium dodecyl sulfate and isopropanol disrupts the nanoparticles, enabling chromatographic separation of RNA, conjugated antibody, and free (unconjugated) antibody while minimizing sample handling prior to analysis. RNA was quantified by UV260 detection, whereas antibody was quantified by UV280 or intrinsic fluorescence detection to maximize sensitivity. The method demonstrated linear response over the evaluated concentration ranges, spike recoveries of 88-122%, and precision below 5% relative standard deviation. Application to purified tLNP formulations demonstrated simultaneous assessment of total RNA and conjugated antibody content, while confirming the absence of detectable free antibody following purification. Together, these results establish online deformulating SE-HPLC as a practical multi-attribute analytical method for characterization of tLNPs, enabling concurrent assessment of total RNA concentration, conjugated antibody concentration, and free antibody concentration using standard HPLC instrumentation.

papers.title: Projection-specific filtering of delta-theta input by layer 5 neurons in mouse secondary visual cortex
papers.abstract: Delta- and theta-band oscillations are thought to coordinate cortical activity and to convey top-down signals, but how the different output neurons of a cortical area transform such rhythmic input is less well understood. Layer 5 contains two projection classes, extratelencephalic (ET) and intratelencephalic (IT) neurons, which carry different information to different targets. Here we asked whether they also differ in how they process slow rhythmic input in the delta-theta range. We combined whole-cell recordings in three stimulus regimes in mouse medial secondary visual cortex (V2M) with local field potential (LFP) recordings in awake mice. With small inputs, IT cells summated strongly and acted as low-pass filters, whereas ET cells resonated at low frequencies, forming moderate-resonance (ET1, about 3 Hz) and high-resonance (ET2, about 5 Hz) subgroups. With large inputs, ET cells amplified depolarisation more than hyperpolarisation, at similar resonance frequencies. When driven to fire by a 4 Hz sinusoid at threshold, cells of all classes fired at a similar phase and kept it nearly constant across cycles. In awake mice, visual stimulation increased deep-layer LFP power across about 1-6 Hz, a band that spans the mean ET1 and ET2 resonance frequencies. Thus, the two output classes of layer 5 in V2M filter slow rhythmic input differently, but once firing, they show no detectable difference in spike timing.

papers.title: Mitochondrial transplantation redirects rather than suppresses the inflammatory response in primary human monocytes
papers.abstract: Circulating monocytes are recruited into inflamed tissue, where local cues determine whether the macrophages they become drive inflammation or resolve it. Because that decision occurs after cells leave the blood, the circulating stage offers a window to alter monocyte programming, and monocyte inflammatory function is closely coupled to mitochondrial metabolism. Here we transplanted freshly isolated, respiration-competent mitochondria from HEK293T cells into primary human CD14 monocytes and characterized the resulting mitochondria-transplanted monocytes (MTM) across surface phenotype, respiration, and inflammatory function. Isolated mitochondria were intact and respiration-competent, with a respiratory control ratio of 8.7 and a coupling efficiency of 78.9 %. Monocytes internalized them in proportion to the dose supplied; within 3 h, 88% of viable cells were positive for labeled mitochondria, with no loss of viability detected; isolated mitochondria did not activate NF-{kappa}B or IRF reporters in THP1-Dual cells. Transplantation reduced the frequency of the pro-inflammatory intermediate subset, increased CD14 by 2.11-fold and HLA-DR by 1.31-fold, and decreased CD163. MTM showed reduced ATP-linked respiration with maximal capacity preserved, and a trend toward a higher maximal-to-basal respiration ratio. Following stimulation with LPS, MTM released markedly less TNF- (0.06-fold) and CXCL10/IP-10 (0.25-fold) and, in most donors, more IL-10 (3.33-fold), while the remaining analytes were largely unchanged. Mitochondrial transplantation therefore shifts primary human monocytes toward a phenotype with selectively reduced inflammatory mediator release and increased IL-10 in most donors. It identifies circulating monocytes as a tractable target for mitochondria-based modulation of inflammation.

papers.title: The ganglioside profile of mouse brain does not respond to changes in dietary n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid supply
papers.abstract: Long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids (LC-PUFAs) of the n-3 and n-6 families are major components of brain lipids, both in terms of levels and biological significance. They play crucial roles in various neurological processes. The brain is largely dependent on food supply of LC-PUFAs and its lipid composition can be modulated by changes in dietary intake. Sufficient dietary supply of the n-3 LC-PUFAs as well as a balanced n-6/n-3 ratio are required for proper brain development and function. As dietary intervention using n-3 LC-PUFAs is considered a promising therapeutic approach to prevent or treat brain disorders, it is important to understand the associated biochemical changes as well as the mechanisms underlying the biological effects. In the present study, we performed lipidomic analyses to document the effects of dietary n-3 LC-PUFA supply on the composition of two families of FA-carrying complex membrane lipids playing important roles in the nervous system: phospholipids and gangliosides. We show that an unbalanced, n-3 LC-PUFA-deficient diet, from gestation to adulthood in mice resulted in decreased levels of docosahexaenoic acid (DHA, C22:6n-3) and increased levels of docosapentaenoic acid (DPA, C22:5n-6) in brain phospholipids, while a n-3 LC-PUFA-supplemented diet was associated with the reverse phenotype. However, the composition of brain gangliosides, which carry mainly saturated and mono-unsaturated fatty acids, was unaffected by the diet, suggesting that they do not directly contribute to mediating the neurological effects of dietary n-3 LC-PUFA manipulation.

papers.title: SEC16A/MAG5-mediated ER export shapes ABA receptor homeostasis
papers.abstract: The phytohormone abscisic acid (ABA) controls plant adaptation to environmental stress through PYR/PYL/RCAR receptors. Regulated receptor turnover through ubiquitination and endosomal trafficking, including ESCRT-dependent vacuolar degradation, is a major mechanism controlling ABA signalling. However, whether ABA receptor homeostasis is established during the early secretory pathway remains unknown. Using complementary cell biological and biochemical approaches, we define a constitutive early secretory pool of the ABA receptors PYR1 and PYL4 associated with the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and the Golgi apparatus (GA). Genetic, cell biological and pharmacological analyses reveal that the COPII scaffold protein SEC16A (also known as MAG5) is required for the proper trafficking and homeostasis of this receptor pool. Loss of MAG5 causes intracellular receptor accumulation, impaired trafficking towards late endosomal compartments and enhanced ABA signalling without affecting endogenous ABA accumulation. Together, our findings establish the early secretory pathway as an integral component of the ABA signalling network and demonstrate that MAG5-mediated ER export shapes ABA receptor homeostasis by coordinating receptor trafficking throughout the endomembrane system, revealing the ER as a key regulatory compartment for ABA receptor homeostasis.

papers.title: An Accessible and Scalable Pipette-Driven Microfluidic Platform for Lipid Nanoparticle Formulation
papers.abstract: Advances in lipid nanoparticle (LNP) technology have increased the need for accessible and scalable methods that accelerate low-volume formulation screening. Here, we describe a disposable microfluidic mixer actuated by a positive-displacement pipette equipped with dual-chamber pipette tip, providing volumetric control at a fixed flow rate ratio without external microfluidic pumps. Computational fluid dynamics analysis predicted shorter micromixing times in the high-shear spiral channel than in the low-shear design. Across three benchmark lipid formulations, the high-shear mixer reproducibly generated smaller LNPs with higher mRNA encapsulation efficiency than the low-shear mixer or manual pipetting. Orthogonal characterization further revealed higher particle concentrations, structural features consistent with compact particles, more uniform mRNA loading, and a lower empty-particle fraction. LNPs prepared using the selected high-shear mixer mediated functional mRNA delivery in 2D cell cultures, a 3D human liver tissue model, and mice. Integration with a liquid-handling robot enabled automated screening of formulation parameters. Dimensionless mixing-time analysis guided enlargement of the mixer geometry for a separate production system, which produced 75 mL preparations at 150 mL/min with particle size and mRNA encapsulation efficiency comparable to those obtained with the small-scale mixer. This platform provides an accessible, automation-compatible approach to LNP formulation screening and a route to larger-scale production.

papers.title: MmuPV1 and HPV E6 Elevate Nuclear Accumulation of IKK? to Impair NF-κB Signaling to Promote Persistent Infection
papers.abstract: The mouse papillomavirus (MmuPV1) E6 oncoprotein is essential for persistent infection and cancer development. Previous studies identified amino acid R130 of MmuPV1 E6 as critical for its interaction with the tumor suppressor MAML1. Mutation of this residue (R130A) disrupts MAML1 binding and prevents disease development in mice. In this study, we demonstrate that MmuPV1 E6 also disrupts NF-{kappa}B signaling through interactions with proteins in the I{kappa}B kinase (IKK) complex. Specifically, the MmuPV1 E6R130A mutant is defective in binding IKK complex proteins and fails to impair NF-{kappa}B signaling in mouse keratinocytes, suggesting that these interactions are necessary for E6-mediated disruption of this pathway. Furthermore, MmuPV1 E6 expression is associated with increased nuclear localization of IKK?, whereas cells expressing the E6R130A mutant exhibit no such increase. These findings suggest that E6-mediated nuclear localization of IKK? depends on its interaction with IKK complex proteins. Importantly, we demonstrate that the human papillomavirus HPV16 E6 oncoprotein similarly impairs NF-{kappa}B signaling and increases nuclear IKK? localization in human keratinocytes, suggesting a shared mechanism between mouse and human papillomaviruses. Additionally, analysis of previously published RNA sequencing data reveals that MmuPV1 E6 induces several transcriptional changes associated with increased nuclear IKK?. Together, these findings demonstrate that both MmuPV1 and HPV16 E6 disrupt NF-{kappa}B signaling in association with increased nuclear IKK? localization. This study provides the first evidence of an E6 oncoprotein interacting with and changing subcellular localization of IKK? to disrupt cellular homeostasis.

papers.title: A genomic prediction framework for growth traits in black soldier fly (Hermetia illucens) breeding programmes
papers.abstract: Background Genomic prediction has been applied in livestock, plant and aquaculture species to accelerate genetic gain. However, its application and potential still remain unexplored in farmed black soldier fly (BSF), an emerging globally important insect production species. Due to the diversity of BSF feed sources, selection strategies need to be evaluated across various feedstocks and production environments to aid in building genomic selection into BSF breeding programmes. In this study, 2,083 BSF larvae from the base population were reared on three diets (SYK: Soy-okara, BSG: brewers' spent grain and FVW: fruit and vegetable waste), and 536 from the F7 population were reared on a chicken starter feed diet. Larvae were phenotyped for four growth traits (LBW, larval body weight; LL, larval length; LW, larval width; LSA, larval surface area) and genotyped across 4,680 SNPs. Genomic prediction was evaluated using seven methods under additive (A) and additive-dominance (AD) models, considering across- and within-diet effects, genotype by diet (G x D) interactions, differences amongst reference and test generations, and SNP densities. Results Performance varied across all scenarios, with LBW showing higher predictive ability (PA) among the growth traits. Accounting for dominance generally improved PA. Multivariate models accounting for G x D performed similarly to, or marginally better than, within-diet predictions. Cross-diet prediction was more variable and generally lower than within-diet prediction, showing reduced transferability across untested nutritional environments. Reducing the SNP density from 4,680 to 3,000 SNPs maintained comparable PA; however, PA decreased below 3,000 SNPs. Across multiple generations, predictive performance declined, resulting from reduced genetic connectivity and possible genotype-by-environment (G x E) interactions between the reference and testing populations. Conclusions Overall, these results provide an application-based framework for genomic prediction in BSF in semi- or commercial production settings. Results also highlight the importance of the genetic model, representative reference populations, and appropriate marker densities for genomic selection.

papers.title: Leave-One-Out-Cross-Validation Based Machine Learning Algorithms for Efficient, Scalable, and Robust Prediction of Artemisinin Resistance in Plasmodium falciparum Kelch13 mutants.
papers.abstract: Emerging Plasmodium falciparum resistance to frontline artemisinin (ART) derivatives threatens global malaria control efforts. Current protocols assigning ART-sensitive (ART-S) or -resistant (ART-R) phenotypes to parasite strains with Kelch13 (K13) mutations remain time-intensive for real-time surveillance. Ring-survival assay (RSA), an ex vivo gold standard mandates laboratory-adaptation under culture conditions and frequently does not replicate clinical ART-responsiveness, thereby limiting its utility for rapidly triaging newly emerging K13 variants. In contrast, advent of artificial intelligence (AI)-derived models hold potential to screen >100 K13 variants within hours, enabling rapid near-real-time prediction of ART-S/R.
