It remains to be seen whether any of these ant species are having or will have a significant impact on the native Icelandic biota. The arrival of Myrmica rubra in Iceland is particularly worrisome, given the impact this species is having in other high latitude areas it has invaded.

papers.title: Environmental Frass Remodels the Larval Gut Microbiome to Enable Black Soldier Fly (Hermetia illucens) Bioconversion of Livestock Manure
papers.abstract: Black Soldier Fly larvae (BSFL) consume nearly any organic material and show promise for the remediation of agricultural waste, including livestock manure. BSFL feeding generates frass, a mixture of unconsumed substrate, larval feces, and microorganisms. We identified a wild population of BSFL (Yuba strain) thriving on rabbit manure, a challenging substrate due to its high lignocellulose content. We investigated if frass extract from this source was necessary and sufficient to support bioconversion of manure and if such effects are altered by captive husbandry. Larvae supplemented with domestic frass failed to grow on rabbit manure but grew well when supplemented with wild-sourced frass. Microbiome analysis revealed that wild-sourced frass contributes a cohort of lignocellulose-degrading microorganisms to the BSFL gut, particularly Rummeliibacillus bacteria and Scedosporium fungi. These growth-promoting effects extended to cattle manure. Following initial seeding with wild-sourced frass, lab-cultured frass ultimately failed to support growth on rabbit manure and the gut microbiome shifted toward bacteria commonly found in domestic BSFL. This study reveals that frass extract derived from environmental sources can improve the bioconversion ability of BSFL and that beneficial microbes are lost during captive-rearing.

papers.title: Redox regulation of 2-carboxy-D-arabinitol 1-phosphate phosphatase in Fabaceae is associated with high Rubisco dark inhibition
papers.abstract: Improving Rubisco regulation is an avenue for improving crop output. Minimizing the buildup of Rubisco inhibitors can allow improved catalytic activity and CO2 assimilation. The enzyme 2-carboxy-D-arabinitol 1-phosphate phosphatase (CA1Pase) degrades certain Rubisco inhibitors, yet the mechanisms for its regulation, including the function of its C domain, are not well understood. In this study we analysed Vigna unguiculata (cowpea) CA1Pase in silico and in vitro for structural regions and motifs related to regulation of phosphatase activity. We identified a highly conserved cysteine pair motif tied to redox regulation and potential homodimer formation. Variations in one or both cysteine residues in this motif across species correlate with lower dark inhibitor accumulation levels as compared to related species. The C domain is identified as having a regulatory function and potential evolutionary origins are explored. These insights may inform future efforts toward optimising Rubisco's complex regulatory processes including inhibitor degradation.

papers.title: The yeast Gcn2 protein kinase mediates P-body formation both through its activity with eIF2α and with non-canonical substrates
papers.abstract: P-bodies (PBs) are control hubs for RNA processing and storage that form when translation initiation is inhibited, including during stress. In yeast, Gcn2 is the sole eIF2 alpha kinase that inhibits translation initiation in response to diverse stresses. We show that PB formation depends strongly on Gcn2 during amino acid starvation but only partially during oxidative stress. Constitutively active Gcn2 also induces PB formation in unstressed cells. Surprisingly, PBs are still constitutively formed in a gcn3 mutant strain that is insensitive to eIF2 alpha phosphorylation suggesting that Gcn2 also promotes PB formation independently of eIF2 alpha phosphorylation. Analysis of several putative Gcn2-substrates involved in RNA metabolism identified several proteins required for Gcn2-mediated PB formation. Among these, Smu2, which was not previously implicated in PB formation, localises to PBs and is required for stress-induced coalescence of mRNA granules into PBs. Together, our findings indicate that Gcn2 promotes PB formation via two complementary routes: eIF2 alpha phosphorylation, which generates untranslated mRNAs, and Smu2-dependent maturation of mRNA granules into PBs.

papers.title: Robust planar morphogenesis in leaf-like organs requires callose-dependent coordination of division and growth
papers.abstract: Planar organs, such as leaves, are key developmental innovations underlying the evolutionary success of plants. In vascular plants, building a planar organ requires coordinating cell division and growth both within the organ plane and across multiple, mechanically distinct cell layers. Phyllids, the leaf-like organs of bryophytes, typically consist of a single cell layer and offer a minimal system to decouple in-plane growth coordination from inter-layer mechanics. Here, we investigate how robust planar morphogenesis is achieved in phyllids, using the moss Physcomitrium patens as a bryophyte model. We show that impaired cytokinesis, caused by the loss of a callose synthase gene, disrupts growth gradients, ultimately yielding smaller, non-planar organs of variable shape. Combining quantitative live imaging with computational modeling, we show that the severity of shape defects in mutants depends on the spatial distribution and developmental timing of local growth arrests. These findings reveal how callose-dependent coordination between cell division and in-plane growth prevents mechanical conflicts and maintains planarity in a monolayered plant organ.

papers.title: Gregariousness can promote invasion success of pest insects while higher environmental heterogeneity decreases it
papers.abstract: Climate change and environmental homogenization are expected to facilitate the expansion of many forest pest insect species and increase the vulnerability of forest ecosystems to insect outbreaks. At present, we lack empirical data on how the antipredator defence traits of pest insects interact with the local environmental conditions and shape outbreak risk. Here we study this and ask 1) how the antipredator defence strategy of pest insects shapes survival under naturally varying predator community, and 2) how is predation risk shaped by the diversity and structure of forests? We tested these questions by conducting a field predation experiment with artificial prey system (prey items made from edible dough) where we manipulated the gregariousness, unpalatability and defensive colouration of prey and tested their effects on prey survival. Additionally, we measured environmental variables and invertebrate predator community structure along the prey transects to analyse how they shape overall predation risk. Our results show that the predation risk was always lowest for gregarious prey irrespective of other defence strategies. Furthermore, our results indicate that predation pressure was lower in more homogenously structured forest areas or areas with a weak quality deadwood continuum in comparison to locations with more natural state forests and good quality deadwood continuum. Altogether, our results suggest that gregariousness can facilitate pest insects to form outbreaks by increasing their survival against generalist predators. However, by maintaining higher heterogeneity in forests, it is possible to ensure higher predation pressure to regulate their population growth.

papers.title: Age-associated repression of HNF4α is a driver and potential therapeutic target in liver metabolic dysfunction
papers.abstract: Aging is a major risk factors for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). However, the mechanisms by which aging disrupts hepatocyte transcriptional networks to drive metabolic dysfunction remain poorly understood. Hepatocyte nuclear factor 4 alpha (HNF4) is a master regulator of hepatocyte identity and metabolic homeostasis, but its role in liver aging has not been defined. Here, we perform a comprehensive multi-omic profiling of young and aged mouse livers combined with targeted HNF4 functional studies to define how aging remodels HNF4-dependent gene regulation and whether HNF4 can be a target to reverse age-associated liver dysfunction. Despite preserved HNF4 expression with age, aging was associated with reduced HNF4 chromatin occupancy and transcriptional activity, accompanied by epigenetic remodeling, including changes in histone acetylation, chromatin accessibility, and DNA methylation. Integration and comparison of HNF4 CUT&RUN with hepatocyte-specific Hnf4a deletion in young and aged livers identified high-confidence overlapping but distinct young- and old- specific HNF4 target gene networks. In young hepatocytes, HNF4 coordinates two complementary transcriptional programs: activation of genes governing hepatocyte identity, lipid metabolism, and metabolic function, while simultaneously inhibiting alternative developmental, proliferative, and inflammatory programs. Spatial transcriptomic analyses further revealed zone-specific specialization of HNF4-dependent gene programs. Aging selectively disrupted these regulatory networks, resulting in compromised liver identity and metabolic gene programs, de-repression of inflammatory pathways and alternative cellular identity programs and disrupted hepatocyte zonation, consistent with age-dependent lipidomic and metabolic changes, hepatic fat accumulation, and immune infiltration. Hepatocyte-specific Hnf4a deletion in young mice recapitulated key features of liver aging, including impaired hepatocyte identity, metabolic dysfunction, steatosis, inflammatory activation and altered hepatic immune-cell composition, while deletion in aged mice further exacerbated steatosis, inflammation, and hepatic dysfunction. Conversely, hepatocyte-specific HNF4 restoration in aged mice significantly reduced hepatic steatosis and lipid accumulation, restored fatty acid metabolic programs, and partially reversed age-associated transcriptional changes. However, inflammatory and interferon-associated programs were not uniformly reversed, revealing differential responsiveness of metabolic and inflammatory pathways to HNF4 restoration. Together, these findings identify age-associated impairment of HNF4 activity as a functional contributor to liver aging, linking dysregulation of hepatocyte identity, metabolic homeostasis, and inflammatory control to age-associated hepatic dysfunction. Importantly, the selective reversibility of metabolic defects following HNF4 restoration establishes HNF4 as a promising strategy for preserving hepatocyte homeostasis and reversing age-associated hepatic metabolic dysfunction.

papers.title: Hypoxic Stress Induces LARP1-Driven Stress Granules That Protect mRNAs from Decay to Sustain Mitotic Cell Cycle Progression
papers.abstract: Hypoxia is a defining feature of solid tumours that elicits extensive transcriptional and post-transcriptional adaptations. Stress granules (SGs) are frequently observed under hypoxia, yet how they assemble and whether they contribute to hypoxic gene regulation remain poorly understood. Here, we show that hypoxia induces SGs through an assembly mechanism distinct from that of classical acute stresses. Hypoxia SG formation occurs independently of the integrated stress response and instead requires the HIF1-REDD1-mTORCC1-4EBP1 axis. Remarkably, hypoxia SGs assemble despite robust ongoing translation, suggesting that additional mechanisms lower the threshold for RNA condensation. We identify LARP1 as a potential determinant of this process, where it promotes G3BP-dependent SG assembly specifically during hypoxia. Despite their distinct assembly mechanism, hypoxia and arsenite SGs recruit broadly similar RNA populations, with selective differences validated by single-molecule FISH, suggesting that conserved principles govern RNA partitioning across different SG states. Functionally, sequestration into hypoxia SGs correlates with enhance protein expression whereby a subset of mRNAs are protected from decay. Transcriptomic analyses further reveal that this protection sustains a broader gene-expression program enriched for MCM complex and mitotic cell-cycle regulators. Accordingly, disruption of hypoxia SGs reduces mitotic progression and proliferative competence during prolonged hypoxia. Together, our findings establish LARP1-mediated condensation as a mechanism that enables SG assembly despite ongoing translation and reveal that SG sequestration preserves selected mRNAs from decay to sustain the gene-expression programs required for long-term adaptation to hypoxia.

papers.title: Accelerating discovery and integration from RNA to Protein with R2T2P
papers.abstract: Integrating transcriptomics and proteomics data remains an unmet challenge in the post-genomics era, discouraging researchers from pursuing integrative approaches to molecular biology research. Leveraging the power of translation profiling, we present RNA to Translation to Protein (R2T2P), a computational platform integrating genome-guided transcriptome assembly with identification of translation and proteins, including a tailored differential analysis framework and support for multiple reference transcriptomes. We applied R2T2P to investigate a cellular model of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD), where ectopic expression of the DUX4 retrogene in skeletal muscle triggers significant alterations in transcription and RNA metabolism. We uncovered hundreds of uncharacterized, highly overexpressed RNAs, including antisense and alternative transcripts, and quantified their contribution to translatome and proteome. Re-analysis of expression datasets from patient-derived myotubes and muscle biopsies validated this alternative transcriptome in FSHD patients, adding a reservoir of bona-fide novel molecular actors in a rare disease. Available at https://github.com/nfdata-omics/R2T2P/, R2T2P is a flexible and powerful workflow in modern integrative biology.

papers.title: Unbiased lineage tracing across the adipose organ decouples developmental origin from anatomical and transcriptomic identities
papers.abstract: The developmental origins of individual adipose depots and whether embryonic lineage dictates adult function remain unresolved. Here, we apply in utero CRISPR-mediated barcoding lineage tracing to construct the first unbiased clonal map of adipose organ development in mice. The developmental hierarchy we uncover challenges several conventions. Remarkably, interscapular brown fat, used as the prototypical brown fat, is the most developmentally isolated brown fat; depots sharing Myf5/Pax3 lineage markers fail to cluster together; mesenteric white fat shares unexpected high clonal ancestry with brown fats despite a radically divergent transcriptome; and subcutaneous white adipose tissues converge transcriptomically despite distant developmental origins. These findings call for a reinterpretation of single-marker lineage tracing data across the adipose organ and propose that adipose depot identity is not solely encoded by embryonic lineage but is substantially shaped by the anatomical niche.

papers.title: Dynamic mechanical sorting biases niche occupancy and lineage outcome during development of bilayered glandular epithelia
papers.abstract: Tissue compartmentalization into basal and luminal domains is a hallmark of glandular epithelia, yet how fate boundaries are established and stabilized during dynamic morphogenesis remains a major unresolved question. Here, using mouse embryonic explants, organoids, quantitative live imaging and genetic perturbations, we show that basal-luminal compartmentalization is not maintained by fixed boundaries, but through continuous positional corrections. We show that differences in cellular adhesion and actomyosin contractility drive these positional corrections by promoting active cell sorting. We further find that these mechanical differences influence lineage specification by controlling cell positioning rather than directly instructing cell fate. Before commitment, mosaic, but not uniform, perturbation of cell mechanics alters niche occupancy and biases lineage outcome, indicating that relative mechanical properties determine access to fate-instructive niches. Conversely, perturbation of Notch and YAP remodels compartment-specific mechanical properties and cell-positioning dynamics, revealing a reciprocal coupling between lineage state and mechanical sorting. Conservation of this mechanism across four glandular epithelia of distinct origins and functions identifies dynamic mechanical sorting as a general strategy for maintaining robust tissue compartmentalization during the extensive growth and cellular rearrangements of branching morphogenesis.

papers.title: A Common Recognition Architecture Across Memory Scales
papers.abstract: Recognition decisions occur across memory episodes that vary vastly in scale, from compact single-item episodes to extended experiences involving hundreds of items. To test how memory scale shapes the neural mechanisms underlying old/new judgments, we recorded EEG while participants performed a recognition memory task across set sizes ranging from 1 to 128 items (spanning 2 to 256 recognition judgments). Classic electrophysiological signatures of recognition, including frontal and parietal old/new effects, persisted continuously across set sizes. Furthermore, multivariate neural classifiers trained on small memory scales generalized robustly across set sizes. Rather than revealing distinct neural formats, increasing memory scale produced systematic, continuous shifts in the timing and strength of a shared recognition response: signals emerged progressively later and weaker at larger memory scales. Temporal-alignment and cross-correlation analyses demonstrated that responses across scales followed a common waveform trajectory, with timing shifts propagating into motor response preparation. Finally, individual difference analyses revealed that this common recognition format exhibits scale-dependent behavioral relevance, tracking working-memory capacity at smaller scales and long-term memory performance at larger scales. Together, these findings demonstrate that recognition signals share a common neural format across scale while changing dynamically in timing, strength, and behavioral relevance, providing evidence for convergence onto a shared recognition architecture.

papers.title: Seasonal H1N1 influenza A virus preferentially infects a pre-existing ciliogenesis-primed secretory cell state
papers.abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAV) infect secretory and ciliated cells of the human airway epithelium , but whether all cells within one cell type are equally susceptible to infection remains unresolved. Here, single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of primary human bronchial epithelial cultures from three donors identified preferential infection of a transcriptionally distinct subpopulation of secretory cells by seasonal H1N1 IAV A/Hawaii/70/2019 . Genes upregulated in this subpopulation showed enrichment for cilium-related gene ontology terms. In an ex post facto approach, this enrichment persisted after excluding genes differentially expressed between infected and mock-treated samples, including those identified in secretory cell-specific comparisons. Single-cell analysis further revealed no significant increase in ciliogenesis scores in infected secretory cells compared to mock infected cells at 6 hours post-infection , arguing against infection-induced activation of the canonical ciliogenesis programme during the initial viral replication cycle . Collectively, these results support preferential infection of ciliogenesis-primed secretory cells and refine IAV tropism beyond cell type to encompass epithelial differentiation state.

papers.title: A largely shared genetic architecture underlies Saccharomyces cerevisiae persistence across different mouse host genotypes
papers.abstract: The extent to which interactions between microbial and host genotypes shape opportunistic pathogen persistence within hosts is an important open question. To assess the contribution of these interactions to persistence, we used Saccharomyces cerevisiae, a genetically tractable model for studying opportunistic fungal persistence in mammalian hosts. A pooled panel of barcoded haploid segregants from a cross between a laboratory strain and a clinical isolate, together with both parents, was introduced intravenously into seven genetically diverse mouse strains. We measured the relative persistence of segregants in mouse brains and livers using barcode sequencing. Persistence showed transgressive segregation in both organs. On average across the two organs, yeast genotype explained 45.2% of the variance in segregant persistence, whereas yeast genotype-by-host genotype interactions explained only 2.9%. Linkage mapping showed that loci detected in more host genotypes generally explained more phenotypic variance than those detected in fewer host genotypes. At some loci, genetic variation correlated with increased yeast persistence across multiple organs (general loci) while at others increased persistence in one organ came at the cost of decreased persistence in another (antagonistic loci). General loci contributed disproportionately to brain persistence, whereas liver persistence reflected contributions from both classes. The clinical parent showed greater persistence than the laboratory parent in every host-organ combination, and the additive effects of detected loci predicted the direction of this advantage. Overall, this work shows that in this system, relative microbial persistence is polygenic, with a strong additive component and only a very small contribution from microbial genotype-by-host genotype interactions.

papers.title: Psychoneuroimmunology of Viral Hepatitis and Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and viral hepatitis (VH) are recognized primarily as hepatic diseases, yet they impose a substantial neuropsychiatric disorders (NPDs) encompassing depression, anxiety, cognitive impairment, and fatigue. Whether these manifestations reflect psychological reactions or biologically grounded psychoneuroimmune dysfunction remains poorly understood. Here, we present a pre-registered systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO 2026 CRD420251081757) synthesizing evidence from 24 studies combining psychosocial outcomes with immune dysregulation markers across HCC and VH populations. Bibliometric and network analyses identified a growing psychoneuroimmunology research hub linking cytokine signaling, microglial activation, blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, and gut-liver-brain axis dysregulation to the neuropsychiatric phenotype of these diseases. Meta-analysis revealed a pooled hazard ratio (HR) of 1.92 (95% CI: 1.09-3.39) for adverse outcomes in HCC and a pooled HR of 2.28 (95% CI: 1.48-3.52) for depression associated to genetic variants in VH. TNF-a, but not IL-6, showed a tendency toward lower levels in VH patients with versus without NPDs, suggesting differential inflammatory roles. The literature, however, remains fragmented by heterogeneous designs and a paucity of longitudinal data. A psychoneuroimmunological approach, integrating immune, endocrine, neural, and psychosocial dimensions, is essential for capturing the full systemic impact of HCC and VH and should inform future mechanistic research and multidisciplinary clinical strategies.

papers.title: Phenotypic variation in divergent mitochondrial haplotypes in migratory three-spined stickleback
papers.abstract: Mitochondria are essential components in life-sustaining organismal processes. The mitochondrial genome can be influenced by selection, and divergent mitochondrial haplotypes have substantial potential to affect interspecies variation in life-history and physiology, yet little is known about whole organism phenotypic changes that might accompany mitochondrial genomic divergence. Three-spined stickleback on the Scottish island of North Uist provide a model to study this as their populations exhibit a well-mixed nuclear genome, yet two highly diverged mitochondrial haplotypes ( trans-Atlantic and European). Three-spined stickleback were sampled from six lochs to investigate associations between mitochondrial haplotype and phenotypic traits including organ size, body size, and ovule volume/clutch size, as well as citrate synthase enzyme activity. Results showed that mitochondrial haplotype has an influence on male gonadosomatic index (GSI) and potentially citrate synthase (CS) enzyme activity. Differences in male GSI may be explained by the timing of male spermatogenesis or potentially a need for larger testes in European haplotype fish. While no other phenotypic trait showed differences between mitochondrial haplotypes, there were many differences between sexes and populations e.g. in body size and organ/muscle size.

papers.title: Novel Tau Interaction Partners as Potential Biomarkers and Therapeutic Targets in Neurodegenerative Diseases
papers.abstract: Alzheimers disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder leading to cognitive decline and ultimately death. One of the main hallmarks of this disease is the accumulation of pathological tau protein into neurofibrillary tangles. To better understand these pathological mechanisms, it is essential to characterize the tau protein interactome in health and disease. In this study, we performed a yeast two-hybrid screening using a human brain cDNA library, from which we identified 15 novel tau-interacting proteins that bind to full-length human tau, or its fragments: the N-terminus, microtubule-binding domain, or C-terminus. We subsequently validated these novel interactions using in vitro co-immunoprecipitation and colocalization assays with both physiological and pathological tau isoforms. Furthermore, their interactions with the human tau protein were analyzed using surface plasmon resonance. Finally, an in silico interactome analysis of these newly discovered tau-binding partners revealed several additional interactors that can link them to downstream processes critical to neurodegenerative pathways Our findings offer fresh insights into tau biology and highlight novel targets for therapeutic intervention and biomarker development.

papers.title: Growth, yield, and quality of hot pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) as affected by the combined application of liquid bio-slurry and NPS fertilizer rates in Kucha, Gamo zone, south Ethiopia
papers.abstract: Hot pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) is a key cash and nutritional crop in Ethiopia, yet its productivity remains constrained by inadequate and imbalanced soil nutrient management. Therefore, the field experiment was conducted in Kucha woreda, Gamo Zone, South Ethiopia, during the 2024/25 cropping season to investigate the effect of liquid bio-slurry and NPS fertilizer rates on growth, yield and quality of hot pepper. The experiment consisted of 16 treatments arranged in a factorial combination of four liquid bio-slurry (LBS) rates (0, 20, 40, and 60 m3 ha-1) and four NPS fertilizer rates (0, 75, 150, and 225 kg ha-1) using a randomized complete block design with three replications. All experimental data were collected following standard agronomic procedures and subjected to analysis of variance using GenStat statistical software (18th edition). The results revealed that both the main and interaction effects of liquid bio-slurry and NPS significantly (p < 0.01) influenced phenological, growth, yield, and quality parameters. The combined application of 150 kg ha-1 NPS and 60 m3 ha-1 LBS produced the highest marketable dry fruit yield (2.94 t ha-1) and total dry fruit yield (3.16 t ha-1), representing a 129.69% yield advantage over the control (1.28 t ha-1) in the case of marketable dry fruit yield. The findings demonstrate that integrated nutrient management using combined LBS and NPS fertilizers significantly enhanced the productivity and quality of hot pepper. Therefore, the application of 150 kg ha-1 NPS combined with 60 m3 ha-1 liquid bio-slurry is recommended for improved hot pepper production for the study area and similar agro-ecological conditions.

papers.title: Can a Tiny Brain Plan? Reconstructing a Predatory Detour in the Jumping Spider Portia labiata
papers.abstract: Planning is the process of evaluating alternative futures to predict outcomes and guide action. Evidence for this process exists in several vertebrates, but remains contested in in-vertebrates. Jumping spiders in the genus Portia show planning-like behavior in lab studies, but how this translates to the wild is unclear, where hunts of potentially lethal spider prey occur over durations of more than an hour in dense foliage. We present the first fully video-recorded wild hunt of any Portia species, with a 3D reconstruction of its forty-two minute long route to attack an orb-weaving spider. The reconstruction suggests P. labiata may have planned its approach, avoiding a route half as long but potentially more conspicuous to the prey's sensory systems.

papers.title: Polyphyletic origins and lineage-specific expansion of chemosensory systems in phylum Actinomycetota
papers.abstract: Phylum Actinomycetota (syn. Actinobacteriota or Actinobacteria), one of the largest well-studied bacterial phyla, is renowned for complex morphology, non-motility, ecological versatility, and secondary metabolite production. Chemosensory systems (CSS) are among the most sophisticated prokaryotic signal transduction architectures, yet their evolutionary distribution in this phylum remains poorly understood. Here, a comparative genomic analysis of 693 high-quality genomes spanning the phylum resolves the diversity, distribution, and evolutionary trajectories of CSS. Despite extensive genomic complexity and ecological versatility, only 6.9% of genomes encode complete CSS clusters, confined to a subset of lineages within a few classes, indicating lineage-specific retention or loss. In contrast, two-component systems (TCS) are ubiquitously abundant, with hybrid kinases enriched in CSS-deficient classes, suggesting functional compensation for the absence of dedicated chemosensory pathways. Basal lineages retain simplified CSS (F1 or F5), whereas Actinomycetes show lineage-specific expansion into multiple classes (F5, F8, F9, and ACF), often co-occurring, indicative of enhanced sensory complexity. The phylogeny of CheA homologs shows a polyphyletic distribution, supporting a mosaic evolutionary history shaped by multiple independent acquisitions, diversification, and gene loss. Collectively, our findings show that, unlike motile bacteria, members of Actinomycetota rely predominantly on TCS-driven regulatory networks, with CSS retained only in select lineages where ecological demands require enhanced environmental sensing. This work provides a phylum-wide evolutionary framework for the emergence, diversification, and functional specialization of CSS in non-motile bacteria.

papers.title: ATF3 Preserves Macrophage Cholesterol Homeostasis during Metabolic Stress
papers.abstract: Background: Macrophages must coordinate immune activation with maintenance of cellular cholesterol homeostasis, yet the transcriptional mechanisms integrating these processes remain incompletely understood. Activating transcription factor 3 (ATF3) suppresses inflammatory and interferon responses and has been implicated in macrophage lipid metabolism, suggesting a role in coordinating immune and sterol-responsive transcriptional programs. Methods: Wild-type and ATF3-deficient bone marrow-derived macrophages were analyzed by bulk RNA sequencing following Toll-like receptor stimulation and under conditions of sterol loading or depletion. Cholesterol content, cytokine production, and sterol-responsive gene expression were quantified. Human metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) datasets and Kupffer cell-specific ATF3 knockout mice were used to assess disease relevance in vivo. Results: ATF3 deficiency enhanced inflammatory and interferon-responsive transcriptional programs while suppressing a sterol-responsive gene module enriched for SREBP2 target genes. This phenotype was conserved across diverse Toll-like receptor stimuli and accompanied by persistent Ch25h upregulation. Despite exhibiting elevated cellular cholesterol, ATF3-deficient macrophages retained transcriptional responsiveness to sterol loading and depletion while demonstrating reduced induction of SREBP2-dependent genes across conditions. IFNAR blockade reduced interferon-responsive gene expression but did not normalize Ch25h or sterol-responsive gene expression. In contrast, CRISPR-mediated reduction of Ch25h partially restored sterol-responsive gene expression in inflammatory ATF3-deficient macrophages. In human MASLD, hepatic ATF3 expression positively correlated with disease severity. In mice, ATF3 was preferentially induced in Kupffer cells during metabolic stress, and Kupffer cell-specific deletion of ATF3 increased liver injury and Kupffer cell lipid accumulation. Conclusions: ATF3 supports sterol-responsive transcriptional programs while restraining inflammatory activation in macrophages. ATF3 loss results in elevated cellular cholesterol, impaired SREBP2-dependent gene expression, and persistent derepression of Ch25h, which contributes to but does not fully explain the sterol phenotype. These findings identify ATF3 as a coordinator of macrophage adaptation to inflammatory and metabolic stress and support a protective role for Kupffer cell ATF3 during metabolic liver disease.

papers.title: All-Atom Structure Tokenizer: AtomLM-9b for Biomolecular Structure Prediction
papers.abstract: We develop an All-atom Structure Tokenizer that compresses biomolecular geometry into discrete structural tokens and achieves high-accuracy all-atom reconstruction. A hierarchical geometric encoder and finite scalar quantization map chemical units to a shared vocabulary of 8,192 tokens, while a joint coordinate de-tokenizer reconstructs backbone, side-chain, nucleic-acid, and ligand heavy atoms. The tokenizer achieves all-atom lDDT scores of 0.832 and 0.835 on CASP14 and CASP15, respectively. Building on this tokenizer, we train AtomLM-9b, an autoregressive language model based on Qwen3.5-9B that predicts structural tokens from molecular identities and connectivity and decodes them into complete atomic structures. We demonstrate, for the first time, protein structure prediction performance comparable to AlphaFold 3 with an all-atom-tokenizer-based structural language model: on the FoldBench protein-protein task, AtomLM-9b achieves a success rate of 75.01%, compared with the published AlphaFold 3 result of 72.93%. These results establish discrete all-atom tokenization as an effective interface between high-fidelity atomic reconstruction and language-model-based structure prediction.

papers.title: Cell cycle progression and stalked cell morphogenesis in Caulobacter crescentus are regulated independently by the flagellum
papers.abstract: Bacteria colonize surfaces and form biofilms to survive in stressful environmental conditions. Many bacteria use an appendage called the flagellum to sense surface contact, and responding to these mechanical cues triggers rapid physiological changes to promote downstream attachment. Bacteria are known to secrete adhesins and alter their motility behavior to facilitate surface colonization, but these changes alone are insufficient to explain the breadth of adaptations observed in surface-attached cells. Disrupting flagellar assembly in the bacterium Caulobacter crescentus constitutively activates the surface sensing pathway, and this gain-of-function phenotype was previously used to identify a suite of flagellar signaling suppressor (fss) genes that promotes surface adhesion downstream of the flagellum. We show herein that a subset of fss genes also regulates the C. crescentus developmental program. Live-cell microscopy analysis of fss mutants identified independent sub-pathways that target stalked cell morphogenesis and cell cycle progression. We identify the predicted chemotaxis genes fssD and fssE as novel regulators of stalked cell morphogenesis and show that these genes act to stimulate the diguanylate cyclase PleD in flagellar assembly mutants. A separate pathway that includes the stator protein MotB and the recently characterized dNTPase FssC regulates entry into S phase downstream of the flagellum. We show that motB regulates cell cycle progression specifically in response to surface cues, and that stator-dependent cell cycle control occurs independently of c-di-GMP and CtrA. This work clarifies the downstream targets of the surface sensing network and establishes a comprehensive model for how surface sensing influences the C. crescentus developmental program.

papers.title: Pseudo-observations of longevity improve detection of resilience-associated genes in the Radiation Late Effects Cohort of rhesus macaques.
papers.abstract: Non-human primates are an ideal model for interrogating the genetic basis of human lifespan and resilience due to their long lifespan compared to other model organisms, development of similar age-related chronic conditions, and genetic similarity. However, like humans, statistical methods for modeling survival suffer from the challenges of dealing with non-proportionality of hazards, large numbers of living individuals that must be censored, and loss-to-follow-up over studies that may last a decade or more. Here we overcome these challenges through the use of pseudo-observations of Restricted Mean Survival Time as a measure of resilience to the acute challenge of radiation exposure and chronic challenges of aging and a Western-style diet in rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta) from the Wake Forest Non-Human Primate Radiation Late Effects Cohort. Our whole-exome analysis used Genome-wide Efficient Mixed Model Association (GEMMA) to identify variants associated with longevity, and a subsequent Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) highlighted the cadherin and integrin signaling pathways as central to this resilience. As dysregulation of cell adhesion and extracellular matrix signaling is central to the development of fibrosis, we tested the functional relevance of these signals using a targeted Combined Annotation Dependent Depletion (CADD) score-weighted Sequence Kernel Association Test-Optimal (SKAT-O) analysis of GSEA leading-edge genes from both the cadherin and integrin pathways. This linked variant burden in PCDHGA5, PCDHGA3, PCDHGB2, PCDHA11, and PSENEN to the severity of myocardial fibrosis, and in IBSP, PDGFD, and LAMC2 to the severity of pulmonary fibrosis observed at necropsy. Critically, we note that the genetic variants are not caused by the radiation but rather create an underlying risk for disease that is then exacerbated by the acute and persistent stressors challenging these animals' intrinsic resilience. The success of this method in identifying biologically relevant genetic variants underlying survival in animals undergoing a strong challenge to their resilience highlights not only the role of genes predisposing animals to fibrosis in lifespan, but the overall utility of pseudo-observations in overcoming the limitations of survival analyses in humans and other long-lived species.

papers.title: Quantifying Excitation-Inhibition Harmony and Its Breakdown during Epileptogenesis in a Spiking Neural Network of the Hippocampal CA1
papers.abstract: Epileptogenesis is often linked to disruptions in excitation-inhibition (E-I) balance, yet its quantitative characterization remains limited. Understanding and quantifying this E-I balance could enable earlier diagnosis and targeted treatment of epilepsy. We investigate competitive E-I harmony and its breakdown using a biologically grounded spiking neural network model of hippocampal CA1 that incorporates two structural pathological mechanisms: pyramidal cell (PC) axonal sprouting and loss of inhibitory interneurons. As recurrent excitatory connectivity increases via PC axonal sprouting or inhibitory interneuron populations decline through interneuron loss, the network undergoes sequential transitions from a healthy phase (HP) to an interictal pathological phase (IIP) and finally to an ictal pathological phase (IP). At the input level, we introduce the competition degree, Cd (= SE / SI), as the ratio of the strengths of excitatory (SE) to inhibitory (SI) synaptic inputs to PCs, to quantify their competitive E-I harmony. As an input-side indicator, Cd remains near 2.6 in HP, exhibits a discontinuous, abrupt jump to ~ 60 at the HP [->] IIP transition and rises further thereafter. At the output level, the corresponding output-side measure, the population-averaged mean firing rate (MFR) of PCs, < fi(PC) >, also exhibits a discontinuous, abrupt jump from ~ 4 to ~ 200 Hz at the HP [->] IIP transition and rises further thereafter, indicating progressive pathological hyperexcitability. Together, these results establish a cause-and-effect framework linking the input-side indicator Cd (cause) to the output-side measure < fi(PC) > (effect). Accordingly, Cd may serve as a potential quantitative biomarker of competitive E-I harmony and its breakdown, providing a computational causal framework that links structural pathological mechanisms to epileptogenic state transitions and offering potential for translation into diagnostic tools and therapeutic applications.

papers.title: Serotonin Reuptake Inhibition Reduces NMDAR-Associated Reward Liability Without Compromising Rapid Antidepressant Efficacy
papers.abstract: Ketamine has changed the treatment landscape for depression by providing rapid antidepressant effects, yet its clinical utility remains limited by psychotomimetic effects and abuse potential. It remains unclear whether rapid antidepressant efficacy can be dissociated from mesolimbic dopamine activation and its associated reward-related effects. Here, we show that the serotonin reuptake inhibitor escitalopram, by enhancing serotonergic signaling, attenuates S-ketamine-induced dopamine (DA) release in the nucleus accumbens (NAc). Inspired by this finding, we designed and evaluated VV147 by incorporating SERT inhibition into NMDAR antagonism to reduce the reward-related liability of NMDAR blockade. Unlike S-ketamine, VV147 did not increase NAc dopamine signaling but retained rapid antidepressant effects in chronic stress models of depression. Together, these findings suggest a potential dissociation between rapid antidepressant efficacy and acute dopamine activation, providing a possible strategy for developing rapid-acting antidepressants with reduced dopamine-related reward effects.

papers.title: An anatomical and day-night atlas links cochlear immunity to adjacent bone marrow
papers.abstract: The cochlea lies within marrow-bearing bone. How this neighbouring marrow relates to cochlear immunity and daily physiology remains poorly resolved. We profiled 160,643 cells from mouse cochlea and adjacent temporal-bone marrow at six times of day, with rhythm inference calibrated for one pooled sample per time. Three-dimensional confocal reconstruction mapped vascular connections between marrow and cochlea and localized neutrophils along this interface. Neutrophils also occupied healthy cochlear fluids. Parabiosis findings were consistent with a local marrow contribution to cochlear immunity. Structural cochlear cells maintained synchronized, light-entrained clocks. Cochlear neutrophil programmes aligned with circulating neutrophils and opposed those in marrow, with independent flow cytometry supporting daily changes in immune composition and CXCR4. A shared night-associated heat-shock programme was attenuated after noise in an independent cohort. These anatomical and temporal data provide a reference for testing local marrow supply and the origins of cochlear immune rhythms.

papers.title: Circadian Clock Coordination of the Notch-to-Wnt Signaling Switch Promotes Regenerative Myogenesis
papers.abstract: Regenerative deficits of muscle stem cells (MuSCs) contribute to progressive muscle loss in muscular dystrophy. Successful regenerative repair requires a Notch to Wnt switch to allow MuSC expansion and myogenic differentiation, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Leveraging complementary genetic and pharmacological approaches, here we identify the circadian clock as a key regulator of the Notch to Wnt signaling transition to promote regeneration with therapeutic potential for dystrophic disease. Circadian clock activity marks cycling myogenic progenitors during muscle regeneration, and clock induction occurs in concert with Notch activation. We identify that key components of the Notch pathway are direct transcriptional targets of the clock that were induced by clock activation. Mechanistically, clock coordination of Notch and Wnt signaling promoted MuSC proliferative expansion while facilitating myogenic progression during regeneration. Importantly, this clock-regulated mechanism was preserved in dystrophin-deficient mouse and human myoblasts, and clock-activating compounds enhanced regenerative myogenesis in dystrophic muscle. Collectively, our findings uncover a circadian clock-controlled mechanism that orchestrates regenerative signaling transition with potential for therapeutic targeting to restore regenerative capacity in dystrophic disease.

papers.title: sPLA2 inhibitor-loaded nanoparticles mitigate spontaneous osteoarthritis in guinea pigs
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease lacking effective disease-modifying therapies. Secreted phospholipase A2 (sPLA2), a key upstream regulator of inflammatory lipid mediators, has been implicated in OA pathogenesis, but its therapeutic potential in age-related OA remains unclear. Here, we evaluated the role of sPLA2 and the efficacy of nanoparticle-mediated sPLA2 inhibition in a spontaneous OA model using female Dunkin-Hartley (DH) guinea pigs. We first characterized OA progression and observed age-dependent increases in cartilage degeneration, synovitis, oxidative stress, and sPLA2 expression and enzymatic activity. We then developed sPLA2 inhibitor (thioetheramide-PC)-loaded nanoparticles (sPLA2i-NPs) and demonstrated their superior ability, compared to free inhibitor, to prevent IL-1{beta}-induced cartilage degeneration in guinea pig cartilage explants. In vivo, intra-articular administration of sPLA2i-NPs from 3 months of age significantly attenuated cartilage destruction, synovial inflammation, and osteophyte formation in 7- and 10-month-old guinea pigs. These structural improvements were accompanied by normalization of anabolic and catabolic gene expression and a marked reduction in synovial fluid sPLA2 activity. Importantly, longitudinal gait analysis revealed that sPLA2i-NP treatment preserved limb loading, propulsion, and locomotor performance, demonstrating functional recovery. No systemic toxicity was observed following long-term treatment. Collectively, our findings identify sPLA2 as a key driver of spontaneous OA and establish nanoparticle-mediated sPLA2 inhibition as a promising disease-modifying strategy for age-related OA.

papers.title: Comparing apples to oranges from photoreceptors to inferior temporal cortex through neural manifolds
papers.abstract: In the neural processing of color, cone photoreceptor outputs are combined over successive stages to form inferior temporal cortex (IT) cells with narrower color tuning and more diverse peak preferences. To understand the benefits of these transformations, we explored the capability of photoreceptor, retinal ganglion cell and IT population responses to distinguish between pairs of natural fruits and vegetables, based solely on their color distributions extracted from hyperspectral images. Simulations with realistic Poisson response variability show that linear separations are possible for many more pairs by IT neurons. Shapes of low-dimensional manifolds extracted from neural population responses explain the improvement.

papers.title: Targeting distinct neuronal populations with AAV vectors reveals neurogenesis-associated anxiolytic effects of JNK inhibition
papers.abstract: c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) regulates stress responses and affective behaviour, but the neural populations mediating these effects remain unclear. Here, we delivered a nucleus-targeted JNK inhibitor to the mouse brain using blood-brain barrier-crossing adeno-associated virus vectors with distinct cellular tropisms. JNK inhibition produced strikingly different behavioural outcomes depending on the neuronal populations targeted. Only AAV-PHP.eB-hSyn1-mediated delivery reproduced the previously reported anxiolytic phenotype, whereas AAV.CAP-B10-hSyn1 increased locomotor activity and depressive-like behaviour and AAV.CAP-B10-mDlx reduced locomotion while enhancing object recognition memory. The anxiolytic response was accompanied by reduced hilar mossy cell abundance and an approximately two-fold increase in doublecortin-positive newborn granule neurons in the dentate gyrus. Notably, this phenotype mirrors our previous findings following selective JNK inhibition in adult hippocampal progenitor cells, implicating the neurogenic niche as a convergent substrate for anxiolytic responses to JNK inhibition. Proteomic analysis of plasma extracellular vesicles revealed widespread alterations in metabolic and inflammatory proteins upon JNK inhibition, despite neuron-restricted transgene expression. Together, these findings demonstrate that the behavioural and systemic consequences of JNK inhibition depend critically on the neural populations targeted and identify hippocampal neurogenesis-associated circuits involving mossy cells as candidate mediators of JNK-dependent anxiety regulation.

papers.title: Glycolysis and interferon transcription in melanoma immunotherapy
papers.abstract: Glycolysis and interferon signalling have both been associated with responses to PD-1 blockade, but their joint transcriptional relationship with treatment outcome remains uncertain. We examined whether a state with high glycolysis and low interferon- response was associated with reduced disease control in melanoma. Fixed Hallmark gene sets were scored by single-sample gene set enrichment analysis in GSE91061, GSE78220 and an additional Liu cohort. Disease control analyses included 47, 26 and 100 patients. Conditional odds ratios for the joint state were 6.06 (exact 95% confidence interval, 1.04 to 65.61), 0.35 (0.026 to 3.11) and 1.03 (0.39 to 2.73), respectively. Holm-adjusted P values for the two initial comparisons were 0.073 and 0.365. The additional exploratory P value was 1.000. Continuous models and analyses that omitted each patient in turn did not provide consistent evidence of an adverse association. IFN scores were negatively correlated with DNA-derived tumour purity in 102 patients (Spearman {rho} = -0.671). Among 40 patients with paired biopsies, disease control was associated with higher on-treatment IFN scores after baseline adjustment, although the paired subset had lower baseline glycolysis than patients without paired profiles. In patient-level single-cell analyses, the baseline CD8 T cell correlation weakened when an alternative rank score used a common gene background. The defined joint state was not consistently associated with poorer disease control across cohorts. Bulk IFN scores were related to tumour purity, and cellular correlations were sensitive to scoring choices. These transcriptomic results do not measure pyruvate concentration, glycolytic flux or STAT1 pyruvylation.

papers.title: Mapping and longitudinal imaging of potentiated synapses in the mouse hippocampus using SynActive-eGRASP
papers.abstract: Identifying individual synapses that undergo long-term potentiation following learning at specific circuits remains a major challenge in neuroscience. To address this problem, we developed SA-eGRASP, a genetically encoded reporter that combines SynActive (SA) targeting with enhanced GFP Reconstitution Across Synaptic Partners (eGRASP). SA drives the expression of the postsynaptic half of eGRASP at potentiated spines via the 5' and 3' untranslated regions (UTRs) of the immediate-early gene Arc, thus enabling selective labeling of individual synapses that are both structurally connected and have undergone potentiation through transsynaptic GFP reconstitution. Here, we validated SA-eGRASP and combined it with high-resolution optical imaging to generate a detailed map of hippocampal CA3-CA1 synapses subjected to potentiation following contextual fear conditioning in mice. The high signal-to-noise ratio of SA-eGRASP, allowed us to track individual potentiated dendritic spines over the course of several days, to investigate the long-term dynamics of CA3-CA1 potentiated dendritic spines, and to study the selective potentiation of a subset of spines upon experience. SA-eGRASP paves the way to the investigation of synaptic engrams by enabling longitudinal, circuit-specific investigation of synapses potentiated during learning in mice performing naturalistic behaviors.

papers.title: PEEK: integrated primer design for silent-mutation and restriction-site engineering, validated in silico and by whole-plasmid sequencing
papers.abstract: Motivation: Silent introduction of restriction sites, direct site insertion, and verification of the result are routine operations in molecular cloning, yet they are typically distributed across separate tools built on inconsistent thermodynamics. Primer design is itself mature and heavily validated; the gap is not accuracy in principle but integration, together with the absence of any explicit account of why one synonymous edit should be preferred over another. Because melting temperature (Tm) gates which primers a tool will accept, any unified tool must first be shown to compute Tm correctly against an external standard, and then shown to produce the edits it proposes. Results: PEEK, a web-based toolkit, unifies silent-mutation discovery, restriction-site insertion, and amplification and screening primer design built on a single thermodynamic model of primer melting temperature (Tm). PEEK's silent-mutation engine identifies the smallest set of synonymous changes required to form a restriction site at a specific position, and ranks the options by codon usage, local mRNA folding, and edit size. Predicted melting temperatures closely matched those of the NEB Q5 Tm Calculator across 17 primers of varying length and GC content (Pearson R^2 = 0.9995, mean absolute error 1.32 C) without any fitted correction, and annealing-temperature (Ta) recommendations exactly matched NEB's rules. In independent trials, a total of 15 silent-mutation designs were translationally silent and contained the intended restriction site. Experimental validation was performed by installing a KpnI site into a 9.9 kb lentiviral CAR plasmid using both a silent-mutation primer and an insertion primer. Whole-plasmid sequencing confirmed that each primer introduced exactly the designed changes, with no off-target differences across the construct and no change to the encoded protein. Availability and implementation: PEEK runs at https://peekbiology.com and requires no registration. Source code, documentation, and test data are available at https://github.com/nkura-arch/PEEK-Protein-Engineering Efficiency-Kit. Implemented in Python 3.11 with Flask, Biopython, and ViennaRNA. Contact: nathan.singh@wustl.edu

papers.title: Changes in anterior cingulate connectivity associated with response to antidepressant treatment for major depressive disorder
papers.abstract: Background: Resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) involving the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and the hippocampal formation has been implicated in major depressive disorder (MDD) and antidepressant response. However, it remains unclear whether connectivity changes in distinct ACC subdivisions and hippocampal formation reflect general antidepressant effects or are specifically associated with clinical improvement. Methods: Forty-one, unmedicated adults with MDD underwent functional MRI before and after 8 weeks of sertraline or bupropion treatment. Seed-based rsFC analyses examined subgenual ACC (sgACC), pregenual ACC (pgACC), dorsal ACC (dACC), and hippocampal formation connectivity. Linear mixed-effects models tested whether connectivity change was associated with treatment response, remission, and dimensional improvement in depressive symptoms. Results: Thirty individuals (73.2%) responded to treatment and 26 (63.4%) achieved remission. Overall, rsFC decreased pre- to post-treatment between (1) dACC and pgACC (but not sgACC and hippocampal formation) and (2) cortical regions primarily involving default mode and frontoparietal networks. When considering treatment response, differences in sgACC and pgACC connectivity with temporal and inferior frontal regions emerged (increased in responders vs. decreased in non-responders). Remission was similarly associated with increased sgACC connectivity with temporal and prefrontal regions, and increased sgACC connectivity with temporal cortical regions related to greater reductions in depressive symptoms. Conclusions: Antidepressant treatment was associated with distinct patterns of ACC connectivity change, with general reductions in dorsal and pregenual connectivity but increases in subgenual and pregenual connectivity associated with favorable clinical outcomes. Findings suggest that changes in sgACC/pgACC connectivity are particularly relevant to antidepressant treatment response. Keywords: Major depressive disorder; Resting-state functional connectivity; Anterior cingulate cortex; Antidepressant treatment; Treatment response; Subgenual anterior cingulate cortex.

papers.title: THiRST: Computer Vision Empowered Three-dimensional High-Resolution Spatial Transcriptomics Analytics
papers.abstract: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics (ST) preserves gene expression within tissue architecture but remains limited to individual two-dimensional (2D) sections, restricting analysis of continuous three-dimensional (3D) structures and cross-section consistency. We present THiRST, a computational framework for reconstructing multi-resolution 3D spatial transcriptomic representations from serial sections. THiRST combines coarse-to-fine morphology-guided registration, spatial matching of ST units, cross-section association of segmented structures, and integration of Visium V2 and high-definition ST. In serial kidney sections, patch-level refinement increased the same-cluster proportions of matched units at adjacent offsets from 63.8% and 65.6% to 70.7% and 70.0%, respectively, while improving expression concordance. The reconstructed correspondences enabled 3D glomerular and object-level expression analysis, with 54.1% of differential genes detected only in 3D. Cross-platform integration further aligned V2 and high-definition measurements in a shared expression space. THiRST demonstrates the feasibility of object-level 3D ST analysis from serial 2D sections and underscores the importance of accurate local registration.

papers.title: Causal Multiscale Modeling of Ocular FLASH Electroretinography: Model Development, Experimental Fitting, and Spin-Glass--Percolation Predictions
papers.abstract: \textbf{Purpose:} To develop a causal multiscale model of retinal electroretinography (ERG) after ocular ultrahigh-dose-rate (FLASH) and conventional-dose-rate (CONV) irradiation, evaluate the framework against published ocular ERG data, and derive prospective dose-response predictions for future validation. \textbf{Methods:} The retina was coarse-grained into $N=200$ functional modules. Local rate equations were formulated as Hodgkin--Huxley-inspired conductance-balance/RC reductions of retinal ion-channel and synaptic pathways. Radiation generated an injury field that altered phototransduction, a-wave and b-wave dynamics and, in the network extension, inter-module coupling and bond survival. A reduced amplitude benchmark and nested M0/M1/M2 causal models were evaluated. \textbf{Results:} The reduced benchmark achieved $R^2=0.9721$ and RMSE $=11.94~\mu$V. M0, M1, and M2 yielded $R^2=0.8546$, 0.8559, and 0.8560, respectively, indicating limited independent identifiability of the network terms from amplitude data alone. Under an exploratory 50\% retained-gain criterion, the reduced benchmark predicted a-wave preservation thresholds of 28.6 Gy for FLASH and 23.7 Gy for CONV, and b-wave thresholds of 29.2 Gy and 24.1 Gy, respectively, corresponding to a model-based functional dose-modifying factor (DMF) of 1.21. \textbf{Conclusion:} The ERG amplitude data support the causal radiation-injury-to-ERG framework, while additional observables will be needed to distinguish the predicted collective-network contributions. The model also provides quantitative dose targets for prospective studies of the FLASH retinal-preservation window and a framework for testing how local retinal injury may propagate into collective dysfunction.

papers.title: A Neurocompliant Ionic Conductive Hydrogel Orchestrates Glial and Vascular Remodeling to Mitigate Traumatic Brain Injury
papers.abstract: Developing conductive scaffolds for neural regeneration is often hindered by the cytotoxicity and mechanical mismatch inherent to conventional electronic fillers. Here, we report an ultrasoft ionically conductive hydrogel engineered by grafting choline-based bioionic liquids (BIL) onto fish gelatin (FiBGel). Systematic optimization yields brain-mimetic conductivity (0.25-0.68 S/m), elastic moduli (0.6-0.9 kPa), and physiological water content (72-81%). In 3D culture, the matrix drives spontaneous neurogenesis, achieving ~90% MAP2+ neurons with robust calcium signaling, while concurrently supporting endothelial network formation. We report the first intracerebral administration of a BIL hydrogel, demonstrating remarkable biocompatibility and immunomodulation. In a traumatic brain injury model, a single FiBGel dose halves reactive astrogliosis, enhances cortical revascularization, and limits lesion cavity expansion. Leveraging an FDA-recognized micronutrient, FiBGel offers a translatable strategy that integrates neuromechanics, conductivity, immune modulation, and vascular support within one injectable scaffold for minimally invasive treatment of brain injuries.

papers.title: Skeletal muscle aging drives sex- and compartment-specific protein insolubility that is modifiable by proteostasis-directed treatments
papers.abstract: Protein aggregation and altered protein solubility indicate proteostatic decline, yet their roles in skeletal muscle aging remain poorly understood. We combined light and electron microscopy, quantitative proteomics, and stable-isotope labeling of skeletal muscle to investigate age-associated changes in protein insolubility, and their responses to exercise and rapamycin. Aged muscle accumulated distinct aggresome and amyloid-positive aggregates despite unchanged bulk insoluble protein content. Instead, aging altered the abundance and soluble-insoluble shifts of lower-abundance proteins across cellular components, particularly mitochondrial, nuclear and extracellular matrix proteins, with greater changes in females. These changes were not broadly explained by intrinsic protein aggregation propensity. Exercise and rapamycin partially reversed age-associated changes in abundance and partitioning without increasing protein synthesis. Together, these findings highlight sex- and cellular component-dependent changes in protein insolubility as important, modifiable aspects of skeletal muscle proteostasis, and indicate that proteostatic maintenance may be a more important target than anabolism for muscle aging.

papers.title: Unveiling immune targets via TriStageHLA: high-throughput screening of peptide presentation, peptide-HLA binding, and immunogenicity
papers.abstract: High-throughput screening of HLA class I epitopes underpins neoantigen vaccine design, T cell therapies, and pathogen immune monitoring, yet proteome-scale prioritization remains challenging under severe class imbalance. We present TriStageHLA, a compact three-stage framework that decomposes epitope discovery into peptide-only screening (PRE), allele-specific binding/presentation prediction (BIND), and immunogenicity prediction (IM). PRE performs early pruning via a LoRA-adapted ESM-2 classifier; BIND integrates quantitative binding affinity and eluted ligand data with a dual-branch architecture combining global cross-attention and local motif extraction; IM is fine-tuned on curated human T-cell assay data with a decoupled LoRA head. Trained on IEDB-derived datasets with per-allele balancing and allele-discordant supervision, TriStageHLA-BIND achieves AUROC of 96.2% and AUPRC of 95.2% on combined BA/EL evaluation, while TriStageHLA-IM reaches AUROC of 81.4\% and AUPRC of 73.8\% on held-out immunogenicity data, improving over the strongest immunogenicity baselines ImmuneApp (70.7% / 63.6%) and BigMHC-IM (60.1% / 51.5%). With substantially fewer trainable parameters than prior models, TriStageHLA enables efficient, calibrated epitope prioritization across binding, presentation, and immunogenicity. Code and pretrained weights are available at https://github.com/SkywalkerLuke/TriStageHLA.

papers.title: MaaD-TAD: an all-atom model of the duplicated PRAMEF/HNRNPCL chromatin domain built from sequence homology
papers.abstract: In the nucleus, the placement of genes in the 3D fold of DNA affects how they function. Models of this fold use two kinds of data: contact maps constructed from Hi-C, and nucleosome maps showing where DNA is wound around nucleosomes. Over evolution, sections of the genome were copied, creating near-identical regions. Reads from these regions cannot be assigned to one copy and are discarded, leaving "void regions" in both maps. We tested MaaD-TAD, a pipeline that models topologically associating domains (TADs) at the atomic level, on the PRAMEF/HNRNPCL locus on human chromosome 1. This challenging locus spans 652 kb, with only 15% of its nucleosome positions known and most contact data missing. To test our hypothesis that copies with similar sequence lie close in space, i.e. homology as a surrogate for proximity, we constructed a map of sequence homology in place of Hi-C and used CSynth to fold it into a 3D path. We then lengthened the path to fit a chromatin fibre, and refined the model by adding cohesin complexes, which stabilize chromatin structure. Cohesin is a ring-shaped protein complex through which a loop of chromatin is threaded; the loop is commonly anchored by CTCF proteins bound on either leg. Using known databases, we placed CTCF sites in our model and joined three to their copies with cohesin rings; in each pair the sites face each other, as loop anchors do. The final model holds 3,359 nucleosomes and about 55 million atoms. Micro-C, an advanced, higher-resolution form of Hi-C, provided data on two other duplicated regions that support our hypothesis: matching copies touched 1.2 to 1.9 times more often than expected. Our approach provides a novel method to reconstruct DNA regions with absent contact data and, to our knowledge, the first all-atom model of a complete TAD.

papers.title: Low-fidelity simulator selection for multi-fidelity inference of epithelial vertex models
papers.abstract: Vertex models link cell division, neighbour exchange, and intercellular forces to epithelial tissue form through parameters such as junctional line tension and perimeter contractility. Bayesian inference of these parameters from data quantifies their uncertainty, but for stochastic models of proliferating tissues it requires many costly simulations. Multi-fidelity simulation-based inference reduces this cost by training on many runs of a cheaper, less accurate ('low-fidelity') simulator before refining with a few full ('high-fidelity') runs. Low-fidelity versions can be constructed in several ways, for example by stopping simulations early, coarsening the timestep, or averaging fewer replicates, but it is unclear which to choose before committing to costly training. To address this, we introduce PRISM (Paired Ranking Index for Simulator Matching), a screen that compares each candidate with the full simulator on paired runs, scoring agreement in cell-packing statistics against cost. For a vertex model of a proliferating tissue, PRISM flags stopping early as unreliable before training; once trained, this choice can produce confidently wrong parameter estimates. By contrast, a coarser timestep, within the range tested, is cheap and accurate; while fewer replicates are accurate but too costly. Using a screened low-fidelity simulator, multi-fidelity inference outperforms approximate Bayesian computation and neural-network inference trained on full simulations alone, at matched cost and with well-calibrated uncertainty. The same pattern recurs for a second vertex model fitted to published Drosophila pupal-wing imaging data, although there stopping halfway proves safe. Together, our findings suggest that which approximations are safe depends on the model, and that screening them before training makes multi-fidelity inference of tissue mechanics practical.

papers.title: MELD: Mutation Effect Learning through Differential embeddings
papers.abstract: We introduce MELD (Mutation Effect Learning through Differential Embeddings), a compact model for predicting the functional consequences of single nucleotide variants (SNVs) by training directly on the wild-type (WT) versus mutant differential. Interpreting SNVs is central to clinical genomics, yet experimental characterization cannot scale to millions of observed variants. Leading sequence-to-function models (Enformer, Borzoi, AlphaGenome) are trained on absolute genomic tracks and score variants post hoc through in-silico mutagenesis (ISM), so the WT-mutant difference never enters the training loss. MELD instead places the logit difference {Delta}z = zmut - zwt inside the supervised objective. It combines a shared CNN-Transformer encoder, a mutant-specific mutation-mask boost, multiscale mutation-centered pooling, and a learned adaptive amplification factor . On ClinVar (1.57M variants), MELD (1.9M parameters) reached an AUROC of 0.986 versus 0.800 for a same-data, same-backbone ISM baseline, with ablations confirming the contribution of each component. On a shared benchmark, it outperformed frozen foundation models with 3-1,300x more parameters (AUROC 0.967 vs. 0.924 for AlphaGenome and 0.936 for Nucleotide Transformer). With only 50, 000 training variants, it exceeded the ISM baseline trained on all 1.48M (AUROC 0.903 vs. 0.796) variants. On BRCA1 saturation genome editing, frozen MELD achieved a Spearman {rho} of 0.42, above Borzoi (0.40), and ClinVar transfer raised it to 0.45. These results demonstrate that direct differential supervision is a compact, data-efficient alternative to post-hoc ISM scoring with substantially larger pretrained models.

papers.title: RCDome: A Multi-Database Human Gene Atlas of Regulated Cell Death
papers.abstract: Introduction: Regulated cell death (RCD) governs tissue homeostasis, development, and disease, and is executed or regulated by specific genes. Yet for the researcher asking which genes execute or regulate a given RCD form, the answer is rarely simple: gene lists for the same form rarely agree across databases, many associations carry no traceable source, and most have never been systematically checked against primary literature. We built RCDome to answer the most basic question a researcher can ask: where did this gene-RCD association come from, and what is the evidence? Methods: RCDome is a multi-database human gene atlas built through a staged architecture integrating multi-source compilation, literature validation and evidence recovery, mechanistic classification, human-governed ontological adjudication, and web deployment. Five complementary evidence channels (PubMed Boolean search, curated databases, AI-assisted screening, manual curation, and Elicit systematic review) were integrated from 20 public databases into a unified matrix. Sixty-two original name strings were canonicalized into 53 RCD-related entities with curator-adjudicated operational definitions and ontological levels. Gene-RCD associations were systematically evaluated through an independent DeepSeek two-call LLM validation, Europe PMC full-text recovery and deep evidence extraction, an independent Consensus literature-search channel, and GPT-4o arbitration of disagreements. Source-grounding controls rejected extracted evidence not found verbatim in the source document, while the governance contract was enforced as executable code. Results: The compendium holds 22,473 association rows spanning 9,265 unique HGNC-validated genes (21,568 unique gene-RCD pairs). Evidence-first adjudication resolved 5,138 pairs (23.8%) as mechanistically involved; across the 4,775 role-resolved pairs, 225 (4.7%) are executors, 4,455 (93.3%) are regulators, and 95 are markers, revealing a small death-executing core embedded in a vast regulatory network. Under a separate seven-class mechanistic criterion applied to all 22,473 rows, only 3,063 (13.6%) were mechanistically confirmed and 286 (1.3%) were database-only with no verifiable paper trail. Conclusion: RCDome makes the RCD evidence landscape measurable and traceable, showing that AI-assisted curation can be verifiable, human-governed, and explicit about uncertainty. It is delivered as a Shiny web application that lets any researcher query the atlas and inspect the evidence behind each association. Availability: RCDome is freely available at https://rcdome.org/ (source code and data at https://github.com/BioCancerInformatics/RCDome).

papers.title: AOPTK: Open-Source Software for AI-Assisted Toxicological Literature Analysis
papers.abstract: Motivation: Toxicologists today face a challenge: although vast amounts of data describing how chemicals affect human health are available across scientific publications and regulatory reports, much of this information remains underutilized because extracting and interpreting evidence across thousands of studies is impractical to perform manually. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in large language models (LLMs), provide new opportunities to automate toxicological literature analysis. Results: Herein, we present the Adverse Outcome Pathway Toolkit (AOPTK), an open-source Python package for AI-enhanced analysis of toxicological and biomedical literature. AOPTK supports (i) automated literature retrieval from databases such as PubMed Central and Europe PMC, (ii) direct processing of full-text articles in PDF format, and (iii) LLM-assisted analysis tools to identify chemicals and extract their relationships to biological effects under user-defined conditions. We demonstrate its utilities through a case-study identifying potential non-genotoxic carcinogens based on their ability to inhibit gap junction intercellular communication (GJIC). The LLM-enhanced analysis achieves 81% agreement with an expert-curated inhibitor list and 95% accuracy in predicting inhibition versus no inhibition when analysing the same subset of 86 publications. Automated retrieval and analysis of 1 124 publications from PubMed Central further demonstrated the feasibility of applying AOPTK to large-scale literature analyses. Availability: The package is developed open source on GitHub, disseminated through PyPI and Bioconda and releases are archived on Zenodo. Individual tools are available in the Galaxy platform for accessible data analysis with user-friendly, findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable (FAIR) and end-to-end workflows provided via WorkflowHub. The tools are available on usegalaxy.eu and usegalaxy.cz and are developed open source on GitHub.

papers.title: Distinguishing evidence accumulation from choice confidence in neural signatures of perceptual decision making
papers.abstract: Human electrophysiology research has identified the centro-parietal positivity (CPP) as an apparent neural correlate of sensory evidence accumulation during perceptual decision-making. The CPP has also been shown to closely scale with subjective confidence. Coupled with the fact of its domain-generality and lack of choice selectivity, this observation raises the possibility that the CPP might in fact trace subjective confidence rather than cumulative evidence, two quantities that are closely correlated in most experiments. To disentangle confidence from cumulative evidence, we used predictive cues with 80% validity to manipulate prior expectations of participants during a contrast discrimination task while recording electroencephalography (EEG). At the time of decision termination, confidence is expected to reach a higher level for validly cued versus invalidly cued choices, whereas the opposite would be expected of a cumulative evidence signal due to biased decision starting points. As expected, valid cues led to faster, more accurate and more confident responses compared to invalid and neutral cues. At the neural level, cues produced systematic increases in preparation of the expected action prior to evidence onset as indexed by premotor mu/beta activity, consistent with cue-biased criterion adjustments. The pre-response CPP amplitude was significantly reduced for validly cued choices and the effect remained even when matching for confidence. Together these findings suggest that the CPP is not a direct read-out of subjective confidence, but an evidence accumulation signal that contributes to both decision formation and confidence estimation.

papers.title: mFrag: Integrating External DNA Methylation References Improves Lung Cancer Early Detection by Fragmentomics
papers.abstract: Fragmentomics analyzes features of circulating cell-free DNA fragments (e.g., fragment length or end motifs) derived from whole-genome sequencing of liquid biopsy samples (blood or other body fluids), enabling non-invasive early cancer detection. Here we present mFrag, a framework that integrates external methylation reference atlases with fragmentomic features for lung cancer detection. mFrag comprises two complementary methods: mFrag-Weight, which uses DNA methylation information to weight fragmentomic features, and mFrag-Net, which integrates fragmentomic features and external DNA methylation data through neural networks. We average the output probabilities of the two methods to obtain a final prediction score. The mFrag model was trained using 287 individuals at risk for lung cancer. In an independent case-control testing set comprising 385 non-cancer controls and 46 cancers (28 stage I, 12 stage II, and 6 stage III or IV), mFrag outperforms a DELFI-style fragmentomic approach, improving PR-AUC from 0.455 to 0.720 and sensitivity at 99% specificity from 0.043 to 0.478, with ROC-AUC from 0.871 to 0.908. For stage I lung cancer, mFrag raises PR-AUC from 0.314 to 0.558 and ROC-AUC from 0.855 to 0.894. Applied to end 4-mer motif features, mFrag likewise improved over an unweighted baseline, with gains contributed by both mFrag-Weight and mFrag-Net.
