We show that highly asymmetric polar growth generates a short daughter cell and a longer mother cell at each division. Nucleoid compaction and positioning change across growth phases, culminating in a highly compacted, asymmetrically positioned nucleoid in stationary phase. ParB presents a subpolar localization, at the nucleoid periphery. Despite this pronounced cellular asymmetry and the presence of a single large chromosome, chromosome conformation capture reveals a global chromosome organization similar to that of bacteria undergoing conventional binary fission Together, these findings uncover a distinctive cell cycle program in Bradyrhizobium. showing that such extreme asymmetry in growth and division, significantly different from closely related characterized -Proteobacteriota, is compatible with conserved principles of chromosome organization.

papers.title: Microscale nonrandomness revisited: An overlooked predictor of ecological change
papers.abstract: Abrupt ecological transitions have driven the development of early warning signal metrics that track how ecological systems respond as external conditions gradually change and systems approach transitions between states. However, their generality and applicability remain uncertain, particularly for short-term ecological dynamics that can occur without directional external change. To address this gap, we propose a general framework based on the hypothesis that microscale nonrandomness, quantified from frequency distributions or spatial patterns, predicts subsequent short-term rates of change in populations and interactions, as well as current macroscale ecosystem states. We applied the framework to four datasets: time series from an incubation experiment of phytoplankton-parasitic chytrid interactions; spatiotemporal field observations of leaf beetles on willow trees and aphids in a crop system; and spatial snapshot data linking soil surface characteristics with aboveground and soil ecosystem properties in a forest vegetations-soil system. We quantified microscale nonrandomness using Morisita I_{delta} from frequency distributions and Moran's I and SADIE from spatial patterns. Across all systems, models incorporating microscale nonrandomness metrics consistently showed greater cross-validated predictive performance than those based on macroscale variables or spatial averages alone. Although their relative performance varied among systems, frequency-based metrics performed as well as or better than spatially explicit metrics in some cases. The consistent improvement across contrasting systems supports the broad applicability of this framework, including under limited data conditions. This framework broadens ecological forecasting to short-term, continuous dynamics beyond those associated with directional environmental change.

papers.title: Elevated precontractile calcium set point is sustained by limited PMCA1 export in dystrophic muscle
papers.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is caused by loss of dystrophin and marked by elevated muscle calcium, usually attributed to contraction-induced membrane damage. Whether calcium rises before muscle can contract, and what sustains it, is unresolved. In Caenorhabditis elegans embryos and patient-derived human myoblasts, dystrophic muscle carries an elevated resting calcium set point before contraction is possible. Embryonic calcium is elevated 400 minutes after fertilization, before movement is detectable or the neuromuscular junction forms. Silencing the plasma membrane calcium pump gene mca-1 raises calcium in wild-type but not dystrophic animals, whereas silencing its paralogue raises it in both: the limitation is specific to that export route. Dystrophic human myoblasts have less pump; pump inhibition or silencing increases calcium preferentially in healthy cells, and raising pump expression lowers calcium most in dystrophic cells. Constrained calcium export is an early, continuing determinant of the dystrophic set point.

papers.title: Increased Cognitive Load Expands, Stabilizes, and Aligns Visual Representation Across the Human Brain
papers.abstract: Cognitive load refers to the mental effort required to perform a task. While previous research has extensively examined its detrimental effects on neural and behavioral performance, much less is known about how the brain actively adapts to heightened demands. Across two fMRI experiments involving visual n-back tasks, we identified several fundamental properties of this adaptive process. First, higher load enhanced and expanded visual representations beyond localized visual regions, leading to widespread visual coding. At the global scale, heightened load promoted cross-regional coordination by increasing representational alignment and strengthening information encoded in interregional functional connectivity patterns. Beyond facilitating stronger visual representation, increased load also reduced neural pattern variability, which led to more stable information coding. Finally, load was encoded independently of other task-relevant information as a separate brain state, supporting its overarching role in guiding visual processing. Together, these findings revealed that the brain adapts to heightened cognitive demands by globally reorganizing neural processing to support flexible cognition.

papers.title: TestNet-PA: Sampling-Zero-Aware Inference of Microbial Presence-Absence Networks
papers.abstract: Microbial presence-absence networks, also referred to as co-occurrence networks, characterize patterns of coexistence and incompatibility among taxa. However, sequencing-based presence--absence analysis can be compromised by pervasive 'sampling zeros' in microbiome data, causing widely used methods such as Fisher's exact test to identify spurious co-occurrence dependence. To our knowledge, no existing method is designed to account for sampling zeros in this setting. We introduce TestNet-PA, a method for testing pairwise microbial co-occurrence dependence. TestNet-PA models each observed zero as arising from a mixture of 'structural' and 'sampling' zeros, with the mixing probabilities governed by library size and relative abundance. Because the relative abundance underlying an observed zero is unobserved, we impute it by borrowing information from other samples. We then construct a quasi-likelihood and develop an EM algorithm to infer dependence between the underlying true presence--absence statuses. Extensive simulations based on real gut, vaginal, and oral microbiome data templates showed that TestNet-PA consistently controlled the FDR while maintaining good sensitivity. By contrast, Fisher's exact test generally yielded inflated FDR. Analyses of the three real microbiome datasets further illustrated how accounting for sampling zeros can affect the inferred co-occurrence networks.

papers.title: No Evidence of an Effect of a Single Mirror Visual Feedback Session on Subsequent Motor Imagery
papers.abstract: Motor imagery (MI) and mirror therapy, based on mirror visual feedback (MVF), are recommended as adjuncts to conventional therapies for upper limb rehabilitation after stroke. Both approaches activate sensorimotor cortical networks despite the absence of overt movement, and their concurrent application has been associated with enhanced neural activation. The present study investigated whether a single session of MVF modulates subsequent kinesthetic Motor Imagery (kMI)-related neural activity. EEG data from 38 healthy participants (MVF: n = 18; sham: n = 20) were analyzed in a mixed pre-post design. Participants performed kMI before and after either an MVF or sham intervention. Analyses focused on mu-band (8-12 Hz) event-related desynchronization (ERD) and its hemispheric lateralization. Although kMI reliably elicited stronger contralateral than ipsilateral mu ERD, MVF did not significantly affect subsequent kMI-related mu ERD or its hemispheric lateralization. These findings suggest that previously reported facilitatory effects of MVF on MI may be more closely related to concurrent application than to immediate aftereffects, while potential effects of repeated MVF exposure on subsequent MI remain to be investigated. These findings provide a foundation for future studies investigating how MVF and MI can be combined to optimize upper-limb stroke rehabilitation.

papers.title: Examining urban weed response to elevated salt levels
papers.abstract: Stressors from the urban environment cause adverse effects on city-dwelling organisms. While there is evidence that some species are adapting to urban stressors, such as the urban heat island and impervious surfaces, other stressors such as road salt are less studied. We investigated whether plants are adapting to elevated salt concentrations with two common garden experiments using three common weed species: Veronica arvensis, Stellaria media, and Lamium purpureum. We collected plants from parks around Baltimore, MD, USA, collecting plant maternal lineages from roadside soils (i.e. higher soil salinity) and inner park soils (i.e. lower soil salinity). We hypothesized that roadside lineages would tolerate salt treatment better than park lineages. In our germination experiment on wild-collected seeds, we observed a non-significant trend where the germination rate of roadside L. purpureum lineages was reduced less by salt treatment than for park genetic lineages, while S. media had similar declines between groups. In our greenhouse experiment on the F1 generation, roadside V. arvensis lineages displayed a less adverse reaction to salt treatment than park V. arvensis lineages. L. purpureum did not display this difference, but roadside lineages of both species exhibited less tissue damage overall. The results of our experiments were likely influenced by the maternal environment, and work on F2 generations is required to confirm them. Our findings show some support for urban salt tolerance adaptation, and point to the heterogeneity of the urban environment and the complexity of plant reactions to salinity.

papers.title: SARDINE unlocks EWAS summary statistics for large-scale epigenetic biomarker analysis
papers.abstract: Epigenetic clocks are increasingly used to study biological aging, yet their interpretation and utility remain uncertain. Meanwhile, the growing wealth of epigenome-wide association study (EWAS) summary statistics remains largely untapped for evaluating these biomarkers. Here, we introduce SARDINE, a statistical framework that estimates epigenetic clock-phenotype associations using EWAS summary statistics, clock weights, and reference methylation covariance, without individual-level data. SARDINE accurately reproduced individual-level association estimates across 38 epigenetic biomarkers and four phenotypes in 15,677 individuals. Applying SARDINE to diverse EWAS datasets revealed substantial heterogeneity in biomarker associations with aging, diseases, and lifestyle factors. By transforming CpG-level EWAS results into interpretable biomarker-level associations, SARDINE unlocks a largely underutilized data resource and establishes a scalable paradigm for systematic biomarker evaluation and discovery in aging research.

papers.title: Onsite fixation preserves phosphoprotein profile in human whole blood
papers.abstract: Phospho-flow cytometry is increasingly used as a pharmacodynamic readout of kinase-pathway activity, including in JAK inhibitor trials. Phosphoprotein states are intrinsically labile ex vivo and are further altered by conventional workflows, which typically involve PBMC isolation, cryopreservation, and transit times of hours to days before measurement. Here, we fix whole blood at collection and quantify six phosphoproteins by mass cytometry, benchmarked against matched cryopreserved PBMCs. Unlike PBMCs, whole blood retained neutrophils, ~75-80% of which were pSTAT3-positive at baseline. Basal pSTAT3 was also markedly higher in whole blood monocytes (~41% positive vs. ~9% in PBMCs), whereas T, B, and NK cells differed by less than 1 percentage point. Stimulation produced subset-specific phosphorylation patterns that were retained after 6 weeks of storage. Because fixation does not require centrifugation and retains neutrophils, samples can be fixed at collection sites without on-site processing laboratories and analyzed centrally in batches.

papers.title: Charting the Structure and Functional Landscape of the SF3B1 Intrinsically Disordered Region
papers.abstract: Despite its essential role in pre-mRNA splicing, the structure and functional significance of the intrinsically disordered N-terminal domain (NTD) of SF3B1, a core component of the SF3b spliceosome complex, remain poorly understood. Here, we combine nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), biochemistry, bioinformatics approaches, with molecular dynamics simulations to characterize the conformational landscape of the SF3B1-NTD and its phosphorylation-dependent remodelling. Specifically, we focus on the 186-341 region (186-341SF3B1), which contains at least four regulatory phosphorylation sites. We reveal that 186-341SF3B1 is highly dynamic, lacking a stable secondary structure, and that phosphorylation of T211, T235, T313, and T328 induces a shift toward more compact states driven by the formation of intramolecular interactions. Additionally, we unveil that 186-341SF3B1 interacts with RNA primarily via the arginine residues flaking one of the conserved tryptophan-centred motifs present within SF3B1-NTD. These interactions are transient and heterogeneous, reflecting a nonspecific yet sequence-dependent recognition mechanism. Collectively, this study provides a comprehensive description of the conformational landscape and functional features of the SF3B1-NTD, and expands the portfolio of its possible interactors, thus broadening our understanding of how intrinsic disorder, post-translational modifications, and sequence-encoded motifs cooperate to regulate pre-mRNA splicing.

papers.title: Visual surfaceomics reveals the substrate-scavenging cell surface of Asgard archaea
papers.abstract: The emergence of eukaryotes from Asgard archaeal ancestors likely required a specialized cell envelope that enabled sustained physical and metabolic interactions with proto-mitochondrial symbionts. While the protrusion-rich cell architecture of Asgard archaea may enable such interactions, the molecular composition of their cell surface and its role in establishing cell-cell contacts remains unknown. Here, we developed a "visual surfaceomics" approach, integrating subtomogram averaging, predictive structural modeling, transcriptomics, proteomics, and expansion microscopy to identify surface proteins in situ. We show that Asgard cell bodies and protrusions lack an archaea-typical paracrystalline S-layer and are instead decorated by two main classes of surface proteins: subtilisin-like serine proteases (SubSs) and oligopeptide-binding proteins (OppAs). SubSs were detected as membrane-anchored dimers and were sparsely distributed across the surface. OppAs showed near-total membrane coverage but lacked any rigid, higher order assembly. Thermal shift assays and single particle cryo-EM showed that OppA binds oligopeptides in vitro. Comparative genomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics suggest that this peptidophilic surface architecture is conserved across Asgard archaeal phyla. Finally, we discovered that the cell surface was remodeled at cell-cell contact sites. Altogether, our integrative approach revealed a metabolically specialized and structurally flexible cell surface that couples extracellular protein degradation with peptide capture and uptake, while potentially contributing to establishing and maintaining the symbiotic interactions of Asgard archaea.

papers.title: Hide and seek in a rainforest canopy : when a fruit-eating carnivore (almost) met its top predator carnivore
papers.abstract: Prey-predator interactions in the wild are spectacular. Common reported cases come from ground-dwelling animals, in open areas and by daylight. Here, we report, for the first time, a sequence with the nocturnal arboreal kinkajou (Potos flavus), being followed ca. 20 minutes apart by one of its predators, the puma (Puma concolor), 33 m aboveground in a rainforest in French Guiana.

papers.title: siRNA/mRNA payload of lipid nanoparticles quantified using fluorescence microscopy and correlation spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have emerged as the most promising vectors to deliver nucleic acids to mammalian cells. Advanced delivery strategies involving multiple nucleic acid species require a reliable determination of RNA payload and LNP size. Here, we use total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy and fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) to determine mRNA payload and siRNA/mRNA codelivered payload. Particularly, FCS proves to be a reliable method for payload determination, independently of fluorophore properties that can be altered during encapsulation. By varying the PEG-lipid fraction relative to the reference ONPATTRO formulation, we find that mRNA payload of enhanced green fluorescent protein (eGFP) coding mRNA increases from [~]10 with LNP size according to a power law with an exponent 1.3. Cryogenic electron microscopy (Cryo-EM) reveals that in this case blebs occur more frequently in small LNPs. For siRNA/mRNA coencapsulation the siRNA fraction within LNPs exceeds that in the initial RNA mixture, suggesting that coencapsulation is competitive and constrained by nucleic acid diffusion. Together, our findings highlight the importance of particle size and encapsulation kinetics in controlling the loading and composition of RNA payloads in LNPs.

papers.title: Multicellular Perturb-seq Reveals Lineage-Specific Transcriptional Control During Human Cardiac Organoid Development
papers.abstract: Heart development requires the coordinated differentiation of multiple cell lineages, including cardiomyocytes (CMs) and endothelial cells (ECs). Transcription factors (TFs) orchestrate lineage specification, morphogenesis, and maturation, yet how cardiac and vascular TFs shape multicellular organization and their interactions remain poorly understood. Many TFs exhibit pleiotropic and stage-dependent effects across cardiac lineages, particularly in cardiac progenitor cells, suggesting the presence of shared regulatory networks that synchronize cardiac and vascular programs during development and in response to stress. Human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) differentiated cardiac organoid provides a physiologically relevant 3D model to study these multicellular interactions, enabling simultaneous differentiation of ECs and CMs within a human genetic context. When combined with CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) based Perturb-seq, this system allows systematic, high-throughput dissection of TF-driven regulatory programs at single-cell resolution. In this study, we investigated how cardiac and vascular TFs coordinate lineage commitment and the cross-lineage signaling in human cardiovascular differentiation.

papers.title: Generalizable sex differences in functional brain organization follow the cortical hierarchy in youth
papers.abstract: It remains unknown if sex differences in human functional connectivity follow a generalizable overarching principle. Here, we tested whether sex differences in functional connectivity during childhood and adolescence are organized along the sensorimotor-association (S-A) axis, a cortical hierarchy spanning unimodal sensorimotor to transmodal association cortex. We analyzed four large-scale, independent datasets of youth ages 5-23 years (total N = 3,355). Across datasets, males showed greater connectivity between functional networks, whereas females showed greater connectivity within networks, most prominently within the default mode network. More broadly, the sensorimotor and association ends of the S-A axis were more segregated in females and more integrated in males. This difference extended to macroscale cortical organization: the cortical hierarchy was expanded in females relative to males along the principal gradient of functional connectivity. Together, these findings identify the S-A axis as a generalizable organizing principle of sex differences in functional brain organization during youth.

papers.title: Energetic and functional development of soil food webs along secondary succession
papers.abstract: 1. As ecosystems develop, aboveground biomass and belowground organic matter accumulate, while energy turnover declines. This trend is largely supported by vegetation studies, but remains unexplored for soil food webs that channel the majority of energy in terrestrial ecosystems. 2. Here, we tested whether successional theory applies to soil food webs across size-based compartments, ranging from microfauna (nematodes) to macrofauna (soil arthropods and earthworms), along a secondary succession in southwestern China, using an energy-flux approach. To assess whether forest restoration by planting follows natural succession, we also compared spruce and larch plantations with secondary birch forest of the same successional stage. 3. Supporting expectations of reduced energy turnover, the results showed an increasing animal biomass-to-energy flux ratio and a functional shift from herbivory-dominated (green) to detritivory-dominated (brown) energy channelling along succession. Soil food web compartments showed contrasting trends: macro-food webs shifted towards bacterial energy channels with decreasing predation, while micro-food webs maintained similar bacterial/fungal energy flux ratios and tended towards increasing predation. The larch plantation supported lower animal biomass than the secondary birch forest, whereas the spruce plantation did not differ. We further found that energy flux correlated positively with microbial biomass and soil animal diversity, but negatively with litter biomass during succession. 4. Overall, we expand successional theory by revealing the transformations in energy use and pathways within soil food webs along secondary succession, thereby advancing understanding of ecosystem functioning and guiding ecosystem restoration. Our results further suggest that tree plantations do not necessarily replicate the belowground development of natural succession, which should be considered in ecosystem restoration.

papers.title: Chemosensory receptor copy number evolution is not associated with host-plant specialization in butterflies
papers.abstract: Chemoreception plays an important role in how insects sense their environment and interact with other organisms. One important ecological role for chemosensory receptors is sensing chemical compounds to locate suitable host plants. Host-plant use is therefore expected to influence insect sensory system evolution as host-plant preferences changes and species become more generalized or specialized. Yet it remains unclear if species that are generalists require a larger chemosensory receptor repertoire. Here, we investigated the relationship between host-plant specialization and the evolution of olfactory receptor (OR) and gustatory receptor (GR) gene families across 87 butterfly species spanning six families. We annotated OR and GR repertoires and used phylogenetic comparative analyses to test whether receptor copy-number was associated with specialist versus generalist host-use strategies or with host-plant breadth. In addition, we reconstructed evolutionary transitions between generalist and specialist strategies and tested whether these transitions were associated with expansions or contractions in gene-family size. We found that OR and GR repertoire size did not differ between specialists and generalists, nor was it correlated with the number of host-plant families used by a species. We also did not find associations between gene family expansions or contractions and transitions between generalist and specialist strategies. Overall, we find that host-plant specialization is not associated with chemosensory receptor repertoire size across butterflies. We suggest that host-plant chemosensory adaptation may depend on other changes such as receptor tuning, expression differences, or changes in specific receptor lineages not captured by our analyses.

papers.title: 2'-O-Methylated ncRNA condensates form a recombination center for IgH synapsis
papers.abstract: How fibrillarin (FBL), an RNA 2'-O-methyltransferase, regulates antibody diversification remains unclear. This study demonstrated that FBL promotes switch (S)-S DNA synapsis at the IgH locus during class switch recombination (CSR), without affecting DNA cleavage. Both RNA-binding and catalytic activities of FBL were essential for CSR. Moreover, MED19 supported DNA cleavage and synapsis by regulating snoRNAs that guide 2'-O-methylation. Mechanistically, FBL methylated -germline transcripts (-GLTs), cis-acting noncoding RNAs forming nuclear condensates harboring machinery for RNA processing, RNP remodeling, and chromatin dynamics. FBL-mediated 2'-O-methylation governed condensate protein composition. FBL suppression aberrantly enriched nucleolar proteins, including WDR74. Crucially, low WDR74 expression in B cells promoted - and -GLT condensate fusion, thereby enhancing S-S synapsis, CSR, and IgH/c-Myc translocation, potentially contributing to poor myeloma prognosis. Altogether, our findings revealed that RNA 2'-O-methylation dictates GLT condensate composition and fusion dynamics to establish a recombination center, driving genomic DNA synapsis in B cells.

papers.title: A single-cell transcriptomic atlas of paper wasp brains highlights Kenyon cells' role in social behavior
papers.abstract: Social insects provide unique opportunities for studying social interactions, but the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying these behaviors are poorly understood. Here, we performed single-cell sequencing to profile the transcriptomes of 96,310 cells across four phenotypes of Polistes fuscatus paper wasps: foundresses, workers, gynes, and males, to determine how social states and social interactions are encoded in the physiology of the central brain. We characterized the cellular diversity of the Polistes brain and demonstrate that a substantial portion of the brain is composed of diverse populations of Kenyon cell neurons. The composition and gene-expression profiles of these Kenyon cells, as well other neural and non-neural cell populations, vary across sex, caste, and season. We also demonstrate that social interactions, and even the mere observation of a social interaction, induce significant transcriptomic responses, including signatures of neural activation, across populations of Kenyon cell neurons. Notably, the transcriptional and activational signatures elicited by observing a social interaction frequently overlapped with those induced by direct social interaction, suggesting that a shared neural program underlies both direct social interactions and social observation.

papers.title: Genomic characterization and evolutionary path of human satellite 1B in primates highlight a dynamic relationship with transposable elements
papers.abstract: Human Satellite 1B (HSat1B) remains one of the least characterized classical human satellite DNAs, despite its massive abundance on the human Y chromosome. Its tripartite ~2.5 kb monomer - comprising an AluY fragment, a GC-rich unit (here named H1B) and an AT-rich block - points to an evolutionary origin tightly linked to transposable elements (TEs). Here, we present the first comprehensive comparative genomic, phylogenetic and transcriptional characterization of HSat1B across 10 primate species using Telomere-to-Telomere (T2T) and chromosome-scale long-read assemblies, combined with DNA-FISH, RNA-FISH and long-read transcriptomic analyses. We demonstrate that while canonical tandem HSat1B arrays are restricted to Homininae (human, chimpanzee, bonobo and gorilla), the core H1B unit and its structural variants (H1Bsv1 and H1Bsv2) occur across all 10 primate genomes, including strepsirrhines (lemur). This indicates that the H1B sequence predates the assembly of the composite HSat1B monomer by at least 60 million years. H1B variants consistently map within TE-rich genomic contexts, supporting a stepwise, TE-mediated model of satellite diversification and mobilization. Within Homininae, humans exhibit a dramatic lineage-specific expansion driven by Yq12 amplification (~14.2 Mb; 92% of total genomic content), whereas non-human great apes carry smaller, highly polymorphic autosomal and Y-linked arrays. Finally, we show that H1B-containing sequences are transcriptionally active in human and gorilla nuclei via RNA-FISH and characterize heterogeneous H1B/Alu chimeric non-coding transcripts in the human male germline. Collectively, our findings uncover the birth and Homininae-specific expansion of a composite satellite DNA seeded by an ancient primate sequence module and sculpted by transposable elements.

papers.title: Generative Models for Novel Enzymatic Reactions: How Far Do They Go?
papers.abstract: Enzyme function prediction is a long-standing problem in biology, and deep learning methods have recently become popular to improve performance on this task. While most of these models focus on classifying enzymes or mapping them to known reactions, predicting unknown biochemical reactions remains underexplored. Here we thoroughly examine an approach that generates reactions absent from the training data from the enzyme alone. Existing methods such as BLASTp or CLIPZyme cannot, by design, output reactions that are absent from their training data or were not supplied at inference. The closest prior model, RxnPred, reports high fingerprint-similarity scores on held-out enzymes, a less stringent criterion than exact recovery, but fails to recover the correct answer on unseen reactions. We present a structure-conditioned generative model that outputs a complete reaction, reactants and products, and evaluate it on EnzymeMap_x, a reaction-disjoint benchmark in which no test reaction appears in training, under exact, stereo-respecting scoring. On this benchmark, within 400 sampled candidates, the model generates the complete, correct reaction for 25.0% of the subset of test enzyme--reaction pairs whose reaction is a new combination of metabolites seen in training. Surprisingly, it also correctly generates a few reactions composed of metabolites it has not seen in training (1.6%), though their embeddings are present in the vocabulary. With a lower budget, re-ranking places the correct reaction first for 5.6% of pairs and in the top ten for 12.4%, when the reaction is assumed not to be already known (0.2% and 8.1% without that assumption) along with confidence scores. Assessed more leniently, the model produces at least one correct reaction known for the enzyme (usually memorised from training) for 71.2% of test pairs. Going further, without any retraining, a sequence-only model given the reactants as well as the enzyme produces the correct product set for 9.5% of pairs within five candidates, without re-ranking. We also present head-to-head comparisons on these tasks with BLASTp, DIAMOND, RxnPred and Horizyn. Structure conditioning improves fingerprint similarity on homology-stratified splits, but a matched sequence-only ablation at the best configuration finds no measurable effect on exact recovery. Data coverage and chemical initialisation of the vocabulary seem to matter more than encoder geometry.

papers.title: Galectin-9 drives thrombo-inflammatory circuits initiating venous thrombosis
papers.abstract: Background: Venous thromboembolism is increasingly recognized as a thrombo-inflammatory disease, yet the pathways linking inflammation to venous thrombus initiation remain incompletely defined. Galectin-9 (Gal-9), a {beta}-galactoside-binding lectin elevated in inflammatory disorders, has no defined role in venous thrombosis. Methods: Using plasma from patients with deep vein thrombosis (DVT), Gal-9-deficient mice, an inferior vena cava stenosis model, intravital microscopy, microfluidics, and ex vivo platelet and neutrophil assays, we assessed the functional contribution of Gal-9 to venous thrombosis. Results: Plasma Gal-9 was elevated in DVT patients, correlated with D-dimer at presentation, and declined over 3-month follow-up. Gal-9 deletion did not alter hemostasis but markedly impaired thrombus initiation, with reduced platelet and neutrophil recruitment to the vessel wall and reduced intra-thrombus neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation. TNF-/IFN-{gamma}-stimulated endothelial cells upregulated Gal-9 and promoted platelet adhesion and fibrin(ogen) deposition, which Gal-9 neutralization partially reversed. Under venous shear, immobilized recombinant Gal-9 potentiated platelet activation and thrombus formation, particularly alongside collagen, whereas Gal-9 inhibition suppressed these responses. Gal-9-activated platelets promoted NETosis and shifted thrombus composition toward a NET-rich inflammatory phenotype. Conclusions: Gal-9 is a previously unrecognized driver of venous thrombo-inflammation, linking vascular inflammation to platelet activation, NET formation, and thrombosis. Genetic deletion attenuated these responses in vivo, and antibody-mediated Gal-9 neutralization suppressed platelet activation and thrombus formation in vitro, identifying the Gal-9 glycan-binding pathway as a therapeutic target that disrupts thrombosis without impairing hemostasis.

papers.title: DisCell: Separating Spillover from Niche Response in Spatial Transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics at single-cell resolution measures every cell in its place in the tissue, but diffusion and segmentation errors also add transcripts of neighboring cells to a cell's counts. This spillover makes a cell resemble its neighbors, and a response to the niche makes cells in the same niche resemble each other. Both tie a cell's expression to its surroundings. The count data alone cannot tell the two apart. Findings from single-cell transcriptomes, such as a gene program that is higher in one niche than in another or signaling genes that change depending on the neighborhood, may therefore be artifacts of spillover. Current models describe a cell by its intrinsic state together with either its niche response or spillover, but none models all three. We present DisCell, the first method that models all three components jointly and measures how robust each finding is to spillover. DisCell is a generative model that describes single-cell gene expression profiles in terms of two latent variables, an intrinsic state and a response to the niche, and adds spillover from its neighbors as a separate term. DisCell fits the model at increasing levels of spillover and recomputes each finding on the spillover-free expression to see how much spillover it withstands. DisCell also estimates the most spillover a section can contain, and a finding that holds even at that amount is not explained by spillover. In simulated tissue, DisCell recovers each cell's intrinsic state and response and tells findings created by spillover apart from genuine responses. On five sections of ovarian and lung tissue, the intrinsic state keeps more of each cell's own properties, measured by its cell-cycle phase, than any competing method that holds as little of its neighborhood. Within each cell type, the model partitions the variation of each gene into intrinsic state, niche response and spillover. Using DisCell, we rank findings about niches by their robustness to spillover and confirm that a previously reported finding withstands spillover, that esophageal cancer cells in niches infiltrated by immune or stromal cells express more of an epithelial-mesenchymal transition program. DisCell also predicts what the gene expression of a cell type would be in another niche, with its spillover part separated, at lower error on most tasks than the competing method built for this purpose. Training the model takes under ten minutes on one consumer GPU for sections of up to 400,000 cells.

papers.title: Tracing the Evolutionary Histories of Human Cholinergic Proteins Across Eukaryotes: A Comparative Phylogenomic Study
papers.abstract: Acetylcholine signalling depends on a coordinated network of enzymes, transporters, and receptors whose evolutionary histories need not be congruent. Here, we examined 26 curated human cholinergic reference proteins across 89 selected eukaryotic proteomes using a human-reference-anchored phylogenomic framework. Candidate sequences were identified through sequence similarity searches and evaluated using domain architecture, orthology assessment, and family-level phylogenetic analyses. Gene-tree/species-tree reconciliation was performed for selected datasets to investigate putative duplication and loss histories. The results revealed heterogeneous patterns among the investigated protein groups. CHAT- and SLC18A3-associated candidates were recovered across multiple sampled bilaterian lineages, whereas SLC5-family-related sequences showed broader representation, including sampled ctenophores, cnidarians, and bilaterians. Within the latter group, a distinct vertebrate-associated subgroup was identified in relation to human SLC5A7. Cholinesterase analyses recovered an echinoderm-associated grouping and distinct vertebrate ACHE- and BCHE-associated groups, although their deeper evolutionary relationship received comparatively lower support. Muscarinic and nicotinic receptor analyses recovered selected subtype- and subunit-associated groupings, but limited taxonomic representation and sequence instability constrained broader evolutionary interpretation. Collectively, these findings reveal heterogeneous taxonomic distributions and phylogenetic relationships among proteins corresponding to the human cholinergic system. The study provides a comparative framework for examining these protein groups while emphasizing that their recovered evolutionary histories must be interpreted in the context of reference-sequence selection, taxonomic sampling, and phylogenetic resolution.

papers.title: TailEnrich enables discovery of dysregulated genes through disease sample enrichment testing
papers.abstract: Identifying differentially expressed genes is fundamental to elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying complex diseases. However, in complex disorders such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), the genes exhibiting dysregulated expression may vary among patient subsets, reflecting the heterogeneity of the underlying pathological processes. Consequently, pathogenic genes are profoundly dysregulated in only a subset of patients. Conventional differential expression tools, such as DESeq2 and edgeR, are primarily designed to detect population-level expression shifts and may have limited power to identify subgroup-specific dysregulation. To overcome this limitation, we developed TailEnrich, a novel computational method that discovers dysregulated genes within patient subsets. TailEnrich independently tests the extreme left (downregulated) or right (upregulated) tails of a gene's expression distribution for disease sample enrichment. We quantify this enrichment using a new metric, i.e. the PE (Percentage of Enriched disease samples) score. On simulated datasets, TailEnrich demonstrates markedly improved accuracy over DESeq2 and edgeR in identifying dysregulated genes specific to patient subsets. Applied to AD gene expression data, TailEnrich uncovers a distinct, biologically relevant set of genes within key pathological pathways that are missed by mean shift-based approaches. TailEnrich provides a novel method for identifying dysregulated genes, and readily extends to other omics data including genomic variants and proteomics to uncover pathogenic genes in complex diseases.

papers.title: Early AAV9-mediated SLC9A6 gene replacement preserves cerebellar structure and motor function in the shaker rat model of Christianson syndrome
papers.abstract: Christianson syndrome (CS) is an X-linked neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorder caused by SLC9A6 loss of function, resulting in NHE6 deficiency and epilepsy, intellectual disability, cerebellar atrophy, and ataxia. Following on our prior gene replacement therapeutic development, we preclinically evaluated AAV9-mediated SLC9A6 gene replacement in the context of promoter selection, dosing, and treatment timing. Intracerebroventricular delivery of neuronal-targeted gene replacement at 1 x 10^11 vector genomes (vg) produced substantial improvements in motor coordination and preserved cerebellar volume, quantified through structural MRI. Early postnatal treatment prevented the development of gait ataxia throughout the longitudinal assessment period, statistically indistinguishable from wildtype controls, with molecular analyses demonstrating restored NHE6 expression and preservation of cerebellar markers. Interestingly, later treatments at timepoints corresponding to early neurodegenerative stages yielded strong initial effects, but these effects were largely lost over time, with half-life modelling demonstrating the need for early treatment. This conflicted with more persistent motor benefit shown in prior work with an engineered capsid, suggesting the need to consider the interaction between treatment timing and capsid-specific tropism and/or persistence. Finally, we built models capable of accurately predicting motor coordination from several protein markers. These findings will impact therapeutic development for CS, with relevance across neurodevelopmental genetic disorders.

papers.title: ER stress-associated IRE1α signalling links impaired QPRT-dependent NAD⁺ biosynthesis to reduced oocyte competence
papers.abstract: Oocyte quality is closely linked to metabolic and organelle homeostasis, but the mechanisms underlying naturally occurring differences in oocyte quality remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify a link between endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, impaired NAD biosynthesis and poor oocyte quality. Poor-grade goat oocytes exhibited profound NAD depletion, accompanied by quinolinic acid accumulation and reduced expression of quinolinate phosphoribosyltransferase (QPRT), suggesting a bottleneck in de novo NAD biosynthesis. Restoring QPRT expression or bypassing this metabolic step improved meiotic maturation. Further analyses revealed altered ER stress signalling, increased IRE1-associated activity and reduced QPRT RNA stability. Recombinant IRE1 processed QPRT RNA in vitro, suggesting a possible link between IRE1 activity and QPRT transcript regulation. Supplementation with nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) restored NAD levels and improved several features of poor-quality oocytes, including calcium homeostasis, oxidative stress and mitochondrial membrane potential. NMN treatment also improved early embryonic development, with its beneficial effects involving SIRT6 activity and changes in DNA methylation-associated fluorescence. Importantly, NMN supplementation improved meiotic maturation in poor-grade bovine and porcine oocytes, indicating that this metabolic intervention may have broader relevance across mammals. Analysis of published human oocyte proteomic data further revealed age-associated changes in ER proteostasis and NAD-related proteins. Together, our findings identify ER stress-associated disruption of QPRT-dependent NAD biosynthesis as a potential contributor to poor oocyte quality and suggest that restoring NAD metabolism may offer a strategy to improve the functional properties of compromised oocytes.

papers.title: RhoGEF Solo regulates cell density-dependent keratin remodeling and desmosome maturation
papers.abstract: Desmosomes (DSMs) are specialized cell-cell adhesion structures that anchor keratin intermediate filaments and play a crucial role in maintaining the mechanical integrity of epithelial tissues. Keratin filaments associate with DSMs in two characteristic patterns: radial spokes extending from DSMs into the cytoplasmic keratin network and circumferential rims connecting neighboring DSMs. Solo is a Rho-guanine nucleotide exchange factor (RhoGEF) involved in cellular responses to mechanical stress and keratin network reorganization. Here, we investigated the role of Solo in regulating keratin-DSM interactions in response to cell density. The number of radial keratin spokes at cell-cell adhesion sites was markedly reduced at high cell density, concomitant with increased Solo localization at these sites. Conversely, Solo knockout (KO) increased the number of radial keratin spokes. Expression of wild-type Solo, but not a GEF-inactive Solo mutant, rescued the increase in radial keratin spokes in confluent Solo-KO cells, indicating that Solo RhoGEF activity is required for this regulation. Inhibition of actin polymerization or ROCK activity also suppressed the reduction in radial spoke density. Furthermore, expansion microscopy and electron microscopy revealed that DSMs in Solo-KO cells remained small and immature even under confluent conditions. Solo was also partially required for the localization of plakoglobin (PG), a core DSM protein, whereas PG-KO markedly increased the number of radial keratin spokes. These findings suggest that increased cell density promotes DSM maturation accompanied by a reduction in radial keratin spokes, and Solo contributes to both processes, potentially through facilitating PG localization at DSMs and regulating Rho-ROCK-dependent actin cytoskeletal remodeling.

papers.title: Walking delays auditory processing in humans alongside a global shift in aperiodic neural activity
papers.abstract: Natural sensory processing unfolds during movement, yet human electrophysiology is usually measured under enforced stillness. Here, we used mobile EEG to test whether walking changes the timing of auditory processing. Thirty adults listened to lateralised pure tones while walking freely or standing. Walking led to a delay in auditory N1 latency (< 10 ms). Control analyses ruled out the possibility that the N1 delay was contaminated by foot strike related noise in EEG. Multivariate decoding further indicated a later emergence of sound location information during walking in the subset of participants with reliable decoding in both states. Walking also produced a scalp wide decrease in the aperiodic exponent of neural responses. A larger global exponent decrease was associated with a larger N1 delay across participants. Together, these findings show that natural walking reorganises the temporal dynamics of human auditory processing and link early sensory slowing to a global change in ongoing cortical state.

papers.title: Neonatal NMDA receptor blockade disrupts prefrontal cortical regulation of social affective behavior: implications for schizophrenia
papers.abstract: Developmental N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAr) hypofunction has been implicated in the pathophysiology of schizophrenia, including cognitive and emotional deficits. However, the neural circuit mechanisms linking developmental NMDAr hypofunction to social affective impairments remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated schizophrenia-related social affective dysfunction induced by neonatal exposure to the NMDAr antagonist MK-801 and examined the contribution of the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), a key hub for socio-cognitive function. Sprague-Dawley rat pups received subcutaneous injections of saline or MK-801 (MK-Low: 0.2 mg/kg; MK-High: 0.4 mg/kg) during the neonatal period. In adulthood, social affective behaviors were assessed using the Social Affective Preference (SAP) and Social Interaction (SI) tests. MK-801-treated rats, particularly the MK-High group, displayed impaired social affective responses, characterized by reduced preference for and investigation of distressed conspecifics. These impairments were ameliorated by chemogenetic inhibition of pyramidal cells in the mPFC, whereas activation of these neurons disrupted social affective behavior in naive rats. Histological analyses revealed reduced parvalbumin-positive interneuron (PVIN) density in the mPFC of MK-801-treated rats. Consistent with the involvement of PVIN dysfunction, selective activation of mPFC PVINs alleviated social affective deficits in MK-801-treated rats. These findings identify impaired PVIN-mediated inhibitory regulation within the mPFC as a circuit mechanism underlying social affective dysfunction following neonatal NMDAr blockade, providing insight into the pathophysiology of schizophrenia-related social impairments.

papers.title: Virtual dynamics of spatiotemporal single-cell interactions
papers.abstract: Building virtual cells and tissues requires reconstructing how interacting cell populations evolve in space and time, yet spatial omics experiments provide only sparse snapshots of this process. Here, we introduce CytoBridge, a computational method that reconstructs continuous virtual cell dynamics from discrete spatial transcriptomic data. Starting from a joint transcriptomic-spatial space, CytoBridge learns stochastic trajectories of cell states, positions, and population sizes through an unbalanced mean-field Schrodinger bridge formulation that explicitly incorporates cell-cell interaction as a dynamical driver. A time-varying interaction graph built from spatial proximity and ligand-receptor priors allows the velocity to be decomposed into an interaction component estimated from observed neighborhoods and ligand-receptor features, and an intrinsic-context component that captures intrinsic regulatory processes and unmeasured contextual influences. Applied to five datasets across three spatial transcriptomics platforms and spanning development, regeneration, and neurodegeneration, CytoBridge accurately generates tissue dynamics at unmeasured time points, follows ligand-receptor signaling through measured and unmeasured stages, and supports hypothesis-generating in silico perturbation. CytoBridge provides a general method for turning heterogeneous spatiotemporal transcriptomic measurements into continuously evolving virtual tissues.

papers.title: The mycotoxin zearalenone couples secondary metabolism to N-acetylglucosamine catabolism
papers.abstract: Fungal secondary metabolites are often viewed as terminal products of specialized metabolism, yet how their production influences the physiology of the producing organism remains poorly understood. Here, we show that zearalenone (ZEA) production is functionally coupled to N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) catabolism in Fusarium graminearum. Transcriptome profiling of a ZEB2-overexpressing strain revealed enrichment of GlcNAc metabolic functions, and exogenous ZEA induced key catabolic genes independently of Zeb2. Among pathway components, NAG, encoding GlcNAc-6-phosphate deacetylase, was critical for GlcNAc utilization, and its loss caused severe GlcNAc-dependent growth inhibition. Genetic impairment of NAG was poorly tolerated under elevated ZEA pathway activity. Conversely, NAG overexpression increased tolerance to exogenous ZEA and alleviated the growth defect associated with ZEB2 overexpression. Together, these findings reveal a functional connection between secondary metabolite production and primary nutrient metabolism and suggest that ZEA-associated metabolic remodeling contributes to the fitness of the producing fungus.

papers.title: RadMultiBench: A Reproducible Dual-Task Benchmark Exposing the Limits of Pre-Trained Vision-Language Models Across Thoracic and Breast Imaging
papers.abstract: We present RadMultiBench, a multimodal benchmark of 6,148 medical images paired with expert radiological impressions across five categories--Breast Cancer, Lung Benign, Lung Malignant, Pneumonia, and Tuberculosis--targeting two core clinical tasks: automated report generation and disease classification. To enable reliable, repeatable experimentation, we provide a reproducible pipeline for data ingestion, de-identification, split management, and standardized reporting of text and classification metrics, facilitating dataset versioning and continuous benchmark testing. We compare three architectures: (1) a classical CNN-RNN with Bahdanau attention (ResNet-LSTM), (2) a general-domain vision-language (V-L) prefix-projection model (CLIP-GPT), and (3) a domain-specific V-L prefix-projection model (BioViL-T). Results reveal a sharp performance divide: the ResNet-LSTM attains near-perfect classification (99.5% accuracy) and is the only model to generate coherent reports (BLEU-4 = 0.021), whereas both prefix-projection models catastrophically fail generation (BLEU-4 [≤] 0.0001); moreover, the domain-specific BioViL-T also fails classification (11.5% accuracy). From a data-engineering angle, the pipeline is productionizable with lineage, feature registries, and continuous integration to guard against silent regressions when updating models or data; from a data-science angle, the benchmark provides baselines and analyses that foreground feature alignment and architectural suitability as first-order concerns, inviting ablations on multimodal objectives, retrieval-augmented encoders, and uncertainty-aware decoding. Overall, RadMultiBench highlights that state-of-the-art status in general V-L domains does not translate automatically to high-stakes clinical tasks, and it furnishes the tooling and evidence base needed to develop robust, clinically viable multimodal systems.

papers.title: Measuring satellite arrays of the human Y chromosome from sequencing reads
papers.abstract: Human Y chromosome satellites vary widely but remain difficult to measure in large cohorts. In response, we developed Yruler, which uses pangenome assemblies to measure satellite lengths, composition and Y dosage from sequencing reads without alignment. Analyses reveal centromere-length differences between related lineages, extend observations of short non-centromeric arrays across a lineage, and show unequal component variability and composition changes with heterochromatin length within lineages. Yruler brings satellite variation into population-scale phenotype studies.

papers.title: UVC Irradiation Induces Time-Dependent Proteomic Remodeling in Geodermatophilus obscurus G20
papers.abstract: Geodermatophilus obscurus G20 is a multi-resistant extremophile observed to survive significant dosages of ultraviolet (UV) radiation. Despite previous work having measured G. obscurus G20s proteome in relation to its genome sequence, its proteomic response to stressors has yet to be explored. This study utilizes bottom-up proteomics with data independent acquisition to derive comprehensive proteomic measurements in both healthy and two UV-stressed conditions induced through 254 nm UV radiation administered at a median lethal dose. The first, an acute response treatment group, was recovered and flash-frozen immediately after UV radiation. The second, a recovery response treatment group, was allowed to incubate for 1 hour following UV radiation. Gene enrichment analysis revealed an increase in NADH dehydrogenase activity among both stressed treatment groups, however the recovery response treatment group experienced additional changes including reduced peptidoglycan synthesis and increased translational activity. Results suggest that the repair process undergone by G. obscurus G20 persists well after initial UV exposure and is likely to be inducing noteworthy energetic demands to facilitate UV induced genomic repair. Proteomic analyses revealed patterns that advance our mechanistic and temporal understanding of the G. obscurus metabolic response to UV irradiation.

papers.title: PARP1-mediated PARylation of SPRTN restrains its DNA-protein crosslink repair activity
papers.abstract: SPRTN is a DNA-dependent metalloprotease that resolves DNA-protein crosslinks, but how its activity is restrained on chromatin remains unclear. Here we show that SPRTN is PARylated in a PARP1- and HPF1-dependent manner. Mass spectrometry datasets identify seven modified residues in the C-terminal region, and substituting them (SPRTN-PARless) strongly reduces PARylation. The Nudix homology domain is required for SPRTN to interact with PARP1 and for efficient PARylation. SPRTN-PARless accumulates faster and to higher levels at laser-induced DNA damage than wild-type SPRTN. PARylation reduces single-stranded DNA binding of both cell-derived and purified SPRTN, and PARG treatment reverses this effect for cell-derived protein. SPRTN-PARless shows increased autocleavage and accelerates clearance of camptotheci-induced TOP1 cleavage complexes. These findings suggest that PARylation acts as negative feedback on SPRTN after its PAR-dependent recruitment, restraining its DNA engagement and proteolytic activity.

papers.title: Application of metagenomic sequencing to improve sessile serrated lesion detection using the faecal immunochemical test
papers.abstract: Most population colorectal cancer (CRC) screening programs use the faecal immunochemical test (FIT), which quantifies occult haemoglobin in faeces and has proven to be effective in detecting and reducing CRC incidence and mortality. Sessile serrated lesions (SSLs) account for up to 30% of sporadic CRC, yet FIT has low sensitivity to detect them. Faecal microbial biomarkers may improve their detection, but FIT samples have not previously been used to study the SSL microbiome. We asked whether FIT samples preserve the faecal microbiome as accurately as fresh collection, and whether they can reveal a microbial signature of SSL. We first reanalysed a published dataset of paired FIT and fresh faecal samples from the same participants. Donor identity explained 63.5% of compositional variance compared with 16.7% for collection method, indicating that FIT preserves the donor-specific signature on which biomarker discovery depends. We then generated shotgun metagenomes from FIT samples of 24 adults scheduled for diagnostic colonoscopy, twelve with at least one clinically significant SSL and twelve with no neoplasia (NN) and compared each group with a published fresh faeces cohort matched on colonoscopy outcome. Collection method explained 6.3% to 7.6% of variance, and no individual species was significantly differentially abundant between methods. Between SSL and NN FIT samples, community structure did not significantly differ, and conservative differential abundance analysis returned no results. More permissive count-based models suggested a depletion of fermentative commensals in SSL. Functionally, SSL samples encoded significantly fewer KEGG orthologs and less polyamine biosynthesis capacity, while orthologs carried by several Bifidobacterium species were more abundant. Many depleted functions reflected Enterobacteriaceae gene content concentrated in a few control samples. No single feature was diagnostic on its own. A multi-feature signature, confirmed in larger cohorts and applied to samples that screening programs already collect, may increase the detection rate of SSLs.

papers.title: Evaluating non-oxidative glycolysis using 13C metabolic flux analysis
papers.abstract: Non-oxidative glycolysis (NOG) converts glucose to acetyl-CoA without emitting CO2 during Escherichia coli bioproduction. Although 13C-metabolic flux analysis (13C-MFA) has the potential to evaluate NOG flux distribution in vivo, the precision of these estimates depends on the labeling patterns of glucose tracers. Because E. coli has multiple native glycolysis pathways, selecting the optimal glucose tracer is important for precise estimates. This study used simulations to evaluate the performance of 18 commercially available glucose tracers in precisely predicting NOG flux. We artificially generated flux distributions of central metabolic pathways, including three types of NOG pathways, and obtained 13C labeling patterns of amino acids metabolized from each glucose tracer. Using these data, we then calculated 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for NOG pathway fluxes. Comparing the sum of CI widths from three NOG fluxes showed that estimation with [1,3-13C]-glucose yielded the narrowest CIs. Several tracers, including [2,3-13C]glucose, were capable of determining fluxes with high precision, but [1-13C]glucose was not one of them, despite often being used for estimating glycolytic fluxes. We then experimentally evaluated [2,3-13C]- and [1-13C]glucose as tracers in E. coli strains with and without the expression of phosphoketolase, which is required for NOG pathways to function. The results suggested that [1-13C]glucose could not detect NOG fluxes, whereas [2,3-13C]glucose estimated the fluxes of all three NOG pathways with narrow CIs.

papers.title: A multipotent mouse distal airway secretory cell population that contributes to both airway and alveolar regeneration
papers.abstract: The distal airway is a spatially distinct compartment whose contribution to lung repair remains poorly defined. We have identified an epithelial cell population enriched in the most distal airways of the mouse lung, that is not present in the alveolar epithelium. Using lineage tracing tools based on Cldn10 expression which marks these cells, we show that the Cldn10+ lineage in homeostatic conditions marks distal airway secretory cells in a highly specific manner, with only a small contribution to multi-ciliated cells and no contribution towards the basal stem cell lineage. Remarkably, these Cldn10+ distal secretory cells proliferate and display a high degree of multi-potency across the lung epithelial axis after injury, generating basal cells, multi-ciliated cells, and alveolar epithelium. In severely remodeled regions after injury, we show that Cldn10 lineage-labeled cells migrate from the airways and differentiate into alveolar epithelial cells. These findings establish the Cldn10 lineage that defines a distal airway secretory facultative progenitor with both intrapulmonary airway and alveolar potential, providing a genetic system for studying distal lung repair.

papers.title: SOPSim: A cell vertex-based application for simulating sensory bristle patterning with dynamic filopodia
papers.abstract: Repeating patterns, such as the bristles on the thorax of fruit flies developed from sensory organ precursor (SOP) cells, play important roles in the lives of flies as they are connected to the central nervous system and help detect environmental cues and threats. Notch signaling is known to regulate the formation of these patterns. Primarily, Notch signaling involves local communication between neighboring cells in direct contact (apical or junctional interaction). However, this short-range interaction alone cannot fully explain the complex biological patterns observed. Further studies have revealed long-range communication between cells through actin-based protrusions known as filopodia. The precise understanding of how the dynamics of filopodia, such as protrusion and retraction, lead to Notch-Delta activation remains unclear, which limits our ability to fully comprehend the mechanisms underlying cell fate decisions and the emergence of spatially organized patterns during tissue development and regeneration. In this study, we extend the modeling framework for Notch signaling by incorporating a filopodia dynamics model driven by myosin-mediated contraction. We address existing gaps by defining criteria under which any given pair of filopodia will physically intersect. We also introduce the local sensory area (LSA), a metric for quantifying local SOP spacing, and use experimental data to calibrate a Notch threshold that distinguishes SOP from epithelial cells. Through numerical simulations, we confirm that long-range communication via filopodia is essential for reproducing the refined patterns observed in vivo. Additionally, we explore how filopodia length, lifetime, and orientation influence the spatial organization of SOP cells. To this end, a Python library has been developed which allows users to perform simulations of Notch Delta signaling via a (1) Graphical User Interface/website, local to the user's computer, (2) via commands in the command line interface, or (3) by calling the simulation using a function via a Python API. This library allows users without computational expertise to easily specify a small number of input parameters and generate simulations of the model.

papers.title: Functional Data Clustering of Filopodia Dynamics
authors: De Silva, S. H. D. S.
papers.abstract: Notch signaling plays a significant role in tissue patterning. During patterning of the fruit fly dorsal thorax peripheral nervous system, basal filopodia extend the spatial range of cell-cell communication, yet it is still unclear how Notch is activated in long range signaling via filopodia interaction. Filopodia undergo dynamic length changes during their lifetime, which could supply the mechanical pulling force required for notch activation. However, their dynamics are often characterized using individual scalar values such as maximum length and extension rate which could obscure more intricate dynamics. Our hypothesis is that signaling filopodia exhibit distinct and recurrent temporal patterns which can be identified by a consideration of their complete lifetime trajectories. Our work analyzes 60 filopodia trajectories at the basal surface of the fly dorsal thorax during patterning. Length profiles were smoothed using cubic B-splines and clustered by first reducing them to their dominant functional principal component followed by the application of various clustering algorithms. We found that 94.29% of the overall trajectory variation is explained by the first four functional principal components which account for variations in maximal length, extension and retraction rate, duration of stationary phase and length fluctuation frequency. Five recurrent temporal profiles (dynamic extension modes) with varying trajectory shapes and physical attributes, were identified using trimmed K-means. These findings demonstrate that whereas the major source of structural variation in filopodia profiles remains the length, extension rate and retraction rate, nontrivial combinations of these create distinct dynamic modes of extension which provide new insight into their length profiles. Our work thus offers a quantitative framework for future research connecting filopodia dynamic extension modes to productive Notch activation.

papers.title: Reinforcement sculpts synaptic ensembles for operant dendritic control
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning requires the selective modification of synapses that contribute to outcome-relevant neural activity, yet the principles underlying these selective modifications remain unclear. Here we combined longitudinal two-photon imaging of identified dendritic spines with a closed-loop optical brain-machine interface (BMI), in which activity from selected apical dendrites of layer 5 motor-cortical neurons controlled an auditory cursor, with target acquisition triggering optogenetic reinforcement. Mice learned to reliably generate the specific dendritic activity that leads to reinforcement. Learning was accompanied by selective strengthening and weakening of individual spines on reinforced dendrites. At individual synapses, the direction of plasticity depended on both the timing of activity relative to reinforced dendritic events and the pre-existing temporal organization of that activity. Furthermore, plasticity was enriched in small task-relevant synaptic groups: spines in synergistic groups were preferentially strengthened, whereas those in antagonistic groups were preferentially weakened. These changes were accompanied by the emergence of increasingly reproducible, selectively recruited, and temporally focused synaptic ensembles, and the incorporation of newly formed spines into these ensembles. Finally, blocking striatal dopamine receptor signaling impaired BMI learning and cortical synaptic reorganization of target dendrites, demonstrating a role for striatal reinforcement in cortical plasticity. Together, these findings reveal how reinforcement of specific dendritic activity sculpts synaptic ensembles that support learned operant dendritic control.

papers.title: Transition Fibers Play a Central Role in Import of a Glucose Transporter into the Flagellar Membrane
papers.abstract: Leishmania parasite promastigotes have a motile flagellum that encompasses a variety of integral membrane proteins, but how such proteins traffic selectively to the flagellum is largely unknown. The flagellar-specific glucose transporter, GT1, binds to the KHARON protein via the transporter hydrophilic amino terminal domain, and KHARON is essential for trafficking of GT1 from the flagellar pocket membrane at the base of the flagellum into the flagellar membrane. A major objective of this study was to determine the mechanism whereby KHARON transports GT1 into the flagellar membrane. We have determined that KHARON is a novel component of the transition fibers that project from the basal body at the base of the flagellum toward the flagellar membrane. We propose that KHARON binds GT1 at the transition fibers and then transfers it to intraflagellar transport (IFT) trains as they enter the flagellum at this site. The IFT trains, associated with the membrane tethering protein TULP, then move GT1 through the transition zone filter into the body of the flagellum. These results provide evidence for a role for transition fibers in transport of membrane proteins into flagella.

papers.title: Responses of Muscle Volume, Strength, and Motor Unit Properties to Bed Rest and Retraining in Young Males and Females
papers.abstract: Sex differences in motor unit (MU) properties to simulated microgravity are unknown. Young males and females completed a 21-day head-down bed rest followed by a 21-day retraining. Bed rest reduced knee extensor strength and volume without sex differences. MU firing rate decreased in both groups, more in females, alongside increased serum C-terminal agrin fragment. After retraining, these measures returned to baseline, whereas strength only partially recovered, remaining below baseline.

papers.title: From Fill to Freeze: Redesigning homeRNA to Enable Robust Sampling and Scalable Downstream Processing Workflows for Remote Blood Transcriptomics
papers.abstract: In-person research can introduce barriers to participation, including proximity to a study site and scheduling constraints. Our lab developed the homeRNA platform to address these barriers, enabling remote blood collection and RNA stabilization for transcriptomic research. To increase the applicability of homeRNA for large-scale studies, a redesigned version was developed with modifications to 1) improve usability for both participants and downstream processing laboratories, 2) allow for high-throughput manufacturing, and 3) extend the shelf life of the stabilizer tube. In this work, we systematically tested this design against anticipated stresses that can occur throughout a remote study (e.g., high temperature exposure during shipment) to identify and characterize its limitations. We found that the homeRNA device can be prepared and stored at room temperature at least three months in advance of sampling with continued shelf life analysis underway. We also found that the homeRNA platform produces RNA of sufficient quality for downstream transcriptomic analysis under standard shipping durations (i.e., 2 days in transit) and ambient-to-high temperature conditions (i.e., 25-40 {degrees}C) and that RNA quality is unaffected by variable blood volumes collected by participants (mean RIN=7.8 in blood volumes 0.25-1 mL). Lastly, we also found that samples can be stored in typical cold storage temperatures and even up to standard room temperature for at least 4 weeks (mean RIN=8.1 after 4 weeks of storage at -80 to 20 {degrees}C). This work validates that the new homeRNA platform is robust to many of the expected stresses that samples can experience during remote studies.

papers.title: An expansive internal chemosensory system in the insect abdomen implicates Gustatory Receptors in diverse aspects of interoception
papers.abstract: Taste and olfactory receptors are gatekeepers that convey chemical information about the external environment. Their role in chemosensory systems has been extensively studied in several model system, which established their role in triggering discrete behavioral as well as physiological responses related to feeding and social interactions. Over time, cases of chemoreceptors expressed internally in organs not linked to the external chemosensory systems of taste and olfaction have been reported. Here, we present the existence of a complex internal chemosensory system in the abdomen of Drosophila melanogaster. We show that the adult fruit fly harbors a complex internal chemosensory system, composed of about 80 to 100 abdominal chemosensory neurons (ACSNs) expressing approximately 20 different Gustatory receptor (Gr) genes, including all sugar receptor and several members of the less conserved bitter receptor genes. The cells expressing specific Gr genes are stereotypically arranged along the entire circumference of the abdominal body wall, in proximity of muscle and fat layers. The ACSN fall into at least nine different subtypes based on co-expression analysis, projection trajectories into the Abdominal Ganglion (AG) and location of cell somata. Identification of different subpopulation of ASCNs expressing discrete combinations of Gr genes indicates that these receptor complexes have new, previously not considered roles in interoception, including monitoring of different nutrients, detection of cell metabolites and their byproducts and chemicals associated with pathogens.

papers.title: Assessing Enclosure Modifications to Enhance Accessibility for Zoo-Housed Meerkats (Suricata suricatta)
papers.abstract: Scientific advancements have contributed to increased longevity of animals in zoos and aquariums, creating a growing need for environments that remain accessible to geriatric animals and animals with disabilities. However, few empirical studies have evaluated whether accessibility-focused enclosure modifications impact species-appropriate behavior. We evaluated the effects of accessibility modifications on a group of four adult zoo-housed meerkats (Suricata suricatta), including one individual with a forelimb amputation and one geriatric individual. Low-level logs and steps were added to the enclosure to provide intermediate heights and facilitate access to elevated areas. Following the introduction of these enclosure modifications, sentry behavior increased, with all individuals engaging in this behavior compared with only one individual during baseline. The meerkats also increased their overall use of low-elevated areas following modification, although individual responses varied. Posture differed between study phases, with meerkats more frequently adopting tri/quadrupedal postures following modification. Together, these findings suggest that relatively simple accessibility-focused modifications can expand opportunities for geriatric animals and animals with disabilities to engage in species-appropriate behavior. More broadly, this case study highlights the importance of empirically evaluating accessibility interventions and incorporating universal design principles into animal spaces to accommodate individuals with diverse physical abilities and promote positive animal welfare.

papers.title: Host-Derived Lipids Sustain Membrane Biogenesis in an Obligate Endosymbiont
papers.abstract: Intracellular symbionts often undergo extreme genome reduction and lose pathways considered essential in free-living bacteria, including membrane phospholipid biosynthesis. Yet how such symbionts maintain their membranes remains poorly understood. The pea aphid Acyrthosiphon pisum harbors the obligate endosymbiont Buchnera aphidicola within specialized host cells called bacteriocytes, providing a tractable system to address this question. Here we integrated untargeted lipidomics, transcriptomics, and functional assays to investigate lipid metabolism across the symbiosis. Although Buchnera lacks nearly all canonical genes for phospholipid biosynthesis, purified Buchnera contained all major phospholipid classes detected in the host, including phosphatidylcholine (PC), phosphatidylserine (PS), phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), phosphatidylglycerol (PG), and cardiolipin (CL). This repertoire differs markedly from conventional bacterial lipidomes, combining canonical bacterial phospholipids with PC, PS, and cholesterol sulfate, features more characteristic of the eukaryotic host environment. Every lipid species detected in Buchnera was also present in aphid tissues, consistent with extensive host contribution to the symbiont lipidome. Yet the Buchnera lipidome was compositionally distinct, with characteristic differences in the relative abundance of individual lipid species. Bacteriocytes were transcriptionally specialized for lipid precursor metabolism, including upregulation of phospholipid precursor synthesis and acetyl-CoA transport pathways. RNA interference targeting host lipid precursor genes reduced Buchnera abundance and disrupted symbiont morphology, linking host lipid metabolism to Buchnera maintenance. We also found that sterol availability influences Buchnera abundance. Together, these findings support a model in which host lipid metabolism sustains membrane biogenesis in a highly reduced endosymbiont and identify membrane lipids as an important dimension of metabolic integration in obligate intracellular symbioses.

papers.title: Persistent and recyclable myosin II minifilaments drive cortical contractility in the early C. elegans embryo
papers.abstract: Non-muscle myosin II is a key regulator of cell and tissue morphogenesis, yet the cortical dynamics of myosin minifilaments in vivo remain poorly understood. Here, we combine SIM-TIRF and single-molecule TIRF microscopy to characterize the structure and dynamics of myosin minifilaments in an early developing embryo. High-temporal-resolution SIM-TIRF imaging revealed diverse minifilament behaviors, including partition-like events, long-range alignment of multiple minifilaments into collective structures we called proto-stress fibers, partial unbinding, and sequential unbinding and rebinding to the cortex. Photoconversion experiments showed that minifilaments persist as intact units after cortical unbinding, diffuse through the cytoplasm, and can be recycled over long distances rather than disassembling upon detachment. Despite these dynamic behaviors, minifilaments are predominantly stationary when bound to actin. Numerical simulations demonstrated that this static behavior is essential to sustain cortical stress within a continuously remodeling actin network. Using myosin motor-domain mutants, we further investigated the contribution of motor activity to these behaviors. Together, our results reveal that myosin minifilaments can persist as stable units while cycling between the cortex and cytoplasm, and that their predominantly static behavior when bound to actin enables sustained force generation in a continuously renewing cortical network. These findings provide new insights into myosin organization, recycling, and force generation during early embryonic development.

papers.title: Midlife nonlinearities across scale in Biondi body amyloid formation in the human choroid plexus
