papers.abstract: Human choroid plexus epithelial cells (CPECs), which produce cerebrospinal fluid and form the blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier, accumulate discrete intracellular amyloid inclusions called Biondi bodies (BBs). Using systematic manual and machine learning approaches on the choroid plexus glomus, we determined the percentages of CPECs containing thioflavin S-stained BBs as well as BB load and spatial distributions in whole slide images from 77 cases across the human lifespan. On average, BB prevalence was near zero until age 40, rose steeply in the 5th and 6th decades, and exceeded 50% after age 70. As prevalence plateaued, BB load continued to rise with age. Accelerated BB accumulation was seen in two cases of diabetic ketoacidosis, including a 16-year-old, while an 85-year-old with the relatively rare APOE2/E2 genotype had fewer BBs than expected. BB prevalence in the choroid plexus glomus was not associated with Alzheimer's disease, but was lower in females than males. Notably, spatial clustering of BBs was universal across cases while nearest-neighbor analyses suggested cell-to-cell, prion-like BB spread that can account for the nonlinearities seen at tissue and population scales. The abrupt, nonlinear BB accumulation during midlife coincides with or precedes other common aging-associated neuropathologies of the human brain, consistent with broad BB and choroid plexus contributions to brain aging and disease.

papers.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals Tumorigenic Lineages and Interactions Persisting and Evolving From Premalignancy to Cancer in the Stomach
papers.abstract: Background & Aims Gastric cancer is often diagnosed at advanced stages, making the premalignant window critical for early detection. However, the epithelial changes that characterize this stage remain poorly defined. We used CTLA4-knockdown (CTLA4KD) mice, which model human CTLA4 insufficiency-associated gastric cancer, that develops autoimmune gastritis, metaplasia, and adenocarcinoma, to define molecular changes across disease progression. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing and 40-color spectral flow cytometry were performed on gastric tissue across premalignant and cancer stages. We evaluated epithelial lineage relationships, cell-cell communication pathways, and candidate markers at the transcript and protein levels in murine and human gastric adenocarcinoma. Results We identified a metaplastic/tumorigenic population in CTLA4KD mice that emerged in premalignancy with a chief cell transcriptomic origin. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed a progressive increase in fibronectin (FN1) signaling from premalignancy through cancer, transitioning from stromal to autocrine signaling in the metaplastic/tumorigenic population. Expression of Embigin (EMB), a fibronectin receptor, increased at both transcript and protein levels in premalignancy and remained elevated in cancer. EMB epithelial cells co-expressed CD133, a cancer stem cell marker, consistent with a stem-like phenotype. EMB expression was also higher in human gastric adenocarcinoma than in matched normal tissue. Conclusions Using a model that captures the full histopathological cascade of gastric tumorigenesis, we delineate single-cell transcriptional programs that persist and evolve from premalignancy to adenocarcinoma. In-depth computational analyses identified novel markers involved in cell-cell communication during tumorigenesis, including EMB, an epithelial marker that persists from premalignancy through cancer in the murine model and validated in human gastric adenocarcinoma, suggesting EMB as a marker of premalignant progression.

papers.title: stem.MAP: Identification of cell-type-specific protein complexes in mammalian embryonic stem cells.
papers.abstract: Protein complexes carry out critical functions during development. Mapping cell-type-specific protein complexes in early embryogenesis is essential for uncovering the molecular mechanisms of embryonic development. We unfortunately currently lack a catalog of protein complexes specific for embryogenesis including embryonic stem cells. Here we develop a proteomics-based machine learning workflow to predict protein complexes present in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESC). Our method integrates data from a cell-type agnostic protein complex resource with co-fractionation mass spectrometry (CF-MS) experiments on mESC. Our resource, stem.MAP, identifies 3,986 complexes encompassing ~133,000 unique interactions, and 8,616 proteins. stem.MAP captures variant complexes critical for stem cell function including the PRC2, BAF and NuRD complexes. stem.MAP also discriminates mutually exclusive interactions specific to embryonic stem cells (e.g. Eif4ebp2 - Eif4e). Finally we observe 1,388 high confidence stem.MAP interactions found only in mESC CF-MS data, many with support from AlphaFold modeling and a gastruloid coregulation network. We make stem.MAP protein complexes available through our web resource: stem.proteincomplexes.org. We anticipate stem.MAP will be beneficial to the study of early development and we expect our proteomics-based machine learning workflow to be applicable to the creation of any context-specific protein interaction network.

papers.title: Optogenetic induction of TAD boundary pairing promotes gene activity
papers.abstract: The genome folds inside the nucleus into distinct structures across multiple levels of organization. Topologically associating domains (TADs) are a ubiquitous architectural feature of genomes delineated by boundaries enriched in the CTCF protein and the cohesin complex. TADs are dynamic structures as their boundaries undergo continuous, short-lived pairing events. Whether the structural integrity of TADs contributes to regulation of the genes within the TAD is unclear. To directly test the structure-function relationship of TADs, we have developed OptoTet, an optogenetic tool to rapidly and directly manipulate chromatin contacts in a controlled fashion using light without the need for mutation or protein depletion. Using the TADs containing the ERRFI1 or MYC gene as model systems, we show that OptoTet promotes TAD boundary looping. When applied to probing the structure-function relationship of TADs, light-induced pairing of TAD boundaries promoted transcriptional activity of ERRFI1 as indicated by increased gene bursting. In contrast, bursting of MYC was insensitive to boundary pairing. Enhanced TAD boundary pairing also partially rescued the effect of depletion of cohesin components on ERRF1 but not on MYC. Our results suggest that TADs boundary pairing dynamics can contribute to gene regulation in a gene-specific manner.

papers.title: Beyond Terrestrial Carnivores: Olfactory Bulb Anatomy in a Semi-Aquatic Mammal
papers.abstract: The organization of the olfactory systems remains poorly understood in mustelids, particularly in lutrines adapted to semiaquatic environments. This study provides the first detailed anatomical, histological, lectin-histochemical, and immunohistochemical characterization of the main (MOB) and accessory (AOB) olfactory bulbs of the Asian small-clawed otter (Aonyx cinereus). Serial transverse and sagittal sections were examined using Nissl and Tolivia staining, a panel of lectins, and neuronal and olfactory immunohistochemical markers. Macroscopically, the olfactory bulbs were prominent and elongated, although no distinct AOB could be identified. Histologically, the MOB displayed a well-developed laminar organization, abundant mitral and tufted cells, and a clearly defined lateral olfactory tract. By contrast, the AOB was small, located dorsocaudally within the olfactory peduncle, and lacked the canonical lamination observed in many other mammals. Its identification was supported by the selective binding of Ulex europaeus agglutinin and strong Gi2 immunoreactivity in glomerular-like structures, whereas Go labeling was weak. LEA and STA labeled the superficial layers of both bulbs, while VVA and SBA recognized only scattered MOB glomeruli. Neuronal markers, including NCAM, NSE, NeuN, PGP 9.5, and {beta}-tubulin III, confirmed the neuronal nature of the AOB, while calretinin strongly labeled its glomerular structures and projection neurons. These findings reveal a marked contrast between a highly developed MOB and a small, poorly laminated but neurochemically differentiated AOB. This organization indicates that the vomeronasal pathway is retained in A. cinereus, although in a structurally reduced form, and provides a comparative basis for investigating chemosensory evolution in semiaquatic carnivorans.

papers.title: Interspecific social contacts spread gut microbiota in wild rodent communities
papers.abstract: Background: The mammalian gut microbiota influences a wide array of host phenotypes and varies substantially among individuals. Among conspecifics, microbiota composition is strongly shaped by microbial transmission through social interactions, yet the extent to which such transmission also occurs across species boundaries remains poorly understood. Here, we combine high-resolution tracking data collected over more than 10 months with gut microbiota profiling to examine social associations, space use, and microbiota similarity among individuals of three sympatric rodent species - wood mice (Apodemus sylvaticus), yellow-necked mice (A. flavicollis) and bank voles (Myodes glareolus), in two woodlands. By integrating multi-species social networks and spatial overlap with individual microbiota data, we test how both conspecific and interspecific interactions shape gut microbiota composition. Results: At both study sites, social associations strongly predicted microbiota similarity among conspecific individuals, whereas spatial proximity consistently predicted microbiota similarity among interspecific pairs. In addition, social associations between mice of different species predicted microbiota similarity, although this effect was weaker than that observed within species and was asymmetric, with evidence for stronger microbial transmission from wood mice to yellow-necked mice than vice versa. By focusing on species-indicative bacterial taxa, we further show that wood mice with more social connections to yellow-necked mice harboured a greater richness of gut bacteria typical of yellow-necked mice. Conclusions: Together, these results demonstrate that individual-level social behaviour can influence gut microbial transmission across species boundaries, particularly among closely related species with overlapping ecological niches. Interspecific social interactions may therefore represent an underappreciated pathway for the acquisition of novel gut symbionts in multi-species communities.

papers.title: Extended Pavlovian conditioned approach training and devaluation in Long-Evans rats using time-restricted feeding
papers.abstract: Pavlovian conditioned approach (PCA) is a useful tool in studying compulsive- and addictive-like behaviors. PCA pairs a cue with reward delivery and rats typically differentiate into three phenotypes (sign-trackers, goal-trackers, and intermediates) based on behavior during the reward-paired cue presentation. Sign-trackers, who preferentially interact with the cue, are more likely to engage in compulsive behaviors and have decreased behavioral flexibility compared to goal-trackers, who preferentially interact with the food cup. However, one limitation to PCA is the use of food deprivation conditions that maintain rats at 80-90% of ad libitum weight, likely increasing stress which may bias animals towards sign-tracking behavior. Furthermore, most behavioral analysis only examines lever pressing and food cup entry, overlooking other behaviors that may better define phenotypes. In the current study male and female Long-Evans rats underwent an extended PCA training paradigm followed by satiety-induced reward devaluation under time-restricted feeding (TRF) conditions. Under TRF, rats continued to gain weight across PCA training and maintained caloric intake relative to ad libitum intake. Expanding the scope of behavioral analysis increased the proportion of ST rats in both early and late PCA training. Rats also increased the time spent interacting with the food cup during the inter-trial interval across extended PCA training. All rats were sensitive to satiety-induced reward devaluation, regardless of sex or devaluation condition. This study helps establish a PCA method optimized for Long-Evans rats with relevance for identifying PCA phenotypes contribution to dysregulated behavior in the context of chronic stress and obesity.

papers.title: Creation of genomic chimeras via megabase scale genome expansion
papers.abstract: An organism's physiology is controlled by its genomic content. Building genomic chimeras would enable melding of the diverse functions and properties of life. However, prior arts in genome synthesis are limited to reconstituting pre-existing functions within a singular genome rather than combining diverse genomic functions across multiple distinct genomes. Existing methods are also prohibitively expensive, labor intensive, and time consuming, and thus fundamentally not scalable for creating large synthetic chimeric genomes. To address all these limitations, we invented Additive Conjugative-CAST Engineering (ACE) combining conjugation with CRISPR-associated transposition (CAST) to deliver and integrate up to half a genome per step from a donor cell into a precisely defined position in the recipient's genome. We have demonstrated ACE's capability to integrate at least a 2-megabase donor genomic segment in a single step and at least 3 megabase in two consecutive steps. Importantly, we confirmed ACE's generality through the creation of multiple genomic chimeras across species, genus, and at least order barriers. With ACE, we further demonstrate such chimeric organisms, or what we call genome expanded organisms (GEOs), can be stably forged from at least three starting bacterial strains, and can be stably maintained to express all their acquired genomic parts in a single chimera. ACE offers a new paradigm of creating artificial lifeforms to combine desired properties and potentially create novel functions beyond the constraints of nature. ACE also offers a unique perspective to probe unexplored plasticity in genome architecture and expression patterns of novel, massively expanded genomes.

papers.title: Learning interpretable compositional features associated with continuous covariates
papers.abstract: Compositional variation as a function of continuous covariates, such as time, presents challenges for learning interpretable features and accounting for their construction in subsequent inference. Motivated by temporal change in isoform usage in genomics, we introduce IsoVita, a statistical framework integrating covariate-informed balance learning designed for compositional data with complementary tests for abrupt and gradual compositional variation. IsoVita estimates a dominant covariate-dependent direction in the log-ratio coordinates and approximates it as a log ratio of their geometric mean proportions between two learned component groups, linking statistical evidence to explicit component membership. Change point and spline tests evaluate this interpretable feature, while a selection-aware permutation procedure repeats feature construction and testing under each permutation. In transcript-level simulations, IsoVita maintained low empirical false discovery proportions with power to detect differences and change point accuracy improving as temporal signals strengthened. However, the performance depended on trajectory shape and study design. Applications to two human brain bulk RNA-sequencing datasets identified widespread temporal variation in isoform composition while retaining transcript-level interpretability. IsoVita integrates interpretable compositional feature learning with inference along continuous covariates, with potential applications beyond transcriptomics. IsoVita is available as a PyPI package (https://pypi.org/project/isovita).

papers.title: Widespread Saccharomyces hybridization in agave fermentations arises repeatedly from asymmetric parental diversity
papers.abstract: Interspecific hybridization can profoundly reshape genomes by bringing together divergent genetic backgrounds, yet its ecological and evolutionary dynamics remain poorly understood at the population level. Here, we identify an extensive hybridization system in traditional agave fermentations across Mexico involving Saccharomyces cerevisiae, a species frequently associated with human-managed environments, and its predominantly wild relative S. paradoxus. A genomic survey reveals unexpectedly high hybrid frequencies in geographically distant regions with contrasting environments. Targeted sampling of distilleries and surrounding natural sites reveals a strong ecological bias, with hybrids recovered almost exclusively from distilleries, although both parental species occur in anthropogenic and natural habitats. Hybrid genomes show extensive architectural diversity, including distinct ploidies, variable parental genome contributions, variable patterns of heterozygosity, and contrasting mitochondrial ancestries. Phylogenomic and population-structure analyses of hybrid subgenomes demonstrate multiple independent origins. These recurrent events show pronounced asymmetry in parental genetic diversity. Hybrids derive from several S. cerevisiae populations, already shaped by extensive introgression, whereas every S. paradoxus subgenome traces to a single genetically differentiated S. paradoxus lineage found exclusively in distilleries, an unexpected association for a predominantly wild species. These findings establish agave fermentations as an exceptional system for studying recurrent interspecific hybridization and reveal how pronounced asymmetry in parental ancestry can shape hybrid formation.

papers.title: Monounsaturated fatty acid depletion is a metabolic pattern of pathogenesis surveilled to activate p38 MAPK innate immunity
papers.abstract: Pathogen infection profoundly remodels host metabolism. Whether hosts sense specific pathogen-induced metabolic changes to identify microbial infection is not known. Here, we find that depletion the monounsaturated fatty acid oleate is a metabolic pattern of pathogenesis, specifically surveilled by the nematode C. elegans to identify active infection with a bacterial pathogen. We previously demonstrated that the enzymatic TIR (Toll/interleukin-1 receptor/resistance)-domain containing protein, TIR-1/SARM1, the key upstream activator of p38 MAPK PMK-1 immunity, is a guard protein in an effector-triggered immune response, positioned specifically on the surface of lysosome-related organelles to sense the toxic effects of bacterial infection. Here, we show that acute loss of oleate in intestinal cells during bacterial infection causes lysosome-related organelles to collapse, which induces the aggregation and activation of TIR-1/SARM1. Further, we find that oleate deficiency is a host vulnerability that concomitantly activates the c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) KGB-1 nutrient sensing pathway, an adaptive response that promotes expression of TIR-1/SARM1 on lysosome-related organelles and is required for survival during infection. These data establish a mechanistic connection between fatty acid nutrition and innate immune regulation, and reveal that specific changes in host metabolism are surveilled to identify pathogen attack.

papers.title: Sexing carnivores from faecal metagenomes: calibrating Rx for stone marten and red fox
papers.abstract: Knowing the sex of the animal that deposited a scat adds value to non-invasive monitoring, but read-ratio sexing methods were developed for human ancient DNA. We examined their use in shotgun metagenomes of seven stone marten (Martes foina) and red fox (Vulpes vulpes) scats. Human DNA, present in every library, was removed by competitive mapping against the host assembly and the human reference. Applying the Skoglund Ry metric to the marten samples yielded 0 to 25 Y-mapping reads per sample and failed to identify either of the two animals that Rx places firmly in the male range, so we adopted the X-to-autosome ratio Rx of Mittnik et al. instead, reimplemented as an open-source, species-agnostic Python tool. To test whether its human-derived thresholds transfer, we simulated female and male genomes of both species and drew 200 replicate subsamples at each of fourteen depths from 1,000 to 100,000 mapped reads. Nine of 11,200 replicates were assigned to the wrong sex, all of them below 2,000 mapped reads; above that depth the only failure was non-assignment, in under 5% of replicates above 7,500 reads and under 1% above 15,000. Applied to the scats, Rx identified four females and two males; one sample with 596 host-assigned reads was left unassigned. With competitive removal of human reads, Rx and its original thresholds are usable in these carnivores.

papers.title: Commensal Engineered Living Materials for Sustained Secretome Delivery and Wound Healing
papers.abstract: Using living cells as dynamic biological factories offers immense potential for the continuous, localized production of therapeutic proteins within compromised tissues. This strategy is particularly compelling for treating chronic non-healing wounds, which lack therapeutics that are able to function effectively in the inflammatory microenvironment. Commensal bacteria have been shown to promote healing in these hostile microenvironments, yet applying live microbes directly onto compromised tissue is clinically unfeasible due off-target safety risks and engraftment challenges. Herein, we establish a well-defined commensal Engineered Living Material (cELM) that allows encapsulation, retention, function, and delivery of native beneficial bacteria for localized production and release of a pro-healing secretome over weeks. We specifically encapsulated a pro-healing human wound bacterial isolate, Alcaligenes faecalis, using biocompatible, click-reactive hydrogel building blocks (thiol- or vinyl-sulfone-functionalized multi-arm poly(ethylene glycol)) and systematically varied the density of the polymer network and of the encapsulated bacteria to establish design rules for creating pro-healing cELMs. Physical confinement in the hydrogel network ensured bacterial biocontainment, while the hydrogel mesh size still permitted diffusion of the therapeutic secretome. Notably, controlling encapsulation density revealed an inverse relationship wherein lower cell densities yielded significantly enhanced per-cell metabolic activity and provided sustained production of pro-healing secreted factors. In a murine diabetic wound model, these A. faecalis cELMs shielded the encapsulated bacteria from host clearance, maintained biocontainment, accelerated re-epithelialization, and improved wound bed maturity. Together, these findings establish design principles for cELMs that couple bacterial biocontainment with sustained secretome delivery, providing a promising platform for localized treatment of chronic wounds.

papers.title: Individual differences reveal shared computational structure in perceptual decision-making
papers.abstract: To discover computational mechanisms of cognition, models typically specify a fixed psychological architecture, treating individual differences as variations within a predefined parameterization. Here, we take a different approach by using the population structure of individual differences to directly drive model discovery. We develop a low-rank neural network that uses this `population geometry' to learn shared computational components and participant-specific weights from trial-level choices, allowing cross-subject variation to constrain the model's architecture. Applied to perceptual decision-making in the Bernoulli Clicks Task across primary and replication datasets, out-of-sample prediction reveals a six-dimensional representation for individual differences: two continuous dimensions of temporal evidence weighting and two of choice-outcome history dependence, alongside participant-specific side bias and signal-to-noise ratio. This low-dimensional organization replicated in an independent dataset. Together, these findings reveal that seemingly disparate decision heuristics reflect different weightings over a small set of shared computational components, and establish a principled methodology for using behavioral variability to discover the mechanistic architecture of cognition.

papers.title: TACO: An open, interpretable model for microsecond-scale TCR specificity prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting antigen-induced T-cell activation from T-cell receptor (TCR) and peptide sequence remains difficult for TCRs and peptides not represented in training data. We present TACO (T-Cell Activation from Chemistry and Orientation), an open statistical model for predicting TCR specificity against HLA-A*02:01-presented peptides. TACO takes as input the peptide sequence and six TCR CDR loop sequences. Learning from binary activation labels, TACO selects a single canonical orientation of the CDR loops over the peptide and learns five amino-acid contact-potential matrices as well as two peptide-exposure profiles.The orientation is fixed and does not require experimentally determined or predicted structures. We evaluate TACO on held-out peptides separated by Levenshtein distance at least four from all training and validation peptides, limiting near-neighbor shortcut learning. TACO achieves AUROC 0.67 on a large held-out activation dataset and 0.68 on IMMREP25 HLA-A*02:01, exceeding the open structure-based models evaluated here and matching the reported AlphaFold3-TCRdock result. The model has 2,019 fitted parameters, retains most within-peptide ranking signal with TCR$\beta$ sequence alone, and reaches 406,000 TCR--peptide predictions per second on CPU. This throughput enables computational evaluation of large TCR-peptide search spaces. We show its potential use for prioritizing candidate target peptides from large peptide libraries, reducing the search space for downstream experimental investigation. TACO fitted parameters also expose candidate physicochemical patterns that can be inspected directly. We release TACO's parameters and complete training, evaluation, and inference code.

papers.title: RPFace: From biased structural benchmarks to generalizable RNA-protein interface prediction
papers.abstract: Modeling protein-RNA complexes with co-folding and docking methods is routine, yet these methods are evaluated on benchmarks whose composition mirrors the deposited structures on which they were trained or tuned, leaving open whether their reported performance reflects true generalization. Here, we focus the evaluation on the region that carries the biological signal: the binding interface. For the first time, we construct and release a fair benchmark that stratifies protein-RNA data into distinct structural and experimental groups, providing a more stringent test of generalization than aggregate averages. On this benchmark, we find that accuracy of detecting the binding site using co-folding methods is concentrated in ribosomal complexes and varies systematically with factors such as experimental modality. For docking methods, it is reliable only when the input conformations are already close to the bound state, and it is inconsistent across RNA classes. Both families of methods fail to transfer to in vivo CLIP experiments. To address this gap, we introduce RPFace, to the best of our knowledge the first model that jointly predicts the binding preference of every protein residue and every RNA nucleotide directly from sequence, requiring no experimental structure, template, or multiple sequence alignment. RPFace combines an ensemble of predicted secondary structures with a multi-modal embedding-enrichment scheme that fuses representations from RNA foundation models and structure prediction models. Unlike existing approaches, it is a very small and fast model that delivers stable performance across structural and experimental conditions, is robust to conformational change, and generalizes to in vivo datasets without extensive pretraining. As a result, RPFace matches the state-of-the-art methods on protein interfaces with no evolutionary information, and outperforms them on RNA interfaces, with the largest gains in zero-shot settings despite using only sequence information. The model, code, and data are available at Github.

papers.title: Genomic evidence of a single domestication origin for modern cattle
papers.abstract: Domesticated cattle occur as humpless taurine and humped zebu, historically explained as two independent domestications in the Fertile Crescent and Indus Valley. We question the validity of this model using whole-genome analyses of cattle and their wild relatives, including extinct aurochs. Zebu derives from admixture between domesticated taurine cattle and Indian aurochs and has elevated genomic diversity from an ancient introgression of a gaur-like or banteng-like population into Indian aurochs. We identify selective introgression in zebu from both 238 Indian aurochs-derived genes enriched for environmental adaptation, and 283 taurine-derived genes enriched for domestication loci. We suggest this process was shaped by polygenic selection. Modern cattle diversity traces from a single domestication event, followed by migration, wild introgression, and selection.

papers.title: Global Data Fitting Enables Kinetic Dissection of Cullin-RING Ligase-Catalyzed Ubiquitylation: From Substrate Priming to Poly-ubiquitin Chain Formation
papers.abstract: The discovery and characterization of the ubiquitin system was founded on classical enzymology approaches that established fundamental principles of protein ubiquitylation. Cullin-RING ligases (CRLs) represent the largest class of human ubiquitin ligases, yet detailed enzymology of these multi-subunit assemblies has lagged behind other systems such as nucleic acid polymerases. Here, we employed pre-steady state kinetics and global data fitting using KinTek Explorer to systematically investigate the kinetic parameters controlling CRL-dependent ubiquitin transfer. Using a well-characterized in vitro reconstituted system exploring CUL2-dependent CRLs, we modeled substrate priming, showing that the system is highly amenable to global fitting of kinetic data. The results show that product dissociation from the CRL is significantly slower than substrate dissociation, explaining previously reported slow steady-state ubiquitylation rates. Extending this framework to poly-ubiquitin chain formation revealed catalytic efficiencies 15-42-fold greater than substrate priming. Comparative analysis of CUL1-dependent and CUL2-dependent systems showed remarkably similar kinetic parameters, including the Km of ubiquitin-carrying enzyme for CRLs, despite differences in substrate receptor and enzyme architecture. We further examined drug-induced neo-substrate ubiquitylation using the pomalidomide-CRBN-SALL4 system, revealing atypical kinetics characterized by rapid ubiquitin transfer paired with an elevated Km, ultimately yielding catalytic efficiencies comparable to natural substrates. The findings establish pre-steady state kinetics and global data fitting as powerful enzymological tools for dissecting CRL-dependent ubiquitylation across different CRL families and substrate contexts, with important implications for understanding both physiological ubiquitylation and therapeutic targeted protein degradation strategies.

papers.title: Single-cell multi-omics identify OTP and NOVA1 as regulators of leptin action in hypothalamic feeding circuits
papers.abstract: Leptin acts directly and indirectly on multiple neuronal populations to regulate feeding and numerous other physiologic functions. However, our understanding of how a single circulating signal coordinates diverse neuronal populations across multiple circuits is limited. To further elucidate how leptin reshapes molecular states in its direct and indirect neural targets, we combined time-resolved single-nucleus transcriptomics and chromatin accessibility profiling to map leptin-induced transcriptional and chromatin state changes across individual neurons in two key hypothalamic nuclei: the arcuate nucleus (ARC), which contains the majority of leptin receptor (LepR) neurons, and the paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus (PVH), an established downstream target of ARC LepR neurons. We found that leptin treatment of leptin-deficient ob/ob mice does not alter neuronal identity, but instead induces coordinated, cell-type-specific transcriptional and regulatory state changes that propagate hierarchically from the ARC to downstream PVH neurons. Integrating RNA velocity, cis-regulatory analysis, and cell-cell communication inference revealed that leptin modulates hypothalamic circuit architecture by selectively strengthening specific interactions while pruning broadly distributed, low-specificity signaling. Although leptin broadly activated STAT3 signaling across LepR neuronal subtypes, integrated multi-omic analyses revealed that activation of STAT3 engages distinct downstream regulatory programs in different neuronal populations, often with opposing physiological functions. Functional analyses identified the homeobox transcription factor OTP, a leptin-responsive regulator selectively induced in AGRP neurons, as a critical mediator of leptin-mediated inhibition of hunger-promoting AGRP neuronal activity and feeding. In parallel, unbiased analysis of PVH neuronal state transitions shows that NOVA1, an RNA-binding protein primarily expressed in inhibitory neurons, is regulated by leptin and alterations of NOVA1 expression bidirectionally control food intake and body weight. Together, these findings define a multi-layered regulatory framework through which leptin regulates hypothalamic feeding circuits to control energy balance.

papers.title: An unprecedented codon reassignment and two new genetic code variants in ciliates
papers.abstract: Ciliates are well-known for frequent nuclear genetic code changes. However, the exploration of ciliate nuclear genomes is an unfinished enterprise, and particular genetic code variants have been previously attributed to some ciliate lineages without solid evidence. We focused on two such groups, the class Litostomatea and deeply-branching lineages of the class Spirotrichea, and by analysing their genomes and transcriptomes we found that some of them employ genetic code variants differing from those suggested before. Particularly notable is the spirotrichean genus Licnophora, which we found to exhibit an unprecedented combination of codon reassignments, i.e. a new genetic code variant. In Licnophora spp., each of the three standard stop codons has a different altered meaning: UAA encodes glutamate, UAG glutamine, and UGA exhibits homonymy, encoding arginine when present in-frame and terminating translation at the coding sequence ends. Contrary to some previous claims, our analyses demonstrated that litostomateans generally employ the standard genetic code, with a single identified exception, the species Balantidium ctenopharyngodoni, which exhibits a codon reassignment never reported before: UGA encoding leucine. Whereas tRNAs decoding the reassigned UAA and UAG codons in Licnophora and UGA in B. ctenopharyngodoni were readily identified in the respective genomic data, the mechanism of UGA decoding as arginine in Licnophora and certain other spirotricheans remains elusive. Our results paint a more complex picture of genetic code evolution in Spirotrichea than assumed before and necessitate an update of the current list of genetic code variants to allow for an accurate prediction of protein sequences in ciliates.

papers.title: Transcriptome reallocation during infection reshapes synonymous codon demand in Botrytis cinerea
papers.abstract: While genomic codon usage is fixed within an individual isolate, the synonymous codons represented in its RNA pool can change when transcription shifts among genes. We tested whether this transcript-level phenotype accompanies infection by reanalyzing 39 libraries from three public Botrytis cinerea RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) time series in S. lycopersicum, Arabidopsis thaliana, and Physcomitrium patens. Gene counts were corrected for coding length, combined with fixed gene-specific codon inventories, and analyzed as centered log ratios within synonymous amino-acid families. Sampling time accounted for 95-98% of fungal codon-demand variation in each series. The association persisted after effective-length correction, unique-only competitive mapping, host-homology exclusion, depth equalization, protein-family weighting, and removal of translation-associated genes. Change vectors over the interpolated, time-aligned 16-24-h interval were positively aligned among studies, whereas later trajectories diverged. Matched reassignments of complete expression trajectories showed more full-series organization than expected in S. lycopersicum and Arabidopsis, but not in P. patens. Codon-preference-weighted abundance and expression breadth also changed through infection, although their directions were not universal. Across systems, large non-translation contributors repeatedly carried ATP-synthase/respiratory and extracellular annotations, although their timing and companion functions differed. Infection-associated transcriptional reallocation therefore repeatedly restructures the synonymous composition of the inferred fungal transcript pool. This establishes a dynamic allocation phenotype and a basis for testing consequences for RNA stability and translation during host-pathogen interactions.

papers.title: Targeting REV1 Exposes Context-Dependent Therapeutic Responses in Colorectal Cancer
papers.abstract: Translesion synthesis (TLS) promotes DNA damage tolerance and contributes to chemotherapy resistance by enabling replication across damaged DNA templates. REV1, a central TLS regulator, is a potential therapeutic target to enhance the efficacy of genotoxic chemotherapy. Here, we investigated the therapeutic consequences of pharmacologic and genetic REV1 targeting in colorectal cancer (CRC) and evaluated the sensitivity of patient-derived CRC organoids to the REV1 inhibitor JH-RE-06. JH-RE-06 enhanced oxaliplatin sensitivity in HCT116 cells and 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) sensitivity in HT-29 cells, whereas reciprocal combinations produced limited sensitization, indicating treatment- and cellular context-dependent responses. siRNA-mediated REV1 depletion similarly enhanced chemotherapy sensitivity, supporting REV1 involvement in these responses. MNNG sensitivity assays and MLH1 expression analyses did not reveal consistent treatment-associated changes in mismatch repair function, while targeted HPRT1 sequencing identified no detectable sequence alterations in the region examined. Chemosensitization was not accompanied by consistent increases in caspase-3/7 activation under the conditions tested. REV1 inhibition also caused LC3-II accumulation and, after prolonged inhibitor exposure, reduced beta-tubulin abundance, indicating additional autophagy-associated and cytoskeletal responses. In two patient-derived CRC organoid models, JH-RE-06 exhibited single-agent growth-inhibitory activity, with mean IC50 values of 2.01 micromolar and 1.4 micromolar, respectively. Together, these findings demonstrate context-dependent chemosensitization and organoid growth inhibition following REV1 targeting, suggesting that its therapeutic consequences may extend beyond canonical TLS-mediated DNA damage tolerance.

papers.title: Mathematical model of phenotypic plasticity predicts interconversion is a drug target for neuroblastoma.
papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma is a paediatric cancer arising from the sympathetic nervous system as neural crest cells, made up of noradrenergic (NOR/ADRN/N), mesenchymal like (MES/S), and intermediate (I-type/I) cell types. These cells can interconvert between types, contributing to treatment resistance and relapse. We developed a mathematical model to investigate how interconversion patterns affect the efficacy of phenotype-specific inhibitors. We used three ordinary differential equations to describe the dynamics of the three populations, including logistic growth, interconversion, and drug-induced death. Of the 64 possible interconversion patterns, five reduced the target population: two for N cells and three for S cells. N targeting patterns were more effective with higher interconversion rates, while mesenchymal targeting patterns were more effective with lower interconversion rates. Stability analysis revealed that natural tumour growth was always unstable, but during treatment, N-suppressing patterns combined with an S inhibitor gave the most consistently stable origin. Testing multi-stage and cyclic treatment schedules revealed that N-suppressing patterns with an S inhibitor, followed by an S-suppressing pattern with an N inhibitor, achieved more reliable remission. Three of the five patterns of interest correspond to reported biological plausibility, and known compounds exist to induce most of the required transitions, supporting the clinical relevance of these strategies for improving neuroblastoma treatment outcomes.

papers.title: A Minimal Synthetic Cleavage Module Enables Selective Degradation of Pathogenic r(CUG) Repeats in Cells
papers.abstract: Although direct RNA degradation offers an alternative to occupancy-driven activity, it has relied on complex natural product-derived cleavage modules such as bleomycin. Here, we show that a compact synthetic Fe(II)-coordinating warhead can be programmed for selective RNA degradation in cells. Coupling this cleavage module to a small molecule that recognizes expanded r(CUG) repeats that cause myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) afforded selective degradation of the pathogenic RNA while sparing wild type and transcripts harboring short r(CUG) repeats. In DM1 patient-derived myoblasts, degradation of mutant repeat RNA reduced DM1-associated pathology including formation of nuclear foci, sequestration of MBNL1, and alternative pre-mRNA splicing defects, without inducing DNA damage. These studies establish that minimal synthetic cleavage modules can replace complex natural product warheads to enable selective degradation of disease-causing RNAs in cells.

papers.title: An expanded evolutionary landscape of H3 histones with variants that destabilize nucleosomes and promote chromatin accessibility
papers.abstract: Histones are among the most conserved proteins in eukaryotes, yet many animal lineages have evolved divergent histone variants with specialized functions. Some broadly conserved variants (e.g., H3.3) have been linked to the regulation of chromatin accessibility in stem cells, but whether highly divergent variants function similarly remains unclear. Here, we characterize the histone repertoire of the acoel Hofstenia miamia, an animal that can undergo whole-body regeneration using adult pluripotent stem cells (aPSCs). We identify two novel histone H3 paralogs, H3-a and H3-b, that are expressed in aPSCs and form a lineage-specific sister clade to H3.2 and H3.3. Despite substantial sequence divergence and reduced compatibility with canonical chaperone machinery, both variants assemble bona fide nucleosomes in vitro. These nucleosomes exhibit reduced stability and incomplete DNA wrapping, and a cryo-EM structure of the H3-b nucleosome reveals the disruption of conserved histone-DNA contacts. In vivo, H3-a and H3-b are upregulated following injury, and their depletion reduces genome-wide chromatin accessibility, suggesting a role in the maintenance of accessible chromatin during regeneration. A survey of H3 sequences across animal phyla shows that H3-a and H3-b belong to a broader landscape of highly divergent H3 proteins, some of which exhibit sequence differences across both the N-terminal tail and histone-fold domain. Together, these findings link histone sequence diversification to chromatin regulation in aPSCs and highlight the underappreciated evolutionary diversity and functional potential of divergent animal H3 proteins.

papers.title: Satellite cell glucocorticoid receptor restrains myogenic commitment without mediating the effects of therapeutic glucocorticoids on muscle repair
papers.abstract: Glucocorticoids (GCs) exert profound effects on skeletal muscle, but the contribution of satellite cell (SatC) glucocorticoid receptor (GR) signaling to muscle regeneration remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the role of GR in SatC homeostasis and assessed whether SatC GR mediates the effects of therapeutic GCs on muscle repair. Conditional deletion of GR in SatC reduced the number of PAX7-positive cells during regeneration in young mice, but did not substantially impair muscle repair in either young or aged animals. Transcriptomic and chromatin profiling revealed that GR occupies genes involved in stem cell fate and developmental signaling, with extensive GR binding already established in quiescent SatC. GR-deficient quiescent SatC showed reduced expression of Yap1, Runx1 and Foxo1, together with increased Myog expression. Similarly, GR silencing in human myoblasts induced early myogenic differentiation markers without affecting proliferation, supporting a conserved role for GR in restraining myogenic commitment. We next examined the effects of two therapeutic GCs on muscle regeneration. Chronic prednisone treatment altered the transcriptional landscape of regenerating muscle in an age-dependent manner, without substantially affecting histological repair. In contrast, dexamethasone administration during the early inflammatory phase delayed regeneration, with persistent necrosis and increased collagen deposition. These effects were comparable in control and SatC-specific GR-deficient mice, indicating that they do not require GR in SatC. Together, these findings identify GR as a regulator of the quiescent, undifferentiated state of SatC, while showing that the effects of therapeutic GCs on muscle repair are largely independent of SatC GR. They further highlight the importance of treatment regimen and physiological context in determining the effects of GCs on skeletal muscle regeneration.

papers.title: The biochemical composition of coronavirus Nucleocapsid proteins drives the bicistronic properties of their sub-genomic mRNAs
papers.abstract: The nucleocapsid (N) gene of coronaviruses (CoVs) encodes a structural RNA-binding protein required for viral assembly. In SARS- and MERS-CoV viruses, reading frame 2 of N contains an overlapping open reading frame (ORF) encoding an innate immune antagonist accessory protein. However, the extent of this dual coding capacity across the CoV family, and the genetic features driving overlapping ORF formation, remain unexamined. Here, we developed an in-silico tool (ORFan) to screen structural gene sub-genomic mRNA sequences from 152 species of coronavirus for the presence of overlapping accessory gene candidates. We found that frame 2 of the N gene in Alpha-, Beta- and Delta-CoVs frequently contains a potential accessory ORF (AcORF), conserved at the subgenus level, unlike the spike, envelope and membrane genes. We also show that CoV nucleotide biases in conjunction with codon biases integral to N protein function drive the relatively high abundances of start codons in frame two and stop codons in frame three, explaining the tendency towards frame 2 AcORFs. We further suggest that viral nucleotide biases and the codon composition required for RNA-binding function facilitate overlapping ORF formation in other virus families

papers.title: Body size cascades from Neodiprion sawfly hosts to Perilampid parasitoids: An investigation of sequential divergence
papers.abstract: Ecological speciation drives diversity in plant-eating insect systems, but it may also generate parallel specialization in parasitoid associates in a cascading effect of "sequential divergence." However, sequential divergence has never been successfully identified in parasitoids of externally feeding insects. To address this gap, we consider the Pinus-Neodiprion-Perilampus neodiprioni system, where plant-associated, externally feeding Neodiprion demonstrate ecological divergence, as supported by body size as a magic trait in sympatric species. It seems possible that this body size differentiation may cascade to Neodiprion's parasitoids via sequential divergence. Therefore, we asked, "Does P. neodiprioni exhibit host-specific divergence in body size that parallels patterns in Neodiprion hosts?" Further, "Does P. neodiprioni exhibit host-related variation in the abdominal region or sexually dimorphic features, supporting reproductive barriers?" Using by-catch samples, we measured body size of P. neodiprioni, reared from Neodiprion lecontei and Neodiprion pinetum hosts. We analyzed body size variation as predicted by host species, parasitoid sex, host sex, host cocoon size, latitude, and their interactions. In addition, we used mixed models to analyze the effects of parasitoid sex and Neodiprion host on three size-based facial features. We found that P. neodiprioni demonstrates host-associated body size variation that mirrors size differences in their Neodiprion hosts. In addition, host-associated size variation occurs in the abdominal region and two sexually dimorphic characters of P. neodiprioni, supporting possible reproductive isolation. Together, these patterns suggest that host magic traits may drive not only within-species ecological divergence, but they can facilitate parasitoids' subsequent morphological differentiation and possible sequential divergence.

papers.title: The long noncoding RNA FOSIL shapes the dynamics of FOS induction
papers.abstract: Immediate-early genes require rapid, transient, and precisely tuned transcriptional activation in response to extracellular signals, yet how this kinetic precision is achieved remains poorly understood. We characterize FOSIL (LINC01220), an inducible lncRNA locus downstream of FOS. Depleting FOSIL RNA delays heregulin (HRG)-induced FOS mRNA and protein accumulation and prolongs the response, indicating that FOSIL sharpens both the onset and the shutoff of the induction wave. Capture Micro-C maps show that FOSIL depletion weakens the chromatin boundary between FOS and FOSIL and increases local compaction across the pre-assembled FOS-FOSIL neighborhood during serum starvation, demonstrating that basal FOSIL production maintains a locally insulated, poised conformation prior to signal arrival. Upon HRG stimulation, FOSIL depletion blunts the rapid movement of the locus toward nuclear speckles, diminishes early speckle-proximal FOS transcription, and extends late firing at speckle-distant alleles. At single transcription active sites, nascent FOSIL activity correlates with closer speckle proximity and higher FOS output, and activating the endogenous FOSIL promoter by CRISPRa, but not supplying FOSIL RNA in trans, enhances both speckle association and FOS induction. Together, these findings support a mechanism where endogenous FOSIL activity coordinates pre-stimulus chromatin folding with dynamic nuclear speckle positioning to fine-tune the onset, amplitude, and resolution of immediate-early gene expression.

papers.title: Quantitative live imaging reveals region-dependent medulloblastoma disseminationin the zebrafish brain
papers.abstract: Medulloblastoma is the most common malignant pediatric brain tumor, and relapse is frequently driven by dissemination within the central nervous system. Yet the early dynamics of tumor spread remain difficult to resolve in vivo. Here, we orthotopically transplanted human medulloblastoma cells into larval zebrafish and followed individual xenografts by longitudinal high-resolution confocal imaging. ONS-76 showed particularly robust dissemination, with hindbrain tumors spreading into the developing cerebellum in 81.5% of larvae, more than fourfold the frequency observed for forebrain or midbrain tumors. Disseminating cells extended along brain-surface and leptomeningeal-like regions and frequently associated with cerebral vasculature. Quantitative analysis of tumor area, perimeter, compactness, convex hull area, and fractal dimension captured changes in growth and spatial complexity over time. Dasatinib reduced tumor expansion and dissemination-related features in a concentration-dependent manner, while higher doses revealed host toxicity. These findings establish a powerful in vivo model for resolving medulloblastoma dissemination and therapeutic response.

papers.title: Automahout: an autonomous image analysis system for cell tracking
papers.abstract: Cell tracking in time-lapse images is complex image analysis that involves detection, linking and proofreading, often requiring the algorithm to be tuned for every new dataset. We present Automahout, an autonomous agent for the Mastodon/ELEPHANT platform that carries out these operations. It looks at the data and tries existing models; where none fits, it annotates reference cells, trains a detector from those sparse annotations, reviews its output against them and feeds the corrections back until its own stopping criteria are met. It then links, checks the lineage and moves on. On three public datasets, a 2D fluorescence culture, a 2D phase-contrast culture and a 3D embryo, it produced lineages without human input and reached TRA scores of 0.95-0.96.

papers.title: scDisentangle: sequential disentanglement for single-cell perturbation response prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting the transcriptional response of single cells to perturbation is a central goal of single-cell modeling, with broad application to analysis and experimental design. Existing methods often fail to beat simple baselines and offer little insight into how biological variation is organized. We present scDisentangle, a model that decomposes single-cell expression into observed attributes and a sequence of residual components, generating counterfactuals that preserve source cell identity. scDisentangle outperformed current models and naive baselines on cytokine stimulation, liver infection, and unseen combinatorial genetic perturbations, on which accuracy was largely independent of how closely a response resembled the average perturbation effect. In an immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis cohort, cell-resolved counterfactuals predicted donor-specific intracardiac CD8+ T cell states from peripheral blood. In a castration-regeneration prostate atlas, predictions recapitulated luminal dynamics and progenitor-marker kinetics upon androgen add-back. scDisentangle's coarse-to-fine latent structure aligned with hematopoietic lineage organization, with early levels capturing a less differentiated core progressively refined into cell-type-specific programs.

papers.title: A reporter mouse model to map RIG-I expression and function in vivo
papers.abstract: The cytosolic RNA sensor RIG-I is a critical component of the innate immune response to RNA viruses, yet few tools exist to track RIG-I in vivo. Herein, we report the development of a RIG-I reporter mouse, termed RIG-ImScar, that enables fluorescence imaging and tractable immunoprecipitation of RIG-I in vivo. These mice revealed enrichment of RIG-I expression in circulatory, lymphoid, and mucosal tissues and broad expression across immune cell types. RIG-I itself is upregulated in response to IFN. To distinguish RIG-I sentinel cells, which are programmed to express RIG-I at steady state, from IFN-responder cells, we crossed RIG-ImScar mice with Mx1GFP mice. Blocking IFNAR with a monoclonal antibody showed that basal RIG-I expression in immune cells was largely independent of type I IFN signaling, although Ly6Chi monocytes required IFNAR for RIG-I expression. To probe functional responses in vivo, we intranasally administered a RIG-I-specific agonist, SLR14. Mapping RIG-I expression across the lung identified alveolar macrophages as a critical RIG-I sensor cell population, and depletion of alveolar macrophages, but not neutrophils, slightly impaired lung IFN responses. Together, these findings support the use of the RIG-ImScar model to probe RIG-I dynamics in vivo and predict functional sensor cell populations across tissues.

papers.title: Auditory Evoked Potentials Differ from Controls and Correlate with Aspects of Cognition in Kabuki Syndrome and Rubinstein-Taybi Syndrome
papers.abstract: Objective Kabuki syndrome (KS) and Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome (RSTS) are two disorders caused by dysfunctional components of the epigenetic machinery and both result in intellectual disability. Mouse models of both KS and RSTS have seen reversal of cognitive impairment with epigenetic treatments. However, a great need exists for biomarkers in these disorders to improve the likelihood of successful clinical trials. This study aimed to investigate cortical auditory evoked potentials (AEPs) in KS and RSTS so that it could potentially be developed into a response biomarker in the future. Methods The amplitude of the N1-P2-N2 complex was measured for passive listening to monotonal auditory stimuli in individuals with KS, with RSTS, and typically developing controls. A standardized cognitive assessment battery was performed and specific subtests were correlated with AEP values. Results Groups differed significantly in P2, N2, and P2-N2 amplitude although RSTS was consistently more different from typically developing controls than was KS. The mid- to late-phase AEP components (P2 and N2) also correlate with cognition within and across these groups particularly with language whereas earlier components N1 and P2 correlate more with measures of executive functioning. Conclusion Late-phase components of AEPs differ in KS and RSTS from each other and from controls. KS and RSTS differ from controls in P2 and N2 amplitude in the same direction and both show a positive correlation between language and P2 amplitude and a negative correlation between language and N2 amplitude. Together they also show an association with N1 and P2 amplitude and executive functioning. Significance AEPs may turn out to be a valuable response biomarker in KS and RSTS individually and together.

papers.title: Do divergent mitochondrial backgrounds alter the fate of nuclear alleles during hybridization and admixture?
papers.abstract: Hybridization brings together genetic variation from different populations or species into admixed genomes. As selection sorts this variation, the fate of each allele is determined by its fitness effect in the new hybrid genomic background. Because mitochondrial genes coevolve with the nuclear genome, they may be especially sensitive to foreign nuclear backgrounds, making them potential "hot-spots" for hybrid incompatibilities. Here, we test whether selection against mitonuclear incompatibilities drives repeatable hybridization outcomes. Specifically, we experimentally evolved three sets of five populations of hybrid Drosophila melanogaster, each carrying the same nuclear chromosomes but paired with one of three increasingly divergent mitochondrial DNA backgrounds. We hypothesized that accumulated incompatibilities would result in different patterns of nuclear admixture among mitochondrial backgrounds. To test this, we tracked nuclear allele frequencies in all 15 populations by whole-genome sequencing at intermediate time points. After 25 generations, we observed that rapid genomic evolution produced a strikingly parallel mosaic of both nuclear ancestries, independent of mitochondrial background. Contrary to our hypothesis, we found no evidence that mitochondrial background1 shaped nuclear admixture, even for interspecific combinations. These results suggest that in species with large effective population sizes, efficient purifying selection limits the accumulation of mitonuclear incompatibilities, allowing selection on nuclear alleles to promote repeatable ancestry sorting immediately following hybridization.

papers.title: U-statistics-based Pairwise Discordance Regression for Joint Mean-Variability Inference in Longitudinal Studies with Missing Data
papers.abstract: Longitudinal studies are central to scientific inquiry across disciplines; yet, statistical analyses have predominantly focused on mean trajectories while treating variability as a secondary or nuisance component. Increasing evidence suggests that temporal variability and heterogeneity themselves encode critical scientific information, particularly in studies with repeated measurements, heterogeneous populations, or rich covariate structures. The classical mixed-effects and location-scale model family represents variability through latent variable components but relies on strong parametric assumptions and often requires numerical approximation or computationally intensive estimation. Here we introduce the semiparametric pairwise discordance regression, a unified framework for longitudinal data that directly models pairwise contrasts to simultaneously characterize mean trajectories, between-subject heterogeneity, and within-subject temporal variability. By targeting pairwise discordances rather than latent variance components, the proposed approach enables robust inference without specifying full parametric distributions for latent components or error terms, provided the specified conditional moment restrictions hold. Pair-level covariate encodings further accommodate flexible covariate structures and allow variability parameters to be interpreted through pairwise contrasts or dissimilarities. Estimation and inference are carried out via (weighted) U-statistic-based generalized estimating equations (UGEE) with a valid sandwich variance estimator, and we extend the fitting procedure to accommodate missing-at-random dropout. We establish the asymptotic distributions of the resulting estimators under mild regularity conditions. Simulation studies demonstrate reliable finite-sample performance in the settings considered, including non-Gaussian errors and misspecified working correlation structures, whereas likelihood-based parametric fits can be sensitive to distributional assumptions or numerically unstable. An application to longitudinal blood pressure during pregnancy illustrates the framework on real data.

papers.title: Modeling circadian rhythm splitting under chronic light and the asymmetric transition kinetics between lighting conditions
papers.abstract: In various vertebrates, chronic light splits the single daily 24-h circadian activity bout into two 12-h behavioral components per cycle, yet the underlying mechanism remains unresolved. Here, we develop a two-lobe biophysical model of the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) to understand this phenomenon. By representing the master clock as interacting ventral core and dorsal shell populations of Kuramoto-type oscillators across bilateral lobes, we suggest that chronic light changes the excitation/inhibition (E/I) balance orchestrated by GABA, which either inhibits or excites SCN neurons. Under constant darkness, excitation dominates and provides in-phase synchronization of the populations. Under chronic light, inhibition dominates, and the ipsilateral and contralateral couplings among the core and shell populations become negative. Consequently, the shells in the left and right lobes oscillate in antiphase, producing the 12-h behavioral rhythm in downstream tissues. We suggest that this E/I balance is shifted by a light-induced change in the expression of chloride cotransporters in SCN neurons. Another key novelty is the introduction of the biologically motivated dynamics of chloride cotransporter expression, which explains the sign inversion of ipsilateral and contralateral couplings under time-varying lighting conditions. The model also reproduces the effects of unilateral SCN lesions: if one lobe is abolished, the remaining intact lobe autonomously stabilizes into a single-bout circadian output with a period comparable to that of the intact system. Finally, we compare our results with experimental data and demonstrate a close agreement.

papers.title: Active site electrostatic effects modulate DBO inhibitor potency against OXA-48 variants
papers.abstract: The OXA-48 class D {beta}-lactamase and its variants are clinically concerning through their carbapenemase and cephalosporinase activity. Effective inhibitors are therefore urgently needed. Diazabicyclooctanes (DBOs) are newly introduced non {beta}-lactam based inhibitors, but their potency is affected by mutations, with the more recently developed nacubactam consistently less potent than avibactam, the first DBO, towards OXA-48 variants. This difference is most pronounced for OXA-48 compared to its variants OXA-163 and -405, which contain mutations in the {beta}5-{beta}6 loop and preferentially hydrolyse cephalosporins over carbapenems. Here we use multiscale simulations to uncover the origin of these differences after determining that the second step of DBO acylation is rate-limiting. Using QM/MM MD simulations we show that nacubactam exhibits a consistently higher energy barrier than avibactam for covalent inhibition of OXA-48-like enzymes, a difference attributable to DBO-specific changes in the active site electric field. Simulations of non-covalent complexes further indicate that weaker binding, due to electrostatic repulsion between the positively charged nacubactam tail and Arg214 in the {beta}5-{beta}6 loop, partially explains the lower potency of nacubactam towards OXA-48, compared to OXA-163 and -405. Combining computational predictions of covalent reaction rates and non-covalent binding affinities accurately reproduces the relative order of experimental IC50 values, and predicts potency towards OXA-517, a recently discovered OXA-48 variant capable of hydrolysing many antibiotics. This work provides mechanistic insight into the inhibition of class D {beta}-lactamases and reveals the origins of differential DBO potency towards OXA-48 variants, highlighting how subtle differences between enzymes modulate inhibitory effects.

papers.title: Organotchi: an open-source tool for the automated segmentation, morphological characterization, and longitudinal tracking of organoids
papers.abstract: Neural organoids are three-dimensional stem cell-derived models widely used to study brain development and model disease. Brightfield imaging offers a non-invasive readout of their growth and morphology, and recent advances have made automated organoid segmentation from such images increasingly attainable. Yet existing tools largely leave morphological characterization, quality assessment, and comparisons between conditions to manual or ad hoc analysis. Here we present Organotchi, an open-source tool that integrates automated segmentation with longitudinal morphological analysis of neural organoids. Organotchi quantifies ten morphological features, including area, perimeter, and eccentricity, and tracks cystic structures over time, reports variability within and between batches, and flags outlier organoids and segmentation failures, supporting objective organoid characterization and enhancing downstream analysis. As a proof of concept, we apply Organotchi to disease modelling, pharmacological perturbation, and protocol optimization in neural organoids. One use case assesses drug response in breast cancer spheroids, demonstrating its use beyond its development domain.

papers.title: Geometric Morphometrics of Pistillate Flowers in Astrocaryum sect. Huicungo (Arecaceae): Taxonomic Implications for the Peruvian Species
papers.abstract: The taxonomy of the Amazonian palm clade Astrocaryum sect. Huicungo remains controversial due to deep discordances between traditional classifications based on qualitative floral traits and recent phylogenomic evidence. To address this, landmark-based two-dimensional geometric morphometrics (4 landmarks, 16 semilandmarks) was applied to evaluate the symmetric component of shape variation in calyx and corolla structures across 549 pistillate flowers from the 11 Peruvian species. Although multivariate analyses (PCA, CVA) revealed continuous morphological variation and extensive phenotypic overlap, perianth geometry retained a significant diagnostic signal. Cross-validated classification rates demonstrated that the corolla exhibited higher discriminatory power than the calyx, while the combined perianth analysis (calyx + corolla) maximized taxonomic assignment accuracy. Furthermore, Mahalanobis distance-based clustering did not replicate traditional subsections: A. chonta and A. ulei exhibited divergent architectures, whereas A. carnosum, A. faranae, and A. huicungo shared profound geometric similarity. This study demonstrates that quantitative perianth morphometrics is a valuable tool for species delimitation in Astrocaryum, supporting the re-evaluation of traditional taxonomic boundaries through an integrative approach.

papers.title: Epigenome-informed Polymer Modeling Reveals Chromosome Folding Landscapes across Distinct Genetic and Epigenetic Contexts
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) genome organization is critical for gene regulation, enabling long-range interactions between genes and distal regulatory elements. Genomic structural variations and epigenetic differences can perturb this organization, contributing to phenotypic variation and tissue-specific gene regulation. Prior studies have assessed the impact of these genetic and epigenetic changes on 3D genome folding, primarily using population-averaged features such as topologically associating domains and loops. However, growing evidence from single-cell and live-imaging studies indicates that chromosomes are highly dynamic and exist as heterogeneous ensembles of conformations. Here, we applied an epigenetic-state-informed polymer modeling framework to generate chromosomal conformational ensembles directly from cell- and tissue-specific epigenomic data. The resulting ensembles reproduced experimental Hi-C maps across cell lines and tissue types. Comparison of these conformational ensembles revealed that, although polymer dynamics were conserved across cell lines, their folding landscapes diverged. These differences arose primarily from cell-line-specific chromatin-state interaction networks and were concentrated in rare, long-lived contacts. Furthermore, modeling a TAD-boundary-disrupting deletion without re-optimizing the model parameters indicated a shift in the chromatin conformational ensemble from predominantly insulated to predominantly fused states. The modeled deletion also selectively strengthened active chromatin contacts and differentially disrupted enhancer contacts involving neighboring genes. Finally, comparison of two tissue types from the same donor revealed epigenetically driven rewiring of chromatin-state interaction networks. These findings establish chromosomal conformational ensembles as a sensitive readout of genome reorganization across distinct genetic and epigenetic contexts.

papers.title: Cell-scale confinement reorders bacterial speed rankings
papers.abstract: Which bacterium swims fastest depends on where the race is run. Speeds are usually measured in open liquid, yet many bacteria live in pores, mucus and host passages no wider than a cell. Using a microfluidic device with eight channel widths (0.80-3.00 m) in one field of view, we tracked unlabeled cells of eight species spanning five motility systems. Chamber height, a polymer additive and channel width each reordered the ranking. Vibrio alginolyticus, the fastest in open liquid, slowed to ~4 m/s in 1.25-m channels, whereas Campylobacter jejuni and Bacillus subtilis kept 33-46 m/s. Open liquid speed did not predict robustness to confinement. In two unrelated lineages, host symbionts that pass through narrow passages during colonization, Caballeronia insecticola and Vibrio fischeri, outran their non-symbiotic relatives in the channels, and crossed them with flagella wrapped around the cell body at nearly the speed of unwrapped cells. Where space is tight, the ability to keep moving, not top speed, sets the ranking.

papers.title: RNA-targeted aminopyridine compounds provide a new antifungal strategy
papers.abstract: While RNA is an emerging therapeutic target class, progress is limited by a shortage of well-defined targets in which ligand binding is coupled to measurable function. The group I intron, a self-splicing ribozyme essential in fungal mitochondria but absent from humans, offers both a tractable platform for exploring first principles of small molecule-RNA targeting and a selective antifungal target. We recalibrated an intron-splicing assay to approximate cellular conditions and performed an extensive, cryo-EM-guided structure-activity relationship campaign against the Candida albicans mtLSU intron. Ligands containing a flexible diamine outperformed conformationally constrained analogues, suggesting a general principle for engaging dynamic RNA surfaces and yielding lead aminopyridine 56 (IC 21.6 nM). Compound 56 synergizes with amphotericin B against C. albicans, suggesting a path for combination therapies. RT-qPCR confirmed direct target engagement in cells. This work establishes the fungal group I intron as a viable, mechanistically distinct antifungal target and a model platform for RNA-targeted discovery.

papers.title: Arrest-associated transcriptional programmes outweigh apoptosis-associated programmes in treatment-naive pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
papers.abstract: Background: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is driven by mutant KRAS, and RAS inhibitors now extend survival in previously treated metastatic disease. Whether treatment shrinks a tumour or only halts its growth depends partly on whether cancer cells die or stop dividing, yet how untreated PDAC cells are balanced between these programmes is unknown. Aims: We aimed to characterise the balance between apoptosis-associated and arrest-associated transcriptional programmes in treatment-naive PDAC and to examine their relationships with tumour subtype, TGM2 expression, tissue organisation, survival and drug sensitivity. Methods and results: We scored 52,999 malignant cells from 18 untreated patients in the Hwang atlas using a transcriptional contrast between genes associated with apoptosis and genes associated with resistance to apoptosis or cell-cycle arrest. In every patient the contrast was shifted toward the arrest-associated side: using equality between the two sides as the dividing threshold, 86.3% of cells with an informative score fell on that side, although the proportion depends on the threshold chosen. The shift recurred in the independent Steele atlas (median 71.6% per sample, range 37.1% to 90.8%). In the discovery cohort, tumours with higher basal-like scores had fewer arrest-side cells, and TGM2 expression was modestly higher on the arrest-associated side in both cohorts. The contrast did not track cell-line drug sensitivity or survival in bulk tumours. Conclusion: Untreated PDAC cells show a reproducible transcriptional bias toward anti-apoptotic and cell-cycle-arrest programmes. Whether this bias predicts cellular responses to treatment remains to be tested.

papers.title: High piRNA abundance is a hallmark of evolutionarily persistent piRNA-producing loci.
papers.abstract: PIWI-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) silence transposons in the germline, and the loci that produce them diverge rapidly between species. Yet, some loci retain both their genomic location and their piRNA production across large evolutionary distances, and the basis for this conservation is unclear. To identify the features that distinguish these persistent loci, we compared piRNA production at orthologous loci in three closely related mouse species, contrasting loci that produce piRNAs in all three species with those that do so in only one. Transposon content and UTR features, often linked to piRNA production, did not distinguish the two groups. Transcription extending beyond gene ends (readthrough) was more frequent at conserved loci, but did not explain conservation once the amount of piRNAs produced was taken into account. Instead, we found that the conserved loci are those that produce the most piRNAs. The same association holds true in human and two other primate species. We speculate that most piRNAs expressed in testis are tolerated molecular noise, and that only the highly expressed minority are likely to be functional.

papers.title: MitoDecode: quantitative phenotypic decoding of mitochondrial stress states from fluorescence images
papers.abstract: The quantitative measurement of mitochondrial stress from fluorescence images of cells remains a challenging task. Existing methods rely on mitochondrial segmentation, manually predefined features, and discrete phenotype severity classes, which are prone to error and bias. Here, we present MitoDecode, a deep learning network that automatically assesses type and severity of mitochondrial stress from fluorescence microscopy images. MitoDecode eliminates the need for mitochondrial segmentation, is parameter-free, and operates across both diffraction-limited and super-resolution optical imaging modalities. It assigns a phenotypic probability profile for each individual cell, indicating both type and severity of phenotypic stress. The readout thus enables comparisons between different stressors and provides clues for underlying mechanisms. Furthermore, the method captures phenotypic shifts continuously across treatment doses, revealing subtle variations that would otherwise be missed. We demonstrate MitoDecode's adaptability across diverse cell types, imaging modalities, and stress conditions, and show that it can reliably detect mitochondrial phenotypes, even when stressors target non-mitochondrial pathways. We validate the reliability of the model with biochemical assays, showcase its utility for phenotypic stress profiling of drug treatments, and envisage its application for early-stage disease detection, drug discovery, and mechanistic lead generation.

papers.title: Dopamine synthesis capacity and tau pathology differentially modulate rest-to-task functional network dynamics
papers.abstract: Optimal cognition relies on large-scale functional brain networks which balance segregation at rest with selective integration during task performance. In aging, these network dynamics are altered. We examined two prominent features of brain aging: dysregulated dopamine function and Alzheimer's disease (AD)-related pathology to examine impacts on brain network dynamics. Young adults and cognitively unimpaired older adults completed resting-state and task-based fMRI and PET imaging of dopamine synthesis capacity ([18F]fluoro-m-L-tyrosine). Older adults were classified as {beta}-amyloid negative/positive using [11C]Pittsburgh Compound-B PET(PiB- or PiB+) and underwent tau-PET scanning ([18F]flortaucipir). Greater rest-to-task network stability and task-related network segregation were associated with better subsequent memory. Compared to young adults, PiB+ older adults showed reduced network stability and both PiB+ and PiB- older adults showed reduced segregation during rest. Higher ventral striatal dopamine synthesis capacity was associated with greater stability within associative networks in young adults, but this relationship was attenuated in older adults and absent in PiB+ participants.
