Notably, ADVISE prioritizes ROBO2 as a progression-associated candidate in excitatory neurons. Experimental validation using CRISPR activation in hiPSC-derived excitatory neurons demonstrates that ROBO2 activation reduces the phosphorylated Tau-to-total Tau ratio. ADVISE thus reveals context-dependent molecular signatures of AD progression and bridges human single-cell discoveries with experimental validation of candidate regulators of AD pathology.

papers.title: Locomotor activity enhances environmental representation by boosting visuo-frontal communication
papers.abstract: During environment exploration we rapidly acquire visual information to identify targets of interest. Here, we discovered that locomotion limits how long natural scenes are viewed dur- ing free exploration. Whether the brain has developed compensatory mechanisms to ensure that sensory information is accurately transmitted to downstream areas during and after locomotion is unknown. We examined this issue by recording the spiking activity of popula- tions of neurons in visual and prefrontal cortex in conjunction with wireless recordings of oculomotor events while macaques moved freely to explore their environment or performed treadmill bipedal locomotion. The communication between visuo-frontal cortical areas was enhanced during and after locomotion to increase visual-evoked responses and population coding accuracy in prefrontal, but not visual cortical neurons. This in turn improved behav- ioral performance in a freely moving visual detection task after locomotion. Electrical stim- ulation further revealed elevated inter-areal synaptic efficacy during locomotor activity. The mechanism whereby locomotion enhances stimulus coding accuracy in prefrontal cortex and behavioral performance by increasing visuo-frontal communication is functionally beneficial during environmental exploration when incoming stimuli are rapidly changing and the win- dow for perceptual decisions is temporally restricted.

papers.title: Discontinuation of GLP-1RA Treatment Reinstates Binge-Like Eating and Drives Body Weight Past Pre-Treatment Levels in Mice
papers.abstract: We examined the impact of semaglutide treatment and discontinuation in a pre-clinical model for binge eating. Treatment reduced body weight and palatable food intake in mice with binge-like eating. Discontinuation reinstated binge-like eating and caused body weight to significantly exceed pre-treatment baseline, revealing specific binge-related risk when discontinuing GLP-1RAs.

papers.title: Life on leaves left a lasting mark on the Methylobacterium core genome
papers.abstract: The extent to which core genomes reflect strictly vertical inheritance remains debated, particularly in ecologically diverse bacterial lineages. Here, we investigate the evolution of the core genome of Methylobacterium, a major leaf-associated bacterial genus, to assess how evolutionary signals vary across genes and whether they relate to functions involved in adaptation to life at the surface of plant leaves (the phyllosphere). Identifying 1,099 protein-coding core genes across 293 genomes, we combined gene tree comparisons, phylogenetic network reconstruction, nucleotide polymorphism patterns, and functional enrichment analyses. We found that most core genes show some deviation from the consensus phylogenetic tree. However, this discordance is not randomly distributed. Across all analytical approaches, genes showing the strongest deviations are consistently associated with functions linked to life in the phyllosphere, including anoxygenic photosynthesis, protection against UV and osmotic stress. These genes are often grouped into conserved clusters in the genome. In particular, a large cluster involved in anoxygenic photosynthesis, including bacteriochlorophyll and carotenoid biosynthesis, shows strong variation in its evolutionary history and organization across lineages, despite maintaining a conserved core structure. Similar patterns of phylogenetic incongruence and gene organization are observed across related Hyphomicrobiales inhabiting the phyllosphere, suggesting that these functions extend beyond Methylobacterium. Together, these results indicate that evolutionary heterogeneity within the core genome is concentrated in genes involved in key ecological functions. While alternative explanations cannot be excluded, these patterns are consistent with horizontal gene transfer contributing to the diversification of traits important for survival and adaptation in phyllosphere bacterial communities.

papers.title: Transferrin receptor binding valency determines the circulating half-life and weight-loss efficacy of Fc-FGF21 in TfR-humanized mice
papers.abstract: Fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) is a promising metabolic hormone with potent anti-obesity effects. It acts in both the central nervous system and peripheral tissues to exert its metabolic benefits. Because its receptors are expressed at low levels in the brain, we hypothesized that enhanced transport across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) would improve its efficacy. To achieve this, FGF21 was fused to Fc(TV35), an engineered Fc fragment that binds the human transferrin receptor (hTfR), to generate Fc(TV35)-FGF21. Fc(TV35)-FGF21 does not bind to mouse TfR, so it produced weight-loss effects in wild-type diet-induced obese mice comparable to those of Fc-FGF21. However, it failed to induce weight loss in homozygous hTfR-humanized mice because of a markedly shortened circulating half-life. Converting Fc(TV35)-FGF21 from a homodimer to a bispecific Fc format with a single hTfR-binding arm partially restored the circulating half-life and weight-loss efficacy. Reducing mouse hTfR zygosity from homozygous to heterozygous did not substantially improve the engineered protein's half-life or weight-loss effect. Taken together, our findings suggest that sustained systemic exposure is a major determinant of FGF21's weight-loss efficacy and that hTfR engagement can shorten its systemic half-life and compromise its therapeutic activity. These results highlight an important design limitation of TfR-based brain vehicles, especially for delivering metabolic hormones with low-abundance CNS receptor targets. As a result, further optimization of shuttle formats to minimize systemic clearance while crossing the BBB is needed for metabolic hormones.

papers.title: Explainable Multimodal Prognostic Modeling Uncovers New Clinically Relevant Pathological Features in a Multi-Institutional Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor Cohort
papers.abstract: Although many patients with a well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (PanNET) are cured after surgical resection, it is hard to predict outcome in these patients. Current prognostic assessment relies largely on Ki-67 proliferation index, tumor stage, and established adverse pathologic features, such as vascular and perineural invasion. However, individually, these variables incompletely explain why patients with similar clinicopathologic profiles sometimes experience markedly different outcomes. To address this challenge, we assembled three independent cohorts with a surgically resected PanNET. In total, we included 1,438 patients with approximately 30,000 histology images, and approximately 12,000 person-years of follow-up. We separately modeled structured clinicopathologic information with Cox regression and tumor-centered pathology images with deep learning on an internal cohort treated at Johns Hopkins Hospital and performed multimodal continuous-time survival modeling to reveal which clinical and pathologic features are most important in predicting patient outcome. Across Cox models of censored time to recurrence-free survival, a text-based clinicopathological model that incorporated known prognosticators achieved a C-index of approximately 0.87, the image-based histology model approximately 0.80, and decision-level late multimodal fusion approximately 0.88 on the internal test set. The clinical model demonstrated strong prognostic discrimination using established risk factors, mainly relying on the TNM stage and Ki-67 index. Primary tumor histology retained substantial prognostic signal, with analysis restricted to tumor-centered regions to reduce reliance on unrelated tissues that might indirectly indicate disease extent. Interpretation of high-attention image tiles revealed regions of importance in the primary tumor, including recognized adverse morphologic features such as the leading edge of the tumor and foci of vascular or perineural invasion. Unexpectedly, intratumoral and peritumoral stroma accounted for nearly 50% of the model's high-attention regions, suggesting that the stroma may yield equal prognostic information to neoplastic cells in recurrence-prediction models. To test generalizability, we further evaluated the trained models in independent cohorts from two institutions with different demographics, where discrimination varied by site (mean late-fusion C-indices of 0.864 and 0.723). Together with the improved discrimination achieved through late fusion, our findings suggest that current clinicopathologic variables can be modeled to form reliable prognosticators, and that routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained slides of the primary tumor contain additional prognostically important information not fully captured by conventional clinicopathologic assessment, such that together, the two sources provide complementary information.

papers.title: MULTI-COHORT TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS REVEALS SHARED INFLAMMATORY SIGNALING AND UROTHELIAL DYSFUNCTION ACROSS IC/BPS PHENOTYPES
papers.abstract: Interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS) is a heterogeneous disorder characterized by bladder pain, inflammation, and urothelial dysfunction, yet the molecular features shared across clinically defined disease phenotypes remain incompletely understood. Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) and acyloxyacyl hydrolase (AOAH), a regulator of TLR4 ligand activity, have been implicated in IC/BPS in clinical and preclinical mechanistic studies. Here, we performed a multi-cohort reanalysis of four independent human IC/BPS transcriptomic datasets spanning bladder tissue and urine sediment from non-ulcer/non-Hunner, ulcerative/Hunner, normal-capacity, low-capacity, non-lesion, and lesion phenotypes. We evaluated immune cell-associated expression, urothelial differentiation and barrier integrity, TLR4 and pro-inflammatory signaling, and AOAH expression. IC/BPS exhibited phenotype-specific immune remodeling, yet shared features were also identified. Bladder-tissue IC/BPS was consistently associated with reduced expression of urothelial differentiation and barrier markers, together with increased TLR4 recognition and pro-inflammatory signaling. AOAH expression was elevated across all three bladder-tissue cohorts and was associated with monocyte/macrophage and pro-inflammatory transcriptional states. TLR4 signaling similarly paralleled myeloid and inflammatory features, whereas inflammatory programs generally showed inverse relationships with urothelial barrier markers. Notably, independently defined severe phenotypes of ulcerative IC and low-capacity IC showed concordant molecular remodeling characterized by increased leukocyte and monocyte/macrophage signatures, enhanced TLR4 signaling, elevated AOAH expression, and reduced urothelial barrier-associated expression. Together, these findings identify reproducible molecular signatures that extend across IC/BPS phenotypes and support a model in which urothelial dysfunction and TLR4-AOAH-associated myeloid inflammatory states coexist across disease phenotypes. These results provide a molecular framework for stratifying IC/BPS beyond clinical labels and identify shared and subtype-specific molecular signatures that may inform therapeutic response evaluation and clinical management.

papers.title: Biological Signaling Pathways Associated with Late Tendon Development in Chicken Embryos and Their Dependence on Mechanical Stimulation
papers.abstract: During embryonic and neonatal development, tendons exhibit rapid changes in mechanics and structure, including increases in collagen content, crosslinking, and fibril length. These functional and structural changes are partly dependent on mechanical stimulation. However, the specific mechanobiological mechanisms driving these changes remain poorly understood. The objective of this study was to identify the potential biological mechanisms and pathways driving tendon maturation into load-bearing materials using an embryonic chick model. Using bulk RNA sequencing, gene set enrichment analysis, and transcription factor analysis, we produced a transcriptomic profile of chick hindlimb tendons during late embryonic development (E16, E18, and E20) and tendons from rigid and flaccid paralysis-treated embryos. Additionally, we assessed the results from two differential expression analysis models to improve the replicability of our findings. Our results suggest that the largest transcriptomic response occurs between embryonic day 16 and 20, and that among paralysis conditions, rigid paralysis produces the greatest effect relative to controls. Across development, we found positive enrichment in processes related to mechanotransduction, extracellular matrix remodeling, cell adhesion, and contractility, and identified candidate pathways upregulated with development, including TGF-{beta}, PI3K-AKT-mTOR, Hippo, circadian rhythm, and focal adhesion signaling. In paralysis-treated embryos, our data suggest impairment in extracellular matrix remodeling and mechanotransduction events. Specifically, we found that both modes of paralysis are associated with a cellular stress response and downregulation of WNT signaling. Together, our findings identify candidate mechanotransduction pathways that are associated with late tendon maturation and altered by paralysis, which may inform tendon tissue engineering and regenerative approaches.

papers.title: NBDC Data Tools: Building Analysis-ready Datasets From ABCD and HBCD Releases in R and Python
papers.abstract: act The NIH Brain Development Cohorts (NBDC) Data Hub provides access to large-scale longitudinal datasets, including the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study(R) and the HEALthy Brain and Child Development (HBCD) Study. The studies release their tabulated data as hundreds of tables with tens of thousands of variables. Turning these files into a dataset for a particular analysis poses substantial informatics challenges, especially when data preparation and analysis workflows must be reproducible and reusable for new releases. We therefore developed NBDC Data Tools, a suite of open-source packages for preparing NBDC data in local or other approved computing environments. NBDCtools is the core R package for dataset construction and processing. The Python package nbdctools either calls the R workflow or assembles datasets natively in Python, and the R package NBDCtoolsData provides the release metadata support for both NBDCtools and nbdctools. Users define a dataset in code by naming the study, the release, and the variables or tables they need. The software then uses the standardized metadata released by the studies to locate the relevant files, join tables on the participant and session identifiers, convert data types, attach labels, and optionally recode non-response codes as missing values. Because the dataset definition is a short script that runs on the original release files, it can be rerun, shared with collaborators, and reported in publications. NBDC Data Tools complements the web-based data platforms of the NBDC Data Hub by providing a reproducible, scriptable path from approved data access to analysis-ready data for statistical analysis.

papers.title: Auditing Biomedical Literature with Blinded AI Peer Review: Where Peer Review Works, Where It Fails, and How to Strengthen It
papers.abstract: Biomedical publishing has grown more than elevenfold since 1991, outstripping human peer review. Unblinded language models cannot audit this literature objectively because they recognize famous authors and journals from training memory. We built BARS (Blinded AI Review System), an automated referee that strips titles, author names, institutions, journal headers, and dates before grading full-text manuscripts on a 10-point scale covering methods, evidence, biology, and reproducibility. We used BARS to generate 1,874 blind reviews across 1,714 unique papers. BARS passed 100% of verified sound controls, caught 77% to 91% of internally flawed papers, eliminated a +0.35-point prestige boost, and more than doubled human referee consistency. Across 320 recent open-access articles (2020-2025) from eight fields, 54% failed on core scientific rigor (<5.0/10; 41% excluding megajournals). Revision at selective journals improved preprints more than twice as much as revision at commercial megajournals (+0.62 vs. +0.30 points; baseline-adjusted p = 0.033), and BARS recalled 98% of unresolved human referee critiques across 100 open-review papers. Across 915 date-blinded papers from 1991 to 2025, average scores fell from 7.6/10 to 5.8/10 as megajournals and template database studies expanded. Blinded self-audits of 238 papers by two senior authors -- and of this manuscript itself -- caught real statistical, control, and table errors in our own work. At four cents per paper, BARS offers a practical quality check for authors, journals, and readers (https://veg.github.io/BARS/).

papers.title: Vorinostat Can Reduce an Ongoing Fibrosis and Preserve Key Liver Metabolic Functions by Selectively Altering Mesenchymal Cell Differentiation
papers.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a major global cause of mortality that is driven by the activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) into extracellular matrix (ECM)-producing myofibroblasts (MyoFs). The lack of predictive human in vitro models has severely hampered the discovery of targeted anti-fibrotic therapies. Here, we describe a human iPSC-derived hepatic micro-organoid (microHO) model, which labels collagen producing cells, to study liver fibrosis pathophysiology and screen drug candidates. We discovered that while multiple drugs prevented fibrosis when co-administered prophylactically with TGF{beta}1, only the FDA-approved pan-HDAC inhibitor Vorinostat (SAHA) successfully reduced an established, ongoing fibrosis and preserved life-sustaining liver metabolic functions in a fibrotic microenvironment, including ammonia detoxification and CYP3A4-mediated drug metabolism. To uncover its mechanism of action, we utilized single-cell RNA sequencing and CRISPR-Cas12a lineage tracing. We found that Vorinostat actively redirects HSC differentiation away from pro-fibrotic MyoFs and toward a distinct, fibrosis-suppressing mesenchymal inhibitory (MesInh) cell. By reversing TGF{beta}1-induced epigenetic silencing, Vorinostat opens condensed chromatin to rescue metabolic gene expression and generates anti-fibrotic effectors that neutralize ongoing TGF{beta}1 signaling. Given its distinct capacity to remodel mesenchymal cell fate and reverse epigenetic repression of metabolic genes at clinically achievable concentrations, Vorinostat represents a highly promising drug for repurposing as a therapeutic for advanced human liver fibrosis.

papers.title: Comparative profiling of sperm small RNAs in cnidarians highlights potential for paternal inheritance
papers.abstract: Small RNAs in mature sperm are crucial regulators of gene expression following fertilization during early development in bilaterians. However, the presence and functions of sperm-derived small RNAs remain poorly understood in early-diverging (i.e., non-bilaterian) metazoans. In this study, we characterize three classes of small RNAs-microRNAs (miRNAs), piwi-interacting RNAs (piRNAs), and tRNA-derived RNAs (tDRs)-in sperm from three phylogenetically and ecologically distinct species from the early-diverging phylum Cnidaria: the sea anemone Nematostella vectensis, the temperate stony coral Astrangia poculata, and the reef-building tropical coral Acropora hyacinthus. All three classes of small RNAs examined were present in sperm from these cnidarians. Most miRNAs were species-specific; however, target prediction analysis revealed enriched putative targets involved in conserved developmental and signaling pathways. piRNAs overlapped with transposable elements and genic regions, indicating a potential dual role in genomic maintenance and gene expression regulation. Characterization of tDRs demonstrated that 5 prime-terminal fragments constituted the primary structural type across the three species, driven by high accumulation of specific isoacceptors including 5 prime-tDR-GlyGCC. Together, these findings provide the first evidence that cnidarian sperm carry a rich repertoire of small RNAs, including both conserved and species-specific types. Their presence suggests that paternal small RNAs contribute important regulatory information to the zygote in cnidarians, implicating paternal small RNAs as possible mediators of epigenetic inheritance in this early-branching metazoan phylum.

papers.title: PPI-Rescue: restoration of eye development via functional reconstitution of a transcription complex.
papers.abstract: The activity of transcription factors (TFs) can be modulated through protein-protein interactions (PPIs) with cofactors which can serve to enhance, repress or alter the specificity of TF function. Current genetic and molecular approaches such as knockout and overexpression studies are likely to affect all possible activities of a TF, presenting a dilemma when attempting to parse out how TFs function within a cell. Hence, there is a need to devise a technique that will allow for mechanistic insight to be gained into the function(s) of discrete transcription complexes. Herein we report ''PPI-Rescue'', an approach that leverages bespoke mutations in TFs and the selective reconstitution of specific complexes to study the molecular properties and biological functions of discrete transcription complexes in vitro and in vivo. We demonstrate PPI-Rescue using the conserved Drosophila transcription factor Sine oculis (So) and cofactor Eyes Absent (Eya). To validate this approach, we engineered a missense mutation, So{Delta}Eya (C110S), that selectively abrogates PPI-Eya to show that PPI-Eya is necessary for the transcriptional activity of So in cultured cells and to promote eye formation in Drosophila. Using heterologous leucine zipper domains, we specifically reconstituted the So{Delta}Eya-Eya PPI and show that this complex is transcriptionally active in cells and can rescue eye development. PPI-Rescue was also used to restore transcriptional activity to So{Delta}PPI (V111E), an allele that mimics the human SIX1(V17E) allele associated with Branchio-Oto-Renal syndrome. PPI-Rescue thus represents an innovative approach to understanding the complex molecular logic of transcription complexes in both development and disease.

papers.title: LRCP: identifying functionally related SNPs and genes from phenome-wide genetic-effect correlations using GWAS summary statistics
papers.abstract: Genetic correlation describes which traits share genetic causes. The transposed question, which variants act alike across the phenome, has no comparable estimator, although it points directly to shared genes, pathways and regulators. Correlations of GWAS Z scores between variants across many traits are easy to compute, but they are confounded by linkage disequilibrium (LD) and, for any pair of variants, by sample overlap and genetic correlation among the GWAS. We show that in 452 Pan-UK Biobank GWAS the effective number of independent traits is only 58, and that naive tests reject 51-70% of null pairs of distal variants. We introduce LRCP (likelihood and regression on cross-products of Z scores), which estimates the phenome-wide genetic-effect correlation{rho} between SNPs by regressing Z-score cross-products on LD cross components, using per-SNP heritability enrichment from the companion method LRCQ and LDSC-derived plug-ins. For variants in different LD blocks the estimator has a closed form, and its standard errors account exactly for the dependence among GWAS. In simulations LRCP is unbiased (absolute bias at most 0.03), its 95% intervals cover 93-98%, and its type-I error is 5.0-5.7%, whereas naive correlations are attenuated by 41-64% and reject up to 51% of null pairs. In Pan-UK Biobank, LRCP recovers the expected signs among PCSK9, LDLR and APOB variants and estimates{rho} = 0.90 between the TP53 polyadenylation variant rs78378222 and MDM2 rs3730556, whose Z scores correlate at r = 0.67 across traits (conditional bootstrap P = 0.015), although this correlation lies along a shared body-size and red-cell trait axis. Single variant pairs are near the resolution of current biobanks, with precision limited by the number of genetically distinct traits. Genome-wide, among 7,793 enriched LD clumps (30.2 million distal pairs), a conditional test finds 17 pairs at FDR 5%, where naive correlation flags 23 million. Simulating the whole screen under the null shows that this test is conservative and that the 113 strongest links (P < 10-5) lie far beyond the null, which yields 0.025 such pairs per screen. Linked genes share Reactome pathways 4.9 times more often than random pairs of enriched loci. The top pairs form 19 modules, the largest of which match known biology: myeloid differentiation (IRF8, CEBPE, IKZF1), LDL and HDL metabolism, iron homeostasis (TMPRSS6, TFRC), the red-cell membrane (SPTA1, ANK1) and type-2 immunity (TSLP, IL13). LRCP turns phenome-wide summary statistics into a map of functionally related variants and genes.

papers.title: The intrinsically disordered N-terminal region of eIF5B nucleates RNA-driven phase separation
papers.abstract: Recently, we found that eukaryotic Initiation Factor 5B (eIF5B) forms cytoplasmic puncta under conditions of cellular stress and that the puncta formation drives an increase in alternative translation initiation. The formation of these puncta depends on the intrinsically disordered N-terminal region of eIF5B (eIF5B-NTR). To address the driving force behind this observation, we reconstituted a purified, binary, in vitro system to study the phase separation potential of the eIF5B-NTR. Utilizing this system, we show that eIF5B-NTR forms RNA-driven condensates at physiological concentrations. Furthermore, we defined the properties of the eIF5B condensates and the amino acid sequence requirements of this polypeptide to form complex liquid-liquid condensates. Truncation mapping identified a central arginine-rich core (residues ~200-400) that drives condensation but forms nearly static droplets in the absence of the rest of the polypeptide. Finally, we tested this model in cells to determine if the in vitro observations apply to the complex cellular environment.

papers.title: Novel Regulators of Sugar-dependent Food Consumption in Drosophila melanogaster
papers.abstract: Diet and genetic background interact to influence food consumption, yet the genetic basis of diet-dependent feeding behavior remains poorly understood. Here, we used genome-wide association analysis (GWAS) to investigate the genetic regulation of sugar-dependent food consumption in Drosophila melanogaster. Food intake was quantified in 176 lines of the Drosophila Genetic Reference Panel (DGRP) using the Con-Ex (Consumption-Excretion) assay on low- and high-sugar foods. Flies showed compensatory feeding, consuming more low-sugar food than high-sugar food, and this behavior was largely maintained across genotypes. Additionally, the magnitude and overall consumption varied several-fold among lines, with broad-sense heritability of 0.53 to 0.66 across sexes and diets. Association analysis across six sex- and diet-specific phenotypes identified 161 variants mapping to 118 candidate genes, which shared almost no loci between dietary conditions, indicating that consumption on the two foods is largely under separate genetic control. RNAi knockdown of candidate genes identified CG42673 and Tmtc2, whose knockdown increased consumption across sexes and diets and was reproduced in independent experiments. Together, these findings show that natural genetic variation contributes substantially to diet-dependent feeding and identify candidate regulators of sugar-based food consumption in Drosophila.

papers.title: Functional Screening of Kv7.5 Channel Variants Associated with Neuronal Dysfunction
papers.abstract: The KCNQ5 gene encodes Kv7.5 channels, which contribute to the regulation of neuronal excitability. Kv7.5 genetic variants associated with neurological dysfunction have been reported, but functional characterization of Kv7.5 variants is limited and causal links to pathogenicity are lacking. We have conducted the first automated patch clamp functional screen of a panel of heterozygous Kv7.5/Kv7.3 channel variants. We tested nine mutations located in diverse locations throughout the Kv7.5 channel and identified some variants with gain-of-function effects (L341I+/-, G347S+/-, P369R+/-, R497C+/-), some with loss-of-function effects (V145G+/-, W303C+/-), and others with no apparent effect (A131V+/-, R359H+/-, R491H+/-). Variants produced a gain of function by left-shifting the voltage-dependence of channel activation alone or in combination with increasing current density. Loss of function occurred as a result of reduced current density. Using these findings, we initiated the first z-score classification to guide understanding of Kv7.5 variant pathogenicity, which can be refined as more variants are functionally characterized and new variants are discovered. Lastly, we observed higher sensitivity to channel block by XE991 in L341I+/-, G347S+/-, P369R+/- gain-of-function variants indicating potential for targeted pharmacogenetic approaches to restore normal Kv7.5 channel function.

papers.title: LRCQ: phenome-wide heritability enrichment of genomic loci from GWAS summary statistics
papers.abstract: Some genetic variants are associated with many traits, but a variant's GWAS statistics are also inflated by the effects of variants in LD with it and by confounding shared by all variants in a study. Existing measures of per-variant pleiotropy, such as counts of significant associations or multi-trait association tests, do not separate these sources. Stratified LD score regression separates them for one trait at a time and only through predefined annotations. We present LRCQ (LD score regression on {chi}2 across many GWAS), which estimates for each locus its phenome-wide heritability enrichment: the variance of its causal effects across a set of traits, relative to an average locus. LRCQ regresses squared Z-scores from 30 or more GWAS jointly on squared LD, with per-trait LDSC intercepts and heritabilities fitted in earlier stages. Its pooled least-squares solution has a closed form whose cost does not grow with the number of traits. Its standard errors account for sample overlap and genetic correlation between GWAS. Squared Z-scores identify enrichment at the resolution of LD clumps, not single SNPs, so LRCQ reports clump-level estimates ("omni-loci"). These estimates can be aggregated over any functional annotation or gene set chosen after the analysis. In simulations with real UK Biobank LD and 30 to 1,000 traits, LRCQ was unbiased for its clump-level estimand. When GWAS share samples its test statistics are strongly right-skewed: normal-reference p-values were up to 10-fold anti-conservative at P < 0.001, and skewness-corrected p-values from the exact third cumulant restored type-I error and FDR control. Model-based standard errors were calibrated once the enrichment estimates plugged into them kept the polygenic background. It ranked enriched loci better than mean {chi}2, LD-normalised {chi}2, multi-trait omnibus tests and significant-association counts in 13 of 16 scenarios. Its main vulnerability was a misspecified LDSC intercept. Applied to 444 Pan-UK Biobank European-ancestry GWAS, LRCQ found strongly non-uniform phenome-wide enrichment: the SD of true clump-mean enrichment was 8.3, against a genome mean of 1. It identified 70 omni-loci (99 LD clumps) at FDR 5%, including CRP, CETP, APOB, AKTIP, SMOX, the SHBG region, CASZ1 and HNF1A. These ranked only moderately with mean {chi}2 and poorly with counts of significant associations. Gene-level phenome-wide enrichment rose with loss-of-function constraint. Phenome-wide heritability was 3-5-fold enriched in coding, conserved, 5' UTR and promoter sequence, and depleted in repressed chromatin. LRCQ turns hundreds of biobank GWAS into an LD-corrected map of where phenome-wide genetic variance lies, and complements its companion method LRCP, which estimates genetic-effect correlations between loci.

papers.title: Can the Human Plastisphere Account for the Rise of Type 1 Diabetes: A Computational Molecular Mimicry Study
papers.abstract: An increased incidence of childhood type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) has been widely documented, but its pathophysiological origins are poorly understood. The post-World War II expansion of the plastics industry in the United States and elsewhere coincides with a marked increase in T1DM incidence; however, no pathophysiological mechanism has been proposed that could justify such a temporal correlation. Here, we leverage recent advances in artificial intelligence and protein structure prediction and binding to show that molecular mimicry is a plausible pathophysiological mechanism for plastic fragments to induce onset of T1DM for individuals with certain HLA haplotypes.

papers.title: Altered Steroidogenesis in Response to Impaired Mitochondrial Protein Homeostasis
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial proteostasis is critical for organelle function, but how it influences mitochondrial steroidogenesis is not understood. We investigated the impact of impaired mitochondrial proteostasis on mitochondrial protein import and how this impacts cortisol production. We found that mild mitochondrial proteostatic stress increased cortisol synthesis whereas severe stress suppressed cortisol, revealing a biphasic steroidogenic response. Mild stress induced increases in cholesterol import and cortisol production in a manner dependent on STARD1-mediated cholesterol transport, which is the first and rate-limiting step in steroidogenesis. Severe stress reduced cortisol synthesis independently of STARD1 activity, indicating this inhibition occurs downstream in steroidogenesis. These findings reveal mitochondrial protein import as a regulatory node linking mitochondrial proteostasis to steroidogenic output. Furthermore, we observed increased cortisol synthesis in rotenone, A53T alpha-synuclein and PINK1-KO models of PD, suggesting that this response is relevant to PD-associated mitochondrial dysfunction. Together, our findings reveal a biphasic steroidogenic response to impairments in mitochondrial quality control with implications in human disease. Our work recognizes a previously unexplored branch of the mitochondrial stress response that enables cellular and physiological adaptations that can be detrimental if constitutively activated.

papers.title: KDM6A is enzymatically active at the Golgi apparatus where it is necessary for maintenance of Golgi apparatus morphology
papers.abstract: KDM6A and KDM6B, lysine demethylases, play a central role in regulation of transcription through their demethylation activity towards H3K27me3 and have also been shown to be dynamically regulated upon epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). In particular, KDM6A has been implicated in a variety of malignancies and is frequently mutated in cancers including those in kidney, bladder, colorectal, and breast. KDM6A and KDM6B function as part of the COMPASS-like protein complex (CLC) which includes methyltransferases KMT2C/KMT2D and the regulatory WRAD-subcomplex. KDM6A total protein is known to be suppressed by TGF-{beta} in MCF10A breast cells; however, our examination of protein localization by immunofluorescence and LC-MS/MS reveals that KDM6A expression is lost in the nucleus but retained in the Golgi apparatus, independent of other CLC complex members. Importantly, KDM6A isolated from a biochemically-separated subcellular membranous fraction possesses the catalytic JmjC domain and is enzymatically active, indicating that KDM6A may have non-nuclear substrates. Further, knockdown of KDM6A and treatment with TGF-{beta} similarly alter Golgi apparatus morphology, in a cell type specific manner, suggesting context-dependent regulatory functions. These findings support a model in which KDM6A is necessary to maintain Golgi apparatus morphology and is enzymatically active outside of the nucleus.

papers.title: AlphaFold 3 Prediction Accuracy and Reliability across RNA Structures and Protein-RNA Interfaces
papers.abstract: AlphaFold 3 (AF3) models RNA and protein-RNA complexes, but when its predictions and confidence metrics can be trusted is unclear. We evaluated AF3 on more than 1,300 protein-RNA complexes and about 270 RNA-only systems, and compared post-cutoff RNAs with pre-cutoff candidates selected by sequence and fold similarity. On structurally novel RNAs, AF3 largely preserves the protein fold, while RNA-fold and interface accuracy drop sharply with little change in predicted RNA confidence score. Input ablations show that protein alignments and templates from RNA-bound proteins govern complex assembly, whereas RNA alignments matter most for single-chain and long RNAs. The most frequent failed interface retains protein-side contacts but places an often-misfolded RNA in the wrong pose. RNA interface confidence only partly distinguishes this error from correct placements. Against CLIP-seq, SELEX and RNAcompete motifs, AF3 usually places the protein against the experimentally observed motif-bearing RNA segment, even where the interface fails, but often not in the native pose. In protein-RNA complexes released in 2026, a score combining AF3 confidence with RNA familiarity and template use ranked RNA chains with accurate folds and correctly placed interfaces better than AF3's ranking score.

papers.title: Comparative Oogenesis in Annual and Non-annual African Killifishes: Oocyte Staging in the Fastest-Aging Vertebrate, Nothobranchius furzeri
papers.abstract: Annual killifishes have evolved specialized reproductive strategies that allow their embryos to survive the seasonal desiccation of ephemeral habitats, yet little is known about how these adaptations arise during oogenesis. We hypothesized that traits contributing to embryonic desiccation resistance may originate from modifications in the follicular wall and egg envelope during oocyte development. Here, we provide a comparative morphological and morphometric characterization of oogenesis in the annual African turquoise killifish Nothobranchius furzeri and the non-annual lyretail killifish Aphyosemion australe, from early oocyte development through Primary Growth (PG), Secondary Growth (SG), Maturation, and Ovulation. Despite their contrasting life histories, both species exhibited a highly conserved sequence of oocyte development. Cortical alveoli accumulated before oil droplets during PG, whereas SG was characterized by the progressive coalescence of yolk globules into a homogeneous fluid yolk mass and the peripheral displacement of oil droplets and cortical alveoli. Oocyte diameter did not differ significantly between species at any developmental stage, and the follicular epithelium followed a similar developmental pattern, suggesting that its basic morphological organization is conserved despite contrasting reproductive ecologies. In contrast, greater interspecific divergence was observed in the zona pellucida, which became significantly thicker in N. furzeri from early SG through Maturation and exhibited distinct patterns of chorionic ornamentation between species. These findings reveal a largely conserved program of oogenesis and follicular epithelial differentiation in annual and non-annual African killifishes, while highlighting greater morphological divergence in the egg envelope. This suggests that different components of the ovarian follicle may exhibit distinct degrees of evolutionary plasticity, with modifications of the zona pellucida potentially contributing to embryo-environment interactions and desiccation resistance in annual species.

papers.title: Joint effects of climate change and urbanization accelerate plant biodiversity loss across urban green spaces
papers.abstract: Urbanization and climate change are rapidly reshaping biodiversity worldwide, yet their combined impacts on ecosystems remain poorly understood. Urban green spaces (UGS) underpin urban biodiversity, but differ widely in their structure, management, and exposure to global change. Here, we examine how these two drivers jointly influence plant communities across five major UGS types (allotments, private gardens, residential green spaces, parks, and ruderal areas) in three socio-culturally distinct Swiss cities. By combining vegetation surveys from 180 sites (60 sites per city) with species-specific thermal niches, high-resolution projections of historical and future urban microclimates, and land-use change scenarios, we trace how climate-driven species loss interacts with the shifting availability of urban habitats to shape biodiversity outcomes by mid-century. We found that UGS types differed markedly in their contributions to biodiversity, with allotments and ruderal areas supporting disproportionately high compositional uniqueness. However, climate change alone was projected to drive substantial plant diversity declines across all UGS types, with 40-80% of species exceeding their thermal niches by mid-century based on climate change scenario and UGS type. Although allotments exhibited relatively greater tolerance due to broader community-level thermal preferences, this advantage was undermined by their rapid decline under urbanization. When considered jointly, climate change and urbanization generated widespread biodiversity losses through complementary mechanisms: climate change drove species declines, while urbanization amplified these losses by disproportionately reducing high-value habitats. These results reveal a consistent trajectory of biodiversity decline across urban landscapes and highlight the need to conserve high-diversity yet shrinking UGS, particularly allotments, while enhancing the ecological value and climate resilience of expanding UGS, such as parks and residential areas, to safeguard future urban biodiversity under global change.

papers.title: Genome-scale metabolic models reveal phylogenetic conservation of amino acid fermentation-linked metabolic traits in soil bacteria
papers.abstract: Soil microorganisms drive biogeochemical cycling of carbon, nitrogen, and other elements, but the partitioning of metabolic fluxes among taxa remains poorly understood, limiting our ability to link community composition to ecosystem function. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) offer a mechanistic framework to connect taxa and their metabolic pathways to these fluxes. However, heterogeneity of soil communities has hampered recovery of high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), constraining application of flux balance analysis (FBA) to soil metagenomes and skewing available GEMs towards cultured model organisms. This gap limits our understanding of soil microbial physiology and responses to disturbance. Here, we present a collection of GEMs for 550 MAGs (497 bacterial, 53 archaeal) recovered from 94 soil samples across the continental United States. As an example application, we used FBA to estimate uptake and secretion of 44 commonly exchanged metabolites and tested whether these fluxes are phylogenetically conserved. While the overall bacterial phylogenetic signal was weak (median r = 0.029), eight metabolites showed significant conservation: amino acids (L-methionine, L-leucine, L-isoleucine), fermentation intermediates (pyruvate, acetaldehyde, ethanol), and amino acid degradation by-products NH and CO2. Most bacterial MAGs were predicted to import branched-chain amino acids, and a subset also secreted pyruvate and ethanol, identifying candidate cross-feeding interactions. Thus, fermentation-linked traits may be phylogenetically conserved and predictable from community composition, whereas most other metabolites showed no detectable signal. Ultimately, this resource enables genome-resolved prediction of soil microbial metabolisms, from cross-feeding and carbon-use efficiency to community responses to disturbance, providing a mechanistic bridge between microbial taxonomy and ecosystem-scale biogeochemistry.

papers.title: Spectral Adaptive Repositioning for Flow-Based Single-Cell Perturbation Modeling
papers.abstract: Predicting transcriptome-wide cellular responses to genetic and biomolecular perturbations is central to functional genomics and therapeutic target discovery. Existing methods assign gene positional encodings derived from arbitrary orderings or static co-expression masks built from unperturbed cells, and cannot capture the functional rewiring induced by perturbations. We present SPEAR, a generative framework built on two complementary positional mechanisms. Spectral positional encoding grounds each gene's position in the geometry of the co-expression network via continuous coordinates derived from the graph Laplacian. Adaptive repositioning then derives each gene's position from its perturbation-conditioned hidden state at every layer, allowing the attention genes exert on one another to reorganize without explicit supervision. Evaluated on genetic, pharmacological, and cytokine perturbation benchmarks, SPEAR demonstrates excellent recovery of differential gene-expression, distributional structure, and perturbation-specific identifiability. SPEAR also captures latent positional relationships that closely map to known transcription factor-target interactions. https://github.com/shouryaverma/SPEAR}{https://github.com/shouryaverma/SPEAR

papers.title: Connectivity of Implicit Statistical Learning Networks is Associated with Language Impairment Severity in Post-Stroke Aphasia
papers.abstract: Rehabilitation of language for individuals with post-stroke aphasia (PSA) requires relearning to use cognitive-linguistic skills, but little is known about how these individuals relearn, or how brain reorganization may support different types of learning. One type of learning critical to language acquisition is implicit-statistical learning (ISL), which supports robust, accurate performance with minimal conscious effort. ISL relies on brain subnetworks that include language areas as well as domain general regions (i.e., salience and cognitive control) with the latter considered less likely to be damaged in individuals with PSA. Using three brain subnetworks associated with ISL, the present study used graph theory metrics to (1) compare their functional connectivity in PSA (n = 30) relative to neurologically healthy controls (n=18), and (2) examine their relationship with aphasia severity in the PSA group. Resting-state functional connectivity was weaker for the language and salience subnetworks in PSA than controls, but not for the cognitive control subnetwork. Additionally, edges within all three networks correlated with aphasia severity, particularly between regions of the right frontal cortex, such that stronger connectivity in these ISL subnetworks were associated with milder aphasia. While it is unsurprising that the damaged left-sided brain regions in the PSA group resulted in connectivity that differed from controls, these differences were also observed in the salience subnetwork. Further, the correspondence to aphasia severity was evident in all subnetworks, highlighting that domain general ISL networks may contribute to variability in language outcomes.

papers.title: scPCIP: cross-species annotation of plant cell types with conserved gene programs
papers.abstract: Single-cell atlases now cover many plant species and organs, yet their cell types are still annotated with marker genes that often fail to transfer between species. Here we show that plant cell identities are captured by gene programs conserved across species. We learned programs for root, leaf, flower and seed cell types on ortholog groups from 112,905 author-labelled cells and implemented them in scPCIP, which annotates cells of species absent from training without a reference. Across 26 held-out datasets, scPCIP outperformed marker-based and plant deep-learning methods, matched supervised classifiers trained on the same atlas and transferred, at lower accuracy, to an independent study; its programs followed tissue position in spatial transcriptomes. The conserved core of each program separated cell types better than its periphery in all 11 held-out species, whereas most species-specific markers turned over. Across organs, leaf bundle-sheath cells carried a root endodermis program in 8 of 12 studies.

papers.title: Spatial architecture of complex antibody formats dictates pharmacokinetics via FcRn-recycling
papers.abstract: Complex antibody formats are advancing in the biotherapeutic landscape to address the need for multi-specificity, tailored valency, and novel mechanisms of action. However, understanding how non-canonical architectures impact fundamental pharmacokinetic pathways remains a critical challenge. While canonical IgGs experience steric hindrance at the endosomal membrane during FcRn engagement, whether -- and how strongly -- this constraint impacts FcRn-mediated recycling across the expanding diversity of non-canonical antibody architectures has remained unknown. By systematically evaluating a diverse panel of rationally designed antibody geometries utilizing orthogonal in vitro assays we demonstrate that spatial layout profoundly influences FcRn-recycling efficiency; inverting the antibody structure by positioning the Fab-domains to the C-terminus (invertbodies) maximizes recycling, whereas crowding the N-terminus severely impairs it. In contrast, non-specific endocytosis was only modestly and inconsistently affected by Fab number, dependent on the Fv-sequence, but not by the spatial architecture itself. Notably, antibody architecture and affinity-enhancing Fc-FcRn mutations act independently yet cooperatively, ultimately revealing a physiological recycling ceiling. These FcRn-recycling dynamics translate with high fidelity to in vivo clearance (CL) in a humanized FcRn mouse model. Across the antibody panel, architecture drove a near 15-fold variance in CL, an effect that collapsed in FcRn-knockout mice. As proof of concept, we applied the invertbody design to a variant of the marketed antibody golimumab, achieving a three-fold reduction in clearance without compromising potency. These findings reveal the magnitude and predictability with which the antibody architecture governs FcRn-recycling and non-specific CL, establishing a rational, generalizable framework to optimize the pharmacokinetics of biotherapeutics.

papers.title: A fibroblast-CD8+ T cell circuit drives a Type 1 shift in allergic inflammatory memory
papers.abstract: Inflammatory memory in barrier tissues often manifests as exaggerated recall responses to previously encountered stimuli. While recall is generally thought to reinforce the Type of inflammation (e.g., Type 1 (T1), Type 2 (T2), or Type 17 (T17)) induced in the primary encounter, whether and how memory responses engage programs beyond the initiating Type is unclear. Here, we adapted well-characterized murine models of T2 atopic dermatitis (AD)-like and T17 psoriasis-like inflammation into repeated challenge paradigms to compare how inflammatory memory is stored and recalled through longitudinal single-cell RNA-sequencing. In T17 inflammation, a network of IL-17-producing {gamma}{delta}T cells, IL-17-responsive keratinocytes and myeloid cells established in primary challenge re-emerged in recall with increased abundance and accelerated kinetics. By contrast, allergic T2 memory drove a particularly exacerbated and durable recall response in which hallmark features of T1 immunity, including interferon (IFN) signaling and cytotoxic lymphocyte recruitment, were unexpectedly layered onto amplified T2 responses. This T2-to-T1 shift was initiated by CD8+ tissue-resident memory T (Trm) cells that expanded with repeated challenge, produced IFN{gamma}, TNF- and IL-13, and closely resembled treatment-refractory Trm cells in AD. Tissue rewiring was supported by Trm-derived T1 cytokines and the IL-4-rich T2 milieu whose synergy on fibroblasts amplified allergic recall via IL-15 and CCL19. By tuning fibroblast IFN responsiveness in vivo, we mechanistically dissect how this fibroblast-CD8+ T cell circuit supports cytotoxic CD8+ T cell responses. In human AD, both arms of allergic recall amplification by this two-cell circuit featuring T1 and T2 effector responses were conserved. Our findings reveal how a stromal-immune circuit drives a clinically relevant T1 immune axis to support allergic inflammatory memory.

papers.title: GeneFamHunter: annotation-independent recovery of divergent and tandemly arrayed gene-family members from genome assemblies
papers.abstract: Motivation: Gene families expand by tandem duplication, diverge and decay, so their members are often missing, fragmented or fused in automated genome annotations, and divergent copies escape pairwise similarity searches. These challenges are particularly pronounced in non-model organisms, for which well-annotated genomes and reference proteomes are often unavailable, limiting the applicability of protein-based gene family recovery methods. Results: We developed GeneFamHunter to recover gene-family members directly from nucleotide assemblies. It searches continuous six-frame translations of overlapping genomic windows using four complementary domain- and profile-based methods, clusters hits while distinguishing tandem paralogs, predicts and validates gene models, and constructs gene trees. Across six Quest for Orthologs genomes, window-based HMMER searches recovered all 130 reference papain-like (C1A) loci, with 21 off-target hits, compared with 45 for stop-to-stop ORF searches; whole-contig HMMER searches recovered 108 (83.1%). With 11 distantly related queries, PSI-BLAST and DELTA-BLAST recovered all reference loci, whereas RPSTBLASTN recovered 98.5-99.2% and TBLASTN, as used by BITACORA, recovered 94.6-95.4%. Across six mite genomes, GeneFamHunter recovered all 209 previously reported C1 loci and identified 37 additional candidate loci. In a separate comparison, it recovered all 128 reference UniProt C1A proteins and identified five additional loci without annotated gene models; OrthoFinder included 35 non-C1A proteins, whereas OMA recovered 98 reference proteins. Availability and implementation: GeneFamHunter is implemented in Bash for Linux and SLURM clusters and is freely available at https://github.itap.purdue.edu/HeLab/GeneFamHunter (MIT license). Benchmark code and data: https://github.itap.purdue.edu/HeLab/GeneFamHunter_benchmarks and Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23744704).

papers.title: A chromosome-level genome assembly of an endangered large carnivore, the wolverine, Gulo gulo gulo (Linnaeus, 1758)
papers.abstract: We describe a chromosome-level, haplotype-resolved genome assembly from a male wolverine (Gulo gulo gulo). The assembly comprises two pseudo-haplotypes of 2,523.2 Mb and 2,288.4 Mb, with 95.8% and 97.8% scaffolded into 20 autosomal chromosomes and sex chromosomes (placed in haplotype one). Assembly completeness is high (BUSCO 98.2% and 88.9%), with 20,337 and 17,692 annotated protein-coding genes for haplotypes one and two, respectively. Compared to existing wolverine genomes, the current genome is more complete and contains both sex chromosomes. This reference genome will be an important resource for population studies and conservation biology of this large carnivore.

papers.title: The Application of 3D Cryo-Volume Electron Microscopy to Visualize and Quantify the Photosynthetic Filamentous Cyanobacterium Anabaena
papers.abstract: Cryogenic volume electron microscopy (cryo-vEM) is a rapidly developing nanoscale imaging approach that enables three-dimensional datasets of vitrified cells and tissues at intermediate resolutions without treatment with chemical fixatives or metal contrasting agents. Our goal was to evaluate the suitability of cryo-vEM for whole cells of photosynthetic organisms such as cyanobacteria. Two species of Anabaena, a filamentous cyanobacterium, were captured on poly-L-lysine-coated grids, vitrified by plunge-freezing into liquid ethane, and mapped by secondary electron and integrated fluorescence light microscopy to identify target cells. Cells of interest were coated with platinum, trenched with xenon, and 3D volumes collected by alternating argon milling and through-lens detector (TLD) imaging on a Thermo Scientific Hydra plasma focused ion beam scanning electron microscope. Volumes were segmented via 2.5D U-Net models, then quantified in Dragonfly 3D World. Block-face images revealed the cell wall, thylakoids, phycobilisomes, carboxysomes, cyanophycin and polyphosphate granules. Whole-cell 3D rendering allowed quantification of carboxysomes, cyanophycin granules, and measurement of thylakoid thickness and spacing in A. inaequalis and Anabaena sp. UTEX 2576. Thus, cryo-vEM provided interpretable whole-cell ultrastructure of cyanobacteria without chemical pre-treatment, and its compatibility with cryo-fluorescence and in situ cryo-ET enables contextual multi-scale perspectives from whole cells to molecular structures.

papers.title: A transient pulse of neuronal ATF4 installs a durable non-autonomous programme promoting healthy ageing
papers.abstract: Stresses occurring transiently and early in life can have long-standing consequences for health, even long after the stress has resolved. Many environmental stressors converge on activating the integrated stress response (ISR), whose major effector is ATF4. However, it remains unknown whether transient ATF4-ISR activation early in life is a mediator of life and healthspan. Here we used inducible, reversible ATF4 gain-of-function in Drosophila to determine how the timing, duration and tissue of ATF4 activation determine ageing outcomes. We found that ATF4 induction confined to early adulthood extended healthspan, reducing mortality risk by approximately 50% across all ages and improving neuromuscular function in aged flies. Multi-organ transcriptomics showed that the acute ATF4 transcriptional response was transient, as expected, but replaced by a distinct, secondary transcriptional programme of metabolic remodelling that was associated with decreased total body protein content. By using tissue-specific ATF4 induction, we found that transient ATF4 activation in neurons was sufficient to extend lifespan, slow age-related locomotor decline and increase starvation resistance in old age. This neuron-restricted activation prevented the costs to body weight and fecundity induced by ubiquitous ATF4 activation. Transient neuronal ATF4 left a lasting non-autonomous imprint on the fat body at old age: induction of heterochromatin genes, reduced transposable element expression, and increased mitochondrial respiratory capacity. These findings show that the duration and tissue of ISR-ATF4 activation are the key determinants of ATF4 actions that promote healthy ageing, while revealing a brain-to-fat body axis initiated by neuronal ATF4 that results in lasting systemic adaptation.

papers.title: Recruitment of intrasegmental and propriospinal interneuron networks of forelimb motor circuitry in chronic cervical contusion spinal cord injury
papers.abstract: Cervical spinal cord injury (SCI) disrupts descending supraspinal input and spinal networks controlling upper extremity motor function, making recovery of arm and hand function a major priority for affected individuals. The vast majority of regenerative strategies have been studied during the acute and sub-acute phases following SCI, while therapeutic testing remains limited for chronic injury, when persistent barriers significantly limit circuit remodeling. We asked whether pharmacologic enhancement of neuronal-intrinsic axon growth capacity through PTEN inhibition could promote forelimb motor recovery and circuit plasticity in a rodent model of chronic cervical SCI. Following C5 hemi-contusion, female rats underwent behavioral testing of forelimb motor function and received PTEN antagonist peptide (PAP) beginning at a chronic time point, and the trans-synaptic tracer, pseudorabies virus (PRV), was injected into ipsilesional triceps to trace forelimb-associated motor circuitry. PAP selectively improved forelimb usage during cylinder paw-preference testing, but not strength, sensorimotor, or gait-related forelimb measures. PAP increased recruitment of PRV-traced local-projecting and propriospinal interneuron networks. In addition, PAP enhanced synaptic input to these recruited propriospinal interneurons, raising the possibility that spared descending pathways may contribute to recovery through spinal relay circuits. Lastly, we mapped the supraspinal connectome providing descending input from brainstem to the lower motor neurons innervating forelimb muscle, and we determined how this connectome was impacted both by SCI and PAP. Together, these findings show that, even in chronic SCI, pharmacological PTEN inhibition can promote forelimb functional recovery and significant circuit remodeling, with spinal interneuron networks emerging as a key site of PAP-induced plasticity.

papers.title: vafSOMA: Detecting cell-layer-fixed somatic mutations in plants
papers.abstract: Somatic mutations are a source of heritable genetic variation in plants and have long been exploited by breeders through selection and vegetative propagation of bud sports. They often arise in specific meristem layers and can become fixed as descendant cell lineages expand during development. Bulk sequencing of plant organs mixes DNA from these layers, so the expected variant allele frequency of a layer-fixed mutation depends on that layer's tissue contribution, which complicates their detection. Here we present vafSOMA, a statistical model that uses tissue composition to detect fixed somatic mutations, assign them to layers and obtain counts for mutation-rate estimation. It accommodates bulk and layer-enriched samples, including those that retain DNA from other layers after enrichment. In simulations, vafSOMA performed close to the best variant allele frequency cutoff chosen in hindsight, without requiring a user-selected cutoff. Its diagnostics flagged layers for which the data did not support separate mutation counts or rates. Analysing replicate organs substantially improved detection of mutations fixed in the branch meristem and yielded estimates close to the simulated stem-cell mutation rate. Application to apricot sequencing data showed that most reference mutations fixed in the dominant layer were recovered from fruit mixtures at high depth, whereas epidermal mutations remained unresolvable in fruit and leaves. These findings suggest that published bulk somatic sequencing studies mainly capture mutations fixed in the dominant tissue layer and may therefore underestimate the combined input of fixed mutations by roughly two- to threefold when layer-specific rates are similar. vafSOMA is available at https://github.com/jlab-code/vafSOMA.

papers.title: Model-Agnostic Decomposition of the Difference in Mean Response Between Two Groups via Game-Theoretic Attribution with Minimum-Switching-Distortion Coupling
papers.abstract: The difference in mean response between two groups can arise from differences in covariate-response relationships, covariate distributions, or both. We propose a model-agnostic decomposition (MAD) of this difference into structure and composition effects. We formulate a cooperative switching game with a model-switch player and individual covariate-switch players, organized into model and covariate unions. MAD employs the Owen value, whose quotient game yields the aggregate structure and composition effects and whose internal game allocates the aggregate composition effect across covariates, and thereby inherits its fair allocation properties. In the internal game, partial covariate switches create hybrid covariate vectors whose joint distributions are not determined by the group-specific covariate distributions alone. To resolve this indeterminacy, we propose a minimum-switching-distortion (MSD) coupling, formulated as an optimal-transport problem. The MSD coupling satisfies admissibility conditions of identity at coincidence, transposition equivariance, and coordinate equivariance, and its sparse support reduces allocation cost. Because MAD imposes no particular functional form, it accommodates machine-learning models that adapt to complex nonlinear and interactive relationships, thereby yielding more accurate decompositions. Simulation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of MAD and the MSD coupling in terms of decomposition accuracy, coupling admissibility, and computational cost. As an illustration, we decompose the difference in mean body mass index between UK and US males aged 30-70 years using microbiome data, at the aggregate level and across microbial genera.

papers.title: Omics-scale decoding of protein N-glycosylation using protein language model embeddings
papers.abstract: Protein language models (pLMs) learn rich sequence semantics from vast volume of protein sequences, yet the information encoded in their high-dimensional embeddings remains largely a black box, posing an interpretability challenge. Here we show that semantic features learned by pLMs can be decoded to reveal biologically meaningful signals using coevolutionary analysis without downstream supervised-training. Building on this insight, we developed MaskNGly, a zero-shot framework that identifies protein N-glycosylation sites directly from PLM-embeddings while achieving performance comparable to state-of-the-art supervised predictors. MaskNGly is computationally efficient and intrinsically transferable, enabling omics-scale characterization of protein glycosylation landscape. Applied across proteomes, it reveals that canonical N-X-S/T motifs gain higher glycosylation propensities with increasing organismal complexity and that glycosylation preferentially occurs at structured, solvent-exposed regions. Mutations altering high-scoring motifs are more frequently disease-associated. The framework also captures signatures of glycosylation-mediated protein allostery. These results establish an interpretable and scalable route to study glycobiology from pLM-embeddings.

papers.title: Particle-Associated Prokaryotic Community Structures in the Bering and Chukchi Seas
papers.abstract: Free-living and particle-associated bacteria play distinct roles in the cycling of organic matter, but how these lifestyles are partitioned in the highly productive, rapidly warming Bering and Chukchi Seas is largely unknown. During the Arctic Shelf Growth, Advection, Respiration and Deposition Rate Experiments (ASGARD) cruise in June 2017, a period of anomalously warm sea surface temperatures, we collected 78 samples at three depths (surface, middle, and bottom) at 12 process stations and sequentially filtered them onto 20 {micro}m, 3 {micro}m, and 0.2 {micro}m filters. Using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and hierarchical clustering of amplicon sequence variant (ASV) relative abundances, we resolved four sample clusters. Although pore size was not used to build the clusters, communities separated into a free-living cluster associated mainly with Anadyr Water (FL1; 0.2 {micro}m fraction) and three particle-associated clusters (PA1-PA3; 3 and 20 {micro}m fractions), several of which were enriched in Bacteroidia. Alphaproteobacteria, Gammaproteobacteria, and Bacteroidia were present in all size fractions, with Gammaproteobacteria most biased toward the free-living fraction. Community structure did not differ with depth, consistent with the shallow, weakly stratified shelf, and distance-based redundancy analysis identified salinity as the sole significant environmental factor distinguishing communities. These results suggest that lifestyle and water-mass origin, rather than depth, structure size-fractionated bacterial communities on the Pacific Arctic shelf, and that freshening and changes in bloom dynamics could reshape particle-associated communities in this region.

papers.title: Factors affecting microbial community composition in Split Lake, MB, Canada
papers.abstract: Split Lake is a large freshwater lake in northern Manitoba, Canada, that receives major inflows from the Nelson River, Burntwood River, and Grassy River. In 1976, during the Churchill River Diversion (CRD) project, most of the water in the Churchill River was diverted into the Nelson River via the Rat River, and the Burntwood River, creating a large inflow pressure in the lower Nelson area, including Split Lake. Decades after its implementation, the Churchill River Diversion still influences ecological and environmental processes in the area. In this study, metabarcoding of the 16S rRNA gene was employed to characterize the microbial community structure of the lake. Environmental factors (temperature, pH, turbidity, dissolved oxygen) and cyanotoxin levels were also assessed. The objectives of this study were to establish a baseline for microbiota across the lake and examine how environmental variables affect microbial population dynamics. The study was conducted in the summer of 2024, encompassing 14 sites on Split Lake and 2 sites on Assean Lake, an adjacent waterbody with minimal influence from hydroelectric infrastructure. Split Lake was found to harbor six distinct microbial clusters, with turbidity and dissolved oxygen levels correlating with different aquatic regimes within the lake. The predominant taxa in Split Lake included Actinobacteria hgcI clade and Cyanobium. Microcystin concentrations measured throughout the study were always below the Maximum Acceptable Concentration (MAC) set for Canadian federal drinking water standards.

papers.title: A biomimetic SPARC platform coupling adaptor recruitment and BRS-Lck condensation for enhanced NK/T cell combination therapy
papers.abstract: Immune cell engineering has proven to be a promising therapeutic strategy for cancers and autoimmune diseases. Compared to classical CAR therapies, engineered T cells with modified TCRs (such as STAR-T and TRuC-T) exhibit lower tonic signaling and higher persistence. Inspired by this, we developed novel Synthetic Parallel Antigen Receptor Complexes (SPARC) based on the NK cell receptor 1 (NCR1) and the TCR chain. These SPARCs can recognize target cells via engineered extracellular domains and transduce signals by recruiting endogenous adaptor proteins (CD3{zeta}/FcR{gamma}). In NK cells,SPARCs confer high antigen specificity against lymphoma and enables NK cells to specifically recognize and kill tumor cells. Mechanistically, the cytoplasmic domain of NCR1 forms condensates with Lck kinase through two conserved basic-rich sequences (BRS), thereby promoting receptor clustering and enhancing NK cell cytotoxicity. Our findings indicate that SPARCs can also be applied to other immune cells expressing CD3{zeta} and FcR{gamma}. Incorporation of costimulatory domains further improves the performance of SPARCs. Furthermore, combining SPARC-engineered T cells and NK cells showed superior efficacy compared to either cell type alone. This biomimetic design preserves low basal signaling, overcomes the recognition limitations of endogenous receptors, and provides a versatile platform for engineering other membrane complexes.

papers.title: BioTrajX: evaluating biological plausibility in single-cell trajectory inference
papers.abstract: Trajectory inference (TI) methods reconstruct cellular progression from single-cell RNA sequencing data, typically by ordering cells along a pseudotime axis. However, different TI methods and analytical choices can produce divergent trajectories from the same dataset, making it difficult to determine which inferred trajectory best reflects the underlying biological process. Existing evaluation strategies often rely on computational benchmarks or qualitative biological assessment, with limited standardized approaches for incorporating a priori biological knowledge. Here, we present BioTrajX, an R package for biologically informed evaluation of pseudotime trajectories using three complementary metrics: Directionality (D), which measures agreement between pseudotime and expected biological progression; Order Consistency (O), which quantifies the coherence of marker-program changes along the trajectory; and Endpoint Validity (E), which assesses enrichment of expected cell states at trajectory endpoints. Together, the DOE metrics provide an interpretable framework for comparing alternative trajectory inference results and evaluating root-cell choices prior to downstream analyses.

papers.title: Sex-specific growth in invasive pink salmon (Oncorhynchus gorbuscha) from two regions in northern Norway
papers.abstract: The recent invasion of pink salmon (Oncorhynchus gorbuscha) along the Norwegian coast has raised significant ecological concerns. Investigating regional differences in marine growth is an important step in evaluating the establishment of pink salmon in new environments. Pink salmon were captured in two northern Norwegian fjords during their return migration to in the summer of 2023; Varangerfjord in Finnmark and Oksfjord in Troms, representing the eastern and western extent of the core areas of the pink salmon invasion. Body size estimates (total length, weight, condition factor) were used to identify differences in sex-specific marine growth at the time of capture. Scales were analyzed to estimate marine somatic growth via the distance between circuli and the position of the last winter circuli (LWC). Estimates of cumulative circuli distance were divided into four marine growth periods that roughly correspond to 1) spring/summer, year one, 2) summer/fall, year one, 3) fall/winter, year one, and 4) spring, year two. Sex-specific and location effects were found in the body size of pink salmon, where males were heavier and had higher body condition than females and Varanger males had the highest estimates of body size. Scale readings revealed that growth rates were highest in the spring of both years (periods 1 and 4), with significantly decreased growth in the fall/winter (periods 2 and 3). Males from the established Varanger location exhibited the highest growth (17-21% total cumulative circuli distance) over all periods compared to the other groups, suggesting that these fish experience more favorable survivorship and marine growth conditions. These insights into pink salmon marine growth emphasize the importance of taking sex and location into consideration in further assessing the species' expansive potential in Norway.

papers.title: The bHLH121-CAT2 module maintains root tip redox homeostasis to confer salt tolerance additively with the SOS pathway in Arabidopsis
papers.abstract: Soil salinity inhibits plant growth, in part, by restricting the availability of essential mineral nutrients such as iron (Fe). Although Fe deficiency frequently coincides with salt stress in the field, the molecular mechanisms integrating Fe homeostasis with salt tolerance remain largely unknown. Here, we identify the Fe deficiency response regulator bHLH121 as a key coordinator of salt tolerance in Arabidopsis. Loss-of-function mutants of bHLH121 exhibit pronounced hypersensitivity to salt stress, with severely impaired primary root elongation and reduced seedling biomass. Transcriptomic and histochemical analyses reveal that bHLH121 is required to maintain reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis specifically in root tips under salt stress. We further demonstrate that CATALASE 2 (CAT2) is a direct downstream target of bHLH121, and that CAT2 overexpression fully rescues the salt hypersensitivity of the bhlh121 mutant. Importantly, this bHLH121-CAT2 module operates independently of the classical SOS pathway, as sos2 bhlh121 double mutants display additive salt sensitivity. Together, our findings uncover a novel regulatory module in which bHLH121 governs root tip redox homeostasis through CAT2 to confer salt tolerance, providing a direct mechanistic link between the Fe regulatory network and abiotic stress resilience in plants.

papers.title: Massively parallel quantification and prediction of monomeric protein yield in Escherichia coli
papers.abstract: Obtaining sufficient quantities of purified proteins in their intended molecular states is essential for biological research and protein engineering. Advances in computational protein design have expanded the functional capabilities of de novo proteins and accelerated candidate generation. However, reliable methods for ranking expected monomeric yield of candidate de novo designs, including molecular binders, fluorescent proteins and enzymes, have yet to be established. Standardized measurements of monomeric yield across diverse sequences remain scarce, limiting our understanding of its determinants and the development of accurate predictors for candidate selection. Here we developed a scalable pooled assay combining peptide barcodes, size-exclusion chromatography and mass spectrometry to quantify monomeric yield for over 39,000 natural protein domain variants, de novo proteins and nanobodies under uniform and standardized Escherichia coli production conditions. We used this dataset to (1) quantify the relationship between folding stability and monomeric yield, (2) benchmark inverse-folding methods, (3) evaluate the utility of structure-prediction confidence metrics in selecting high-yield design candidates, and (4) identify sequence and structural patterns in nanobodies associated with monomeric yield and monomer-to-dimer yield ratios. We further developed ESMC-MonoYield, a protein language model fine-tuned to predict monomeric yield from amino acid sequence alone, and prospectively demonstrated enrichment of high-yield candidates among BindCraft-designed binders. Our approach enables standardized, large-scale measurement of monomeric yield across diverse proteins, and establishes monomeric yield as a sequence-encoded property that can be learned, predicted and ultimately designed.

papers.title: Complementary chemical and effect-based risk assessments reveal ecotoxicological risks in Caribbean coastal bays and coral reefs
authors: van de Loosdrecht, N. C. J.
papers.abstract: Anthropogenic chemical pollution poses a significant, yet often unquantified threat to coral reef ecosystems. This study investigated the occurrence, dispersal, and ecotoxicological risks of chemical mixtures in three inland bays of Curacao (Southern Caribbean) and adjacent coral reefs during wet and dry seasons. Passive sampler extracts were analyzed with targeted chemical analysis and effect-based methods. Inland bays acted as reservoirs for chemical pollution, each exhibiting a unique chemical fingerprint likely linked to surrounding land use. Targeted chemical concentrations were higher during the wet season, particularly inside the bays, indicating rainfall-driven mobilization of terrestrial contaminants.
