Many compounds exceeded their predicted no-effect concentrations, while mixture toxic pressure was low to moderate and highest inside the bays. In contrast, bioassays integrating the effects of the entire mixture revealed a potential ecotoxicological risk, with activation of the Nrf2 oxidative stress pathway dominating across reef sites. The two lines of evidence were complementary: target compounds identify the bays as pollution sources, while bioassays show mixture effects are strongest on the reefs. Hence,targeted chemical analysis alone is insufficient to evaluate ecotoxicological risk. Our multidisciplinary approach provides a framework for prioritizing key chemical indicators and bioassays to monitor coral reef water quality.

papers.title: Context, not contradiction: a pan-cancer framework for conforming and nonconforming co-expression programmes
papers.abstract: Reports of a gene's role in cancer frequently conflict: the same transcript is described as an adverse prognostic marker in one tumour type and a favourable one in another, and such discordance is usually attributed to cohort differences or to irreproducibility. An alternative explanation is that the transcriptional company a gene keeps genuinely differs between lineages. That claim is testable, but testing it requires separating real lineage-dependence from three artefacts that pervade pan-cancer co-expression analysis: public summaries report only coefficients above a fixed threshold, a gene in a recurrently gained region acquires correlates through dosage alone, and conservation across cancer types is assumed rather than measured. We present a framework that addresses all three for any index gene. Correlations are recomputed threshold-free from each cohort's expression matrix; transcripts are partitioned into cis and trans sets relative to the index gene after retired symbols are resolved; a recurrence rule freezes the gene set before any downstream analysis; cohorts are scored against expression-decile-matched permutation nulls; and copy number is residualised out using the cis set as a built-in positive control, so the adjustment is shown to work before the trans result is read. Applied to PTK2, encoding focal adhesion kinase, across 17 TCGA cohorts, expression was associated with poor outcome in several cancers and better outcome in others, independently of tumour purity. The framework shows this is not noise: cohorts separate into conforming and nonconforming groups enriched for different biology. The 44-transcript trans programme is unchanged by copy-number adjustment while the cis control collapses by 38%, and co-expression is recoverable within individual tumours in 133 of 243 single-cell cases.

papers.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Links Group-Specific Plasma Proteomics to Regional Structural Neuroimaging in Alzheimer's Disease
papers.abstract: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology begins years before clinical symptoms, highlighting the need for scalable biomarkers that capture biological changes across the AD continuum. Broader plasma proteomics may capture systemic processes that vary with disease stage, yet their relationship to AD-related brain neurodegeneration remains unclear. We aimed to identify plasma proteomic signatures across cognitively normal (CN), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and AD and evaluate their neuroanatomical associations. Methods: We analyzed 146 plasma analytes from 565 Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) participants (58 CN, 396 MCI, 111 AD). Group-specific proteomic signatures were identified using pairwise classification models with nested 5*5 cross-validation. SHAP quantified feature importance, with the top 15 proteins per comparison being prioritized for MRI association analysis. We analyzed 103 regional structural MRI volumes harmonized across 57 acquisition sites using ComBat. Separate ordinary least squares regression tested protein-MRI associations, adjusting for age, sex, APOE4, diagnosis, and intracranial volume, followed by Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Results: Classification models using proteomic data achieved AUC of 0.956 +- 0.017 for CN vs MCI, 0.963 +- 0.011 for MCI vs. AD, and 0.836 +- 0.085 for CN vs. AD. SHAP identified group-dependent proteomic signatures. No protein-MRI associations survived FDR correction for CN vs. MCI. In MCI vs. AD, higher cortisol was associated with lower left precuneus and superior parietal volumes, while higher osteopontin was associated with lower left paracentral and accumbens volumes. In CN vs. AD, higher vitronectin was associated with lower posterior corpus callosum volume. Conclusion: These findings suggest that plasma proteomics capture group-specific systemic biological signals across the AD continuum. Linking ML-prioritized plasma proteins to regional brain structure provides neuroanatomical context for blood-based biomarker discovery.

papers.title: Single-probe, high-yield spatial mapping of diverse short RNA motifs
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics has revolutionized our understanding of RNA biology. Hybridization-based methods map mRNA transcripts by tiling multiple labeled probes along each molecule to generate a visible fluorescent signal, restricting applicability to long transcripts. Short RNA motifs, consequently, can only accommodate a single probe and remain a spatially invisible dimension of RNA biology. Here we present SMOOTHY-FISH, a single probe strategy that directly visualizes short RNA motifs at the single-molecule resolution. By optimizing probe brightness, binding specificity, and target accessibility, our single ~20-nucleotide probe reached the practical ceiling of hybridization-based detection. We quantitatively mapped previously inaccessible short motifs - splice-isoform junctions, individual microRNAs, and structural conformations - in single cells and mouse brain tissues, each validated against orthogonal methods. This unveiled biological phenomena that were previously unknown: ratios of alternatively spliced isoforms are tightly regulated across cell populations, subcellular miRNA fractions are precisely maintained, and a designed RNA structure was found to have a prominent alternative conformation. These findings demonstrate that short RNA motifs possess key spatial information that has yet to be discovered. With SMOOTHY-FISH's optimized single probe technique, short RNA motifs are converted into a new routinely measurable axis of spatial transcriptomics.

papers.title: Polygenic polymorphisms cooperate to drive expansion of HCMV adaptive NK cell and NK-like T cell populations
papers.abstract: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) infection drives the expansion of several innate and innate-like lymphocyte populations. Characterized by high cell surface expression of NKG2C, these populations include the adaptive CD56+ Fc{epsilon}RI{gamma}- NK cell, an NK-like TCR{beta}+CD8+ T cell population and a V{gamma}9/V{delta}1+ T cells. Beyond NKG2C expression, both the adaptive NK cell and the NK-like T cell population exhibit enhanced cytokine response to antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC). Expansion of each population is only observed in 30-40% of HCMV+ individuals and is independent of expansion of each other. In this study, we evaluated 200 healthy donors and identified several immunogenetic factors that influence NKG2C expression across the three lymphocyte populations. NKG2C (KLRC2) copy number and allelic polymorphism was associated with NKG2C+ NK cell frequency and surface expression density in HCMV- but not in HCMV+ individuals. Investigating other genetic loci encoding proteins related to adaptive NK function, we found that CD16a and HLA-E alleles act cumulatively with NKG2C copy number to drive NKG2C expression on lymphocytes among HCMV+ individuals. Polymorphism of the NKG2C ligand HLA-E influences strength of NK cell activation via NKG2C, where NK responsiveness was lower in individuals with the HLA-E*01:03 genotype, while CD16a polymorphism influenced strength of ADCC response among NKG2C+ TCR{beta}+CD8+ T cells. Based on these observations, we conclude that genetic polymorphisms in NKG2C, CD16a and HLA-E shape the NKG2C+ repertoire, influence NKG2C-mediated NK function and dictate capacity of ADCC in response to HCMV infection. Immunogenetic polymorphism among NKG2C-related genes therefore tunes innate immunity to HCMV infection providing additional protection beyond adaptive immunity.

papers.title: Heat-evolved strains of the coral symbiont Cladocopium proliferum have diverged in exon usage
papers.abstract: Experimental evolution at 31{degrees}C produced strains of the coral symbiont Cladocopium proliferum (Symbiodiniaceae) that show increased thermal tolerance in culture, and some of them also raise the bleaching tolerance of coral. Here we investigated how exon usage and alternative splicing have diverged in the heat-evolved strains (SS3, SS5, SS8) from their wild-type cultures (WT10) by reanalysing published transcriptomes of the strains in symbiosis with Acropora kenti larvae at 27{degrees}C using limma, DEXSeq and rMATS. Exon usage separated the strains from an unselected wild-type strain, with 1,308 genes with differential exon usage for SS8, 4,931 for SS5 and 10,464 for SS3, and 59% to 72% of these genes showed no differential expression. SS8, the only strain that also raises the bleaching tolerance of coral larvae, was the closest to the wild type, while a shared set of 757 genes changed in all three heat-evolved strains together. Junction level splicing events (rMATS) did not follow this order (721, 687 and 847 events against WT10), and skipped exons were the most common type, followed by alternative 5' splice sites. Between SS8 and the non-protective strains, alternative 5' splice sites were the most common type (91 of 291 events against SS5 and 68 of 207 against SS3), and retained introns were nearly as common as skipped exons. No GO term was enriched in the shared set or the SS8 lists, but both held genes with a possible link to heat tolerance, among them a mitochondrial glutathione peroxidase in the shared set and a glutathione S-transferase in which SS8 differed from the non-protective strains. Future studies of heat-evolved symbionts should therefore include exon level and splicing analyses to resolve the fine scale differences between strains that gene level analyses miss.

papers.title: CD200R1 Marks a Branchpoint During Human Natural Killer Cell Development in Tonsils
papers.abstract: Human natural killer (NK) cells arise from common innate lymphoid cell (ILC) progenitor and precursor populations that are selectively enriched within secondary lymphoid tissues (SLTs) and that complete their terminal differentiation through stages of progressively lineage-restricted downstream developmental intermediates. We identify two subsets of tonsil CD94/NKG2A+NKp80- (stage 4A) NK-cell development intermediates that show differential expression of the inhibitory receptor, CD200R1. Ex vivo single-cell transcriptomic, DNA methylation, phenotypic, and functional analyses demonstrate that CD200R1 stage 4A cells represent an immature, oligopotent precursor population enriched for tissue-resident and cytokine-responsive programs. In contrast, CD200R1- stage 4A cells show more restricted NK-cell developmental potential concomitant with features of mature NK cells. These findings help to refine the human NK cell developmental pathway in tonsils and highlight CD200R1 as a useful marker delineating an uncommitted developmental state linking microenvironmental cues to NK-cell maturation and plasticity.

papers.title: Adaptation of breast cancer cells to serum-free defined medium reveals changes in proliferation, adhesion, and lipid metabolism
papers.abstract: Cancer cell metabolic dependencies are strongly influenced by nutrient availability, yet conventional culture conditions contain non-physiological nutrient concentrations and poorly defined serum components that may obscure metabolic vulnerabilities. Here, we investigated the adaptation of three breast cancer cell lines to physiologically relevant, serum-free defined medium (DM). Using a stepwise reduction in fetal bovine serum (FBS), we evaluated proliferation, adhesion, morphology, and transcriptional changes in HER2-positive SK-BR-3, triple-negative MDA-MB-231, and ER-positive/HER2-positive BT-474 cells. The three cell lines differed substantially in their ability to adapt to serum-free conditions. MDA-MB-231 cells adapted readily, maintaining proliferation and adhesion without exogenous substrate coatings. SK-BR-3 cells also achieved sustained proliferation in serum-free DM, but required a serum-derived coating to maintain adhesion. In contrast, BT-474 cells failed to sustain adhesion and proliferation following complete serum withdrawal, although they remained proliferative in medium containing 1% FBS. Adapted cells retained characteristic HER2 or vimentin expression despite changes in morphology and proliferation. RNA sequencing revealed extensive transcriptional remodeling, including reduced expression of cell-cycle-associated programs in SK-BR-3 cells and enrichment of cholesterol homeostasis gene sets in SK-BR-3 and MDA-MB-231 cells. Expression of cholesterol regulatory genes, including SREBF2, HMGCR, and LDLR, increased across all three lines. Together, these findings highlight cell-line-specific adhesion requirements and shared metabolic responses to serum withdrawal, establishing a framework for developing defined culture systems to investigate cancer metabolic dependencies through genetic screening.

papers.title: Photographic age gap is associated with frailty and predicts survival in laboratory mice
papers.abstract: Ageing studies in mice need biomarkers that are cheap, non-invasive and repeatable. We asked how much of a mouse's age can be read from an ordinary photograph, and whether the part that cannot be explained by age carries biological information. We assembled 2,846 photographs of 1,292 mice (four strains, 1 to 34 months old) from seven facilities and predicted age with a frozen self-supervised vision model (DINOv2) and a ridge regression, always tested on facilities the model had never seen. Absolute age transferred poorly between facilities (median absolute error 138 days), because each facility's photographs carried an offset. Relative age transferred well: among mice photographed in the same session, the older mouse was predicted older in 65% of pairs, rising above 95% for age differences over 500 days, and the later photograph of the same mouse was predicted older in 63% of repeat pairs. Sex, in comparison, was inferred more reliably (87%). Mice predicted older than their age were frailer (+0.12 SD per 100 days) and had shorter survival (hazard ratio 1.14 per 100 days), and fourth generation (G4) telomerase-deficient mice looked 151 days older than their wild-type controls. Routine photographs therefore carry a real biological age signal that can be read at no extra cost, best used to compare mice photographed together.

papers.title: Cascaded Dual-Targeting (WTW/TAT) Liposomes Delivery DOX for Precision Glioblastoma Treatment
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains difficult to treat because the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and blood-tumor barrier (BTB) severely limit drug transport into tumor tissue. To address these delivery constraints, we developed a dual-targeted liposomal nanoplatform (WT-LIP) that integrates a WTW dual-targeting peptide to promote receptor-mediated BBB transcytosis and specificity to GBM and a TAT peptide to enhance post-barrier penetration and tumor-cell uptake, enabling sequential barrier crossing and GBM targeting. DOX@WT-LIP efficiently encapsulated doxorubicin (DOX) and increased endothelial transport in vitro, achieving a permeated dose of 60.74 {+/-} 2.14% at 480 min, while producing deeper transendothelial penetration and greater downstream tumor killing in a BBB/GBM co-culture. In orthotopic U251-luc models, DiD-labeled WT-LIP showed enhanced brain/tumor accumulation (G/B = 2.16 {+/-} 0.06), and DOX@WT-LIP markedly suppressed tumor growth (74.92% inhibition), improved survival, and exhibited comparatively reduced systemic toxicity. This work highlights a ligand-guided strategy that couples efficient BBB transport with tumor-selective delivery to improve GBM chemotherapy.

papers.title: Role of Very Long-Chain Fatty Acyl-Ceramides in Endocytic Uptake
papers.abstract: Specialized endoplasmic reticulum (ER) subdomains termed ER sterol exit sites (ERSES), transiently contact endocytic sites to locally supply sterols, which in turn initiate actin polymerization and drive membrane invagination. Osh2, an oxysterol-binding protein (OSBP)-related protein (ORP), mediates the non-vesicular sterol transfer at ER-endocytic contact sites (ER-ECS). In search for additional ERSES components, we identified Fat1, a fatty acid (FA) transporter and acyl-CoA synthetase with specificity for very long-chain (VLC) FAs (C20-C26). Analysis of VLC-FA anabolic and catabolic pathways revealed a specific requirement for VLC fatty acyl-ceramides (VLCA-Cers) in the constriction of endocytic invaginations. Strikingly, the Cer synthase physically interacted with the endocytic machinery, pointing to a direct role of VLCFA-Cers in membrane remodelling. Consistent with this view, molecular dynamics and live-cell imaging of a Cer probe indicated that the ORPs Osh1 and Osh3 contribute to Cer export from at ER-ECS and and that their depletion recapitulates the endocytic defects observed in the absence of VLCFA-Cer. Our findings establish that local transport of VLCA-Cers is required for endocytic budding and reveal ERSES as hubs where Cer and sterol biosynthesis and transport converge

papers.title: A Phenomenological Model of Synaptic Activity in the Blowfly Lamina
papers.abstract: Estimates of the effective Poisson rate obtained from voltage recordings of Large Monopolar Cells (LMCs) in the blowfly lamina, measured in response to repeated light-contrast stimuli, are on the order of 5x105 events per second. These values imply that if vesicle exocytosis at photoreceptor-LMC synapse consisted of statistically independent quantal release events, the mean release rate would need to be at least this large to account for the observed signal and noise characteristics. Such a scenario is highly implausible, as it would correspond to an exocytosis rate of approximately 400 vesicles per second per active zone, or equivalently to the turnover of a membrane area comparable to that of all six photoreceptor axon terminals within a lamina cartridge more than twice per second. Relaxing the assumption of statistical independence, however, allows for substantially larger effective Poisson rates. In earlier work, we demonstrated that temporal regularization of release events- particularly through a reduction in low-frequency noise power spectral density- can increase the effective Poisson rate without altering the underlying mean release rate. Additionally, the contrast-to-current impulse response function of the extracellular space has been shown to be approximately equal in magnitude and opposite in sign to that of the LMCs, suggesting that both signals arise from the same chloride current. This observation provides a potential physiological mechanism for vesicle regularization, although it was previously described only in qualitative and simplified terms. In the present work, we develop a phenomenological model that incorporates these findings together with additional physiological parameters from literature to account for the regularization of vesicle release.

papers.title: Neural dynamics become significantly faster and more nonlinear at the peak of information processing
papers.abstract: The temporal scale at which neural populations preserve stimulus information is often treated as fixed, even though population activity changes rapidly during sensory processing. Whether the information-optimal scale changes within a single stimulus-evoked episode, and what determines its evolution, remains unclear. We developed Integration-Split, a decoding-based framework that estimates the time-varying temporal resolution of population spike trains. Across four visual paradigms and throughout the mouse visual hierarchy, the optimal scale contracted after stimulus onset and subsequently re-expanded. This pattern persisted across stimulus temporal frequencies and was largely absent in a hippocampal control. The optimal scale varied inversely with stimulus decodability, reaching its finest resolution when stimulus identity was most accurately decoded. Beyond this association, independently estimating the signal-noise autocorrelation balance across candidate window widths identified the window that maximized the autocorrelation-based signal-to-noise ratio, and this optimal width closely followed the Integration-Split trajectory. Consistent with these findings, stronger nonlinear predictive structure coincided with finer optimal temporal resolution, consistent with the idea that shorter integration windows are needed to preserve informative nonlinear population structure that would otherwise be attenuated by temporal averaging. To test the functional relevance of this organization, we trained a Transformer solely to decode stimulus identity, without providing the optimal temporal-scale pattern or Integration-Split outputs. Its learned attention exhibited a similar contraction-and-recovery profile, and disrupting heads with stronger correspondence produced larger decoding deficits. Together, these findings reveal a dynamically changing, information-optimal temporal scale in population coding, shaped by the evolving balance of signal and noise autocorrelation and by nonlinear population structure, and independently recapitulated in the learned attention of a Transformer trained without temporal-scale supervision.

papers.title: Contributions of Site Heterogeneity in Multi-site Brain-Phenotype Predictions
papers.abstract: Machine learning studies of brain-phenotype associations typically summarize accuracy with a single Pearson correlation, yet in harmonized multi-site data this metric is shaped by training-set size, feature and outcome variability, and true effect heterogeneity. We analyzed structural MRI data from the Reproducible Brain Charts consortium. After preprocessing and quality control, 3486 participants from 9 sites were retained. Three training set compositions were used to understand contributions of site heterogeneity after harmonization: within-site (Local), size-downsampled multi-site (Multi-Down), and full multi-site (Multi-Full). Another site-agnostic strategy (Overall) pooled all sites into a single dataset. All strategies included the target site in the training and testing samples. These analyses separate the contribution of the site effect from that of sample size. Between-site heterogeneity was extensive (age I^2 {approx} 95%). The overall correlation of age prediction (r = 0.73) exceeded the within-site meta-analytic estimate (Multi-Full r = 0.63). The improvement of correlation in the pooled dataset was driven by a mechanical inflation from the larger outcome variance. At matched sample size, within-site training outperformed harmonized multi-site training. Increasing the multi-site training sample size did not yield a significant advantage over within-site training. The apparent advantage of cross-dataset training thus appears to reflect training-set size rather than a benefit of multi-site composition per se. The same pattern generally held for the weaker brain-p-factor signals. Together, these results indicate that between-site heterogeneity in machine learning brain-phenotype prediction persists after harmonization. We recommend reporting site-level prediction accuracy and feature dispersion and standard deviation of the outcome variable alongside any pooled estimate to improve inter-site and inter-study comparison of machine learning prediction accuracy.

papers.title: Basal ganglia output guides decision-making by state destabilization
papers.abstract: To execute learned behavior, the nervous system can undergo an activity-state transition between the current and the learned activity states. Here, using adult zebrafish, we show that their basal ganglia output induces such state transitions for goal-directed behavior. After learning the Go/No-go task in virtual reality, the striatal indirect pathway responds to negative values of a conditioned cue and the absence of sensory feedback by different neuronal populations. The pallidal output pathway integrates these negative value signals and then broadcasts the integrated signal to the Dc area in the pallium (fish cortex). Optogenetics and mathematical modeling suggested that this pallidal output activity uniformly destabilizes ongoing Dc activity states, thereby facilitating behavioral state transitions toward the behavioral state with the minimum pallidal output activity. This mechanism explains how pallidal output activity guides goal-directed behavior beyond potential barriers between activity states underlying different behavioral states.

papers.title: Feeding experiments with Senegal bichir Polypterus senegalus provide evidence for diet-related tooth damage and dental microwear
papers.abstract: Dental microwear is a useful tool for reconstructing jaw movements and diet in toothed vertebrates, but its application to fishes (Actinopterygii and Chondrichthyes) remains limited. This is partly due to the lack of experiments directly linking diet and microwear in these groups; only one highly-derived teleost (Actinopterygii, or ray-finned fishes) species of recent origins, the three-spined stickleback Gasterosteus aculeatus, has been subject to controlled feeding experiments. As sticklebacks are suction or ram feeders that live on macroplankton and insect larvae and do not use their dentitions for prey processing, the absence of experimental data from other fish species limits our ability to interpret dental microwear and infer diet and feeding style in a wider range of fossil and living species with various ecologies. Here we present the results of a second feeding experiment involving fishes using the basally-branching, biting, often-piscivorous ray-finned fish Senegal bichir Polypterus senegalus to evaluate whether controlled diet differences can generate detectable tooth damage and dental microwear patterns. Individuals were fed four different food items - loaches, shrimp, pellets, and mealworms - for one, two, and three months. We then examined tooth tip damage and linear microwear (scratches). Shrimp and mealworm feeding produced short scratches, whereas pellet and loach feeding produced long scratches. Most teeth exhibited apical tip damage despite the presence of a solid enameloid acrodin cap (a characteristic of ray-finned fishes), with damage being larger in loach-fed individuals and smaller in those fed with mealworms. Our results suggest a possible relationship between diet, tooth damage, and dental microwear in non-durophagous fishes which never-the-less use teeth for prey capture and processing, offering a framework for inferring diet in extinct forms with similar ecomorphology to Polypterus.

papers.title: Roost: Avian Influenza Host Genomics Resource
papers.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) causes mass mortality in poultry and wildlife, and puts already threatened species at further risk. Understanding differences in host susceptibility requires evidence currently scattered across publications, surveillance reports and genomic resources. We present Roost, a web resource that brings together more than 1,300 publications and reports, surveillance detections, and a catalogue of over 2,000 avian genome assemblies. Large language model-assisted literature analysis and comparative genomics link species, genes and molecular mechanisms to their supporting evidence. Around 51% of species with HPAI detections are not represented in the analysed corpus. Research concentrates on poultry, model organisms, and a small set of immune pathways. Research tracks neither mortality magnitude nor extinction risk; species with the largest recorded die-offs and threatened hosts alike remain largely unstudied. Roost makes this evidence, along with genome analyses, accessible to researchers and conservation practitioners, connecting documented disease with host biology and highlighting priorities for sequencing and functional research. Roost is available at http://josephguhlin.com/Roost

papers.title: Vision-language representations link food perception to subjective valuation
papers.abstract: Subjective values of foods guide dietary decisions. Yet, how the brain computes such values from visual input remains unclear. Here, we show that visual food valuation relies on higher-level conceptual representations captured by a multimodal vision-language deep neural network model. Using food images and human ratings (N = 194 and 200), we found that a vision-language model predicted subjective value more accurately than vision-only models. Representational analyses demonstrated that, compared with the vision-only model, the vision-language model preferentially encoded higher-level food attributes, including perceived healthiness, while encoding less image-level visual information. Multivariate analyses of fMRI data (N = 31) showed that embedding features from both models corresponded to activity patterns along the visual pathways. Critically, vision-language features showed greater correspondence than vision-only features in the fusiform gyrus, a downstream region of the ventral visual pathway. These findings suggest that higher-level conceptual representations link visual food processing to subjective valuation.

papers.title: Deterministic DNA-first discovery reveals recurrent genomic architectures
papers.abstract: Genome mining typically begins with known genes or protein families, which can make systems defined primarily by genomic organization difficult to detect. We developed a DNA-first framework combining asymmetric-covariance natural-vector representations with generic positional recurrence, joining separately calibrated signals through genomic coordinates. In benchmarks of array-associated reverse transcriptase (ART) loci, the target-free mathematical arm localized seven of eight predeclared loci, including all seven with exact-array coordinates. Dual-arm signals occurred in none of three non-array RT controls and in one of five UG27 systems, indicating selectivity within these small control sets. A separate profile-guided search of 6.12 Gb identified five candidate array-associated RT-like systems. In an independent 54.38-Gb evaluation of this profile-guided arm, structural compatibility was 24/32 under a historical-rule mirror, 12/32 after novelty-only selection, and 0/17 for architecture-selected complete ORFs; the two 32-member panels shared six exact sequences. Together, these results suggest that mathematical features of raw DNA can complement protein-directed searches in nominating genomic architectures for experimental RNA-to-DNA studies.

papers.title: Layer-Specific Source-Anchored Transfer Learning for Multi-Omics Survival Prediction in Younger Breast Cancer Patients
papers.abstract: Background: Younger breast cancer patients (<50 years) often present with more aggressive disease and distinct molecular characteristics, yet predictive models for this group are underpowered due to small sample sizes. Most existing models are built on older populations and may not translate directly, particularly across multiple omics data types. To address this, we developed Layered Source-Anchored Transfer Elastic Net (LSAT-EN), which adaptively borrows from the older source cohort while allowing borrowing strength to vary across omics layers according to their similarity between source and target cohorts, while performing EN variable selection. Methods: Patients aged >=60, >=55, and >=50 years were used as the source to improve prediction in patients aged <50 years. LSAT-EN were evaluated in group-correlated simulations and in TCGA-BRCA integrating 6 omics layers. Binary survival at 2-4 years was assessed by AUC; censored survival by Harrell's C-index and 2-5-year inverse probability of censoring weighted (IPCW) AUC. Results: In simulation, LSAT-EN achieved the highest AUC under moderate source-target heterogeneity (sigma^2=0.25; 0.747- 0.802), outperforming GAS-EN (0.735-0.767), overall EN (0.683-0.710), individual EN (0.646-0.767), and glmtrans EN (0.640-0.733) across target training sample sizes (nT). Its advantage was greatest under higher source-target heterogeneity (sigma^2=4), particularly with small nT, where LSAT-EN achieved AUCs of 0.689- 0.789 compared with 0.590-0.771 across competing methods. In TCGA-BRCA data, LSAT-EN improved discrimination relative to overall and individual EN in all binary and Cox models across all time horizons and source age groups. The method also identified clinically/ biologically important mRNA and miRNA, as well as useful candidate miRNA-mRNA pairs, indicating powerful biomarker discovery capability. Conclusion: LSAT-EN is a powerful TL method for improving prediction for younger breast cancer patients; The framework may support prediction in other underrepresented populations with limited target-cohort data to advance cancer disparity ML research.

papers.title: Lipidome of Compact Myelin from Cortical Regions of the Aging Murine Brain
papers.abstract: Age-related cognitive decline has been associated with neurodegeneration in cortical white matter tracts. The trajectory of white matter degeneration over the lifespan follows a similar pattern in humans, primates and rodents including the loss of myelin integrity and concomitant loss in myelinated axonal segments. Previous studies suggest that biochemical alterations in myelin begin to occur well prior to myelin loss. To better understand these biochemical determinants underlying white matter degeneration, we investigated the lipid composition of myelin isolated from young adult, middle-aged and aged murine brain. Compact myelin was enriched from cortical regions using a refined density centrifugation protocol and profiled the lipidome using LC-MS/MS. Over 2000 lipid species were identified, with the relative expression of 414 species changing over the age-span. The myelin lipidome from young mice was biochemically distinct compared to the aging cohorts. Aging was characterized by an overall decrease in high abundant species of glycerophospholipid and sphingolipids, including phosphocholine, phosphoethanolamine, sphingomyelin and cerebrosides. Pathway analysis by LipidSig 2.0 and lipid ontology analysis by LION/web highlighted alterations to lipid metabolism and membrane biophysical properties related to bilayer stability and organization. These data support the concept that myelin lipid compositional changes are apparent by middle age which underly structural changes in myelin at later ages. The findings provide greater insight into age-related biochemical alterations in the myelin sheath and may aid in strategies to mitigate white matter degeneration over the lifespan.

papers.title: One digit too many: brain rhythms and autonomic responses at the limits of working memory capacity
papers.abstract: Physiological measures vary with working memory load, but whether they identify when demands exceed a person's working memory capacity remains unclear. We assessed neural and autonomic responses to exceeding digit span by one digit. During an adaptive digit span task, we recorded EEG, pupillometry, and photoplethysmography from 123 participants. We compared each participant's digit span (approximately 70% correct full-sequence recall) with sequences one digit longer (span+1), operationally defined as overload. Full-sequence accuracy decreased from 74.1% to 51.5%, and subjective mental demand increased. Baseline-normalized pulse wave amplitude (PWA) was lower in span+1 from the first digit through terminal retention period. PWA was lower on correctly recalled than erroneous span+1 trials. Phasic pupil responses increased across serial positions but were smaller in span+1 at late span-matched positions; responses did not differ between conditions at their final digits. Non-baseline-corrected pupil diameter was larger in span+1 before sequence onset and during terminal retention, whereas non-baseline-corrected PWA did not differ. Frontal midline theta increased with serial position and was greater during terminal retention in span+1. Alpha and beta power decreased with serial position, and differed between conditions only at late positions. Terminal beta suppression was greater on correctly recalled span+1 trials. Thus, exceeding calibrated span impaired recall without producing a common physiological breakpoint. The findings suggest that reaching this limit does not immediately lead to resource exhaustion or disengagement. Physiological responses showed shifts in timing consistent with adjustments in preparation for recall of the longer sequence, along with increased effort before and during longer sequences.

papers.title: Fragment Covalent Bond Formation at SOS1 Tyr-884 Inhibits KRAS Nucleotide Exchange
papers.abstract: The activation of the KRAS oncogene from its inactive GDP-bound state to its active GTP-bound state is mediated by Son of Sevenless (SOS) exchange factors. Small-molecule inhibition of SOS1 has been achieved, with three compounds currently in clinical trials. These compounds bind to SOS1 and disrupt a crucial interaction between SOS1 Tyr-884 and KRAS Arg-73. Here, we screen libraries of aryl sulfonyl fluorides to explore covalent bond formation at Tyr-884 as a strategy for covalent inhibition of SOS1-KRAS binding. Initially, ten fragments were tested and several inhibited KRAS nucleotide exchange by SOS1. X-ray crystal structures revealed that one reaction site for the fragments was Tyr-884, but mass spectrometry and nucleotide exchange assays with wild-type and mutant SOS1 indicated additional reaction sites. To identify candidates specific to Tyr-884, we conducted a larger screen and identified fragment 11 (SOF-599). The fragment formed an adduct predominantly at Tyr-884 and inhibited KRAS nucleotide exchange by SOS1 in a time- and concentration-dependent manner. Fragment 11 (SOF-599) exhibited a half-maximal inactivation concentration (KI) of 12 micromolar and a reaction half-life of 6 h. These findings establish 11 (SOF-599) as a promising starting point for the development of covalent SOS1 inhibitors as an alternative strategy to existing non-covalent antagonists.

papers.title: Mating behaviour, mate choice, and reproduction in Tyrophagus curvipenis (Acari: Acaridae)
papers.abstract: Mating behaviour and mate choice can influence reproductive output, but these aspects remain insufficiently studied in many mite species. This study investigated mating behaviour, mate choice, and the reproductive consequences of repeated mating in Tyrophagus curvipenis (Acari: Acaridae). First, we described the mating sequence and quantified the duration of pre-copulation latency and copulation duration. Mating involved initial contact, dorsal mounting, repositioning into a tail-to-tail copulatory position, and sperm transfer. Copulation lasted substantially longer than the pre-copulation latency. Second, we examined mate choice in relation to kinship. Neither males nor females showed a significant preference for siblings or unrelated partners. Third, we examined mate choice in relation to mating status. Males preferred virgin partners, whereas females showed no significant preference between virgin and previously mated partners. Copulation duration was shorter with previously mated partners, although the underlying cause remains unclear. Finally, we examined female reproductive performance under three mating-frequency treatments: one mate, two mates, and unlimited access to mates. Mating frequency did not affect the pre-oviposition period but significantly affected the oviposition period, daily oviposition rate, and total fecundity. Females with unlimited mating opportunities had the longest oviposition period and produced the most eggs. Among females that mated once, longer copulation was positively associated with both oviposition period and total fecundity. These findings characterise mating behaviour in T. curvipenis and show that mate choice and mating frequency are associated with different aspects of reproduction. Further work is needed to determine whether these patterns reflect differences in sperm transfer, fertilisation, or other effects of mating.

papers.title: An end-to-end in silico framework for truth-based validation and regression testing of clinical genome sequencing pipelines, from simulated reads to reportable findings
papers.abstract: Clinical genome sequencing pipelines change often, and each change requires proportionate revalidation. Guidelines accept in silico data as a supplement but leave variant interpretation outside pipeline validation, and, to our knowledge, no framework tests a pipeline against a known truth up to the reportable finding, so report specificity is not measured. We present a source-available framework that tests a pipeline end to end, from sequencing reads to the report, against a truth fixed before any run. It plants expert-curated pathogenic and benign variants from the same genes, and optionally synthetic variants that no database holds, into the GIAB HG002 germline background and records the expected class and report decision of each variant. It then simulates reads and runs secondary and tertiary analysis as black boxes through exchangeable adapters. Findings are compared with the truth at the call-set and report levels, each failure is assigned to the first pipeline stage where it appears, and a variant-by-variant comparison of two runs serves as a regression test. We applied the framework to nf-core/sarek with DeepVariant and to the ACMG/AMP classifier BIAS-2015, using 243 ClinGen-curated variants in five test sets. Single-nucleotide variant recall against the HG002 benchmark was 99.5% on simulated and 99.3% on real reads, and every planted variant was present in the reads and called with the correct genotype. The report included 115 of 117 pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants (98.3%) but withheld only 106 of 126 variants that must not be reported (84.1%), mainly because variants of uncertain significance were upgraded and recessive carriers were reported. Without ClinVar-derived criteria, report sensitivity fell to 74.4%. Most false reports of one test set came from diploid calling of the male chromosome X, and haploid calling removed them without side effects. In supplementary experiments, indels were called completely up to 20 bp, and BIAS-2015 left 74% of synthetic loss-of-function variants unreported because it combined criteria by the 2015 rules. The framework measures report-level sensitivity and specificity and localizes regressions, so it can supplement validation on human samples and support change control.

papers.title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Reveals Distinct Cellular and Molecular Features of Steroid-Induced Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head Compared to Alcohol-Induced Osteonecrosis and Hip Osteoarthritis
papers.abstract: Osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) remains a devastating complication of glucocorticoid therapy and alcohol abuse, yet the pathophysiology is poorly understood. Using single-cell RNA sequencing, we analyzed femoral head specimens from patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty due to steroid-induced ONFH, alcohol-induced ONFH, or hip osteoarthritis (OA). Our comprehensive analysis across conditions revealed etiology-specific cellular compositions and transcriptional profiles. Steroid-induced ONFH demonstrated a distinctive immunological signature characterized by a neutrophil-predominant, elevated innate-to-adaptive immune cell ratio compared to alcohol-induced ONFH or OA. T cell analysis revealed impaired maturation in steroid-induced ONFH, with abundant naive T cells but reduced mature CD4+ T cells and CD4+ memory T cells compared to both alcohol-induced ONFH and OA. In addition, compared to alcohol-induced ONFH, steroid-induced ONFH was associated with an increase in exhausted/dysfunctional CD8+ T cells which suggests an impaired response to stress and reflects chronic immune dysfunction. Within stromal cell populations, steroid-induced ONFH demonstrated an increase in pericytes, endothelial cells, and mesenchymal cell with osteogenic features as compared to both alcohol-induced ONFH or OA. These findings collectively reveal novel cellular mechanisms underlying steroid-induced ONFH which may contribute to further investigation of etiology-specific pathogenesis and treatment strategies.

papers.title: GOParsimony: parsimonious saltation across the Gene Ontology digraph for efficient functional annotation
papers.abstract: Background. The Gene Ontology (GO) is standardly probed by biological researchers keen to discern the functional tendencies of their gene/protein data sets. However, lists of GO terms are often ontically overwhelming, and need to be filtered to remove redundancy. Methods for such filtering either employ predefined lists of terms that may not actually be relevant to a specific gene/protein set, or apply arbitrary thresholds, such as for semantic distance (i.e., GO term dissimilarity). Methods. Here, I introduce the tool GOParsimony, which is designed to avoid such issues and to pick out the most parsimonious (i.e., simplest, most concise) explanation for the functional tendencies of any set of proteins/genes. It achieves this by saltating across the GO digraph, assigning and updating cascades of term precedence until convergence. The set of GO terms assigned precedence = 1 is the most parsimonious set. Hierarchical clustering with other GO terms with higher precedence levels can be investigated for clues about functional modules. Results. GO term precedence graphs and two-dimensional heatmaps of GO terms and genes/proteins are output, along with other plots that can be cross-referenced for functional insights. In test analyses for five example data sets from budding yeast and human, GOParsimony consistently produces reduced GO term lists that have greater significance and low or intermediate coverage of the space of significant GO terms, when compared to other distributed methods in default mode. GOParsimony can be obtained at: https://github.com/pmharrison/GOParsimony .

papers.title: The Segmentome: a novel representation of the DNA methylome identified by a Bayesian HMM framework
papers.abstract: Motivation: DNA methylation is organized along the genome into regions of relatively stable methylation (i.e. fully methylated or fully unmethylated regions), separated by transition zones. Differences in the boundaries of these methylation zones across cells can result from various regulatory and epigenetic mechanisms. Most DNA methylome studies, however, are focused on the detection of differentially methylated regions (DMRs), and this organization within a single methylome remains under explored. Furthermore it is unclear whether a segment-level descriptor can capture cell identity. Results: We introduce the segmentome, a segment-level representation of the methylome, and an unsupervised Bayesian hidden Markov model that infers it from WGBS data without predefined methylation thresholds or labels. The model combines CpG methylation levels with read-pattern entropy, local CpG correlation and CpG count to divide the genome into unmethylated, methylated and transition zones, the last characterized by heterogeneous read patterns. Applied to 207 samples of 39 human cell types, segmentome profiles grouped samples by cell type in an unsupervised manner (adjusted Rand index 0.55, adjusted mutual information 0.72). We next generated a segmentome atlas consisting of top segmentome biomarkers per human cell-type. These markers were capable of cell-of-origin determining in cell-free DNA and white blood cell samples. These results suggest that segmentation is a unique framework for analyzing DNA methylome.

papers.title: SQANTI-evidence: isoform-resolved, evidence-tiered structural annotation of unannotated genomes from long-read RNA-seq
papers.abstract: Long-read RNA sequencing captures full-length transcripts, yet current annotation pipelines fail to properly curate the data for gene prediction. We present SQANTI-evidence, a workflow that annotates a genome from long reads alone, without a reference annotation or protein database. SQANTI3-curated transcripts enter the annotation as observed, with isoforms and untranslated regions; AUGUSTUS predicts genes at loci without read support. In benchmarks, the curated layer was the most precise gene set in five of seven species, recovered twice as many exact isoforms as BRAKER in mammals and placed 3' ends nearest the poly(A) site. We annotated 13 ERGA datasets.

papers.title: Habitat degradation destabilizes complex metacommunities by disrupting dispersal
papers.abstract: Habitat loss and fragmentation are rapidly reshaping ecosystems worldwide, yet their consequences for ecological stability remain unresolved. Classical theory, pioneered by Robert May, established rigorous criteria for stability; however, these apply to spatially well-mixed communities, limiting their relevance to habitat degradation. Here, we develop a metacommunity framework that integrates classical stability theory with spatial dynamics to determine how anthropogenic habitat degradation reshapes ecosystem stability. We show that metacommunities exhibit three distinct dynamical regimes following a perturbation (e.g., drought or forest fire): stable regime (perturbations decay and species persist), reactive regime (perturbations are transiently amplified, which increases extinction risk under repeated disturbances), and unstable regime (perturbations grow, causing extinctions even after a single disturbance). Dispersal fundamentally reshapes these stability transitions, converting unstable communities into reactive ones and reactive communities into stable ones. While homogeneous dispersal progressively stabilizes communities, heterogeneous dispersal maximizes stability at intermediate strengths. We further show that habitat loss and fragmentation can be comparably effective at driving species extinctions by shifting metacommunities from stable to reactive and ultimately unstable regimes, demonstrating that fragmentation per se can be as important as habitat loss. Our findings reveal that reactivity is both an early-warning signal of impending instability and a state of elevated extinction risk under recurrent disturbances. By linking stability transitions to changes in population persistence under nonlinear dynamics, our results bridge classical stability theory with spatial ecology and provide a general framework for predicting how ecological complexity and dispersal jointly govern both ecosystem stability and population persistence under habitat degradation.

papers.title: Decoding Cell-type Specific Gene Regulation with CellReg3D by Integrating DNA Large Language Models and 3D Genome Structure
papers.abstract: Gene regulation is a core biological mechanism crucial for organismal growth and development. Recent advances in deep learning, coupled with increasing computational resources, have enabled large-scale modelling of gene regulatory processes. While numerous models have been proposed, effectively capturing long-range genomic interactions remains a central challenge. Here, we introduce CellReg3D, a multiscale and multi-modal deep learning framework designed to model cell-type-specific gene regulation by integrating local sequence patterns with long-range genomic interactions. Existing approaches often overlook the contribution of 3D genome architecture and face limitations in combining sequence-based features with chromatin interaction data. Specifically, CellReg3D overcomes these gaps by leveraging a DNA language model to encode sequence-level information and incorporating Hi-C-derived 3D chromatin interactions to capture chromatin spatial organization. We demonstrate that CellReg3D effectively learns epigenetic patterns and chromatin activity states, achieving state-of-the-art performance in predicting epigenetic marks and gene expression profiles across multiple cell types. Using interpretable methods, we illustrate how the model identifies cell-type-specific regulatory mechanisms and prioritizes functional non-coding variants. Furthermore, we apply CellReg3D to enhance the interpretation of expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) and uncover novel potential gene regulatory interactions. Overall, CellReg3D offers a integrative framework for decoding regulatory genomics, unifying sequence and 3D genome structure data to advance variant prioritization, disease mechanism discovery, and personalized functional genomics.

papers.title: Cross-species epigenomic signatures of exceptional longevity: Insights from Jonathan the Giant Tortoise and human centenarians
papers.abstract: Can epigenomic signatures of exceptional longevity transcend species boundaries? By comparing findings from a previously published epigenomic study of Jonathan, a 194-year-old giant tortoise, based on buccal scrape and saliva samples, with the analyses of publicly available DNA methylation data from exceptionally long-lived humans based on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), this comparative study reveals intriguing molecular parallels across evolutionarily distant species. Human individuals aged 110+ years exhibited significantly higher global methylation entropy than those aged 60-82 years. Furthermore, 12 candidate genes displayed a distinctive promoter methylation entropy profile, with lower values at the youngest and oldest ages than in intermediate-age groups. Strikingly, these genes were enriched in telomere-related biological processes, highlighting a compelling link between epigenomic patterns and pathways implicated in aging. The correspondence between the findings in humans and previously reported observations in Jonathan suggests testable hypotheses about epigenomic signatures of exceptional longevity that may be conserved across species and extend beyond tissue-specific effects.

papers.title: Anticipatory Threat of Shock Reduces the Number of Items Reported From a Brief Visual Display: Evidence for Capacity Loss Along the Scanning Order
papers.abstract: Background: Anticipatory anxiety impairs working memory, but whether it also limits the earliest, high-capacity stage of visual storage is unclear. We asked whether the mere expectation of an aversive electrical stimulus reduces how many items people can report from a briefly flashed display, and whether any loss is spatially uniform. Methods: Eighty-eight healthy adults aged 18-25 years were randomly allocated to a threat-of-shock condition (surface electrodes on the wrist and the instruction that a painful stimulus might be delivered; none was) or a control condition (n = 44 each). Participants viewed a 4 x 3 letter matrix for 400 ms and performed untimed written whole report. Correct recall (0-12), intrusions and the position of each reported letter were scored. Groups were compared with Welch's t test, the Mann-Whitney U test, bootstrapped effect sizes, a binomial generalised linear model and a Bayes factor; spatial effects were tested with generalised estimating equations (GEE) accounting for letters nested within participants. Results: The threat group reported fewer correct letters (3.41 +/- 1.09) than controls (4.70 +/- 1.29); Welch t(83.6) = 5.11, p < .001, Hedges' g = 1.08, 95% CI [0.70, 1.53], BF10 ~ 7,549. Intrusions did not differ (p = .376). Recall declined more steeply from left to right under threat (group x column chi2(3) = 11.24, p = .011), with losses confined to the third and fourth letters of the top row (FDR-corrected q <= .003). Conclusions: Anticipatory threat reduced the amount of information transferred from a brief display into a reportable form without increasing guessing. Intact first items and depleted later items along the habitual reading order indicate a reduced number of items read out of a rapidly decaying visual store, rather than a hemifield-specific bias. The single-trial design and the absence of a manipulation check limit mechanistic inference.

papers.title: Physical sensorimotor contingencies facilitate learning in monkeys
papers.abstract: Animal studies in neuroscience routinely use virtual tasks that deviate significantly from the animals' natural behavioral repertoire. This choice is often necessary for conducting careful and controlled experimentation. However, this approach raises a fundamental question: do virtual tasks expose neural computations and mechanisms associated with naturalistic tasks? In this study, we explore how naturalistic settings influence learning timescale and generalization behavior in rhesus monkeys. By training animals in a maze-solving task and comparing their behavior across two environments, we observe significant differences. Specifically, we found that a realistic setup using physical objects enabled learning that was orders of magnitude faster than the learning timescale observed in a comparable computerized virtual environment. Furthermore, we noted limited transfer of performance between the physical and virtual settings. These findings underscore the need for understanding how task environments shape learning and generalization, with potential implications for the design of future neuroscience and AI experiments.

papers.title: Calves function as social magnets in a species with high fission-fusion dynamics, the Asian elephant
papers.abstract: Individuals living in fission-fusion societies may face unique challenges in maintaining social relationships, as the repeated fission of social units can limit opportunities for social interaction. However, the presence of young offspring may often necessitate cooperation among individuals. To understand whether offspring promote sociality in fission-fusion species, we studied wild Asian elephants (Elephas maximus) in southern India. Using nearly 5900 female group sightings collected over 9 years, we tested whether calf presence predicted female group size and associations. The numbers of adult, young adult, and subadult females in groups were 2-2.5-fold higher in calf presence than absence, which may facilitate collective defence of calves. Furthermore, the number of females without their own dependent offspring, who often provide allomaternal care, was also higher in calf presence than absence. Social network analysis revealed that adult females formed more numerous and stronger associations in calf presence than absence, which may facilitate consistent allomaternal care. Our results thus suggest that the need to protect calves and to provide allomaternal care likely promote sociality among female elephants. We propose that dependent offspring may function as social ties in fission-fusion species, contingent upon the prevailing conditions and the socioecological pressures that have shaped their social systems.

papers.title: The collective effect of non-nicotine constituents on the reinforcing and neuropharmacological effects of comprehensive cigarette smoke and electronic nicotine delivery system (ENDS) aerosol extracts in rats.
papers.abstract: Tobacco product extracts containing nicotine and non-nicotine constituents are useful for understanding the collective role of these constituents in tobacco use disorder (TUD). However, few studies have used extracts with both water-soluble and non-water-soluble constituents with accompanying chemical analysis, or compared behavioral and neuropharmacological effects across product types. To address these limitations, we compared the relative abuse liability of cigarette smoke (CS) and electronic nicotine delivery system (ENDS) aerosol (EA) extracts to nicotine alone using intravenous self-administration in rats, and examined effects on nucleus accumbens (NAc) dopamine (DA) release and binding/function at nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) and other addiction-related receptors in vitro. CS extract contained higher levels of several behaviorally active non-nicotine constituents than EA extract. Both extracts produced a downward/leftward shift in the descending limb of the unit dose-response curve relative to nicotine alone, while only CS extract produced greater compensatory increases in responding compared to nicotine alone. Demand intensity (Q0) was lower for CS but not EA extract, relative to nicotine alone, whereas demand elasticity for both extracts was similar to nicotine alone. Stress-induced reinstatement was comparable between CS extract and nicotine alone but attenuated for EA extract. CS extract, but not EA extract, showed greater potency for 4{beta}2 nAChR activation and substantial binding across numerous non-nAChRs (DA, serotonergic, opioid) relative to nicotine alone at a high screening concentration. CS extract, but not nicotine alone, also inhibited cyclooxygenase (COX)-1 and -2 at smoking-relevant concentrations. There was no difference in NAc DA release between formulations. These findings indicate non-nicotine constituents contribute to certain reinforcing and neuropharmacological effects of CS, and to a lesser extent EA. Our finding of COX inhibition by CS extract warrants further investigation as a potential mechanism contributing to the effects of CS and TUD.

papers.title: Dissociable Oscillatory Alpha and Aperiodic Neural Dynamics Underlie Atypical Attentional Control in Children With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)
papers.abstract: Children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) often have difficulty maintaining goal-directed attention when task-relevant and task-irrelevant information compete for processing resources. The present study investigated whether this difficulty reflects distinct abnormalities in demand-related attentional regulation and distractor-related neural responses. We recorded electroencephalography (EEG) signals from 45 children with ADHD and 45 typically developing (TD) children while they performed a visual detection task under low and high visual demands, with simultaneous task-irrelevant standard and deviant sounds. EEG power spectra were parameterized to separate oscillatory alpha activity from aperiodic activity, as putative indices of attentional regulation and cortical excitation/inhibition (E/I) balance, respectively. TD children showed adaptive demand-related alpha modulation, whereas children with ADHD showed an atypical alpha response pattern, including reduced frontal modulation and atypical posterior alpha enhancement; this demand-related group difference was observed in oscillatory alpha activity but not in aperiodic activity. In contrast, ADHD-related abnormalities in responses to auditory distractors were more clearly reflected in the aperiodic slope. Children with ADHD showed atypical distractor-related aperiodic modulation, suggesting reduced stability of neural background activity, potentially reflecting disrupted cortical E/I balance when irrelevant sounds had to be ignored. Furthermore, multivariate machine learning classification demonstrated that relying on these sensitive neural signatures yielded robust discrimination between children with ADHD and TD controls, with significant predictive performance emerging shortly after stimulus onset and sustaining throughout information processing. These findings suggest that oscillatory alpha activity and aperiodic neural dynamics show differential sensitivity to distinct attentional abnormalities in ADHD, with alpha oscillations primarily reflecting demand-related regulatory deficits and aperiodic activity primarily reflecting distractor-related neural instability.

papers.title: Concurrent metacognitive evaluation is dissociable from perceptual evidence accumulation in the parietal cortex
papers.abstract: Adaptive behavior requires not only accumulating evidence toward a choice but also monitoring its reliability in real time. A central question is whether such concurrent uncertainty is read out directly from the circuit that accumulates perceptual evidence, or is computed by a separate process that runs alongside it. We trained two macaques on a perceptual discrimination task in which they could abandon deliberation at any moment and request assistance, so that uncertainty responses were in parallel with, rather than appended to, evidence accumulation. Behaviorally, a race between distinct perceptual and uncertainty accumulators outperformed models in which the opt-out decision was derived from the perceptual decision variable alone. To ask where the second accumulator resides, we recorded single units in the lateral intraparietal area (LIP), a canonical sensory-motor transformation area, and compared population dynamics with recurrent neural networks instantiating two architectures: one in which uncertainty is computed within the perceptual accumulator, and one in which it is computed outside and triggers the uncertainty response there. LIP exhibited all of these signatures for perceptual choices and none for uncertainty responses. Uncertainty-related activity rose late and stereotypically, lacking the coherence-scaled ramp of an accumulator, and separable from the perceptual accumulation. They are all predicted by the segregated architecture. Concurrent uncertainty is thus represented in LIP but is unlikely to be computed within LIP, indicating that metacognitive monitoring during deliberation is a dissociable operation rather than a derivative readout of the LIP perceptual circuit; its anatomical substrate is not localized here.

papers.title: SafeLens: A Statistically Controlled Nonlinear Machine Learning Framework for Characterizing Hidden Dynamics in Event-Locked Neural Activity
papers.abstract: Machine learning has advanced rapidly over the past decade, yet event-locked neural activity is still analyzed predominantly with traditional statistics and linear models. While traditional linear methods provide computationally tractable statistical control for pre-selected features or trial-averaged waveforms, they miss subtle nonlinear and trial-varying neural dynamics. Nonlinear models can capture these complex patterns, but their feature reliance is opaque and notoriously difficult to threshold statistically. We introduce SafeLens (Searchlight Analysis of Fluctuation Events, Leveraging Extensive Null Sampling) to combine the power of nonlinear machine learning with the rigorous false-positive control of traditional statistical inference. At each position of a sliding window, a random forest learns to discriminate event-locked activity from interleaved resting-state neural activity using multiscale temporal derivatives. Randomized feature ablation inverts slope polarity in held-out trials to map the random forest models' reliance on specific rising versus falling excursions across the time-frequency space. SafeLens then establishes an empirical null by running the same pipeline on separate resting-state recordings, training forests to discriminate rest from rest. This empirical null translates each channel's complex nonlinear resting dynamics into a model-matched noise floor on the map's linear reliance scale, allowing a single threshold to control the family-wise error rate against the channel's own background structure rather than a summary statistic of its baseline. When we injected simulated cortico-cortical evoked potentials (CCEPs) into resting intracranial EEG recordings, SafeLens recovered ~2.5 times as many polarity-resolved deflections as trial-average thresholding and the closest data-driven method, maintaining its advantage under trial-to-trial variability while yielding ~5-11 times fewer false components, ~2-5 times lower mean boundary error, and superior single-trial latency tracking as a timing prior. In eight patients, CCEPs remained detectable above chance until 1,040 ms after stimulation, compared with 570 and 455 ms for those benchmarks. Together, these findings establish SafeLens as a novel solution for enabling nonlinear models to uncover subtle, trial-varying neural dynamics under strict statistical control.

papers.title: 2D U-NET Deep Learning Architecture for Atherosclerotic Lesion Segmentation and Quantification
papers.abstract: Mice are commonly used for experimental atherosclerosis research, and a common procedure involves morphometric analysis of atherosclerotic lesions on Oil Red O-stained cross-sections of the aortic root. However, manual measurement of atherosclerotic lesion sizes on numerous histological sections is tedious and time-consuming. Here, we developed a deep learning model based on convolutional neural network to quantify atherosclerotic lesions in cross-sectioned aortic roots of mice. Microscopy images were taken from cross-sectioned aortic roots of genetically diverse F2 mice derived from BALB/cJ and LP/J Apoe knockout mice and fed 12 weeks of a Western diet. Aortic cross-sections were stained with Oil Red O and hematoxylin and images captured. Atherosclerotic lesions were manually segmented in 2553 images using Zeiss AxioVision. These images were split into 1,533 for training the U-NET model, 510 for validation, and 510 images for testing. The developed model was evaluated for its performance to measure atherosclerotic lesions by comparing with manual measurement in test images. The model achieved a high degree of accuracy, with an F1 score of 0.82, a Jaccard score of 0.72, a Recall of 0.80, a precision of 0.87, and a correlation coefficient value of 0.98. While manual lesion measurement took approximately 5 minutes per image, the model performed the task in ~3.35 seconds, reducing measurement time by 98.9%. The developed 2D U-NET model provides a new platform for rapid and accurate quantification of atherosclerotic lesion sizes on Oil Red O-stained sections.

papers.title: Adaptation and conservation of turtle visual opsins over a deep phylogenetic divergence
papers.abstract: The ecological radiation of organisms in diverse light environments depends, in part, on adaptive alterations within visual systems, particularly retinal photoreceptors and their visual pigments. Evidence of visual adaptation occurs across vertebrate lineages but is notably lacking in turtles, despite their complex visual system with up to eight photoreceptor cell types and five visual pigments. This lack of knowledge is especially pronounced in side-neck turtles (Pleurodira), as nearly all information on turtle vision derives from hidden-neck turtles (Cryptodira). Here, we bridge this ~200-million-year evolutionary gap by investigating visual opsin evolution using an eye transcriptome and whole-genome sequences from 59 turtle species spanning both suborders, as well as an additional 42 representative reptile species. We estimated selective pressures using codon-based evolutionary models, testing for positive selection and long-term shifts between turtles and other reptiles, between suborders, and among major habitat types. We also analysed spectral tuning sites to assess how spectral sensitivity diverged between and within suborders. Our analyses revealed remarkably conserved turtle visual opsin sequences, with phylogeny-wide positive selection detected only in LWS. Habitat explained more shifts in selective pressure than taxonomy, with long-term shifts detected across all five opsins. Spectral tuning sites predict conserved UV sensitivity of SWS1 across cryptodirans, consistent with the few species previously characterised, whereas shared changes identified in pleurodirans predict violet sensitivity, revealing previously unrecognized divergence in short-wavelength vision between turtle suborders. This study advances our understanding of turtle visual system evolution and highlights the need for conservation strategies that account for their distinct visual capabilities.

papers.title: Thalamic stereo-EEG detects sleep stages N2 and N3 with discrimination approaching scalp EEG
papers.abstract: Sleep and epilepsy interact strongly during sleep stages N2 and N3, when synchronization of brain rhythms is increased. Sleep staging relies on scalp EEG, which is often absent or incomplete during stereo-EEG monitoring and unavailable from implanted devices, while thalamic leads are increasingly implanted for epilepsy neuromodulation. Given the role of the thalamus in spindle generation and slow oscillation dynamics, we hypothesized that thalamic channels would identify N2 and N3 (N2+N3) better than other intracranial sites. We analyzed 477 h of stereo-EEG with simultaneous scalp EEG from six adults, including 46 thalamic bipolar channels on 11 electrodes. Two classifiers were evaluated on identical channels: a random forest with hidden Markov decoding (RF + HMM) trained leave-one-participant-out, and the pretrained SleepSEEG algorithm developed without thalamic channels. The primary endpoint was discrimination of N2+N3 from other stages as classified from scalp EEG by a sleep expert. Among regions sampled in all participants, thalamic channels performed best (area under the curve [AUC] 0.94 with RF + HMM and 0.93 with SleepSEEG across whole recordings; 0.88 and 0.86 at night). With RF + HMM, thalamic channels outperformed mesial temporal and temporal neocortical channels in all six participants across whole recordings. The advantage persisted against channel-count-matched subsets and a white-matter control with both classifiers. Individual thalamic electrodes reached AUCs of 0.79-0.99 with RF + HMM (10 of 11 at least 0.89). These offline findings support thalamic N2+N3 detection and motivate real-time evaluation for sleep-targeted neuromodulation.

papers.title: Top2All: Benchmarking sparse-to-transcriptome reconstruction from high-expression profiles across sex- and sex-steroid-defined conditions
papers.abstract: Transcriptome-wide profiling at single-cell resolution is limited by sparse detection of gene expression, raising the question of how much transcriptomic information can be recovered from a small set of highly expressed genes. We developed Top2All, a Mouse-Geneformer-based framework for reconstructing transcriptome-wide expression from sample-specific sparse inputs. Using 24 cell-number-normalized RNA-seq profiles of mouse adrenal zona fasciculata cells across eight experimental conditions defined by sex and sex-steroid milieu, we evaluated condition-aware and no-condition models under replicate-wise out-of-fold and leave-one-condition-out validation. Top2All achieved near-unity sample-wise correlation with measured expression, but similarly high correlations were obtained using simple reference profiles, whereas gene-wise evaluation revealed substantially greater differences among methods. Explicit condition information did not consistently improve reconstruction, indicating that sex- and sex-steroid-associated condition information was already strongly encoded in the sparse expression profiles. Nearest-neighbor retrieval provided a stronger baseline than learned reconstruction, and input-depth analysis showed that increasing the number of input genes did not monotonically improve performance. These findings show that a relatively small set of highly expressed genes contains substantial information about transcriptomic state, while accurate reconstruction of gene-specific biological variation remains challenging. Sparse-to-transcriptome models should therefore be evaluated using gene-wise metrics, strong reference baselines, and tests of generalization beyond conditions represented during training.

papers.title: Reference-Guided De Novo Retrieval of 3D Chromatin Organizational Features with Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Chromosome conformation maps reveal spatial genome organization through recurring contact patterns, some associated with established architectural features and others with less understood biological processes. Identifying instances of a pattern across these maps is necessary to investigate its biological associations and recurrence across experimental settings. However, conventional feature callers typically target predefined patterns, offering limited support when researchers can provide examples of a feature of interest but lack a dedicated detection method. We introduce Chromatin Fetch (C-Fetch), a reference-guided retrieval framework that uses examples of a desired feature and a contrasting class to rank and assign contact-map patches at provided candidate coordinates. C-Fetch learns a reusable representation through weakly KL-regularized 3D autoencoding of structurally related, non-temporal Hi-C and Micro-C patches without architectural feature labels. We demonstrate retrieval of biologically defined contacts, visually specified patterns, and established architectural features. Polycomb-guided retrieval identifies contacts enriched for PRC2-associated signals, exceeding enrichment from loop-guided assignments at 5 kb, while queries resembling condensed domains retrieve patches with progressively stronger rectangular enrichment at higher ranks. Loop-guided retrieval increases aggregate focal enrichment relative to complete Mustache proposal sets across four held-out maps, and selected contacts show greater focality loss after cohesin depletion than matched remaining candidates. Retrieval also extends to Region Capture Micro-C and HiChIP, with ranking agreement retained across biological replicates and reduced sequencing depths. Together, these results establish reference examples as a flexible means of specifying contact-map features of interest, enabling biological investigation, exploration of visual patterns, and refinement of existing calls across datasets and technologies.

papers.title: Deep phenomics of human PBMCs using a 31-marker spectral flow cytometry panel
papers.abstract: Functional cytokines orchestrate leukocyte-mediated innate and adaptive immune responses within the host following infection or immunization. In contrast, lymphocyte-mediated activation-induced markers (AIMs) are predominantly associated with adaptive immune responses. Regulatory T cells (Tregs) primarily function to balance the immune response by preventing excessive inflammation and maintaining self-tolerance. Currently, conventional intracellular cytokine tracking or cytokine-independent AIMs methodology is available for studying antigen-specific lymphocyte or T cell responses in humans. However, this approach faces challenges due to the difficulty in simultaneously deep immunophenotyping the key functional cytokine signatures, AIMs, and nuclear signature of FoxP3+ Tregs. Using spectral flow cytometry, we developed a 31-parameter panel to profile simultaneously major immune cell subsets (B cells, NK cells, DCs, monocytes) along with T cells, memory phenotypes, functional cytokines by tracking established Th1 markers IFN{gamma}, TNF and IL-2; Th2 markers IL-4/5/13 and the Th17 marker, IL-17, AIMs and FoxP3+ Tregs in human PBMCs in steady state as well as in mitogen stimulated conditions. For AIMs, CD69, CD134 (OX40) and CD137 (4-1BB) are included and validated. We also re-validated our panel to profile antigen specific Th1/2/17 cells or AIMs distribution after peptide stimulation.
