Fentanyl increased the frequency of LC bursts independent of exposure history and was coupled to transient elevations in breathing. LC coupled ventilation (LC-Ve) persisted through ROU. After ROU, OIRD magnitude diverged across mice. Mice developing an adaptive ventilatory response (AVR) showed a smaller OIRD that coincided with improved ventilation outside LC bursts and reduced LC-Ve gain. Mice with the non-adaptive response (NVR) show no improvement in OIRD or ventilation outside LC bursts, resulting in an unchanged reliance on LC-Ve. While LC-Ve reflexively counters OIRD acutely, it may also drive oscillations to destabilize blood gas homeostasis, perpetuating pathophysiology with repeat use. Thus, LC-coupled breathing appears to be a physiological signature of divergent respiratory responses with a history of fentanyl exposure.

papers.title: The IFN-γ-inducible GTPase IIGP1 regulates mitochondrial remodeling and immunometabolic reprogramming during inflammatory macrophage polarization
papers.abstract: Macrophages are key effector cells of the innate immune system that undergo dynamic polarization into functionally distinct phenotypic states, ranging from classically activated inflammatory (M1) to alternatively activated (M2) macrophages. Inflammatory macrophage polarization requires coordinated integration of cytokine signaling, metabolic reprogramming, and mitochondrial remodeling. However, the molecular effectors that control inflammatory signaling for mitochondrial metabolism and remodeling remain poorly defined. Using quantitative mass spectrometry-based proteomics, we identified Interferon-inducible GTPase 1 (IIGP1) as one of the most robustly induced proteins during inflammatory macrophage polarization. Its expression is governed by the IFN-{gamma}-JAK-STAT1 signaling axis and is crucial for this polarization process. IIGP1-deficient macrophages exhibited significantly impaired iNOS induction, nitric oxide production, pro-inflammatory gene expression, co-stimulatory surface marker expression, and morphological remodeling. Further, IIGP1 associates with mitochondria and its absence impairs key characteristics of inflammatory macrophages, including glycolytic metabolic reprogramming, mitochondrial redox adaptation, membrane potential regulation, and structural remodeling. Consistent with these defects, IIGP1-deficient macrophages displayed impaired intracellular killing of Escherichia coli and Salmonella Typhimurium. Collectively, these results point to IIGP1 as an IFN-{gamma}-inducible effector that facilitates efficient inflammatory macrophage polarization and antibacterial immunity by linking inflammatory signaling to mitochondrial homeostasis and immunometabolic reprogramming.

papers.title: Defining nutrient dependencies of intestinal Klebsiella pneumoniae guides rational probiotic engineering
papers.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a major cause of antibiotic-resistant infections, yet the ecological determinants enabling its intestinal expansion remain poorly defined. Here, we combined in vivo transcriptomics and metabolomics to identify carbon sources exploited by K. pneumoniae during colonization of the antibiotic-disrupted gut across strains and dietary contexts. Despite its metabolic breadth, K. pneumoniae consistently exploited a restricted set of substrates, including arabinose, raffinose, oligogalacturonate, arabitol, xylose, and gluconate, that contributed to intestinal fitness, with related metabolic signatures also observed in antibiotic-treated human samples. Guided by these findings, we engineered Escherichia coli Nissle to enhance consumption of these nutrients and assembled a defined consortium, NICHE, designed to reinforce colonization resistance through nutrient competition. NICHE restricted intestinal expansion of multidrug-resistant and hypervirulent K. pneumoniae in preventive and therapeutic settings, with efficacy influenced by dietary nutrient availability. Together, this work defines exploitable K. pneumoniae nutrient dependencies and a framework for rational probiotic engineering.

papers.title: DarHTG is a tripartite phage defence system for purine DNA base ADP-ribosylation
papers.abstract: Bacteria evolved a variety of phage defence strategies to combat the constant onslaught of viral threats. DarTG toxin-antitoxin systems provide phage defence by ADP-ribosylation of bases in single-stranded DNA which interferes with viral replication and aborts phage infection. Here, we describe DarHTG, a system widespread among bacteria, that combines DarTG with a non-processive superfamily I helicase functioning as co-toxin for DarT and thereby enabling the ADP-ribosylation of double-stranded DNA. We identified two such DarHTG subclasses which catalyse the ADP-ribosylation of adenosine and guanosine bases, respectively, and reverse these modifications with structurally unique ARH superfamily antitoxins. Thus, DarHTG antitoxins expand the known macromolecular target spectrum of the ARH enzyme class to nucleic acids. These DarHTG systems confer resistance to a broad range of bacteriophages and can be triggered by the highly charged tails of viral single-stranded DNA-binding proteins, which occlude the active site of the ARH antitoxin.

papers.title: Res ipSAE adhuc loquuntur: What the directionality of predicted aligned error in cofolding models can tell us about scoring diverse molecular complexes
papers.abstract: AlphaFold 3 (AF3) and Boltz-2 estimate confidence in predicted biomolecular complexes using the interface predicted template modeling (ipTM) score, which is derived from probability distributions of predicted aligned errors (PAEs) between molecular tokens. These errors are directional: the predicted position of tokens in one molecule is evaluated relative to coordinate frames defined by tokens in another. The PAE matrix is therefore asymmetric, but AF3 reports the maximum of the two directional pairwise ipTM scores, whereas Boltz-2 reports them separately. In both programs, the TM-score scaling parameter, d0, depends on molecular system size rather than solely on the component being scored. In protein-protein complexes, including disordered regions and domains unrelated to the interface can further lower ipTM. I previously introduced the interaction predicted score from aligned errors (ipSAE) to address these limitations for protein-protein complexes. Here, I extend ipSAE to interactions involving proteins, nucleic acids, small-molecule ligands, and atomic ions. The framework makes three explicit choices for each molecular pair: which component supplies the alignment frames, which tokens are scored, and how d0 is defined. For different molecular types, I propose aligning on the more complex molecule and scoring the simpler one. For protein-ligand complexes, this entails aligning on protein residues, scoring all ligand heavy atoms without a PAE cutoff, and using a fixed d0 of 2 [A]. In benchmarks of 102 protein-ligand complexes predicted by AF3 and Boltz-2, this ipSAE formulation yields a substantially wider range of confidence scores than native ipTM. On a held-out set of 82 complexes, ipSAE thresholds of 0.5 for AF3 and 0.8 for Boltz-2 classified ligand placements with balanced accuracies of 0.938 and 0.862, respectively, using a ligand RMSD threshold of 5 [A]. Protein-DNA benchmarks support the same directional scoring scheme, while smaller protein-RNA benchmarks provide a preliminary assessment. These results establish a framework for interpreting predicted structural confidence across different classes of biomolecular interactions and suggest that directional scoring may also be useful for computationally designed protein binders. The new freely available ipSAE code is available from: https://github.com/DunbrackLab/IPSAE2.

papers.title: ANABOLIC FAILURE, NOT CATABOLIC ACTIVATION, UNDERLIES GLYCOGEN DEPLETION IN CERVICAL CARCINOGENESIS: A MULTI-COHORT TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS
papers.abstract: Abstract Background. Cervical epithelium loses its glycogen as disease grade rises, an observation old enough to underpin iodine-based visual screening, but which arm of glycogen metabolism accounts for the loss has not been established. The expectation from cancer metabolism is catabolic: that stored glycogen is mobilized and glycolysis activated. Methods. We analyzed 238 specimens from four publicly available cohorts across three sample types: 128 laser-capture-microdissected epithelial samples, 35 bulk-tissue samples, and 75 exfoliated cytology samples in two sets (44 and 31; GSE27678). We prespecified a 33-gene panel comprising four modules: glycogen synthesis, glycogen degradation, glycolysis, and squamous differentiation. For each specimen, we calculated module scores using single-sample gene set enrichment. Differential expression was assessed with limma, pathway enrichment with fgsea, and classification performance with bootstrap confidence intervals for ROC curves. We documented all analytical decisions and their rationale. Results. Synthesis and differentiation fell with grade in all four cohorts, while degradation and glycolysis stayed at their normal-tissue baseline. All seven differentiation genes were reduced in carcinoma, and all seven occupied the top 5.1% of the ranked transcriptome, with CRNN the most down-regulated of 21,755 genes. Synthesis failed selectively, through GYS2 and PPP1R3C only, with the ubiquitous synthase GYS1 unchanged. The glycolytic module separated from normal epithelium at no grade (p 0.45 to 0.62), classified CIN3 or worse at an area under the curve of 0.569 with an interval spanning chance, and showed no enrichment in carcinoma. Synthesis separated from normal first, at CIN2, and differentiation at CIN3. The composite index tracked grade in the discovery cohort (Spearman rho 0.652, p 7.9e-17) but offered no discriminatory advantage over its differentiation component alone (0.832 against 0.832). Conclusions. Glycogen depletion in cervical carcinogenesis reflects failure of a tissue-restricted synthetic axis, GYS2 and PPP1R3C, within a collapsing squamous differentiation program, not catabolic activation. Measuring all four candidate mechanisms on one scale in the same specimen is what allows the catabolic explanation to be excluded rather than merely left untested. The pattern holds across two array chemistries and three specimen preparations, including the exfoliated cytology that screening already collects, and the synthesis and differentiation modules together are the molecular counterpart of what iodine staining reports. These are transcript-level findings and define no clinical threshold.

papers.title: The pupal stage shapes life-history trade-offs across metamorphosis
papers.abstract: Dealing with ecological stressors during development often comes at the expense of later-life performance. Although such trade-offs are well studied as two-stage systems such as larva-adult trade-offs, they are rarely examined across multiple developmental stages, limiting our understanding of how ecological effects are integrated throughout complex life cycles. We addressed this gap using a multistage experimental framework in Aedes aegypti, where we exposed individuals to predation risk during the larval stage, the pupal stage, both stages, or neither, and quantified developmental, physiological, and adult fitness traits. Contrary to expectations, predation risk across successive stages did not produce cumulative fitness costs, and traits varied in their responses. Both males and females emerged faster when exposed to risk, with lighter bodies, but males paid an additional cost of reduced starvation resistance when the pupal stage was exposed. Surprisingly, despite their lower body mass, females showed enhanced reproductive performance when both stages were exposed to risk. Overall, responses were stage- and sex-specific, with exposure during the non-feeding pupal stage imposing greater life-history costs than larval exposure alone. Measurements across the larva-pupa-adult continuum further revealed that traits such as body mass and energy reserves respond differently before and after metamorphosis, highlighting the role of the pupa in mediating trade-offs. Our findings identify the pupal stage as a critical mediator of life-history trade-offs and demonstrate the value of a multistage framework for understanding the role of each stage in life-history evolution.

papers.title: Ultrasensitive Regulation in the Tryptophan System in Escherichia coli Provides Effective Noise Mitigation
papers.abstract: The tryptophan system in Escherichia coli maintains intracellular concentration of tryptophan in a narrow band regardless of the nutritional status and uncertainty in its environment. The system is characterized by three distinct regulations namely, genetic regulation, mRNA attenuation and enzyme inhibition, that use the tryptophan concentration as a feedback signal. It has been shown previously, that the multiple feedback loop design is responsible for rapid synthesis of tryptophan when faced with starvation. It is well known that a design with rapid response to external signals also implies poorer noise mitigation properties. This work investigates the design elements that limit the adverse impact of the multiple feedback loop architecture on noise propagation in the tryptophan system using a frequency response analysis. Specifically, we use sinusoidal input describing functions to approximate the transfer characteristics of the ultrasensitive regulators and then obtain the frequency response of the closed-loop feedback system. The study suggests that the tryptophan system of E. coli has evolved to simultaneously satisfy the two properties of rapid response and noise mitigation. Particularly, the multiple feedback loop is responsible for the rapid response, while the nonlinear regulation provides effective noise mitigation.

papers.title: KobA mediates kinesin-1-dependent transport of dynein-dynactin to microtubule plus ends
papers.abstract: Cytoplasmic dynein transports diverse cargoes toward microtubule minus ends following activation by the dynactin complex and cargo adapters. In elongated cells such as fungal hyphae and neurons, dynein must first undergo kinesin-1-dependent transport to microtubule plus ends to engage cargoes, but the mechanism linking these opposing motors remains poorly understood. Here, we identify KobA in the filamentous fungus Aspergillus nidulans as a kinesin-1-binding, coiled-coil protein essential for kinesin-1 (KinA)-mediated plus-end transport of dynein and dynactin. KobA binds the C-terminal cargo-binding domain of KinA. Interestingly, KobA is not required for the general function of KinA in supporting hyphal growth alongside myosin-V, but is specifically required for the microtubule plus-end accumulation of dynein-dynactin even when KinA is activated. Mechanistically, KobA enhances the interaction between KinA and dynactin-dynein. Within its disordered N-terminal region, KobA harbors a Spindly motif typically present in dynein-activating cargo adapters that engage the dynactin pointed end. AlphaFold-3 predictions suggest that the Spindly motif of KobA also binds the dynactin pointed end, and in support of this notion, point mutations within the KobA Spindly motif disrupt the KinA-dynactin association, causing dynein to decorate microtubules rather than accumulate at plus ends. Together, our findings establish KobA as a novel adapter that utilizes a classic cargo adapter Spindly motif to link kinesin-1 to dynein-dynactin, ensuring targeted plus-end delivery of the minus-end motor.

papers.title: Long term survival of chronically demyelinated axons in the taiep rat
papers.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an inflammatory demyelinating disease of the CNS in which neuroaxonal loss underlies permanent neurological disability. Axon loss in MS has been attributed to several causes, including loss of trophic/metabolic support from the myelin sheath. However, the contribution of chronic demyelination to axonal demise has been difficult to ascertain, due largely to the lack of long-lived models and uncertainty about the location of the primary injury site in long fibre tracts in MS patients. Here, we examine chronically demyelinated axons using light and electron microscopy of spinal cord tracts of 1- to 24-month-old taiep rats, in which the gene that is mutated, Tubb4a p.A302T, is expressed highly in oligodendrocytes. We find that small diameter axons in the dorsal column can survive for many months following demyelination. This is associated with significantly increased densities of oligodendroglia, and supernumerary glial cell processes. We hypothesise that trophic and metabolic support, sufficient to support axon survival, can be achieved through close contact between axons and glia. While efforts to restore myelin in MS remain crucial to recovering normal neurological function, myelin per se might not be a prerequisite for axonal survival under all circumstances.

papers.title: Circadian feeding rhythm loss drives sex-specific β-cell dysfunction in diet-induced obesity
papers.abstract: Diet-induced obesity (DIO), modeled by a high-fat diet (HFD), adversely affects circadian glucose homeostasis partly by dysregulating fasting/feeding cycles. However, its impact on circadian {beta}-cell function and relevant transcriptional programs remains unclear. To investigate this, we exposed male and female C57BL/6 mice to either chow or HFD for eight weeks and assessed behavioral (feeding/activity), physiological (glucose tolerance/insulin secretion), transcriptomic (RNA sequencing (RNA-seq)), and epigenomic (Assay for Transposase-Accessible Chromatin using Sequencing (ATAC-seq)) circadian rhythms. Additionally, we tested whether normalizing fasting/feeding cycles via time-restricted feeding (tRF) during the dark- or light-phase of the circadian cycle could mitigate DIO's deleterious effects. DIO disrupted circadian fasting/feeding rhythms, with greater disruption in males than females (p<0.05 vs. CHOW). In males, DIO abolished circadian regulation of glucose tolerance and in vivo glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) (p<0.05 vs. chow), whereas female mice maintained circadian glucose homeostasis. RNA-seq analysis of male islets revealed a 42.1% reduction in circadian-regulated transcripts under DIO, with weakened rhythms in key {beta}-cell pathways such as insulin secretion. Moreover, ATAC-Seq analysis indicated reduced chromatin accessibility of genes/pathways related to insulin secretion and glucose hemostasis under DIO (p<0.05 vs. chow) during both dark- or light-phase of the circadian cycle. Notably, dark-phase time-restricted feeding (tRF) restored circadian glucose tolerance, GSIS, and islet gene expression, whereas light-phase tRF enhanced {beta}-cell function during the normally inactive/light phase of the circadian cycle, further suppressing circadian rhythmicity of the islet transcriptome. Motif analysis indicated that DIO suppressed the activity of D-box transcription factors (TFs) (DBP and TEF) while enhancing the activity of ETS family TFs (ELK1, ETS2, ELF2, and GABPA), which was partly mitigated by dark-phase tRF. Our study demonstrates that DIO disrupts circadian {beta}-cell function and gene expression by dysregulating fasting/feeding cycles in male mice and reveals significant sex differences in how DIO affects circadian glucose homeostasis and {beta}-cell function.

papers.title: NRT2.2 is essential for nitrate uptake and carbon-nitrogen balance in Nannochloropsis oceanica
papers.abstract: Nitrate is the dominant nitrogen source for marine microalgae, yet how it is taken up remains poorly understood in many ecologically and biotechnologically relevant species. Here we show that NITRATE TRANSPORTER 2.2 (NRT2.2) is the principal nitrate transporter of the oleaginous marine microalga Nannochloropsis oceanica. N. oceanica encodes only two NRT2 proteins and, unlike land plants and green algae, lacks a recognizable homolog of NITRATE ASSIMILATION-RELATED 2 (NAR2), the partner protein that green-lineage NRT2s require for activity and plasma membrane targeting. CRISPR knock-outs and confocal imaging showed that NRT2.2 is located at the plasma membrane and is required for nitrate uptake, whereas its paralog NRT2.1 cannot compensate for its loss. When nitrate was resupplied after nitrogen starvation, nrt2.2 mutants did not take up nitrate and did not resume growth, while they recovered normally with ammonium. Their photosystem II efficiency fell below that of fully nitrogen-starved wild-type cells, and chlorophyll content was reduced, while total protein remained stable. Fixed carbon was redirected into storage, with lipids and carbohydrates accumulating above the levels of all strains after 3 days of nitrogen starvation. Loss of NRT2.2 therefore mimics a prolonged nitrogen starvation, even though nitrate is available. Because nitrate was present but could not be used, recovery from starvation depends on the capacity to take up nitrate, not only on its availability. In the ocean, where nitrate is depleted for long periods and resupplied episodically, NRT2.2 is thus likely to set how quickly Nannochloropsis can use new nitrate inputs and resume growth.

papers.title: Partial agonists and heteromeric Kainate receptor desensitization
papers.abstract: Kainate receptors (KARs) are glutamate-gated ion channels that mediate fast excitatory synaptic transmission in the central nervous system. KARs assemble as homo- or heterotetramers composed of five subunits (GluK1-5), with heteromeric assemblies representing the predominant native population. Although KARs share overall structures and basic functional properties with other ionotropic glutamate receptor subfamilies, they exhibit distinct gating kinetics, particularly with respect to desensitization. While earlier studies have demonstrated how agonist binding drives gate opening and subsequent desensitization, the mechanisms governing partial agonism and desensitization of KARs, especially in heteromeric KARs, remain incompletely understood. Here, we combine electrophysiology and microscale thermophoresis binding assays to elucidate how distinct KAR partial agonists control KAR desensitization and its recovery. While the onset rates of desensitization of homo- and heteromeric receptors activated by high/saturating concentrations of partial agonists are conserved between GluK2 and GluK2/GluK5 receptors, recovery from desensitization in heteromers is significantly slower than in homomers. Together with structural modeling and analysis of the GluK2 and GluK5 ligand binding domains (LBDs) in complex with orthosteric ligands, we show that agonist residence time and the extent of LBD bi-lobe closure across various agonists take precedence over subunit composition in governing KAR desensitization.

papers.title: Cryo-EM structures of Cereibacter sphaeroides ferrochelatase reveal an oligomeric state that occludes the substrate-binding site
papers.abstract: Protoporphyrin IX (PPIX) is the last shared intermediate of heme and (bacterio)chlorophyll ((B)Chl) biosynthesis. Insertion of iron into PPIX by the PPIX ferrochelatase (FeCh) PpfC produces heme, whereas magnesium insertion by magnesium chelatase (MgCh) initiates (B)Chl synthesis. Chlorophototrophic organisms must regulate this biosynthetic node to ensure the correct flux of PPIX to each of these crucial tetrapyrrole products, presenting a particularly acute problem for the facultative bacterium Cereibacter (previously Rhodobacter) sphaeroides, which can switch between chemotrophic (respiratory) and phototrophic (photosynthetic) growth modes. To elucidate the structural basis for the catalytic and regulatory functions of C. sphaeroides FeCh (PpfCCs), we used cryogenic electron microscopy to determine its structure, to our knowledge the first such information for a Gram-negative or phototrophic organism. We determined the 2.6 [A] structure of an active site mutant of PpfCCs, which forms a dimer with a monomer-to-monomer interface that coordinates two hemes. We also determined a 2.5 [A] structure of the wild-type enzyme, in which two dimers interact in a homotetrameric arrangement that occludes PPIX binding at the active site of each monomer. We propose that the PpfCCs dimer likely docks onto the inner membrane in a manner analogous to the human enzyme, whereas the tetramer represents a transiently inactive state whereby the hydrophobic lips and active site are both occluded. These novel oligomerization states of FeCh may have evolved to influence the flux of tetrapyrroles through the heme/BChl branchpoint in purple bacteria.

papers.title: ExPert infers causal perturbations from cell states across biological and clinical contexts
papers.abstract: Pooled single-cell CRISPR screens have driven substantial effort toward models predicting the response to a perturbation. We posed the inverse question: which perturbation produced an observed cell state? Here we developed ExPert (Extracting Perturbations), which learns one prototype per perturbation in a latent space shared by 12 cellular contexts, trained on 8,964 perturbations and 19.5 million cells, and ranks 19,895 candidate genes per query, over half absent from training. ExPert more than doubled held-out-context recall over the best existing method with 1,000-fold less compute, and transferred without retraining to drugs, protein degradation and combinations. In alcohol-associated liver disease it implicated mRNA export, unchanged in expression, and we experimentally confirmed nuclear poly(A) retention and isoform switching. In primary mitochondrial disease it recovered the affected complex from blood, localized the signal to monocytes, and flagged a misdiagnosed control. Perturbation atlases can thus be queried in reverse, from state to likely driver.

papers.title: Herboxidiene and EGFR expression in A172 glioblastoma cells
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma carries a five-year survival of about 10%, and EGFR amplification is one of the molecular criteria that define the disease in the 2021 WHO classification of central nervous system tumours. SF3b inhibitors, which displace the U2 snRNP from the intron branch point, suppress EGFR expression in lung adenocarcinoma cells by causing retention of EGFR intron 2. We asked whether the same route operates in glioblastoma, using A172 cells, which express wild-type EGFR together with an in-frame tandem duplication of exons 18-26. Herboxidiene inhibited A172 proliferation: DMSO-treated cultures reached 2.32 times their day 0 reading by day 3 (SD 0.61), whereas every herboxidiene concentration from 0.125 to 1 M held the cultures at or below their starting value and differed from the vehicle on days 2 and 3 (Dunnett, p < 0.05). RT-PCR across EGFR exons 2-3 showed no intron 2-retained product at any concentration; instead the spliced product decreased relative to ACTB, to 0.43 of the vehicle value at 0.125 M, without deepening further up to 1 M. EGFR protein fell, but the two forms behaved differently: the 170 kDa wild-type band was no longer detectable from 0.13 M, whereas the 190 kDa duplicated form persisted at every concentration and declined only gradually, to 0.30 of the vehicle value at 1 M. RT-PCR of CDKN1B (p27) showed retention of introns 1 and 2 at 0.5 M in A172 and in A549 lung adenocarcinoma cells. In A172 cells, therefore, herboxidiene suppresses EGFR expression without the intron 2 retention seen in lung adenocarcinoma lines, and the growth inhibition is not accounted for by loss of EGFR alone. The proliferation data are the mean and SD of three series; the RT-PCR and western blot experiments were each performed once, without replicates or statistical testing, and should be read as preliminary.

papers.title: ROCK inhibitor Ripasudil reduces Alzheimer pathological proteins and enhances cellular bioenergetics
papers.abstract: Rho-associated kinase (ROCK) inhibitors have been explored as an Alzheimer Disease (AD) therapeutic agent. In this study, we aim to determine the efficacy of a potent ROCK inhibitor, ripasudil, in impacting AD pathological protein tau in mice. The time-course study showed that ripasudil rapidly penetrated mouse brains, reaching maximal concentration half an hour post-injection. To determine the efficacy of ripasudil, we injected AppNL-G-F knock-in mice with ripasudil at 30 mg/kg and sacrificed them after three hours. We used Tandem Mass Tag labels and compared the proteomic profiles of mouse brains exposed to ripasudil to those exposed to saline. We also treated AD-patient-derived Neural Stem Cells (NSCs) with ripasudil and performed a Seahorse Mito Stress Test to evaluate their impact on mitochondrial activity. Bioinformatics analysis of the proteomic profiles revealed differentially enriched components of chromosome. The Mito Stress Test of NSCs revealed significant increases in basal oxygen consumption, ATP-linked respiration, maximal respiration, and reserve capacity oxygen consumption compared to untreated NSCs. Importantly, we found a significant reduction of Tau and pTau 396 in brains of mice treated with ripasudil. Overall, our findings highlight the feasibility and promise of ROCK inhibitor ripasudil as an AD therapeutic agent.

papers.title: Synthetic lethality of p97 inhibition and PSMC2-overexpressionovercomes bortezomib resistance in multiple myeloma
papers.abstract: The aim of the present study was to analyze genomic profiles obtained from multiple myeloma (MM) patient tumors to identify prognostic classifiers of clinical response and survival following bortezomib monotherapy and then target key actionable classifiers that underly bortezomib resistance. We discovered higher levels of proteasome PSMC2 messenger RNA in myeloma cells from patients that did not respond to bortezomib and that higher PSMC2 expression correlated with inferior progression-free and overall survival. Pharmacologic screening revealed that CB-5339, an ATP-competitive inhibitor of the molecular chaperone p97/VCP that shuttles ubiquitin-conjugated substrates to proteasomes, was synthetic lethal in MM cells engineered to overexpress PSMC2. p97 co-immunoprecipitated with 26S proteasomes affinity-purified from PSMC2-overexpressing cells which exhibited greater activity and reduced bortezomib sensitivity relative to PSMC2-KO cells. Bortezomib treatment followed by in-situ cross-linking and western blotting revealed higher levels of K48- and K63-linkage-specific ubiquitin chains covalently bound to 26S proteasomes isolated from PSMC2-KO cells compared to proteasomes affinity-purified from PSMC2-overexpressing cells. Western blotting demonstrated higher levels of 19S RPs, 26S proteasomes, and a PSMC2-PSMC1-PSMD2 subcomplex in PSMC2-overexpressing cells relative to PSMC2-KO cells. CB-5339 and bortezomib co-treatment synergistically targeted tumor cells obtained from MM patients previously exposed to bortezomib therapy and reduced the in vivo growth of PSMC2-overexpressing myeloma xenografts in mice. Taken together, we have discovered a genetic vulnerability that provokes proteasome-intrinsic bortezomib resistance and validated the potential of synthetic lethality to guide therapeutic interventions. Our study reaffirms that transcriptomic heterogeneity in MM is a primary driver of prognostic variability.

papers.title: Paraquat Inhalation Produces Male-Biased Dopaminergic Neuron Loss and Motor Deficits in Mice: Relevance to Parkinsons Disease
papers.abstract: Long-term exposure to paraquat (PQ), a widely used herbicide, has been linked to increased risk of Parkinsons Disease (PD) in agricultural workers and rural communities in the United States (US), findings further supported by experimental animal studies. Although banned in many countries across the globe, PQ remains widely used in the US. Inhalation of PQ has been known to induce systemic organ failure at acute concentrations. However, prolonged low-dose inhalation from agricultural spraying and pesticide drift has not been readily evaluated for its potential to contribute to neurodegenerative diseases in vivo. Instead, many experimental studies have relied on systemic routes of exposure, which do not effectively replicate the most common route of exposure to PQ in the environment. In the current study, Parkinsonian features were examined in mice that had been exposed via whole-body inhalation to PQ aerosol for either 40 or 60 days. Levels of PQ in brain were highest in olfactory bulb, followed by frontal cortex and then brainstem in both sexes. After 60 days of exposure, male-specific impairments in locomotor activity were observed, in addition to reductions in striatal dopamine, in substantia nigra tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) expression and number of TH+ dopaminergic neurons, the latter being considered the primary basis of PD, along with increased olfactory bulb -synuclein levels. As such, these studies confirm the dopaminergic neurotoxicity of inhaled PQ. These findings raise significant concerns as to the contribution of PQ exposures to the continued increase in the incidence of PD in the US.

papers.title: Pathology foundation-model embeddings reveal a morphological landscape of breast lesions beyond diagnostic categories
papers.abstract: Background: Despite rapid advances in computational pathology, including foundation-model embeddings, most approaches remain classifier-based. Breast lesion pathology is an area of unmet clinicopathological need and a compelling setting for morphology-based modeling: diagnostic categories occupy overlapping morphological spectra and reflect heterogeneous pathways of tumor development, thereby posing substantial challenges for pathological diagnosis and subsequent clinical decision-making. However, approaches to delineate morphological continua across diagnostic categories and tumor development remain understudied. Here, we leveraged morphology-based foundation-model embeddings to define a morphologic state space across breast lesion categories and dissect how these embeddings could reflect a pathobiological continuum or sequence associated with tumor development. Methods: To model breast lesion categories in continuous morphology space, we established a leakage-controlled, patient-aware workflow using the frozen foundation model Prov-GigaPath and the BReAst Carcinoma Subtyping (BRACS) dataset, a pathologist-annotated hematoxylin-and-eosin (H&E) breast lesion dataset spanning normal tissue, benign proliferative lesions, atypical lesions, ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) and invasive carcinoma (IC). Using the BRACS training split, we defined a train-derived principal component analysis (PCA) morphology space. We then performed two complementary analyses: normal-rooted k-nearest-neighbor (kNN)-Dijkstra graph-distance scoring to derive a trajectory-like morphology score without imposing the full ordinal diagnostic sequence; pairwise Energy distance and squared maximum mean discrepancy with a radial-basis-function kernel (RBF-MMD2) to quantify order-free distributional separation among diagnostic categories. Validation and test data were projected into the train-defined reference space to assess reproducibility. Results: Prov-GigaPath embeddings defined a train-derived morphology space with category-associated organization. Without imposing the full diagnostic sequence, normal-rooted kNN-Dijkstra graph distances recovered a trajectory-like morphology arrangement from normal/benign to malignant lesions. Order-free Energy distance and RBF-MMD2 further supported graded separation among lesion categories. Validation and test datasets preserved the pathological organization. Furthermore, morphological embeddings dissected DCIS heterogeneity associated with concurrent invasive carcinoma, without requiring additional molecular information. Conclusions: Leveraging morphology-based foundation-model embeddings, we defined a morphologic state space across breast lesion categories, allowing nuanced positioning of breast lesions along a pathobiological continuum associated with tumor development. Our approaches pave the way for extracting biologically and clinically relevant information from routine histopathology to guide molecular testing, individualized risk assessment, and cost-efficient clinicopathological decision-making.

papers.title: Genome-wide CRISPRi-seq maps essential-gene contributions to aminoglycoside susceptibility in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
papers.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic ESKAPE pathogen whose multiple intrinsic and acquired antibiotic resistance mechanisms restrict treatment options. Essential genes offer potential antimicrobial targets, but their vulnerability to partial inhibition and contribution to antibiotic susceptibility remain incompletely characterized. Here, we developed a rhamnose-inducible CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) platform and an 83,078-guide library for genome-wide screening in PAO1, with mismatch guides enabling graded repression. Fitness profiling in antibiotic-free Mueller-Hinton medium identified 743 genes whose repression reduced competitive fitness and revealed sequence features associated with guide performance. Combining full-match and mismatch-guide responses revealed substantial variation in essential-gene fitness effects across predicted repression strengths, while comparison of fitness profiles between Mueller-Hinton medium and fetal bovine serum identified condition-dependent effects alongside a conserved fitness landscape. Under aminoglycoside exposure, we identified 118 recurrent sensitizing and 120 recurrent protective gene knockdowns, including many targeting essential and fitness-associated functions. Growth and killing assays with individual strains confirmed that CRISPRi targeting of atpI, accC, secA and ftsZ enhanced tobramycin activity. Finally, transcriptome analysis of these knockdowns confirmed target silencing, captured polar effects on neighboring genes and revealed distinct but overlapping transcriptional responses. Together, these findings quantify the variable fitness costs of essential-gene repression and identify candidate targets for potentiating aminoglycoside activity. IMPORTANCE Essential bacterial genes are difficult to study because their complete disruption prevents growth. Yet knowing that a gene is essential does not reveal how strongly its activity must be reduced to impair growth. Here, we developed a method to examine how reduced gene expression affects fitness across the genome of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a major cause of difficult-to-treat infections. This approach identified essential functions particularly vulnerable to partial depletion and mapped how gene repression alters aminoglycoside susceptibility. Repressing selected genes impaired growth and disproportionately increased killing by tobramycin. These tools and datasets provide a resource for prioritizing candidate antibacterial targets and investigating whether partial inhibition of essential functions can enhance the activity of existing antibiotics.

papers.title: Adipocyte Kindlin-2 Coordinates an E-cadherin/β-catenin/IGFBP2 Endocrine Axis to Regulate Skin Regeneration and Diabetic Wound Healing
papers.abstract: Skin wound healing is a complex, multicellular process essential for maintaining tissue integrity and homeostasis. Despite advances in biomaterial and cell-based therapies, the mechanisms by which adipose tissue regulates skin regeneration remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify adipocyte Kindlin-2 as a critical regulator of cutaneous wound repair. Adipocyte-specific deletion of Kindlin-2 markedly accelerates wound closure in mice by enhancing fibroblast proliferation, angiogenesis, and suppressing inflammation. Transplantation of visceral white adipose tissue (vWAT) from Kindlin-2-deficient mice similarly promotes wound healing, indicating an endocrine contribution of vWAT to skin regeneration. Mechanistically, loss of Kindlin-2 promotes E-cadherin proteolysis, resulting in increased release of a 33-kDa C-terminal fragment (CTF2) that activates {beta}-catenin signaling and induces transcriptional upregulation and secretion of insulin-like growth factor binding protein 2 (IGFBP2). Elevated circulating IGFBP2, in turn, stimulates integrin signaling in target cells to enhance wound repair. Pharmacological inhibition of {beta}-catenin signaling abrogated the healing advantage conferred by Kindlin-2 deficiency. Conversely, local delivery of IGFBP2 via lentiviral significantly accelerates wound closure in both wild-type C57BL/6 and diabetic ob/ob mice. Collectively, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized adipose-skin endocrine axis governed by Kindlin-2 and IGFBP2 that orchestrates tissue regeneration. Targeting this Kindlin-2/E-cadherin/{beta}-catenin/IGFBP2 pathway offers a promising therapeutic strategy for enhancing wound healing, particularly in chronic and diabetic wounds.

papers.title: Dissecting the genetic basis of DUS characters in Pakistani wheat varieties
papers.abstract: Distinctness, Uniformity and Stability (DUS) testing is fundamental to varietal characterization and the protection of Plant Breeders Rights (PBRs), but conventional DUS assessment relies predominantly on morphological characteristics whose expression may be influenced by environmental conditions, developmental stage and observer-related variation. Integrating character-specific molecular markers with conventional DUS assessment may therefore improve the reproducibility and genetic resolution of varietal identification. This study investigated the genetic architecture of DUS characteristics in a panel of 102 historical and modern Pakistani wheat varieties using genome-wide association studies (GWAS). Phenotypic variation was evaluated using distribution, correlation and hierarchical clustering analyses, while the germplasm was genotyped using a wheat genotyping-by-targeted sequencing platform. After quality filtering, 21,670 high-quality single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were retained for analyses of genetic diversity, population structure, linkage disequilibrium (LD) and marker-trait associations. Population structure analysis indicated extensive admixture, with cross-entropy supporting K = 9 ancestral components, whereas hierarchical genetic clustering separated the germplasm into five broad groups. The first three principal components explained 8.09%, 7.20% and 5.39% of the total genetic variation, respectively. GWAS using BLINK and FarmCPU identified significant associations for several diagnostically important DUS characteristics. Growth habit was strongly associated with SNP 1B_129176704, with an additional signal on chromosome 5B. Shattering showed its strongest association at 1D_445256324, accompanied by several closely linked SNPs in the same region and a secondary significant locus at 7B_703502819. Flag leaf length was associated with a cluster of SNPs on chromosome 6A, while tiller density showed a major association with 5D_205488820. These findings demonstrate substantial phenotypic and genetic diversity within Pakistani wheat germplasm and identify genomic regions that merit validation as character-specific molecular tools to complement conventional DUS testing and PBR implementation.

papers.title: Coupled Modeling of Tumor Volume and ctDNA Dynamics in HPV-Associated Anal Squamous Cell Carcinoma
papers.abstract: Response to anti-PD-1 immunotherapy in advanced HPV-associated anal squamous cell carcinoma (ASCC) varies and is assessed by infrequent imaging that lags behind tumor biology. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) can be sampled frequently and reflects near-real-time tumor activity yet is rarely built into mechanistic models of treatment response. Using longitudinal tumor volume and HPV ctDNA from 26 patients treated with pembrolizumab, we found that baseline ctDNA scores tracked tumor burden but did not distinguish responders from non-responders, whereas ctDNA after one treatment cycle had a higher relative decrease in responders, six weeks before the next scan. We developed an ordinary differential equation model linking tumor volume to the ctDNA released by tumor cells. Sensitivity, identifiability, and model-selection analyses reduced it to two patient-specific parameters, proliferation and shedding rates, which reproduced individual volume and ctDNA trajectories, including a transient ctDNA spike at treatment onset. Proliferation was faster in non-responders. This framework supports model-based, ctDNA-guided monitoring of immunotherapy response.

papers.title: Extensive membrane lipid remodeling at the host-parasite interface of Toxoplasma gondii
papers.abstract: Phosphoinositides regulate diverse membrane trafficking and signaling events in eukaryotic cells, yet their transbilayer distribution remains largely unexplored, particularly at host-parasite membrane interfaces. Here, we determined the membrane leaflet localization of phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate (PtdIns(4)P) and phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PtdIns(4,5)P2) in Toxoplasma gondii using quick-freezing freeze-fracture replica labeling combined with phosphoinositide-specific probes. Both phosphoinositides were predominantly localized to the cytoplasmic leaflet of the parasite plasma membrane, whereas only weak labeling was detected in the inner membrane complex. PtdIns(4)P, but not PtdIns(4,5)P2, was additionally detected on intracellular vesicles, while mature micronemes lacked detectable labeling for either phosphoinositide. Surprisingly, both phosphoinositides exhibited nearly symmetric distributions between the two leaflets of the parasitophorous vacuole membrane (PVM), in striking contrast to their asymmetric localization in the parasite plasma membrane. Together with our previous demonstration that phosphatidylserine and phosphatidylethanolamine also lose their transbilayer asymmetry in the PVM, these findings indicate that the PVM undergoes global membrane lipid remodeling that extends from major phospholipids to phosphoinositides. We propose that this extensive lipid reorganization represents a defining structural feature of the apicomplexan PVM and provides a new framework for understanding membrane identity at the host-parasite interface.

papers.title: Quantum Dot-Based Non-invasive Monitoring of Sinusoidal Endothelial Scavenger Function in Steatohepatitis
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and its progressive form, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), represent urgent medical challenges. Current non-invasive assessments rely on serum indices or tissue stiffness, and none visualizes functional changes within the liver, hindering drug discovery and patient management. In this study, we developed a non-invasive technique using semiconductor quantum dots, as blood-borne foreign particle mimics, to evaluate the scavenger function of liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs) via near-infrared optical imaging. Progression from MASLD to MASH induced a significant decline in the scavenger capability of LSECs, resulting in a marked reduction of intrahepatic quantum dot retention. Mechanistically, we demonstrated that quantum dots are recognized and internalized by scavenger receptor class A (SR-A) on LSECs, and that SR-A-mediated uptake progressively diminishes with increasing MASH severity. Crucially, quantum dot retention levels significantly correlated with both the progression and regression of MASH pathology. These findings demonstrate that quantum dot-based optical evaluation of LSEC scavenger function offers a highly sensitive, non-invasive diagnostic platform for staging MASH and assessing therapeutic efficacy.

papers.title: APP functions at the endomembrane system
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: APP is a type I transmembrane protein, and its intracellular domain (AICD) interacts with FE65, X11, and mDAB1, et al., through the YENPTY motif. Accordingly, it has been proposed that the functions of APP are similar to Notch, which regulates gene expression through releasing NICD after combining with its ligands. However, the detailed underlying mechanisms of how FE65 is regulated by APP, as well as their target genes, remain unknown. METHODS: We overexpressed APP695 in N2a cells, and deleted/mutated APP in H4 cells by CRISPR-Cas9, respectively. The impacts of APP overexpression and ablation were detected by proteome comparison and immunoblotting. Thereafter, the subcellular localizations of APP and its binding protein FE65 were examined by immunofluorescence. RESULTS: APP overexpression not only resulted in its retention in Golgi apparatus (GA) and Endoplasmic reticulum (ER), but also induced FE65 clustering. In addition, it significantly reduced the protein level of ATF4 in N2a cells. On the contrary, knockdown of FE65 restored the protein level of ATF4. More importantly, APP overexpression also impaired autophagy. In contrast, knockout of APP rescued LC3 conversion. Of note, the APP Swedish mutant did not impact ER stress or the autophagic flux. Nevertheless, it facilitated the cleavage of APP-CTFs by gamma-secretase. DISCUSSION: The evidence presented in the current study demonstrates that APP is involved in stabilizing the endomembrane system and the subcellular transport of FE65. More importantly, the role of APP in regulating autophagy indicated that full-length APP could be considered a therapeutic target for preventing the development of AD.

papers.title: A candidate HNRNPU-CHD2 RNA-processing axis in neurodevelopmental disease
papers.abstract: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in HNRNPU, which encodes a nuclear RNA-binding scaffold protein, cause a neurodevelopmental disorder with epilepsy, intellectual disability and brain malformations, but the programs that link HNRNPU dosage to neuronal dysfunction remain poorly defined. We depleted HNRNPU in Human embryonic kidney 293T (HEK293T) cells, profiled gene expression and alternative splicing, intersected the two datasets, and asked which of the resulting genes already carried a neurodevelopmental annotation. Knockdown produced 5,643 differentially expressed genes and 21,728 high-confidence splicing events; 1,222 genes changed at both levels, and two pre-specified neurodevelopmental panel genes were among them: CHD2 and DYRK1A. In K562 eCLIP experiments, 107 reproducible HNRNPU peaks were detected across the CHD2 gene body, and three of the four regulated exons introduce a reading-frame shift whose premature termination codon lies far upstream of the final exon junction, predicting nonsense-mediated decay. Public K562 knockdown data reproduced the rise in CHD2 mRNA and the same skipped-exon change, and CHD2 depletion in the neural line SH-SY5Y altered cell-cycle, DNA-repair and neural gene programs. HNRNPU therefore constrains a frameshift-prone splicing switch in CHD2, a candidate route from HNRNPU haploinsufficiency to loss of functional CHD2 if these transcripts are degraded.

papers.title: Brazilian bryophytes: a national-scale comprehensive dataset of species richness and geographic distribution
papers.abstract: Bryophytes (Anthocerotophyta, Marchantiophyta, and Bryophyta) remain under-sampled in large-scale biodiversity databases in Brazil, despite their ecological importance. In Brazil, Flora e Funga do Brasil recognizes 1,618 bryophyte species distributed across six biomes that are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic pressures such as deforestation, agricultural expansion, and climate change. Nevertheless, knowledge of species geographic distributions remains fragmented and based on scattered records. Flora e Funga do Brasil serves as the official taxonomic reference for the country, providing the accepted species list and serving as a baseline for biodiversity studies. However, as it was designed as a nomenclatural and taxonomic checklist, it does not integrate primary occurrence records with geographic coordinates and collection dates. Consequently, occurrence data remain dispersed across herbaria, digital repositories, and the scientific literature, without dynamic updates linked to the official checklist. This disconnect between the taxonomic framework and primary occurrence records limits macroecological and biogeographical analyses at national scales, which depend on standardized georeferenced biodiversity databases. To address this gap, we compiled 102,528 bryophyte occurrence records from herbarium specimens, using data from GBIF and the speciesLink network, complemented by field collections from the Caatinga and records from the Cryptogamic Herbarium of the State University of Piaui. All records were georeferenced and curated, including verification of inconsistent coordinates, removal of duplicates, and taxonomic standardization using Bryonames. When available, information such as collection date and collector was retained. The dataset comprises 1,821 species, 125 families, and 442 genera. Bryophyta (mosses) was the most diverse group (1,056 spp., 84 families, 310 genera), followed by Marchantiophyta (745 spp., 37 families, 124 genera) and Anthocerotophyta (19 spp., four families, seven genera). Among mosses, the most species-rich families were Sphagnaceae (79 spp.), Fissidentaceae (76 spp.), and Pottiaceae (76 spp.). Among liverworts, Lejeuneaceae dominated with 335 species, followed by Lepidoziaceae (58 spp.) and Plagiochilaceae (51 spp.). Among hornworts, Anthocerotaceae, Dendrocerotaceae, and Notothyladaceae each included six species. Regionally, the Southeast showed the highest richness (1,338 spp.), followed by the South (974 spp.), Central-West (937 spp.), Northeast (897 spp.), and North (763 spp.). Regarding biomes, the Atlantic Forest (1,523 spp.) and Amazon (1,054 spp.) were the most species-rich, followed by the Cerrado (810 spp.), Caatinga (671 spp.), Pampa (269 spp.), and Pantanal (61 spp.). These patterns reflect both ecological gradients and historical sampling biases. This dataset bridges the gap between the official taxonomic checklist and primary occurrence data by integrating multiple sources into a standardized, openly accessible database. It provides a robust tool for studies in macroecology, biogeography, and conservation, enabling analyses of spatial patterns of species richness, endemism, and taxonomic, functional, and phylogenetic diversity across environmental gradients. It also supports species distribution modeling, climate change impact assessments, biodiversity hotspot identification, and conservation planning at regional and national scales. Users are encouraged to cite this article when using the dataset and to report downstream applications derived from it.

papers.title: Mapping bacterial bile amidation across the bile salt hydrolase family
papers.abstract: Evaluating enzyme activity and specificity in complex microbiomes is challenging. The recent discovery that bacterial bile salt hydrolases (BSHs) also function as transaminases in the human gut microbiome highlights what remains to be disentangled, even within one of the most extensively studied microbiomes. BSHs as transaminases can conjugate bile acids with bioavailable amines to produce bacterial bile amidates (BBAs). The implications of BBAs for human health are rapidly evolving, but our understanding of which BSHs produce which specific BBAs remains limited. Here, we connect BSH sequence and function by evaluating the transaminase activities of 115 BSHs and reveal distinct amine specificities using molecular networking. Additionally, we identify enzymatically generated BBAs distributed across life-stage, tissue-, and disease-specific human samples by mining public metabolomics repositories, highlighting the previously unrecognized catalytic diversity of BSHs and their potential relevance to human health.

papers.title: FoxO1 and HNF1α cooperatively remodel nucleosome architecture and mechanical stability to activate transcription
papers.abstract: How different transcription factors (TFs) cooperate to bind nucleosomal DNA targets remains unclear. Cryo-EM and force spectroscopy show that the pioneer factor FoxO1 binds superhelical location (SHL) +2 of nucleosomes assembled on the human IGFBP1 promoter, enhances distal DNA unwrapping, destabilizes the histone core, and reduces nucleosome mechanical stability. TF HNF1 binds SHL +5/+7 as a dimer, induces extensive DNA unwrapping without perturbing the histone core, and reshapes nucleosome disassembly dynamics. FoxO1 enhances HNF1 recruitment, and together they stabilize the nucleosome during its mechanically-induced disassembly trajectories. In-cell nucleosome footprinting on active promoters shows that FoxO1 binding enhances unwrapped nucleosomes and subnucleosomes presence, while HNF1 increases stabilized and breathing nucleosomes and reduces the subnucleosome population. Combined, they display an intermediate nucleosome phenotype. Our data leads to a model where FoxO1 destabilizes the nucleosome and enhances HNF1 recruitment, and together they remodel nucleosome architecture both in vitro and in native chromatin.

papers.title: Mixing, competence, and commitment set the stability of cell identity
papers.abstract: Cells maintain their identities in the face of molecular noise, yet can change them rapidly when cued. Here, we treat this tension as a problem in the control of a stochastic system. We represent a cell identity as a set of molecular configurations, or microstates, among which cells undergo stochastic transitions, and measure its stability by the effective rate of commitment to another identity, using a Markov model in which committed cells are removed. Mixing, competence, and commitment provide three channels for tuning this rate. They govern microstate transitions, how commitment is distributed among microstates, and the overall speed of commitment, respectively. Control over the effective commitment rate is shared between commitment and mixing in proportions that always sum to one. Interventions with the same effective commitment rate cannot be told apart by survival alone but, given the microstate transition rates, can be distinguished by the fraction of cells in each microstate or by how quickly cells sorted on permissive microstates commit. When competence varies in time, pulsed commitment signalling commits more cells than sustained signalling of equal dose, by an amount that grows with the depth of that variation, whereas with constant competence pulsing gains nothing in the models we studied. This suggests a possible function for pulsatile signalling, such as that of ERK, which the experiments we propose could test. Finally, reanalysing single-cell imaging of mouse embryonic stem cells leaving naive pluripotency, we estimate that cells take about as long to acquire competence as they then wait to commit, and we specify experiments to identify which channel drives this exit.

papers.title: A compact three-way junction oligonucleotide probe for widefield and super-resolution imaging of RNAs and proteins
papers.abstract: Molecular imaging of RNAs and proteins requires methods that preserve nanoscale organization while enabling large-scale tissue analysis. However, weak or low-abundance targets often need signal amplification, which can increase labeling size, background, or signal spread and compromise super-resolution imaging. Here, we report a compact three-way junction (3WJ) oligonucleotide probe platform for multiscale RNA and protein imaging. The design couples paired target recognition with junction assembly and recruitment of preassembled amplifier complexes, while tunable amplification balances signal strength and labeling size. Using DNA origami and single-molecule localization microscopy, we show enhanced signal while retaining the ability to resolve nanoscale target patterns. The platform improves RNA detection and supports simultaneous RNA-protein super-resolution imaging in cells. It also enhances protein detection in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissues under low-numerical-aperture, large-field imaging conditions. Together, this programmable 3WJ platform enables sensitive RNA and protein detection across scales, supporting super-resolution analysis of molecular organization and large-field tissue mapping.

papers.title: Structure-Function Analysis of an Infantile Rhabdomyosarcoma Fusion-Oncogene Reveals Domain Requirements for Tumorigenesis
papers.abstract: Rhabdomyosarcoma is a pediatric soft-tissue sarcoma that reflects impaired skeletal muscle differentiation. Spindle cell/sclerosing rhabdomyosarcoma is a histological subtype found in children and adults. In children under two, spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma is genetically driven by fusion-oncogenes of transcription factors or co-activators important for skeletal muscle lineage commitment and development. The most common fusion-oncogene in this group is VGLL2::NCOA2, a fusion between vestigial-like family member 2 (VGLL2) and nuclear receptor coactivator 2 (NCOA2). Children with fusion-driven rhabdomyosarcoma are treated with general chemotherapy, surgery, and radiation, which are not specific to the molecular underpinnings, and increase risk of secondary malignancies and premature death. Previously, we showed that VGLL2::NCOA2 is transforming in mouse myoblasts and transgenic zebrafish tumor models. Here, we build on this work by detailing the structure-function relationship of the retained VGLL2::NCOA2 protein domains to define domain requirements and their molecular interactions for tumorigenesis. We created deletion mutants of the VGLL2 vestigial/Tondu (TDU) domain and the NCOA2 activating domains 1 and 2 (AD1 and AD2), and a double mutant lacking the TDU+AD1 domains and assessed their function in a mouse myoblast model. We find that the TDU and AD1 domains support nuclear fusion-oncogene localization, transformation in vitro, and tumorigenesis in a mouse allograft model. Furthermore, transcriptomic analysis demonstrates that the TDU or AD1 mutant VGLL2::NCOA2 drives an upregulation of myogenesis gene sets and supports terminal differentiation. Overall, our results indicate that VGLL2::NCOA2 requires the TDU and AD1 domains for optimal transformation, and that targeting these domains, or their interacting protein partners, represents a therapeutic opportunity.

papers.title: Tissue geometry patterns epidermal stem cell fate in murine interfollicular skin
papers.abstract: How tissues maintain spatial patterns of stem cell renewal and differentiation despite continuous cellular turnover remains poorly understood. Here, we show that microscopic undulations of the dermal-epidermal junction (DEJ) are associated with distinct stem cell behaviors in the mouse epidermis. Using longitudinal intravital imaging and quantitative analysis of cell morphology and lineage dynamics, we find that local DEJ curvature predicts the subsequent fate of daughter cells up to three days before mother cell division. Cells residing in concave valleys preferentially produce proliferating descendants, whereas convex ridges are associated with increased differentiation. These spatial biases are reflected in the expression of stem- and differentiation-associated markers and accumulate into differences in long-term clonal expansion. Remarkably, DEJ geometry remains stable for weeks, persisting across multiple generations of epidermal cells. Moreover, human epidermal equivalents grown on devitalized dermis recapitulate the preferential retention of basal layer cells in valleys, indicating that living dermal cells are not required for this spatial organization. Our findings suggest that stable tissue architecture can pattern stem cell fate probabilities across generations, contributing to functional stem cell heterogeneity.

papers.title: Simulating the dynamics of gene regulatory systems at cellular scale
papers.abstract: The temporal nature of eukaryotic gene expression is the result of a complex, non-linear, dynamical system of regulatory processes. So far, models of such systems trade realism for tractability by using strict simplifying assumptions. These simplified models are often unfaithful to our biological understanding; however, without such simplifications, analytical solutions become more challenging and these dynamical systems must then be studied through simulation. Here, we explore the question of how this complex web of gene regulatory connections can be faithfully simulated for all tens of thousands of genes that usually define a eukaryotic organism. We present a proof-of-principle model and simulator, GeneRegulatorySystems.jl which is based on a biophysical chemical master equation that overcomes three key restrictions. First, it allows an exact stochastic simulation of fully non-linear gene expression dynamics, including feedback control, to parsimoniously capture cause and effect relationships of gene regulation. Further, it includes a general framework for implementing diverse mechanisms of gene control such as protein mediated degradation, RNAi, and protein complex formation. Finally, it scales realistically to tens of thousands of genes. We achieve this by introducing a domain-specific programming language to aid the design of experimental protocols from small-scale, well-studied, scenarios of gene regulation inspired by dynamical systems biology up to large-scale, single cell omics experiments with interventions. In this way, our framework provides a grammar of in silico experimental design that can capture single-cell gene expression dynamics for entire genomes.

papers.title: Scalable Contact-Gated Stochastic Operators and Universal Reduction Laws for Macromolecular Protein Dynamics, Allostery, and Kinetics
papers.abstract: Constructing continuous, thermodynamically reversible reduced equations of motion from atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) that scale from fast-folding miniproteins to multi-domain allosteric enzymes in explicit water remains a foundational problem in computational biophysics. Across 15 molecular systems (890,000 SHA-256-verified frames, 0.89 us cumulative sampling) spanning 13 structurally diverse proteins from Chignolin (d=18) to explicit-solvent Adenylate Kinase (d=426, 40,110 particles) and Maltose-Binding Protein (d=738, 49,215 particles), plus two analytical verification peptides (d=2, 4), we formulate a contact-gated, GENERIC-regularized stochastic operator on the backbone torus T^d. We show that collective slow modes compress sub-linearly across two orders of magnitude in chain length - with spectral participation ratio scaling as PR(d)=1.061 d^0.494 (95% CI [0.332, 0.666], Delta AICc=-18.15) and short-time diffusion rank as r_D^90(d)=0.799 d^0.930 (Delta AICc=-14.39) - whereas cumulative 90% equilibrium variance in large native-basin enzymes transitions to extensive proportionality (10.0% blind extrapolation error vs. 35.7% for small-protein power laws). Consequently, macromolecular tractability above d>200 requires off-diagonal sparsity rather than global PCA truncation alone: universal peptide-plane crankshaft anti-correlation (mean R(psi_i, phi_i+1)=-0.603 +/- 0.054) and sparse 3D tertiary contact gating (mean k_eff=5.97, reaching 99.3% sparsity at d=738) enable a sparse directed acyclic contact-graph Cholesky estimator scaling empirically as O(d^0.92) in time and O(d^1.06) in memory (65.8x memory compression, 99.6x faster than Graphical LASSO, and higher blind held-out log-likelihood +0.303/d vs. dense +0.205/d on MBP). Biophysically, relative solvent-accessible surface area (rSASA_i) unifies dry linear equipartition in protein cores (alpha_core=1.00, 12.33% blind thermal error) with viscosity-coupled loops (alpha_loop=1.28) and peptides (alpha_peptide=1.57); parameter-free kinematic projection reproduces solution NMR Lipari-Szabo S^2 order parameters (mean r_s=+0.483 across four BMRB enzymes, Ubiquitin Pearson r=+0.921) and X-ray B-factors (mean r_s=+0.276); and 13-fold zero-shot Leave-One-Protein-Out transfer predicts unseen protein operators directly from static PDB coordinates (r_s=+0.706, R^2=+0.359 ridge; r_s=+0.721, R^2=+0.410 GBDT). Applied to functional discovery, explicit-solvent apo toroidal operators localize mechanical domain-closure hinges in AdK (PR-AUC=0.348) and MBP (AUROC=0.690 vs. 0.446 ANM), resolve distal Met20 <-> FG catalytic loop coupling in E. coli DHFR (71.6% recovery at 93.2% sparsity) and beta1-beta2 <-> Ile44 routing in Ubiquitin (7.1x amplification) on blind trajectories, and quantify sub-diffusive Mori-Zwanzig reaction-coordinate memory (mean gamma_M=0.593 +/- 0.126). A validation-tuned head-to-head benchmark against Markov State Models, TICA, Smoluchowski diffusion, Elastic Network Models, and unconstrained SDEs across all 13 proteins maps the physical regimes where continuous contact-gated GENERIC operators (lowest Frobenius error 0.288, exact 0.000 spurious entropy vs. median 65.79 kB/ns/d, IQR 53.76-104.66, mean 346.17) and discrete or harmonic baselines each excel.

papers.title: irAEGIS: Pathway-guided interpretable prediction of immune-related adverse events
papers.abstract: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) are major complications of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy and remain difficult to predict prior to treatment initiation. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) provides a unique opportunity to characterize immune states associated with future irAE development. However, translating single-cell measurements into accurate and biologically interpretable patient-level risk predictions remains challenging. Existing approaches typically aggregate cellular profiles into patient-level summaries, thereby obscuring cell type specific signals, or rely on complex deep-learning architectures that offer limited insight into the biological pathways and mechanisms underlying their predictions. Here, we present irAEGIS, a pathway-guided interpretable model for predicting irAE risk from pre-treatment scRNA-seq data. irAEGIS incorporates prior biological knowledge through gene set constrained representation learning, aggregates pathway activities within individual cell types, and integrates cell type specific risk signals through a hierarchical prediction framework. This design enables predictions to be decomposed into contributions from individual cell types, pathways, and genes, providing interpretable explanations across multiple biological resolutions. Across simulated datasets and independent pre-treatment ICI cohorts, irAEGIS consistently outperformed seven existing methods. Beyond predictive performance, irAEGIS identified biologically coherent immune programs associated with irAE risk. In non-small cell lung cancer, irAEGIS highlighted neutrophil-associated inflammatory pathways linked to future irAE development, whereas in melanoma, it identified apoptotic and immune activation pathways in CD8+ NKT-like cells associated with severe irAEs. These findings were independently supported by pathway enrichment, cell-cell communication, and trajectory analyses. Together, irAEGIS provides a biologically informed and interpretable model for linking single-cell immune states to patient outcomes, enabling both accurate risk prediction and mechanistic insight into immune-related adverse events. More broadly, irAEGIS establishes a general strategy for interpretable phenotype prediction and biological discovery from single-cell transcriptomic data.

papers.title: Human senataxin uses distinct peripheral elements to unwind R-loops and act on RNA polymerase II
papers.abstract: Persistent R-loops and paused or stalled RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) elongation complexes can threaten genome stability. Senataxin (SETX) contributes to R-loop resolution and RNAPII regulation, but their intimate connection during transcription makes the individual contributions of these activities difficult to distinguish in cells. To determine whether these activities rely on the same molecular features, we investigated the structure and biochemical properties of the SETX helicase domain (SETX-HD). Cryo-EM defines the conserved helicase core and RNA-binding channel of SETX-HD, while biochemical analyses identify distinct roles for two peripheral elements: a previously uncharacterised C-terminal RNA-binding domain (CT-RBD) and the prong subdomain. In reconstituted mammalian transcription assays, SETX-HD promotes passage beyond a defined RNAPII pause and elongation-complex dissociation on the same template. The CT-RBD stabilises RNA engagement and is required for efficient R-loop unwinding, whereas its deletion preserves both RNAPII-associated activities. Conversely, replacing the native SETX prong with its fungal Sen1 counterpart preserves R-loop unwinding but impairs both RNAPII outcomes. These reciprocal separation-of-function effects establish that a common SETX-HD RNA-translocation core depends on distinct peripheral elements for R-loop unwinding and action on mammalian RNAPII. This separation provides a direct route to determine how these activities contribute to SETX function in cells.

papers.title: A comparative analysis of BrdU and EdU genotoxicity shows that trypanosomatids exhibit unique responses to the presence of these thymidine analogs in their DNA
papers.abstract: The thymidine analogs 5-bromo-2'-deoxyuridine (BrdU) and 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine (EdU) are widely used to monitor DNA synthesis. Although studies have reported EdU toxicity in certain cell types, no reports to date describe genotoxic effects associated with BrdU/EdU use in trypanosomatids, etiological agents of neglected tropical diseases. This lack of studies raises two possibilities: either these nucleotides are not toxic to these parasites, or the observed genotoxicity was not relevant under the experimental conditions used. Here, we assessed the potential toxicity of BrdU and EdU across three pathogenic trypanosomatids: Trypanosoma cruzi, Trypanosoma brucei, and Leishmania major. Our findings show that EdU has greater genotoxic potential than BrdU. Nevertheless, trypanosomatids respond markedly differently to DNA alterations caused by this analog: T. cruzi cells stop replicating and accumulate in S phase, T. brucei tolerates the DNA lesions generated, while part of the L. major population appears to display an altruistic behavior that benefits the survivors. Furthermore, in silico assays suggest that, once incorporated into DNA, the ethynyl group increases the EdU's polarity, thereby altering DNA structure more strongly than BrdU does after the first round of DNA replication. Together, our findings suggest that using thymidine analogs in trypanosomatids should be preceded by rigorous preliminary analysis, especially when using EdU. Otherwise, the data may be biased by a BrdU/EdU-triggered DNA damage response. We believe this study may serve as an atlas to guide the initial selection of thymidine analog concentrations and exposure periods.

papers.title: Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models
papers.abstract: Recent advances in protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction frameworks have the potential to accelerate computational drug discovery. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond their training sets. Mutation-dependent drug responses present a challenge to these methods because there are often large effects from relatively small perturbations. Here, we systematically benchmark diverse mutational effect and drug-target affinity prediction models using deep mutational scanning datasets spanning 11 inhibitor conditions for the MET kinase domain. Across both mutational effect prediction and drug-target affinity tasks, current AI models produce largely ligand-invariant predictions despite experimentally distinct inhibitor-dependent fitness landscapes. Ligand-aware geometric models, including LigandMPNN and LASErMPNN, partially recover experimentally validated resistance-associated hotspots, highlighting the importance of explicitly modeling protein-ligand interactions and local structural flexibility. In contrast, deep learning affinity prediction models underestimate mutation-induced changes in binding affinity. This deficiency likely reflects mutation-invariant structural priors derived from co-folded structure prediction frameworks and the absence of mutation-conditioned supervision in current affinity datasets. Finally, we further extended our analysis to several kinase-inhibitor deep mutational scanning datasets and confirm the overall trends. Our findings suggest that a primary limitation in improving performance on this task lies in the scarcity of mutation-conditioned protein-ligand training data rather than model architecture alone.

papers.title: FoXSight: Facilitating Computational Hit Identification in Crystallographic Fragment Screening Experiments
papers.abstract: X-ray crystallographic fragment screening reveals how small molecules bind to proteins, providing important starting points for drug design. Identifying these weak binding events remains difficult when electron density signals are noisy, partially occupied or obscured by solvent, and campaigns may comprise thousands of datasets. Here, we present FoXSight, a computational method for hit identification in crystallographic compound screening. FoXSight applies Difference-of-Gaussian (DoG) filtering to multi-reference subtraction maps to detect recurring, target-specific density features associated with bound ligands. Its output maps remain visually interpretable and support subsequent ligand modeling. We evaluated FoXSight on in-house and public datasets spanning seven protein targets, comparing its maps with PanDDA where suitable comparison data were available. FoXSight was successfully used as the primary hit identification tool in a challenging crystallographic fragment screening campaign for human Cathepsin L, where the output of established methods was impractical to inspect systematically.

papers.title: Distinct medial septal GABAergic pathways differentially regulate spatial memory and network activity
papers.abstract: Septal GABAergic projection neurons form distinct pathways to subregions of the hippocampal formation, including the hippocampus proper and the medial and lateral entorhinal cortices. Parvalbumin (PV+) and calbindin expressing (CB+) projections target different types of interneurons and thereby differentially regulate neuronal activity in the downstream area. Consistent with the idea of dissociable functional roles, inhibition of septal PV+ neurons impairs reference memory whereas inhibition of septal CB+ neurons impairs both reference and working memory. Here, we show that these functions are differentially supported by specific projection pathways: PV+ projections to the dorsal hippocampus and medial entorhinal cortex (MEC) support reference memory, whereas CB+ projections to the MEC support both reference and working memory. At the network level, septal PV+, but not CB+, neurons regulate theta oscillations. Together, these findings further define the roles of septal PV+ and CB+ pathways in orchestrating network activity and supporting specific forms of memory.

papers.title: Synthetic reaction-diffusion patterning in mammalian cells
papers.abstract: During development, periodic patterns arise through reaction-diffusion (RD) circuits involving local activation and long-range inhibition (LALI). Natural systems are complex, typically entangling regulation and transport in the same morphogens.
