It remains unclear what minimal circuits are sufficient for LALI patterning in mammalian cells, and whether they can be implemented in a modular fashion, allowing independent control of regulation and transport. Here, we designed synthetic LALI circuits using three natural and synthetic signaling systems, BMP, Activin, and the SNIPR pathway, and showed that they generate spatial patterns with distinct characteristic spatial scales. Model-guided design allowed flexible morphogen reassignment, with BMP4 acting as either short-range activator or long-range inhibitor. Gene expression noise degraded long-range order but preserved the dominant local spatial scale. Together, these results provide a modular, extensible synthetic framework for engineered patterning in mammalian cells.

papers.title: Interactive effects of Nutrient Enrichment and Water Scarcity on Floral signaling and visitation
papers.abstract: - Floral traits remain an underexplored frontier in global change biology compared to their vegetative counterparts. As anthropogenic change involves simultaneous shifts in resource availability, focusing on isolated stressors may overlook complex biological responses. Characterizing the interactive effects of these stressors is therefore crucial to move beyond additive models and accurately predict the stability of pollination services in a transforming world. - The individual and interactive effects of nutrient enrichment and water scarcity were investigated on the floral traits and pollinator visitation rates of five grassland species. - While species identity emerged as the dominant driver of overall trait variation, across-species responses were also present. Among the abiotic drivers, nutrient enrichment emerged as the primary influence, significantly increasing flower number and achromatic contrast while decreasing floral area, chromatic contrast and chroma. Conversely, water scarcity primarily reduced plant height and increased floral chroma and hue. The two factors also often interacted in their effects. The changes in visual traits scaled up to changes in pollinator visitation, but the specific effects were largely species-specific. - Ultimately, our findings demonstrate that anthropogenic stressors act in divergent ways to reshape floral phenotypes and pollinator visitation, advancing our understanding of plant-pollinator interactions under compounding global pressures.

papers.title: Characterizing nascent readthrough transcripts in human cells
papers.abstract: Termination of transcription by RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) is critical to appropriately define transcriptome and proteome identity; yet mechanisms of termination regulation are incompletely understood. Current models suggest critical roles for the exonuclease XRN2, which is posited to "torpedo" out RNAPII after degrading uncapped and RNAPII-tethered nascent transcripts and posit an allosteric model wherein elongating RNAPII loses its processivity downstream of the transcription end site (TES) via unknown mechanisms. Here, we used nascent RNA Bru-seq to interrogate transcription termination across 16 human cell lines of distinct lineages, as part of the ENCODE 4 project, to identify key regulatory modes. We find that > 75% of protein-coding genes engage in readthrough transcription under homeostatic conditions. Exposing human cells to oxidative stress or hyperosmotic conditions or splicing inhibitors cause an increase in readthrough transcripts globally. Using an auxin-inducible degradation approach we find that depletion of BRD4, MED14 or XRN2 increases the extent and pervasiveness of readthrough transcripts while depletion of SUPT16H results in shorter readthrough transcripts. Our study provides a comprehensive view of homeostatic readthrough transcripts in human cells and delineates key components regulating transcription termination.

papers.title: An RNA-centric atlas of human cell cycle regulation
papers.abstract: Cell cycle progression is orchestrated by protein networks coordinating cell growth and division, yet the role of RNA-mediated mechanisms remains underexplored. Here, we define an RNA-centric landscape of human cell cycle control using palbociclib-synchronised normal diploid cells, profiling long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), transposable elements (TEs), alternative splicing (AS), and RNA-binding proteins (RBPs). We identify 104 cell cycle-regulated lncRNAs and validate lncRNA ENSG00000230615, whose perturbation alters cell cycle progression and downregulates neighbouring KLF17. Across the transcriptome, 297 TE loci exhibit differential expression dynamics during the cell cycle, with Alu elements upregulated during the G1-to-S transition. Cell-cycle-dependent AS changes affect 598 genes, with alternative 5' splice sites showing the largest shift in usage at the G1-to-S transition. Furthermore, we show that cytokinesis proteins act as non-canonical RBPs with RNA-dependent stability. This study provides a comprehensive resource on RNA-based cell cycle control and highlights an underappreciated layer of regulation mediated by RNA mechanisms.

papers.title: Stop-Flow Lithography Using Hydrodynamic Flow Resistance Regulation and Hydraulic Compliance Minimization for Size-Tunable Anisotropic Multilayered Microparticles Fabrication
papers.abstract: Stop-flow lithography (SFL) enables the fabrication of microparticles with designed geometries and material compositions, but its performance relies on rapid flow stopping, which remains particularly challenging in multi-inlet systems with high hydrodynamic flow resistance and hydraulic compliance. Here, we develop a pneumatic-controlled SFL platform with a framework based on flow resistance regulation and hydraulic compliance minimization for fabricating size-tunable anisotropic multilayered microparticles. Our analysis indicates that flow-stopping behavior is governed by the release of extra fluid volume stored in the system due to hydraulic compliance, which arises from the deformation of microfluidic components and the compressibility of the fluid within them. Through numerical modeling and analysis, we identify deformation in the PDMS inlet port region as the dominant contributor to the stored extra fluid volume. By regulating the flow resistance of the tubing relative to that of the outlet channel, the stored extra fluid volume can be preferentially released forward through the outlet or backward through the inlet tubing, enabling rapid flow stopping across configurations with 500, 250, and 100 m outlets. Furthermore, by supporting the PDMS membrane beneath the inlet region with a rigid glass substrate and reducing its dimensions, the hydraulic compliance and consequently the stored extra fluid volume are significantly reduced. With these strategies, microparticles with well-defined boundaries can be fabricated at short, flow-stopping, delay times, and the flow profiles obtained in multi-inlet systems can be preserved during flow stopping and transferred into particle patterns.

papers.title: Combined elevated temperature and CO2 alter Wolbachia abundance and host fitness but not cytoplasmic incompatibility in a stored-product pest
papers.abstract: Coinfecting endosymbiont strains may respond differently to environmental change, with consequences for host performance and reproductive incompatibility. We investigated an isofemale line of Callosobruchus chinensis coinfected with the cytoplasmic incompatibility (CI)-inducing Wolbachia strains wBruCon (Con) and wBruOri (Ori), together with derived Con-only and uninfected sublines. Beetles were maintained under control conditions (30{degrees}C, ~500 ppm CO2) or under combined elevated temperature and CO2 (32{degrees}C, ~1000 ppm CO2; eT&CO2). In coinfected adults, Ori relative abundance declined under eT&CO2, whereas Con abundance increased in females. Con responses also depended on host sex and infection status, with singly infected males showing particularly high abundance under control conditions. However, CI expression remained stable across environmental conditions. Coinfected females laid fewer eggs than uninfected females, whereas host life-history responses to eT&CO2 varied among traits and generations. eT&CO2 accelerated development and reduced adult longevity, while reduced egg-adult survival emerged in the F2 generation. It also reduced F1 fecundity but only in the uninfected subline. Strong and partial CI associated with Con and Ori, respectively, remained evident under both environmental conditions. Equilibrium analyses incorporating relative fecundity, CI intensity, and maternal transmission suggested lower infection persistence under eT&CO2 in the F1 generation but higher persistence in the F2 generation. Sensitivity analysis suggested contribution of improved relative fecundity of infected females in the latter. Overall, the two Wolbachia strains exhibited contrasting, sex-dependent abundance responses to eT&CO2, while CI expression remained stable. These findings suggest that climate change may alter symbiont infection dynamics in economically important pests, with potential implications for symbiont-mediated traits, including pesticide resistance.

papers.title: Organelle Aging Predicts Human Disease
papers.abstract: Aging affects cellular organelles differently, but whether subcellular aging predicts human disease remains unknown. Here, we integrated organelle-enriched proteins in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid proteomes from 61,931 individuals to model aging of 10 organelles across the human lifespan. Organelle aging was heterogeneous with lysosomes, plasma membranes, and Golgi compartments accelerating rapidly after age 60. Individuals with four or more prematurely aged compartments exhibited up to 22-fold higher kidney disease risk and up to 8-fold higher mortality risk. Major diseases are characterized by distinct organelle aging signatures and disease risk increased with the number of accelerated organelles. APOE-{varepsilon}4 dosage was associated with lysosomal and mitochondrial aging and reduced PDP1 levels, implicating altered energy metabolism. Decomposition of organelle signature coefficients into biological programs further showed that diseases are associated with distinct subcellular patterns. These findings establish organelle-resolved aging as a measurable dimension of human biology, revealing subcellular mechanisms underlying disease susceptibility and resilience.

papers.title: IDENTIFICATION OF CANDIDATE GENES UNDERLYING A NOVEL QTL FOR ROOT LENGTH AND DIAMETER IN BARLEY IN RESPONSE TO SALINITY
papers.abstract: Salinity is a major agricultural problem that decreases growth and yield of crops and is expected to worsen with climate change. Improving salt tolerance through breeding could be facilitated by identification of genetic loci and candidate genes affecting root traits that enhance water and nutrient uptake while limiting accumulation of toxic ions. In this study, a Clipper x Sahara 3771 doubled haploid (DH) barley mapping population was screened for root growth responses to saline conditions in a controlled environment. Quantitative trait loci (QTLs) were mapped for root traits including seminal root length, root diameter and root potassium. Major QTLs affecting seminal root length and average root diameter were detected in the distal region of the short arm of chromosome 2H, indicating that this region is a key determinant of root architecture under both control and saline conditions. The linkage map was improved by using newly designed assays for SNPs on chromosome 2H and a 2.5-Mb interval was identified for investigation of candidate genes. Bulked segregant RNA sequencing (BSR-Seq) of contrasting salt-tolerant and salt-sensitive DH lines identified differentially expressed genes associated with root growth maintenance and ion homeostasis in root tips. These findings identify specific region on chromosome 2H as a major genomic region affecting barley root architecture, especially under saline conditions, and identify differentially expressed candidate genes in that region.

papers.title: Endogenous PROM1 activation redistributes liver cancer cells along a preexisting differentiation axis
papers.abstract: CD133 is widely used as a marker of stem-like cells in hepatocellular carcinoma, yet its functional contribution remains incompletely defined. In PLC/PRF/5 cells, acute CRISPR activation of endogenous PROM1 suppresses hepatic programs, whereas PROM1 knockdown elicits an opposing hepatocyte-identity response, together defining a PROM1-responsive transcriptional axis. Single-cell profiling shows that this axis is preexisting and tracks endogenous PROM1 heterogeneity, separating a hepatocyte-like, PROM1-low compartment from a PROM1-enriched, less hepatocyte-like compartment. Sustained PROM1 activation reduces the hepatocyte-like compartment and shifts the population toward intermediate positions along this axis. Related transcriptional patterns are detectable in an independent HuH-7 dataset and a human HCC case. Endogenous ALFA tagging identifies candidate CD133-associated proteins. Together, these findings support CD133 as an active contributor to tumor-cell state redistribution, extending its role beyond a mere marker of stem-like populations.

papers.title: A compact motif vocabulary is differentially interpreted across human cell types
papers.abstract: How a common genome generates diverse human cell types may depend less on distinct cis-regulatory vocabularies than on context-dependent use of a shared one. We have developed CNN-CR, an interpretable neural network that learns regulatory motifs while predicting gene expression across 116 human biosamples. Promoter regulation proves highly compressible: dozens of recurrent motif families retain most of the predictive information of much larger cell-type-specific vocabularies and generalize to cellular contexts excluded from their discovery. These motifs are conserved at their binding sites and enriched at fine-mapped regulatory variants. Cellular context acts at two levels: chromatin state gates which motif instances are available for regulatory use, whereas reader identity determines how accessible motifs are interpreted. ChIP-seq data reveal frequent shifts in reader occupancy across cell types, and genome-scale perturbations support corresponding context-dependent reader functions. Thus, regulatory diversity can emerge through differential access to and interpretation of a compact shared DNA vocabulary.

papers.title: Apolipoprotein E4 Exacerbates Aβ Oligomer-Induced Synaptotoxicity through Promoting Autophagic Degradation of Glutathione Peroxidase 4
papers.abstract: Extensive synaptic loss and progressive neurodegeneration are defining pathological hallmarks of Alzheimer's disease (AD), primarily driven by soluble A{beta} oligomers and neurofibrillary tangles. The apolipoprotein E4 (APOE4) isoform further aggravates these pathological cascades, yet the precise molecular mechanisms underlying AD pathogenesis remain poorly elucidated. Store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) deficiency in neurons has been proven to exert a detrimental effect on dendritic spine integrity and function. Herein, we investigated whether SOCE dysregulation contributes to A{beta}O-induced synaptotoxicity and how APOE4 modulates this pathological process. In primary neuronal cultures, co-treatment with A{beta}O and APOE4 markedly reduced synapse density and impaired dendritic arbor complexity, compared with A{beta}O treatments combined with APOE3 or APOE2 isoforms. Consistently, neurons exposed to A{beta}O plus APOE4 exhibited significantly lower SOCE amplitudes than those treated with A{beta}O and APOE3. In line with SOCE suppression, the A{beta}O/APOE4 combination specifically downregulated stromal interaction molecule 1 (STIM1) protein expression, with no observable change in STIM2 levels. Mechanistically, A{beta}O/APOE4-mediated STIM1 reduction was dependent on p62-selective autophagic degradation. Notably, exogenous STIM1 overexpression effectively rescued the deficits in dendritic arbor complexity. Furthermore, STIM1 downregulation induced by A{beta}O and APOE4 initiated the autophagic degradation of glutathione peroxidase 4 (Gpx4). This autophagy activation was attributed to decreased Bcl2 expression and occurs independently of STING accumulation. Subsequent Gpx4 insufficiency further triggered excessive accumulation of reactive oxygen species and disrupted mitochondrial cristae morphology in neurons. Collectively, our findings uncover a previously unrecognized mechanism whereby APOE4 exacerbates A{beta}O-induced synaptotoxicity. Specifically, the combination facilitates p62-mediated selective autophagic degradation of STIM1, which suppresses Bcl2 expression and ultimately promotes robust Gpx4 autophagic degradation, driving neuronal synaptic damage.

papers.title: Yap is a key regulator of tracheoesophageal separation during foregut development
papers.abstract: Separation of the anterior foregut into the esophagus and trachea involves dynamic cellular movement that requires the coordinated activity of multiple signaling pathways and transcription factors. Disruption of this process can result in esophageal atresia (EA) with or without tracheoesophageal fistula (TEF), manifesting in five major anatomical types (Types A-E). Here, we examine the role of the Hippo pathway effector Yes-associated protein (Yap) in foregut separation. Conditional deletion of Yap in the dorsal and medial portions of the anterior foregut endoderm leads to the formation of Type A EA/TEF, isolated EA. This separation defect only occurs in Sox2-CreER;Yaploxp/loxp but not in Shh-Cre;Yaploxp/loxp mutants. Our findings further reveal that Yap mutants exhibit a reduction in Sox2+ esophageal progenitor cells accompanied by the absence of the middle esophageal segment. Combined deletion of Yap and Taz (transcriptional coactivator with PDZ-binding motif) also results in isolated EA accompanied by severe craniofacial abnormalities. Therefore, loss of Yap causes a distinct Type A EA/TEF, which differs from existing mouse models of EA/TEF that predominantly exhibit the Type C phenotype. Our findings also suggest that epithelial cells at the dorsal-ventral boundary play a critical role in tracheoesophageal separation.

papers.title: SMARCA4 MUTATIONS PROMOTE CHEMOTHERAPY RESISTANCE IN T-ACUTE LYMPHOBLASTIC LEUKEMIA THROUGH ALTERED CHROMATIN REMODELING AT AP1-ASSOCIATED REGULATORY REGIONS
papers.abstract: Chromatin remodelers play a critical role in orchestrating chemotherapy responses in cancer cells. Components of the SWI/SNF complex are frequently mutated across cancer types, with the ATPase subunit SMARCA4 among the most commonly altered. In T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL), however, SMARCA4 mutations are rare at diagnosis but enriched in relapse samples, suggesting a potential role in therapy resistance. Using isogenic T-ALL cell lines with or without SMARCA4 mutations, we show that mutant SMARCA4 confers resistance to a broad range of chemotherapeutic agents. By combining ATAC-seq and RNA-seq, we demonstrate that SMARCA4-mutant cells display an attenuated transcriptional response to chemotherapy accompanied by impaired remodeling of AP-1-associated regulatory regions linked to stress response. These cells downregulate stress-related genes while maintaining expression programs associated with cellular fitness. Pharmacological inhibition of AP-1 phenocopies this response, further supporting a functional link between SWI/SNF-mediated remodeling at AP-1-associated regulatory regions, AP-1 activity, and chemotherapy sensitivity. Together, our findings indicate that SWI/SNF-mediated remodeling of these regions contributes to an effective chemotherapy-induced stress response, and that its failure provides T-ALL cells with a survival

papers.title: An Efficient Microfluidic Platform for Organ-Specific CyclicMultiaxial Loading and Differentiation of Progenitor Cells
papers.abstract: Mechanical loading is a fundamental regulator of tissue development, maturation, and function, yet existing in vitro systems predominantly apply uniaxial load/strain to cell-laden hydrogels, limiting their ability to reproduce physiologically relevant multiaxial on-chip tissue mechanics. Here, we present an engineered system to apply controlled multiaxial mechanical loading to real scaffolds with undifferentiated cells. The system enables programmable cyclic stretching and relaxation at the cell scaffold level and is compatible with both cell-laden native scaffold and engineered soft tissues. We have quantified the strain field experienced by the tissue with distinct mechanical loading periods using computation simulations and validated these with systematic experiments, demonstrating reproducible and various organ-relevant multiaxial strain profiles. As proof of concept, we applied the approach to human cardiac tissues, where cyclic multiaxial mechanical loading of mononuclear cells laden native tissue scaffold promoted cardiac structural organization and supports the emergence of spontaneous contractile activity. This approach provides a generalizable method for reproducing physiologically relevant tissue mechanics in vitro and enables systematic investigation of mechano-regulation across a plethora of human tissues.

papers.title: Molecular basis of Cyclin B1-CDK1 recruitment by MAD1
papers.abstract: The interaction between Cyclin B1-CDK1 and MAD1 recruits kinase activity to the nuclear pore complex and kinetochore corona to sustain spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC) signaling. Here, we characterize a short linear motif (SLiM) within MAD1 that mediates its interaction with Cyclin B1. This SLiM peptide is specific for B-type cyclins and lacks the canonical "RxL" cyclin-binding consensus sequence, suggesting a distinct mode of cyclin recognition. Using a combination of deep mutational scanning, structural analysis by cryogenic electron microscopy, and binding affinity measurements, we define the molecular basis of the Cyclin B1-MAD1 interaction. These approaches reveal that a short MAD1 peptide binds as an -helix to the RxL-binding hydrophobic patch of Cyclin B1. The interaction employs hydrophobic contacts that overlap with those used by canonical RxL motifs, but is distinguished by additional contacts and sequence features that confer preferential recognition by B-type cyclins while excluding other cyclin types. We also show that the MAD1 motif is sufficient to confer B-type cyclin-specific substrate phosphorylation in mitotic cells. Together, these findings reveal a non-canonical, B-type cyclin-specific helical binding mode that ensures selective Cyclin B1-CDK1 recruitment at two critical stages of SAC signaling, and suggest potential strategies for selective therapeutic targeting of this interaction.

papers.title: Development and cross-cohort evaluation of a multimodal deep-learning model for ER, PR and HER2 status classification in breast cancer
papers.abstract: Background. Estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR) and HER2 status guide systemic treatment in breast cancer. Multimodal models are rarely benchmarked against key biomarker molecular baselines or evaluated for cross-cohort calibration. We assessed incremental value, dependence on label-proximal HER2 transcripts, and transport of discrimination and calibration. Methods. A model combining whole-slide images, transcriptomes, age and stage was developed in TCGA-BRCA (1051 patients; ER/PR/HER2 analysis sets: 1001/998/1006) and evaluated in CPTAC-BRCA (120 patients; 118/113/95). CPTAC had been observed during earlier development and included 13 HER2-positive cases. Analyses included paired model comparisons, transcript removal, alternative loss functions and recalibration. Internal discrimination used pooled out-of-fold predictions; external discrimination used fold-mean estimates, with ensemble calibration reported separately. Internal calibration and macro-AUC uncertainty were interpreted as exploratory. Results. Internal AUCs were 0.943 for ER, 0.901 for PR, and 0.860 for HER2; external AUCs were 0.952, 0.937, and 0.918, respectively. External macro-AUC was 0.936 for the multimodal model and 0.957 for logistic regression using ESR1, PGR, and ERBB2 (difference -0.021). Removal of the extended 29-transcript 17q12-q21 region changed HER2 AUC by -0.035 [-0.058 to -0.013] (95% CI) internally and by -0.042 [-0.089 to -0.007] externally relative to the baseline multimodal model. For external 15-model ensemble predictions, recalibrated HER2 expected calibration error (ECE) was 0.236, exceeding the ECE reference ceiling of 0.125, while calibration-in-the-large was -1.657 [-2.373 to -1.023] (profile-likelihood 95% CI), indicating systematic overprediction. ER and PR also showed overprediction. In paired fold-mean comparisons, HER2 ECE and Brier score favoured the three-transcript model (ESR1, PGR, and ERBB2). Conclusions. A multimodal deep-learning model achieved high discrimination across cohorts but did not demonstrate clear incremental value over a parsimonious three-transcript baseline, while cross-cohort calibration remained a substantial challenge. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating incremental value, calibration, and clinical utility alongside discrimination when assessing AI-based prediction models for medical use.

papers.title: Structural Basis for Inhibition of Human Anion Transporter SLC26A6/PAT-1
papers.abstract: PAT-1, encoded by the gene SLC26A6, is an exchanger of small organic and inorganic anions including oxalate and chloride in the kidney and the intestines. PAT-1 dysfunction is implicated in nephrolithiasis and hyperoxaluria, and its modulation is a potential therapeutic strategy to treat cystic fibrosis. PAT-1 has two small molecule inhibitors: DIDS, a non-specific anion exchanger inhibitor; and PAT1inh-B01 which is highly specific to PAT-1. In this study, we report high-resolution cryo-electron microscopy structures of the human PAT-1 homodimer in complex with these inhibitors to reveal their different inhibition mechanisms. These structures also uncover the complex interactions between the transmembrane, STAS and N-terminal domains, with implications on its ion exchange function. Hence, this study provides mechanistic insight into PAT-1 molecular function and inhibition, and contributes to our understanding of SLC26 transport mechanisms.

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Protein Language Models for Dual-Target Antimicrobial Peptide Discovery Under Strict Homology Constraints
papers.abstract: The worldwide escalation of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a severe challenge to modern public health, necessitating novel classes of therapeutic agents. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) represent highly promising alternatives to small-molecule antibiotics due to their co-evolutionary resilience and rapid membrane disruption dynamics. However, translating computational AMP leads into clinical drug candidates remains bottlenecked by off-target cytotoxicity, predominantly hemolytic activity against mammalian erythrocytes. Although pretrained foundational protein language models (PLMs) have rapidly advanced molecular property prediction, current architectures frequently isolate antibacterial potency and cytotoxicity into disconnected single-task pipelines or succumb to catastrophic performance drops under strict homology-controlled evaluations. Recently, the Quantitative Mapping of Antimicrobial Peptides (QMAP) benchmark proposed that frozen PLM embeddings show weak linearly accessible features for hemolytic activity (HC50) resulting in poor rank correlation ({rho} < 0.25) on out-of-distribution sequence splits. In this work, we introduce an end-to-end multi-task parameter-efficient transfer learning framework designed to simultaneously optimize antibacterial potency and minimize mammalian cytotoxicity without sequence leakage. Built upon ESM-2 (150M), our architecture incorporates Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) into self-attention projections, fine-tuning approx 0.70% of model weights. To restore gradient interference originating from disparate membrane lysis mechanisms, we implement an adaptive multi-task loss guided by Kendall homoscedastic uncertainty weighting. Evaluated across predefined QMAP benchmark splits enforcing a 60% maximal sequence identity threshold, our joint architecture remarkably outperforms conventional linear probes, tree-based regressors, and frozen foundational models. The framework achieves an E. coli potency rank correlation of {rho} = 0.6132 (r = 0.6816) and successfully elevates hemolytic toxicity correlation to {rho} = 0.5374 (r = 0.5541). To establish real world utility, we deploy the optimized joint network to screen a curated in silico library of 749 de-novo designed peptides, successfully isolating selective cationic-amphipathic candidates possessing Therapeutic Indices (TI = HC50/MIC) up to 144.03 while effectively deprioritizing broadly lytic motifs (TI < 2.0). These findings demonstrate that parameter-efficient adaptation unlocks fine-grained bioactive structural semantics in foundational PLMs, providing an accurate, scalable framework for therapeutic peptide engineering.

papers.title: A respiratory microdomain links ubiquinone biosynthesis to succinate dehydrogenase in an apicomplexan mitochondrion lacking Complex I
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial complex I (CI) is a major entry point for NADH-derived electrons and an important site of redox regulation in most eukaryotes. However, apicomplexan parasites, including Toxoplasma gondii, lack CI, raising a fundamental question of how mitochondrial respiration is organized in these parasites. Here, we identify a parasite-specific mitochondrial microdomain that physically and functionally couples ubiquinone (UQ) biosynthesis to succinate dehydrogenase (SDH). Using proximity labeling, membrane-based yeast two-hybrid analyses, reciprocal co-immunoprecipitations, and blue native PAGE, we show that UQ biosynthesis proteins associate with parasite-specific SDH subunits and co-migrate as a high-molecular-weight assembly. Knockdown of TgCoq4, a component of the UQ biosynthesis pathway, reduced SDH activity, and adding exogenous UQ to the assay did not restore it, indicating that UQ availability is not sufficient for efficient succinate oxidation. FCCP stimulates malate- and TMPD/ascorbate-supported respiration to maximal capacity but fails to do so with succinate as the substrate. This result, combined with reactive oxygen species (ROS) data, suggests that succinate causes over-reduction of the UQ pool, limiting further electron flow. We also find that CIII associates with the UQ synthesis machinery, suggesting a larger protein assembly. Together, these findings reveal that UQ biosynthesis and electron transport are physically and functionally integrated in T. gondii, defining a previously unrecognized organization of mitochondrial respiration in an organism lacking CI.

papers.title: A cytotoxicity dataset for data-driven design of ionizable lipid nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are widely used to deliver nucleic acid therapeutics, but the design of safe LNPs remains challenging due to the complex activity relationships among structure, composition, and physicochemical properties. Here, we present a curated dataset, the Lipid Nanoparticle Cytotoxicity Database (LNPCD), which aggregates 1,413 LNP cytotoxicity measurements across 1,288 unique ionizable lipids drawn from 11 high-throughput combinatorial studies. Lipid structures were generated computationally from the published libraries and manually verified against the original publications. Each record pairs a machine-readable SMILES representation of the ionizable lipid with its measured viability endpoint and the associated experimental descriptors, including cell line, dose, and cargo type. The dataset provides a traceable resource for examining how ionizable lipid structure and experimental conditions relate to in vitro cell viability, and for developing and evaluating computational models of lipid nanoparticle cytotoxicity.

papers.title: IER3-N-cadherin axis contributes to apoptosis resistance in dermal fibroblasts under profibrotic conditions
papers.abstract: Background: Persistent activation and resistance to apoptosis of dermal fibroblasts contribute to pathological skin fibrosis. Immediate early response 3 (IER3) is a stress-responsive protein involved in cell survival, but its role in cutaneous fibrosis remains unclear. We investigated the functional significance of IER3 in dermal fibroblasts and its potential contribution to fibrosis. Methods: IER3 expression was examined in skin samples from patients with systemic sclerosis, keloids, and hypertrophic scars. Primary human dermal fibroblasts were stimulated with transforming growth factor-{beta}1 (TGF-{beta}1). RNA sequencing, siRNA-mediated gene silencing, quantitative PCR, and flow cytometric apoptosis assays were performed to investigate the downstream mechanisms and functional consequences of IER3 expression. Results: IER3 expression was increased in dermal fibroblasts within fibrotic skin lesions and was induced by TGF-{beta}1 independently of SMAD3 and MEK/ERK signaling. Transcriptomic analysis identified CDH2, encoding N-cadherin, as a downstream target of IER3. Moreover, TGF-{beta}1 induced CDH2 expression in a SMAD3 phosphorylation-dependent manner. IER3 knockdown attenuated TGF-{beta}1-induced CDH2 expression, whereas CDH2 knockdown did not affect IER3 expression. Furthermore, CDH2 knockdown enhanced staurosporine-induced apoptosis in TGF-{beta}1-stimulated fibroblasts, accompanied by a shift in apoptosis-related gene expression toward a pro-apoptotic profile. Conclusion: Our findings identify a previously unrecognized IER3-N-cadherin regulatory axis that may promote dermal fibroblast survival by suppressing apoptosis under profibrotic conditions. Targeting this pathway may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for persistent skin fibrosis.

papers.title: Differential sensing with imprinted and non-imprinted organic electrochemical transistors reduces calibration drift in wearable sweat cortisol sensors
papers.abstract: The output of a wearable cortisol sensor drifts over days for reasons unrelated to cortisol, so a calibration made on the first day soon stops being valid. In our differential organic electrochemical transistor, a PEDOT:PSS transistor coated with a molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) for cortisol is paired with one coated with a non-imprinted polymer (NIP) of the same composition, and the NIP response is subtracted. Over four calibrations in artificial sweat across 14 days, the response of the MIP alone shifted by 15% to 22% of its range on day 1, whereas the differential output shifted by 1% to 10%, and the variation between days at 1 to 10nM fell by 65% to 70% on average for individual pairs. In sweat from one participant, read against the calibration from day 1, both outputs tracked the direction of visible changes in salivary cortisol, while the MIP alone diverged from the differential output, consistent with the laboratory drift.

papers.title: Chronic hypertension disrupts the blood-brain barrier in the ventral hippocampus in females but not males in a rat model of vascular cognitive impairment
papers.abstract: Background: Chronic hypertension is a leading cause of cerebrovascular disease, ischemic stroke, and cognitive impairment. In addition, anxiety and hypertension often co-exist, however, little is known about the relationship between the two. Understanding how chronic hypertension impacts limbic brain regions such as the ventral hippocampus may provide insight into how cerebrovascular contributes to altered emotional behavior. Methods: An open field task was used to quantify locomotion, exploratory behavior, thigmotaxis, rearing and risk assessment behaviors in adult (7-month-old) male and female normotensive Wistar rats and spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR; n=8/group). Blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability was assessed by measuring extravasation of sodium fluorescein, 3 kDa Texas red dextran and 10 kDa cascade blue into the ventral hippocampus. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays were used to measure markers of vascular signaling, inflammation, and central nervous system-specific proteins indicative of neuroaxonal and glial injury in serum from separate groups of male and female SHR (n=6/group). Main effects and interactions between two independent variables (sex and hypertension) were determined using two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Tukey's post-hoc tests. Circulating factors were compared using a Welch's t-test. Relationships between BBB permeability and anxiety-like behavior were determined using Pearson's correlations. Results: Chronic hypertension increased circulating inflammatory factors and BBB permeability in female but not male rats. BBB permeability did not differ by sex in male and female normotensive rats. There was an anxiolytic effect of chronic hypertension on exploratory-related anxiety-like behavior, including less thigmotaxis, lower latency to cross through the center of the arena, and increased unsupported rearing. Risk assessment behavior, quantified as stretch-attend posture, was increased in female SHR. BBB permeability in the ventral hippocampus was correlated with anxiety-like behavior in females, but not in males, suggesting sex-dependent mechanisms of hypertension-induced changes in emotional behavior. Conclusions: These findings implicate a role for chronic hypertension-induced BBB disruption in neuropsychiatric disorders in the female sex and advances our understanding of cerebrovascular vulnerability in deep limbic brain regions.

papers.title: Differential effects of chronic hypertension and sex on vascular density along the septotemporal axis of the hippocampus in a rat model of VCID
papers.abstract: Background: Chronic hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for vascular contributions to cognitive impairment and dementia (VCID), yet vascular changes that precede cognitive dysfunction remain poorly understood. This is particularly relevant for the hippocampus, a deep brain structure critical to memory function, which differs along its septotemporal axis functionally and in its susceptibility to hypoxic/ischemic injury. The impacts of hypertension and sex on hippocampal vascularization remains unclear and could contribute to the development/progression of VCID. Methods: In this study, adult male and female Wistar and spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) were used at 5 months old, an age before memory impairments. Vascular density and morphometric parameters in dorsal and ventral hippocampus were quantified using high-resolution confocal microscopy and 3D vascular reconstruction. Results: In SHR, vascular density was increased in the dorsal hippocampus in males and across dorsal and ventral hippocampus in females compared to normotensive rats. Diameter and length of the microvasculature shifted to be smaller and longer during hypertension in males, but not females. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate chronic hypertension increases vascular density differentially by sex along the septotemporal axis of the hippocampus in mid adulthood that may increase vascular resistance and potentiate perfusion deficits or increase sites of blood-brain barrier disruption and contribute to VCID.

papers.title: Intraspecific trait variation shapes macro-scale patterns ofniche breadth and range size
papers.abstract: Morphological variation within species may promote adaptation across ecological and geographic space, perhaps reflecting evolutionary plasticity and adaptability. Based on this concept, species with greater intraspecific variation in morphological traits may be expected to occupy broader ecological niches and larger geographic ranges. However, even in the age of global trait datasets, intraspecific morphological variation remains poorly quantified at broad taxonomic and geographic scales, limiting our understanding of how trait flexibility shapes ecological and biogeographic patterns. Focusing on 161 species of bulbuls, a widespread avian family containing some of the most abundant bird species in the world, along with some of the rarest and most restricted in range, we conducted global-scale sampling of morphological traits. These included beak shape, tarsus length and wing length, associated with dietary niche, foraging strategy and dispersal, respectively. Using phylogenetic models, we tested whether ecological niche breadth and geographical range size are predicted by intraspecific morphological variation quantified from 8,251 museum specimens and 5,627 live captures. Our results demonstrate that morphological trait variation predicts both ecological niche breadth and geographic range size. Furthermore, widespread species exhibit greater morphological variation than restricted-range species even when comparisons are constrained to equivalent geographic extents, consistent with the hypothesis that intraspecific trait variation facilitates range expansion rather than simply accumulating as a consequence of occupying a larger range. These results identify intraspecific morphological variation as a potentially important, yet largely overlooked, predictor of ecological traits and biogeographic distributions in birds.

papers.title: Strategy-dependent causal relationships between large-scale cortical activity and perceptual decisions
papers.abstract: Animals can adopt different internally generated strategies to solve decision-making tasks, but whether cortical regions distinctly contribute to decisions under different strategies remains unknown. To address this problem, we analyzed three datasets comprising either cortical widefield imaging, or optogenetic inactivation of dozens of cortical locations in 54 mice, all performing the same sensory-evidence-accumulation task. Using Generalized Linear Model-Hidden Markov Models (GLM-HMMs), we found that the mice adopted one of three underlying strategies: an engaged, stimulus-driven state, and two disengaged states characterized by large side biases. The specific effects of inactivation of cortical regions depended on behavioral strategy: during engaged states, inactivation tended to increase side bias, while the opposite was true in biased states. For engaged states, these effects were most prominent when frontal regions were inactivated. Moreover, neural decoding analyses from cortex-wide activity revealed that frontal regions preferentially encode the animals' choices during engaged states relative to biased states. Our results suggest that distinct patterns of large-scale cortical dynamics underlie decisions under different task strategies and identify the frontal cortex as an important substrate of engaged-strategy control.

papers.title: Transcriptomic Analysis of Innate Immune Responses to Toxoplasma gondii in Bat Cells
papers.abstract: Bats exhibit remarkable tolerance to numerous viral infections, a phenotype associated with distinctive adaptations in innate immune and inflammatory pathways. Whether these adaptations also shape responses to nonviral intracellular pathogens remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the interaction between the protozoan parasite Toxoplasma gondii and epithelial cell lines derived from the black flying fox (Pteropus alecto). We found that both type I and type II strains of T. gondii readily invaded and replicated in bat cells, demonstrating a high degree of cellular permissiveness to infection. Surprisingly, transcriptomic analysis revealed remarkably limited early host responses despite progressive intracellular parasite replication. A pronounced transcriptional response emerged only at later stages of infection, coinciding with extensive parasite replication and cellular damage, and was characterized by changes in genes associated with inflammatory signaling, metabolic adaptation, and tissue remodeling. Together, these findings reveal an unusual interaction between bat cells and an intracellular protozoan pathogen, characterized by efficient parasite replication and markedly delayed host transcriptional activation. Our results suggest that distinctive regulation of cellular responses to intracellular infection may extend beyond viral pathogens and represent a broader feature of bat immune biology.

papers.title: Enzymatic attachment of antigens to probe immune modulation by skin commensals
papers.abstract: The skin colonist Staphylococcus epidermidis induces potent T and B cell responses, which can be redirected against antigens of interest by genetic engineering. However, since many taxa in the microbiome are genetically intractable, the utility of this method is limited. Here, we use recombinant sortase to conjugate antigens to the surface of a wide range of Gram-positive bacterial species, and we show that this non-genetic method can be used to generate protective immunity in vivo.

papers.title: N-GLYcanyzer monitoring of a microperfusion process reveals critical parameters' impact on Trastuzumab biosimilar N-glycoform time evolution
papers.abstract: Controlling monoclonal antibody (mAb) N-glycosylation as a critical quality attribute (CQA) remains challenging in continuous and intensified biomanufacturing, where conventional end-point analyses obscure dynamic pathway responses. Here, we deployed the N-GLYcanyzer process analytical technology (PAT) for automated monitoring of a microperfusion process that reveals critical parameters' impact on Trastuzumab biosimilar N-glycoform time evolution across a 20-day culture duration of Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells in a ~2 mL scale-down microbioreactor perfusion platform. Using offline PAT assays combined with our integrated at-line PAT workflow, we systematically screened six perfusion process parameters: carbon source, viable cell density (VCD), perfusion rate, temperature, and pH. While nutrient limitation and thermal/acidic stress significantly disrupted N-glycans maturation, notably triggering high-mannose (Man5) accumulation and severe productivity penalties under pH 6.7 and 39 {degrees}C operation, targeted feed supplementation with galactose and MnCl2 consistently shifted glycoform profiles away from G0F toward galactosylated species (G1F, G1F', G2F). Crucially, coupling this combined feed strategy with an intensified perfusion rate (1.2 VVD) achieved a sustained, desired galactosylation shift without a productivity cost. These findings demonstrate that nutrient feed composition and perfusion rate are primary levers for steering continuous intensified microperfusion processes for biologics production with desired N-glycoform states and highlight the utility of automated at-line PAT like N-GLYcanyzer for enabling real-time attribute-based control in continuous biomanufacturing.

papers.title: Single-cell characterization of 3D CLL spheroid model that recapitulates lymph node microenvironment-driven phenotypes and in vivo drug responses to ibrutinib
papers.abstract: Lymph node (LN) microenvironmental signals promote chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) cell survival, proliferation, and treatment resistance. We previously developed a 3D culture model that recapitulates key features of this protective LN niche. Using single-cell RNA sequencing of ex vivo paired peripheral blood and LN samples, together with matched patient-derived CLL spheroids, we investigated how microenvironmental cues shape CLL phenotypes and their response to ibrutinib. A total of 3 functional CLL states (resting, activated, proliferating) were identified, with expanded populations of activated and proliferating subsets in 3D cultures. After 5 days of in vitro ibrutinib treatment, CLL cells shifted toward a resting phenotype, reflecting published responses in patients at 6 months. Activated CLL cells showed relative resistance to ibrutinib, associated with TLR9-MALT1-MYC pathway activation. The 3D model recapitulated tissue-specific T cell phenotypes observed in patients, and computational analyses predicted several T-to-CLL cell-mediated interactions supporting the LN niche. Collectively, these data reveal distinct ibrutinib responses among CLL subsets and establish the 3D model as a physiologically relevant platform.

papers.title: ORTHOTOPIC TUMOUR INDUCTION PROTOCOL SHAPES TUMOUR MICROENVIRONMENT
papers.abstract: Robust preclinical cancer models are essential for studying tumour progression and evaluating therapeutic strategies. Orthotopic implantation of tumour cells into the mammary gland is widely used to model triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), yet substantial variation exists in the number of cells used to initiate tumours, often without explicit consideration of how this parameter shapes tumour biology. Here, we systematically assess how tumour cell number at implantation influences the tumour microenvironment using the 4T1 orthotopic TNBC model. Mammary tumours initiated with different cell numbers exhibited comparable early growth kinetics and gross size, yet diverged markedly in cellular density, hypoxia, necrosis, proliferation, vascular integrity, and immune cell infiltration. High-density tumours displayed increased HIF-1 staining and necrosis, alongside differences in vascular-associated markers and increased macrophage recruitment. Conversely, low-density tumours remained highly proliferative, less necrotic and exhibited higher PDGFR{beta} staining. Importantly, tumour cells disseminated systemically within days of implantation across all conditions, although differences in colony recovery and ex vivo expansion were not statistically significant. Together, these findings demonstrate that tumour initiating protocols are powerful determinants of tumour state, with potential implications for dissemination frequency and tumour cell fate at distant sites. Rather than representing a source of experimental variability alone, this understanding provides an opportunity to intentionally tailor orthotopic models to investigate specific stages of disease progression and therapeutic response, thereby enhancing cross-study reproducibility and translational relevance.

papers.title: FedEpitope: Parameter-Efficient Federated Protein Language Models for Linear B-Cell Epitope Prediction
papers.abstract: Linear B-cell epitopes are antigenic regions recognised by antibodies that play crucial roles in vaccine development, antibody production, and other therapeutic applications.Their prediction can support peptide-based vaccine candidate screening and diagnostic assay development, but the experimental data required for model development may be distributed across institutions that cannot freely pool their records. We present FedEpitope, a federated framework that adapts the ESM-2 protein language model for peptide-level linear B-cell epitope prediction using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), keeping client-partitioned data local and restricting the communicated trainable model state to approximately 1.11 MB. Simulated benchmarks of FedAvg and FedProx algorithms, evaluated using homology-aware data splits of five biologically heterogeneous, organism-partitioned clients, achieve promising global test performance without centralising training data, with FedAvg outperforming all single-client models in mean AP, F1, and MCC. Additional experiments characterise post-federation personalisation, record-level differential privacy, sensitivity to controlled client heterogeneity, LoRA rank, and generalisation to the independent BCPreds and NetBCE benchmarks, demonstrating the feasibility of parameter-efficient federated protein language model adaptation for data-localised B-cell epitope prediction and the associated trade-offs among predictive performance, personalisation, privacy, communication efficiency, and distribution shift.

papers.title: Concrete waste as a source of calcium and alkalinity for coccolithophore cultivation: an experimental test of carbon dioxide removal and sequestration
papers.abstract: Cultivation of calcifying microalgae has been proposed as a route to carbon dioxide removal (CDR), but biogenic calcification releases CO2 unless the calcium supplied also adds alkalinity. We used cultures of the coccolithophore Chrysotila sp to test whether hydrated lime (Ca(OH)2), supplied as a reagent or within ground waste concrete, can provide both calcium and alkalinity. In a 26-day factorial batch experiment, we monitored pH, nitrate and dissolved calcium. Calcite was quantified by thermogravimetric analysis. Nitrate concentration decreased and calcite accumulated in all algal treatments, indicating that lime or concrete did not inhibit growth or calcification. Lime and concrete raised culture pH significantly whereas the algal growth rate inferred from nitrate drawdown did not differ among treatments. Calcite production was 3.6-fold higher with lime than in seawater (4.5 vs. 1.2 mg L-1 d-1) and highly variable with concrete; lime and concrete cultures remained supersaturated with respect to calcite ({Omega} {approx} 7-10 vs. 0.2). Carbonate-system calculations indicate that the added alkalinity raises the equilibrium CO2 uptake capacity of the medium by ca. 3.4 mmol kg-1, offsetting CO2 released by calcification. These results provide proof of concept for coupling coccolithophore cultivation with concrete waste reuse for CDR.

papers.title: KH1 Domain of Poly C Binding Protein 1 (PCBP1) Interacts with Utrophin-A mRNA and Modulates Utrophin-A Expression in Mouse Myoblasts
papers.abstract: Utrophin upregulation is an attractive strategy to ameliorate Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD). Here, we investigated whether the murine poly(C)-binding protein 1 (PCBP1) directly interacts with the utrophin-A mRNA, and how the interaction shapes the fate of utrophin-A in muscle cells. As no experimentally validated structure of the murine PCBP1 is available, AlphaFold2 was utilized to predict the structure of the full-length protein and the KH1-KH2 domain of the protein. The more stable and reliable model of the KH1-KH2 domain of PCBP1 was then docked with the 5'UTR of the utrophin-A mRNA, and the top-ranked docked complex was utilized for MD simulation to identify the most stable hydrogen bond-forming amino acid residues from PCBP1. ITC showed a thermodynamically favorable spontaneous interaction between the full-length PCBP1 and the 5'UTR of utrophin-A mRNA, but the deletion mutant of PCBP1, lacking the predicted contact region, failed to exhibit any interaction. This observation was also confirmed by an RNA-immunoprecipitation assay in C2C12 cells. However, the mutant PCBP1 was unable to alter the expression of the utrophin-A in the C2C12 cells. In cells, PCBP1 overexpression lowered utrophin-A expression, while shRNA knockdown produced reciprocal increases. A 5'UTR-luciferase reporter mirrored this observation. Finally, subcellular fractionation showed that PCBP1 promotes nuclear retention of utrophin-A transcripts and reduces their cytoplasmic availability, with reciprocal shifts upon PCBP1 knockdown. Considering earlier work on PCBP2, our data suggest both paralogs recognize the same 5'UTR element, and the KH1-dependent interaction represses utrophin-A by coupling nuclear retention to reduced protein output. Thus, the PCBP1-5'UTR interaction emerges as a potent target for utrophin de-repression in DMD.

papers.title: Dissociable norepinephrine and dopamine representations during strategic decision-making and reward learning
papers.abstract: Adaptive decision-making in competitive environments requires learning from immediate reward outcomes while tracking longer-timescale information to adjust behavioural strategies and remain unpredictable against others. Dopamine (DA) and norepinephrine (NE) have long been implicated in reward-guided behaviours, but their contributions to strategic choice remain unclear. We trained mice to play a zero-sum matching pennies game against a computer opponent that exploited regularities in their choice and reward history, such that optimal performance required stochastic choice decoupled from immediate reward. We combined fibre photometry recordings, behavioural and neural modelling, and a within-subject multi-task design to determine how NE and DA contribute to strategic choice in the matching pennies game versus reward-guided behaviour in a two-armed bandit (2AB) task. DA responses were dominated by trial-by-trial reward outcomes and consistently tracked model-derived reward prediction errors (RPE) across tasks and behavioural states. In contrast, NE activity reflected salient task events, predicted upcoming choice switches, and tracked longer-timescale variables including model-inferred behavioural strategy and average reward rate. In addition, NE responses were selectively enhanced following rewarded switches when these outcomes were informative for deciding whether to stay in or switch from the current strategy; and this enhancement could not be explained by RPE. Incorporating pre-choice NE activity into a reinforcement-learning model to modulate choice generation improved model prediction in matching pennies but not in the 2AB task. Together, these findings reveal complementary neuromodulatory correlates of competitive decision-making across timescales: DA primarily guides learning from immediate outcomes through RPE, whereas NE additionally represents contextual information and choice stochasticity relevant for shaping long-term strategies.

papers.title: A Reproducible Pre-Transplant γδ T-cell Effector Signature Reveals Immune-Metabolic Programs Associated with Kidney Allograft Rejection
papers.abstract: Despite optimized immunosuppression, acute kidney transplant rejection affects 10-20% of recipients within the first year, and no reliable pre-transplant molecular test exists to identify patients at high risk, independent of the donor HLA matching. Across three independent cohorts of kidney transplant recipients, profiled by bulk RNA-sequencing with T-cell receptor repertoire analysis, flow cytometry, CyTOF with paired metabolomics, we identified a reproducible depletion of {gamma}{delta} T cells associated with rejection: an elevated {beta}/{gamma}{delta} T cell ratio in two post-transplant, biopsy-matched cohorts, and depletion of specific {gamma}{delta} T effector clusters in a third, longitudinally sampled cohort. In this third cohort, {gamma}{delta} T cell depletion was already present at the pre-transplant baseline in patients who subsequently developed rejection and remained detectable across the transplant course, indicating that it reflects recipient baseline immune biology rather than a consequence of graft injury. Longitudinal metabolomic profiling in this cohort identified time-dependent metabolic changes, including in amino acid metabolism that co-occur with the {gamma}{delta} signature and converge with it upon multi-omics integration. At the pre-transplant baseline, {gamma}{delta} T-cell marker expression alone showed exploratory discriminatory value for rejection risk (AUC = 0.69), improving marginally when integrated with metabolomic features (AUC = 0.71); larger prospective studies will be needed before clinical translation.

papers.title: DPYD links glial lipids and myelination to sleep duration
papers.abstract: The regulation of sleep is heritable and conserved across species1,2, but the governing genetic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the role of DPYD--which encodes the pyrimidine catabolic enzyme, dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase--in sleep. Using a cross-species approach, we show that DPYD and its orthologs act specifically in glia to promote sleep through the regulation of brain lipids. In mouse and zebrafish, we find that DPYD orthologs are enriched in oligodendrocyte lineage cells, and their loss reduces myelination and sleep independent of DPYDs established role in uracil catabolism to {beta}-alanine. Genetic and pharmacological manipulations of myelin in zebrafish show that altering myelination is sufficient to perturb sleep duration. In Drosophila, which lack myelin, we find that the DPYD ortholog acts in ensheathing glia to promote sleep through formation of glial lipid droplets, a proposed evolutionary precursor to myelin. Furthermore, a human GWAS-identified sleep variant2 resides in a conserved cis-regulatory element that selectively contacts the promoter of DPYD within oligodendrocytes, connecting the human genetic association to oligodendrocyte-specific control of DPYD. Together, these results identify a deeply conserved role for glial lipids in sleep regulation and establish DPYD as a mechanistic link between myelin biology and sleep.

papers.title: Lac1-dependent ceramide synthesis couples septum assembly to cell separation in Schizosaccharomyces pombe
papers.abstract: Ceramides are precursors of complex sphingolipids and bioactive membrane lipids. In the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe, they are produced by a ceramide synthase with two catalytic subunits, Lac1 and Lag1, which are redundant but not functionally equivalent: only Lac1 is required for normal growth and cell size. Why Lac1 has this unique role, and how ceramide synthesis contributes to cell morphogenesis, remain unknown. Here, we show that Lac1 couples septum assembly to cell separation. Cells lacking Lac1 die predominantly during cell separation and build septa with a thinner primary layer and markedly thicker secondary layers, accompanied by altered deposition of {beta}-(1,3)-glucans and galactomannan. These defects are not rescued by osmotic stabilization. The essential glucan synthase Bgs4 is mislocalized to cytoplasmic granules, and total {beta}-(1,3)-glucan synthase activity is partially reduced. Nevertheless, Ags1, Bgs1 and Bgs4 accumulate to higher levels and persist almost twice as long at the division site, indicating defective clearance rather than delivery of the septum-synthesis machinery. Plasma membrane sterol distribution remains unaffected. To accurately impair ceramide synthesis, we isolated thermosensitive lac1-ts alleles in a lag1{Delta} background. Their substitutions cluster in the conserved TRAM/LAG1 domain. Metabolic labeling showed that these alleles reduce ceramide synthesis at the restrictive temperature. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated that two substitutions perturb distinct contacts with C26-CoA, while Lac1-M167T loses its endoplasmic reticulum localization. Acute inactivation recapitulates the deletion phenotype, causing septum accumulation and cell death. Together, our findings establish that Lac1-dependent ceramide synthesis is required for the orderly completion of septum assembly and cell separation.

papers.title: GNG2-MRAS interaction regulates SHOC2-dependent RAF activation and MAPK signaling
papers.abstract: Dysregulation of the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathway is a hallmark of many human cancers and RASopathies. The SHOC2-MRAS-PP1C; (SMP) holophosphatase complex is a crucial regulatory node of this pathway. It activates the MAPK pathway by dephosphorylating the inhibitory phosphoserine on RAF kinases and thereby relieving RAF autoinhibition. Although GNG2, the {gamma}-subunit of heterotrimeric G proteins, has recently emerged as a negative modulator of MAPK signaling, its molecular mechanism of action remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify GNG2 and its truncated variants as inhibitors of SMP complex assembly by directly targeting MRAS. Using NanoBiT live-cell bioluminescence, co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), biolayer interferometry (BLI), and molecular dynamics simulation studies, we demonstrate that full-length GNG2 (residues 1-71aa) and two helical fragments ({Delta}1, residues 1-29aa and {Delta}2, residues 30-71aa) bind MRAS, disrupt SMP complex formation, and therefore prevent RAF dephosphorylation. Expression of the truncated GNG2 variants significantly reduced phosphorylation of ERK in cells, consistent with inhibition of pathway activation. Furthermore, a short peptide synthesized from the GNG2 {Delta}2 sequence effectively disrupted SMP complex formation in both purified protein systems and live cells and potently attenuated MAPK signaling. Molecular dynamics simulation studies revealed that GNG2 variants engage with the Switch I/II regions of MRAS, sterically interfering with SHOC2-PP1C association. Together, these findings establish GNG2 as a direct regulator of SMP complex assembly and demonstrate that GNG2-derived peptides represent a promising strategy for disrupting SHOC2-MRAS interactions and suppressing MAPK signaling in RAS/RAF-driven pathologies.

papers.title: An Ovol1 Variant in Endothelial Cells Regulates Slug and is Essential for Pathological Angiogenesis
papers.abstract: During development, the blood vasculature expands by sprouting angiogenesis, but the programs that guide this process can become dysregulated in the pathological angiogenesis of neovascular diseases leading to excessive disorganized blood vessels. We previously reported that in endothelial cells, the pro-mesenchymal transcription factor Slug critically regulates angiogenesis through a partial and reversible endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (pEndoMT); however, the upstream regulators that activate Slug and may contribute to pathological activation of the pEndoMT pathway in disease are still poorly understood. Here, we show that endothelial cells express an unusual low molecular weight variant of Ovol1 - a zinc-finger transcription factor that regulates mesenchymal transition in epithelial cells. Ovol1 and Slug are co-expressed in angiogenic endothelial cells, and using ChIP, we confirm direct Ovol1 binding to the endogenous Slug gene at a species-conserved binding motif. Whereas Ovol1 is typically a transcriptional repressor in epithelial cells, we find using a combination of silencing RNA and lentiviral overexpression constructs that the endothelial Ovol1 variant upregulates Slug, and is sufficient to drive pEndoMT marker expression and enhance endothelial cell migratory capacity. Silencing of Ovol1 abolished sprouting angiogenesis in a 3D in vitro sprouting angiogenesis assay, whereas constitutive overexpression of Ovol1 produced overaggressive and disorganized hypersprouting that depends upon Slug. We generated Ovol1 or Slug endothelial-specific knockout mice (Ovol1ECKO and SlugECKO) and found that healthy developmental angiogenesis of the neonatal mouse retina proceeds relatively normally in knockout animals. By contrast, Ovol1 was reduced in established post-natal blood vessels but became strongly re-expressed in tumor endothelial cells, and we found that colorectal cancer syngraft growth was significantly reduced in both Ovol1ECKO and SlugECKO mice alongside a failure of tumor angiogenesis. Lastly, neovascularization in the oxygen-induced retinopathy (OIR) model was also reduced in SlugECKO mice. In conclusion, we report that an endothelial Ovol1 variant upregulates Slug and drives a mesenchymal-like state, and that this Ovol1-Slug pEndoMT signaling axis is essential for pathological angiogenesis in neovascular disease models.

papers.title: Path knockout: an analysis tool for connectome-driven circuit discovery
papers.abstract: Neural circuits in the brain transform sensory information into perceptual, emotional and motor output. The connectome -- a synaptic-resolution wiring diagram of all neurons in a nervous system -- provides a neuroanatomical blueprint for identifying different circuits that mediate specific computations. However, its sheer scale and complexity pose a significant challenge in extracting functionally relevant multi-synaptic pathways. Here we established path knockout, a connectome analysis method that identifies dominant multi-synaptic pathways. Path knockout uses the input fraction of each synaptic connection as a surrogate for the probability that information transfer succeeds across that synapse and calculates approximate probability, or connection strength, that at least one path succeeds among all multi-synaptic paths between defined source and sink neuron populations. It then quantifies the importance of each interneuron by assessing the impact of its removal on the connection strength. We demonstrate that path knockout outperforms other methods for pathway analysis and identifies known and novel interneurons in the Drosophila circuits. Using path knockout, we identified a convergent circuit motif linking sexually dimorphic aggression command neurons to a shared isomorphic visual pursuit pathway. Path knockout is implemented such that it runs in minutes on a standard computer. Thus, path knockout provides a scalable and generalizable framework for connectome-driven circuit discovery.

papers.title: Direct Bioconjugations of Diverse Payloads using an Extraordinarily Donor-Promiscuous Flavin Transferase
papers.abstract: Site-specific protein conjugation is a widely used tool in chemical biology research and is the foundation of many biotechnological and biomedical applications. A key enabling technology are repurposed post-translational protein modifying enzymes, where variants with broad donor and acceptor substrate promiscuity were developed into general-purpose bioconjugation platforms. However, direct enzymatic attachment of bulky or structurally diverse payloads is often limited by low reaction efficiencies and difficulties in preparing suitable donors. Consequently, conjugation typically relies on two-step strategies in which an enzyme first installs a bioorthogonal handle on the target protein, followed by chemical attachment of the payload. These enzyme-first, chemistry-second approaches limit chemistry to bioorthogonal reactions that leave a molecular footprint. Here, we introduce direct ADDing, an enzymatic bioconjugation platform based on our discovery of the exceptional donor promiscuity of the flavin transferase ApbE. We show that ApbE accepts a remarkably broad range of donor substrates provided they carry an adenosine diphosphate (ADP) anchor. The prevalence of ADP-containing compounds in nature provides access to diverse building blocks and an extensive biochemical toolbox for donor generation. Exploiting these resources, we demonstrate multiple strategies for preparing compatible donors and achieve direct, site-specific enzymatic conjugation of diverse small molecules, peptides, proteins, and synthetic polymers.

papers.title: Characterizing the Metabolic Fate and Pharmacokinetics of the RyR2 Inhibitor ent-Verticilide
papers.abstract: ent-Verticilide is a synthetic macrocyclic depsipeptide and ryanodine receptor 2 (RyR2) inhibitor with potential therapeutic applications in cardiac arrhythmias. This study characterized its in vitro metabolism and in vivo pharmacokinetics to better understand factors that may influence its disposition. Metabolic stability was evaluated in mouse, rat, dog, and human liver S9 fractions, followed by CYP reaction phenotyping in human liver microsomes and metabolite profiling in human and rat liver S9 fractions. Pharmacokinetics were evaluated in rats following intravenous and oral administration. ent-Verticilide underwent rapid, NADPH-dependent depletion across all species, with in vitro half-lives ranging from 2.1 to 5.3 min. CYP reaction phenotyping indicated that CYP3A was the predominant CYP subfamily involved in its metabolism. Eight putative metabolites were identified in human and rat liver S9, primarily resulting from hydroxylation, oxidation, and desaturation, with generally similar metabolite profiles between species. In rats, ent-verticilide exhibited a systemic clearance of 29.6 mL/min/kg, a steady-state volume of distribution of 4.86 L/kg, and a terminal half-life of 6.85 h following intravenous administration. Absolute oral bioavailability was 10.5%. Overall, these findings show that ent-verticilide undergoes extensive oxidative hepatic metabolism and provide an initial DMPK framework for its continued preclinical development.

papers.title: CardioShift: Resolving cell-to-cell functional heterogeneity in hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes from high-throughput single-cell imaging
papers.abstract: High-content screening of human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) is widely used for disease modeling, yet standard pipelines rely on whole-well averages that obscure cell-to-cell heterogeneity. Moving from well-averages to single-cell analysis reveals hidden variations, but may introduce a pseudoreplication bias if cells are analysed as independent data points. We present CardioShift, an open-source bioimage informatics framework designed to map single-cell distributions by properly accounting for this nested variance structure. Applying this framework to 32,818 Ca2+ transients and 10,719 contractility-lipid profiles, we show that cell-to-cell variability represents the largest source of variance for most functional parameters, demonstrating how traditional well averages mask condition-dependent phenotypes. Furthermore, unsupervised clustering identifies condition-dependent shifts in functional subpopulations, including a distinct cellular state that accumulates lipids but maintains baseline contraction kinetics that was not detected using well- and single-cell averaging approaches. CardioShift provides a robust analytical approach to resolve hidden single-cell distributions.

papers.title: RELAY: Relational In-Context Learning for Cellular Perturbation Prediction
papers.abstract: Cellular responses to perturbations vary across multiple experimental variables, such as perturbation identity, cell type, donor, and dose, defining a multidimensional condition space in which each measured population occupies one coordinate. Existing methods predict unmeasured conditions using explicit representations of these variable values, generalizing unseen values therefore depends on the availability and quality of such representations. We present RELAY, a relational in-context model that predicts unmeasured coordinates from measured responses at related coordinates. For each target, RELAY uses measured control--perturbed pairs from conditions that share one or more experimental variables with the target, such as the same perturbation in another cell type. The model receives only which variables are shared, not their values, and uses these demonstrations to predict the target response. We evaluate RELAY on chemical, genetic, and cytokine perturbation datasets under two settings: unseen combinations, where test values are individually observed during training but not in their target combinations, and unseen variable values, where test values are introduced only through context at inference. RELAY outperforms existing in-context methods on unseen variable values and supervised perturbation-prediction methods on unseen combinations. All resources will be open sourced, including code and data.

papers.title: Wolffia globosa -derived nanovesicles as a natural source of bioactive metabolites with neuroprotective potential against methylglyoxal-induced oxidative stress
papers.abstract: Plant-derived nanovesicles (PDNVs) have attracted increasing attention for their potential biomedical applications, particularly in oxidative stress-related diseases and neuroprotection. Wolffia globosa, an emerging functional food and potential future food source, is rich in phytochemicals associated with health-promoting properties. Harnessing W. globosa-derived nanovesicles (WGNVs) represents a promising strategy for expanding the biomedical applications of this plant. In this study, WGNVs were isolated and characterized, and their neuroprotective potential was evaluated in vitro. The isolated WGNVs exhibited nanoscale dimensions and a lipid bilayer structure. Biochemical analyses revealed substantial total phenolic and flavonoid contents, alongside intrinsic antioxidant activities. Untargeted metabolomic profiling identified a diverse repertoire of metabolites, including major constituents subsequently validated using independent analytical approaches. These findings provided a foundation for investigating the neuroprotective effects of WGNVs in a methylglyoxal (MGX)-induced model of neuronal oxidative stress. High-resolution confocal microscopy demonstrated the cellular localization of WGNVs within neuronal cells, providing evidence of interactions between plant-derived nanovesicles and neuronal cells. WGNV treatment attenuated MGX-induced free radical accumulation and oxidative stress responses while preserving cellular morphology integrity. Collectively, this study provides foundational evidence of the physicochemical characteristics, metabolite composition, and in vitro neuroprotective potential of WGNVs. These findings highlight WGNVs as a promising naturally derived nanocarrier platform for investigating plant-animal interkingdom interactions and exploring potential therapeutic applications across a broad range of biomedical fields.

papers.title: Accumulation of two distinct alleles causes astringency loss in cultivated polyploid persimmon
papers.abstract: Persimmon fruit accumulates high levels of proanthocyanidins (PAs), causing extreme astringency. In pollination-constant and non-astringent (PCNA) cultivars, PA accumulation ceases early in fruit development. Although the PCNA trait is recessively controlled by the ASTRINGENCY (AST) locus, its causal gene has remained unknown. Using haplotype-resolved forward genetics in a hexaploid genetic background, we identified the previously uncharacterized TANNIN (TAN) as the causal gene. Long-read sequencing revealed that PCNA originated through the accumulation of independently derived ast alleles that cause transcriptional deficiency of TAN. These findings resolve the complex genetic basis of natural astringency loss in persimmon and provide a framework for molecular breeding. Further investigation of TAN function would uncover mechanisms underlying massive accumulation of PAs in persimmon fruit and insight into specialized metabolite sequestration.

papers.title: Biosensor-guided genome-wide CRISPR screens enable cis,cis-muconic acid overproduction in yeast
papers.abstract: Classical pathway metabolic engineering relies on enhancing strain productivity through the introduction of rationally identified genetic perturbations, which while useful, are time-consuming and miss unintuitive targets. Genome-wide CRISPR screens offer an alternative by efficiently sampling genomes, enabling the engineering of novel phenotypes, and are further enhanced when combined with high-throughput strain interrogation methods. Here, using Saccharomyces cerevisiae, we engineered small molecule biosensors into population enrichment tools using zeocin resistance and fluorescence as signal outputs. We then introduced the multi-functional genome-wide CRISPR (MAGIC) library that targets every gene for activation, interference, or deletion, thus creating biosensor-aided MAGIC, or senMAGIC. As a case study, we utilized senMAGIC to identify single genetic determinants that improve productivity of the nylon precursors protocatechuic and cis,cis-muconic acids (PCA and ccM). These were then randomly assembled as triple gRNA-tRNA arrays for multiplexed gene perturbations to identify combinatorial effects. Top gRNA hits were then confirmed using direct genomic integrations in senMAGIC-free production strains, resulting in identifying known as well as novel targets that increase PCA and ccM titres.
