PX domain requires its target lipid for the transition from electrostatic hopping to stable bilayer docking, while autophagy lipid kinase can dock spontaneously to anionic lipid bilayers even in the absence of its substrate lipid. In principle, the slowly diffusing, bilayer-docked states of PX domain and autophagy lipid kinase could be interrupted by unbinding-hopping-rebinding events. However, such events are not detected for PX domain in the presence of target lipid (DO)PI(3)P nor for autophagy lipid kinase in the presence of substrate lipid (DO)PI. Instead, unbinding-hopping-rebinding events are only observed for autophagy lipid kinase in the absence of substrate lipid, indicating that the presence of a specific binding lipid reduces the frequency or spatial amplitude of such events. Overall, the findings provide evidence that p40Phox PX domain possesses a search mechanism involving electrostatic hopping that speeds its acquisition of target lipid, as previously observed for PH domains. The evidence indicates that the autophagy lipid kinase also exhibits electrostatic hopping/skating behavior that is proposed to play a functional role by speeding regulatory encounters with autophagy lipid kinase activators and effectors. Moreover, the ability of the lipid kinase to spontaneously dock to anionic membranes without a target lipid could facilitate its distribution across broad regions of the growing autophagosome. Finally, the autophagy lipid kinase exhibits multiple translational modes that we hypothesize are enabled by its two membrane docking feet.

papers.title: NTAD: A longitudinal neuroimaging dataset of Alzheimer's disease pathology
papers.abstract: We introduce the New Therapeutics in Alzheimer's Disease (NTAD) dataset, a multi-modal and longitudinal imaging dataset from 70 biomarker-positive people with early dementia or Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) due to Alzheimer's Disease (AD), assessed over 2.5 years, and 35 healthy controls assessed at baseline. The data include simultaneous magneto- and electro-encephalography (M/EEG), 3-Tesla structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), Amyloid-beta; positron emission tomography (PET), fluid proteomic biomarkers in cerebrospinal fluid and blood, and a battery of clinical and neuropsychological assessments. 11C UCB-J PET was undertaken for a subset of participants. For people with AD, assessments were repeated at approximately three weeks, 15 months, and 28 months after baseline. The data can be accessed through the Dementias Platform UK (DPUK), including pre-processed M/EEG and T1 MRI in pseudonymised BIDS format. With the pressing need to develop treatments for slowing, reversing, and preventing AD, these data provide an opportunity for identifying and validating novel biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease neurophysiology, as well as understanding its treatable pathology.

papers.title: Application of organic fertilisation such as poultry manure enhanced carbohydrate, fat and vitamin C contents of Huckleberry (Solanum scabrum) more than mineral fertilisation in Buea-Cameroon
authors: Nkeudem Asoba, G. N. A. T.
papers.abstract: Huckleberry (Solanum scabrum), is a vital indigenous leafy vegetable in sub-Saharan Africa(SSA) and Cameroon, serving as a rich source of vitamins, proteins, and minerals. This study evaluated the nutritional composition, growth, and yield parameters of huckleberry produced using organic and inorganic fertilizers in Buea. A randomized complete block experiment with four blocks compared four fertilisation regimes: pig manure, poultry manure, control, and urea. 6 weeks after planting (WAP), growth parameters; plant height, leaf number and leaf area were measured alongside cumulative yield. Harvested samples were analysed to determine total protein, carbohydrate, fat, and vitamin C contents. Data were subjected to analyse using a two-way analysis of variance. Fertilizer application significantly (P<0.05) enhanced plant performance compared to the unfertilized control. At 8 WAP, urea had the most vigorous vegetative growth, having the highest mean plant height (25.92 cm), maximum leaf count (29.38), and total yield (20.72 tons/ha). Nutritionally, urea produced the highest total protein content (290.30 mg/100 g), but reduced vitamin C level (24.20 mg/100 g) below the baseline of the control (27.53 mg/100 g). Poultry manure had the highest content of carbohydrates (6.52%), fats (7.8%), and vitamin C (42.57 mg/100 g). The study demonstrates a clear trade-off between crop yield and specific nutritional attributes based on nutrient sources. While urea enhanced plant growth and yield, organic amendments like poultry manure improved the micronutrients like carbohydrate and fat composition of huckleberries. Future work should focus on integrated application of poultry and pig manure with urea to see their effects of huckleberry performance, nutrient contents and soil health. Keywords: fertilizer, huckleberry, urea, poultry manure and pig manure

papers.title: Age Associated Shifts Toward Anaerobic Taxa and Amino Acid Degradation Potential in the Canine Oral Microbiome
papers.abstract: Introduction: Periodontal disease is common in dogs and is associated with changes in oral microbial community composition. How the canine oral microbiome restructures across age at both ecological and metabolic levels remains incompletely characterized. Methods: We analyzed shotgun metagenomic buccal-swab profiles from 1,125 dogs using MetaPhlAn. Functional profiles from HUMAnN were analyzed at pathway and functional-group levels. We annotated species-level taxa with oxygen preference and evaluated oxygen-tolerant and anaerobic taxa abundances across age. We also characterized community structure, metabolic potential, Shannon diversity, and age and weight prediction using nested cross-validated Elastic Net models. Results: Age was associated with substantial restructuring in the oral microbiome. Mean oxygen-tolerant taxa abundance decreased from 67.5% in puppies to 29.1% in mature dogs, whereas anaerobic abundance increased from 14.3% to 53.8%. The oxygen-tolerant: anaerobe log-ratio declined with age (Spearman {rho} = -0.616). Metabolic profiles also varied with age, with higher amino-acid-degradation potential and lower glycolysis and central-carbohydrate potential, and aerobic-respiration-I abundance in older dogs. Shannon diversity increased with age ({rho} = 0.537, p < 0.001). Elastic Net models trained on microbiome species abundance predicted age (Pearson r = 0.609; R-squared = 0.371) and weight (r = 0.498; R-squared = 0.248) with moderate accuracy. Discussion: Canine age was associated with coordinated changes in oral-community oxygen preference and metabolic pathways. These findings extend prior taxon-specific observations by examining a broader ecological shift and metabolic potential in the canine oral microbiome. This provides a reference for future longitudinal or clinical studies of oral maturation and periodontal disease.

papers.title: Stable large-scale network architecture and structured individual variability in the awake mouse brain
papers.abstract: Large-scale functional networks provide a scaffold for brain activity, but their population architecture and inter-individual variability remain poorly defined in the awake mouse brain. Here we introduce the Awake Mouse Connectome Project (AMCP), a population-scale multimodal MRI resource comprising 212 sex-balanced awake mice. Using this dataset, we generated high-precision in vivo tissue probability maps, derived a reproducible whole-brain functional network atlas and quantified structured variability in network connectivity across animals. The resulting atlas defined a stable large-scale architecture aligned with structural topology, while inter-individual functional connectivity variability followed organized connectional gradients rather than random dispersion. We further benchmarked the clustering-derived scaffold against conventional group independent component analysis (GICA) and release the GICA network atlas as an accompanying resource. AMCP further provides empirical scaling relationships linking sample size, scan duration and connectome precision. These analyses indicate that mean functional connectivity and functional connectivity variability have distinct sample-size requirements, providing a protocol-specific guidance for studies focused on group-average connectivity and inter-individual variability. Individualized network parcellations derived from the AMCP scaffold improved behavioural prediction relative to group-average features for selected behavioural domains, indicating functional relevance of subject-specific network architecture. Together, AMCP establishes an open dataset, tissue-template resource, clustering-derived and GICA functional atlases, and analysis toolbox for reproducible awake mouse connectomics and for translational studies linking circuit mechanisms to large-scale brain organization.

papers.title: GxE and changes to the genetic architecture of flowering time in an overwintering environment
papers.abstract: Characterizing how the expression of genetic variation changes across environments is essential for understanding evolution in complex environments, the evolution of phenotypic plasticity, and the genetic architecture of adaptation. We investigated how the phenotypic distribution, large-effect loci, and polygenetic architecture of flowering time in Arabidopsis thaliana changes when grown in an ecologically realistic environment compared to standard chamber conditions. We grew 479 A. thaliana accessions in an overwintering common garden that have previously been phenotyped in growth chambers by the 1001 Genomes Project (2016). Our findings suggest there is extensive GxE for flowering time between the overwintering common garden and the growth chamber environments. None of the large effect loci that we identified using a multivariate Genome Wide Association Study (GWAS) were shared across growth conditions. We find evidence of allelic differential sensitivity, conditional neutrality, and antagonistic pleiotropy contributing to GxE for flowering time between growth conditions. Our results also suggest that the effects of genetic variation across multiple flowering time regulatory pathways is revealed when grown in a more ecologically realistic environment. The effect sizes for the most significant 1% of SNPs are moderately correlated between the outdoor and growth chamber conditions which indicates a partially shared genetic basis. Overall, our findings highlight how making inferences about the genetic basis and evolution of complex traits may be dependent on conducting experiments in ecologically realistic environments.

papers.title: Lesion-Derived Estimated Functional and Structural Connectomes Predict Post-Stroke Recovery Outcomes
papers.abstract: Accurate prognosis after stroke remains challenging, limiting the ability to predict individual recovery. While advanced connectome MRI can provide further prognostically-useful information regarding affected brain networks, its impractical nature has given rise instead to lesion-based estimates of network disruptions. Here, we present a novel pipeline that leverages our recently developed connectome analysis tools to estimate structural disconnection (eSDC) and functional connectivity (eFC) directly from N=96 patient lesion masks for use in predicting motor, language, attention and memory outcomes at multiple timepoints after stroke. Our approach jointly leverages our Network Modification (NeMo) Tool, a database of white matter tractography results that estimates structural disconnectivity (eSDC), and the Krakencoder, a joint autoencoder that estimates functional connectomes (eFC) from the NeMo Tool's output. Models based on eSDC and eFC predicted almost all outcomes, particularly motor outcomes, significantly better than models that used patients' fMRI-based observed FC (oFC) and models based on only lesion information and covariates. Estimated connectome measures also i) retained meaningful inter-individual variability when compared to observed functional connectomes, ii) reflected population-level, stroke-related changes in functional connectomes, and iii) resulted in outcome prediction models with feature importances that aligned with expected networks of relevance to the given outcome. Feature importance analyses also identified distinct predictive signatures across both modality and outcome domain, indicating that eSDC and eFC capture non-redundant, biologically meaningful information about post-stroke network disruption. Together, these findings establish our lesion-based estimates of post-stroke structural and functional connectomes as a practical, information-rich alternative to advanced imaging in patients. This approach allows for probing an individual's affected neural circuitry underlying stroke impairment and recovery, paving the way toward more efficient, accessible, and personalized approaches to post-stroke prognosis and intervention.

papers.title: Resonant Recognition Model analysis of cGAS: conserved spectral frequencies and a divergent naked mole-rat phase signature
papers.abstract: Background: Cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS) is a cytosolic DNA sensor with additional noncanonical nuclear functions, including suppression of homologous recombination (HR) in humans. In the naked mole-rat (NMR), cGAS instead promotes HR through a FANCI-RAD50-dependent mechanism, a functional reversal attributed to four C-terminal amino acid substitutions. Whether such functional divergence is reflected in primary-sequence-derived spectral features is unknown. Methods: We applied the Resonant Recognition Model (RRM) to cGAS sequences from fourteen mammals and to FANCI sequences from eight species. Sequences were converted to numerical series using EIIP values and analyzed by discrete Fourier transform; consensus spectra were generated by point-wise multiplication of individual power spectra. Phase differences between cGAS and FANCI were computed at frequencies of interest. Spectral amplitudes at the dominant shared frequency were correlated with body mass, lifespan, and lifespan-to-body-mass ratio. RRM frequencies were converted to electromagnetic wavelengths using the Cosic formulation ({lambda} = 201/f_RRM). Results: The cGAS consensus spectrum contained four prominent peaks (f = 0.0392, 0.0765, 0.2539, 0.4229), with 0.2539 dominant. Three FANCI peaks (0.04138, 0.2479, 0.4332) were close to cGAS peaks, and the combined cGAS+FANCI consensus retained peaks at 0.2539 and 0.04077. Spectral amplitude at f = 0.2539 correlated with body mass (r = 0.647, p < 0.05) and with lifespan-to-body-mass ratio (r = -0.677, p < 0.01); the NMR showed the lowest amplitude. Human cGAS-FANCI phase difference was 3.1297 rad, 0.0118 rad from opposition, satisfying the RRM interaction criterion; the NMR cGAS-FANCI pair gave 1.7319 rad, approximately {pi}/2, which does not satisfy the criterion. Conversion of the dominant frequency yielded a predicted wavelength of 792 nm (378.5 THz), in the near-infrared range. This prediction is testable in transparent vertebrate models: zebrafish respond to NIR light, and red-light pre-treatment has been reported to improve survival after lethal gamma irradiation in zebrafish embryos. Conclusions: RRM identifies conserved spectral features in cGAS consistent with a cGAS-FANCI relationship, and amplitude at the dominant frequency varies with life-history traits. The phase analysis does not support a direct interaction signature for NMR cGAS-FANCI, a negative result consistent with a chromatin-mediated mechanism. The cross-species phase comparisons suggest that NMR FANCI, not only NMR cGAS, may contribute to the distinctive interaction mode. The predicted 792 nm wavelength provides a concrete, experimentally accessible parameter for testing whether RRM-derived frequencies can modulate radiation resistance in a transparent vertebrate model. These results are hypothesis-generating and require experimental validation.

papers.title: Large-scale forward genetics reveals genetically separable components of plant cell proliferative capacity
papers.abstract: Plant cell cultures underpin regeneration, transformation and emerging applications in biotechnology and plant cell agriculture, yet the genetic determinants of proliferative performance remain poorly characterized. Here, we combined large-scale forward genetics with automated image-based phenotyping to quantify 27,648 calli representing 2,880 Arabidopsis thaliana T-DNA insertion lines. Of these, 2,456 lines produced calli smaller than the WT population mean, whereas only 190 produced larger calli, revealing a strongly asymmetric phenotypic distribution. Enhanced callus growth was not consistently associated with increased vegetative growth, indicating that these traits can be genetically uncoupled. Validation of selected high-growth mutants in suspension culture identified lines with enhanced biomass accumulation, while serial propagation revealed independent variation in sustained proliferative capacity. Thus, callus growth, whole-plant growth, short-term suspension biomass accumulation and sustained proliferation represent distinct, not necessarily coupled components of proliferative performance. These findings establish a scalable framework for identifying genetic determinants relevant to the development of improved plant cell production lines.

papers.title: Distinct processing of visual motion by transcriptomic cell types in the superior colliculus
papers.abstract: How the brain organizes visual processing across distinct neuron types is a fundamental yet unresolved question. Here we study how visual motion is processed by transcriptomically defined cell types in the superior colliculus (SC). We generated or identified transgenic mouse lines to target three transcriptomic types of neurons in the superficial SC, the Cbln4+, Vip+, and Grp+ neurons. We find that each of these cell types encodes distinct ranges of stimulus direction, speed, size, and spatial and temporal features. In response to ecologically relevant visual flows, the three cell types occupy partitional spaces in the encoding manifold. The three cell types also show unique morphology and connectivity, including their retinal and intracollicular input and projection patterns. Together, these results reveal a genetic logic for visual motion processing in the SC, where transcriptomic cell types are likely the basic computational units with their specific feature selectivity, morphology, and input-output connectivity.

papers.title: A baseline for aquatic parasite diversity in West African mangroves: host-parasite records, DNA barcodes, and an experimental design for future use
papers.abstract: Macroparasites represent a major fraction of biodiversity and biomass in marine ecosystems, yet remain substantially underrepresented in ecological surveys and food-web models, particularly in the Global South. This study addresses this geographic bias by providing the first comprehensive ecological survey of macroparasite communities of fishes in a West African Marine Protected Area (MPA) and adjacent Open-Access Area (OAA) characterised by mangrove forests. We collected 5,020 parasite specimens from 10 fish and one crab species in the Saloum Delta, Senegal, identifying 27 parasite species across all major taxa. Our findings include 15 new records for Senegal of which 11 are also new for West Africa. Additionally, 64% of host-parasite combinations constitute new host records. We provide 208 DNA barcodes, offering the first molecular data for 31% of these species globally and establishing a reference library for future DNA metabarcoding efforts in the region. Using sample size-corrected biodiversity indices and mixed-model analyses, we detected significant variations in parasite infracommunities and component communities between the MPA and OAA, demonstrating the feasibility of using comparative study designs to monitor fisheries impacts on parasite diversity in the Saloum Delta. Furthermore, the identification of trophically transmitted parasites provided evidence of unstudied food-web connections, e.g. predator-prey linkages between fishes and higher-trophic-level definitive hosts including birds and elasmobranchs. By integrating morphological identification, molecular data, and archiving of voucher specimens into publicly accessible, curated collections, this study establishes a new baseline for marine parasite biodiversity in West Africa and provides a methodological blueprint for surveying understudied regions.

papers.title: Mapping the sequence determinants of constitutive activity in GPCRs
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) signal not only in response to ligands but also in their absence. This basal, or constitutive, activity has distinct physiological consequences and is the only functional measurement available for orphan receptors. It is also hard to compare receptors because each is reported relative to its own baseline. Here, we measure basal activity on a single scale across the human GPCR family. Pairing a barcoded library of all human GPCRs with a transcriptional cAMP reporter, we scored 901 receptor constructs in one pool experiment. Basal activity forms a continuous distribution, and many of the highest-scoring recipes have prior reports of ligand-independent activity, with orphan being strongly represented. We then exhaustively mutated one of them, GPR161, and measured its effects on protein abundance, surface expression, and cAMP signaling. Of the 528 positions, only 10 specifically alter signaling independent of expression. Constraints on basal signaling are dominated by reepotro biogenesis, which requires multiphenotype scanning to resolve. Together, these datasets place basal activity on a common scale across the GPCR family and provide a template for dissecting it at residue resolution.

papers.title: Brain mitovesicles undergo stage-specific remodelling during the progression of amyloid-β pathology
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is an early feature of Alzheimer's disease that shows nonlinear changes as the disease progresses. However, how these changes are reflected in the mitochondrial material released by brain cells remains poorly understood. Mitovesicles are a recently described extracellular vesicle subpopulation of mitochondrial origin that provide a unique insight into mitochondrial alterations in the brain and could potentially show how nonlinear changes evolve across disease stages of amyloid-beta pathology. Here, we isolated forebrain-derived small extracellular vesicles and mitovesicles from wild-type and Amyloid precursor protein (App) knock-in (AppKI) mice, carrying familial AD mutations and progressively accumulating amyloid-beta plaques, at presymptomatic (2-month) and symptomatic (12-month) stages using high-resolution density gradient fractionation. Vesicle identity and composition were assessed by morphological, biophysical and quantitative proteomic analyses, and mitovesicle respiratory function was measured by extracellular flux analysis. We show that mitovesicles carry a distinct, predominantly mitochondrial inner membrane proteome that is remodelled by age and disease in a stage-specific manner. Compared with small extracellular vesicles, mitovesicle proteomic profiles captured disease progression more clearly, with symptomatic AppKI mice forming the most molecularly distinct group. At the presymptomatic stage, AppKI mitovesicles showed reduced mitochondrial protein representation, most notably of fatty acid {beta}-oxidation and lipid-metabolism proteins associated with astroglial and vascular signatures, preceding any detectable respiratory impairment. At the symptomatic stage this reversed: AppKI mitovesicles were enriched for oxidative phosphorylation, mitochondrial membrane and transporter proteins, yet showed reduced Complex IV-linked respiration, revealing a dissociation between mitochondrial cargo abundance and respiratory function. Selected cargo changes were not mirrored in whole-brain tissue, indicating selective remodelling of mitovesicle content. Comparison with mitovesicles from post-mortem human Alzheimer's disease frontotemporal cortex and hippocampus identified a conserved 62-protein mitovesicle core, dominated by oxidative phosphorylation subunits and mitochondrial carriers. In addition, 25 of these proteins were enriched in mitovesicles derived from Alzheimer's and AppKI forebrains, defining a conserved mitovesicular disease signature. Together, these findings establish forebrain-derived mitovesicles as a dynamically remodelled vesicle population that reflects progressive mitochondrial dysfunction in the Alzheimer's disease brain and provides a cross-species resource for future biomarker and mechanistic studies.

papers.title: Gαq-mediated contact release is required for efficient mitochondrial quality control
papers.abstract: Lysosomes and mitochondria are highly dynamic organelles whose coordinated interactions are essential for cellular homeostasis, while their dysfunction contributes to numerous human diseases. Here, we identify the mitochondrial outer membrane protein Fis1 and the RabGAPs TBC1D15 and TBC1D17 as novel interacting partners of the heterotrimeric G protein -subunit Gq. Using mitochondrial proteomics, co-immunoprecipitation, proximity ligation assays, and in vitro binding studies with purified proteins, we demonstrate that Gq forms a complex with Fis1 and TBC1D15/TBC1D17 through a non-canonical interaction interface. Gq localizes to mitochondria-lysosome contact sites, where it regulates the dynamic balance between contact formation and dissociation. Loss of Gq resulted in enlarged and clustered lysosomes and increased the extent and duration of mitochondria-lysosome contacts. Live-cell imaging revealed prolonged organelle tethering in Gq-deficient cells, while proximity ligation and three-dimensional reconstruction analyses localized Gq and TBC1D15 to mitochondrial tips closely associated with lysosomes. This localization, together with increased mitochondrial fission and altered mitophagic turnover following Gq loss, links the regulation of contacts at mitochondrial tips to mitochondrial fragmentation and quality control. Re-expression of Gq, but not the non-canonical interaction-deficient mutant, restored normal lysosomal morphology, contact-site dynamics, mitochondrial fragmentation, and mitophagy. Together, these findings identify a Gq as a dynamic regulator of mitochondria-lysosome untethering and connect contact site turnover with mitochondria fragmentation and mitophagy. Our work uncovers a novel link between G protein signaling, organelle communication, and mitochondrial quality control.

papers.title: Reducing the Risk of Gradient Induced EEG Hardware Heating During Simultaneous EEG-fMRI
papers.abstract: Simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and functional MRI (fMRI) has the potential to provide a more complete characterisation of brain function. Acquiring these data simultaneously requires the EEG hardware to be MR safe, since the EEG cap, amplifiers and powerpacks must be located within the MR environment. Placing them in this environment exposes them to both static and varying (radiofrequency (RF) and gradient) magnetic fields, presenting a potential heating risk. Previous studies have typically positioned the amplifiers and powerpacks outside of the bore, meaning that this risk is largely limited to the EEG cap. However, current guidelines recommend positioning the amplifiers within the bore. This reduces the distance between the EEG electrodes and amplifier, improving EEG signal quality and reducing risks of RF heating at the electrodes, but presents a potential heating risk for the amplifiers and powerpacks from the varying magnetic field gradients. In this study, we demonstrate that placing the amplifiers and powerpacks in the bore presents a significant heating risk, both at 7T and 3T. At 7T, we show that EPI sequences with a slew rate of at least 88 T/m/s resulted in significant heating of the EEG amplifiers. This heating effect could be negated by reducing the slew rate to 61 T/m/s. At 3T, we replicate the EEG amplifier heating and show that an alternative approach to reducing the gradient slew rates experience by the hardware is to increase the distance between the EEG amplifier/powerpacks and the isocentre of the magnet. Increasing the distance between the EEG hardware and MR isocentre by 30 cm mitigates the heating risk to the amplifiers and powerpacks, regardless of sequence parameters (e.g., slew rate). Therefore, whilst reducing the distance between the electrodes and amplifiers may improve EEG signal quality and reduce the potential for electrode RF heating, we show that risk of heating of hardware by gradient switching is greatly increased. This is particularly important to consider with the faster gradient slew rates available on modern MRI scanners, desired to increase spatial resolution. Experimenters must make careful decisions about hardware placement to ensure that the EEG-fMRI setup they use is safe, taking account of the varying risks that are posed by different approaches.

papers.title: Facing the waves of negative mood: Trait mindfulness moderates the links between physiology and emotion
papers.abstract: Trait mindfulness is a dispositional ability characterized by awareness, non-judgment, and acceptance of internal and external experiences. Stress is associated with numerous psychological and physical health concerns including depression and anxiety. Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) have consistently been shown to reduce perceived stress and improve a variety of other health outcomes. However, the mechanisms through which mindfulness confers these benefits are not yet fully understood. This study aimed to examine (1) the relationship between trait mindfulness and changes in cortisol following a negative Mood Induction Procedure (MIP) and (2) whether trait mindfulness moderates the relationship between changes in cortisol and mood reactivity following a negative MIP. Participants were recruited from the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex (N = 25 participants) and completed a series of self-report questionnaires, negative and positive mood induction, and mood assessments. Participants provided salivary cortisol samples before and after negative MIPs. Results indicated that, following the negative MIP, sadness and anxiety were associated with greater reductions in cortisol. Trait mindfulness moderated these associations. Overall, these findings contribute to a broader understanding of emotional responses to negatively-valenced stressors and how they are mitigated by mindfulness. They suggest support for future applications of mindfulness-based interventions in high-stress populations.

papers.title: Parkinson Disease vs Aging Features Impairments in Formation and Release of a Power Grip in Real and Pantomimed String-Pulling
papers.abstract: Parkinson disease (PD) impairs skilled reaching tasks but less is known about its effects on rhythmic bimanual actions. We used a bimanual hand-over-hand string-pulling task that requires repeated reach, grasp, pull, push and release movements. We predicted that participants with PD would show impairment in making the rotary skilled hand movement of retrieving the string, analogous to impairments observed in single handed target reaching. Nine participants with PD (mean UPDRS-III: 24.6), 16 older adults, and 10 young adults successfully performed a real string-pulling task and then pantomimed the action. Video analyses combined optical-flow estimation of whole-body movement speed, markerless 2D pose estimation of upper-limb kinematics, and expert frame-by-frame scoring of hand and finger shaping. Machine-learning classification then identified the discriminative information carried by these multilevel movement components. Participants with PD showed lower movement speed, a smaller hand workspace, and reduced hand and finger shaping, with older adults showing intermediate values. All participants grasped the real string with a power grip, but participants with PD showed reduced rotary movements of the arm and the wrists and absent of arpeggio-like sequential finger movement during grasp and release. During pantomime, participants with PD moved faster and made larger hand movements, while grasp-related hand opening and finger sequencing was reduced or absent. The findings suggest that PD is expressed across this multicomponent movement manifold, and that the movement organization changes with task demands: real string pulling requires formation and release of a power grip, whereas pantomime does not place demands on grasping ability.

papers.title: Systematic Spike Sorting Errors Revealed by Juxtacellular Ground Truth in the Awake Brain
papers.abstract: Existing ground-truth data for spike sorting come almost entirely from anesthetized or in vitro preparations. Yet phenomena expected to challenge spike sorting most (spike overlap and bursting) depend on brain state and differ in the awake brain. Therefore, error estimates from existing benchmarks may not transfer to awake recordings, and the types of errors in the awake brain remain largely uncharacterized. To address this, we generated a ground-truth dataset (16 neurons) using paired juxtacellular-extracellular electrophysiology in awake mice, and found spike sorting performance, particularly recall, to be lower than conventional benchmarks might suggest. Generally, false negatives sharply increased with intrinsic physiological factors like bursting, whereas false positives were more strongly associated with extrinsic factors, such as putative spike overlaps. To quantify contributions to errors from intrinsic and extrinsic factors, for each observed juxtacellular waveform we predicted the corresponding extracellular waveform. In the best-performing sorter, we estimate approximately half of false positives were attributable to credulous attempts to resolve putative overlaps. Bursting and putative overlaps were each associated with a roughly doubled false negative rate when they occurred separately, and with a sevenfold increase when they occurred together. These co-occurrences accounted for approximately 40% of a typical neuron's false negatives, despite comprising only approximately a fifth of its spikes. Thus, the moments when spike sorters must rely on the assumption of waveform invariance the most to resolve overlaps are exactly the moments when bursting makes that assumption least valid. We also estimate that three-quarters of false negatives had been detected but assigned to other units. These spikes were not cleanly oversplit: post-hoc merging was not productive because the loss in precision was three times the gain in recall. Because bursting and spike overlaps often co-occur, sorting spikes by waveform similarity and repairing the result by post hoc merging is unlikely to adequately balance precision and recall in the situations of greatest scientific interest. That is, while bursting and spike overlaps may involve only a minority of spikes, the resulting sorting errors may disproportionately distort the interpretation of neuronal population dynamics. We thus conclude that uncertainty quantification in sorters' output is essential.

papers.title: Electroencephalographic activity patterns distinguish interdigitated default and frontoparietal networks
papers.abstract: The brain is comprised of distributed functional networks that operate on diverse time scales. Evidence from precision fMRI shows that canonical networks, including default (DN), frontoparietal control (FPCN), and dorsal attention (dATN), each fractionate into multiple finely interdigitated networks. However, as fMRI is blind to fast processes underlying neural communication, there remains a need to neurophysiologically characterize individual-level network fractionation. To address this need, we conducted a simultaneous EEG-fMRI study, including multiple sessions per individual, resting-state and task conditions, and carbon wire loop sensors for optimized artifact correction. Using precision network mapping, we discovered dissociable electrophysiological correlates of blood-oxygen-level-dependent activity for two networks within the boundaries of the canonical DN. One (DNa) related more positively with alpha and high-beta power, while another (DNb) related more negatively with theta and low-beta power. Univariate and machine learning analyses further revealed electrophysiological dissociations between networks within the canonical FPCN (FPCNa versus FPCNb) but not dATN. The network-specific electrophysiological activity patterns were reliable across sessions, only modestly variable between resting-state and demanding task conditions, and observable for neighboring nodes of different networks across multiple cortical zones. Our findings provide insight into rhythmic neural processes that fine-grained networks may engage to support divergent cognitive operations.

papers.title: Marked Mutants Allow for Rapid Non-Invasive Genotyping of Zebrafish by Visual Inspection Alone
papers.abstract: Genetic analysis in zebrafish relies heavily on invasive, labour-intensive molecular genotyping. This limits throughput and phenotypic analysis, particularly for homozygous mutants that lack readily detectable phenotypes at early developmental stages. To overcome these limitations, we adapted CRISPR-mediated knock-in strategies to insert complete secondary marker cassettes (including promoter, fluorophore and polyA), directly into coding exons of target loci. This simultaneously disrupts target gene function and permanently labels mutant alleles, which we term Marked Mutants. Crossing heterozygous Marked Mutant alleles targeting the same gene but carrying distinct fluorescent secondary markers linked to each allele, enables unambiguous non-invasive visual identification of wild-type, heterozygous and biallelic mutant progeny as early as 24 hours post fertilisation. To test the scalability and robustness of our approach, we generated eight independent Marked Mutant alleles targeting mitfa, tdp43 and tdpl, using secondary markers comprising hatching gland (he1.1), pancreas (ins) or pineal gland (exorh) promoters driving expression of GFP, RFP or BFP. We found germline transmission efficiencies comparable to conventional CRISPR mutagenesis, with approximately 30% of fluorescence-selected F0 adults transmitted on-target insertions to the F1 generation. All Marked Mutant alleles behaved as loss-of-function alleles, demonstrating effective disruption of target gene function. By combining four independent Marked Mutant alleles, each carrying a distinct fluorescent secondary marker, we could prospectively identify tdp43/tdpl double compound heterozygous embryos by visual inspection alone before phenotypic onset. Only embryos carrying all four Marked Mutant alleles developed the characteristic lethal double-knockout phenotype, while siblings carrying fewer alleles remained phenotypically normal. By eliminating routine PCR genotyping and invasive fin clipping, Marked Mutants simplify colony management, facilitate combinatorial genetics, reduce animal use, and provide a practical platform for rapid non-invasive zebrafish reverse genetics.

papers.title: Closed-loop acoustic stimulation promotes local slow oscillation train initiation and persistence in elderly adults
papers.abstract: Slow oscillations (SOs) during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep support memory consolidation and metabolic waste clearance. Aging is associated with reduced SO amplitude and density and disrupted temporal organization, characterized by more isolated events and shorter SO trains. We investigated whether closed-loop acoustic stimulation (CLAS) could enhance the initiation and persistence of rhythmic SO activity in elderly adults. Twenty-seven participants underwent a baseline night followed by an experimental night, during which online-detected SOs were either stimulated using CLAS (STIM; n = 16) or left unstimulated (SHAM; n = 11). We quantified the proportions of isolated and consecutive SOs, train-initiation probability, and SO train length. Analyses assessed local effects around online-detected SOs and global effects across NREM sleep using offline detection. Locally, CLAS reduced the proportion of isolated SOs and increased the proportion of consecutive SOs, train-initiation probability, and mean train length. Global overnight effects were weaker but directionally consistent, primarily reflecting a shift toward longer SO trains. These changes occurred without a significant between-group difference in the change in SO density, and local effects remained significant after adjustment for SO density. Thus, CLAS promoted sustained rhythmic activity beyond changes in SO occurrence. These findings suggest that CLAS can modify the temporal organization of SOs in elderly adults, supporting its potential to mitigate age-related disruptions in SO dynamics. Temporal organization measures may complement conventional amplitude and density measures when evaluating CLAS effects. Further studies should establish whether these changes translate into cognitive benefits or improvements in other aspects of brain health.

papers.title: Unpredictable chronic stress redistributes novelty-evoked exploratory space use and yields method-dependent identification of resilient-like archetypes in zebrafish
papers.abstract: Unpredictable chronic stress (UCS) produces heterogeneous behavioural outcomes, but identifying resilient individuals remains challenging because post-stress behaviour is multidimensional and classification depends on the analytical framework. We characterised novelty-evoked exploration in 178 adult zebrafish (89 unstressed reference, 89 UCS-exposed) using four Novel Tank Test variables: distance travelled, line crossings, upper-zone entries and upper-zone time, from a historical LAPCOM dataset from four independent cohorts. Behaviour was robustly normalised to control distributions within cohorts. In the unstressed population, principal component analysis revealed a dominant exploratory gradient (PC1 = 74.9%; PC2 = 18.7%), whereas weighted k-nearest-neighbour Louvain analysis yielded a stable two-profile partition. However, null-model inference and resampling did not support discrete behavioural populations, indicating a predominantly continuous reference architecture. UCS significantly redistributed individuals within this architecture (PERMANOVA: F(1,173) = 8.10, R2= 0.0423, p = 0.0016), reducing occupancy of the higher-exploration reference profile from 55.1% to 24.7%, while multivariate dispersion, Mahalanobis distance and global correlation structure showed no detectable differences. De novo Louvain analysis identified lower- and higher-exploration configurations, but correspondence with the control reference was asymmetric: all 44 lower-exploration fish mapped to the lower reference profile, whereas only 22 of 45 higher-exploration fish mapped to the higher reference profile. Thus, higher exploration after UCS was insufficient to define a resilient-like response. Across five analytical frameworks, resilient assignments ranged from 9 to 45 individuals and susceptible assignments from 23 to 68, with partial individual-level convergence. These findings support reference-integrated behavioural stratification for identifying resilient- and susceptible-like candidates for physiological, cellular and molecular validation.

papers.title: TileScope quantifies spatial gene expression relationships beyond colocalization
papers.abstract: Gene expression patterns within the same tissue region can exhibit similar correlation or enrichment, but still differ in their organization within regions and at their boundaries. We present TileScope, a framework for analysing genes and transcriptional programs within predefined tissue regions, their components and their contacts with neighbouring regions. TileScope combines regional enrichment, within-region correlation, cross-correlation over distance and expression differences near specific boundaries. Repeated spatial partitions and consensus aggregation show how these measurements depend on the grouping of spots or cells. Across 30 controlled constructions derived from glioblastoma and hepatocellular carcinoma data representing ten spatial expression scenarios, combined measurements separated arrangements that individual statistics left ambiguous, including coincident patches, gradients and expression localised at region boundaries. In 30 human glioblastoma sections, TileScope distinguished shared regional enrichment from internal covariation and identified hypoxia-associated expression localised at region boundary despite negligible within-region correlation. In newly acquired Visium profiles of control and myeloid-targeted MCT1-knockout (KO) orthotopic GL261 mouse gliomas, proliferation and myeloid programs were enriched in tumour peripheries but showed opposite within-periphery-region correlations. Proliferation was higher near the tumour-facing boundary in both samples, whereas myeloid expression was higher near the tumour-facing boundary in the control and farther within periphery in the KO condition. Xenium applications on glioblastoma and breast cancer samples demonstrated feasibility with irregularly spaced individual cells and different regional annotations. TileScope provides spatially explicit descriptions of gene and program relationships, linking their organization within tissue compartments to their sensitivity to aggregation.

papers.title: Functional Reconstitution of Human OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 in Proteoliposomes: Effect of Bicarbonate Gradients and Substrate-specific Stimulation on Transport
papers.abstract: The hepatic organic anion transporting polypeptides OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 are critical for the clearance of widely prescribed drugs, hepatotoxins, and endogenous metabolites. However, the thermodynamic driving force governing their transport has remained a subject of debate due to the complexity of cellular models. Here, we report a defined, reconstituted proteoliposome system to study the transport kinetics of isolated human OATP1B1 and OATP1B3. Through direct functional assays, real-time counter-ion tracking, and a novel ABCG2-OATP1B1 functional co-reconstitution, we identify an outwardly directed bicarbonate gradient as a thermodynamic driving force for concentrative substrate uptake. In contrast we find no evidence for the proposed role of reduced glutathione efflux as a possible driving force. Targeted mutagenesis experiments revealed that the conserved TM3 residue His115 is needed to couple the bicarbonate gradient to concentrative substrate uptake, mechanistically linking substrate antiport to local pH-sensitive bicarbonate processing. We also investigated the substrate-specific stimulatory effect of the green tea catechin epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) on OATP1B3 transport, confirming that this effect is intrinsic to OATP1B3, substrate specific, and does not need the involvement of other cellular proteins. Our findings define the energetic basis of OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 hepatic xenobiotic clearance.

papers.title: HLAResolver: A statistical framework for resolving HLA ambiguity in T-cell response data
papers.abstract: Large-scale models of T-cell recognition require training examples that specify the complete T-cell receptor (TCR)-peptide-human leukocyte antigen (HLA) complex. Multiplexed Identification of T-cell Receptor Antigen Specificity (MIRA) is a high-throughput assay that identifies TCRs associated with responses to specific peptides, but does not determine which HLA presents each peptide. Because a donor can carry up to six distinct class I HLA-A, HLA-B, and HLA-C alleles, each response may have several candidate presenting HLAs. To narrow this set of candidate presenting HLAs, we developed HLAResolver, a statistical framework that combines MIRA response patterns across HLA-typed donors with NetMHCpan predictions of peptide presentation. For each peptide, HLAResolver uses negative-binomial regression to jointly estimate associations between HLA alleles and TCR response counts, accounting for differences in assay yield. NetMHCpan eluted-ligand predictions guide sparse regularization, favoring alleles with stronger predicted presentation while allowing strong MIRA response evidence to support alternatives. To assess whether this integration provides an advantage over either approach alone, we compared HLAResolver with NetMHCpan, which predicts peptide-HLA presentation, and the Restrictor Analysis Tool for Epitopes (RATE), which infers HLA associations from T-cell response patterns. Using held-out MIRA experiments, we assessed each method's ability to predict observed responses and the number of candidate HLAs it assigned. At matched specificity for predicting MIRA responses, HLAResolver achieved higher sensitivity while selecting fewer candidate HLAs per peptide than either comparator.

papers.title: Allocating resources across time in a cumulative allocation game
papers.abstract: We investigate an alternative to decision under risk where players begin with an endowment of wealth, and their goal is to increase this wealth as rapidly as possible by repeatedly investing part of it. In such a Cumulative Allocation Game (CAG), expected wealth can grow exponentially but - if wealth ever goes to zero - the game is over and the participant wins nothing (ruin). CAGs can be used to model a wide range of biological and economic activity from casino gambling to animal foraging to stock market investment (Kelly Criterion). However, there is little previous research concerning human performance in CAGs and how it relates to human performance in similar decision-under-risk tasks. In two experiments we asked participants to complete four CAGs designed to allow us to test a series of hypotheses about human performance and compare it to normative play maximizing their log rate of growth. In the main experimental conditions, participants performance was initially close to normative but their proportion bet decreased by almost a factor of two over the course of the experiment. This reduction in proportion-bet decreased their expected rate of growth by roughly 25% - a substantial deviation from optimal. Why would participants systematically abandon a normative strategy? We conjecture that a possible reason is loss aversion, well documented in decision under risk. We conjecture that while loss aversion in decision under risk is sub-optimal, there is an intrinsic asymmetry between losses and gains in CAGs that could explain the loss aversion we observe.

papers.title: A Whole-Mouse-Brain Model of Coupled Neural Masses: Analysis of Network Dynamics
papers.abstract: Neural mass models coupled through empirical structural connectomes are widely used to simulate whole-brain activity, but the dynamics of the resulting large, delay-coupled networks are rarely analyzed directly. We present a dynamical systems analysis of 434 Jansen-Rit neural masses coupled by the Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas at the canonical single-node parameter values. Pseudo-arclength continuation of the network equilibria in the global coupling scale and in the baseline external input, with stability determined from the characteristic roots of the delayed linearization by Beyn's contour-integral method, indicates where the network must oscillate and where it can rest. Simulations show that the oscillatory regime is chaotic: the maximum Lyapunov exponent is positive for the empirical connectome, grows with network size and coupling scale, and is insensitive to the conduction delays, but it is suppressed when the arrangement of connection weights is flattened, shuffled, or rewired. The same weight modifications that suppress chaos drive the network toward full synchrony and abolish metastability, as measured by the Kuramoto order parameter. We discuss the consequences of these findings for fitting whole-brain neural mass models to empirical data.

papers.title: Protection against disseminated disease following reinfection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis requires CD8+ lymphocytes
papers.abstract: Concomitant immunity is protective adaptive immunity conferred by pre-existing infection against subsequent exposures. This phenomenon is effective in the context of human tuberculosis (TB) and has been successfully recapitulated in non-human primates (NHPs). We previously demonstrated that depletion of CD4 T cells prior to secondary challenge with Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) only partially abrogated protection, implicating a critical role for additional cell types. Here, we describe the effects of depleting CD8 expressing cells in this model. CD4+ T cells in the airway were unable to compensate for lost cytotoxicity due to CD8 depletion. Contrary to the results of CD4 depletion, CD8 depleted animals exhibited a unique inability to limit Mtb dissemination, with significant lymph node involvement despite a short 4-week infection. These data suggest that concomitant immunity relies on non-redundant roles played by CD8+ lymphocytes. Thus, future vaccines should be designed to induce effective responses by both CD4+ and CD8+ populations to maximize efficacy.

papers.title: Sensory recurrence and convergent integration in the C. elegans connectome
papers.abstract: The synaptic wiring of Caenorhabditis elegans has a global feed-forward architecture, from sensory to motor neurons. Yet, whole-brain optogenetic mapping shows that signals do not flow predominantly forward, and sensory neurons respond to more neurons than they drive. Where the wiring contains pathways leading back to their starting point is unclear. Here, we locate this recurrence using the feedback coefficient, derived from the Kubo-Martin-Schwinger framework for directed networks, which quantifies the proportion of walks reaching a neuron that originate from itself. The connectome has about three times more recurrence than strength-matched random networks, with the largest excess in sensory neurons, whereas random wiring places it on highly connected neurons. Along the thermotaxis pathway, this produces a recurrence gradient from thermosensory neurons to integrating interneurons. The ordering replicates in five reconstructions, including two independent adults, persists when reciprocal contacts are preserved or gap junctions removed, but vanishes with only short paths or loop counts. Convergence shows the reverse pattern, with every neuron receiving walks from fewer sources than in random wiring, especially sensory neurons. The wiring extends from a sensory periphery folding back on itself to interneurons and motor neurons integrating many sources, a candidate structural substrate for non-feed-forward signalling.

papers.title: Quantifying direct and indirect maternal effects on male vervets rank post-dispersal
papers.abstract: Early life experiences have important fitness consequences across animals, with maternal environments playing a crucial role in some species survival and reproduction during adulthood. A potential pathway linking maternal behaviour with individual fitness is dominance rank, which in some primates - like cercopithecines - is maternally inherited during the juvenile period and strongly linked to individual social behaviour and reproductive success. While females of these species maintain their rank for life in their natal group, males disperse and must integrate into new dominance hierarchies. In this context, the long-term effects of maternal characteristics on male rank post-dispersal and the potential of males social behaviour in mediating this relationship remains unexplored. Using 16 years of data from a wild vervet monkey population (Chlorocebus pygerythrus), we tested the effects of maternal rank, grooming and proximity on the rank males acquired their first year post-dispersal. In addition, we measured the extent to which the males own social behaviour both pre- and post-dispersal mediate this relationship combining Bayesian social networks with mediation analyses. We did not find support for a mediating effect of males social behaviour on the relationship between maternal characteristics and male rank post-dispersal. Instead, we found that maternal characteristics influence males social behaviour during the juvenile period and that males own social behaviour post-dispersal (grooming out-degree) is related to their rank when they integrate into a new group. In addition, we found that consistency in males social behaviour pre- to post-dispersal is restricted to grooming behaviour, highlighting the different roles of proximity and grooming relationships in vervet societies. Taken together these results reveal very limited long-term effects of maternal characteristics on male behaviour during the heavily underexplored process of dispersal and the flexibility of male vervet social behaviour following a change in social environment.

papers.title: State-dependent emergence of coupling between oscillatory and aperiodic neural activity
papers.abstract: Neural oscillations and aperiodic activity are two quintessential mesoscopic-level features arising from shared circuits, yet what governs their relationship remains unclear. Here we show that coupling between oscillatory frequency and aperiodic exponent is sporadic and state-dependent. Bias-reduced analyses of 3,245 intracranial contacts from 61 awake subjects showed significant coupling in only <13% of contacts per band. A connectome-constrained dynamical model predicted that neither changes of input to local circuit nor removal of long-range connections modulated the coupling; whereas stronger local inhibitory feedback drove covariation between oscillatory frequency and aperiodic exponent. The model predictions were supported by three independent experiments: transcranial stimulation shifted each component independently and focal ablation of remote cortical tissues did not change coupling; whereas coupling emerged during seizures that altered local excitatory-inhibitory balance. These results suggest that the relation between periodic and aperiodic neural activity is neither intrinsically independent nor coupled, but determined by local circuit states.

papers.title: Extracellular DDR1 targeting remodels collagen-rich tumor stroma and local immunity
papers.abstract: Collagen rich stroma can restrict immune cell access and sustain immune exclusion in solid tumors, but strategies that directly target extracellular matrix organizing receptors remain limited. Here, we develop cross reactive nanobody Fc proteins against extracellular discoidin domain receptor 1 (DDR1) and identify DDR1nb 3 Fc as a lead molecule with activity in immunocompetent mammary and pancreatic tumor models, including an orthotopic pancreatic model. Tumor control is accompanied by altered collagen architecture and remodeling of the intratumoral immune compartment rather than consistent direct tumor-cell growth inhibition. Single cell profiling with mouse level compositional and pseudobulk analyses reveals reproducible pathway level remodeling of tumor associated neutrophils, while Ly6G positive cell depletion significantly modifies the antitumor effect of DDR1nb 3 Fc. These findings identify extracellular DDR1 as an actionable regulator of collagen rich tumor stroma and support its targeting as a strategy to reshape the tumor microenvironment and promote tumor control.

papers.title: Brain-wide representations of olfactory behavior in C. elegans
papers.abstract: Olfactory navigation emerges from dynamic interactions between sensory input, brain activity state and the animal's own movements. In C. elegans, a compact nervous system enables brain-wide imaging in behaving animals exposed to controlled olfactory environments, with an undulatory locomotion that reduces navigation to transitions among forward runs, reversals, and turns. Here, we used tracking microscopy to record and compare brain-wide neural activity in crawling worms navigating spatial odor gradients or isotropic environments, and in immobilized worms responding to temporal odor pulses. Across conditions, we identified strongly correlated brain-wide activity patterns spanning olfactory sensory neurons, interneurons, and premotor interneurons. Comparisons between navigation in odor gradients and exploration in isotropic environments revealed a compact functional circuit linking olfactory sensory neurons, interneurons, and premotor neurons. Comparisons between different odors distinguished sensory activity relationships associated with odor identity from a shared sensorimotor circuit for navigational movement. Comparisons between crawling and immobilized animals revealed profound differences in motor-state transitions and brain-wide correlation structure, further demonstrating the dependence of sensory representations and motor decision-making on behavioral context. Our findings reveal a functional organization linking olfactory sensory activity to navigational movement and show how this organization depends on behavioral state and environmental context.

papers.title: A novel 5-HT2A receptor-linked signalling pathway involving NAADP-mediated lysosomal Ca2+ release
papers.abstract: Currently there is major research interest in the therapeutic potential of serotonergic psychedelic drugs across a range of neuropsychiatric disorders1-3. Such drugs exert psychedelic and neuroplastic effects, both likely linked to therapeutic outcomes, via agonist action at the 5-HT2A receptor4-7. This receptor is assumed to generate downstream intracellular signalling via an interaction with either Gq protein coupling and formation of the second messenger inositol trisphosphate (IP3), or through triggering the effector {beta}-arrestin2. Central to the IP3 pathway is mobilisation of Ca2+ stored in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Here, we report the unexpected discovery that the 5-HT2A receptor also signals via an additional second messenger, nicotinic acid adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NAADP), which mobilises Ca2+ release from lysosomal stores. This effect was revealed through measurement of changes in cellular NAADP levels, pharmacological inhibition of NAADP and direct biosensor measurement of lysosomal Ca2+ release and was produced not only by 5-HT but also by a range of psychedelic drugs in a receptor-specific manner. Moreover, genetic ablation of the NAADP pathway reduced markers of both hallucinogenic and neuroplastic effects of psychedelic drug administration in mouse models. These findings reveal the involvement of a novel, therapeutically relevant signalling pathway in psychedelic drug action.

papers.title: Oligodendrocytes may provide the extra density of α-synuclein filaments from multiple system atrophy
papers.abstract: Prion-like templated seeding of a-synuclein filaments is thought to underlie the spreading of multiple system atrophy (MSA) and other synucleinopathies through the brain. Here, we used -synuclein filaments extracted from the brains of individuals with MSA to induce seeded aggregation in undifferentiated human neuroblastoma SH-SY5Y cells, human iNeurons, mixed primary murine cortical cells and murine oligodendrocyte-enriched primary cultures, all overexpressing human -synuclein, followed by determination of the cryo-EM structures of the seeded filaments. Whereas MSA seeds comprise two protofilaments with an unidentified non-proteinaceous density located between protofilaments, seeding resulted in the formation of filaments with a single protofilament. Only the seeded structures derived from oligodendrocytes contained an extra density that resembled that of the seeds. This suggests that oligodendrocytes may provide the chemical component that is responsible for the extra density at the protofilament interface of MSA filaments. In support, the injection of MSA seeds into the striatum of transgenic mice expressing human -synuclein under the control of the oligodendrocyte-specific proteolipid protein promoter, also yielded seeded filaments with a single protofilament and a similar extra density.

papers.title: Detecting deception in event narratives: the analysis of response latencies and error rates to unexpected questions.
papers.abstract: Deception is a central phenomenon in the study of human behaviour, and in forensic and investigative contexts it assumes significance due to its potential consequences. Although the unexpected questions technique has shown promising results, its application to the narration of a false autobiographical event remains underexplored. This study aims to fill this gap using the unexpected questions technique in an investigative interview setting. A total of 60 participants were randomly divided into two groups: the honest group was asked to describe their most recent day trip, while the deceptive group was asked to memorise a narrative describing a day trip. Both groups underwent an audio-recorded interview containing control, expected and unexpected questions. The results showed that both groups exhibited longer response latencies and higher error and inaccuracy rates in response to unexpected questions, but these indices were significantly higher in the deceptive group (p = .022 for response latency, uncorrected for multiple comparisons; p < .001 for error and inaccuracy rates). The findings suggest that longer response times and higher error and inaccuracy rates during unexpected questions may reflect not only the difficulty of the questions, but also additional cognitive demands faced by deceptive participants. Furthermore, these indicators were used to classify a subject as deceptive or honest using machine-learning algorithms. Within the sample, the model showed excellent cross-validated discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.967), suggesting that these indices may have diagnostic potential worthy of further investigation.

papers.title: Comparison of Hydroponic and Substrate-Based Methods for Screening Pea Genotypes for Resistance to Fusarium oxysporum.
papers.abstract: Abstract Pea (Pisum sativum L.) is one of the most economically and nutritionally important legumes due to its protein, vitamin, and mineral content. It also represents a source of income for producers. One of the major constraints on pea production is vascular wilt caused by the fungus Fusarium oxysporum. One strategy for disease management is the use of resistant varieties, which highlights the need for efficient methodologies to evaluate genotype responses to the pathogen. The objective of this study was to compare the efficiency of hydroponic and conventional substrate-based methods for evaluating the responses of pea genotypes to F. oxysporum under semi-controlled conditions. The hydroponic method used a modified Hoagland and Arnon nutrient solution with adjusted nutrient concentrations, whereas the conventional substrate-based method used plastic bags containing one kilogram of peat. The pathogen inoculum was obtained from pea plants affected by the disease in the municipality of Puerres, Narino, Colombia (isolate FPUE02). In both methods, six pea genotypes and an uninoculated control were evaluated using a randomized complete block design with three replicates. Plant growth parameters, disease incidence, and disease severity were recorded. The hydroponic method showed greater sensitivity in discriminating among susceptible genotypes and facilitated the monitoring of disease progression in the roots. These results highlight the potential of the hydroponic method as a tool for the phytopathological evaluation of pea germplasm.

papers.title: Hierarchical Uncertainty Transformation During Multimodal Comprehension
papers.abstract: Human communication requires combining information from different modalities even when each source is incomplete or ambiguous. Yet how uncertainty is coordinated as distinct semantic representations interact and converge remains unclear. Here we propose a hierarchical uncertainty transformation framework and test it across four gesture-speech experiments combining behavioral measures, information-theoretic modelling, and electroencephalography. Rather than being uniformly reduced as information accumulates, uncertainty changed its computational form across three interdependent levels: uncertainty within modality-specific semantic representations, bidirectional but asymmetric changes during cross-modal interaction, and uncertainty associated with multisensory convergence. These computational distinctions were accompanied by differentiated but temporally overlapping neural associations. Modality-specific uncertainty was expressed relatively early, whereas cross-modal transformation and convergence were most prominently associated with activity in the N400 range. Critically, both the neural expression and statistical coupling of these computational quantities varied with the semantic information available from gesture and speech. Together, these findings show that multimodal comprehension involves a context-dependent reorganization of uncertainty across interacting representations, providing a computational framework for understanding how coherent meaning emerges from heterogeneous and uncertain information.

papers.title: Bridging Bibliometrics and Biology: A Framework for the Relevance Scoring and Biological Stratification of Scalable MeSH Co-occurrence Networks
papers.abstract: Systematic literature review is often limited by the rigidity of search strings, which often miss non-obvious but highly relevant topics. Controlled vocabularies such as Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) facilitate the review process, but relationships between terms, and their relevance to a hypothesis of interest, are rarely stated explicitly. Presented here is a MeSH term extraction and networking technique, seeded by a single query for Allergic Contact Dermatitis, forming a "themed" network of terms. The resulting co-occurrence network is pruned by an unsupervised consensus of Metropolis-criterion likelihood search strategies, isolating a significant core subgraph and filtering out incidental co-indexing. Symmetrically normalized Article Relevancy Scores (ARS) then evaluate each article against the network's weighted terms across the annotated MEDLINE corpus, correcting for publication volume bias; Mean Relevancy Scoring (MRS) inverts these scores back onto the terms, scoring each MeSH term by the mean ARS of the articles carrying it to measure its specificity to the query. Benchmarked against the expert-curated Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) for Allergic Contact Dermatitis, the network recovered key event terminology and identified highly specific literature that standard retrieval methods overlooked. This data-driven approach quantitatively assesses associated MeSH terminology, extracting biologically relevant concepts and key relationships directly from the underlying structure of the literature. By automating the discovery of these latent connections, the framework provides a reproducible, scalable foundation for understanding the biomedical literary space surrounding a given search string, assisting systematic review creation, mechanistic pathway mapping, and hypothesis generation across biomedical disciplines.

papers.title: Organic Fertilizer Substitution for Chemical Fertilizer Improves Yield, Medicinal Active Compounds and Amino-Acid Profiles of Dendrobium officinale with Multi-Index Comprehensive Evaluation
papers.abstract: Dendrobium officinale (D. officinale) is an important medicinal horticultural crop. Its wild resources are threatened by over-exploitation. Fertilization regimes that balance yield and medicinal quality are urgently required for its artificial cultivation. This study aimed to investigate the effects of reduced chemical fertilizer combined with organic fertilizer on the yield and quality of D. officinale, and screen the optimal combined fertilization pattern, so as to provide a theoretical basis for standardized fertilization in D. officinale cultivation. A bed-cultivation experiment was carried out in greenhouse. Seven treatments were set up, including no fertilizer application (CK), sole chemical fertilizer (CF), 20% organic fertilizer substitution for chemical fertilizer (T20), 40% organic fertilizer substitution for chemical fertilizer (T40), 60% organic fertilizer substitution for chemical fertilizer (T60), 80% organic fertilizer substitution for chemical fertilizer (T80), and single organic fertilizer application (OM). Plant growth traits, yield, active ingredients, protein and amino acid components of D. officinale were determined. The membership function method was adopted for comprehensive evaluation of all treatments. Fertilization significantly improved the growth traits, yield and quality of D. officinale. Compared with CK, stem length, stem diameter and yield under fertilized treatments increased significantly by 15.5%-60.3%, 34.2%-64.7% and 65%-143.2%, respectively; dendrobine, polyphenols and alcohol-soluble extract contents increased significantly by 21.2%-83.7%, 14.0%-49.1% and 10.8%-26.9%, respectively. The highest plant growth and yield were observed under sole chemical fertilizer treatment. With the increase of organic fertilizer substitution ratio, plant growth and yield decreased gradually, while medicinal active ingredients including dendrobine, polysaccharides and flavonoids showed a trend of rising first and then falling. A total of 17 amino acids were detected in all treatments. T40 and T60 treatments significantly increased total amino acids, essential amino acids, as well as contents of medicinal, umami and bitter-tasting amino acids, whereas excessive proportion of organic fertilizer led to the decline of amino acid contents. Most growth, quality and amino acid indicators showed significant or extremely significant positive correlations with each other. The comprehensive evaluation order by membership function method was T40 > T60 > CF > T20 > T80 > OM > CK, and T40 obtained the highest comprehensive evaluation value. Sole chemical fertilizer contributes to yield increase of D. officinale, while combined application with organic fertilizer improves its medicinal quality. The 40?% organic substitution scheme provides a feasible fertilization strategy for high-quality greenhouse production of this medicinal horticultural plant.

papers.title: PhenoMe: An interactive AI framework for interpretable, microscopy-driven phenotyping
papers.abstract: Extracting meaningful biological patterns from microscopy image datasets requires tools that quantitatively connect visual similarities and experimental context. Deep learning models, and in particular novel foundation models, have the capacity to translate images into high-dimensional embeddings that can better represent complex visual patterns. Using these complex representations analytically and linking them to experimental information, it is possible to build advanced exploratory and phenotyping capabilities. Here, we present PhenoMe, an open-source, model-agnostic framework to handle pretrained foundation model-derived image representations alongside quantitative image properties and experimental metadata. PhenoMe integrates multiple scriptable and interactive workflows for embedding space visualisation, dimensionality reduction and clustering, similarity-based comparison and retrieval of representative images for each phenotype, among others. It also supports correlation analyses that link the embedding structure to interpretable image properties. We demonstrate PhenoMe's capabilities on seven public microscopy datasets, ranging from cell painting assays, nanoscale synaptic images, drug-response analyses and dynamic cell-phenotyping. These case studies show how readily available image representations can support data contextualisation, curation and analysis. Through guided notebooks, reproducible configurations, extensible model wrappers and a napari plugin, PhenoMe makes representation-based microscopy exploration accessible to researchers without dedicated technical expertise. PhenoMe lays the groundwork for applying foundation models and representation learning to microscopy data analysis.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling of human cartilage reveals coordinated changes in fibronectin expression, splicing, and receptor signaling during osteoarthritis progression
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is defined by progressive loss of articular cartilage, but how chondrocytes change as the disease advances is unclear because most studies have focused on end-stage tissue. We profiled human knee articular cartilage across the full range of macroscopic OA grade, from young healthy to aged severe OA donors, by bulk RNA sequencing of 92 knees, single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 108,600 chondrocyte nuclei from 30 donors and single-nucleus multiome sequencing of 24 of these donors, treating grade as a continuous variable. With increasing grade, cartilage increased extracellular matrix (ECM) synthesis and remodeling genes, lost glucocorticoid-responsive, lipid-metabolic and antioxidant programs, and changed the splicing of a small set of ECM transcripts, led by the extra domain B (EDB) exon of fibronectin (FN1). Nine chondrocyte clusters were present in every disease stage and formed a continuum ordered by cartilage zone and hypertrophic differentiation, with PRG4+ superficial and COL10A1+ hypertrophic chondrocytes as the only distinct cell types at its ends and a pre-hypertrophic state between them. With grade, all clusters shared a response in which ECM production rose and homeostatic programs fell, and they differed in which of its components was strongest: ECM production in the superficial cells, the secretory pathway in the hypertrophic and CYTL1+ cells, and inflammatory signaling in the ANXA1+ and CRISPLD2+ cells. Inferred communication between chondrocytes was remodeled with stage. FN1 was induced in every cluster in excess of its fibril-assembly machinery, together with the fibronectin-cleaving protease HTRA1, and FN1 signaling shifted in receptor use from integrin 5{beta}1 toward CD44 and, less robustly, v{beta}8, accompanied by a rise in TGF-{beta}/SMAD response genes. In four early-OA donors, tenascin-C was already largely induced and the FN1 receptor shift from 5{beta}1 toward CD44 was partly present, whereas the rise of FN1 outside superficial chondrocytes, of FGF1 and of developmental and ossification programs came with progression. Chromatin accessibility changed in the same direction across clusters, with regions linked to FN1 opening and regions linked to ITGA5 closing. OA progression in human cartilage therefore appears to be a change of chondrocyte state that differs in emphasis along a zonal and hypertrophic continuum and includes changes in fibronectin regulation, production, processing, and receptor engagement.

papers.title: PHATE-Derived Ancestry Coordinates Capture Continuous Population Structure in Human Genomic Data
papers.abstract: Population genetic data are increasingly visualized using low-dimensional embeddings as ancestry coordinates, yet how these methods represent population structure can depend strongly on sampling and construction choices.
