Multimodal data analysis identified the posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) as hub of stress processing beyond cognitive input, with increased glucose metabolism and attenuated BOLD deactivations. This was accompanied by reduced PCC connectivity within the default mode network and increased influence onto frontoparietal and dorsal attention networks. Endocrine stress responsivity was further reflected in lower resilience sub scores, failure to downregulate anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) metabolism during stress, and an inverse relationship between ACC glucose metabolism and anterior insula functional connectivity. These results indicate that acute psychosocial stress does not merely increase overall energy demand but reconfigures the relationship between regional metabolism and large-scale network organization, which further differs with individual endocrine stress responsivity. Our findings unify the roles of stress and the DMN in brain disorders, providing a multimodal framework for assessment in patient populations.

papers.title: Hydrogel crosslinking mechanisms influence the release and functional delivery of lipid nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Hydrogels have emerged as attractive vaccine delivery platforms because they enable controlled modulation of antigen availability. However, how different hydrogel environments affect the release and functionality of mRNA-loaded lipid nanoparticles (mRNA-LNPs) remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the release, stability, cellular uptake, and transfection capability of LNPs released from four hydrogel systems representing distinct crosslinking mechanisms: covalently crosslinked poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG), ionically crosslinked alginate, thermoresponsive Poloxamer 407 (P407), and protein-based Matrigel/collagen hydrogels. All hydrogel types enabled release of LNPs over days, with lower polymer concentrations generally exhibiting faster nanoparticle release. PEG offered greatest tunability of release kinetics; at the same time the recovery of the LNP-incorporated fluorescent dye DiI was reduced to about 80 %, indicating partial dye leakage. Alginate hydrogels exhibited recovery of DiI below 50 % and broader particle size distributions after release, while P407 hydrogels largely preserved LNP characteristics. CyroTEM analysis revealed that mRNA-LNPs kept at 37 , including those released from hydrogels, exhibited a more compact and electron-dense morphology than mRNA LNPs maintained at 4 . Notably, although quantitative recovery from Matrigel/collagen hydrogels was limited, released LNPs achieved approximately 80-90 % of the eGFP expression compared to mRNA-LNPs that have not been embedded. Importantly, cellular uptake and transfection experiments demonstrated that all investigated hydrogels released biologically active mRNA-LNPs capable of mediating protein expression. Moreover, our findings show that hydrogel composition is a critical determinant of mRNA-LNP release, stability, functional delivery and morphology of the released particles. This work provides design principles for the development of hydrogel-based mRNA delivery systems aimed at sustained antigen availability and prolonged vaccine responses.

papers.title: Functional pocketomes and complete allosteric maps of five protein kinases
papers.abstract: Protein kinases are central to regulation, dysregulated in many diseases, and the targets of a hundred clinically-approved drugs. Structural conservation of kinase active sites makes the development of selective inhibitors challenging. Targeting allosteric sites can increase selectivity, overcome resistance mutations, and activate kinases. However, most kinases have no known allosteric sites. Moreover, the conservation of allosteric regulation in proteins with the same structural fold is unclear. Here, we address this question by using >390,000 measurements of mutational effects on activity and abundance to construct complete comparative energetic and allosteric maps of five human protein kinase domains: SRC, FGR, JNK2/MAPK9, ZAK/MAP3K20, and TSSK2. For inhibition, all five kinases have distance-dependent allosteric regulation. However allostery is anisotropic, and each protein has a distinct allosteric architecture and surface to therapeutically target. A set of inhibitory allosteric pockets close to the active site is conserved in all five proteins, but more distal allosteric pockets are protein-specific. These include pockets that are activatory in one kinase and inhibitory in another. Differences in allosteric regulation are particularly striking for activation, where the allosteric maps are highly diverged. Our results show that proteins with the same structural fold have different energetic architectures and allosteric pockets. Mapping the 'functional pocketomes' of kinases and other clinically-important targets should empower the development of more selective therapeutics.

papers.title: Pangenome Graph Node-Phenotype Association shows GWAS-like quality results with only few individuals
papers.abstract: Purpose: We introduce GraNPA (Graph Node-Phenotype Association), a method that performs a phenotype-sequence association analysis on a pangenome vari- ation graph (PVG). This PVG is built using a small number of individual genome sequences and does not require additional population materials or kinship information for qualitative phenotypes. This approach minimizes the number of individuals required for association studies and mitigates the impact of reference bias in variant calling within these types of analyses. Background: A PVG is a representation of the multiple alignment of a set of complete genomes. It contains all variations, ranging from single nucleotide poly- morphisms (SNPs) to large structural variations (SVs), and these are represented as nodes in the graph. By integrating phenotype information within these nodes, we can assign a Score (S ) to each one and identify regions related to the phe- notype directly within the PVG. These regions represent statistically significant shifts in S distribution, indicating their involvement in the phenotype. Finally, GraNPA provides their positions and scores for further analysis. Results: This method was tested using different simulated contexts and two publicly available datasets: the Sub1A gene locus for Asian rice Oryza sativa in a 13 individuals PVG, and the insertion responsible for the white-headed in cattle (Bos taurus) with a PVG of 24 individuals. Source code of GraNPA is available here https://forge.ird.fr/diade/graphgwas/granpa under GNU GPLv3. Conclusion: GraNPA was able to identify the expected area in two simulated datasets, as well as the loci responsible for these two known traits, using only a few dozen complete genomes from these PVGs. Although this method is currently limited to qualitative phenotypes, it paves the way for more efficient methods that rely on PVGs and a small number of individuals.

papers.title: Kinetics and Evolution-guided Design of High Fidelity CRISPR-Cas Endonucleases
papers.abstract: Finding high-fidelity CRISPR-Cas variants is critical for both the precision of in vitro DNA detection and the safety of in vivo gene-editing therapeutics. However, the large size of the Cas enzymes and the distinct selection criteria between its natural evolution and clinical practice lead to extensive experimental trials and limited success rate for de novo design, directed evolution and protein language model (PLM)-based filtering. Here, we present a physics-driven, PLM-assisted approach that utilizes atomistic molecular dynamics simulations and automated path searching to efficiently obtain the atom-level kinetic insights, including the transition state structures, for the conformational changes of R-loop formation that dictate the off-target DNA recognition and cleavage by Cas. We show that these kinetic insights can pinpoint the fidelity-diminishing protein residues during the early stage of target recognition. Integrated with PLM-filtering of the mutants on these sites, this approach identified high-fidelity SpyCas9 and FnCas12a variants (4.49-fold and 6.69-fold increase respectively from wild-type), surpassing previously reported counterparts at minimal cost of only a few wet-lab validations (cellular genome-editing and ribonucleoprotein cleavage assays respectively).

papers.title: Guide-tree bias of whole genome alignment can mislead phylogenomic analyses
papers.abstract: Whole-genome alignment (WGA) is widely used for genome-scale phylogenetic inference, and most scalable WGA pipelines rely on progressive alignment guided by a pre-specified tree. Among progressive whole-genome aligners, Progressive Cactus is a successful state-of-the-art method. However, analyses of real and simulated avian data indicate that guide-tree choice can influence downstream tree inference; star guide trees do not remove this effect and can exacerbate long-branch attraction artefacts. We have developed a consensus strategy based on the Progressive Cactus framework by generating a small set of alternative guide-tree alignments and retaining only homology relationships consistently recovered across all alignments. In simulation experiments, consensus alignments improve precision, bring inferred site-pattern frequency distributions closer to those of the true alignments, and recover more true splits than single guide-tree alignments. In a real landbird (Telluraves) dataset, we observe a strong bias towards single binary guide trees and long-branch attraction for less resolved trees. While the reconstructed tree still depends on the phylogenetic method and taxa sampling, our consensus alignment has no clear bias. We implemented a hierarchical consensus workflow that only locally resolves uncertainty in the guide tree. Therefore, the computational cost increases only moderately, for example by an estimated 68 percent for a recently published large-scale alignment of more than 300 modern birds (Neoaves) taxa.

papers.title: Evolutionary Coupling of Flagellar Motility and Type VI Secretion Systems Across Bacteria
papers.abstract: Bacteria use both motility and antagonism to compete in spatially structured environments, but whether these traits evolve together across broad bacterial diversity remains unclear. We developed a spatial kin-competition model predicting that motility should couple robustly with contact-dependent weapons by increasing encounter rates with competitors, whereas coupling with diffusible weapons should be weaker and context-dependent. To examine the evolutionary hypotheses motivated by the model, we performed a comprehensive analysis of 11,365 bacterial genomes across the bacterial Tree of Life (ToL). By utilising large-scale homology-based searches, we annotated flagellar, T6SS, and bacteriocin components and then applied phylogenetic comparative models to examine evolutionary associations. T6SS presence was strongly associated with flagellar motility: T6SS-positive lineages were predominantly flagellated, and BayesTraits supported a dependent model of FliC and T6SS evolution. In contrast, bacteriocins did not show detectable evolutionary coupling with flagellar motility. Transition-rate analyses further indicated that T6SS gain was strongly biased towards motile bacterial lineages, even though T6SS loss was common overall. These results indicate different macroevolutionary associations of flagellar motility with T6SS and bacteriocins, consistent with the qualitative hypothesis motivated by our model.

papers.title: Microfluidic generation of alginate microbeads containing in situ-formed apical papilla stem cell spheroids and NecroX-5-loaded nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSC) are key players in regenerative medicine due to their immunomodulatory properties and ability to promote tissue repair. However, their therapeutic efficacy is often limited by rapid clearance following transplantation. MSC spheroids have shown enhanced functional properties, and we hypothesize that encapsulating them within hydrogel microbeads could offer additional protection and improve their viability. We developed a continuous, single-emulsion droplet-based microfluidic protocol that forms MSC spheroids in situ within alginate droplets overnight (In-Bead), before cross-linking and bead retrieval. Unlike double-emulsion approaches, the single-emulsion format yields homogeneously distributed nanomedicines, and the short, cell-permissive cross-linking produces ultra-soft, tissue-mimetic (~150 Pa) beads that remain retrievable. SCAP were successfully encapsulated within 275 um alginate microbeads, forming spheroids of approximately 80 um in diameter. Encapsulated SCAP spheroids retained their immunomodulatory properties. The process was further optimized by incorporating nanomedicines into the alginate solution before the formation of droplets, thus forming hybrid beads (Sph.Beads/NP). Nanomedicines were loaded with NecroX-5, a necrosis inhibitor, to improve SCAP viability further. Live/Dead assays indicated a protective effect of the nanomedicines, supporting the potential of this system for advanced cell delivery in regenerative applications.

papers.title: Censoring-aware Gaussian process modeling identifies time informative functional dynamics associated with spoilage status of modified atmosphere packaged broiler meat
papers.abstract: Microbial spoilage of packaged meat is driven by complex microbial succession and related metabolic activity, yet conventional shelf-life assessment is mainly based on shelf-life studies relying on culturing and sensory analysis. In routine quality assurance, results are obtained retrospectively, and they are only indirectly linked to the metabolic activity related to sensory deterioration. Functional, time informative approaches that capture the active metabolic state of the spoilage microbiome and predict the rate of spoilage are lacking. We developed a censoring-aware Gaussian process (CAGP) framework to model longitudinal pathway expression profiles from broiler meat metatranscriptomes collected over consecutive storage days at 4 or 6{degrees}C. Samples were annotated using odor-based sensory scores defining fresh, early-spoilage, and late-spoilage phases. Because observed zeros in pathway-level data may reflect non-detection rather than true absence, the model treats low values as left-censored observations below a detection threshold while estimating smooth temporal trajectories with uncertainty. In leave-one-out prediction within the 4{degrees}C time series, predicted sampling days differed from the true days by an average of 0.43 days, and predicted spoilage phases agreed with the sensory classification. Trajectories learned at 4{degrees}C also transferred to an independent 6{degrees}C time series at the spoilage-phase level, suggesting that shared functional spoilage programs are preserved despite temperature-dependent changes in spoilage rate. Cross-entropy ranking further identified pathway modules carrying time- and phase-informative signals across temperatures. Overall, this framework provides a probabilistic approach for linking metatranscriptomic functional dynamics to sensory spoilage progression, supporting shelf-life assessment beyond retrospective microbial enumeration. Microbial spoilage of packaged meat is driven by complex microbial succession and related metabolic activity. The current tools to assess product quality and determine shelf life do not fully serve food manufacturers. Functional time informative approaches that capture the active metabolic state of the spoilage microbiome and predict the rate of spoilage are lacking. We developed a censoring-aware Gaussian process (CAGP) framework to model longitudinal pathway expression profiles of broiler meat spoilage microbiomes. We used two series of metatranscriptomic data generated in our previous study of samples stored either at 4 or 6{degrees}C. The samples had also been annotated with odor-based sensory scores defining fresh, early-spoilage, and late-spoilage phases. The 4{degrees}C time series were used to develop and evaluate the temporal prediction framework, while the independent 6{degrees}C series were used to assess whether the functional spoilage trajectories learned at 4{degrees}C could generalize across temperature conditions. The CAGP models smooth temporal trajectories of pathway activity while accounting for uncertainty and for observed zero values that may arise from non-detection rather than true biological absence. In this framework, zeros are treated as left-censored observations below a soft detection threshold. Within the 4{degrees}C time series, leave-one-replicate-out (LORO) and leave-one-day-out (LODO) analyzes predicted the sampling time of held-out samples with mean absolute errors of 0.43 and 0.78 days, respectively. In the LORO analysis, predicted spoilage phases also largely agreed with the sensory classification. When trajectories learned at 4{degrees}C were applied to the independent 6{degrees}C samples, the predicted samples retained their temporal ordering along the spoilage trajectory, suggesting the preservation of shared functional spoilage programs despite temperature-dependent differences in spoilage rates. Cross-entropy ranking further identified pathway modules carrying time- and phase-informative signals across temperatures. Overall, this framework provides a probabilistic approach for linking metatranscriptomic functional dynamics to sensory spoilage progression, supporting shelf-life assessment beyond retrospective microbial enumeration.

papers.title: Convergent genome- and gene-level constraints shape repeated environmental adaptation in grasses
papers.abstract: Grasses (Poaceae) dominate terrestrial ecosystems and sustain global food security, yet the genomic principles enabling their repeated adaptation to extreme environments remain unresolved. Combining dense phylogenomic sampling, global environmental data, and genomic large language models (gLLMs), we characterize the mutational targets underlying environmental shift across 687 genomes from 561 species spanning 17 climate zones. We identify 17-30 phylogenetically independent transitions into extreme temperature, water, and soil environments, accompanied by convergent shifts in genome-scale molecular properties, including the Nitrogen-to-Carbon balance and the biosynthetic cost of the proteome. Our gLLMs-informed phylogenetic mixed modeling framework identifies 330 genes that repeatedly associated with distinct axes of environmental variation, highlighting the importance of protein modification and localization within extracellular and organellar compartments. Overlaying independent convergent selection tests identifies 27 high-confidence candidates for further characterization. Together, our results show that grass adaptation is canalized by layered constraints at genome-wide and gene-specific scales, producing predictable evolutionary trajectories.

papers.title: Dynamic adhesion device of phage OE33PA drives Gram-positive host recognition
papers.abstract: Bacteriophages (phages) infecting Gram-positive bacteria must bind to host receptors across thick cell walls to initiate infection, yet the underlying structural mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we report cryo-electron microscopy structures of the Oenococcus oeni siphophage OE33PA, providing the first high-resolution view of a phage infecting this wine-industry bacterium. While the overall virion architecture is conserved, the adhesion device displays distinctive features. Its receptor-binding proteins adopt multiple orientations, revealing an intrinsically dynamic assembly. In situ cryo-electron tomography captures distinct conformations upon host attachment, providing rare structural insight into interactions with Gram-positive hosts. Functional assays further show that a mobile carbohydrate-binding module in the distal tail protein mediates host cell binding. Additionnally, the tape measure protein adopts a hexameric organization, updating the prevailing trimeric model in siphophages. Together, these findings reveal a dynamic adhesion device in a phage infecting Gram-positive bacteria and highlight the structural and functional diversity of phages.

papers.title: Artificial Reactivation of a Cocaine-Associated Ensembles in the Dorsal Dentate Gyrus Attenuates Cocaine Prime-Induced Reinstatement of Drug-Seeking
papers.abstract: Relapse-prevention strategies aimed at reducing relapse following abstinence primarily focus on reducing cravings that lead to drug-seeking triggered by stress, drug-related cues, or re-exposure to the drug. Because addictive drugs form persistent associative contextual memories, we investigated how reactivation of cocaine-related hippocampal memories influences subsequent drug-seeking. Here, we tagged dorsal dentate gyrus (dDG) memory ensembles involved in encoding either a first or fourth cocaine exposure (15mg/kg, i.p) in male and female c57BL/6 mice using a TetTag approach. Mice underwent cocaine conditioned place preference (CPP), extinction, and reinstatement. We assessed whether optical reactivation of tagged cocaine-related ensembles could substitute for a cocaine priming injection to reinstate CPP, whether reactivation altered cocaine-induced reinstatement, and if these effects differed depending on stage of drug exposure. We also compared these effects to reactivation of saline-associated ensembles. Cocaine produced robust locomotor activation during conditioning and sensitization developed across repeated drug exposures. Reactivation of a cocaine-related engram alone did not reinstate CPP. However, reactivation of the first cocaine exposure engram attenuated cocaine-induced reinstatement. In contrast, reactivation of the fourth exposure engram did not confer this protective effect. Interestingly, reactivation of saline-associated ensembles also reduced cocaine-induced reinstatement specifically in females, suggesting dDG ensemble reactivation may modulate relapse-related behavior through interference or neuromodulatory disruption of cocaine-associated representations, consistent with our prior work. These findings raise the possibility that early contextual experiences form competing or destabilizing representations that interfere with later cocaine-seeking when reactivated. Females also displayed greater sensitivity to locomotor-inducing effects of cocaine memory reactivation, although this was dissociated from CPP. Together, these findings show that cocaine memories are distinct across drug experience and selective reactivation of dDG engrams can differentially influence drug-seeking.

papers.title: Increased Beta-Band Input to Spinal Motor Neurons is Not Confined to the Responding Muscle During a Go/No-Go Task
papers.abstract: During movement preparation and inhibition, the sensorimotor cortex shows alpha- and beta-band oscillations that are also expressed in the discharge of spinal motor neurons. Whether this oscillatory activity is confined to the motor neurons innervating the muscles involved in the prepared action is unknown. Here we combined electroencephalography with recordings of spinal motor neurons innervating the tibialis anterior. Participants held a submaximal dorsiflexion while performing a Go/No-Go task in which the instructed response was either a ballistic dorsiflexion or handgrip, making the tibialis anterior the responding or a non-responding muscle, respectively. Alpha- and beta-band power increased after the imperative cue in both cortical activity and motor neuron output, including when the tibialis anterior was not involved in the response. Because power modulations in motor neuron output can be confounded by the concurrent change in discharge rate, we assessed the oscillatory activity shared across motor neurons by calculating coherence between disjoint subsets, which is largely insensitive to discharge rate. We then used simulation-based inference to identify synaptic input modulations compatible with our observations. These analyses indicated that beta-band common input increased whether or not the tibialis anterior was involved in the response, whereas alpha-band input increased only when it was the responding muscle. The concurrent decrease in discharge rate and torque was attributed to reduced net excitatory drive, whereas alpha- and beta-band inputs accounted for the increase in synchronisation. These results demonstrate that cue-related oscillatory inputs reach spinal motor neurons more broadly than classically assumed, and shape motor neuron synchronisation.

papers.title: Naked antisense oligonucleotides access the cytosol during early endocytic trafficking
papers.abstract: Phosphorothioate-modified antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) enter cells, but their site of productive escape remains uncertain. We combined live-cell imaging and ratiometric pH measurements to follow a Malat1-targeting ASO internalized without a delivery vehicle. In U2OS cells, less than 4% of internalized ASO reached the nucleus under conditions that reduced Malat1 RNA by >90%. Most ASO accumulated in late endosomes, endolysosomes and lysosomes as foci and broadly distributed luminal signal. These compartments underwent neutralization without detectable membrane rupture or galectin-3 recruitment. ASO foci showed constrained motion, consistent with association with endolysosomal constituents. L-leucyl-L-leucine methyl ester-induced membrane damage or Calcium dependent lysosome exocytosis released dextran while retaining luminal ASO. Loss of the stress-granule scaffolding proteins G3BP1/2 modestly enhanced ASO activity without detectable endolysosomal damage. Tantalosin, a small molecule that perturbs endosomal recycling, redistributed the ESCRT-III protein IST1 to endosomes. It enhanced early escape of SYTOX Green and ASOs, detected by nuclear accumulation, and increased Malat1 knockdown, with cell-type-dependent responses. Tantalosin did not detectably increase nuclear ASO accumulation after sequestration in late compartments. These findings place productive ASO escape early in endocytic trafficking, most likely in early or recycling endosomes, before sequestration in largely nonproductive late compartments.

papers.title: Gut microbiome stratification reveals functional metabolic signatures linked to host health
papers.abstract: The human gut microbiome exhibits reproducible taxonomic configurations, yet the ecological processes linking them to health remain unclear. We applied the five-enterosignature (ES) model to 5,169 metagenomes of Le French Gut participants and developed a rule-based framework that stratifies continuous microbiome variation into interpretable partitions. Across these partitions, hydrogen disposal pathways formed distinct functional gradients, reproduced in an international meta-cohort (n = 5,107). Partitions dominated by Prevotella enterosignature showed greater sulfate-reduction potential, ES-Firmicutes-associated partitions greater methanogenesis potential, and ES-Bacteroides-enriched partitions greater acetogenesis potential. The latter were also characterized by oxidative-stress and mucin-degradation signatures, altered fecal mucin O-glycosylation, and less favorable health indicators, including more frequent digestive symptoms, higher perceived stress, and more psychotropic drug prescriptions. These patterns were also accompanied by distinct dietary profiles. Our findings link hydrogen metabolism, redox-associated functions, mucin utilization, diet, and host health, and support enterosignature-based partitioning for cross-cohort comparisons and future stratified interventions.

papers.title: Revealing the Hidden Landscape of Public Metabolomics Data Reuse in MetaboLights
papers.abstract: Introduction: Metabolomics has historically lagged behind transcriptomics and proteomics in the scale and formalisation of public data reuse. Building on earlier manually assessed studies of metabolomics data reuse, this study provides an updated characterisation of confirmed reuse in MetaboLights. Objectives: This study aimed to characterise confirmed reuse of MetaboLights datasets in the published literature, quantifying its volume, reuse type, temporal trajectory, and dataset-level concentration. Methods: MetaboLights dataset accessions (MTBLS#) were used to retrieve candidate publications from five literature sources via a Python-based pipeline. Candidates were manually validated and classified by primary category and scientific domain; analytical modality was assigned from dataset metadata. Results: There were 274 confirmed reuse publications: Method or Tool Development (64.6%), Secondary Biological Analysis (16.8%), Data Integration or Meta-analysis (13.5%), and Educational Use or Protocol Illustration (5.1%). LC-MS was assigned to 70.1% of confirmed reuse publications; cumulative counts increased over time, and dataset-level reuse was highly asymmetric. Conclusion: Within the detected publications, MetaboLights datasets were predominantly reused for computational method development with secondary biological analysis being less frequent at present, underscoring the repository's value as a resource to obtain benchmarking datasets. Identifier-based searches may miss reuse activities when MTBLS identifiers are not consistently cited, reinforcing the community imperative for standardised dataset reporting and high-quality metadata deposition.

papers.title: A unified photosensitizer platform for in situ DNA, RNA, and protein directed proximity labeling
papers.abstract: Cells depend on the spatial organization of proteins, RNA, and DNA into discrete subcellular compartments. Previous methods have largely centered on measuring spatial organization based on only one of these biomolecular classes at a time. Here, we demonstrate that POCA photocatalytic proximity labeling can serve as a unified photosensitizer-based platform for profiling the proximal proteomes of protein, RNA, and DNA targets within a single experimental framework. We show that POCA can harness standard immunofluorescence or in situ hybridization workflows to specifically target organic fluorophore photosensitizers to intracellular targets for proximity labeling in fixed cells. POCA-targeted proximity labeling requires minimal cellular input and does not require genetic engineering. Additionally, POCA photosensitizers are selected to also be fluorescent, enabling direct confirmation of on-target localization by imaging prior to proteomic analysis. To demonstrate broad utility, we apply POCA across multiple molecular targets spanning protein, RNA, and genomic DNA, including components of the nuclear pore complex, nucleolus, nuclear speckles, telomeres, and pericentromeric heterochromatin. By anchoring proximity labeling to both a protein and an RNA within the same nuclear compartment, we resolve shared and distinct proximal proteomes from orthogonal molecular perspectives.

papers.title: Regulatory plasticity of the rdar biofilm morphotype in clinical uropathogenic Escherichia coli and its modulation by ciprofloxacin
papers.abstract: Background: Red, dry and rough (rdar) biofilm formation in Escherichia coli is characterized by the coordinated production of extracellular cellulose and amyloid curli fimbriae. Although rdar biofilm formation has been extensively characterized in laboratory strains, its clinical relevance and implications for antimicrobial treatment remain poorly understood. Methods: We screened 146 consecutive E. coli isolates from patients with urinary tract infections in Lahore, Pakistan (2017-2019) for Congo red morphotypes at 28 degrees C and 37 degrees C. Antimicrobial susceptibility was determined by disc diffusion and compared between morphotypes using the Fisher exact test. Fourteen isolates were whole-genome sequenced, the csgD-csgBA intergenic region was aligned, and csgD expression was quantified by qRT-PCR. The effect of 10 micrograms/mL ciprofloxacin on rdar morphotype expression, matrix ultrastructure and biofilm formation was examined in ciprofloxacin-resistant isolates (MIC at least 128 micrograms/mL). Results: Rdar-like colony morphotypes were expressed by 36.3% (53/146) of isolates at 28 degrees C and 29.5% (43/146) at 37 degrees C. Nucleotide polymorphisms in the csgD-csgBA intergenic region clustered within annotated OmpR, IHF and CsgD binding regions and were associated with, but did not individually predict, the mode of rdar morphotype expression. Isolates carrying the rdar morphotype were distributed across diverse E. coli phylogroups and sequence types. Resistance to aztreonam, cefuroxime and cephradine was more frequent among smooth and white isolates, whereas resistance to nitrofurantoin was more frequent among isolates rdar-positive at 28 degrees C (45.2% versus 20.2%, p = 0.0097); fluoroquinolone resistance did not differ between morphotypes. Subinhibitory ciprofloxacin (10 micrograms/mL) suppressed rdar biofilm formation, disrupted extracellular matrix architecture and abolished surface colonization on glass, in ciprofloxacin-resistant isolates. Conclusions: Our findings establish the rdar morphotype as a clinically relevant biofilm phenotype in uropathogenic E. coli and show that subinhibitory ciprofloxacin suppresses rdar biofilm formation in ciprofloxacin-resistant isolates. These results underscore the importance of considering antibiotic-mediated modulation of biofilm behavior when interpreting treatment responses and designing strategies to combat persistent urinary tract infections.

papers.title: A multimodal dataset of EEG, eye-tracking, and physiological signals during naturalistic smartphone interactions
papers.abstract: Smartphones have become pervasive tools for communication, information consumption, and digital interaction, yet the neurophysiological dynamics associated with naturalistic smartphone use remain insufficiently characterized. Here, we present a multimodal physiological dataset collected during ecologically valid smartphone interaction and a subsequent relaxation condition. Twenty-three participants engaged with their most frequently used smartphone application (primarily gaming or short form video) for ten minutes, followed by a five-minute passive viewing of a standardized nature video. Simultaneous recordings were obtained from electroencephalography (EEG; 64 channels), wearable eye-tracking, photoplethysmography (PPG), and galvanic skin response (GSR) sensors. Questionnaire-based assessments, including the smartphone addiction scale (SAS) and the mobile phone problematic use scale (MPPUS), are also collected to characterize individual differences in smartphone-related behavioral traits. All data streams are synchronized using transistor-transistor logic (TTL) trigger signals to ensure precise temporal alignment across modalities. The dataset is organized according to the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) specification and is publicly available on OpenNeuro (Accession Number: ds007537). This dataset enables the investigation of neural, ocular, and autonomic responses during smartphone interaction and supports multimodal analysis of diverse smartphone behaviors while preserving ecological validity.

papers.title: Conserved catalytic activity of animal TIR domains functions in TLR4 signaling
papers.abstract: The Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) domain is important for immune signaling across bacteria, plants, and animals. In animal innate immunity, TIR domains are thought to function as adaptors mediating protein-protein interactions, yet studies in bacteria and plants revealed that TIR domains often act as enzymes that produce immune signaling molecules. Here, we show that catalytic activity is a conserved property of TIR domains across the animal tree of life. We find that TIR domains from evolutionarily diverse animals, including the TIR domain of human TLR4, are enzymes that can produce cyclic ADP-ribose (cADPR). We further show that the catalytic residue of TLR4 TIR domain is required for TLR4 signal transduction in human macrophages. Substitution of the catalytic glutamate abolishes LPS-induced inflammatory responses and disrupts Myddosome assembly, revealing a previously unrecognized functional requirement for the TIR catalytic site in TLR4 signaling. Beyond animals, we identify a TIR domain from green algae that produces 3'cADPR, suggesting deep evolutionary conservation of TIR-mediated signaling. Together, our findings establish enzymatic activity as a widespread and evolutionarily conserved property of TIR domains and reveal a functional role for the conserved catalytic site in mammalian innate immune signaling.

papers.title: In vivo discovery of blood-brain barrier opening small molecules with FishNAP
papers.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) maintains neural homeostasis by tightly regulating molecular exchange between the circulation and the brain, but it also restricts drug delivery and thereby limits treatment of neurological disorders. Pharmacological agents that transiently and safely increase BBB permeability could therefore improve brain drug delivery, yet their systematic discovery has been constrained by the limitations of existing approaches. Here we present FishNAP, a non-invasive, high-throughput zebrafish platform for real-time in vivo assessment of BBB permeability. Screening 2,320 FDA-approved small molecules identified seven that increased BBB permeability in zebrafish, with barrier integrity recovering within 24 hours in each case, indicating reversible modulation. Three of these compounds, Calcitriol, Lovastatin and Sunitinib, which act through distinct signaling pathways, also increased BBB permeability in adult mice through both tight junction disruption and increased transcytosis. FishNAP thus enables the identification of conserved modulators of BBB function with translational potential for brain drug delivery.

papers.title: Modulation of lipid metabolism by thapsigarin inhibits hepatitis C virus infection by multiple mechanisms
papers.abstract: Thapsigargin (Tg), an inducer of endoplasmic reticulum stress and the unfolded protein response (UPR), has broad-spectrum antiviral activity, although the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we characterized its antiviral mechanism(s) using hepatitis C virus (HCV) as a model. Pre-treatment with Tg partially inhibited HCV RNA replication, but more strongly reduced extracellular viral titer and RNA, suggesting a block to later stages of infection. Its antiviral effects against HCV infection are likely UPR-independent, since treatment with tunicamycin, which activates the UPR by a different mechanism, did not exert the same antiviral effect. Given the importance of lipid droplets (LDs) and lipid metabolism in mediating HCV assembly and egress, we examined Tg-mediated effects on lipid homeostasis. Tg treatment upregulated the expression of lipid synthesis genes, including FASN and DGAT1/2, and led to the accumulation of enlarged LDs. Tg also induced expression of CIDE-C, a mediator of LD fusion. Silencing CIDEC expression impaired Tg-induced LD enlargement and rescued viral RNA replication, but not extracellular titer, from Tg inhibition, demonstrating that Tg-mediated LD remodeling contributes to replication defects without significantly affecting assembly or egress. Intracellular viral titers were unchanged in Tg-treated cells, indicating intact virion assembly but a defect in secretion. Consistently, Tg treatment reduced both apolipoprotein B and E secretion, but not that of Gaussia luciferase, suggesting that specific disruption of the very low-density lipoprotein secretion pathway by Tg could impair efficient HCV egress. Together, our findings reveal that modulation of lipid homeostasis by Tg inhibits HCV RNA replication and egress by distinct mechanisms. This work has antiviral implications for other viruses that rely on lipid metabolism during infection.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals organizational properties of the mouse spinal cord and alterations in neuropathic pain
papers.abstract: The spinal cord integrates diverse somatosensory inputs and executes motor outputs through anatomically and functionally distinct circuits. Here, we employed spatially resolved single-cell transcriptomic profiling of the adult mouse spinal cord to gain insights into the organizational logic of the spinal cord. Our results reveal distinct spatial and laminar distributions of neuronal subtypes, including axial level and sex-specific differences. Many neuronal subtypes exhibit close spatial proximity, implicating regionally specific patterns of connectivity and circuit functions. Additionally, neuronal subtypes within the dorsal horn exhibit a wide range of predicted cell-cell communication motifs, as assessed by the spatial distribution of neuropeptide- and other ligand-receptor pairs. Finally, we identified several neuronal subtypes with altered transcriptomic and predicted cell-cell communications in a model of neuropathic pain. This spatially resolved cellular and molecular map of the spinal cord will facilitate the decoding of circuit mechanisms underlying somatosensory and motor functions in health and disease.

papers.title: Identification of cis-Acting Elements that Regulate Influenza A Virus Segment 7 Differential mRNA Splicing
papers.abstract: Influenza A virus segment 7 encodes the M1 matrix protein and M2 ion channel from an unspliced primary transcript (mRNA1) and spliced mRNA2, respectively. Both proteins are essential for efficient virus replication, but the intrinsic sequences that determine segment 7 splicing balance are not fully defined. Here, we systematically investigated how conserved cis-acting splicing elements regulate segment splicing. We found that while the splice acceptor sequence is optimal, both potential upstream polypyrimidine tracts regulate splicing, with the 5' region acting positively and the 3' region negatively to maintain M1 expression. Nucleotide A713 is the most likely mRNA2 branch point, but potentially with redundancy from other local adenosines. Mutagenesis of the mRNA2 splice donor sequence showed that it is nearly optimal but that nucleotides 51 and 55 modestly downregulate splicing efficiency. Most introduced mutations that change splicing balance are nonsynonymous in M1. Nevertheless, polypyrimidine tract and branch point mutations that significantly perturbed M1:M2 balance resulted in viable viruses. In contrast, the splice donor sequence was largely intolerant of mutation. We conclude that M1:M2 balance is maintained via suboptimal splice donor and polypyrimidine tract splicing signals, with the latter allowing more evolutionary flexibility to vary the ratio and/or M1 sequence

papers.title: RegEvol: detection of directional selection in regulatory sequences through phenotypic predictions and phenotype-to-fitness functions
papers.abstract: Regulatory DNA controls when and where genes are expressed, making it a key driver of phenotypic evolution. Yet detecting selection in non-coding regions remains difficult, as most approaches rely on sequence conservation or changes in substitution rate rather than molecular effects. RegEvol bridges this gap by linking machine learning-based predictions of transcription factor binding to explicit evolutionary models. It uses the distribution of predicted mutational effects to infer fitness functions under different evolutionary scenarios including random drift, stabilising selection, and directional selection. Through maximum-likelihood estimation, it identifies the regime that best explains observed changes along a lineage from an ancestral sequence. When substitution numbers are limited, such as along short evolutionary branches, likelihood differences can be aggregated across sets of regulatory elements to increase statistical power. RegEvol corrects biases that affected previous tests based on machine learning of transcription factor binding, while remaining conservative across different levels of divergence. Applied to over 3 million Drosophila melanogaster regulatory regions, we identify 5.1% under directional selection, enriched near reproductive and immune genes. Applying the aggregation strategy to human CTCF binding across tissues reveals enrichment of directional signals in nervous and male reproductive systems. The framework is readily applicable to experimentally detected regulatory elements with alignable ancestral sequences and is flexible to future advances in understanding regulatory function, providing a powerful basis for investigating adaptation in non-coding regions.

papers.title: TrkC has distinct spatiotemporal dynamics compared to TrkA and TrkB
papers.abstract: Neurotrophins (NGF, BDNF, NT-3, NT-4) are critical regulators of neuronal development and have been implicated in a range of neurodegenerative disorders. They signal through three tropomyosin receptor kinase receptors (TrkA, TrkB and TrkC). TrkC can exist as an alternately spliced isoform (TrkCKID) that includes an exon-16 derived kinase insert domain (KID). Here, we have utilised FRET and BRET biosensors to compare the spatiotemporal dynamics of TrkA, TrkB and TrkC. TrkA and TrkB displayed robust concentration-dependent ERK signalling, dimerisation and trafficking, and also provided evidence for receptor activation by non-canonical ligands. While the KID-lacking TrkCdeltaKID showed ERK signalling comparable to TrkA and TrkB, TrkCKID displayed markedly reduced downstream ERK signalling. Interestingly, TrkCdeltaKID and TrkCKID exhibited slower trafficking away from the cell surface than TrkA or TrkB, but a strong ability to dimerise. Overall, these findings reveal that TrkC possesses unique regulatory mechanisms that may provide opportunities for tailored neurotrophic drug discovery.

papers.title: A Precisely Controlled Long-Acting Immunosuppression Platform Enables Prolonged Survival of Vascularized Composite Allografts
papers.abstract: Vascularized composite allotransplantation (VCA) restores complex multi-tissue defects but remains limited by the need for lifelong immunosuppression. Daily oral tacrolimus, the primary maintenance regimen, poses adherence challenges and produces large peak-trough fluctuations within a narrow therapeutic window, resulting in toxicity and periods of under-immunosuppression. Although injectable depots could improve adherence, existing systems frequently generate prolonged supratherapeutic exposure. Most rely primarily on depot matrix properties to govern release kinetics, which alone are insufficient, and in certain systems uncontrolled solvent efflux during phase inversion can exacerbate early burst release. To address these limitations, we developed PRECISE (Programmable, Retrievable, Embedded Controlled ImmunoSuppression Encapsulator), a graft-injectable, in situ-forming depot engineered to precisely regulate systemic tacrolimus exposure. PRECISE integrates a polymeric matrix with rationally selected small-molecule excipients that interact with tacrolimus at the molecular level and modulate solvent dynamics during phase inversion, enabling release control beyond polymer tuning alone. Notably, rapamycin, under select dosing conditions, can also interact with tacrolimus and regulate solvent dynamics, enabling controlled co-delivery of a complementary immunosuppressive combination. This integration of drug-excipient and drug-drug interactions introduces a previously unexplored mechanism for controlling systemic exposure in in situ-forming depots. In a rat hindlimb transplant model, monthly intragraft administration of PRECISE maintained systemic tacrolimus and rapamycin concentrations within the therapeutic window for over 300 days, prolonged graft survival, expanded regulatory T cells, and induced donor-specific hyporesponsiveness. Translational validation in fully MHC-mismatched (SLA Class I and II) pigs, one of the most stringent large-animal transplant models, demonstrated sustained therapeutic drug levels, preserved graft vascular integrity, and graft survival through 90 days. Collectively, these findings establish PRECISE as the first long-acting immunosuppressive platform to maintain systemic drug concentrations precisely within the therapeutic window while enabling controlled dual-drug immunosuppression and the first long-acting immunosuppressive system validated in a fully MHC-mismatched large-animal VCA model, with broad applicability to solid-organ transplantation.

papers.title: NKX2.2 is required for timely NEUROG3 extinction and segregation of competing lineage programs in human pancreatic endocrine progenitors
papers.abstract: Pancreatic endocrine progenitors commit to the NEUROG3+ lineage before resolving into mono-hormonal cell types. The homeodomain factor NKX2.2 is required for islet formation in mice and humans, but its role at the endocrine progenitor stage is undefined. We generated NKX2.2-null human embryonic stem cells and differentiated them towards endocrine lineages. Mutant progenitors induced NEUROG3 and formed endocrine committed cells at near wild-type frequency. Single cell transcriptomics showed persistent NEUROG3 in mutant cells running , {beta} and {delta} programs, co-activation of the mutually exclusive ARX and PAX4 networks, and no terminal lineage factor induction. Reanalysis of published islet NKX2.2 ChIP-seq showed that chromatin state at bound elements, not occupancy alone, predicted the direction of transcriptional change, including at NEUROG3, NKX6.1, ARX and PAX4. End-stage cultures yielded few insulin+ cells, with excess somatostatin, ghrelin, polyhormonal and hormone-negative cells. NKX2.2 is therefore dispensable for endocrine specification but required for resolution of endocrine fates.

papers.title: Human ribosomes interactions reveal the binding landscape of neomycin
papers.abstract: Aminoglycosides such as neomycin are clinically limited by toxicity, commonly attributed to the inhibition of mitoribosomes. Here, we investigate this model by integrating Cryo-EM and functional assays to assess neomycin's binding landscape and functional consequences for human ribosomes. Cryo-EM reveals extensive multi-site binding of neomycin on both human mitochondrial and cytosolic ribosomes in vitro, including conserved regions of the decoding center. In contrast, ribosomes isolated from neomycin-treated cells show markedly different patterns, with no detectable neomycin density on the mitoribosomes and reduced occupancy at a subset of cytosolic ribosome sites. Functional assays indicate that neomycin remained active in cells, inducing widespread stop-codon readthrough while having minimal effects on global mitochondrial and cytosolic protein synthesis. Together, these findings highlight a disconnect between the structural binding landscape and ribosome-associated neomycin recovered following cellular exposure, while linking neomycin exposure to altered translational fidelity with minimal effects on global protein synthesis.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of tumor microenvironment remodelling
papers.abstract: During tumorigenesis, interactions between tumor and stromal cells progressively remodel the tumor microenvironment (TME) towards pro-tumoral functions. Understanding early TME remodeling dynamics is therefore crucial for developing interceptive therapies. However, clinical samples typically provide isolated, late tumorigenesis snapshots. To overcome this limitation, we generated triple-negative breast cancer mice that develop multifocal, asynchronous tumors along a continuous luminal-to-basal transdifferentiation trajectory. Ordering spatial transcriptomes from 100+ ducts along this trajectory reveals the spatiotemporal dynamics and molecular mechanisms of TME remodeling, identifying early stromal programs and signaling axes as potential targets for disease interception before establishment of invasive niches. The stromal spatiotemporal remodeling dynamics are conserved across genetically heterogeneous patient-derived xenograft models and treatment naive human TNBC cohorts, supporting the translational relevance of our findings. Our study shows that temporal ordering of spatially-resolved disease snapshots unravels some of the molecular forces that, starting from the cell-of-origin, propel cells/microenvironments along a disease trajectory.

papers.title: Assessing the Replicability of Scientific Claims in Drosophila Immunity Through an Analysis of 400 Publications
papers.abstract: Drosophila immunity has been the focus of intense study and has impacted other research fields including innate immunity and agriculturally or epidemiologically relevant investigations of insect pests and vectors. We have performed a reproducibility project that analyses the conceptual replicability of claims from articles published on Drosophila immunity before 2011. To assess replicability, we extracted claims from 400 articles on the Drosophila immune response to bacteria and fungi and performed preliminary verification by comparing these claims to other published literature in the field. Using alternative approaches, we also experimentally tested some unchallenged claims, with no published follow-up. The intent of this analysis was to centralize evidence on insights and findings to improve clarity for scientists that may base research programs on these data. All our data are published on a publicly available website associated with this article (https://ReproSci.epfl.ch/) that encourages community participation. This article provides a short summary of claims that were found to have contradictory evidence, which may help the community to assess past findings on Drosophila immunity and improve clarity going forward. Statistical analysis of this reproducibility study and metascience insights obtained from this approach are discussed in a companion article.

papers.title: timePlex: Increasing mass spectrometry throughput using time-encoded sample multiplexing
papers.abstract: Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) can enable precise and accurate quantification of analytes at high-sensitivity, but the rate at which samples can be analyzed remains limited. Throughput can be increased by data-independent-acquisition (DIA) using short separation times and by multiplexing samples in the mass domain with plexDIA; yet multiplexing along one dimension scales throughput only linearly with plex. To enable combinatorial scaling of proteomics throughput, we developed a complementary DIA strategy that multiplexes samples in the time domain, termed `timePlex'. timePlex staggers and overlaps the separation periods of individual samples. This strategy is orthogonal to isotopic multiplexing, which enables combinatorial multiplexing in mass and time domains, and thus multiplicatively increased throughput. We demonstrate this with a 27-plex (3-timePlex and 9-plexDIA) exceeding 1,200 samples (4M protein datapoints) per day. These results establish timePlex as a framework for multiplexing both label-free and labeled samples that supports sensitive and accurate protein quantification and combinatorial scaling.

papers.title: Disruption of Plasma Membrane Lipid Asymmetry Alters Cellular Energetics
papers.abstract: Biological membranes often feature unequal and actively maintained concentration gradients of lipids between bilayer leaflets, termed lipid asymmetry. Lipid asymmetry has been linked to many cellular processes, but the mechanisms that connect lipid trans-bilayer concentration gradients to cellular functions are poorly understood. Here we systematically map the cellular processes affected by dysregulation of lipid asymmetry by knocking out flippases, floppases, and scramblases in mammalian cells. We identify broad alterations to core metabolic pathways, including nutrient uptake, neutral lipid turnover, the pentose phosphate pathway, and glycolysis. Lipidomics, respirometry, lipid and metabolic imaging, and live-cell calorimetry revealed elevated neutral lipid and ATP consumption rates, coupled with increased heat loss per unit biomass synthesized despite slower growth. This suggests that compensatory maintenance of lipid asymmetry strains the cellular energy budget, shifting the cell from a growth-promoting anabolic state to a more energy-using catabolic state. Our data indicate that lipid asymmetry and its active maintenance are linked to cellular energetics, reflecting either the energetic cost of maintaining lipid asymmetry or its putative role as a cellular store of potential energy akin to proton and ion transmembrane gradients.

papers.title: Carcinogen-induced DNA adducts amplify APOBEC mutagenesis through nucleotide excision repair
papers.abstract: Extrinsic and intrinsic factors induce mutations in somatic cells that play a key role in cancer development. Tobacco smoke contains carcinogens that contribute to cancers of the lung and head & neck. The APOBEC family of DNA cytosine deaminases is a prominent endogenous source of mutation, generating characteristic signatures (SBS2 and SBS13) that often co-occur with the tobacco-associated signature SBS4 in tumors from smokers. Here, we challenge the prevailing view that mutational processes act independently and additively. We show that 4-nitroquinoline 1-oxide (NQO), a widely used model for tobacco carcinogenesis, sensitizes cells to APOBEC3B (A3B)-mediated mutagenesis, resulting in a significant increase in oral carcinoma development in vivo. NQO exposure markedly amplifies APOBEC-associated SBS2 mutagenesis, without a corresponding increase in NQO-associated SBS4 mutations. Moreover, a large proportion of A3B-catalyzed SBS2 mutations occur as strand-coordinated pairs within 32 nucleotides of each other, supporting a model in which nucleotide excision repair (NER) of NQO-induced DNA adducts generates short single-stranded DNA intermediates that are accessible to APOBEC-catalyzed deamination. These APOBEC mutation pairs - termed didyma (Greek for twins) - exhibit distinct genomic features consistent with a NER-initiated mechanism, differing from other types of clustered mutations (omikli and kataegis). A3B exhibits processive deamination on NER-like tracts in vitro. Didyma formation in human cell lines and yeast depends on NQO exposure, catalytically active A3B, and functional NER (XPA in human cells and Rad14 in yeast). Computational analyses of lung and head & neck tumor genomes show that both APOBEC mutagenesis and didyma are elevated in cancers from smokers compared to non-smokers. Elevated levels are also observed in normal lung tissues from smokers prior to tumor development. Additional tumor types without obvious links to smoking also exhibit didyma. Collectively, these results indicate that exogenous DNA adduct-forming carcinogens can amplify mutagenesis by endogenous APOBEC enzymes and that mutational processes can interact synergistically to shape tumor genomes during cancer initiation and progression.

papers.title: Prediction of Tubulin Inhibitor Sensitivity in Colon Cancer
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer is the second most common cause of cancer death worldwide. Despite advances in molecular strategies for stratifying patients with colorectal cancer, their clinical implementation remains limited. Previous efforts have mainly focused on the development of prognostic gene expression signatures; however predictive biomarkers remain essential for translating molecular insights into effective therapies and ultimately enhancing patient outcomes. This study advances the translation of a molecular signature identified in colon cancer toward new therapeutic options for clinical applications. We leveraged public gene expression datasets to develop a prognostic 37-gene signature in colon cancer and validated its prognostic value across six clinical cohorts. We subsequently investigated the biological processes associated with the signature and its predictive potential for therapeutic response. We further evaluated its predictive capability for tubulin inhibitor response using paclitaxel in vitro and in vivo in patient-derived preclinical models. The signature showed prognostic performance comparable to published gene expression signatures across six independent cohorts without clinical covariates. The signature was associated with the mitotic phase of the cell cycle and identified a population of patient-derived colon cancer models sensitive to tubulin inhibitor drugs, subsequently referred to as the Colon Tubulin-Inhibitor Expression Signature (ColoTubIn). Low ColoTubIn scores were associated with increased paclitaxel sensitivity. Hence, ColoTubIn performs comparably to existing prognostic signatures while additionally identifying a molecularly defined subgroup of colon cancers with therapeutic potential. ColoTubIn is of particular interest since it can serve as a basis for drug repurposing strategies leveraging existing safety data to accelerate translation into the clinic.

papers.title: Rapid and widespread transcriptional plasticity underlies host shift in a specialist herbivore
papers.abstract: Insect herbivores employ many adaptive mechanisms to successfully colonize host plants. Transcriptional plasticity is one mechanism that enables broad host use in polyphagous insect herbivores; however, whether specialist herbivores use transcriptional plasticity or undergo epigenome modifications to cope with host shifts remains largely unexplored. We measured the transcriptome and epigenome of the specialist aphid herbivore, Daktulosphaira vitifoliae, after transfer to new hosts using RNA-seq and whole-genome bisulfite sequencing. We found the transcriptome of D. vitifoliae is highly plastic and responsive to host genotype - 3,706 genes (28% of expressed genes) are significantly differentially expressed in at least one contrast comparing host genotypes. Most host-responsive genes (2,667 genes) were upregulated when feeding on the non-native host Vitis vinifera and enriched for genes encoding predicted secretory effectors, detoxification enzymes, and cuticle- and chitin-associated proteins. We found gene co-expression modules that correlated with variation in fitness suggesting plasticity in transcriptional networks contributes to D. vitifoliae adaptation to host plants. We also identified a previously undescribed family of proline-rich secretory proteins conserved across the Aphidomorpha infraorder of insects. Unlike the transcriptome, DNA methylation did not dramatically respond to host transfer and positively correlated with stably expressed genes; thus, gene body DNA methylation may help stabilize gene expression when insects move to new host environments. Together, these results provide new insight into the molecular mechanisms of host use in insect herbivores.

papers.title: Endocrinology reveals seasonal reproductive dynamics in three Malagasy fruit bats
papers.abstract: Bats (Chiroptera) are a highly diverse mammalian order with over 1,500 species, roughly 200 of which are Old World Fruit Bats (family: Pteropodidae). Many pteropodid bats, especially those residing in seasonal environments, experience seasonal reproductive cycles, including discrete periods of gestation and lactation, which underpin cyclic energetic costs. These discrete seasonal life history events have consequences for conservation management (e.g., population viability) among wild fruit bat populations; however, little is known about the seasonality of reproduction in many pteropodid bat species. Here, we aimed to elucidate the reproductive biology of three species of pteropodid bats endemic to the island of Madagascar: Pteropus rufus, Eidolon dupreanum, and Rousettus madagascarensis. We leveraged plasma samples collected in part with a longitudinal field study, from 2019 and 2020. We adapted three standard reproductive assays previously validated in humans to quantify seasonal changes in reproductive hormones for bats and applied a mixture model approach to determine hormone cutoffs indicative of pregnancy in females and mating readiness in males. As predicted, we found that pregnant females showed the highest levels of estradiol and progesterone and adult males the highest levels of testosterone. Additionally, female P. rufus and R. madagascariensis showed clear seasonality in reproduction with peaks in estradiol and progesterone in August and October, respectively. Seasonality was less clearly discernible in female E. dupreanum and in male testosterone data. Our results demonstrate that hormone-based reproductive classification is a powerful tool for identifying reproductive status in free-ranging bats. These physiological data refine previously reported reproductive calendars critical for demographic modeling and conservation management of threatened Pteropodidae bats.

papers.title: Rapid gastrointestinal tract transit time in volant vertebrates, with implications for gut microbiome convergence: Results from a meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Flying birds and bats have simplified gastrointestinal tracts (GITs) and low intestinal mass to support flight. While previous work showed reduced GIT passage times in birds relative to other vertebrates, GIT passage times have never been collectively quantified for bats. We conducted a meta-analysis of published digesta passage times across vertebrates, comparing volant and non-volant vertebrates, while considering the effects of body mass and diet. We hypothesized that, like flying birds, bats have significantly faster digesta passage times relative to nonvolant vertebrates, likely due to their adaptations for flight. Our study supports this, revealing significant differences in passage times among flying and non-flying groups, with bats exhibiting faster transit times compared to non-volant vertebrates. Using a phylogenetic comparative analysis, we show that flight and diet have a strong effect on GIT transit times across diverse taxa, while body mass plays a more limited role. Accelerated transit times in bats likely promote the rapid turnover of gut contents, which may contribute to their distinct GIT microbe compositions. Unique among mammals, bat GIT microbiomes are dominated by Pseudomonadota bacteria, a pattern also observed in flying birds. We hypothesize this convergence may result from rapid GIT transit times quantified here for volant taxa.

papers.title: Bayesian model-based method for clustering gene expression time series with multiple replicates
papers.abstract: Background: In this study, we introduce a Bayesian model-based method for clustering transcriptomics time series data with multiple replicates. This technique is based on sampling Gaussian processes (GPs) within an infinite mixture model from a Dirichlet process (DP). Our method uses multiple GP models to accommodate for multiple differently behaving experimental replicates within each cluster. We call it multiple models Dirichlet process Gaussian process (MMDPGP) mixture model. We compare our method with state-of-the-art model-based clustering approaches for handling gene expression time series with multiple replicates. Results: To demonstrate the accuracy of our method we use it to cluster synthetically generated data sets. The clusters produced by our method on the synthetic data had a significantly higher purity score compared to the state-of-the- art approaches. We also present a case study where all methods are applied for clustering RNA-Seq time series of Clostridium botulinum with three different experimental replicates. The results obtained from the gene enrichment analysis showed that the number of significantly enriched sets of genes is larger in the clusters produced by MMDPGP. Conclusions: By modelling each replicate with a separate GP, our method can use the natural variability between experimental replicates to learn more about the underlying biology.

papers.title: Head movement allocation in freely-moving macaques learning object-context sequences
papers.abstract: Flexible learning and long-term memory are hallmark features of primate cognition that are shaped by interactions with changing environments. A comprehensive understanding of these brain-body-environment interactions requires minimal constraints on behavior, and environments rich with conditional cues that encourage diverse behavioral dynamics. In this study, we introduce a multi-level enclosure (Treehouse) that allows for independent control of spatially distributed touchscreens for studying cognition in freely moving macaques. To test flexible learning, two monkeys completed trials consisting of a regular sequence of conditional object choices (targets) across four distinct spatiotemporal contexts (screens). Both monkeys acquired numerous unique, conditional object-context sequences without detriment to new learning as memoranda accumulated. They also successfully recalled their correct choices after weeks without exposure. To assess how monkeys allocate movement during learning and memory-guided decision making, we tracked their head kinematics and used recurrent neural networks to decode different aspects of their engagement with the environment during the choice epoch of the task. One such model predicted the position of the object about to be touched, including on error trials, tracking overt gaze towards objects. Separate models decoded sequence corner, the ordinal step, and the individual screen stations the monkeys occupied, despite identical stimulus layouts and behavioral demands at each station. Head movements also showed efficiencies that the task did not require: under conditions of uncertainty, monkeys were biased in their initial search locations to the targets that were closest to reach, and across days they made smoother head movements as training progressed, with no change in accuracy. These results demonstrate the potential of immersive 3-D environments, in which body kinematics can shed light on animals' goals, and reveal that situated learning in primates can be rapid, capacious, durable, and flexible.

papers.title: WCRC-25: A novel luminal Invasive Lobular Carcinoma cell line model
papers.abstract: Breast cancer is broadly divided histologically into no special type (NST) and special subtypes, of which invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC) is the most common. ILC is distinguished by discohesive, single-file growth from loss of E-cadherin (CDH1). Few ILC cell lines exist, limiting mechanistic study of this understudied disease. Here we describe WCRC-25, a novel ILC cell line established from a pleural effusion of a patient with metastatic ILC. While WCRC-25 lacks ER expression, it is molecularly defined as luminal with Her2-like features, and shows anchorage-independent growth and haptotactic migration toward Collagen I. Sequencing identified a CDH1 Q706* truncating mutation alongside FOXA1, CTCF, BRCA2 and TP53 mutations shared with the patient's metastases, while copy-number and optical genome mapping revealed structural rearrangements typical of ILC. Transcriptomic AKT-pathway signatures predicted, and cell-based assays confirmed, sensitivity to PI3K/AKT inhibition. WCRC-25 also engrafted and spontaneously metastasized in vivo. WCRC-25 is a valuable new tool for dissecting ILC biology and therapeutic vulnerabilities.

papers.title: Revisiting the role of cAMP in Drosophila aversive olfactory memory formation
papers.abstract: In aversive olfactory conditioning in Drosophila melanogaster, an odor (the conditioned stimulus, CS) is paired with an electric shock (the unconditioned stimulus, US). Rutabaga adenylyl cyclase, which synthesizes cAMP in Kenyon cells (KCs), has long been proposed to act as a coincidence detector, synergistically activated by calcium/calmodulin in response to odor-evoked KC activity and by Gs downstream of shock-evoked dopamine signaling. This framework implies that CS+ responsive KCs, which receive both CS and US signals, should be distinguishable from the remaining KCs by elevated cAMP levels, such that elevated cAMP would selectively mark these KCs for memory-related plasticity. However, our live imaging revealed that olfactory stimulation alone activates dopaminergic signaling and elevates cAMP broadly across KC axons, with only weak spatial correspondence to sparse local Ca2+ responses, such that CS+ responsive KCs could not be distinguished from the remaining KCs by bulk cAMP levels. This observation challenges a key prediction of the Rutabaga coincidence-detection model. Our findings instead suggest that cAMP concentrations do not selectively mark CS+ neurons. Rather, we propose that the compartmental population dynamics of cAMP across the {gamma} lobe represent a KC-intrinsic expression of valence, integrated across compartments from multiple dopaminergic inputs. Associative conditioning reshaped dopamine responses to the CS+ odor, with corresponding changes in this compartmental cAMP pattern. Simultaneous imaging of cAMP and acetylcholine (ACh) revealed that conditioning establishes an inverse relationship between this pattern and ACh release for the CS+ but not for the CS- odors; this relationship was absent in rutabaga mutants. Pharmacological elevation of cAMP suppressed ACh release from KCs. These findings suggest that cAMP-dependent suppression of ACh release from KCs may shift the valence of the CS+ odor toward a more aversive state in conditioned flies, thereby contributing to aversive olfactory memory formation.

papers.title: Proportional variability relative to lower abundances: An interpretable and efficient index of deep lows in population time series
papers.abstract: Variability in population abundances is usually measured with the coefficient of variation (CV) or the standard deviation of log-transformed data (SDL), both of which are biased for non-Gaussian dynamics and zero counts. Proportional variability (PV_hi), which scales each pairwise difference relative to the larger of the two abundances, avoids reference to the mean but responds only weakly to isolated crashes and to the depth of declines. I introduce PV_lo, an index of proportional variability relative to lower abundances, based on all pairwise comparisons and bounded between 0 and 1. Zero counts are handled without data transformation. A sorting-based algorithm reduces the computation from O(n^2) to O(n log n), making the index applicable to long time series. In example series and simulations (Gaussian, Cauchy, rare-crash, bimodal and gradual-decline regimes), PV_lo remained sensitive to crashes and to the contrast between abundance levels, whereas PV_hi levelled off, but PV_hi was more robust against heavy-tailed extremes. In a comparison with series of ordinary fluctuations, PV_lo and SDL separated crashes better than PV_hi and the CV only if the ordinary variability of a population was unknown, and PV_lo did not outperform SDL; during a sustained decline the indices differed little. PV_lo is a computationally efficient index that responds to deep lows on an interpretable ratio scale without transformation of the data, an alternative to SDL that is relevant for screening many populations in a conservation context.

papers.title: Superior Frontal Gyrus Cortical Thickness Mediates the Association Between Openness to Experience and Theory of Mind: Evidence from the Human Connectome Project
papers.abstract: Background: Theory of mind (ToM), the capacity to infer the mental states of others, varies considerably across healthy adults. Openness to experience has been linked both to social-cognitive abilities and to thinner prefrontal cortex, but whether cortical structure statistically accounts for the association between openness and ToM is unknown. We tested whether bilateral superior frontal gyrus (SFG) cortical thickness mediates this association. Methods: Data from 1,049 healthy young adults with complete data were drawn from the Human Connectome Project. ToM was indexed by accuracy on the Heider-Simmel social animation task, openness by the NEO Five-Factor Inventory, and SFG thickness by FreeSurfer. Models adjusted for age, sex, intracranial volume and fluid intelligence; indirect effects were tested with 5,000 bootstrap resamples, and Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction was applied. Results: Openness showed a positive total effect on ToM accuracy (beta = .081, p = .009). Higher openness was associated with thinner left and right SFG (beta = -.085 and -.084), and thinner SFG with higher ToM accuracy (beta = -.082 and -.075). Indirect effects were significant (left: .0069, 95% CI [.0010, .0158]; right: .0063, 95% CI [.0007, .0146]), accounting for approximately 8.5% and 7.8% of the total effect, and remained significant after rank-based normalisation of the ceiling-affected ToM scores. Conclusions: SFG cortical thickness partially and statistically mediates the association between openness to experience and social cognition. Because the data are cross-sectional and effects are small, the findings do not establish a causal mechanism, neural efficiency or synaptic pruning, but they identify a candidate structural pathway for longitudinal testing.

papers.title: Enhancing Germination and Assessing the Longevity of Native Plants' Seeds with Dormancy through Different Priming Techniques
papers.abstract: Vachellia pachyceras and Convolvulus oxyphyllus are native species of arid and semi-arid desert regions, including Kuwait. They are inherently adapted to extreme conditions characterized by high temperature, prolonged drought and limited rainfall. They contribute significantly, to restore the ecosystem by providing food and shelter for wildlife. Despite their ecological importance, seed germination in both species is constrained by dormancy, and natural recruitment of seedlings is limited by narrow and unpredictable rainfall windows, severely restricting opportunities for establishment. In this context, seed priming is an effective pre-sowing technique that enables uniform and rapid germination within the short window of favorable conditions. This study aims to identify the optimal seed-priming techniques for these two keystone native species and to assess the effect of priming on seed longevity. The seeds were scarified to remove the physical dormancy prior to priming treatments. Relative seed longevity was measured for primed seeds through artificial ageing and analyzed using probit analysis and analysis of variance. Results showed that hormonal priming [(mechanical scarification + 100 ppm gibberellic acid (GA3)] for six hours and hydropriming (mechanical scarification + soaking in water) for 8 hours (h) were effective treatments among the tested priming treatments for V. pachyceras. The estimated p50 value (i.e., number of days to lose seed viability to 50%) was 22 days for hormonal priming and 21 days for hydropriming. Mechanical scarification followed by one and half hour of hydropriming was the most effective in C. oxyphyllus (p50 = 74 days). Based on these results, the longevity of V. pachyceras and C. oxyphyllus could be considered medium. Further studies are needed to determine the effectiveness of seed priming on additional ecologically and economically important native species to achieve success in revegetation programs.

papers.title: Pycea: a scverse toolkit for single-cell lineage tracing analysis
papers.abstract: Lineage tracing enables reconstruction of cellular histories in development, regeneration, and disease, but integrating lineage data into single-cell analysis workflows remains challenging.
