Under shear flow, many oxEGCG-dependent perturbations partially reverted toward free Syn, whereas interactions near the NAC-C-terminal boundary were preferentially retained, coinciding with formation of oligomers and short, thick fibrils. These findings identify oxidation state and flow as determinants of EGCG action on Syn and show that Rheo-NMR distinguishes interactions that persist during shear-promoted assembly.

papers.title: The periplasmic substrate-binding protein ThuE is required for sucrose uptake and multiplication of Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000 in tomato leaves
papers.abstract: Phytopathogenic bacteria depend on host-derived carbon for successful colonization of plant tissue. While sucrose is among the most abundant sugars in the leaf apoplast, the steps that limit its acquisition by Pseudomonas syringae are not known. In this study, we used base editing to generate mutants of six candidate sucrose utilization genes in P. syringae pv. tomato DC3000 (Pto). Loss of either the sucrose hydrolase ScrB or both levansucrases had no detectable effect, whereas the growth defect in the loss of the outer membrane porin mutant scry was overcome by raising external sucrose. Loss of the periplasmic substrate-binding protein ThuE impaired growth both in vitro and in planta, reducing bacterial populations to approximately two orders of magnitude lower in tomato leaves. Sucrose import through a single non-redundant inner membrane ABC transporter is therefore required for Pto multiplication in planta and serves as a potential target for controlling bacterial speck disease.

papers.title: Capturing the rhythm: methodological choices shape inference from circadian activity data
papers.abstract: Abstract 1. Statistical tools and analytical decisions for analysing animal activity data are often limited and poorly justified, particularly with respect to model choice, sampling design and temporal aggregation. These shortcomings can constrain our ability to draw accurate and biologically meaningful inferences about behaviour. 2. We interrogated 24 h activity data taken from individual males and females derived from five Drosophila melanogaster populations to generate a general framework for collecting and analysing activity data that systematically compares common model classes, continuous verses fragmented sampling strategies, and alternative temporal aggregation choices (time-bin sizes). 3. Our analyses identified generalised additive mixed models (GAMMs) applied to high-frequency continuous data with small-moderate bin sizes (1-5 minutes) as providing the most robust and interpretable inference for our complex, high-frequency activity data. 4. However, our interrogation of the data set confirmed that analytical and sampling decisions need to be tailored to the study species, the timing of activities and the nature of the behaviour of interest. Accordingly, polynomial and cosinor generalised linear models, increased but biologically targeted snapshot sampling, and bin sizes smaller than one hour yielded adequate analyses with similar biological conclusions when appropriately matched to the system. 5. Our approach provides an accessible decision-making framework for activity analyses that allows researchers across behavioural, ecological and evolutionary studies to justify and optimise choices about data collection and modelling. Such an approach improves the biological relevance of inference and supporting the use of modern tracking and analytical technologies.

papers.title: Estrogen remodels large-scale cortical dynamics to promote behavioral persistence
papers.abstract: Sex-steroid hormones remodel the brain on slow timescales of hours to days to coordinate adaptive behaviors with changing bodily physiology. Yet how this slow remodeling reorganizes and constrains neural computations that govern behavior on a moment-to-moment timescale remains poorly understood, particularly in cortical regions that support flexible social decision-making. Here we combined longitudinal high-density neural recordings, quantitative behavioral phenotyping and estrogen-receptor manipulation in female mice across low and high estrogen states. Tracking behavior and neural dynamics using this dense sampling approach revealed that high estrogen increased signatures of behavioral and neural persistence. High estrogen reversibly increased male-directed social preference and behavioral persistence, effects that were abolished by estrogen receptor alpha knockdown in the medial prefrontal cortex. In the mPFC high estrogen produced more persistent neural states that were more closely aligned with ongoing behavior, increased state discriminability, and compressed within-state dimensionality. At the single-neuron level, estrogen increased tuning selectivity, lengthened intrinsic timescales, and stabilized social representations across days, even within the same neurons tracked longitudinally. High estrogen also strengthened recurrent connectivity during the resting state, exhibiting preferential connectivity between similarly tuned ensembles. Finally, incorporating these connectivity changes into a mean-field dynamical-systems model was sufficient to reproduce increased behavioral and neural-state persistence. Together, these findings show that estrogen oscillates cortical computations across multi-day timescales, flipping the prefrontal cortex from flexible to persistent regimes that play a role in sustaining potentially costly social behaviors.

papers.title: Representation learning of somatic missense mutation landscapes across cancer types
papers.abstract: Somatic missense mutations are pervasive in cancer genomes, yet existing studies have largely compressed them into mutation burden, mutation signatures, or driver gene annotations. Such representations obscure mutation-specific context and higher-order dependencies, leaving the latent biological structure of somatic mutation landscapes insufficiently characterized by systematic, data-driven approaches. Here we present MMRL, a pan-cancer Missense Mutation Representation Learning framework that learns the representations directly from somatic missense mutation profiles. By integrating mutation-associated features including gene identity, trinucleotide context, AlphaMissense pathogenicity, amino acid substitution and protein positional information, MMRL uses self-supervised learning to capture higher-order patterns among missense mutations across ~50,000 tumor samples from diverse cancer types. Across three pan-cancer cohorts, MMRL embeddings consistently achieved higher cross-validated prognostic discrimination than TMB and remained significantly associated with overall survival after adjustment for cancer type and TMB, as well as age where available. This prognostic value was also observed among patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors. Unsupervised clustering analysis of MMRL embeddings identified nine mutation subtypes in the TCGA pan-cancer cohort, with distinct survival outcomes, cancer-type compositions and mutational signature profiles, indicating that the learned embedding space captured clinically and biologically meaningful structure. Attention-based analyses further indicated that MMRL captured context-dependent mutation patterns beyond mutation frequency and predicted pathogenicity. Together, MMRL provides a data-driven strategy for decoding somatic missense mutation landscape and may facilitate precision oncology.

papers.title: Arthroscopic Raman Probe Provides Biomarkers of TMJ Tissue Composition that Account for Tissue Function
papers.abstract: Background: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders affect up to 25% of the population and may require diverse surgical interventions. However, intraoperative decision-making relies largely on visual assessment, which does not quantitatively characterize tissue composition or mechanical function. Raman spectroscopy offers a nondestructive approach to molecular-level tissue characterization, but its application to TMJ tissues remains unvalidated. Methods: An arthroscopy-compatible Raman probe was used to characterize mandibular condyles (n=15 porcine, n=11 human) and human articular discs (n=7). Raman-derived biomarkers associated with glycosaminoglycans (GAG), collagen (COL), water (H2O), and hydroxyapatite (HA) were evaluated against condylar indentation modulus and disc tensile modulus. Arthroscopic measurements in cadaveric TMJs assessed technical feasibility, while hyperspectral Raman imaging characterized spatial compositional distributions. Results: For condylar cartilage, combined GAG and H2O biomarkers accounted for 86% of the variation in indentation modulus (R2=0.86), compared with 4% for Outerbridge grading (R2=0.04). For articular discs, combined proline and water-associated biomarkers accounted for 88% of the variation in tensile modulus (R2=0.88). Raman spectra acquired in situ under simulated arthroscopic conditions were comparable in quality to ex vivo measurements. Raman imaging revealed distinct compositional patterns in healthy and degenerated tissues, including GAG depletion and cartilage thinning in degenerated condylar cartilage. Conclusions: Raman-derived biomarkers are strongly associated with TMJ cartilage and disc mechanical properties and outperform Outerbridge grading in explaining variation in condylar indentation modulus. Arthroscopic Raman spectroscopy is technically feasible and may complement visual assessment by providing objective compositional information to support future development of tissue-informed surgical decision-making.

papers.title: Transient Partial Inhibition of DNA Polymerase α Promotes Chromatin Plasticity and Enhances Human Cell Reprogramming
papers.abstract: Somatic cell reprogramming requires extensive remodeling of epigenomic and transcriptional state, yet the mechanisms that enhance chromatin plasticity during cell-fate conversion remain incompletely understood. Beyond its essential role in genome duplication, DNA replication provides a dynamic window for chromatin remodeling and may therefore influence cellular plasticity during reprogramming. Here, we show that low-dose, transient inhibition of the lagging-strand DNA polymerase (Pol ) complex markedly enhances reprogramming of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). Fine-tuned inhibition of the catalytic subunit PolA1 increases cell survival under reprogramming-associated stress and enhances cellular resilience to diverse external stresses, preserves genomic stability, and accelerates the acquisition of pluripotent features. PolA1-inhibited cells undergo rapid increases in chromatin accessibility following reprogramming factor delivery and display accelerated progression toward the iPSC state. Consistent with enhanced developmental plasticity, colonies derived from PolA1 inhibitor-treatment display dome-shaped morphology, increased expression of several naive pluripotency markers such as SUSD2. Integrated imaging and single-nucleus multiomic analyses establish transient PolA1 inhibition as a potent regulator of early chromatin remodeling during reprogramming. Functionally, PolA1 inhibitor-derived iPSC lines maintain stable pluripotency and exhibit enhanced differentiation potential, including increased embryoid body budding and accelerated cardiomyocyte differentiation and maturation. Notably, transient and low-dose PolA1 inhibition alters replication-coupled histone incorporation without reducing DNA replication speed or affecting cell cycle progression. This two-step regime primes human PBMCs for sustained gains in reprogramming efficiency with pre- and post-treatment. Together, these findings identify replication-coupled chromatin regulation as an underappreciated mechanism regulating human cell fate plasticity and demonstrate that transient modulation of Pol can simultaneously enhance epigenomic plasticity and preserve genome stability during reprogramming.

papers.title: GLESKit: an MCP-based system for gene-level biomedical investigation and evidence synthesis
papers.abstract: Biomedical investigation at the gene level requires researchers to combine expression data, functional annotations, pathways, interaction networks, genetic associations, drug evidence and literature. Accessing these resources involves databases, analysis tools and scripts that require bioinformatics expertise, complicating the production of clear, reviewable reports. We present GLESKit, a gene centred system that connects these steps through the Model Context Protocol and retains data, analyses, sources and reports within a study workspace. We evaluated report production with 15 author curated GeneReportBench tasks and question answering with a gene level subset of BixBench, a reference biology benchmark for agentic systems. GLESKit completed all 15 reports with a mean committee score of 0.904, although evidence quality varied, and earned positive credit on 35 of 39 scored human BixBench questions with a mean of 0.438. In paired tests, configurations with skills scored 0.145 higher across 20 questions and 0.085 higher across five reports.

papers.title: Heterogeneous self-couplings enable scale-invariant memory and cognitive flexibility without criticality
papers.abstract: The hierarchical organization of the brain underlies its ability to process information across multiple time scales and support flexible behavior through context-dependent computation. Here, we study a recurrent neural network model with heterogeneous self-interactions across nodes, capturing key features of neuronal circuits, including intrinsic diversity of dynamical time scales and multistable low-dimensional manifolds. We investigate the emergence of scale-invariant dynamics without assuming criticality, challenging the view that power-law statistics necessarily arise from self-organized critical states. We show that heterogeneous self-interactions alone are sufficient to generate scale-invariant memory in subcritical regimes, while enhancing the network's dynamical richness and computational capacity. Notably, this mechanism promotes the spontaneous emergence of hierarchical organization. We assess the functional implications of this framework using short-term memory tasks and the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test, which probes cognitive flexibility and adaptive rule switching. Compared to models with heterogeneous time constants, our approach achieves comparable performance with more parsimonious synaptic modifications, while preserving scale-invariant dynamics.

papers.title: Rules of disengagement: orexin-arousal and dopamine-utility as separable axes
papers.abstract: Staying on task, leaving it, and coming back to it are processes we experience daily. They depend on task utility and arousal, but the neurochemical processes behind this interplay are unknown. In mice performing a decision-making task with shifting reward size, we identified latent engagement states and the transitions between them. Pupil-linked arousal and dopaminergic utility coding predicted these transitions along separable axes. Orexin antagonism with almorexant disengaged mice at low reward, an effect mediated by pupil-linked arousal and not by dopamine. GLP-1 receptor agonism with semaglutide reduced the gain with which accumbal dopamine integrates reward history, which predicted the progressive disengagement it caused, with no detectable contribution from arousal or orexin. Fast striatal and slow accumbal dopamine codes predicted engagement on their own timescales. These results decouple orexin-driven arousal from dopamine-mediated utility coding in task engagement, with implications for two widely used drug classes and for disorders of motivation.

papers.title: Towards a complete diploid chicken genome
papers.abstract: The repetitive and heterochromatic parts of microchromosomes and dot chromosomes have impeded the creation of a complete, haplotype-resolved chicken genome. To overcome these challenges, we employed a trio-sequencing approach, utilizing long reads from a female chick, supplemented by parental long-read data for accurate haplotype phasing. This strategy produced nearly complete, haplotype-resolved paternal and maternal assemblies, with 14 residual gaps. Telomeric sequences remain missing in two paternal and four maternal chromosomes, suggesting a still incomplete assembly. GGswu2 resolved more than 50 Mb of previously unresolved regions, predominantly within dot chromosomes. The dot chromosomes exhibit low nucleotide diversity but a high density of structural variants between haplotypes. We found that the centromere sizes and relative positions of centromere cores sometimes differ between the two haplotype genomes. These findings suggest that comparative genomics must incorporate the high-resolution of these dynamic complex regions to fully understand avian genome evolution and genetic complexity.

papers.title: Semidilute Polymer Scaling Controls PEG-induced Protein Phase Separation
papers.abstract: When does polyethylene glycol (PEG) mass concentration provide a common measure of crowding strength across polymer chain lengths? Here we use bovine serum albumin (BSA) and PEG as a controlled depletion system and measure both coexisting phases to determine binodals, tie lines, and critical points across PEG molecular weights of 4--100 kDa. Phase diagrams for PEG 20, 35, and 100 kDa approximately collapse in mass-concentration coordinates, consistent with semidilute polymer scaling. Generalized free volume theory (GFVT) describes the BSA binodals and tie lines. It also approximately describes binodals for three additional globular proteins in PEG 35K, extending the comparison across proteins spanning 7.2--66.4 kDa. For the binary PEG mixtures tested, GFVT approximates the binodals using an effective polymer size corresponding to the weight-average molecular weight. These results identify a regime in which PEG mass concentration (g/L) provides a transferable measure of depletion-induced crowding.

papers.title: An invariant network architecture with broadly expressed regulators distinguishes cell-type from cell-state identity in situ
papers.abstract: Core regulatory networks (CRNs) of tissue-specific master transcription factors (TFs) are essential for defining cell identity and are widely used to reprogram cells and to decipher pathogenic mechanisms. However, to date, CRNs have only been described at the cell-type level: their characteristics in the distinct states that a single cell type can adopt have not been examined. This leaves open what the cell-type CRNs actually represent. Here, using the zonated hepatocyte states of the mouse liver as a model system, we construct the first state-level CRNs in a native tissue. For this purpose, we developed a robust LCM-Spatial-ATAC-seq method that achieves bulk-level data quality from microdissected cell populations. By identifying what is shared among the state-level CRNs, we determined what is cell-type defining: an invariant sub-network of core-regulatory TFs (crTFs) that maintains identical positions and conserved interactions in the CRNs. Unexpectedly, the top positions of this invariant sub-network are occupied by broadly expressed TFs rather than the well-established master TFs, which reside downstream. Yet the state-level CRNs are clearly different, both in terms of composition and interactions. The former are dominated by zone-specific regulators, whereas the latter are spread throughout the network, encompassing about one third of all interactions between the states. Thus, our results reveal a novel dual character of a cell's CRN: an invariant sub-network that defines the cell-type identity, together with a variable peripheral network that underlies its state specialization.

papers.title: Representational geometry of punishment learning across basolateral amygdala neurons
papers.abstract: Punishment learning allows animals to suppress actions that cause harm while maintaining actions that earn reward. Although the basolateral amygdala is necessary for punishment learning, how its population activity changes across learning, and how this activity reflects an action's consequences, remain unknown. We used longitudinal calcium imaging to track 1,147 basolateral amygdala neurons in male mice across instrumental training, punishment, choice test, and punishment extinction. Punishment learning transformed basolateral amygdala neuron activity associated with the punished action. This activity diverged from that associated with the unpunished action and became aligned with activity evoked by the punisher itself. This alignment was action and contingency specific. It preserved the direction of individual neurons' responses to the punisher: neurons activated by the punisher become more activated by the punished action alone, whereas neurons inhibited by the punisher become more inhibited by the punished action alone. We then asked whether reward and punishment were encoded separately or on a common value dimension across basolateral amygdala neurons. Punishment added a strong shock component to action-related activity without reducing its reward component, while reward and shock themselves occupied largely orthogonal population directions. Thus, during punishment learning, basolateral amygdala population activity can encode opposing consequences of the same action instead of simply changing what that action is worth.

papers.title: Mental replay rescales the subjective duration of past events via alpha and theta oscillations
papers.abstract: Human memory recall is flexible in time, allowing past events to be mentally replayed at variable speeds. However, it remains unclear whether temporally rescaled replay distorts the perceived duration of remembered events, and whether such distortion is tied to changes in the retrieved content. Here we instructed participants to mentally replay previously encoded naturalistic videos at compressed, expanded, or self-paced (free) speeds while recording scalp electroencephalography (EEG). Replaying an event at an expanded pace lengthened participants' subsequent judgments of its original duration relative to free and compressed replay, and the longer an event had been replayed, the longer it was judged to have lasted. Crucially, recalled memory content was unaffected, with gist accuracy and recalled detail comparable across speed conditions. During replay, alpha and theta power were reduced under compression, and both interacted with the speed instruction in predicting reported duration. Specifically, alpha power exhibited a stronger positive relationship with duration judgments under compressed replay than under free or expanded replay. Conversely, the relationship between theta power and reported duration was significantly more positive under expanded replay than under free or compressed replay. Neural pattern similarity between instructed and later spontaneous replay varied with replay speed, yet this reinstatement neither predicted reported duration nor mediated the oscillatory effects. These findings suggest that remembered duration is not read out from the amount of content retrieved but reconstructed at retrieval through oscillatory dynamics, decoupling the subjective scaling of time from the content of memory.

papers.title: Harness engineering enables a multi-agent LLM system to generate cross-domain hypotheses beyond single-investigator reach
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate scientific hypotheses, and a more capable model is widely assumed to drive output quality. We tested this with a biology-focused multi-agent system coupling an LLM to five Model Context Protocol servers exposing 66 external tools. Upgrading the Synthesizer and Critic from Claude Sonnet 4.6 to Opus 4.8 initially appeared to improve quality, count, and reliability. Under a fully matched harness (identical prompts, schema, hypothesis count, and queries), the differences vanished: scores were indistinguishable on an iPSC-reprogramming task and favoured Sonnet 4.6 on a CHO cell-line-engineering task (18.4 vs 17.4; Welch t = 2.89, p < 0.05). The dominant, controllable driver of quality is therefore the prompting harness, not the model tier. We then introduce the ABCD-Stack (contract-gated prompting, diversity-first generation, adversarial refinement, and cross-family evaluation), which builds these properties in as architecture and shifts outputs toward explicitly falsifiable, causally framed hypotheses beyond the reach of a single-domain investigator. The hypotheses are falsifiable by construction but not yet experimentally validated.

papers.title: Specialisation of photosynthetic biochemistry in C4 chloroplasts potentiates distinct cell-specific functionality of different chloroplast-to-nucleus retrograde signalling pathways.
papers.abstract: Chloroplasts are key environmental sensors for plant cells. Upon exposure to abiotic stresses such as excess sunlight and heat, reactive oxygen species (ROS) in chloroplasts are sensed to trigger chloroplast-to-nucleus signalling pathways for acclimatory nuclear gene expression. There is extensive biochemical- and cell type-specialisation of chloroplasts, such as those in heat-resilient plants performing C4 photosynthesis, but how these specialisations intersect with chloroplast-to-nucleus signalling remains unclear. Here we show that specific chloroplast-to-nucleus signalling networks are functional in specialised leaf cell types of the C4 model species, Setaria viridis. RNA-sequencing, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy and metabolomics on cell type-enriched fractions, complemented with mutant analyses provided evidence for cell-specific enrichment of chloroplast-to-nucleus retrograde signalling pathways correlating with the photosynthetic specialisation in these cell types. Singlet oxygen (1O2)-responsive beta-cyclocitral ({beta}-CC) /dihydroactinidiolide (DHA) signalling and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2)-responsive 3'-phosphoadenosine 5'-phosphate (PAP) signalling pathways were specific to mesophyll cells, in line with enrichment of photosystem II and linear electron flow to photosystem I, respectively in this cell type. In contrast, bundle sheath cells were enriched for the rapid, ROS-independent retrograde signalling pathway mediated by the Calvin cycle product, dihydroxyacetone phosphate (DHAP), consistent with the exclusive localisation of the Calvin cycle to C4 bundle sheath cells. Taken together, our results provide insights into how chloroplast- and cell type-specialisation intersect with stress signalling in plant cells and identify photosynthetic biochemistry as a key driver of cell-specific cellular signalling.

papers.title: Amino Acid Metabolic Signature Links Pediatric Environmental Enteric Dysfunction to Maternal-Fetal Growth Restriction Across Two Independent Cohorts
papers.abstract: Environmental Enteric Dysfunction (EED) is a leading contributor to childhood stunting. Most EED literature derives from postnatal pediatric cohorts, leaving unclear how much of the metabolic signature reflects acquired intestinal pathology versus growth restriction originating earlier. We applied genome-scale metabolic modeling to explore whether metabolic features of pediatric EED overlap with those of maternal plasma proteomes associated with adverse early-life growth. Duodenal transcriptomics from the Study of Environmental Enteropathy and Malnutrition (SEEM; 52 children with EED, 24 controls) and maternal plasma proteomics from the Alliance for Maternal and Newborn Health Improvement (AMANHI; n = 2,485 pregnant women) were integrated with the Human1 model using Reaction Inclusion by Parsimony and Transcript Distribution (RIPTiDe), followed by flux sampling and Linear Discriminant Analysis, across five growth-related proxies (small-for-gestational-age, low birth weight, preterm birth, stunting, and wasting). Amino acid and nucleotide metabolism were prominent among the top discriminating reactions in EED and most proxies. Of the 50 reactions distinguishing EED from control, 24 (48%) were among the top reactions in at least one proxy, and 19 (38%) with low birth weight, the largest of any proxy. These exploratory findings suggest shared metabolic pathways across tissues and life stages and motivate longitudinal studies.

papers.title: Multiscale Transcriptomic Architecture of the ALS Motor Cortex
papers.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) exhibits marked clinical and molecular heterogeneity, but how this heterogeneity is organized within disease-relevant central nervous system regions remains incompletely understood. Because pooled cross-region analyses may confound regional variation with subtype structure, we focused on the motor cortex, a key site of ALS pathology, to resolve its internal transcriptomic organization. Using approximately 600 postmortem motor cortex transcriptomes from the Target ALS resource, we applied gene set variation analysis to generate sample-level pathway activity profiles and performed consensus clustering in pathway space. We identified seven reproducible ALS motor cortex subtypes characterized by distinct inflammatory, damage-response, metabolic, glial, and neuronal/synaptic programs. Donor-held-out projection recovered the seven subtype assignments with a mean balanced accuracy of 0.939, supporting the reproducibility of the pathway-defined subtype structure in unseen donors. Mapping these bulk-defined programs to an independent motor-cortex single-nucleus RNA-seq dataset revealed distinct cellular contexts, while cell-type marker adjustment showed that cellular differences contributed to, but did not fully account for, subtype-associated pathway variation. The seven subtypes also recapitulated major molecular programs reported in previous ALS subtype frameworks while resolving them into finer motor-cortex-specific states. Rather than forming isolated molecular classes, these subtypes occupied a structured pathway-space landscape with both discrete subtype-centered peaks and continuous biological gradients. Principal component analysis and representative pathway overlays defined a major axis from an upper inflammatory/damage region to a lower neuronal/metabolic/remodeling region, with C7 forming a neuronal/synaptic connector within the lower landscape. Co-expression network analysis further supported this multiscale organization, revealing family-level network backbones, subtype-specific modular refinements, and bridge-like rewiring. Metadata-informed analyses showed that this molecular architecture was not primarily organized by disease duration. Instead, the landscape was more clearly associated with clinical and genetic-background variables, including ALS/FTD family history and mutation-related signals. In particular, family-history-positive and C9orf72 repeat expansion-positive samples were more represented in the lower neuronal/metabolic/remodeling region, whereas family-history-negative samples and C9orf72-negative cases were more represented in the upper inflammatory/damage region. These findings support a model in which ALS motor cortex heterogeneity is organized as a multiscale transcriptomic architecture more closely associated with genetic-background variables than with disease duration. This framework provides a basis for subtype-aware biological comparison, future patient-stratification, biomarker, or therapeutic target-prioritization studies.

papers.title: iGEX: an interactive Gene EXpression exploration platform for the analysis of transcriptomic and proteomic datasets
papers.abstract: High-throughput transcriptomic and proteomic studies have generated a rapidly expanding collection of publicly available datasets. However, extracting biological insight from these resources often requires researchers to repeatedly download, reformat, integrate and analyse individual files using specialised tools. This process is time-consuming and often requires coding expertise. Here, we present iGEX, an interactive exploration platform that can incorporate publicly available and user-generated transcriptomic and proteomic datasets into a single visual workspace to simplify the analysis of multiple transcripts and/or proteins across numerous datasets. iGEX enables researchers to select gene/protein targets and experiments and compare expression patterns across biological conditions and experiments. User-generated data can be examined alongside numerous public resources such as EMBL-EBI Expression Atlas, Bgee, and PaxDb to determine whether any observed patterns are evident across experiments, species or experimental contexts. Users can visualise and move directly between data tables, principal component analysis, expression and correlation heatmaps, hierarchical clustering and volcano plots, all of which are editable and downloadable.

papers.title: BaitBench: a comprehensive tool for building, as-sessing, and predicting outcomes for hybrid capture enrichment probes
papers.abstract: The effectiveness of hybridization capture sequencing, a powerful lab technique to isolate and characterize low-abundance samples from complex nucleic acid mixtures, relies heavily on creating a robust probe set. There are a variety of tools that design, evaluate, or simulate capture probes, however, these tools are often siloed and frequently difficult to use. To our knowledge there is no tool that connects all steps of the hybridization capture probe development and analysis process. Here we introduce BaitBench, a comprehensive tool to aid in the design, assessment, and simulation of target capture probes. BaitBench wraps or reimplements in Rust several current tools, and implements a thermodynamic model for simulating capture. Integrating steps allows us to track simulated reads through the whole process enabling us to report sources of false positives and reasons for false negatives. Easy to read output files and the ability to run via command line or GUI interfaces increases usability. We validated BaitBench against publicly available data and achieved a high correlation ({rho} = 0.916), demonstrating its accuracy and translation to real-world settings. Code is available at github.com/niel-infante/BaitBench, with installers for Mac and Windows available at github.com/niel-infante/BaitBench/releases.

papers.title: Behavioral Markers of Essential Tremor Correlate with Distributed Alteration of Brain Functional Connectivity
papers.abstract: Essential Tremor (ET) is a common motor disorder characterized by involuntary oscillations of the upper limbs during voluntary movement. Although increasing evidence implicates dysfunction of the cerebello-thalamo-cortical pathway, ET remains a diagnosis of exclusion, as no definitive biological marker currently exists. To better characterize ET, we recently hypothesized that impaired compensation of sensorimotor delays within the long-latency feedback pathways may generate the tremor-like oscillations observed in ET. This theory suggests that the mean spectral amplitude (MSA), derived from limb kinematics, may serve as a potential marker of ET. Here we investigated the relationship between MSA, standard clinical assessment (Fahn Tolosa Marin Tremor Rating Scale; FTM-TRS), and brain connectivity derived from resting state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI). Using seed-based analyses, we replicated previous findings of reduced functional connectivity between the dentate nucleus and components of the cerebello-thalamo-cortical pathway in ET patients compared with neurologically intact (NI) age-matched participants. Graph-theoretical analyses of whole-brain functional networks revealed distributed alterations in network topology across motor-related cortical and subcortical regions. Several graph metrics correlated with FTM-TRS scores and/or MSA, particularly within motor-related cortical and subcortical circuits, including the thalamus, basal ganglia, and cerebellum in ET. These findings indicate that ET is characterized by distributed alterations in functional brain networks beyond reduced connectivity of dentate nucleus and highlights MSA as a candidate quantitative marker linking altered brain connectivity to sensorimotor delay-driven tremor oscillations.

papers.title: Does a map-level insulation constraint improve sequence-based prediction of 3D genome folding? A Stage 1 Registered Report with a reverse-complement-equivariant state-space model (HiFold-Mamba)
papers.abstract: Background. Sequence-to-contact-map models are trained with pixel-wise losses, although the features of interest (insulation, domain boundaries, loops) are summaries of the map. Insulationbased losses help Hi-C resolution enhancement. No pre-specified test has asked whether they improve sequence-based prediction, judged against annotations independent of the training data. Proposed study. HiFold-Mamba predicts 448 x 448 maps at 2,048 bp from 1,048,576 bp of DNA on the DNALongBench contact-map task. Every component is reverse-complement-equivariant: convolutional tower, bidirectional Mamba blocks, multi-scale mixer and symmetric pairwise head. We pre-register three hypotheses: >> H1: it exceeds each of three trained baselines (reproduced Akita, a parameter-matched Transformer and a parameter-matched CNN) by [≥]0.01 stratum-adjusted correlation (SCC). >> H2: an insulation and boundary loss, computed from the predicted map with the operator used on the observed map, improves boundary AUROC and loop AP against independent 4DN boundary calls and ENCODE CTCF ChIA-PET loops, at equal training steps and without loss of SCC. >> H3: pretraining plus few-shot adaptation beats training from scratch on four held-out cell lines.Tests use a paired bootstrap over 237 one-megabase test blocks (one-sided = 0.025). Pilot data. >> Verification. The benchmark target, the window coordinates and the networks equivariance were verified. >> Locus-shared reference. Copying other cell lines measured maps at the same locus matches published Akita on the benchmarks SCC (0.227 vs. 0.230). >> SCC weightings. Two weightings in common use weight distance strata in opposite directions and agree only moderately ({rho} = 0.54). >> Comparison rule. In simulations calibrated on the pilot data, a per-block-best comparison against several baselines has no power. We therefore test against each baseline, which gives [≥] 90 % power at a true gain of 0.02 when between-model correlation is [≥] 0.95. >> H2 positive control. On validation windows, observed maps recover the independent boundaries (AUROC 0.61 - 0.91) and loops (0.86 - 0.90). This fixed the insulation window and showed that these annotations are largely shared across cell types.

papers.title: Intrinsic immune receptor triggering mechanism informs rational chimeric receptor design
papers.abstract: The T cell receptor (TCR) couple antigen recognition to T-cell activation and immune homeostasis. As an eight-subunit assembly, TCR activation operates as a highly coordinated, multi-subunit signaling event. However, which subunit serves as the primary trigger upon ligand engagement still remains unresolved. we identify CD3{varepsilon} as a triggering subunit whose intracellular domain (ICD) is released from the plasma membrane during TCR activation. Elevated membrane tension facilitates this transition from a membrane-proximal to a membrane-distal conformation. The released ICD forms condensates through phase separation with free or co-receptor-associated Lck. These condensates recruit additional CD3{varepsilon} ICDs from neighboring TCRs, triggering resting receptors and promoting further recruitment of TCRs and Lck to amplify proximal signaling. The CD3{varepsilon} ICD alone support robust T cell activation independently of its own ITAM. We observe a similar triggering mechanism in several activating receptors in T and nature killer (NK) cell. These findings support a unifying model in which designated subunits initiate multi-subunit immune receptor activation through phase separation with key kinases. Guided by this model, we engineered triggering molecules (TRIG) that lack canonical intracellular signaling modules. These TRIG molecules recruit endogenous immune receptors in a ligand-dependent manner and efficiently activate both T cells and NK cells. This mechanism provides a basis for designing chimeric receptors that activate immune cells through endogenous receptor signaling.

papers.title: Distinct profiles and antibody production by splenic and lymph node antibody-secreting cells in Trypanosoma cruzi infection
papers.abstract: Evidence from bone marrow and intestinal lamina propria studies indicates that antibody-secreting cell (ASC) characteristics are shaped by the local microenvironment; yet whether secondary lymphoid organs harbor distinct ASC populations during infection remains unclear. Here, we investigated plasmablasts (PB) from the spleen and inguinal lymph nodes (LN) in acute Trypanosoma cruzi infection. Although PB from both tissues expressed canonical ASC markers, they displayed distinct transcriptional, phenotypic, and functional profiles. Splenic PB upregulated genes and proteins associated with inflammation, immunomodulation, and B-cell interactions. Activated and naive B cells also exhibited tissue-specific transcriptional programs, suggesting that local cues influence B-cell differentiation. Consistent with these differences, spleens from infected mice contained more T follicular helper cells, whereas LN were enriched in regulatory T cells. High-dimensional flow cytometry identified multiple PB subsets differentially represented between tissues. Functionally, splenic PB secreted higher levels of IgM, IgA, and IgG, including both parasite-specific and autoreactive antibodies. In contrast, LN PB preferentially produced IgG against peptide 72 of the shed acute-phase antigen (SAPA), despite lower overall T. cruzi-specific antibody production. These findings demonstrate that secondary lymphoid organs harbor distinct PB populations adapted to their local microenvironments during acute infection

papers.title: Pre-stress functional brain connectivity is associated with subsequent anxiety during war-related stress
papers.abstract: Individuals exposed to major real-world stressors show markedly different psychological outcomes, but whether this heterogeneity is associated with pre-existing neural characteristics remains unclear because neuroimaging is rarely performed beforehand. We acquired resting-state fMRI in healthy adults before the unforeseen onset of war-related stress. Approximately 13 months later, during ongoing war-related stress, participants (n = 31) were assessed for anxiety, depressive symptoms, perceived stress and post-traumatic stress symptoms. Among 144 associations spanning 36 predefined corticolimbic and reward-related connections and four outcomes, lower baseline functional connectivity between the right nucleus accumbens and right amygdala was associated with greater subsequent anxiety. This association survived permutation-based family-wise error correction and adjustment for baseline depressive symptoms, age and sex. These findings provide preliminary prospective evidence that pre-existing functional organization of threat- and reward-related circuitry is associated with individual differences in anxiety during prolonged adversity.

papers.title: Alignment-Free k-mer Analysis Reveals Age-Associated k-mer Signals in Canine Buccal DNA and Cell-Free DNA
papers.abstract: Aging is associated with progressive molecular and cellular changes that alter chromatin organization, epigenetic regulation, and microbial community structure. While DNA methylation-based biomarkers have demonstrated age-prediction performance, the potential of alignment-free sequence analysis for detecting age-associated signals remains unexplored. We performed a k-mer-based analysis of whole-genome sequencing datasets from two canine cohorts: 1,187 buccal DNA samples and 100 cell-free DNA (cfDNA) samples. Age-associated k-mers were identified through correlation analysis, and sequence motifs and nucleotide composition patterns were characterized across both sample types. Ridge regression models were used to predict age from k-mer frequency profiles, and synthetic datasets were generated under biological compositional assumptions to evaluate potential drivers of the observed signals. Age-associated k-mer signals were identified in both buccal DNA and cfDNA, with substantially stronger patterns observed in buccal samples. Buccal-derived k-mers exhibited more pronounced motif patterns, stronger GC and AT enrichment trends, and improved age-prediction performance relative to cfDNA. Nucleotide enrichment trends differed between sample types, suggesting that distinct biological processes may contribute to age-associated sequence composition changes in buccal DNA and cfDNA. Simulation analyses successfully reproduced major enrichment trends observed empirically, and age-associated signals were largely preserved following restriction to read-start sequence composition. These findings demonstrate that alignment-free k-mer analysis can detect age-associated sequence composition signals in canine DNA and highlight its potential as a computationally efficient complementary approach for aging biomarker discovery.

papers.title: Sex-based differences in fibrosis markers in human abdominal aortic aneurysms
papers.abstract: Background: Abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA) are a complex degenerative vascular disease. The role of fibrosis in AAA progression is unclear. Our study evaluated the impact of fibroblast activation protein (FAP), collagen, and vimentin on AAA fibrosis and progression. We hypothesized that FAP may influence fibrosis and disease severity in AAA, with potential sex-specific differences. Study Design: Multi-centered transcriptomic analysis of aortic samples from 15 human AAA and 5 non-AAA was performed to evaluate cell-specific fibrosis gene expression profiles. Histopathological and molecular analysis of 26 male and female AAA samples (mAAA and fAAA) and 29 male and female normal abdominal aortas (mNAA and fNAA) was performed to assess whole-tissue fibrosis markers and signaling. Results: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis identified eight major cell clusters with distinct sex-based distributions. Although vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) and fibroblast clusters had reduced counts in both male and female AAAs, they more highly expressed FAP and COL1A1 genes, particularly in females. Whole-tissue analysis demonstrated elevated extracellular matrix deposits with markedly increased collagen type 1 in both mAAA and fAAA. Alpha-smooth muscle actin (-SMA)-positive VSMCs were also reduced in mAAA and fAAA, but FAP was notably elevated, and robustly in fAAA. FAP-positive fibroblasts in fAAA exhibited increased expression of fibrosis markers, suggesting a unique pro-fibrotic phenotype. Conclusion: Our study reveals a sex-based difference in AAA tissue, with elevated fibrosis markers and increased FAP levels in females, suggesting its significant role in disease progression. These findings underscore the potential of FAP as a unique tissue biomarker for AAAs and warrants further investigation into novel targeted therapies that aim to stabilize AAAs, particularly in female patients.

papers.title: Rapid switching of in-phase and anti-phase interhemispheric rhythms within a single theta cycle: a mechanistic explanation
papers.abstract: The granular retrosplenial cortex (RSG) supports memory consolidation and spatial navigation. In vivo recordings of local field potential (LFP) from RSG reveal coexisting gamma (30-80 Hz) and spline (100-160 Hz) oscillations, coupled to distinct phases of the background theta ([~]8 Hz) rhythm. Remarkably, bilateral recordings reveal that gamma and splines exhibit divergent interhemispheric phase relationships: gamma is in-phase across hemispheres, while splines are anti-phase. Here, using numerical bifurcation analysis of next-generation neural mass models, we show that RSG oscillations within a single hemisphere can be understood as alternation of PING (pyramidal-interneuron gamma) and ING (interneuron gamma) mechanisms in an excitatory-inhibitory network. Theta-frequency external drive to the inhibitory population switches the network between these two rhythms. Next, we build canonical interhemispheric circuits, composed of two such excitatory-inhibitory modules, delay-coupled across hemispheres. These circuits switch between in-phase gamma and anti-phase splines within a single theta cycle, reproducing the cross-spectral statistics of experimental RSG recordings. Finally, we present analytical results for threshold-linear neural mass models, showing cross-hemispheric phase patterning is governed by the ratio of cross-hemispheric delay to local inhibitory delay; we obtain explicit ranges of this ratio for which RSG-like patterning could be expected. Our work establishes that the unique oscillatory profile of RSG can be explained parsimoniously by minimal interhemispheric circuit configurations and provides a framework for experimental interrogation of interhemispheric rhythms.

papers.title: Digital twins forecast individual immune trajectories
papers.abstract: The human immune system differs markedly between individuals and changes in response to infection, vaccination and treatment. AI virtual cells are being built to simulate cellular responses to perturbation. Yet these models, like most immune-response predictors, describe each person by a single pre-challenge measurement and forecast change from patterns pooled across people. Digital twins, updated with every new observation of an individual, could forecast how that person's immune state changes. Here we present ImmuneTwins, which builds these twins from single-cell profiles by personalizing a shared virtual-cell model with each individual's observations. In two external populations, ImmuneTwins reduced immune-age error by 32% and 42% relative to the best existing method. During repeated influenza vaccination, its twins predicted the direction of immune-cell change 35% more accurately than the best published method, and their error fell by 27% as observations accumulated. The twins revealed that immune cells and plasma proteins recover about half their deviation from a persistent personal reference within 90 days, whereas response size varies between challenges. They further localized B-cell remodelling in exceptional longevity and anticipated patient-specific immune trajectories during myeloma treatment. These results establish virtual-cell digital twins for forecasting individual immune change and identifying each person's characteristic immune features.

papers.title: A convergent proline biosynthetic step couples cell wall integrity to virulence in Cryptococcus neoformans
papers.abstract: Metabolic adaptation is essential for the pathogenicity of the opportunistic fungus Cryptococcus neoformans. Although amino acid biosynthesis pathways are critical fitness determinants in fungal pathogens, the physiological contributions of proline biosynthesis remain incompletely understood, with most studies focusing on proline catabolism. Here, we characterized the proline biosynthetic enzymes Pro1, Pro2, and Pro3 in C. neoformans. Proline is produced by two routes that converge on {Delta}1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate (P5C): a de novo pathway from glutamate via Pro1 and Pro2, and an arginine-derived bypass via Car1 and Car2--both requiring Pro3 for the final reduction of P5C to proline. Although all biosynthetic mutants were strictly auxotrophic for proline, their requirements for virulence differed markedly: in a murine infection model, pro1{Delta} and pro2{Delta} mutants retained full virulence, whereas pro3{Delta} exhibited significantly attenuated virulence accompanied by growth defects and impaired cell wall integrity. Genetic disruption of P5C-generating routes partially restored distinct pro3{Delta} phenotypes, with PRO2 deletion alleviating delayed growth and combined PRO2 and CAR2 deletion partially restoring cell size, while cell wall defects remained unresolved. This dissociation indicates that growth requires proper balance of P5C-generating metabolic flux, whereas cell wall integrity depends on a distinct mechanism that is not resolved by blocking P5C production. Together, these findings identify Pro3 as a metabolic gatekeeper coupling proline biosynthesis to cell wall homeostasis, establishing the biosynthetic branch of proline metabolism as a previously unappreciated determinant of fungal pathobiology.

papers.title: Bridging Sensory Extraction and Decision Dynamics: Face Pareidolia Emergent from Bottom-Up and Top-Down Interactions
papers.abstract: Face pareidolia-the illusory perception of faces in everyday objects-provides a unique window into how the human brain resolves visual ambiguity. Whether pareidolia arises from bottom-up sensory processing or top-down, expectation-driven feedback, is currently debated. Here we recorded electroencephalography (EEG) while participants viewed rapid serial visual presentation (RSVP) streams of images, each of which was an object-to-face morph generated along a 21-image continuum via text-to-image diffusion models. Time-resolved representational similarity analyses revealed a clear spatiotemporal dissociation, in which early occipitotemporal areas tracked physical feature changes linearly, while later frontocentral channels collapsed this structural gradient into a sharp, sigmoidal profile reflecting discrete categorical decisions (face-like versus object-like). To characterise information transmission between these regions, we implemented a novel transformation-based representational connectivity analysis. These analyses uncovered an initial feedforward flow of information that transferred and transformed posterior linear traces into anterior sigmoidal representations. Crucially, partitioning the image continuum revealed that unambiguous stimuli (faces or objects) were predominantly resolved via feedforward information flow, whereas ambiguous pareidolic images recruited prolonged top-down feedback. Furthermore, perceptual decision sensitivity was biased by animacy priors and directly predicted individual behavioural reaction times during the task. Together, the findings help reconcile prior debate by establishing that face pareidolia is neither a feedforward process nor an isolated top-down projection, but an active, multi-stage recurrent process driven by feedforward feature extraction and top-down categorical resolution.

papers.title: Live-cell, single-molecule imaging resolves the dual nature of mRNA silencing by SARS-CoV-2 Nsp1
papers.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 nonstructural protein 1 (Nsp1) is a conserved viral factor that potently silences host transcripts by binding ribosomes. Yet how it acts at the level of individual mRNAs remains unclear, with competing models arguing that Nsp1 blocks translation initiation, stalls ribosome elongation, cleaves mRNA, or does all three. Here, we use Nascent Chain Tracking to quantify in living cells how Nsp1 reshapes mRNA abundance and translation dynamics with single-molecule resolution. Using reporter transcripts that vary in UTR architecture, initiation mode, and open reading frame length, we find that Nsp1 mainly silences our reporter transcripts by reducing their numbers rather than inhibiting initiation. Two routes to Nsp1-mediated mRNA loss are identified, both requiring cap-dependent initiation: an early route acting during or shortly after initiation and a later route associated with downstream translation that depends in part on ZNF598. Together, these two mechanisms make Nsp1 an efficient and robust suppressor of host gene expression. We further find that reporters containing the SARS-CoV-2 UTRs remain susceptible to Nsp1-mediated mRNA loss, but the 5' and 3' UTRs cooperate to increase translation output. Neither viral UTR alone increased translation beyond the host reporter, whereas combining both UTRs substantially enhanced translation in the absence of Nsp1. Together, our results reveal that Nsp1 uses dual, cap-dependent routes to promote mRNA loss across the translation cycle, while the SARS-CoV-2 UTRs provide a cooperative translational advantage rather than robust protection from Nsp1.

papers.title: Influenza A virus H5Nx genotypes assigned by genetic similarity are incongruent with global phylogenies
papers.abstract: Influenza A virus H5N1 and other H5 subtypes (H5Nx) have broad host ranges and pose a pandemic risk. Since early 2022, H5 clade 2.3.4.4b has predominated globally, causing unprecedented mortality in wild birds, poultry, and mammals, with spillovers to humans. Accurate viral classification is essential for tracking H5Nx variant emergence and spread, but reassortment among genome segments with distinct evolutionary histories complicates genotyping. H5Nx genotype assignment tools, GenoFlu in North America and Genin2 in Europe, assign segments to clusters by genetic similarity to reference sequences and define genotypes as constellations of segment clusters. However, genetic similarity does not necessarily imply recent shared ancestry because mutations may occur multiple times across the tree and branches may exhibit variable evolutionary rates. Furthermore, similarity is defined relative to references that may inadequately represent diversity. We evaluated the congruence of genetic similarity-based H5Nx clusters and genotypes with phylogenies of global sequences across eight segments. Publicly available H5Nx nucleotide sequences from 41,366 samples were assigned genotypes using GenoFlu and Genin2, and maximum likelihood phylogenies were inferred for each segment. Phylogenetic clusters were identified using TreeCluster for a range of patristic distance thresholds and CD-HIT clusters were identified for a range of genetic similarity thresholds. Clustering methods were evaluated based on phylogenetic purity, monophyly, and diversity. Reassortment within predominant GenoFlu and Genin2 genotypes was evaluated based on their phylogenetic cluster spans. Expectedly, GenoFlu was largely unable to assign genomes from outside of North America, South America, and Antarctica from 2022 to 2025, whereas Genin2 assignments struggled outside of Europe, Africa, and Western Asia. Only 14.2% of GenoFlu clusters were monophyletic, while Genin2 clusters were more variable across segments (overall 49.3% monophyletic). Despite CD-HIT yielding genetic distance clusters of similar size to TreeCluster, they were less monophyletic (44%) and encompassed greater phylogenetic diversity. We identified several genotypes, such as GenoFlu B3.13, D1.1, and D1.3, with internal segments that had diversified into contiguous clusters. Similarly, the wide phylogenetic span of GenoFlu genotypes B3.5 and A3, and Genin2 genotypes EA-2020-C, EA-2021-AB, and EA-2022-CH suggest they may erroneously combine multiple reassortants. Genetic similarity-based H5Nx genotyping tools are rapid, stable, and sufficient for broad categorization, but may group viruses with distinct evolutionary histories and fail to assign divergent viruses, risking biased surveillance, modeling, and risk assessment.

papers.title: Targeting the RNA regulator HuR in acute traumatic brain injury mitigates secondary injury and improves functional outcome by suppressing neuroinflammation
papers.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) affects ~2.5 million people annually in the US. Minutes after TBI, microglia and astrocytes initiate a neuroinflammatory cascade which promotes secondary injury via cytotoxicity, blood-brain barrier damage, edema, and immune cell recruitment. HuR, an RNA regulator, plays a critical role in the glial response by promoting the expression of proinflammatory mediators including IL-6, IL-1{beta}, TNF-, COX-2, CCL2, and CXCL1 via adenine and uridine-rich elements in the 3' untranslated region of their mRNAs. Here, we assessed SRI-42127, a small molecule HuR inhibitor developed by our group, on neuroinflammatory responses, secondary injury, and functional outcome after TBI. Male mice underwent controlled cortical impact (CCI) followed by peripheral administration of SRI-42127. Functional outcomes assessed included: motor function (balance beam/rotarod) and memory function (object location/recognition). Edema, lesion volume, and BBB permeability were assessed by MRI, brain water content, and Evans blue dye extravasation. HuR nucleocytoplasmic translocation, neuronal loss/apoptosis, microglial and astrocyte activation, and neutrophil infiltration were quantified by immunohistochemistry. Proinflammatory mediator induction was assessed by RT-qPCR and/or immunoblot. Results showed that SRI-42127 treatment improved spatial memory and fine motor performance in the first week in parallel with a reduction in edema, vascular permeability, lesion size, and neuronal loss/apoptosis. There was attenuated microglial activation and astrogliosis, decreased neutrophil infiltration, and suppression of proinflammatory mediator induction. Mechanistically, SRI-42127 inhibited HuR nucleocytoplasmic translocation in microglia and astrocytes. In summary, SRI-42127 potently suppresses neuroinflammation and secondary injury after TBI, improves functional outcomes, and identifies HuR as a new therapeutic target in TBI.

papers.title: ARG-PASS v2.0 expands global resistome surveillance to reveal previously unrecognized antibiotic resistance genes reaching the human gut
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a significant global public health threat, and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) that bacteria depend on to withstand treatment are its molecular basis. How ARGs move from environmental reservoirs into the human microbiome, and eventually into human pathogens, remains one of the most important unresolved questions in AMR research. The environmental reservoir remains poorly described and the routes connecting it to human microbiomes are largely inferred rather than observed. Describing that reservoir requires computational methods able to recognise ARGs that share little similarity with known enzymes, yet retain accuracy after experimental validation to enable scalable applications. Dietary exposure through unprocessed ferments offers a tractable setting in which such a route can be observed directly. Here we introduce ARG-PASS v2.0 and first apply it to a lake metagenome from Kolkata, India, where 10 of 11 tested candidates across diverse ARG classes were functionally confirmed after expression in Escherichia coli. Given their clinical relevance, we then predicted 918 class B1 metallo-{beta}-lactamases (MBLs) from MGnify and the PLSDB, with most diverging from characterized enzymes, but as widely distributed. Often tracking their hosts distribution, we find that most class B1 MBL diversity lies outside human-associated microbiomes. Cross-referencing against the Unified Human Gastrointestinal Protein catalogue identified a carbapenemase, an ANT, and class A {beta}-lactamases from Bacillus sonorensis and Bacillus licheniformis, detected in South Korean fermented soybean paste (doenjang) as well as gut isolates of populations consuming these foods. Together, these results point to a largely chromosomal reservoir of ARG diversity that reaches the human gut through both resident and generalist hosts. Once in the human microbiome, treatment may be compromised directly if the host is an opportunistic pathogen, or after transfer to a clinical pathogen.

papers.title: Hippocampal replay repairs the cognitive map for flexible planning
papers.abstract: Hippocampal replay is structured: prospective replay typically precedes retrospective replay, each aligns with the animal's future and past paths, and replay sometimes targets abandoned goals. We propose that replay repairs the cognitive map. A map that supports efficient planning precomputes expected paths; because plans terminate at the goal, the goal is part of the structure it represents. Every goal change therefore leaves the map incorrect and requires two repairs: one for the goal adopted, one for the goal left behind. The larger is expressed first, and the path each takes determines what it depicts, accounting for replay's ordering, direction, and paradoxical content. The model also generates the predictions that this ordering should invert when past and future paths converge. Recordings from rats foraging in an open arena confirm this: replay order is not as fixed as previously believed, but varies with trajectory geometry and the proximity of the abandoned goal.

papers.title: SRSF1 coordinates transcription and alternative splicing to modulate p53 and apoptosis
papers.abstract: Serine/arginine-rich splicing factor 1 (SRSF1) regulates alternative splicing and acts as a proto-oncogene, but its transcriptional functions remain poorly characterized. We combined time-course RNA sequencing and experimental validation to characterize SRSF1-dependent transcription and alternative splicing. We validated 66 of 142 splicing events, including 43 unannotated in GENCODE and 15 containing previously unannotated exons. Thirty-five events showed concordant regulation across HEK293, MCF-7, and PC-3 cells, including 17 in 16 genes associated with p53 functions. SRSF1 overexpression reduced total p53, increased basal Ser15 phosphorylation, and increased apoptosis under basal and cisplatin-treated conditions but not following doxorubicin. SRSF1 increased transcription of 28 genes, including 18 consistently regulated across all three cell lines. Mechanistic studies linked transcriptional activation to P-TEFb mobilization from the 7SK snRNP. Analyses of 33 TCGA cancer cohorts and 47 GTEx normal-tissue cohorts identified widespread positive associations between SRSF1 expression and these genes. Additional analyses identified associations with breast cancer subtypes, thyroid differentiation, and renal cancer clinical outcomes. These findings establish concurrent SRSF1-dependent transcriptional and splicing programs associated with cellular signaling, genome maintenance, p53 regulation, and cancer biology.

papers.title: A Blast Fungus Effector Targets a Tubby-like F-box Protein to Suppress Plant Immunity
papers.abstract: The blast fungus Magnaporthe oryzae is one of the most destructive pathogens of rice, secreting effector proteins that reprogram host cells to enable infection. Identifying plant targets of these fungal effectors is central to understanding how blast disease is established, but the targets and mechanisms of most effectors remain unknown. Here, we show that a Zinc finger (ZiF)-family effector, Tie1, targets the rice Tubby-like protein (TLP) family, which are membrane-associated plant immunity regulators whose exact functions have not been defined. Tie1 binds a range of rice TLPs and specifically engages with the Tubby-like domain of OsTLP7. Co-expression in planta with Tie1 re-localises this domain from the plasma membrane to the cytoplasm and nucleus, a shift also observed by disrupting the OsTLP7 phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2)-binding site in the absence of the effector. By combining AlphaFold3 structural predictions with allelic variation, we define a putative Tie1/OsTLP7 interface distal to the PIP2-binding site. Furthermore, Tie1 induces transcriptional activation activity of the OsTLP7 Tubby-like domain, and Tie1 overexpression in stable Arabidopsis lines leads to upregulation of genes that repress jasmonic acid (JA) signalling. Taken together, our results indicate that Tie1 inhibits PIP2 binding by OsTLP7 to drive its re-localisation to the nucleus and thereby modulating transcription to suppress JA-mediated plant immunity.

papers.title: Cortical organoid diffusion MRI reveals protocol-associated spatial reproducibility and increasing apparent diffusivity with diffusion time
papers.abstract: Early human cortical development involves rapid cytoarchitectural changes that are difficult to study non-invasively. Diffusion MRI can probe developing microstructure and membrane water exchange, but model assumptions are difficult to validate in human tissue. Cortical organoids provide a tractable platform for relating diffusion measurements to tissue architecture. We scanned six fixed cortical organoids at 9.4 T, three grown under directed and three under undirected differentiation protocols, at three diffusion times and b-values up to 7000 s/mm2 Center-to-periphery profiles of diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI) metrics were reproducible across directed organoids but more variable across undirected organoids, consistent with nuclear staining. Unexpectedly, DKI-derived apparent mean diffusivity (MD) increased with diffusion time in more than 80% of tissue voxels in both batches, opposite to previous organoid measurements. Across 12,348 analytically simulated two-compartment substrates and Monte Carlo diffusion simulations in sphere packings, this trend emerged in permeable substrates with a marked contrast between extracellular and apparent intracellular diffusivities. Detailed Monte Carlo trajectory analysis of a representative substrate showed that fitted MD increased despite decreases in displacement-derived and second-cumulant diffusivities, revealing an exchange-sensitive finite-b effect involving higher-order signal contributions. These findings support using cortical organoids to probe early microstructure, test diffusion models, and investigate potential emerging diffusion biomarkers.

papers.title: Asymmetric Adaptation of Catch-up Saccades with Artificial Central Scotomas
papers.abstract: In fully-sighted individuals, pursuit and saccadic eye movements work together to foveate moving targets; pursuit attempts to match target velocity, while catch-up saccades re-align the fovea to the target if it deviates during pursuit. Although saccade-pursuit interactions are well understood in healthy individuals, much less is known about how these mechanisms adapt in the presence of central vision loss. Here, we simulated central vision loss in healthy young adults to examine plasticity in saccade-pursuit mechanisms and investigated whether and how catch-up saccades adapted over five days of visual tracking. Twenty-five fully sighted participants performed a task in which they pursued a moving target that stepped position randomly (designed to elicit catch-up saccades) while viewing with a gaze-contingent central scotoma. The scotoma was shaped like a bitten cookie to encourage use of a specific preferred retinal locus (PRL) corresponding to the peripheral location with the highest acuity. By the end of the five days of repetition, most participants showed catch-up saccade endpoints shifted towards the PRL rather than the fovea. On average, endpoints shifted 0.5 deg towards the PRL between days 1 and 5 (range=0.3-1.5 deg), with significant shifts in 13 of the 25 participants. Adaptation was asymmetric; shifts were largest when the target moved in the direction opposite the scotoma bite and smallest when it moved towards it. In summary, we observed adaptation of saccade-pursuit interactive mechanisms through the re-referencing of catch-up saccades from the fovea to PRL. These results provide a promising avenue for rehabilitation in central vision loss aimed at improving eye movements and encouraging PRL use. Ultimately, such an approach may enhance residual visual function and quality of life.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of protease-inhibitor gene family counts under different counting units and genome annotations
papers.abstract: Background: Gene family sizes are often compared across species using the protein sets released with genome assemblies. However, counts of domain-positive protein entries can differ from counts of genes when an annotation contains several entries per gene, and genomes are annotated by different pipelines. In this study, we measured how these two factors change the counts of protease-inhibitor domain families. Results: Seven protease-inhibitor families were counted in eight animal genomes. Collapsing protein entries to genes reduced the counts in 36 of 48 species-family combinations, by up to 4.6-fold (Kunitz/BPTI in Aedes aegypti, 23 entries in 5 genes), and reversed the order of two species in 9 of 196 pairwise comparisons. In 218 of 223 gene-family records with several positive entries, all entries shared CDS coordinates with the representative entry. Two annotations of the same leech (Hirudinaria manillensis) assembly differed in a family-specific way. In the published annotation, 38 of 50 Antistasin-positive genes and both Hirudin-positive genes had no same-strand gene model in a second annotation, whereas most Kunitz/BPTI, Serpin, TIL and Thyroglobulin genes had one-to-one partners. A search of the eight assemblies without gene models detected all 338 annotated Kunitz/BPTI-positive genes when the queries included proteins of the same species. Queries from other species recovered only 31-83% of these genes, and Kunitz-like candidate regions outside the annotations were most numerous in the tick Ixodes scapularis. For the mosquito and the tick, the second public annotations shared nearly all gene-model coordinates with RefSeq and were therefore excluded from the comparison of annotation sources. Conclusions: These results indicate that gene family counts depend on the counting unit and on the annotation source. Comparisons across species should count each gene once and state how domain positivity was assigned to genes. In addition, the source and version of each annotation should be reported, the annotations should be checked against the genome assembly, and the overlap of gene models should be examined before two annotations are compared.

papers.title: Multi-Lab Testing of Early Preclinical Discoveries Identifies Promising Treatments
papers.abstract: A fundamental challenge in drug development is the frequent failure of early laboratory research to translate into clinical benefit. One promising solution is to confirm findings from exploratory single-laboratory studies across multiple laboratories before clinical testing. We investigated this approach following the conduct of preclinical multi-laboratory studies across different fields of medicine. For this, we evaluated effect sizes, experimental rigor, and a set of criteria to identify determinants of confirmation success. When tested under increased rigor, only a fraction of multi-laboratory studies confirmed the initial results. The underlying effect size reduction was associated with outcome-relevant experimental differences between exploratory and confirmatory stages. In summary, multi-laboratory studies proved highly informative and served as an effective filter for promising treatments.

papers.title: A Chemigenetic Fluorescence Lifetime Biosensor for Dopamine Sensing
papers.abstract: Measuring the precise dynamics of specific neuromodulators in neurons is key to understanding how information is transmitted and processed in the brain. Despite the growing use of intensity-based neurochemical sensors such as dLight in recent years, it remains challenging to monitor the dynamics of multiple neurochemicals simultaneously in live neurons. In contrast to intensiometric sensors that are susceptible to artifacts caused by changes in sensor expression and rapid photobleaching, fluorescence lifetime-based sensors are less affected by these factors and can provide more stable measurements. Here we introduce dHaloLife635, a chemigenetic fluorescence-lifetime-based dopamine (DA) sensor that exhibits a fluorescence lifetime decrease of 0.21 ns upon dopamine binding. dHaloLife635 consists of a G protein-coupled dopamine receptor (hDRD1), a circularly permuted HaloTag (cpHaloTag), and a HaloTag ligand-functionalized cell-permeable dye (JF635-HTL). Dopamine binding to dHaloLife635 induces a conformational change in the cpHaloTag that alters the local environment of the conjugated dye, thereby changing its fluorescence lifetime. In live HEK293T cells, dHaloLife635 responds to dopamine but not to serotonin, L-DOPA, or GABA, and only marginally to norepinephrine, with selectivity for dopamine over norepinephrine confirmed in primary neurons, demonstrating excellent specificity. Together, these results establish dHaloLife635 as an initial step toward a broader family of chemigenetic lifetime sensors that exhibit distinct fluorescence lifetime signatures upon binding their respective analytes, thereby potentially enabling highly specific and sensitive monitoring of multiple neurochemical dynamics in vivo over extended timescales.

papers.title: Ensemble viewing reshapes neural representations of same-race and other-race faces
papers.abstract: The other-race effect, better recognition of same-race than other-race faces, is established for individual faces. Whether this benefit is reflected in neural representations of face ensembles, as when viewing a crowd, remains unclear. We recorded electroencephalography responses from 22 East Asian adults viewing synthetic East Asian (same-race) and White (other-race) faces in two formats: individually and in six-face ensembles. Multivariate decoding and generative image reconstruction assessed neural discriminability, representational geometry and recoverable visual content. Behavioral testing confirmed a same-race recognition advantage. The corresponding neural decoding advantage depended on viewing format and was not preserved for race-homogeneous ensembles, although their constituents retained it when viewed individually. Early ensemble decoding instead favored other-race faces. Race organized ensemble representations and reconstructed latent vectors matched ensemble summary targets above chance. Independent judgments revealed format-dependent race differences in reconstructed age and arousal relative to model-derived references. These findings constrain accounts of same-race expertise: its benefit for neural discriminability depends on whether faces are represented individually or collectively. Recoverable ensemble-summary information can also coexist with systematic appearance shifts, linking the organization of neural representations to their visual content.

papers.title: Notch-independent Her6 contributes to control of neural stem cell maintenance by shifting Notch signaling from lateral inhibition towards lateral induction mode
papers.abstract: The growing brain faces the challenge to establish stable spatially defined neural proliferation zones that accomplish both neural stem cell (NSC) maintenance and dynamic neurogenesis. We investigated the relative impact of Notch signaling, Notch-dependent, and Notch-independent HES/Her transcription factors on target gene expression in the larval zebrafish brain. Both genetic evidence and transcriptional network analysis reveal a pivotal role of Her6, a Notch-independent HES1 homolog, in NSC control. Her6 at G1, and Notch signaling at G2, regulate distinct cell cycle control genes, favoring arrest. Her6 and Notch activity combined differentially control delta, jagged, lfng and notch3 expression to potentially shift Notch signaling mechanisms from Delta-driven lateral inhibition to Jagged-Notch3-mediated lateral induction. Indeed, we detect in situ spatial expression profiles consistent with lateral induction in high her6 expressing regions of the larval and adult brain. Her6-dependent lateral induction may spatially organize coherent populations of long-term NSCs in active proliferation zones.
