Their formation depends on non-canonical signaling in which the kinase JAK1 activates two required parallel pathways (via ERK1 and AKT1) that converge on the transcription factor c-Fos. Inhibiting JAK1, either parallel pathway or depleting c-Fos, prevents oncostatin M-induced loss of barrier function. These results identify a permeability mechanism distinct from the junction disassembly driven by the cytokines that have dominated this field and implicate kinases already targeted by approved drugs as potential points of intervention. More broadly, vascular barriers are transiently loosened during immune-cell trafficking and metastasis, raising the possibility that diverse forms of vascular permeability arise through regulated nanoscale remodeling rather than junctional breakdown.

papers.title: Genomic Potential vs. Pathogenic Reality: Functional Virulence Variation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
papers.abstract: Despite the rapid expansion of bacterial genome sequencing, predicting pathogen virulence from genomic information remains a major challenge. To study this association, we integrate comparative genomics, functional phenotyping, host-pathogen interaction assays, and infection outcomes across a diverse collection of 28 Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates, representing clinically relevant diversity in serotype, type IV pilus group, and flagellar type. While virulence-associated systems were broadly retained across the strain collection, isolates displayed substantial variation in phenotypic behavior and pathogenicity. Genotypic classifications based on pilus, flagellar, siderophore, or secretion system characteristics were poor predictors of virulence-associated phenotypes. Pathogenicity in a Galleria mellonella model varied markedly among strains and was most strongly associated with surface-associated motility, whereas other virulence traits and quorum-sensing genotypes showed limited predictive value. In a three-dimensional lung epithelial cell model, inflammatory responses were negatively correlated with activity of the type III secretion system effector ExoS, suggesting a role in modulation of host immune signaling. Together, these findings demonstrate that virulence emerges from functional deployment of conserved virulence repertoires, rather than their mere presence. By linking genomic diversity to phenotypic expression, pathogenicity, and host responses within a single strain collection, this study highlights fundamental limitations of gene-content-based virulence prediction and underscores the importance of integrating genomic and functional data to better understand P. aeruginosa virulence.

papers.title: Interpreting Graph Neural Networks for Antibacterial Drug Repurposing against Acinetobacter baumannii
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii, whose carbapenem-resistant strains are classified by the World Health Organization as a critical priority, has motivated machine-learning screens for new antibacterials, but translating predictions into chemical hypotheses requires evaluating the molecular features on which a model relies. A graph neural network ensemble achieves competitive predictive performance against a descriptor-augmented reference model on the same antibacterial screen while using only atom features and connectivity, allowing interpretation to focus on the molecular graph without a separate input of handcrafted descriptors. The atom-level explanations identify features supporting the model's activity predictions under perturbation and restoration, while comparisons with equally sized perturbations within each molecule distinguish piperazine as the most consistently supported recurring contributor to predicted activity. Prospective screening of the Drug Repurposing Hub followed by developability and safety assessment yields a ranked shortlist for experimental follow-up and leads to testing of CE3F4, which reduced A. baumannii growth by 57% at 0.25 mM in a preliminary assay with a non-monotonic concentration--response profile.

papers.title: Transcriptomic similarity guides source selection beyond tissue lineage
papers.abstract: Perturbational and pharmacogenomic maps remain incomplete across cellular contexts, leaving a practical source-selection question before response prediction: which measured context should inform an unmeasured target? We tested whether baseline transcriptomic similarity ranks candidate sources for held-out targets, separating source ranking from aggregation and transfer-uncertainty decisions. Similarity tracked matched-response concordance in LINCS and GSE306429; selected-source utility exceeded random expectation in GSE306429 ({Delta}U = 0.034; P = 0.002) and in exact-time-matched MIX-Seq tasks ({Delta}U = 0.046). In the full GDSC2 analysis, the drug-balanced ranking effect was 0.359 (95% CI, 0.337-0.383). In a lineage-restricted analysis of the same eligible subset, within-tissue ranking remained positive at 0.130 (95% CI, 0.119-0.141), retaining 35.8% of the same-subset global effect (0.363; 95% CI, 0.342-0.386). Global transcriptomic top-1 selection exceeded tissue-matched random selection by 0.154 (95% CI, 0.143-0.164). Thus, baseline similarity adds source-ranking information after tissue matching in the evaluated setting, while ranking alone does not resolve whether to aggregate sources or how to quantify transfer uncertainty.

papers.title: Retinal Phd2 ablation partially rescues Crb1Crb2-associated Leber congenital amaurosis and alters metabolic signaling
papers.abstract: Leber congenital amaurosis (LCA) is a severe early-onset retinal dystrophy caused by pathogenic variants in several genes, including CRB1. CRB1-associated LCA is characterized by disrupted retinal polarity, lamination, and photoreceptor organization, with no restorative treatment. We investigated whether retinal deletion of Phd2 (Egln1), encoding prolyl hydroxylase domain protein 2 (PHD2), could provide mutation-independent neuroprotection in a severe developmental model of CRB1-associated LCA. Using conditional Crb1/Crb2-deficient mice, we additionally deleted Phd2 throughout the neural retina and assessed retinal function, structure, visually guided behavior, and glycolysis-associated gene and protein expression at one and two months. Compared with Crb1/Crb2-deficient mice, additional Phd2 deletion partially improved scotopic responses and significantly increased the optomotor spatial-frequency threshold, whereas b-wave and cone-mediated responses remained impaired. Phd2Crb1Crb2-deficient retinas displayed more organized photoreceptor rosettes containing rod- and cone-marker-positive cells, in contrast to the diffuse outer-retinal disorganization and nuclear-layer amalgamation observed in Crb1/Crb2-deficient retinas. Polarity- and synapse-associated proteins showed improved local compartmentalization within these structures. Metabolic responses were temporally selective: Glut1 and Vegfa transcript levels increased at one month, whereas GLUT1 and LDHA protein levels increased at two months; Pdk1 transcript levels decreased at 2M, whereas PDK1 protein abundance remained unchanged. Although Phd2 deletion did not correct the underlying Crumbs-complex defect or normalize retinal lamination, and elevated Vegfa coincided with persistent vascular abnormalities, these findings demonstrate that retinal Phd2 deletion partially modifies the structural and functional consequences of severe Crb1/Crb2 deficiency and supports further investigation of PHD2-associated metabolic signaling as a potential disease-modifying target for severe CRB1-associated retinal degeneration.

papers.title: A computational investigation of pathways for ex vivo differentiation and dysfunction of healthy and patient T cells
papers.abstract: Adoptive T cell therapy is a promising field in cancer immunotherapy that leverages the natural ability of T cells to target and kill cancer cells. A crucial step in this therapy involves the ex vivo expansion of memory-like and effector-like T cells, but limiting their differentiation into exhaustion-associated phenotypes remains a challenge. Mathematical model-informed strategies to optimise T cell expansion may be able to exploit our understanding of T cell differentiation, but there is a large amount of uncertainty and disagreement in the biological literature regarding the ways in which T cells differentiate and become exhausted. We therefore conduct a large-scale mathematical investigation to help further our understanding of T cell differentiation during short-term ex vivo expansion. Using observations from biological literature, we first construct thousands of potential pathways connecting distinct T cell phenotypes and then formulate corresponding ordinary differential equations to test hypotheses regarding T cell differentiation and dysfunction. We fit each model to experimental data describing the ex vivo expansion of T cells originating from healthy individuals and cancer patients and accept those that most closely describe the data. From our findings, we hypothesise that cancer may alter T cell differentiation kinetics rather than the structure of the differentiation pathway, which has significant potential to inform therapeutic strategies. Our analysis proposes that T cells may not differentiate unidirectionally ex vivo; most accepted models suggest that the cells dynamically switch between functional phenotypes. We postulate that effector-like cells may be prone to upregulating inhibitory receptors that drive exhaustion, and find that modelling effector-like proliferation is unnecessary to capture observed population dynamics. Our hypothesis-testing framework generates recommendations for promising future research avenues and may pave the way to improve the production of patient-tailored T cell populations for adoptive cell therapy.

papers.title: L-DOPA Rescues Reach Height but Not Trajectory Area in a Bimanual String-Pulling Behavior in Parkinsonian Rats
papers.abstract: While gross motor changes in Parkinson's disease, bradykinesia, hypokinesia, difficulty initiating movement, have been well studied in rodent models of the disease, limb movements, and especially bimanual coordination deficits, are more difficult to study in these animal models. Here we describe a novel bimanual string-pulling task that can be used to generate a rich repertoire of behaviors that require limb and bimanual coordination in rats with unilateral 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA) lesion. We show that 6-OHDA lesion significantly reduces string speed, pulling bout duration, paw speed especially during reaching, and reduces the area of paw trajectories during pulling. However, it does not affect the variability around that movement trajectory. We also show that levodopa (L-DOPA) treatment restores many of these measures but not all. L-DOPA restores paw speed and string-pulling speed and fully restores paw reach height and pulling bout duration, but has no effect on trajectory area. Together, our results demonstrate that dopamine depletion differentially effects features of this bimanual coordination task, that L-DOPA mostly, but not fully, restores string pulling performance, and opens up a new avenue for measuring the effect of Parkinson's disease treatments on motor movement, allowing for better assessment of how effectively treatments restore motor activity.

papers.title: Adolescent Sugar-Induced Miswiring of Hippocampal Neurons Drives Adult Motivational Dysfunction in rats
papers.abstract: Adolescence, a critical period for hippocampal maturation, involves the integration of newly generated neurons into circuits underlying adult behavior. While adolescent, but not adult, sugar overconsumption triggers lasting motivational deficits, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that adolescent-born dentate gyrus granule neurons causally mediate adult reward-seeking behavior. Strikingly, sucrose overconsumption during adolescence abolishes this function, inducing selective remodeling of synaptic inputs and disrupting their functional integration.

papers.title: Spontaneous neural activity in the developing ant olfactory system
papers.abstract: Spontaneous neural activity is a pillar of mammalian neurodevelopment. In mammals, developing olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs) show spontaneous activity patterns that depend on the olfactory receptor (OR) they express. This activity is necessary for proper sorting of OSN axons into olfactory bulb glomeruli. This contrasts with the simpler olfactory system of the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster, where antennal lobe glomeruli form without functional ORs. Compared to Drosophila, ants have a vastly expanded olfactory system and, unlike Drosophila, require functional ORs for proper development. This raises the possibility that ants, like mammals, rely on spontaneous neural activity. To test whether developing ant OSNs are spontaneously active, we performed live calcium imaging in translucent pupae of the clonal raider ant Ooceraea biroi, using a transgenic line expressing the genetically encoded calcium indicator GCaMP6s in OSNs. Developing O. biroi OSNs exhibit spontaneous calcium transients from the earliest stages of glomerulus formation, and features of this activity change over the course of metamorphosis. During early stages, activity is faster, varies widely between cells, and is uncorrelated across the OSN population. By mid-metamorphosis, activity has slowed, with longer calcium events and fewer peaks per cell. As pupae approach eclosion, a new mode appears, with rhythmic, sawtooth-shaped calcium events that synchronously engage OSNs in both antennae. This stage-dependent spontaneous activity suggests that the expanded ant olfactory system may use a developmental logic more akin to mammals than to Drosophila.

papers.title: Phase Separation of Intracellular Proteins Influences Synaptic Bistability
papers.abstract: Synaptic bistability at the post synaptic density has been proposed to be the result of the nucleation and evaporation of receptor clusters. The exact biophysical mechanism underlying these inter-receptor attractions that can trigger nucleation remains to be elucidated. Emerging evidence demonstrates that numerous postsynaptic density submembrane proteins, that interact with various membrane receptors, can undergo phase separation, necessitating a revised conceptual model. By employing Langevin dynamics simulations of coarse-grained scaffold proteins and interacting membrane receptors, we study how phase transitions of scaffold proteins alter receptor clustering at the membrane. In our model, scaffold macromolecules can undergo phase separation and interact with receptor molecules at the model membranes. We observed that the presence of scaffold polymers across the membrane creates an attractive interaction between otherwise purely repulsive receptors. By systematically varying the number of receptors at the membrane, we dissected the coupling between receptor clustering and the phase behavior of scaffold macromolecules. We show that the propensity for receptor clustering is enhanced by the condensation of scaffold proteins. We then used two different scaffolds and systematically varied the interaction between them, to change the spatial organization of two condensed phases w.r.t. one another. Interestingly, we observed that receptor clustering can be reduced by co-phase separation of scaffold macromolecules, indicating the role of competing interactions in receptor clustering. Our work advances understanding of receptor-mediated signaling and phase separation, providing insights into cellular compartmentalization and biochemical regulation at the synapse.

papers.title: Brain state locks silent memories in a trained fly connectome
papers.abstract: Complete connectomes now exist for insect nervous systems, but whether a fixed wiring diagram can learn, and what its memories consist of, is unknown. Here, we trained a spiking model of the whole male Drosophila central nervous system, 167,106 neurons with fixed wiring, to plan moves and to remember a visual cue. Spikes write the cue into neuronal adaptation, which holds it silently until the next input reads it out. Cells that hold the trace are enriched for transcripts of a calcium-activated potassium channel in fly cell atlases. The learned readout recalls the trace only in the brain state of learning: the same trace evokes a different response at another delay, and a disease-like loss of potassium current rewrites the trace and changes how it is read. Learning in the new state is spared. Memory failure can arise from a change of state rather than a loss of storage.

papers.title: A Synthetic Virology Platform for Rapid Prototyping of Influenza A Virus mutants
papers.abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a significant public health threat, with the need for effective vaccines and antiviral therapies remaining a high priority. In vitro testing is paramount in studying novel IAV viruses and their immunogenicity. To address this need, we developed a synthetic virology approach to rapidly prototype and test IAV mutants with altered antigenic sites. By strategically inserting restriction sites within an ambisense plasmid, we generated a tool where we can seamlessly replace either 1) the full hemagglutinin (HA), 2) the HA globular head domain to generate head/stalk chimeras or 3) the five canonical antigenic sites. The cloning inserts can be computationally designed and artificially synthesized, enabling rescue of synthetic Influenza A viruses. Using this platform we rescued IAV H1N1, H3N2 & H5N1, and went on to prototype their respective antigenic site mutants & chimeric IAVs using viral genome sequence alone. This platform could be useful for generating vaccine seed strains or to study anti-viral immunity.

papers.title: A Synthetic Consensus Chiroptera IFN-β Induces IFN-I Signaling Across Diverse Bat Taxa
papers.abstract: Bat-associated viruses consistently spill over from bats into humans and other animals. Many bat-associated viruses, including Marburg virus and Nipah virus, cause severe disease in humans but their presentation is subclinical in bats. Advancements in tools and resources to study bat innate antiviral immune responses, including the type I IFN (IFN-I) pathway, are needed to evaluate the mechanisms that underlie differential infection outcomes between reservoir bats and spillover hosts. Commercially available IFN-Is are not bat-specific, and conspecific IFN-Is are impractical to produce for the over 1,500 described bat species. Here, we design and validate a bat order-level consensus IFN (Chiroptera IFN-{beta}) that is functional in bat cells from six diverse bat families, including representatives from both suborders. Using Jamaican fruit bat cells, we demonstrate that Chiroptera IFN-{beta} induces an IFN-stimulated gene repertoire comparable to conspecific IFN-{beta}. This valuable resource can accelerate the capacity of the field to study bat innate antiviral responses and illuminate differences between bats and humans.

papers.title: A mechanistic classification of GNAO1 mutations links Gβ γ sequestration to hyperkinetic disease and treatment response
papers.abstract: Go is the most prevalent G protein subunit in the brain and is critical for signal transduction through G protein-coupled receptors. Mutations in the gene encoding Go (GNAO1) cause a rare neurodevelopmental disorder with involuntary movements (NEDIM) and, in some patients, developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE). Here, we integrate human genetic analysis with cellular assays to define mechanistic classes of GNAO1 mutations and in vivo approaches to evaluate therapeutic strategies. We grouped variants into two functional categories: those predicted to sequester G{beta}{gamma} and those with reduced Go expression and therefore increased G{beta}{gamma} signaling. Analysis of patient data revealed that mutations predicted to impair G{beta}{gamma} release are significantly associated with NEDIM. Using the GNAO1R209H/+ mouse as a model of NEDIM, we evaluated two small molecules: caffeine, a nonselective adenosine receptor antagonist, and gallein, a selective modulator of G{beta}{gamma}-effector interactions. Both compounds significantly reduced hyperlocomotion in the open field test. Whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology revealed sex- and cell type-specific hyperexcitability in spiny projection neurons within the dorsolateral striatum of GNAO1R209H/+ mice. Together, these findings implicate dysfunction of dorsolateral striatal pathways in GNAO1-related disorder and suggest that mechanistic understanding of disease variants can guide targeted therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Rugnux: from diffraction images to structure at synchrotrons and XFELs in one program
papers.abstract: Rising data rates in macromolecular crystallography outpace multi-program pipelines on computing clusters. Rugnux, a single GPU-accelerated program, turns rotation or serial still diffraction images into merged data and an initial structure. At synchrotrons, results arrive seconds after the last image; on one workstation, 207 public datasets from 36 sources took a median of 15 s each, with deposition-quality. Serial XFEL data were processed faster than the collection rate, enabling real-time structure determination.

papers.title: Cancers relax selection on charge at the mitochondrial complex I quinone cavity
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial complex I translocates protons through hydrated channels whose connectivity and electrostatics are both defined by structure, but whether they are distinctly constrained is unknown. From a 2.39 cryo-EM structure modelling 2,945 ordered waters, we built the proton wire of the seven mtDNA-encoded ND subunits and scored all 40,166 missense substitutions on two near-orthogonal axes (r = 0.17): electrostatic shift at proton-loading sites, and topological disruption of the wire. Across 858 germline variant sites, loading sites (0.51) and cut vertices (0.67) are both depleted. In tumours only loading sites are enriched (1.42 TCGA, 1.67 PCAWG, 1.29 MSK-IMPACT), a 3.06-fold difference tested as a wire class tissue-type interaction (P = 3.6 10-). It survives adjustment for conservation, burial and coverage, and is concentrated in ND1 within 15 of the quinone cavity, not spread along the proton path. Selection separates charge from connectivity, without establishing a fitness benefit.

papers.title: Preclinical Development and Safety of Laterally Spreading Dual AAV.SPR-MYO7A Vectors for the Treatment of Usher Syndrome Type 1B
papers.abstract: Usher syndrome type 1B (USH1B), caused by mutations in MYO7A, is the most severe form of Usher syndrome and accounts for more than 50% of USH1 cases. Affected patients are born profoundly deaf with vestibular dysfunction and develop progressive retinitis pigmentosa, for which no approved treatment exists. The MYO7A coding sequence exceeds the packaging capacity of adeno-associated virus (AAV), the gold standard vector for retinal gene therapy. To overcome this, we developed dual AAV hybrid and overlap platforms to reconstitute full-length MYO7A expression in photoreceptors and retinal pigment epithelium. Modification of cDNA split points, and reduction of non-coding sequence yielded optimized vector pairs that produced higher full-length MYO7A levels with substantially reduced truncated protein. Packaging in the laterally spreading AAV.SPR capsid enabled supraphysiological MYO7A expression in cynomolgus macaques at macular and distal retinal sites without requiring foveal detachment, an important safety consideration for USH1B patients with remaining central vision. A six-month GLP toxicology study confirmed that ATSN-301, an AAV.SPR-based dual vector reconstituting MYO7A driven by the smCBA promoter, was well tolerated at all doses, with a No Observed Adverse Effect Level established at 1.2E11 vg/eye, supporting its clinical advancement for USH1B.

papers.title: Executive and language systems competitively shape predictive processing during reading
papers.abstract: When we read, our brains constantly generate predictions about upcoming words, which is thought to make comprehension faster and more efficient. Yet it remains unclear whether this predictive mechanism relies on the same domain-general executive resources the brain uses for other demanding cognitive tasks, or operates largely independently within the language system. Here we tested this question using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) in twenty-five healthy adults, who performed self-paced naturalistic reading, an n-back task, and a dual task of concurrent reading and n-back, allowing us to place competing demands on cognitive resources. In three sessions, we stimulated the left angular gyrus alone, the angular gyrus together with dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, a hub of executive control, or delivered sham stimulation, and used computational modeling of decision-making to isolate how each brain state altered the underlying cognitive processes. Combined stimulation of the angular gyrus and prefrontal cortex selectively weakened the reading-time costs of unexpected words, but only when reading competed with the working-memory task, revealing that linguistic prediction draws on executive resources specifically under cognitive load. Computational models showed that the relationship was bidirectional: Unpredictable words also disrupted concurrent working-memory decisions, slowing the accumulation of evidence and increasing response caution. Together, these findings show that predictive language processing is not a fixed, encapsulated function but is dynamically coupled to executive control when cognitive demands compete. Our results provide evidence that prediction during language comprehension is embedded within a broader, demand-sensitive cognitive architecture that flexibly coordinates linguistic and executive resources.

papers.title: Iron sensing modules participate in rhizospheric pH perception in rice
papers.abstract: Rhizospheric pH has emerged as one of the most important environmental factors regulating plant fitness in almost every aspect of plant physiology and development. Interestingly, the information on how plant perceive rhizospheric pH is still not well understood. In this report we have elucidated the intricate mechanism where rhizospheric pH mediated changes in relative Fe availability are sensed by the plants to initiate complex physiological responses. Using root specific RNA-seq, ICPMS, hormone quantification and physiological validation in rice, the study revealed Fe availability to be a critical determinant of rhizospheric pH where the relative Fe toxicity towards acidic pH and Fe deficiency towards alkaline pH is deduced by the plant in the form of JA-auxin crosstalk regulating the physiological responses against rhizospheric pH.

papers.title: AN INTEGRATED HEART-ON-A-CHIP NAM RESOLVES DISTINCT CLINICAL PHENOTYPES OF MYOCARDIAL ISCHEMIA-REPERFUSION INJURY
papers.abstract: Background: Reperfusion is required for myocardial salvage yet itself injures the heart, and cardioprotective interventions that reduce infarct size experimentally have repeatedly failed to improve outcomes in patients. These interventions are evaluated against viability or infarct size alone, whereas ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury produces structural, biochemical, and contractile dysfunction in the same tissue. No in vitro new approach methodology (NAM), however, resolves all three within one system. Methods: A NAM was created within a heart-on-a-chip platform, which was constructed by culturing neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs) on muscular thin films. Cardiomyocytes were subjected to normoxia, 2 hours of ischemia, and ischemia followed by 2 hours of reperfusion. Sarcomeric architecture was quantified by immunofluorescence, cardiomyocyte injury by LIVE/DEAD staining and cardiac troponin I release into conditioned media, while contractile stress and spontaneous beat frequency were recorded on the same films before and after each condition. Results: Under ischemia, z-line density decreased while architectural metrics were preserved, indicating cell loss rather than sarcomere disorganization. Furthermore, viability decreased, troponin elevated, and every contractile stress component declined, while spontaneous beat frequency was unchanged. Reperfusion fractured this uniform depression. Cell death and troponin release increased further, yet structure was unchanged from ischemia, so every functional change occurred on a depleted but architecturally intact cardiomyocyte population. Systolic stress recovered partially, whereas diastolic stress exceeded baseline, leaving active stress suppressed despite oxygen recovery. Beat frequency increased with pronounced variability. Conclusions: This heart-on-a-chip NAM resolved structural, biochemical, and contractile injury that global indices conflate, distinguishing ischemic from reperfusion pathophysiology. Interestingly, individual readouts corresponded to distinct clinical syndromes of ischemic injury, positioning this platform for future testing of cardioprotective candidates against the full injury phenotype.

papers.title: Arena3D 3.0: a web server for exploring, analyzing, annotating and sharing multilayered networks in 3D
papers.abstract: Multilayer networks describe biological entities linked by several kinds of relation or measured under several conditions. Arena3D 3.0, a complete reimplementation of Arena3Dweb, gives each layer its own place in an interactive 3D scene. Networks are uploaded or imported from STRING, IntAct, OmniPath, NDEx, Reactome and the Gene Ontology. Twelve layouts, seven in 3D, are available, and node copies can be aligned across layers. Layers are drawn as floors or 3D containers in thirteen arrangements, including 3D hive plots. Communities and annotated groups can be laid out apart and outlined as hulls or fog clouds, and edges can be bundled. Analyses cover node and multilayer metrics, distributions and perturbation, with chord, Sankey, heatmap, UpSet and UMAP views. Networks go to Cytoscape, Gephi Lite, NORMA and JBrowse 2, gene lists to Flame, and a REST API gives programmatic access. Arena3D 3.0 is free at www.arena3d.org without login.

papers.title: Individualized brain-body signatures of positive emotions revealed by large-scale multimodal neurophysiological recording
papers.abstract: Using one of the most comprehensive multimodal biosensing datasets in affective research, densely sampled within individuals, we asked how emotions are instantiated in each person's brain and body. Four participants viewed 168 emotion-evoking videos during 128-channel EEG and 28 autonomic, ocular and facial recordings. Cross-validated elastic-net classifiers distinguished each of 15 positive and neutral emotions from baseline in every participant (mean accuracy 87-97%). We found that no emotion was predicted by a single marker and each reflected a multimodal ensemble of cortical and autonomic activity whose composition was largely person-specific. Yet physiology-derived groupings converged selectively with self-report; Interest-Awe-Amusement-Satisfaction and Entrancement-Aesthetic Appreciation recurred across individuals based on physiology. Across emotion groups, frontal and posterior delta, posterior alpha and electrodermal activity formed a shared backbone, plausibly reflecting affective and sensory engagement, whereas cardiovascular and facial signals varied between people. This framework yields individualized, objective neurophysiological indicators of emotion, potentially aiding personalized diagnosis.

papers.title: Co-transcriptomic network analysis of host-parasite interactions reveals genes underpinning parasite fitness
papers.abstract: Interactions between parasites and their host organisms generate continuous variation in infection outcomes. Although dual transcriptome studies have demonstrated extensive molecular dialogues between interacting species, it is still unclear how natural variation in host and parasite gene regulatory networks and coordination between them contribute to diverse disease phenotypes. Here, we re-contextualized co-transcriptomes from recombinant inbred lines of the plant-parasitic root-knot nematode Meloidogyne hapla infecting Medicago truncatula host plants with relative measures of infection intensity as a proxy for parasite load. We used infection intensity to estimate interaction gradients on gene expression by calculating its covariance with transcript levels. Quantitative analyses of interaction gradients for host and parasite transcriptomes identified major differences in development-related transcriptional programs along the infection continuum. In addition, integrated network analyses connected host cell wall remodeling with parasite protein production and secretion. Silencing of candidate root-knot nematode genes reduced host galling and parasite reproductive fitness, providing experimental support for our network-derived predictions. Together, our findings present an integrated systems genetics framework connecting naturally occurring genetic variation to quantitative disease phenotypes.

papers.title: Multi-resolution humanness scoring of antibodies via a region-isolated language model
papers.abstract: Antibodies recognized as foreign can elicit anti-drug antibodies that compromise efficacy and safety, making humanness scoring, estimating how human-like a sequence appears, an early, repeated step in antibody development. Widely used scores reduce a variable domain to a single framework-dominated number, leaving the complementarity-determining regions (CDRs) grafted during humanization, diversified by generative models weakly supervised and rarely audited. Here we introduce IgScope, a 23-million-parameter antibody language model trained from scratch that scores humanness at chain, IMGT-region, and residue resolution; a region-isolated attention module confines attention to within-region pairs, and chimeric-sequence training supplies region-level supervision. On 2.38 million held-out chains, masking all framework tokens leaves CDR accuracy unchanged, and back-mutated murine residues in human frameworks are detected at 93.4% accuracy. At chain level, IgScope matches the strongest published correlation with clinical anti-drug-antibody incidence (r = 0.567, n = 217) and outperforms a same-protocol recomputation. Region-level scoring exposes what chain-level scoring conceals: antibodies designed de novo by four generative models pass whole-chain humanness (0.966-0.988), while their CDRs score far below natural (P < 1e-30) in every chain class. Quality control turns the same resolution to the mirror-image question: in humanized-mouse platforms, whose domains are human by design, IgScope scores the domain as human and, in HUGO-Nano chimeric VHHs, isolates only the FR2 signal of four camelid hallmark residues deliberately retained to stabilize the VHH. IgScope gives antibody humanization a verified foundation and generative design an audit.

papers.title: IG-28 enables identification and quantification of high-confidence isoforms from large bulk and single-cell full-length cDNA datasets
papers.abstract: The technology to sequence full-length transcriptomes from bulk and single-cell samples has rapidly advanced. As a result, full-length cDNA datasets now reach billions of reads in size which is beyond the capability of most established isoform identification tools. Here, we introduce IG-28 which addresses this challenge with its capability to process and analyze large fl-cDNA datasets fast and using minimal computational resources. In contrast to its predecessor Mandalorion, IG-28 is not limited to bulk fl-cDNA but is capable of parsing, processing, and analyzing single-cell fl-cDNA datasets. It does so in a lightweight, flexible manner, integrating seamlessly with established scRNA-seq analysis workflows. We benchmarked IG-28 against a variety of established and new isoform identification tools using several bulk and a complex single-cell fl-cDNA dataset and found that IG-28 consistently outperformed the other tools by identifying high-confidence public isoforms.

papers.title: Metabolic and transcriptional responses reveal co-option of symbiotic processes during early soybean-soybean cyst nematode interaction
papers.abstract: The biochemical mechanisms by which virulent populations of soybean cyst nematode (Heterodera glycines, SCN) overcome host resistance are critical to understanding this economically important pathogen. Here, we deployed metabolic and transcriptome profiling of soybean roots during the SCN infection and establishment process to investigate the molecular and biochemical mechanisms of pathogen establishment. Across samples from a time series spanning nematode invasion to syncytium maturation, we demonstrate that compatible SCN infection does not bypass host immunity but systematically remodels it. In a compatible interaction between soybean carrying the high-copy Rhg1 resistance locus challenged with HG Type 2.5.7 SCN virulent on this host, we identify a 72-metabolite defense signature spanning isoflavonoids, triterpenoid saponins, and phenylpropanoids that persist across all infection stages. Despite activation of this metabolic defense signature by the pathogen on infection, defense transcription is near silence by 3 days post-infection, while defense metabolites persist, revealing a critical decoupling of transcriptional and metabolic defense programs at the precise window of syncytium initiation. Suppression of phenylpropanoid accumulation occurs downstream of PAL transcription, indicating a block at the metabolic level invisible to transcriptomics alone. By 5 days post-infection, cytokinin accumulation coincides with nodulin gene induction and phospholipid remodeling consistent with activation of the legume symbiosis program during syncytium maturation. Together, these findings establish that compatibility arises not from failed recognition but from progressive immune dismantling, including suppression of defense chemistry and co-option of the legume-rhizobium symbiosis machinery.

papers.title: A comprehensive identification protocol for postcranial bones of Southeast Asian Ruminantia. Part 3: Morphological criteria for large-sized species
papers.abstract: Postcranial remains of large-bodied ruminants are abundant in the Late Quaternary record of continental Southeast Asia, yet their taxonomic attribution remains one of the least resolved problems in the zooarchaeology of this biodiversity-rich region. We address it here with an osteological identification protocol covering the six large ruminant species of the mainland: Bubalus bubalis, Bos javanicus, Bos sauveli, Bos gaurus, Budorcas taxicolor and Rusa unicolor, built from a comparative sample of 109 skeletons. A total of 148 discrete characters over 27 skeletal elements representing 442 states were defined on a restricted set of individuals, then scored across the entire sample. Most proved remarkably stable within taxa with 80.0% of the character/taxon combinations showing a dominant state at a frequency above 95%, and a substantial number of states occurred in a single family, subfamily, genus or species. Character combinations for taxonomic identification were then evaluated by the use of two supervised machine learning methods, a random forest model and a naive Bayes classifier at each of four taxonomic ranks. The two behaved almost identically, with mean accuracies of 95-94% for families, 93% for subfamilies, 89% for genera and 76% for species; only the three closely related and unevenly sampled species of Bos resisted consistent separation. The weighted naive Bayes models are distributed as a standalone web application in which any combination of states observed on a single element returns attribution probabilities for every rank. Together these results offer a transparent and statistically explicit alternative to expert judgement for the identification of Late Quaternary postcranial mammal remains, in Southeast Asia and elsewhere.

papers.title: A comprehensive identification protocol for postcranial bones of Southeast Asian Ruminantia. Part 2: Morphological criteria for small and medium-sized species
papers.abstract: The taxonomic identification of postcranial elements from small and medium-sized ruminants represents a significant challenge in zooarchaeological and Late Quaternary paleontological studies, particularly in biodiversity-rich regions such as continental Southeast Asia. This study presents a comprehensive osteological reference framework for the small and medium-sized Ruminantia of this region, based on a comparative sample of 228 specimens representing 14 species across three families (Bovidae, Cervidae, and Moschidae). Osteological characters were first described on a small initial specimen set and subsequently scored across the full sample. Although a small number of character states were found to be unique to specific taxa, most proved highly variable, limiting their individual identification potential. To address this, a Random Forest and a Naive Bayes classifier were applied to assess the discriminatory power of character combinations across four taxonomic ranks (Family, Subfamily, Genus, and Species) on independent bones. Both approaches performed similarly, achieving mean identification accuracies of 87-86% at the family level, 69% at the subfamily level, 50% at the genus level, and 35-33% at the species level. The Naive Bayes models were further deployed as an interactive web application, allowing users to perform bone identification based on any combination of observable character states from a single anatomical element. Our results highlight the limits of morphological identification of postcranial elements in this taxonomic and biogeographic context, while demonstrating that a transparent, reproducible, and statistically grounded approach can still represent a significant step forward for zooarchaeological and Late Quaternary paleontological studies in Southeast Asia and beyond.

papers.title: Auditory tracking magnitude, temporal alignment, and anatomical distribution during wakefulness and propofol-based anesthesia
papers.abstract: General anesthesia attenuates auditory responses, but response magnitude alone does not describe how residual activity aligns with sound over time or varies across the brain. We jointly characterized these aspects of auditory tracking using stereoelectroencephalography (sEEG) in 13 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy during wakefulness and clinically defined unresponsiveness under propofol-based anesthesia. The same rhythmic humming sequences were presented at approximately 1.61 Hz in both sessions. During anesthesia, stimulus-rate power showed widespread reductions and phase alignment with the stimulus rhythm was less consistent, although responses remained detectable at some recording channels. During wakefulness, response strength decreased with cortical surface distance from posteromedial Heschl's gyrus; this distance-response relationship was weaker during anesthesia. In a contrastive learning analysis (CEBRA), low-dimensional embeddings derived from anesthesia recordings yielded lower acoustic-envelope decoding accuracy on held-out data and lower consistency across model fits. Together, these findings characterize how attenuated auditory tracking is expressed jointly in response magnitude, temporal alignment, and anatomical distribution.

papers.title: CellMethMarker provides an integrated database of human cell- and tissue-type-specific DNA methylation markers
papers.abstract: Cell- and tissue-type-specific DNA methylation markers provide epigenetic signatures of cellular identity and are widely used to infer cellular origin from bulk and single-cell methylomes. Existing resources mainly emphasize disease-associated biomarkers, methylome atlases, genomic annotations or RNA-based cell markers, leaving an unmet need for an integrated region-level resource dedicated to such markers. Here we present CellMethMarker (http://gu-zhanglab.hfcas.ac.cn/CellMethMarker), a curated database integrating 347,514 de novo markers derived from uniformly processed whole-genome and reduced-representation bisulfite sequencing datasets, 2,203,507 literature-derived marker records and harmonized metadata for 2,810 samples. CellMethMarker enables cell- and tissue-centered marker retrieval, coordinate-based search, genome-browser visualization, interactive methylation analysis and data download. In an independent single-cell methylome atlas, these markers recover the expected cell-type-associated methylation patterns, and a platform-matched reference built from them lowers the mean deconvolution error from 0.365 to 0.144. CellMethMarker therefore links region-level DNA methylation variation to cellular identity and supports methylome-based cell-type annotation and deconvolution.

papers.title: A preclinical platform for focused ultrasound delivery from microplate to awake brain
papers.abstract: Background. Focused ultrasound (FUS) has broad therapeutic potential, but its mechanisms of action are poorly understood. Preclinical FUS research enables rigorous interrogation of understudied parameters, but fragmented, single-purpose benchtop devices prevent standardized acoustic exposure across models. Objective. To describe a unified preclinical FUS platform for cell culture, ex vivo tissue, and awake stereotaxic in vivo delivery in one lightweight system, validated using glioblastoma as a disease model. Methods. We performed single-well FUS delivery to 96-well microplates, single-well delivery to freshly resected human glioblastoma tissue, and stereotaxic transcranial delivery to awake, head-fixed mice ambulating freely on a floating cage. Output was independently calibrated in free field, with measured microplate insertion loss. Pulsed low-intensity focused ultrasound (pLIFU) was applied to GL261-bearing mice, resected human glioblastoma, and macrophage cell lines. Results. Awake stereotaxic pLIFU produced acute tumor signal attenuation in GL261-bearing mice (mean log2 fold-change -1.66 versus +5.20 controls, p = 0.016) with bioluminescence evidence consistent with focal targeting. Ex vivo pLIFU produced directionally consistent immunophenotypic shifts in human glioblastoma (increased iNOS+, decreased Arg1+ populations). In vitro, pLIFU reduced CD80 on immunosuppressive macrophages to 73% of baseline in RAW 264.7 cells (p = 0.0008, n = 5) and 64% in THP-1 cells (p = 0.0006, n = 2), with MHC II upregulation in RAW 264.7 (ratio 1.65, p = 0.004) and ARG1 reduction in THP-1 (ratio 0.52, p = 0.0025). Conclusions. A unified preclinical FUS platform validated across in vitro, ex vivo, and awake in vivo applications enables stereotaxically guided transcranial FUS in awake, head-fixed mice ambulating in an exploratory manner during sonication, and single-well microplate treatments.

papers.title: Revealing multiscale architecture of the intact human spine using hierarchical phase contrast tomography
papers.abstract: Background: Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provide detailed clinical assessment of the human spine; however, their millimeter-scale spatial resolution limits direct visualization of tissue microarchitecture and interfaces. Hierarchical phase-contrast tomography (HiP-CT) enables ex vivo non-destructive, micron-resolution imaging of intact human organs without exogenous contrast agents, extending anatomical assessment to spatial scales inaccessible to conventional clinical imaging. Purpose: To evaluate the capability of HiP-CT to visualize macro- to microanatomy of an intact adult human spine ex vivo. Methods: An intact spine (C1-L5) from a 62-year-old male donor without known skeletal disease was formalin-fixed and imaged by HiP-CT at the European Synchrotron. Whole-spine imaging was performed at 16.26 m isotropic voxels, with selected regions of interest imaged using 2.2 m voxels. Ex vivo MRI using clinical sequences was performed for anatomical comparison. Three-dimensional segmentation and quantitative analyses included intervertebral disc (IVD) grading, annulus fibrosus fiber tracing, and vertebral trabecular micro-morphometry. Results: HiP-CT enabled high spatial-resolution, multiscale imaging of the intact human spine, simultaneously visualizing vertebral bone and endplate, IVDs, spinal cord and meninges, nerve roots and ganglia, vasculature, ligaments, and musculature. Three-dimensional segmentation and virtual sectioning mapped neurovascular anatomy and vertebral vascular supply, without exogenous contrast enhancement, while preserving their relationships with surrounding tissues. Whole-spine images enabled quantitative analysis of annulus fibrosus fiber organization and vertebral trabecular microarchitecture, permitting the detection of focal posterolateral fiber disruption at the L4-L5 IVD and regional differences in trabecular architecture between cervical and lumbar vertebral bodies. Local tomography resolved annulus fibrosus lamellae, vertebral endplate Haversian systems, and facet joint hyaline cartilage at micron resolution. Conclusions: HiP-CT enables non-destructive, multiscale three-dimensional imaging of the intact human spine while preserving tissue relationships across spatial scales and hard-soft tissue boundaries. HiP-CT could provide an ex vivo microanatomical reference for future correlation with clinical imaging investigations of spinal disease and in the development and validation of imaging biomarkers.

papers.title: Integrating stool chemistry measurements with metagenomics in adults reveals distinct gut health profiles
papers.abstract: Stool chemistry metrics, including calprotectin, lactoferrin, and secretory IgA, are used to assess gut inflammation in clinical or research settings. However, these measures in isolation provide a limited view of gut physiology and lack microbial context. Shotgun metagenomics offers a comprehensive assessment of the gut microbiome's taxonomic composition and functional potential, yet its integration with stool chemistry metrics remains underexplored. We analyzed 877 adult stool samples with paired shotgun metagenomic sequencing and chemistry measurements to integrate the microbiome with 12 stool chemistry metrics. Calprotectin, lactoferrin, and secretory IgA were associated with shifts in microbiome composition (beta diversity), while deviations from typical levels of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), including butyrate, were associated with both changes in alpha diversity and microbiome composition. Network analysis revealed two distinct microbial neighborhoods: one associated with higher butyrate and lower calprotectin and lactoferrin and another associated with lower butyrate and higher calprotectin and lactoferrin. Machine learning models trained on taxonomic and functional data showed modest discrimination of stool chemistry states, performing best for SCFA deficiency and less well for host-derived inflammatory metrics. Together, these findings systematically characterize microbiome-stool chemistry relationships across a large paired dataset, providing a framework for interpreting stool chemistry metrics in the context of shotgun metagenomic profiles.

papers.title: Stop guessing thinning distances: a data-driven framework for spatial thinning parametrization for ecological modelling
papers.abstract: Spatially heterogeneous sampling and uneven publication effort in biodiversity repositories limit ecological niche characterization and habitat suitability modelling, affecting downstream inferences at regional and global scales. Spatial thinning offers a widely used strategy to mitigate these biases due to its simplicity and scalability. However, researchers typically select thinning parameters using heuristic or arbitrary criteria, often independent of species-specific characteristics, which introduces an additional, largely unquantified source of potential error. Here, we propose a data-driven framework for spatial thinning parameterization that replaces heuristic decision-making with principled, reproducible criteria. We define optimality as the stability of thermal niche estimates derived from empirical data, rather than as an agreement with a known true distribution. The framework integrates two complementary approaches. The Last Stable Thinning Parameterization (LS-TP) identifies the largest thinning intensity that preserves the stability of species-specific niche descriptors. Biogeographic-size Dependent Thinning Parameterization (BD-TP) links thinning intensity to species' geographic range size and scales spatial filtering across taxa with different distributional properties. Using seagrasses as a model system, we evaluated the framework across a global compilation of more than 100,000 occurrence records. Our results showed that optimal thinning parameters varied systematically with species range size and that uniform thinning approaches led to either excessive information loss or reduction of spatial clustering. Furthermore, the framework identified species for which available data did not support stable niche characterization, as these species failed to meet stability criteria even at the smallest thinning parameters. We recommend explicitly acknowledging this limitation in future studies and prioritizing increased sampling effort for such undersampled taxa. Our approaches provide a first step toward explicit, data-driven spatial thinning parameterization, with direct implications for ecological niche modelling, biodiversity assessment, and climate-driven distribution analyses.

papers.title: Human infection with an ape Plasmodium vivax-like parasite
papers.abstract: An unusually divergent Plasmodium vivax parasite was reported in a Swedish patient with recent travel. Using whole-genome sequencing, we show that the infection was caused by a strain of ape P. vivax-like, providing evidence of the zoonotic potential of these parasites that infect wild gorillas and chimpanzees in central Africa.

papers.title: Multimodal epi-mode 3D quantitative phase and fluorescence microscopy enables supervised volumetric virtual fluorescence in bulk tissue
papers.abstract: We introduce a multimodal microscope that combines quantitative oblique back-illumination microscopy (qOBM) with wide-field epi-fluorescence deconvolution microscopy to acquire intrinsically co-registered phase and fluorescence volumes of fresh, bulk tissue. Using paired qOBM phase and DAPI fluorescence images of fresh ex vivo mouse brain tissue, we train a supervised conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) to predict DAPI-like nuclear contrast from the structural information encoded in the phase images. Results not only demonstrate high-fidelity image translation but also show improved imaging depth and more homogeneous staining. Additionally, we combine the qOBM phase contrast with captured or virtual fluorescence nuclear images to produce volumetric pseudo-H&E representations of fresh tissue, enabling a supervised approach for achieving robust virtual histological staining. This work paves the way for virtual fluorescence imaging of many more structural targets and supervised virtual histological staining of thick, unaltered, bulk tissues ex vivo and potentially in vivo. Such capabilities could have significant implications for biological research as well as for point-of-care, intraoperative, and other clinical applications.

papers.title: Structures of MyD88 and its oncogenic mutant reveal DNA binding with implications for cytosolic DNA sensing
papers.abstract: MyD88 is a universal adaptor that connects to Toll-like receptors and interleukin-1 receptors through its Toll/IL-1R homology (TIR) domain and activates inflammatory signaling via its death domain (DD). However, how MyD88TIR serves as the platform for these functions and if it has additional functions remain unclear. Here, we report cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of MyD88TIR and its cancer-specific mutant L252P (previously L265P) mainly in ring and spiral forms, respectively. Both assemblies are formed by antiparallel double-filaments, using canonical TIR interfaces within each strand but unique surfaces between the strands, and position MyD88DD at the same sides of the assemblies for self-oligomerization and pathway activation. Surprisingly, these WT or L252P filaments are bound to dsDNA using the concave sides of the rings and the spirals. In vitro assays and cellular studies establish that MyD88 directly binds dsDNA and promotes inflammatory cytokine expression, particularly pro-IL-1{beta}, following dsDNA transfection or viral infection. Notably, these responses are unaffected by deficiency of UNC93B1, the essential chaperone required for trafficking endosomal nucleic acid-sensing TLRs. Structure-guide MyD88 mutant that disrupts dsDNA binding specifically compromises dsDNA-induced transcriptional program while maintaining TLR signaling. RNA-seq further reveals that MyD88 plays a crucial role in inducing gene expression upon dsDNA sensing and that about half of cGAS-dependent genes are also MyD88-dependent. Together, our structural, biochemical and genetic data support the findings that MyD88 directly engages with cytosolic dsDNA and cooperates with cGAS to promote the full innate immune transcriptional response.

papers.title: Interpreting Short Tandem Repeat Variations with Genomic Foundation Models in Olive
papers.abstract: Short tandem repeats (STRs) are highly mutable, multiallelic variants with distinctive mutation dynamics and have been associated with phenotypic variation across diverse species. However, genome-wide STR variation remains poorly characterized in olive, and the large number of naturally occurring alleles creates a challenge for variant interpretation. Genomic language models offer a potential way to assess how STR length changes alter learned sequence representations, but their responses to natural multiallelic STR series have not been systematically evaluated. Here, we identified 117,119 polymorphic STRs across 212 Iranian and Mediterranean olive accessions. STRs recovered the major SNP-defined ancestry axes while resolving additional geographically structured subcomponents. We then quantified STR-induced embedding perturbation using three plant genomic language models: AgroNT, PlantCAD2, and GPN. Across all three models, embedding distance generally increased with repeat-length difference from the reference allele, and 7,417 loci were embedding-sensitive in all three models. These signals were robust to fixed-length input construction and exceeded those of matched nonrepetitive indels at most tested loci. Integration with oil-composition associations prioritized four exploratory loci supported by all three models. Overall, we provide a genome-wide olive STR resource and show that plant genomic language models capture reproducible responses to natural STR length variation. Combining cross-model embedding evidence with phenotype association provides a potential framework for prioritizing candidate STRs for further investigation.

papers.title: GBactPro: cross-species bacterial promoter prediction using element-resolved promoter definitions
papers.abstract: Accurate bacterial promoter prediction supports genome annotation, but many models use fixed-length promoter windows anchored to transcription start sites (TSSs) rather than promoter-element boundaries. We developed the General Bacterial Promoter Predictor (GBactPro), a convolutional neural network-bidirectional long short-term memory (CNN-BiLSTM) framework using promoter sequences resolved by the Promoter Architecture Scanner. Using Escherichia coli-trained models evaluated across 43 bacterial species, we compared eight input designs and identified the contiguous -35/spacer/-10 core as optimal (mean AUROC = 0.9859). Species-specific models showed broad transfer in a 43 x 43 evaluation. Joint training on all 43 species achieved a mean AUROC of 0.9943 across their held-out test sets and outperformed four established predictors under matched-length benchmarks. In genome-wide E. coli scanning, GBactPro achieved AUROC and AUPRC values of 0.979 and 0.160 under stringent full-containment matching (0-bp tolerance), increasing to 0.997 and 0.323 under a 100-bp tolerance. False-positive predictions overlapped H-NS binding regions more frequently than true positives (24.4% versus 18.8%), and predictions also overlapped promoters derepressed in an H-NS-knockout dataset. Prediction precision varied across four TSS classes. These findings demonstrate that element-resolved promoter definitions improve cross-species prediction and support genome-wide identification of candidate bacterial promoters.

papers.title: Genomic signals of local adaptation in UK black alder populations (Alnus glutinosa)
papers.abstract: Black alder (Alnus glutinosa) is a native tree species in the British Isles, which it colonised after the last glaciation from continental refugia. It is now a widespread pioneer species, thriving on wetlands and riverbanks. We present whole genome sequence data for 324 alder seedlings grown from seed collected from 44 populations across the UK. Among these we found two triploids and one sample with trisomy at chromosome five. Removing these, we found little population genetic structure apart from diverging northern populations with lower diversity. Using Latent-Factor Mixed Models (LFMM) analyses we identified 1,364 loci whose allele frequencies were significantly associated with environmental variables. Of these loci, 93% were associated with the number of snow days. In contrast, the greatest total genomic signal (variance in SNP effect sizes of 7.38 million SNP loci) was observed for mean temperature of the wettest quarter and annual number of frost days. Estimates of maladaptation using 1.49 million SNPs, predicted that northern populations are worst adapted to present and future worst-case climates. Our results suggest that similarity of source-site temperature variables should be prioritised when choosing seed sources for new planting, and northern populations could benefit from assisted gene flow from the south.

papers.title: Cardiac unloading via a transvalvular pump prevents arrhythmias following myocardial ischemia / reperfusion by preserving coronary microcirculation and cardiomyocyte nanostructure
papers.abstract: Cardiac damage in the aftermath of myocardial ischemia / reperfusion (MI/R) compromises both electrical and mechanical function, predisposing patients to arrhythmia and heart failure. Microvascular obstruction (MVO) is increasingly recognized as a sequela of MI/R and a contributor to proarrhythmic cardiac remodeling. While transvalvular unloading (TVU) using a percutaneously delivered pump is garnering appreciation as a means of limiting infarct size and preserving mechanical function following percutaneous coronary intervention, its benefits for arrhythmia prevention remain unclear. We used a porcine model to test the hypothesis that cardiac unloading prior to and through reperfusion mitigates MVO, preserves cardiomyocyte nanostructure, and alleviates arrhythmias following MI/R. Anesthetized domestic swine undergoing acute ischemia (LAD occlusion, 90 mins) and reperfusion (120 mins) were randomized to TVU (n=5) and no treatment (control; n=6) treatments. Thioflavin-S was infused into the mid-LAD to assess coronary microcirculation and quantify MVO. Arrhythmia burden was assessed by in vivo electrocardiography using 3 lead EKG. Cardiac tissues were preserved for histology and optical microscopy studies. Compared to no treatment controls, TVU hearts evidenced significantly reduced infarct area (48 +/- 5 % vs. 59 +/- 11 % p = 0.03) and MVO (19 +/- 4 % vs. 27 +/- 5% , p = 0.03) normalized to area at risk and a higher myocardial salvage index (52 +/- 5 % vs. 41 +/- 11% p = 0.03). Extensive perivascular edema, and neutrophil infiltration observed in controls was markedly reduced in TVU hearts. Confocal microscopy and spatial pattern analysis revealed significantly mitigated disruption of gap junctions and NaV1.5 dissociation from N-cadherin in TVU hearts compared to controls. Importantly, severity-adjusted arrhythmia burden during reperfusion was significantly lower in TV-P hearts (8+/-8 vs. 12+/-5 episodes lasting greater than 5seconds in controls). Our results demonstrate that TVU effectively prevents arrhythmias during reperfusion by preserving coronary microvasculature and cardiomyocyte nanostructure.

papers.title: A high-resolution protein-RNA binding atlas for structure-aware interaction prediction and post-transcriptional regulatory modeling
papers.abstract: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) control post-transcriptional gene expression by regulating RNA processing, localization, stability, and translation. However, our understanding of RNA regulation remains limited by the resolution, scale, and uniformity of available RBP binding maps. Here we introduce eclair CLIP (ecCLIP), a high-throughput CLIP-seq platform that combines endogenous protein tagging for uniform affinity capture with ligation-free library preparation to generate high-resolution RNA-protein binding profiles. We applied ecCLIP to 67 endogenously tagged RBPs in HEK293T cells, generating a high-quality transcriptome-scale atlas that recovered known binding preferences and captured post-transcriptional regulons linked to RNA half-life. To test the utility of the atlas, we incorporated ecCLIP into Borzuki, a Borzoi-derived sequence-to-function model trained on complementary RNA degradation, expression, CLIP, and Perturb-seq data. Inclusion of ecCLIP data improved RNA half-life prediction and assessment of 3' UTR variant effects on RNA stability, demonstrating that our atlas helps capture RNA dynamics. To directly model the cis-regulatory grammar underlying these RBP-RNA interactions, we developed Pythia, a structure-aware neural network architecture that incorporates context-free grammar-inspired fixed convolutions to explicitly encode RNA base-pairing features. Pythia predicted RBP binding from sequence and structural context and decomposed predictions into sequence- and structure-dependent components. We tested this decomposition for five RBPs using massively parallel reporter CLIP (MPRC) binding assays in cells, using synthetic RNA libraries containing mutations designed to preserve or disrupt predicted RNA structures across nominated binding sites. We used the same MPRC strategy to confirm allele-specific binding effects for variants prioritized by Pythia. Together, ecCLIP and Pythia provide a resource for structure-aware decoding of RNA-protein interaction grammar and interpretation of post-transcriptional regulatory variation.

papers.title: Strategies for Overcoming the Purification Challenges of Meis1 and HoxA9 and Their Functional Characterization
papers.abstract: Transcription factors are critical regulators of homeostasis, and disruption of their function is a common underlying mechanism in cancer. The homeobox Myeloid Ecotropic Integration site-1 (Meis1) and its binding partner Homeobox A9 (HoxA9) are among the most highly dysregulated transcription factors in cancer, particularly in Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML). Upregulation of HoxA9 is observed in more than 50% of AML cases and is a predictor of poor prognosis. Meis1 forms a cooperative DNA complex with HoxA9 and is required for HoxA9-mediated leukemogenesis. However, the mechanism by which HoxA9 and Meis1 interact and form a complex with DNA is unknown. To study the molecular mechanisms behind the HoxA9-Meis1-DNA complex and support future development of inhibitors, we describe optimized procedures for the recombinant expression and purification of full-length Meis1 and HoxA9. The constructs with an N-terminal His-tag showed degradation, but the addition of a small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO)-fusion tag improved solubility and stability for both proteins. Conditions were optimized for SUMO cleavage to obtain tag-free Meis1 and HoxA9 with high purity. We showed that both purified proteins bound to DNA with nanomolar affinities using a fluorescence polarization (FP) binding assay. The SUMO-fusion HoxA9 showed a distinct binding profile compared to the tag-free HoxA9 and formed a cooperative complex with Meis1. The tag-free HoxA9 appeared to oligomerize under the assay conditions. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report to visualize the HoxA9-Meis1 cooperative interaction in a high-throughput assay. Our work establishes a foundation for future studies to decipher the protein-protein interaction of Meis1-HoxA9 and the development of inhibitors.

papers.title: Season-long head acceleration exposure, prior contact-sport history, and cognitive performance in British amateur American football players
papers.abstract: Background: Head acceleration events (HAEs) are common in contact sports, but season-long exposure and its relationship with cognitive performance in amateur British American football remain poorly characterised. Methods: Thirty male players were recruited from three British amateur American football teams. Selected Sport Concussion Assessment Tool 6 (SCAT6) components and computerised tasks were assessed across the season. Seasonal analyses included 20 participants, and exposure-linked analyses included 17. Helmet-sensor events were attributed to participants and restricted to participant-assignment and baseline-to-post-season calendar windows. Mixed-effects models assessed seasonal outcomes. Principal component analysis (PCA) summarised standardised baseline-to-post-season changes, and six exposure associations were evaluated. Results: Players recorded a mean of 768 (SD 482) events. Several individual tests improved across the season. The first principal component (PC1) explained 21.9% of change variance and had loadings with opposing signs. Prior seasons had a nominal association with PC1 (slope -0.153, 95% CI -0.305 to -0.00018; r2=0.233; p=0.0498), which did not survive six-test Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) adjustment (p=0.299). No in-season exposure association survived adjustment. Conclusion: Repeated-test performance improved, while exposure associations remained uncertain. The mixed PC1 pattern cannot be interpreted as a uniform measure of global cognitive worsening or improvement.

papers.title: DSSNA: Automated Nucleic Acid Structure Analysis in Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: This work presents DSSNA (Define Spatial Structure of Nucleic Acids) v2026, a free and open-source standalone GROMACS module for the automated analysis of nucleic acid structures from atomic coordinates that reproduces the core functionality of X3DNA and DSSR while extending it to the analysis of molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories. The algorithm identifies and classifies canonical and non-canonical base pairs, hydrogen-bond networks, stacking interactions, helices, and other elements of nucleic acid secondary and tertiary structure, using neighbor-search algorithms for efficient analysis of large trajectory datasets and a modular output system that lets users select the structural metrics required for a particular analysis. Application to a 1 s MD trajectory of a GUAA tetraloop mutant of the sarcin--ricin domain of Escherichia coli 23S ribosomal RNA (PDB: 1MSY) showed that persistent canonical base pairs form the structural core that maintains the secondary-structure profile, whereas most non-canonical base pairs and stacking interactions are transient. These results demonstrate that DSSNA enables the characterization of both static nucleic acid structures and the temporal evolution of structural interactions in MD simulations.

papers.title: A matrikine organizes the dendritic cell- T cell triads that build tertiary lymphoid structures
papers.abstract: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) predict checkpoint-inhibition response, and conventional dendritic cells (cDC) are required to build and maintain them. What licenses tumor niches is not fully understood: chemokines recruit cells but do not specify TLS-archetypal DC:CD4+T:CD8+T triad composition. We show that the organizing signal is a matrix fragment. Proteoglycan versican (VCAN) proteolysis releases the matrikine versikine constitutively in CXCL13-replete germinal center light zones. In tumors, versikine is released inducibly within CXCL13-rich stromal niches. Versikine activates CD11b+ cDC, expands cDC1, and suffices for triad assembly. Versikine-conditioned DC engage progenitor-exhausted CD8+ T-cells (Tpex) and Tpex-sustaining, Th1-polarized follicular helper CD4+ T-cells. Excess unproteolyzed VCAN inverts this toward DC-Treg crosstalk and Tpex loss. Versikine (mRNA or recombinant protein) plus anti-PD-L1 eradicated experimental tumors reverse-translated to model adverse-prognosis, VCAN-proteolysis-weak patients from a prospective PD-1 blockade trial in oligometastatic colorectal cancer. The extracellular matrix instructs, rather than merely scaffolds, the multicellular units of antitumor immunity.

papers.title: Ibuprofen impairs fracture healing by disrupting neutrophil-mediated tissue repair
papers.abstract: Neutrophils are among the first immune cells recruited to fractures, yet their contribution to bone repair remains poorly understood. Anti-inflammatory use has been linked to increased risk of non-union fractures, while prolonged neutrophil activity or failed clearance of neutrophil-derived DNA in the form of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), can also impair fracture healing. Using dynamic live imaging and cellular perturbation in adult zebrafish, we show that neutrophils play a key role in shaping the early fracture microenvironment. Neutrophils rapidly accumulated at fractures where they released NETs and exhibited the activation of gene programmes associated with matrix remodelling. Compromising neutrophil recruitment, via ibuprofen treatment or orthogonal genetic and pharmacological perturbations, dramatically increased incidence of fracture non-union and lead to altered callus architecture through delay of osteoblast differentiation and impaired mineralisation. Mechanistically, neutrophils actively interacted with key structural proteins, including laminin, fibronectin, and collagen I, through uptake, recycling and active de novo secretion pathways. Together, our findings reveal that neutrophils establish a provisional emergency fracture matrix that templates subsequent bone repair, providing a mechanistic link between early non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) exposure and impaired skeletal healing.

papers.title: Development of auxin reporters in oilseed rape (Brassica napus)
papers.abstract: Auxin is a key phytohormone that regulates all aspects of plant growth, development, and environmental responses, making the precise analysis of its distribution and signaling essential for understanding plant adaptation and physiological processes. However, despite the agricultural importance of oilseed rape (Brassica napus), the lack of robust, species-specific molecular tools limits detailed studies of hormone signaling in this crop. Here, we developed and characterized reporter systems for the sensitive visualization and quantification of auxin distribution and signaling in B. napus. The DR5cc auxin signaling reporter and a novel synthetic auxin-responsive reporter, BIP3, assembled from promoter fragments of three oilseed rape Aux/IAA genes, were generated to drive GUS expression. In hairy roots, both reporters showed auxin-responsive expression in the root apical meristem that became broader after auxin treatment. In transgenic seedlings, flowers at anthesis, and 12-day-old embryos, DR5cc exhibited a more defined expression pattern than BIP3. To monitor real-time auxin dynamics under abiotic stress, DR5cc fluorescent reporters were employed in hairy roots. Mannitol and NaCl treatments induced a time-dependent increase in fluorescence, peaking at 6-12 h before returning to basal levels after 24 h. Furthermore, dual-reporter assays enabled simultaneous monitoring of auxin and cytokinin signaling, revealing distinct hormone-specific spatial responses in hairy roots. Finally, we established a quantitative DII (qDII) reporter system using degron domains from B. napus Aux/IAA proteins, providing a quantitative readout of auxin depletion. Together, these reporter systems enable spatial, temporal, and quantitative analyses of auxin dynamics during development and stress adaptation in oilseed rape.

papers.title: HOMED enables hierarchical and multimodal optimization of DNA methylation deconvolution across tissues
papers.abstract: Cellular heterogeneity is a major confounder in bulk DNA methylation data for epigenome-wide association studies. Existing reference-based DNAm deconvolution methods often ignore hierarchies among related cell types and may generalize poorly across datasets due to limited variability in reference profiles. We developed HOMED (Hierarchically Optimized Methylation Deconvolution), a framework that integrates cell-lineage hierarchies, single-cell RNA sequencing-guided deconvolution, and paired bulk RNA-seq/DNAm data for CpG signature optimization. Across simulated and real peripheral blood mononuclear cell, lung, and placental datasets, HOMED consistently yielded the highest PCCs and lowest RMSEs, outperforming existing scRNA-seq-guided DNAm deconvolution methods, improving accuracy, resolution, and cross-tissue generalizability.

papers.title: Multi-omics uncover interactions in the vaginal microbiome and a type II secretion/Tad pilus system in Gardnerella species
papers.abstract: Background: The vaginal microbiome is a key determinant of women's health, with Lactobacillus-dominant communities protecting against bacterial vaginosis (BV) and related adverse outcomes. Dysbiosis involves a decline in lactobacilli and overgrowth of anaerobes, with Gardnerella species central to initiating polymicrobial aggregates. However, the genetic determinants of community assembly, biofilm formation, and interspecies interactions remain poorly understood. This study investigated the genomic and functional basis of these traits using an integrated multi-omics approach. Results: Long-read whole-genome sequencing of clinical Gardnerella isolates yielded closed genomes and revealed a pangenomic split correlating with high- versus low-biofilm phenotypes, linked to clade-specific genomic islands and allelic variants. Functional gene modules within these regions distinguished G. vaginalis from G. piotii, contributing to nutrient acquisition, cell wall metabolism, and colonization. Integrated 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and proteomics of all pairwise dual-species co-cultures of five key vaginal bacteria showed that G. vaginalis and L. iners acted as dominant ecological drivers, outcompeting neighbors and triggering asymmetric proteomic remodeling. Differential expression of a gene within a putative operon encoding a conserved type II secretion/Tad pilus system, revealed by integrating the pangenome with the proteome, implicated this system in interspecies interactions. AI-based structural predictions of the complex suggested isoform-specific differences in protein folding between G. vaginalis and G. piotii. In parallel, metagenomic analysis of 93 women showed the operon was more abundant in BV samples than in healthy controls, linking it to dysbiosis.
