The heatwave increased the probability of complete and partial mortality more in large than in small Pocillopora colonies. Remarkably, elevated partial mortality persisted for at least three years after the thermal stress had subsided, indicating substantial delayed impacts. Contrary to the rapid recovery historically observed on Mo'orea's reefs following other disturbances, coral cover continued to decline for four years after the bleaching event, with no evidence of recovery. Our findings reveal that bleaching impacts extend far beyond the heatwave itself. Persistent delayed mortality of surviving colonies can limit reef recovery for years, indicating that post-bleaching demographic processes may be a major, yet underappreciated, determinant of coral reefs' resilience.

papers.title: Validation of a Commercially Available Non-Woven Fabric Electrode for Mouse Electroretinography
papers.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the performance and usability of a commercially available non-woven fabric electrode as a cost-effective and user-friendly alternative to standard corneal contact lens electrodes for recording murine electroretinograms. Methods: Using a paired design, full-field electroretinograms were recorded in the same mice using the commercially available non-woven fabric electrode and a conventional contact lens electrode. Key parameters evaluated included (1) stability of baseline noise, (2) dark-adapted intensity-response curves (0.01-100 cd{middle dot}s{middle dot}m-2), (3) light-adapted intensity-response curves (3-100 cd{middle dot}s{middle dot}m-2), (4) 20-Hz and 30-Hz flicker responses, (5) extended recordings targeting slow c-wave kinetics under dark-adapted conditions, and (6) inter-eye consistency via bilateral simultaneous recordings. Results: Eliminating the need for viscous lubricants, the non-woven fabric electrode simplified placement on the cornea, alignment, and re-application. It yielded a-wave and b-wave amplitudes and peak times comparable or superior to those obtained with standard contact lens electrodes. Notably, during prolonged recordings, the non-woven fabric electrode yielded significantly larger c-wave amplitudes while maintaining equivalent baseline noise stability. Bilateral simultaneous recordings demonstrated high inter-eye correlation and low variability of measurements between contralateral eyes. Conclusions: The non-woven fabric electrode provides high-quality, reproducible electroretinographic recordings comparable to (and for c-waves superior to) those obtained using standard corneal contact lens electrodes. This method facilitates standardized data acquisition and improves inter-laboratory reproducibility of murine electroretinography. Translational Relevance: By reducing financial and technical barriers, this non-woven fabric electrode offers an alternative to specialized recording setups, improving experimental throughput and efficiency in ophthalmic research.

papers.title: Kcs1-dependent inositol pyrophosphates promote DNA double-strand break repair via Pho80-Pho85 in budding yeast
papers.abstract: The cleavage of membrane-bound phosphoinositides produces inositol polyphosphates (IPs) and pyrophosphates (PP-IPs), small water-soluble signaling molecules that are highly conserved in eukaryotes and play a critical role in cell metabolism. Loss of the inositol pyrophosphate kinase (PP-IPk) Kcs1 and its mammalian ortholog IP6K1 was previously shown to cause hypersensitivity to genotoxic stress and reduced homologous recombination (HR) repair. To identify the mechanism linking PP-IPs to DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair, we combined quantitative proteomics with biochemical, genetic, and cell-cycle analyses in budding yeast. We found that loss of Kcs1, but not the PP-IPk Vip1, caused increased sensitivity to the radiomimetic drug zeocin. kcs1{Delta} cells displayed persistent Rad53 signaling and elevated {gamma}-H2A levels, remaining arrested in G1/S during treatment and accumulating in G2/M for hours after damage removal. Unexpectedly, Kcs1-dependent PP-IPs promoted DSB repair independently of the core HR machinery and of cell-cycle stage. Quantitative proteomics revealed increased levels of PHO pathway proteins in zeocin treated kcs{Delta} cells, and deletion of the CDK inhibitor PHO81 substantially rescued zeocin hypersensitivity, indicating that constitutive inhibition of the Pho80-Pho85 cyclin-dependent kinase underlies the DNA repair defect caused by Kcs1 loss. This function of Pho80-Pho85 was mechanistically distinct from its canonical role in phosphate homeostasis, and partially independent of its connections to Ku80 regulation. Together, our findings identify Kcs1-dependent PP-IP signaling as a new upstream input controlling Pho80-Pho85 activity during the DNA damage response, establishing an HR-independent axis for genome maintenance and linking PP-IP metabolism to the DNA damage response in eukaryotic cells.

papers.title: Winnow-tax: sensitive and precise taxonomic profiling of low-coverage organisms in shotgun metagenomes
papers.abstract: Accurate species-level profiling of shotgun metagenomes becomes difficult when an organism is represented by only sparse sequence coverage. Per-read k-mer classifiers can retain sensitivity under these conditions, but short reads from conserved or shared genomic regions can generate false-positive calls among closely related references. More conservative marker-gene and genome-containment approaches generally provide stronger species-level specificity but may lose sensitivity as genomic sampling becomes sparse. We present winnow-tax, a two-stage taxonomic profiling pipeline that separates sensitive candidate nomination from genome-level confirmation. Candidate species are nominated using sylph, Kraken2, and a branch-rescue procedure, then reads are competitively recruited to a sample-specific reference set. Species presence is evaluated using read support, observed genome breadth, and a Lander-Waterman-based breadth ratio that compares observed breadth with the breadth expected at the measured mean depth. In a controlled synthetic community of 82 genomes with human DNA background, winnow-tax maintained a stronger precision-sensitivity balance than Kraken2/Bracken, sylph, and MetaPhlAn 4 as genome coverage decreased, with its advantage concentrated near the low-coverage detection boundary. In the CAMI III Toy Longitudinal Human Gut benchmark, winnow-tax had higher sensitivity than sylph (0.803 versus 0.672), lower precision (0.923 versus 0.970), and a modestly but significantly higher F1 score (0.858 versus 0.793). In a clinical enteric stool cohort with culture/PCR reference testing, winnow-tax achieved the best performance for Salmonella, detecting 33 of 43 culture-positive samples with two false-positive calls (F1 0.846 versus 0.811 for sylph). Together, these results support the advantage of a profiling strategy in which read-level classifications are accepted only when their genomic evidence is distributed as broadly as expected given the sequencing depth.

papers.title: On-demand surround suppression explains the spatiotemporal window of the tilt illusion
papers.abstract: What we see at one location depends on what surrounds it. Such contextual effects are thought to arise from neural signals that travel across the retinotopic representations. Because these signals need more time to travel longer distances, a more distant surround should influence perception most strongly when presented earlier, compensating for its delay. We tested this prediction in human observers using a visual illusion in which a central target appears tilted away from the orientation of its surround (tilt illusion). Measuring the temporal window of this illusion using psychophysical reverse correlation revealed the opposite: the most effective surround occurred progressively later as distance increased. Computational modelling demonstrated that this reversal is explained if the visual system sends out a query that recruits contextual information on demand. Perceptual appearance may thus be constructed through temporally unfolding interactions in which context is actively gathered, not passively received.

papers.title: FlyAnatoView: Visualization of Drosophila Single-cell RNA-seq Datasets on Anatomographs
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) is a powerful approach for characterizing gene expression at single-cell resolution and identifying distinct cell populations within complex tissues. However, tissue dissociation disrupts the spatial relationships among cells, making it difficult to determine their original anatomical locations and interpret gene expression patterns in the context of tissue organization. To address this limitation, we developed FlyAnatoView (https://www.flyrnai.org/tools/rna_seq_base/web/svg_files/), a resource that projects scRNA-seq data onto anatomical diagrams of Drosophila melanogaster. By integrating gene expression data with anatomical representations, FlyAnatoView helps restore spatial context and enables users to explore expression patterns across tissues, organs, and cell types. This resource provides an intuitive way to connect transcriptomic profiles with anatomical structures, facilitating the interpretation and exploration of scRNA-seq datasets.

papers.title: Assessing the Functional-Structural Reorganization of Connector Hubs in Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
papers.abstract: Recent years have seen a rise in investigations on the organizational principles of brain networks in healthy and pathological conditions. Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is a compelling case as its focal pathology is accompanied by widespread network disruptions. However, how TLE affects functional connector hubs, regions supporting long-range and inter-network communication, remain poorly understood. We mapped connector hub reorganization in patients with TLE relative to healthy controls. Patients exhibited widespread connector hub reductions in the ipsilateral occipital, cingulate, precuneus and hippocampal regions as well as the bilateral pallidum. Hub reductions occurred alongside the emergence of new hubs in contralateral regions. We furthermore observed strong associations between hub reductions and microstructural alterations in subcortical structures and the hippocampus. These findings demonstrate widespread, asymmetric connector hub reorganization extending beyond the epileptogenic temporal lobe, revealing distinct patterns of network disruption and brain-wide reorganization.

papers.title: Beyond the glass: testing visitor effects on the behavior of teleost fish in public aquaria
papers.abstract: Zoos and public aquariums serve as essential hubs for wildlife conservation, public education, and scientific research; however, the success of these missions depends upon maintaining high animal welfare standards despite constant human presence. A primary concern is the 'visitor effect': the modification of animal behavior due to human presence. While this phenomenon is well-documented in captive mammals and has been explored in Chondrichthyans, it remains largely unexamined in teleost fish, despite evidence of their sensitivity to human stimuli in natural environments. This study addresses this knowledge gap by investigating the behavioral responses of 13 teleost species to varying levels of visitor density, direct human solicitations, and ambient noise. Our multivariate analysis reveals that the total number of visitors present in the aquarium and the direct sonic human solicitations (such as knocking on the glass) are significant drivers of behavioral changes. We observed high inter-taxonomic variability: while Euxiphipops sextriatus, Dascyllus aruanus, Zebrasoma flavescens, Chaetodontoplus mesoleucus and Pygoplites diacanthus showed marked sensitivity through significant modifications in their behaviors the others (Amphiprion percula, Chaetodon rafflesia, Chromis viridis, Chrysiptera parasema, Heniochus chrysostomus, and Lactoria cornuta) showed no obvious behavioral changes. Furthermore, acoustic analysis indicates a complex soundscape where global visitor density correlates with increased sound amplitude, particularly in the 100 Hz to 400 Hz range, a critical band for teleost hearing, suggesting that visitor-induced noise is distinct from the aquarium's technical background noise (pumps, aerator etc). These findings underscore that the 'visitor effect' is not a uniform phenomenon but a complex interaction shaped by species-specific sensitivity and distinct anthropogenic actions. Our results highlight the necessity of incorporating species-specific behavioral data and acoustic monitoring into welfare management protocols to better mitigate the impact of human presence on captive fish populations.

papers.title: Single-Cell Atlas of Non-Functioning Gonadotroph Tumors and Anterior Pituitary Reveals Lineage Infidelity and Clinically Associated Transcriptional Programs
papers.abstract: Non-functioning gonadotroph (NFG) tumors are the most common type of non-functioning pituitary adenomas and cause significant morbidity through mass effect. The molecular programs that distinguish NFG tumor cells from normal gonadotrophs and underlie tumor growth remain poorly understood. The aim of this study was to define transcriptional differences between NFG tumors and the normal anterior pituitary gland (APG) at single-cell resolution and to identify programs associated with tumor growth. We performed single-cell/nucleus RNA-sequencing of 21 NFG tumors and 8 APG samples, followed by integrative analyses of differential gene expression, regulatory networks, and cell-cell communication. We profiled 77,342 APG cells and 152,649 NFG tumor cells. Within the APG, we identified novel marker genes for each neuroendocrine cell type and distinct transcriptional signatures of anterior and posterior pituitary stem cell populations. Compared with normal gonadotrophs, tumor cells shared a core transcriptomic signature conserved across samples despite inter-tumor heterogeneity. Many conserved genes were markers of non-gonadotroph neuroendocrine and stem cells, suggesting that lineage infidelity is a recurrent feature of NFGs. Pseudobulk profiling identified genes positively correlated with tumor volume, including the known oncogenes CAD, BRF2, and SOX12. Finally, tumors showed increased proportions of myeloid, endothelial, and mural cells and crosstalk between tumor, immune, and stromal populations. This study defines transcriptomic signatures of cell identity in the normal APG and NFG tumors. Our findings reveal programs associated with NFG lineage infidelity and tumor growth, highlighting candidate predictors of patient outcomes and potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Mixtures of stably coexisting species overyield
papers.abstract: Diverse plant communities usually produce more biomass than monocultures, an advantage that strengthens over time and is attributed mainly to the complementarity effect - the extra biomass produced, relative to monocultures, when species exploit different resources, share fewer enemies or facilitate one another. Yet whether this advantage is a mere tendency of diverse communities, or something that every persistent community must have, has remained unknown. Here we show that stable coexistence requires a positive complementarity effect, with vanishingly rare exceptions, and that underyielding communities are significantly more likely to lose a species within two years or sampling steps, across four long-term biodiversity experiments, with odds of losing a species nearly three times higher than in other communities. In the twenty-five years since the complementarity effect was defined, the link between biodiversity effects and species coexistence had only been established theoretically for two species in competition or observed as a correlation; our theoretical result makes it a general property of multispecies communities, in which the complementarity effect scales with two established measures of how securely species coexist - local and structural stability. Our analyses are, to our knowledge, the first to test a coexistence prediction - impending species loss - prospectively in biodiversity experiments, from a functioning measure alone, turning a measure of what diversity does into a diagnostic of whether diversity can persist. Stable coexistence and higher productivity are thus intrinsically linked: biodiversity does not merely benefit ecosystem production on average; biodiversity that endures cannot but benefit it through complementarity. We anticipate that this diagnostic will turn existing biodiversity experiments, sown grasslands and intercrops into early-warning systems for species loss, since it requires only the biomass of each species in mixture and in monoculture - data these systems already collect, and that agronomists already combine into the land equivalent ratio - and that it will extend to forests, through the growing networks of tree diversity experiments and mixed-species plantations where the same measurements are made.

papers.title: High-Frequency Focused Ultrasound Directly Activates the Auditory Midbrain and Protects Against Noise-Induced Hearing Loss in Guinea Pigs
papers.abstract: Although focused ultrasound (FUS) offers promising opportunities for neuromodulation, its ability to activate central auditory neurons remains uncertain. We targeted the central nucleus of the inferior colliculus (CNIC) in anesthetized guinea pigs using 20-MHz FUS while recording cochlear and cortical activity. Consistent with previous studies, FUS delivered through a small craniotomy evoked cortical responses through indirect cochlear activation, potentially mediated by skull mechanical coupling. However, under conditions that minimized cochlear interaction, FUS induced c-Fos expression in the CNIC and auditory cortex, suggesting direct central activation of the auditory afferent pathway. FUS additionally engaged the auditory efferent system, presumably through medial olivocochlear neurons. FUS delivered before acoustic trauma nearly prevented noise-induced hearing loss, limiting threshold shifts to <10 dB compared with ~60 dB in controls. Gentamicin abolished both efferent modulation and protection, implicating cochlear efferent mechanisms. Together, these findings support FUS for auditory neuromodulation and cochlear protection against acoustic injury.

papers.title: A peptidomimetic inhibitor blocks Vibrio cholerae adhesin FrhA.
papers.abstract: Cholera is a diarrheal disease resulting from colonization of the small intestine by the Gram-negative bacterium Vibrio cholerae. The peptide-binding domain (PBD) of the adhesion protein FrhA is critical for V. cholerae intestinal colonization and biofilm formation. Antagonists of the FrhA-PBD were designed based on the tripeptide motif H-Trp-Thr-Asp-OH. Constraining the N-terminal tryptophan as a 1,2,3,4-tetrahydro-{beta}-carboline-3-carboxylic acid (Tcc) residue and X-ray analysis of a co-crystal with the FrhA-PBD define the minimal inhibitory motif. Moreover, H-(R)-Tcc-Thr-Asp-OH exhibited nanomolar binding affinity (Kd = 101 {+/-} 30.2 nM) to the FrhA-PBD, blocking adhesion protein-mediated bacterial hemagglutination and reducing biofilm formation in vitro. Intestinal epithelial cell adhesion to the FrhA-PBD was also blocked by the Tcc tripeptide (IC50 = 24 M; 95% CI, 11-51 M), which resisted chymotrypsin proteolysis. The activity of this peptidomimetic inhibitor and the atomic-level understanding of FrhA-PBD binding provide insights for developing anti-adhesion therapies to treat cholera.

papers.title: Rapid changes in wing size and shape during the transition to laboratory conditions in a Neotropical drosophilid
papers.abstract: The establishment of laboratory populations provides an opportunity to document rapid phenotypic changes across generations, although the processes underlying these changes may be difficult to disentangle. Using geometric morphometrics, we investigated changes in wing size and shape in the Neotropical drosophilid Drosophila sturtevanti. We compared field-collected males (Field) with descendants from 12 isofemale lines established independently from field-collected females, in the first (F1) and tenth (F10) laboratory generations. Wing size showed heterogeneous responses in F1, followed by a consistent reduction across all lines by F10, possibly reflecting differences among founders and developmental conditions, including larval density and temperature. Wing shape changed significantly in every line between Field and F1 and between F1 and F10. Changes in wing shape followed broadly similar directions from Field to F1 but became more heterogeneous among lines from F1 to F10. Total shape variance increased significantly between Field and F1. Within-line shape variation was not significantly lower in F1 or F10 than the variation observed in Field, while between-line shape variance increased from F1 to F10. These patterns are consistent with the possible expression of previously cryptic genetic variation following environmental change and the exposure of phenotypic effects of pre-existing genetic variation as homozygosity increases within isolated lines. Our results demonstrate that substantial morphological changes can be detected within the first laboratory generation and continue during subsequent maintenance, highlighting the potential of geometric morphometrics of insect wings for documenting rapid phenotypic change.

papers.title: Mental Timing in Locomotion: Walking Across Real and Imagined Distances
papers.abstract: The present study aimed to directly replicate the seminal findings of Decety et al. (1989), while also extending the original work with a larger sample size and additional statistical analyses. Thirty healthy adults completed both imagined and executed walking tasks over distances of 5, 10, and 15 meters. Participants also completed the Movement Imagery Questionnaire 3 (MIQ 3). Temporal correspondence between imagined and executed walking was assessed using repeated-measures ANOVA, correlation analyses, Bayesian equivalence tests, and Bland Altman analyses. Walking duration increased significantly with distance, while no significant differences were observed between imagined and executed walking times. Bayesian equivalence tests provided evidence supporting temporal equivalence between the two modalities, and Bland Altman analyses indicated good agreement with minimal systematic bias. Strong positive correlations were found between imagined and executed durations at all distances. MIQ-3 scores were not significantly associated with differences between imagined and executed walking durations. Overall, the findings successfully replicate and extend the original results reported by Decety et al. (1989), providing additional evidence supporting temporal equivalence between motor imagery and movement execution. By combining a larger sample size with contemporary statistical approaches, the present study strengthens support for the principle of functional equivalence for highly automated and cyclic movements.

papers.title: Personalized disordered circuit modeling reveals diverse neurobiological routes to transdiagnostic symptoms
papers.abstract: Precision psychiatry research has strived to characterize the neural circuitry underlying transdiagnostic symptoms with the goal of devising biologically informed diagnostic and treatment strategies. However, few clinically actionable findings have emerged from these initiatives. One potential complication in reaching this goal is that similar symptoms may arise from distinct patterns of neurobiological dysfunction. Therefore, models that can provide insight into where an individual's disordered circuits are located are important. Here, we developed a data-driven approach to identify individualized patterns of disordered connectivity using a large (n=317), transdiagnostic population with extensive fMRI data. Connectome-based predictive modeling identified functional connectivity networks associated with a broad array of psychiatric symptoms. Symptom networks were aggregated, and connections contributing most strongly to each individual's symptoms were identified to construct personalized "disordered circuit models". Within these models, many features were associated with specific diagnoses and patterns of comorbidity, despite the symptoms exhibiting no diagnostic specificity. This suggests that similar symptoms can emerge through diverse neurobiological mechanisms depending on an individual's diagnostic profile. By characterizing patient-specific neural dysfunction, disordered circuit modeling offers a promising framework for advancing precision psychiatry by accounting for diverse mechanisms from which symptoms may arise.

papers.title: A longitudinal naturalistic fMRI study of trait anxiety and cross-phase consistency in subjective fear signature expression
papers.abstract: Persistent fear is a central feature of anxiety, but it remains unclear whether this persistence is more closely related to the consistency of conditioned-threat processing or to the consistency of subjectively experienced fear. Using a longitudinal naturalistic viewing fMRI paradigm, we examined whether trait anxiety was associated with cross-phase consistency in the expression of two validated fear-related neural signatures. Forty-two participants completed two fMRI phases separated by approximately three months, viewing the same 18 naturalistic videos followed by a resting-state segment, resulting in 19 analysis segments for cross-phase analyses. We applied two pre-trained signatures of subjective fear and threat conditioning, independently developed by separate research groups, to estimate their expression over time and examined how consistently each signature was reexpressed across phases within participants. We found that higher trait anxiety was significantly associated with greater cross-phase consistency in subjective-fear signature expression, with a significantly stronger association than for threat-conditioning signature expression. The anxiety-consistency association was also stronger for the subjective-fear signature than for a general negative-affect signature. This association became more prominent over longer temporal windows and was not detected in the average time series of the amygdala, ventromedial prefrontal cortex, insula, or hippocampus. These findings suggest that individual differences in trait anxiety are associated with the consistent cross-phase reexpression of distributed neural patterns related to subjective fear. Taken together, this study demonstrates how predictive brain models combined with longitudinal naturalistic viewing can provide a new approach for examining individual differences in trait anxiety across repeated experiences of the same naturalistic contexts.

papers.title: The Cardiovascular Benefit of Menopause Hormone Treatment is Age-Dependent in Ldlr-/- Mice
papers.abstract: Background: The risk of Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) increases in women after menopause, coinciding with declining estrogen levels. However, menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) has not consistently reduced ASCVD events in post-menopausal women, despite improvements in lipid profiles. The mechanisms underlying the diminished cardiovascular protective effects of estrogens during MHT remain poorly understood. Methods: Atherosclerosis was established in 11-month-old female Ldlr-/- mice through Western diet feeding. To investigate the effects of menopause and 17{beta}-estradiol (E2) treatment on atherosclerotic burden during lipid normalization, mice were switched to a chow diet and subjected to ovariectomy (OVX) with and without E2 treatment. To determine the contribution of inflammation to ASCVD risk during MHT, a cohort of mice received Ifn{gamma}-/- bone marrow transplant (Ifn{gamma}-/-BM) before hormone treatment. To assess the influence of age on ASCVD risk during MHT, parallel studies were conducted in young mice, beginning at 12 weeks of age. Outcomes included lipid profiles, HDL function, circulating cytokines, atherosclerotic burden, liver lipid metabolic pathways and transcriptomic profiles, and hepatic estrogen receptor signaling. Results: OVX increased atherosclerotic burden compared with sham-operation. E2 treatment following OVX failed to reduce established atherosclerosis in older mice but reduced atherosclerosis in young mice during diet-induced lipid normalization. In older mice, E2 treatment increased circulating IFN&#947, impaired HDL antioxidant and cholesterol efflux functions, and promoted inflammatory and vulnerable plaque phenotypes. Suppression of inflammation through Ifn{gamma}-/-BM transplantation restored HDL function and the ability of E2 treatment to reduce atherosclerosis in older mice. In contrast, E2 treatment following OVX in young mice limited inflammation and improved HDL function. E2 treatment increased liver fatty acid metabolic signaling in both older and young mice but increased liver 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE) levels only in older mice. This age-dependent response was associated with remodeling of hepatic estrogen receptor (ER) expression, characterized by reduced ER&#945 and increased in G protein-coupled ER expression with aging. Liver transcriptomic analyses identified inflammatory and interferon-associated signatures following OVX+E2 treatment in older mice. qPCR analyses across older and young mice suggested age-associated differences in inflammatory transcripts in response to E2. Conclusions: These findings suggest that aging alters the hepatic response to E2 treatment following ovariectomy, promoting oxidative stress and inflammatory signaling that contribute to persistent systemic inflammation and compromise the ability of E2 to reduce atherosclerosis.

papers.title: A rare pre-existing progenitor-like Primed SMC compartment is the dominant inferred source of SMC-derived cellularity in vascular injury and atherosclerosis
papers.abstract: The contribution of pre-existing smooth muscle cell (SMC) states to vascular lesions remains unresolved. Here we identify a rare, progenitor-like Primed SMC compartment before lesion formation in sham-operated carotid arteries and across Myh11-lineage marked mouse aortic datasets, with a Primed-like counterpart in non-diseased human aorta. Primed SMCs retain SMC identity while combining attenuated contractile programmes with conserved niche-associated (Cd34, Fst, Tnfrsf11b) and matricellular (Vcam1, Thbs1, Timp1) cores, overlaid by vessel-specific developmental signatures (Nrn1, Gdf10, Scx). After carotid ligation and during high-fat diet-induced atherosclerosis in Ldlr-/- and Apoe-/- mice, disease-associated Primed, cycling and fibrochondrocyte populations preferentially map to baseline Primed SMCs, whereas contractile SMCs are depleted as inferred feeder sources. Concordant trajectory, graph-based and cross-dataset analyses support a model in which this pre-existing compartment is the dominant inferred source of SMC-derived lesional cellularity. These findings favour expansion and diversification of the Primed compartment over widespread phenotypic switching of contractile SMCs.

papers.title: Traits and hidden states: is self-fertilization associated with rates of diversification across mating and sexual systems?
papers.abstract: Angiosperms, the most diverse group of land plants, possess considerable variation in sexual expression and mating strategy. Reproductive biology is a key determinant of fitness, and may help answer a persistent question in evolutionary biology: why are some areas of the tree of life more species-rich than others? State-dependent speciation-extinction methods (SSEs), which associate traits with patterns of diversification, can be used here. Previously, SSEs have been used within families to investigate the hypothesis that selfing is an evolutionary "dead end." To the best of the authors' knowledge, no study has looked across families, which would increase power to more generally test this hypothesis. Here, we examine the impact of 1) mating system and 2) sexual system on diversification across 18 phylogenetically diverse families. We also discuss how more recent advances in SSE models (i.e., "hidden state" models) influence our interpretation of these patterns and evaluate how the relationship between mating and sexual systems can be leveraged to gain insight into the impact of reproductive biology on evolutionary outcomes. We find that the mating system does not better explain patterns of diversification when compared to null models, but the sexual system often does. We also find family-level heterogeneity in our results, which suggests conclusions drawn from studies on individual families may not be consistent with any broader trend.

papers.title: Microbial profiling of Drosophila in French Guiana reveals candidate microbial taxa associated with native and invasive host.
papers.abstract: Invasive alien species (IAS) represent a major threat to biodiversity, human health, and economy. Yet the role of host-associated microbiomes in invasion processes remains poorly understood in natural systems. Here, we investigated the bacterial and fungal microbiomes of IAS and native Drosophila species collected along an anthropization gradient in French Guiana. Analyses of Drosophila communities revealed that IAS establishment is limited outside coastal habitats. Using bacterial 16S rRNA and fungal ITS metabarcoding of pooled individuals, we assessed microbial diversity, composition, and structure across host species, host category (invasive vs. native), and locality. Bacterial communities associated with IAS harboured reduced alpha diversity and distinct community structure compared to native Drosophila species, and host phylogenetic relatedness and locality also contributed to bacteriome variation. In contrast, fungal communities were mainly structured by locality and host species. We further identified core and exclusive taxa, compared bacteriome composition between native and IAS hosts using global reference datasets, and integrated information from the microbiome literature. This approach led to the identification of 45 bacterial and fungal candidate taxa potentially associated with host adaptation or competitiveness across coastal and rainforest environments. Overall, our results highlight microbiome variation as a potential component of invasion dynamics in Neotropical Drosophila.

papers.title: Very Early Cortical Auditory Responses to Speech in Humans
papers.abstract: A foundational measure of the auditory system's ability to process sound correctly is the auditory brainstem response (ABR) and middle latency response (MLR) complex, but their dependence on stimulus complexity and behavioral relevance is poorly understood. Here we recorded noninvasive, simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG) in adults listening to both naturalistic speech and clicks, and computed the resulting temporal response functions (TRFs). The TRF's ABR-MLR complex for speech listening contains a very early cortical peak (11 ms latency), which has not been well-characterized, and is absent for click stimuli. Other significant differences in latency and source between the speech and click MLR complexes point to further differences in their auditory processing, in thalamus and cortex. In contrast, the speech and click TRF's ABR complex both share a similar, prominent wave V response. In summation, the use of naturalistic speech reveals how early auditory responses reflect its ethological relevance.

papers.title: Appellian Neural Networks
papers.abstract: The movement of articulated bodies, whether biological or robotic, involves two interrelated computational challenges. Inverse dynamics determines the forces or torques required to achieve a specified movement, while forward dynamics computes the resulting accelerations from given forces or torques. Although both computations are governed by the same equations of motion, they are typically implemented as separate inverse and forward mappings in both model-based and data-driven approaches. This division can obscure the underlying structure common to both problems. Here, we introduce the Appellian Neural Network (ANNet), a physics-informed neural network that unifies both computations through a shared learned representation by modeling a single scalar quantity from classical mechanics, specifically Appell's acceleration energy. Inverse dynamics is obtained by differentiating the learned energy function with respect to acceleration to recover joint torques. Forward dynamics is computed without retraining by embedding the same learned energy landscape into an optimization objective, where the unregularized minimum satisfies the Gibbs-Appell equation. The resulting accelerations are then integrated forward in time. ANNet is evaluated using a double pendulum paradigm. For trajectories not encountered during training, both inverse and forward simulations demonstrate accuracy and real-time capability. Both computations propagate input noise similarly to their analytical counterparts, and adaptation of the inverse dynamics to a modified pendulum generalizes to forward simulation without additional forward-specific training. These results establish a first-principles approach for employing a single learned representation to support both inverse and forward dynamic computations.

papers.title: Molecular basis of competence for neural induction in the chick embryo
papers.abstract: Competence is the capacity of a cell or tissue to respond to a specific inducing signal from a neighbouring tissue, by changing its fate in a specific direction. Neural induction is the process by which the epiblast of the early embryo responds to signals from the organizer (the tip of the primitive streak in amniotes) by forming a neural plate. Here we study why three regions of the early chick embryo lack competence to respond to neural induction by a grafted organizer: the outer anterior area opaca and the posterior area opaca at primitive streak stages (HH3+-4-), and the inner anterior area opaca at head process stage (HH5), in comparison with the competent anterior inner area opaca at HH3+-4-. Molecular analysis of these tissues, and their temporal dynamics following exposure to the organizer, reveals several differences. Among them, increased BMP and decreased ERK signalling characterise the non-competent regions. Inhibition of BMP can restore competence to HH5 epiblast; a combination of BMP-inhibition with ERK-stimulation by FGF8 can confer competence to the outer area opaca, whereas none of these can endow posterior epiblast with competence for neural induction. We conclude that spatiotemporal competence of epiblast for neural induction is regulated by several mechanisms, including extracellular signals.

papers.title: Species phylogenetics using intraprotein residue dependence inferred with protein foundation models
papers.abstract: Traditional molecular phylogenetic inference uses multiple sequence alignments and amino acid substitution models that generally assume that sites evolve independently. In contrast, protein foundation models (pFMs) are deep learning models that reveal residue dependence patterns within sequences. There are two types of pFMs: Evolutionary Scale Models (esm-pFM) for analyzing individual protein sequences, and MSA Transformer (msat-pFM) models for analyzing MSAs. Using pFMs to analyze sequences produces residue attention matrices (RAMs) and sequence attention matrices (SAMs), respectively. RAMs and SAMs can be used to estimate pairwise distances and, thus, reconstruct phylogenies using the Neighbor-Joining (NJ) method. Here, we compare the performance of RAM-NJ and SAM-NJ phylogenies in reconstructing established species relationships across different proteins and taxon sets. Surprisingly, RAM-NJ phylogenies were generally as accurate as SAM-NJ phylogenies even though RAM inference does not require construction or analysis of an MSA. Our results show that pFM-based analyses can recover species relationships without conventional substitution models or, in the case of RAMs, a multiple sequence alignment. These results suggest that evolutionary relationships are reflected not only in primary sequence differences between species, but also in the sequence-specific patterns of inter-residue dependence produced by pFM analysis of individual sequences. However, pFM phylogenies are less accurate than those obtained with standard maximum likelihood approaches, underscoring the need to further develop methods to harness RAMs and SAMs more effectively.

papers.title: Chronic In Vivo Imaging of a Focal Cortical Dysplasia Mouse Model Reveals Progressive Neuronal Loss with No Senolytic or Antiseizure Efficacy Following Dasatinib-Quercetin Treatment
papers.abstract: Objective: Focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) type II is a common cause of pediatric drug-resistant epilepsy with no disease-modifying treatment. It arises from somatic mutations in the mTOR pathway that produce a mosaic population of mTOR-hyperactive dysmorphic neurons (DNs) with a senescence phenotype. A recent report showed that oral dasatinib-quercetin (DQ), both putative senolytics, selectively eliminates these neurons and abolishes seizures in an Mtorp.S2215F model. However, this has not been tested in a second FCD model and neuron loss was shown only by cross-sectional histology. Methods: Using chronic cranial windows and longitudinal in vivo two-photon imaging, we tracked genetically labeled neurons over eight weeks. In a mosaic MTORp.L2427P FCD model on a C57BL/6J background, we combined imaging with continuous video-EEG, immunohistochemistry (IHC), and LC-MS/MS pharmacokinetics in 47 mice. Seizure and pharmacokinetic sampling were extended to a smaller Swiss/CD1 cohort, the strain used previously. Results: Imaging revealed progressive loss of mTORmut (16.7%) and non-mTORmut (13.1%) neurons, with minimal loss in unmatched non-FCD controls. In IHC, lesions contained Beta-galactosidase-positive (B-Gal+) cells, but oral DQ showed no evidence of eliminating DNs or reducing seizure frequency, duration, or burden; seizures also persisted in CD1 mice. B-Gal+ cells tended to be less dense after DQ, but not significantly after correction. These data are more consistent with a senomorphic than a senolytic effect. Brain dasatinib (median 8.5 nM) exceeded its Src/ABL IC50, whereas quercetin (median 12 nM) was nearly two orders of magnitude below its BCL-XL affinity. Significance: Longitudinal tracking of single neurons shows progressive loss of labeled neurons in an FCD model, whereas the reported senolytic and antiseizure effects of DQ were not reproduced. DQ should not be assumed to act as a senolytic across FCD models, strains, or MTOR variants. Dependence on strain, mutation, or brain exposure bears on clinical translation.

papers.title: EEG-guided robotic control of transcranial magnetic stimulation
papers.abstract: Brain-state-guided and closed-loop transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) protocols have emerged as methods for decreasing the outcome variability and increasing the therapeutic effectiveness of stimulation protocols. However, existing brain-state-dependent TMS systems control only stimulation timing, while the location is fixed and manually adjusted between blocks or sessions. This limits targeting distributed cortical networks in a flexible brain-state-dependent paradigm. We developed a method that jointly manages TMS pulse timing and location automatically controlled by electroencephalography (EEG)-derived brain state. A machine-learning algorithm infers the brain state in real time to guide robotic coil placement. We present a proof-of-concept study in which EEG controlled both the target site and the timing of TMS. A pre-trained convolutional neural network discriminated between resting state and movements performed with the right or left hand; the classifier output determined the hemisphere in which primary-motor-cortex hand area was stimulated. Preprocessing and decoding of 2-s EEG segments required 150 ms, and the robot took 7.5 s to move from the vertex home position to the predefined motor targets. The EEG-guided robotic TMS method expands the toolkit for brain-state-dependent neurostimulation by enabling closed-loop control of stimulus location based on EEG-derived brain states, including volitional activity. Thus, the method can benefit both neuroscience research and clinical neuromodulation applications, such as by optimizing stimulation parameters to the brain state that produces optimal rehabilitation outcomes in spinal cord injury or motor disorders.

papers.title: Determinants of persistence in sequential effort-based decision-making
papers.abstract: Goal-directed behavior often requires sustained effort across a sequence of interdependent decisions, yet the determinants of persistence in such contexts remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how individuals regulate persistence in a novel sequential effort-based task in which they controlled an avatar through successive checkpoints to reach a final goal and could make repeated attempts following failure. At each attempt, participants could choose either to persist in the same task or to disengage toward an easier but less rewarding alternative. We found that decisions to persist or disengage were jointly shaped by multiple interacting factors. Disengagement increased with task difficulty and lower skill level. It also increased with repeated attempts and varied with time-on-task, indexing fatigue, and with accumulated errors, indexing lack of progress. Conversely, proximity to the goal promoted persistence and shaped decision dynamics with greater hesitation when disengaging near the goal. Notably, clearing the first checkpoint produced a sharp increase in persistence, suggesting that early success plays a pivotal role. Furthermore, persistence reflected both retrospective and prospective evaluations of effort, with prior investment promoting commitment and anticipated effort reducing it. Finally, disengagement was preceded by short-term performance decline but not by a detectable increase in decision conflict. Together, these findings provide a comprehensive account of persistence in sequential effortful tasks, showing that decisions to persist or disengage are jointly shaped by multiple factors related to fatigue, (lack of) progress, goal proximity, and early success.

papers.title: Creatine phosphagen system regulates energy metabolism and growth of trophoblasts
papers.abstract: The creatine (Cr)-creatine kinase (CK)-phosphocreatine (PCr) system maintains ATP homeostasis in tissues with high energy demands, but its role in early human placental development remains poorly understood. We characterized Cr-CK-PCr system components across gestation and investigated its function in trophoblast development. Proteins involved in Cr biosynthesis, transport, and utilization were examined in first-trimester, second-trimester, and term human placentae (n=3-6/group). Components showed gestational age- and compartment-specific localization. The biosynthetic enzymes AGAT and GAMT localized predominantly to fetal villous mesenchyme and broadly across villous compartments, respectively. CKB was enriched in fetal mesenchyme, whereas CKMT1 was broadly expressed across trophoblast subtypes. The main Cr transporter SLC6A8 was abundant in syncytiotrophoblast early in gestation but shifted predominantly to fetal blood vessels at term. To determine functional importance, primary human trophoblast stem cells (hTSCs) were treated with a creatine analog, cyclocreatine (cCr; 0-40 mM), for 48 h. Treatment with 20 mM cCr reduced proliferation (P<0.001), decreased EGFR expression (P<0.05), induced cell-cycle arrest (P<0.0001), and increased apoptosis (P<0.0001). cCr also impaired mitochondrial and glycolytic function (P<0.01) with morphological evidence of mitochondrial stress. Consistently, treatment of primary human trophoblast organoids with cCr reduced organoid growth and EGFR expression (P<0.05). Together, these findings demonstrate that the Cr-CK-PCr system is dynamically expressed across human placental development and that disruption of Cr/PCr metabolism compromises trophoblast bioenergetics, proliferation, and survival, supporting its importance in placental development and providing a foundation for investigating its contribution to pregnancy disorders associated with altered placental energy metabolism.

papers.title: A near-complete human pancreatic cancer genome
papers.abstract: Genomic changes are central to cancer, so sequencing is essential for understanding tumor evolution and advancing precision medicine, but resolving somatic variants and methylation is challenging in regions with repeats, reference gaps, and germline variants. To identify the full spectrum of somatic variants, including complex rearrangements, we construct and curate near-complete, haplotype-resolved assemblies of the most recent common ancestor of an early-passage, broadly-consented hypodiploid pancreatic cancer cell line and matched normal tissues. The tumor assembly recapitulates all 35 chromosomes observed by karyotyping, including translocation-induced hybrid chromosomes containing dynamic dicentric and fused centromeres, nested foldback inversions causing 14 breakpoints with a haplotype switch in a single derivative chromosome, and centromeric satellite tandem duplications up to 136 kbp. Our tumor-normal assembly-based benchmark expands previous multi-technology ensemble benchmark approaches, adding >8,000 somatic small variants altering ~40 kbp and 149 somatic SVs altering 939 kbp, including 2,764 small variants and 126 SVs not represented on GRCh38. Additionally, 5,111 somatic small variants change representation because they alter germline variants on GRCh38, impacting mutational signatures. Most source-resolved somatic LINE insertions originate from two non-reference germline LINE insertions with accessible promoter elements. These assemblies demonstrate that centromeric, acrocentric, telomeric, and other polymorphic regions, conventionally excluded from analysis, harbor extensive somatic and epigenetic changes and provide curated paired tumor-normal benchmarks to advance algorithms for repetitive regions of cancer genomes.

papers.title: BaSiCPy: Scalable and Robust Shading Correction for Optical Microscopy Images
papers.abstract: Quantitative fluorescence microscopy is frequently confounded by spatially varying illumination and temporal intensity drift. Although BaSiC is a widely adopted retrospective correction method, it can fail when foreground content is strongly correlated across images, a common regime in time-lapse, tiled and volumetric acquisitions, and its application often requires manual parameter tuning that limits reproducibility and scalability. We introduce BaSiCPy, a foreground-aware implementation of BaSiC that improves illumination profile estimation under correlated foreground structures, provides automatic hyperparameter selection and accelerates large-scale processing through GPU support. BaSiCPy is distributed as an open-source Python package with graphical and programmatic interfaces, facilitating integration into contemporary bioimage analysis workflows.

papers.title: Integrating Metabolic Networks into Hybrid Bioprocess Models
papers.abstract: The optimization and control of bioprocesses require robust in silico models that can accurately capture the complex and dynamic behavior of living cells. While hybrid models that combine machine learning with mechanistic equations have emerged as a powerful tools, they often require relatively large datasets and might yield inconsistent predictions that violate the stoichiometry of metabolism. In this study, we introduce FBA-Hyb, a multi-scale hybrid modeling framework that tightly integrates genome-scale metabolic networks via flux balance analysis (FBA) into its architecture. In our FBA-Hyb framework, artificial neural networks predict key FBA inputs (substrate uptake rates and FBA objectives) while a surrogate FBA module translates them into the metabolic fluxes that govern the bioprocess. A key novelty is that the FBA optimization step is replaced by a surrogate generated with symbolic regression, which encapsulates the FBA model into a compact analytical expression. This allows easy backpropagation through the integration of the neural controlled differential equation based FBA-Hyb bioprocess model. We validated FBA-Hyb against a standard hybrid model (Std-Hyb) using two Escherichia coli fed-batch case studies. In the first study, FBA-Hyb achieved a 42% average improvement in predictive accuracy (R2) during a leave-one-process-out cross validation. Crucially, FBA-Hyb maintains strict stoichiometric feasibility even during extrapolation. Meanwhile, an alternative approach based on standard architectures leads to stoichiometrically inconsistent solutions in 22% of the cases analyzed. In the second case study, we demonstrate how FBA-Hyb effectively simulates unmeasured chemical species and discovers a metabolic shift in sulfate-limited regimes during bioprocessing. By providing a modular, biologically consistent, and computationally efficient architecture, FBA-Hyb offers a robust foundation for the next generation of bioprocess models and sustainable process optimization.

papers.title: Transgenerational pathogen defence extends beyond behavioural avoidance
papers.abstract: Transgenerational plasticity can prepare descendants for environmental stress, but its generality and adaptive value remain unclear. Here we tested for adaptive transgenerational effects of exposure to the bacterial pathogen Pseudomonas vranovensis across five Caenorhabditis species. Pathogen exposure reduced rate-sensitive fitness in all five species, but behavioural responses varied across species and generations. In C. elegans, exposed parents and their F2 descendants showed increased pathogen avoidance. In C. remanei, pathogen exposure increased attraction in females, whereas their F2 female descendants showed greater avoidance. We found no F2 behavioural response in C. kamaaina, C. tropicalis or C. briggsae. Remarkably, however, ancestral exposure increased F2 larval survival on the pathogen in C. elegans, C. remanei and C. tropicalis. In C. tropicalis this survival benefit occurred without behavioural avoidance. The two species showing transgenerational avoidance had the closest sequence matches between the bacterial small RNA Pv1 and its candidate neuronal target maco-1, suggesting a possible molecular basis for variation in the response. Our results show that shared susceptibility to a pathogen does not imply similarity in transgenerational response, and that ancestral exposure can benefit descendants without inheritance of pathogen avoidance.

papers.title: Assessing nonlinear associations between body mass index and brain microstructure across adolescence in the ABCD Study
papers.abstract: Importance: Adolescent body mass index (BMI) is linked to brain microstructural alterations, but it is not known if this association is uniform across the BMI range. Objective: To characterize the shape of the association between adolescent BMI and brain microstructure across the BMI range. Design: Baseline, and 2-, 4-, and 6-year follow-up brain imaging and BMI from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive DevelopmentSM Study, analyzed between June 2025 and June 2026. Setting: Multicenter, population-based study including 21 sites distributed across the US. Participants: 10,361 adolescents (5,034 [48.5%] female; aged 9-18 years) from this population-based cohort study were included after quality control of complete data. Exposures: Centers for Disease Control BMI extended percentiles and percent from median BMI. Main Outcome and Measure: The primary outcome was the restricted normalized isotropic (RNI) signal fraction derived from diffusion imaging which indexes water confined within spherical cellular structures and is sensitive to microstructural properties including cellularity. Results: A total of 10,361 participants (5,034 [48.5%] female; aged 9-18 years) contributed 21,629 imaging observations across four timepoints. Higher BMI percentile was associated with greater RNI in bilateral reward- and appetite-related subcortical gray matter and white matter tracts, with effects varying spatially within structures, and with generally greater magnitude in males. Across these structures, the association increased steeply above the 80th percentile. This acceleration reflected compression of the percentile scale at high BMI; when BMI was reparameterized as percent from median, the association with RNI was approximately linear. Conclusions and Relevance: Our results suggest that BMI is associated with brain microstructure in a graded manner within white matter tracts and subcortical gray matter related to reward, executive function, and appetitive control. This indicates that the effect of BMI on microstructure is not confined to weight extremes and should be accounted for when modeling brain-body-behavior relationships during adolescence.

papers.title: Single-cell spatiotemporal transcriptomics reveals the origin, cellular heterogeneity and regulatory network of seed fiber cells in poplar
papers.abstract: Poplar (Populus spp.) is globally important for timber and afforestation, and is also a model system for woody perennials. However, the molecular control of reproductive organ development, particularly that of the epidermal trichomes on seeds known as seed fibers (fluff), which cause environmental and health concerns, remains poorly understood. Here, integrating single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) with spatial transcriptomics, we constructed a spatiotemporal atlas of female poplar capsules that resolves the cellular composition of the organ and positions each cell type within its native tissue context. We traced the developmental trajectory of seed fibers, showing that they originate from placenta epidermal cells, and identified three functionally distinct fiber cell subtypes involved in initiation, photosynthesis and elongation. Network analysis identified candidate regulators including PtoPDF2, PtoMYB38 and PtoHDG11. PtoPDF2 activates PtoMYB38 and PtoSTK2 by binding L1-box motifs in their promoters, revealing a module that governs seed fiber initiation. Together, our study provides a framework for seed fiber development in poplar and candidate targets for breeding low-fluff cultivars.

papers.title: HERCULES: a deep-learning framework for RNA-binding region localization and mutation-effect prediction
papers.abstract: RNA-binding proteins regulate essential steps of RNA metabolism, yet identifying RNA-interacting regions and prioritizing sequence variants that alter binding remain challenging from protein sequence alone. Here we present catRAPID signature 2.0 HERCULES (Hybrid framEwoRk for RNA-binding domain loCalization and mUtation anaLysis using physicochemical and languagE modelS), an approach combining a fine-tuned ProteinBERT model with residue-level physicochemical descriptors to predict global RNA-binding propensity, localize interaction sites and estimate the impact of amino acid substitutions. The language model captures domain-scale sequence context, whereas the physicochemical module provides sensitivity to local residue changes. On an independent benchmark, HERCULES discriminates RBPs from non-RBPs with an AUROC of 0.86. At residue resolution, it enriches high-scoring positions within annotated interaction regions across canonical, non-canonical and putative domain classes, while maintaining strong performance on an independent InterPro benchmark. Protein microarray experiments using disease-associated repeat RNAs (CGG, CAG and interrupted CAACAG repeats) independently support multiple non-catalogued candidate RBPs prioritized by HERCULES. Using curated UniProt variants associated with impaired RNA binding, HERCULES also prioritizes deleterious substitutions from predicted changes in binding propensity. By integrating protein-level classification, residue localization, variant-effect prediction and experimental validation, HERCULES provides an interpretable framework for prioritizing RNA-binding proteins, interaction regions and mutation-sensitive sites. HERCULES is freely available at https://tools.tartaglialab.com/hercules and as an open-source Python package at https://github.com/tartaglialabIIT/hercules.git.

papers.title: Early clonal dominance at priming sets the trajectory for broad HIV serum neutralization
papers.abstract: Germline-targeting vaccines aim to elicit HIV-1 broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs), but determinants of serum bnAb induction remain unclear. We previously showed that Q23-APEX-GT2 primes diverse V2-apex bnAb precursors in outbred rhesus macaques (RMs). To assess their maturation into authentic bnAbs, we infected immunized RMs with CAP256.SU SHIV. Four of six developed heterologous serum neutralization breadth, with one neutralizing ~70% of viruses tested. Early autologous neutralization and B-cell priming efficiency post-prime correlated with post-infection breadth. Longitudinal lineage tracing in lymph-nodes and blood revealed that recruitment and expansion of diverse long-CDRH3 V2-apex B-cell precursors, followed by early dominance of one or two clones, predicted serum breadth. Structural analyses showed that non-neutralizing lineages failed despite cross-reactive Env binding, owing to unfavorable V2-apex approach angles and limited glycan engagement. Together, these findings identify priming efficiency and early clonal dominance as key determinants of serum bnAb induction and provide a framework for HIV vaccine design.

papers.title: Ribosome-Associated GTPase Drg1 Links Cytosolic Translation to Mitochondrial Homeostasis
papers.abstract: Coordination of the functionalities among key organelles is essential for maintaining the complexity and adaptability of the eukaryotic cell. Functionally versatile proteins, such as GTPases, often assume important roles in this process. A ribosome-binding GTPase called Developmentally-regulated GTP-binding (Drg) protein is a conserved family of GTPases that promotes protein synthesis and regulates cytoskeletal dynamics, suggesting their importance for cell growth and proliferation. Mitochondrial proteostasis requires coordination between cytosolic translation and the targeting, import, and assembly of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial proteins. However, the ribosome-associated factors that support this coordination remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify the conserved GTPase Drg1, one of the two Drg paralogues in eukaryotic cells, as a translation factor required for mitochondrial homeostasis and cellular fitness. Human Drg1 and its cofactor Dfrp1 are associated with translating ribosomes and co-sedimented with polysomes. Deletion of Drg1 in HEK293T cells caused altered mitochondrial architecture, reduced mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP production, and impaired expression of a mitochondrially targeted reporter. Re-expression of wild-type Drg1 restored ATP production and reporter expression, whereas a GTPase-deficient Drg1 mutant failed to provide comparable rescue in ATP production, demonstrating that Drg1 catalytic activity is required for its cellular function. Mitochondria-directed APEX2 proximity proteomics further connected Drg1-dependent translation to proteins involved in mitochondrial protein import, respiratory-chain function, and mitochondrial protein synthesis. Reporter analyses indicated that Drg1 loss preferentially compromises productive translation toward the 3' region of the coding sequence. Together, these findings establish Drg1 as a ribosome-associated translation factor that supports the synthesis and homeostasis of proteins required for mitochondrial function. At the molecular level, loss of cellular homeostasis that is caused by compromised translation of cytoplasmically synthesized proteins functionally related to mitochondria underpins the observed phenomenon. Our results reveal a previously underappreciated connection between the cytosolic translation machinery and mitochondrial maintenance and provide a framework for understanding how defects in a conserved translational GTPase impair cellular energy metabolism and physiology.

papers.title: EzrA coordinates septal organization and nucleoid occlusion in Staphylococcus aureus
papers.abstract: Envelope biogenesis in Staphylococcus aureus is concentrated at the septum and encompasses peptidoglycan synthesis, teichoic acid production, and the targeted secretion and anchoring of YSIRK/GXXS signal peptide-bearing surface proteins. How S. aureus spatially restricts these processes to the dividing crosswall remains unclear. EzrA is a membrane-anchored protein structurally related to eukaryotic spectrins that has been implicated in linking cell division to envelope synthesis, yet its precise contribution remains undefined. Here, we show that EzrA spatially couples peptidoglycan synthesis with the surface display of septal proteins. In ezrA null cells, newly synthesized peptidoglycan is incorporated in a dispersed pattern rather than confined to the septum, teichoic acid synthesis is increased, and surface protein display is elevated. In wild-type cells, nascent peptidoglycan and nascent Staphylococcal protein A anchoring sites colocalize at the septum; this spatial coupling is lost in the absence of EzrA. ezrA null cells also exhibit impaired nucleoid occlusion, with septal ingression over the chromosome leading to chromosome guillotining. Together, these findings suggest that EzrA constitutes a spatial organizing system at the septum, coordinating multiple envelope biogenesis processes while linking septal organization to nucleoid occlusion, a parallel spatial positioning system, to ensure faithful chromosome segregation and cytokinesis.

papers.title: Natural scene segmentation dynamics reveal iterative Bayesian inference
papers.abstract: The visual system operates by segmenting visual inputs into distinct perceptual objects. Segmentation is dynamic, as revealed by the tempo of perceptual choices and neural activity in the visual cortex. Dynamics for natural stimuli however, are poorly understood because natural scene segmentation is ambiguous and subjective. We measured subjective human segmentation maps for natural images using an innovative paradigm, and uncovered richer spatiotemporal dynamics than predicted by current theories of segmentation. To explain these dynamics, we introduced Iterative Bayesian Inference algorithms for segmentation that iteratively integrate visual inputs with the prior expectation for local smoothness. When visual inputs were consistent with such a spatial prior, iterative inference was faster. Such a predicted relationship between spatial prior and inferential dynamics was evident in our data and correctly reflected each individual participant's spatial biases. We conclude that iterative Bayesian inference sets the tempo for a fundamental function of natural vision.

papers.title: Molecular basis of mitogen-activated protein kinase ERK2 activation by its upstream kinase MEK1
papers.abstract: The RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway relays extracellular signals into a cellular response and its dysregulation leads to many pathologies, particularly cancer. Much is known about the individual components of the pathway, however, details of their interactions and how specificity is maintained is still poorly understood. Here, we determined cryo-EM structures of the MAP2K MEK1 activating its substrate MAPK ERK2, the final event in the cascade. We define the molecular details of specificity and activation of ERK2 and examine the mechanism of substrate recognition using solution techniques and molecular dynamics. Binding of the substrate MAPK leads to release of the MAP2K catalytic machinery, a mechanism enhanced in many gain of function disease mutations. Further, we observe that ERK2 release is not required for nucleotide exchange, suggesting how a processive mechanism could proceed. Our data advance the understanding of MAPK signalling specificity and provide a starting point for drug development.

papers.title: Memory erasure by dopamine-gated retrospective learning
papers.abstract: Erasing outdated memories is crucial for adaptive behavior. Yet once a cue-outcome association is learned, repeated cue exposure without outcome suppresses conditioned behavior without erasing the underlying memory. This allows rapid behavioral recovery when outcomes are reintroduced. Here, we confirm this limitation for standard prospective extinction protocols that present cues without the associated outcome, but show that true memory erasure is achieved by inverting the paradigm: presenting outcomes without associated cues, i.e., retrospective extinction. We demonstrate that orbitofrontal cortex activity at outcome is necessary for the rapid behavioral recovery following prospective extinction, and that mesolimbic dopamine activity at outcome is necessary for retrospective extinction. These findings reconceptualize extinction mechanisms and suggest complementary strategies to mitigate relapse and erase maladaptive memories.

papers.title: Co-evolutionary dynamics of defense systems and anti-defense genes in chromosomes and mobile genetic elements of Enterobacteriaceae
papers.abstract: Bacterial defense systems undergo rapid evolutionary changes, yet the specific contributions of the genomic compartment (chromosomal versus mobile genetic element [MGE]) to these dynamics remain unclear. We analyzed 6,907 genomes from 213 species of Enterobacteriaceae using a phylogenetic birth-death model to quantify gain, loss, expansion, and reduction of defense (DEF) and anti-defense (anti-DEF) gene families. We found that DEF turnover differs from the background dynamics of the genomic elements that carry them. Direct comparisons among DEFs further revealed differences in loss and copy-number dynamics across genomic compartments, with the highest rates on chromosomes, intermediate rates on plasmids and ICEs/IMEs, and the lowest rates on prophages, whereas the relative balance between gain and loss and between expansion and reduction remained similar across chromosomes and MGEs. MGE-associated anti-DEFs showed higher loss, expansion, and reduction rates than DEFs, whereas chromosome-associated anti-DEFs showed lower gain rates than DEFs. Finally, we found that gains and losses of DEFs and anti-DEFs were positively correlated across bacterial lineages, with positive associations observed for both matching (that is, antagonistic) and non-matching pairs. Together, these results show that genomic background affects the overall flux of DEFs and anti-DEFs, and that turnover of DEFs and anti-DEFs is evolutionarily coupled across lineages.

papers.title: Asymmetrical Glyco-Engineering of Monoclonal Antibodies Provides Insights into α-Gal Immunogenicity
papers.abstract: Glycosylation heterogeneity of therapeutic monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) necessitates precise glycoengineering to optimize effector functions, such as those mediated by Fcgamma-receptors (FcgammaRs). However, current enzymatic remodeling methods are limited in scope, producing only a narrow spectrum of glycoforms and unable to achieve complete control over defined asymmetrical structures. Here, we report a multi-step, fully enzymatic platform for the solution-phase synthesis of a comprehensive library of biantennary mAb glycoforms, offering complete control over the alpha1,3- and alpha1,6-mannose arm architecture. This strategy uses a single domain of the beta-N-acetylglucosaminidase StrH (GH20-2) to achieve regioselective hydrolysis of the GlcNAc residue on the alpha1,3-mannose arm of the intact antibody, thereby introducing asymmetry. Next, the remaining terminal GlcNAc residue at the alpha1,6-antenna can be enzymatically extended with a beta1,4-galactoside and sialoside or alpha1,3-galactoside. Remarkably, after this extension, recombinant GnT-I can reintroduce the GlcNAc at the alpha1,3-mannosyl antenna, allowing precise control over glycan branching and composition. This robust, two-stage enzymatic remodeling methodology, demonstrated on infliximab and cetuximab, unlocks a broad chemical space of biantennary Fc glycans for comprehensive functional studies. We employed these well-defined glycovariants to determine the minimum structural requirements for anti-alpha-Gal IgE binding and to systematically evaluate binding affinities toward FcgammaRs, providing new insights for the rational design of next-generation immune-therapeutics.

papers.title: Proteomic analysis in Alzheimer's disease with psychosis reveals a shared AD proteomic landscape and a separate molecular signature of postsynaptic density disruption
papers.abstract: Background and Hypothesis: Alzheimer's disease with psychosis (AD+P) is a subgroup of AD patients with more rapid cognitive deterioration. While our previous study showed that AD+P is associated with loss of prefrontal cortex postsynaptic density (PSD) proteins, identifying proteins in the broader cellular environment that influence PSD loss addresses a critical knowledge gap about synaptic dysfunction mechanisms in early disease stages. Study Design: We conducted a proteomic analysis comparing prefrontal grey matter cortex tissue homogenates from elderly normal controls (n=18), individuals with AD+P (n=61), and individuals with AD-P (n=48). Study Results: AD+P showed the most pronounced alterations relative to controls (178 proteins with q<0.05), although alterations in AD-P and AD+P relative to controls were highly similar (R2=0.965, p<0.001). Weighted-gene correlation network analysis (WGCNA) identified four modules significantly associated with disease status comparing AD subjects to controls, but none differed significantly between AD+P and AD-P. We identified 15 proteins significantly correlated with PSD yield across all samples, including ENPP6, linked to AD+P by GWAS. Additionally, PSD yield-associated proteins showed minimal overlap with altered AD proteins (1 of 137). Proteins negatively correlated with PSD yield were enriched for presynaptic endocytosis, whereas the one WGCNA module significantly correlated with PSD yield was enriched for inflammatory terms. Conclusions: Our findings suggest a model in which AD+P arises from the combination of quantitative alterations within a shared AD proteome profile and a superimposed set of protein alterations correlated with PSD yield that confer distinct mechanisms of synaptic vulnerability and psychosis risk.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN: Omnidirectional 3D Printing of Anisotropic Nanofibrous Peptide Hydrogels
papers.abstract: The authors have withdrawn this manuscript because the work has since been expanded with substantial new data and reorganized into two separate manuscripts, each with a revised author list. Therefore, the authors do not wish this work to be cited as reference for the project. If you have any questions, please contact the corresponding author.

papers.title: Ancestral tributyltin exposure produces male-specific brown adipose thermogenic dysregulatoin
papers.abstract: Obesity is a global health challenge increasingly linked to environmental obesogens. Tributyltin (TBT), a model obesogen that activates PPARgamma and RXR, promotes transgenerational obesity in mice, but whether developmental and ancestral exposure impairs energy balance remains unclear. Brown adipose tissue (BAT) contributes to energy expenditure and thermoregulation through UCP1-dependent and -independent pathways. We tested whether TBT exposure disrupts BAT function in F1 and F3 descendants of exposed F0 dams. We measured body composition before and after high-fat diet (HFD) challenge and assessed resting core body temperature, BAT gene expression, mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) content, and mitochondrial electron transport chain (ETC) capacity. TBT-line males accumulated more fat after HFD without changes in lean mass despite similar mass-scaled food intake. Before HFD, core body temperature was lower in F1 and F3 TBT-line males, indicating impaired thermal homeostasis before increased adiposity. Candidate-gene qPCR did not show uniform suppression of thermogenic genes; instead, Ucp1 mRNA increased while Ucp2 mRNA decreased in F1 males, indicating dysregulation. Transcriptomal profiling revealed altered thermogenic signaling and consistent downregulation of mitochondrial electron transport chain genes across F1 and F3 males. Relative mtDNA content was unchanged, whereas complex-specific respirometry revealed reduced complex I- and II-associated respiratory capacity, providing evidence of impaired electron transport. No consistent effects occurred in females. These findings identified an early, male-associated BAT phenotype characterized by thermogenic dysregulation, reduced mitochondrial ETC capacity, and impaired thermal homeostasis. They support a model in which impaired BAT mitochondrial function contributes to later susceptibility to diet-induced obesity.

papers.title: Structural Definition of Neutralizing Epitopes within and around the HKU1 Receptor-binding Site Reveals Cell Context-Dependent Neutralization
papers.abstract: Endemic human coronaviruses (HCoVs), such as HCoV-HKU1, account for ~30% of common colds each year and can cause serious upper and lower respiratory infections, yet no licensed vaccines or therapeutic antibodies target HCoVs. Despite being endemic to the human population, little is known about the antigenic landscape of HCoV-HKU1. Here, we characterized key interactions between the HCoV-HKU1 spike (S) protein and monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) isolated from convalescent HCoV-HKU-1-positive peripheral blood mononuclear cells collected prior to the COVID-19 pandemic. We isolated 14 mAbs that bound distinct regions of S, including the receptor-binding domain (RBD), N-terminal domain, and S2 subunit. Structural and functional studies revealed three groups of RBD-specific mAbs targeting diverse footprints within and around the TMPRSS2 receptor-binding site: (1) H501-022, which recognizes the TMPRSS2-binding site and thereby blocks receptor engagement; (2) H501-008, which binds a distinct epitope outside the TMPRSS2-binding site that is shared with HCoV-OC43; and (3) H501-018, which recognizes both up and down RBD conformations at a distinct, non-overlapping epitope outside the TMPRSS2-binding site. H501-008 weakly neutralized live HCoV-OC43 in vitro and protected mice against lethal HCoV-OC43 challenge. Notably, the three RBD-specific mAbs potently neutralized HCoV-HKU1 pseudovirus in TMPRSS2-overexpressing cell lines, but exhibited limited neutralizing activity against authentic HCoV-HKU1 infection in primary human airway epithelial cells. Together, these findings structurally define the antigenic landscape within and around the HKU1 receptor-binding site and demonstrate that receptor-binding site recognition alone is insufficient to predict physiologically relevant antibody-mediated neutralization.

papers.title: Keeping an Eye on Plasticity Genes: Insulin/TOR Pathway Components Mediating Nutritional Plasticity of Eyes Within and Between Sex
papers.abstract: The eyes of insects exhibit extreme morphological variation through changes in size and shape.
