Outcome(s): Differentiation of B cell subsets involved in IgAN and production of IgA, Gd-IgA1, and IgG. Analytical Approach: Flow cytometry, ELISA, cytometric bead array, and Western blotting. Results: Mucosal cytokine stimulation induced robust differentiation of B cells into CD38high plasmablasts and CD138high plasma cells, with a disproportionate expansion of Gd-IgA1 populations in IgAN. Compared with controls, PBMCs from IgAN patients demonstrated markedly increased production of Gd-IgA1, predominantly in polymeric form and strongly enriched for {lambda} light chains (~90% vs ~51%). This response was accompanied by selective expansion of Gd-IgA1{lambda} plasma cells, identifying a disease-specific, highly responsive B cell compartment. Limitations: The cytokine combination was selected to reflect key signals present in mucosal immune environments, although in vivo conditions are more complex. Conclusions: Mucosal cytokine signals directly amplify pathogenic B cell responses in IgAN, driving production of polymeric, {lambda}-enriched Gd-IgA1. These findings provide mechanistic validation for therapies targeting the mucosal-systemic axis and offer a biologic explanation for the clinical efficacy of gut-directed corticosteroids and BAFF/APRIL inhibition.

papers.title: JOINT ACTION AWARENESS IN MACAQUES DURING A MULTIPLAYER VIDEO-GAME CONTEXT
papers.abstract: In behavioral neuroscience, research in nonhuman primates often relies on video game like paradigms, including studies of social interaction and joint action. In social studies, establishing whether animals monitor their partner and are aware of their reciprocal interactions in these abstract laboratory settings is essential for interpreting the processes underlying cooperative performance. Here, we examined spontaneous head orienting behavior in two macaques performing a cooperative visuomotor task under highly controlled conditions. The animals sat side by side with their heads unrestrained and used isometric joysticks to control their respective cursors displayed on a shared screen. Depending on trial instructions, they performed either individual actions (SOLO action, SA) or joint actions (JA) to obtain a reward. We quantified spontaneous head rotations toward the partner as an ethologically relevant behavioral indicator of social monitoring. Partner directed head turns occurred more frequently during JA than during SA trials. Crucially, their rate increased with the number of errors made by the partner during JA trials. Together, these findings indicate that macaques monitor their partner during abstract, computer-mediated cooperative interactions and that this monitoring is driven by the performance of the partner. Such spontaneous, context specific orienting toward the partner supports the interpretation that macaques are aware of their dyadic engagement, even in video game like settings. Our results therefore highlight the suitability of controlled visuomotor paradigms for investigating the cognitive-motor processes underlying joint action in nonhuman primates.

papers.title: An open-source, 3D-printable droplet microfluidics platform with strobe-enhanced microscopy
papers.abstract: Droplet microfluidics underpins many single-cell, precision biomedical, and nanomaterial techniques. However, implementing these methods reproducibly remains challenging outside specialised laboratories due to high equipment costs, operational inflexibility, mechanical impracticality at the microscope stage, as well as open-source pumping solutions that are inadequately validated for low-flow stability. We present an accessible, research-grade, open-source droplet microfluidics platform integrating a compact, microfluidics-optimised microscopy stage with networked syringe-pump control. Designed for local digital fabrication, primarily 3D printing, and widely available components, the platform supports reproducible builds across diverse settings. This setup enables stable droplet generation, observation of rapid droplet dynamics, and automation-ready networked workflows. The microscopy module uses a Raspberry Pi camera and microsecond stroboscopic illumination to capture sharp images of fast-moving droplets without the need for a high-speed camera. A modular hardware interface and extensible, web-accessible software stack provide a path to integrate additional modules and laboratory automation beyond the configuration evaluated here. For infusion, we introduce an open-source syringe pump optimised for low reliable flow rather than maximum rates, combining gearbox-assisted stepper mechanics with workflow-centric control that enables manual intervention (keypad control) and remote operation (web interface and automation hooks). We benchmark droplet regimes, size tuning, and time-stability under low-flow conditions (between 25 and 2500 uL/h) relevant to advanced assays and demonstrate biomedical readiness through the encapsulation and incubation of cells, beads, and bacteria in monodisperse droplets. The platform has been replicated across laboratories in Latin America and globally, including independent builds, supporting reproducibility. All design files, firmware/software, analysis notebooks, and benchmark datasets are openly released.

papers.title: Semaglutide Increases Striatal Leptin Sensitivity, Impacting Dopaminergic Response to Cocaine
papers.abstract: There is accumulating evidence that the GLP-1 analog, semaglutide, might effectively curb intake of cocaine via brain dopaminergic functioning, despite limited brain penetrance. However, there is currently no established mechanism elucidating how chronic semaglutide treatment regulates the dopaminergic response to cocaine. Cocaine is a highly addictive substance that produces rewarding effects primarily through antagonism of the dopamine transporter (DAT). Therapeutics for cocaine use disorder (CUD) have long targeted DAT in the hope of reducing cocaine intake. Metabolic hormones such as leptin and insulin have been shown to influence DAT, and for that reason have been explored for the regulation of cocaine reward and behavior. Interestingly, while semaglutide does not penetrate the brain, it does peripherally modulate metabolic hormones that enter the brain. Through fast-scan cyclic voltammetry and behavioral experimentation, we examined the effects of chronic semaglutide treatment on dopamine signaling, cocaine-induced dopamine release, and locomotor sensitivity. We determined that chronic semaglutide inhibits dopaminergic reward induced by cocaine. Surprisingly, semaglutides effects on cocaine reward were blunted in mice fasted overnight, suggesting a mechanistic dependence on metabolic hormones. Semaglutide administration generated significant reductions in fasting blood leptin, as well as enhanced striatal leptin sensitivity compared to vehicle controls. Preceding cocaine exposure, application of leptin to fasted mice restored semaglutides regulation of cocaine. Our results exhibit a potential mechanism for semaglutide-induced cocaine reward inhibition, emphasizing the potential of central leptin signaling as a therapeutic target for CUD.

papers.title: Early Insulin Signaling Defects and Oxidative Stress Kinase Activation Precede Tau Pathology in PS19 Tau Transgenic Mice
papers.abstract: Pathological tau accumulation is a hallmark of Alzheimers disease (AD), yet its relationship with impaired insulin signaling remains unclear. Previously, we reported altered IRS1 phosphorylation reduced p IR beta, and GLUT3 expression in young AD transgenic mice prior to overt pathology. Here, we investigated insulin signaling and oxidative stress pathways in the Tau P301S (PS19) mouse model. We found that alterations in phospho IRS1, phospho IR beta, and the glucose transporters GLUT3 and GLUT4 occur before pathogenic tau deposition. In stable tau expressing human neuronal cell lines, tau expression was similarly associated with impaired insulin signaling. Concurrent dysregulation of insulin signaling and activation of oxidative stress responsive kinases, accompanied by increased microglial abundance, were evident in 2 month old PS19 mice and persisted into adulthood. Together, these findings demonstrate that insulin signaling abnormalities and oxidative stress kinase activation are early and sustained features of PS19 tauopathy, preceding the onset of overt neuropathology.

papers.title: Novel retinoic acid receptor-related orphan receptor gamma inverse agonist enhances checkpoint blockade in hepatocellular carcinoma: a preclinical mouse study
papers.abstract: Background and Aims: Neutrophil-associated inflammation is associated with poor outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but tumour-intrinsic regulators of neutrophil recruitment and checkpoint response remain unclear. We evaluated whether inhibiting retinoic acid receptor-related orphan receptor gamma (RORgamma) alters neutrophil recruitment, programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression, and response to PD-L1 blockade. Approach and Results: Survival associations were analysed in The Cancer Genome Atlas HCC cohort. Neutrophil migration toward HCC cells and PD-L1 expression were assessed after RORC silencing or TF-S10 treatment. Immunocompetent mice bearing orthotopic Hep-55.1c tumours received vehicle, TF-S10, anti-PD-L1, or combination treatment. Higher S100A9 and CXCL8 expression was associated with shorter survival (P = 0.000459 and P = 0.0004413, respectively), and tumour-bearing mice had higher neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratios (P < 0.0001). RORgamma targeting reduced neutrophil migration and intratumoural Ly6G+; infiltration while increasing tumour-cell PD-L1 expression in vitro. Combination treatment reduced endpoint liver tumour volume versus anti-PD-L1 monotherapy (P < 0.01). Half of combination-treated mice had tumour volumes less than or equal to 0.10 cm^3 and none exceeded 1.00 cm^3, compared with 62% of controls exceeding 1.00 cm^3. Histologically, 85% of combination-treated mice had less than or equal to 10% liver tumour involvement, versus no controls. Combination treatment also reduced tumour-associated neutrophil populations and peripheral neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratios. All active treatments reduced pulmonary metastatic burden versus controls, without significant differences among treatment groups; 53% of combination-treated mice had no detectable lung metastases. Conclusions: RORgamma inhibition reduces neutrophil recruitment and increases tumour-cell PD-L1 expression. Combined RORgamma inhibition and PD-L1 blockade improves hepatic tumour control in preclinical HCC and warrants further investigation.

papers.title: Joining Two Perspectives of the Proteome with the Trypsin+HTA Protease Workflow
papers.abstract: Proteolysis can be completed in a single-step, rapid (5-30 minutes) reaction using hyperthermoacidic archaeal (HTA) proteases. Protocol simplicity and stability of HTA proteases in ambient storage conditions removes many logistical barriers to widespread deployment of proteomic analysis. HTA protease cleavage selectivity is complex but quantitatively reproducible and generates peptides that negligibly overlap with trypsin. Tryptic and HTA protease peptides emphasize different proteins and provide complementary coverage of amino acid sequence and post-translational modification (PTM) sites. Digestion of a sample's separate aliquot with HTA protease is a minor addition to trypsin-based workflows, but LC-MS analysis of both sets of peptides is not practical for large cohorts. This manuscript evaluates the identifications and reproducibility of LC-MS analysis of tryptic and HTA protease peptide mixtures. Adding HTA protease peptides to 20% increased total protein identifications by 24% on average in neat plasma and identified 216 additional biologically interesting modifications compared to conventional trypsin-only bottom-up proteomic analysis. This approach is reproducible and does not increase sample preparation or analysis time. Peptides from each protease present independent opportunities to quantify overlapping proteins and a quantification model was developed in which, for each protein, the most complete protease data is selected for primary quantitation and data from the second protease is used to infer missing values. This cross-protease inference is more accurate than minimum, mean, or nearest neighbor imputations. Finally, biomarkers discovered through HTA protease peptides are amenable to rapid HTA protease only proteomic workflows thus streamlining translation from discovery to fieldable applications.

papers.title: Maternal repression of imprinted genes in endosperm by gene body demethylation
papers.abstract: Removal of TE-like DNA methylation from regulatory elements drives canonical genomic imprinting of both maternally and paternally expressed genes in endosperm (MEGs and PEGs). In both cases, the maternal copies are demethylated, allowing binding of either activating or repressing factors. Here we report that removal of CG-only gene body methylation also drives imprinting, resulting in maternally repressed PEGs as the most common form of imprinting in maize. These body methylated PEGs express broadly across tissues and lack H3K27me3 except in endosperm, where maternal copies acquire it in domains extending through and beyond genes. We also found that partial gene body demethylation is widespread in endosperm, usually does not result in imprinted expression, and is mediated by DNA glycosylases/lyases (DNGs). These and other data indicate that gene body methylation can shield select genes from PRC2 repression, and its maternal removal by DNGs explains the majority of PEGs in both maize and rice but has a weak impact in Arabidopsis thaliana. We hypothesize that increased gene expression noise arising from gene body demethylation--both with and without imprinting--is beneficial in endosperm.

papers.title: Thermodynamic, Electrochemical and Practical Constraints on Electromicrobial Formate Assimilation
papers.abstract: Electromicrobial production (EMP) technologies aim to combine renewable electricity, CO2, and engineered microbes to make energy-dense molecules at efficiencies exceeding photosynthesis. CO2 can be electrochemically reduced to formate, which is far easier to handle at the bench than H2 or an electrode, but formate carries only two electrons per carbon against the six in a biofuel. The remaining electrons must come from oxidizing additional formate, from H2 oxidation, or from extracellular electron uptake (EEU), and no rigorous comparison of these options coupled to the choice of carbon assimilation pathway currently exists. We calculate upper-limit efficiencies for butanol production by six carbon assimilation pathways, each paired with all three electron delivery mechanisms, using electrochemical parameters drawn from a survey of the recent literature. Electrical to butanol energy conversion efficiencies range from 35.5 to 51.7%, corresponding to solar-to-fuel efficiencies of 11.7 to 17%, so even the least efficient route exceeds the 8% theoretical ceiling of algal photosynthesis. The serine variant of the reductive glycine pathway reaches an electrical energy conversion efficiency of when using H2 oxidation, within 1.9 points of the most efficient pathway, and is the only high-efficiency option that tolerates O2. This makes an EMP system that combines electron delivery by formate coupled with the serine variant of reductive glycine pathway highly attractive, as it presents few barriers to rapid, iterative engineering in the lab, and a high theoretical ceiling. Drawing both carbon and electrons from formate costs 6.2 points against H2 at a state-of-the-art whole-cell voltage (2.2 V). However, this small penalty is amplified three-fold by any rise in the CO2-to-formate cell voltage, and reaches 13.5 points at the highest whole-cell voltages reported for scaled-up CO2-to-formate electrolyzers, where formate-only operation falls to 11.2 electrical-to-fuel and 3.7% solar-to-fuel efficiency, below the ceiling of photosynthesis, against 24.7 and 8.1% for H2 (only just above algal photosynthesis). Our choice between a formate-only system and one coupled to H2 oxidation or EEU therefore depends on our belief about the trajectory of CO2 reduction technology. If whole-cell voltages continue to fall at the rate of the past decade, formate alone is the right target, and the simplicity of its workflow is bought at low cost. However, if that improvement plateaus, the electron delivery mechanism must be swappable, and a system should be designed from the outset so that it can be. At the US Department of Energy SunShot target of 2 cents per kilowatt hour, the electricity to make a US gallon of butanol costs $1.40 for a formate-only system at the state of the art, rising to $5.45 at the highest scaled-up electrolyzer voltage reported, against $1.23 and $2.47 for formate and H2 system.

papers.title: Pruning the Search, Not the Signal: Adaptive-Banding Needleman-Wunsch Sequence Alignment via Protein Language Model Confidence
papers.abstract: Dynamic programming (DP) yields exact quadratic-time (O(NM)) pairwise sequence alignments. Static banding heuristics (O(NW)) fail catastrophically on low-identity (<30%), asymmetric insertions/deletions (indels), or extreme length ratios, dropping core-block Sum-of-Pairs (SP) score recovery to 20%-50%. Conversely, recent protein language model (PLM) aligners evaluate all N x M cells without search grid constraints. To bridge this gap, we introduce Adaptive-Banding Needleman-Wunsch (AB-NW), pruning the search space without sacrificing sequence alignment signal by leveraging PLM contextual representations to construct a confidence-adaptive DP corridor prior to fine-resolution DP while keeping downstream scoring unmodified. AB-NW downsamples residue embeddings, computes a coarse alignment, and sets per-row corridor bounds via normalized confidence metrics. Evaluated via JIT-compiled buffers, this reduces time complexity to O(NW_bar) and space to O(NW_max), where W_bar << M. Benchmarked across three PLM backbones (ESM2-8M, ESM2-35M, ProtBERT) across nine structural challenge categories, AB-NW recovers >98.9% of exact unconstrained alignment scores and core-block SP accuracy across static banding failure modes (Twilight Zone, Asymmetric Indels, Extreme Aspect Ratios) while eliminating 55.3%-78.8% of active DP cells. On large protein sequence matrices (N, M >= 3,700), AB-NW eliminates 87.6%-91.7% of cells, achieving speedups of 9.79x-13.30x (pure DP) and 1.73x-2.94x (end-to-end), reaching up to 18.12x on unbiased controls (p < 0.05 to p < 10^-15), making AB-NW practical for large-scale, high-throughput sequence alignment pipelines.

papers.title: Multi-Peptide Prompting Enables In-Context Learning in Protein Language
papers.abstract: Protein language models (PLMs) are trained primarily on individual protein sequences, yet many peptide-discovery problems require inference from only a small number of labeled examples. Here, we show that single-sequence PLMs can perform in-context peptide learning without gradient updates, task-specific retraining, or architectural modification. We introduce multi-peptide example prompts (MPEPs), in which demonstration peptides are concatenated with glycine spacers and used as context for scoring query peptides by their prompted probability. We evaluate this approach across a synthetic pattern-completion task, secondary-structure classification, and MHC-II binder prediction using both encoder-only ESM-2 models and decoder-only ProGen2 models. Across tasks, performance improves with the number of peptide examples and with model scale, indicating that PLMs can extract shared sequence-level properties from prompted examples. We further introduce a difference score that contrasts positive-example and negative-example MPEPs, reducing compositional biases in raw PLM probabilities and substantially improving classification. On MHC-II binder prediction, MPEP-based classification with larger ESM-2 models matches or exceeds low-data classifiers trained on frozen ESM-2 embeddings, while requiring no training. These results reveal an unexpected in-context inference capability in single-sequence PLMs and establish MPEP conditioning as a lightweight strategy for low-data peptide classification.

papers.title: Fundamentals on the Kinetic and Thermodynamic Analysis of Oligonucleotide DNA Hybridization by Surface Plasmon Resonance: A Guide for HIF1α Antisense Design.
papers.abstract: Antisense oligonucleotides (ASO) are nucleotide polymers that hybridize to sense strands and have been successful in treating a variety of diseases. A wide range of strategies have been investigated to optimize and develop ASO for clinical studies. A key objective for this study was to provide an overview of the range of detailed data that can be obtained and provide an updated method review on how to design surface plasmon resonance (SPR) kinetic experiments for DNA oligonucleotide hybridization studies that can also be applied to other ASO including peptide nucleic acids (PNA). We describe many lessons learned from published literature and provide a state-of-the-art strategy and methods for generating not only kinetic but also thermodynamic characterizations of oligonucleotide hybridization. In this study we have performed an SPR kinetic and thermodynamic analysis for the hybridization of HIF1 antisense DNA strands to its immobilized Intron2-Exon3 splice site sense DNA strand to provide insight, in general, on the optimal length and insight into optimal design of DNA ASOs. We provide a process on how to design experiments to: 1.) obtain oligonucleotide-length dependent kinetics, 2.) analyze reactions to obtain association and dissociation rate kinetics (ka, kd), assess if hybridization follows a 2-state model and to obtain kinetic dissociation constants (Kd), 3.) perform temperature-dependent hybridization kinetics to obtain thermodynamic values ({Delta}H{degrees}, {Delta}S{degrees} and {Delta}G{degrees}) that can give insight into the molecular interactions driving hybridization, 4.) compare experimental thermodynamic values to values derived from nearest-neighbor prediction models to identify atypical reactions and importantly 5.) enable calculations to predict oligomer hybridization affinity at the physiological 37 {degrees}C temperature to assess if the design of the oligomer will have the required cellular activity for a therapeutic effect. The strategy and results presented throughout the paper are compared to previous SPR reports and suggestions made to optimize kinetic studies.

papers.title: Optimizing Oxylipin Analysis with Liquid Chromatography Mass Spectrometry through Bio-Inert Systems and Ion Funnel Adjustments
papers.abstract: Oxylipins are potent signaling lipids that affect inflammation, vascular tone, and metabolism, making them relevant in many diseases. Oxylipins are measured with liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS), but challenges in quantification arise due to low abundance and rapid degradation. In this study, we optimize LC-MS methods to improve the quantification of oxylipins in human plasma, given growing interest in oxylipins and their impact on clinical research. Plasma samples were obtained from healthy participants, and oxylipins were concentrated by solid-phase extraction. Quantification was performed with a reversed-phase targeted LC-MS/MS method on an Agilent 6495D triple quadrupole with transitions for 248 oxylipin species. Given the rapid degradation of oxylipins with bio-reactive surfaces, we compared both standard and bio-inert (Altura) columns, standard and bio-inert LC setups, and ion funnel voltage. By decreasing voltages applied to ions inside the ion funnel, signal was increased for most oxylipin species while peak quality was maintained. Fully bio-inert setups quantified more compounds and had increased levels of some compounds, but fewer epoxyoctadecadienoic acid (EpODE) species. To explore this further, analytical-grade alpha-linolenic acid (ALA), the direct precursor of EpODEs, was injected and observed to form EpODEs within the instrumentation when using stainless steel columns. These data suggest that oxylipins benefit from fully bio-inert systems and optimized pre-mass analyzer parameters. The stainless-steel components of the column may also contribute to epoxidation reactions of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), generating oxylipin species during analysis. Finally, various human sample matrices were assessed for compatibility with oxylipin quantification, including granulocytes, mononuclear cells, erythrocytes, skeletal muscle, and THP-1 cells, a human-derived monocyte cell line.

papers.title: From wings to tails: a general framework for inferring dispersal potential from morphology
papers.abstract: Dispersal shapes gene flow, range dynamics, and extinction risk, yet direct measures of dispersal are unavailable for most taxa. Here, we test whether the aspect ratio of propulsive surfaces, an established proxy in birds, provides a general morphological basis for inferring dispersal potential. Using sharks as a model taxa, we find caudal fin aspect ratio was positively associated with swimming speed and geographic range size. Applying this proxy across 452 species, we find no evidence of a latitudinal gradient in dispersal potential, in contrast to dispersal patterns reported for birds, due to the lack of a direct effect of environmental temperature on the geographic distribution of caudal fin aspect ratio. Higher dispersal potential was associated with pelagic habitats, larger body size and greater oxygen uptake capacity. Because aspect ratios can be measured from museum specimens and illustrations, this approach could enable comparisons of dispersal potential across air- and water-dwelling vertebrates.

papers.title: Aclarubicin disrupts RNA polymerase II progression at replication-coupled histone genes
papers.abstract: Anthracyclines are effective chemotherapeutic agents that cause DNA and chromatin damage. One member of the anthracyclines, aclarubicin, has gained therapeutic interest due to its ability to kill cancer cells through chromatin-based mechanisms, thus avoiding the off-target effects associated with DNA damage. However, the molecular mechanism of action leading to aclarubicin-induced chromatin damage remains elusive. Here we performed Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation (CUT&Tag) of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) and other transcriptional regulators in human cells followin aclarubicin treatment. We found that aclarubicin strongly disrupts the replication-coupled histone genes, resulting in a nonproductive accumulation of Pol II transcription machinery here beyond the levels at other genes. We attribute this sensitivity to the dense Pol II loading and rapid transcription of the histone genes, which intensify the chromatin-disrupting effects of aclarubicin. Together, our findings shed light on the mechanism of aclarubicin as an anticancer drug and point to the replication-coupled histone genes as a target for therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Dissociation between impaired explicit spatial remapping and preserved implicit neural dynamics in Alzheimers disease
papers.abstract: The hippocampus supports spatial memory by dynamically integrating external sensory inputs with intrinsic neural circuit dynamics during novel experience. In Alzheimer's disease (AD), despite impaired hippocampal spatial remapping, learning and memory-related hippocampal representations can remain partially preserved, a phenomenon consistent with cognitive resilience (Gomez-Isla and Frosch 2022, Jia, Xu et al. 2025). However, the hippocampal ensemble coding patterns associated with these preserved memory abilities remain remains unclear. We hypothesize that intrinsic temporal structures of neuronal firing continue to facilitate the encoding of new spatial information. Using the AppNL-G-F rat model, we recorded hippocampal CA1 activity across multiple days during a familiar-novel context alternating task. We found a dissociation between impaired explicit spatial coding and preserved implicit temporal coding in the AD hippocampal network. Explicit spatial coding was impaired, as place cells showed weak discrimination between distinct contexts and failed to exhibit improvement across days. In contrast, implicit temporal coding exhibited experience-dependent refinement, with cofiring dynamic becoming increasingly context-specific across long-term experience. Further analysis suggested that the enhancement of implicit cofiring may be associated with the increased consistency of neural ensemble reactivation during sharp wave ripples in awake rest. Taken together, these findings reveal an explicit-implicit dissociation in the AD hippocampal network, suggesting that the experience-dependent refinement of implicit temporal coding may support preserved learning-related hippocampal network dynamics despite impaired spatial remapping.

papers.title: Alternative management strategy influences litter microbiome dynamics in a commercial broiler rearing system
papers.abstract: Background: Pre-harvest litter management is a key determinant of broiler production conditions, influencing NH generation, nutrient retention, and microbial reservoirs that accumulate across production cycles. Conventional chemical and physical management strategies can support flock health, but their effects on bacterial populations are often transient and may not account for the microbial interactions that govern persistence, exclusion, and community succession. Here, we evaluated an alternative litter management strategy combining a postbiotic intervention with reduced-rate NaHSO across two broiler growouts, with litter sampled at the end of each flock to determine effects on prokaryotic microbiome structure, physicochemistry, and Enterococcus abundance. Results: Alternative management influenced observed richness and phylogenetic diversity and was associated with lower relative abundance of Enterococcus, including E. cecorum and E. hirae group. Sequencing- and dPCR-derived Enterococcus abundance estimates were correlated across samples; however, treatment-associated differences in relative abundance were not consistently accompanied by lower absolute copy number at terminal sampling, indicating changes in proportional representation rather than uniform reductions in Enterococcus abundance. In complementary in vitro assays, isolate responses to the postbiotic were strain-, concentration-, and time-dependent and were not uniformly sustained. Responses near the nominal application-mixture range were modest, whereas the largest and most persistent reductions in viable recovery occurred only at higher concentrations. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate that alternative litter management can alter prokaryotic community structure and the proportional representation of selected bacterial taxa under commercial production conditions while maintaining comparable flock performance. Collectively, the field and in vitro observations are more consistent with broader management-associated restructuring of the litter microbial community than with sustained direct antimicrobial effects, providing a basis for microbiome-informed approaches to understanding and managing litter ecology across successive production cycles.

papers.title: Comparative metabolomics identifies recurrent age-associated pathway remodeling across species
papers.abstract: Aging is accompanied by widespread metabolic change, but it remains unclear which features are shared across species with different physiology, lifespan, and sampling contexts. To address this, we employed a pathway-centered comparative metabolomics framework to evaluate age-associated metabolic remodeling across wild African savanna elephant, mouse, and Drosophila melanogaster. Drosophila provided a controlled adult time course to map age-associated metabolite trajectories, while mouse and elephant plasma datasets allowed us to test whether these pathway signatures extended to mammalian aging. Adult Drosophila showed extensive metabolomic remodeling, with significant metabolites organizing into distinct temporal trajectory classes. Cross-species aging-associated metabolic correspondence was more apparent at the pathway level than at the level of individual metabolites. Pathway scores derived from Drosophila increased progressively with fly age, successfully distinguished young and old mice, and captured age-associated stratification across the elephant lifespan. Notably, lipid metabolism, particularly carnitine and fatty acid metabolism, together with nucleotide-related pathways, consistently emerged as the core features of aging across analyses. These findings suggest pathway-level metabolic remodeling is a recurrent feature of cross-species aging.

papers.title: Prefrontal activation predicts response latency and is shaped by age and lifestyle
papers.abstract: Neurological and neuropsychiatric conditions affect 43% of the global population, many shaped by modifiable lifestyle exposures, yet their relationship to cortical haemodynamics is poorly characterised. The dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) is a particularly tractable target: it underpins executive function, is disrupted across neuropsychiatric and age-related conditions, and lies on the cortical surface, within reach of scalable optical neuroimaging. We present LUCID, a longitudinal study of 98 healthy adults combining consumer wearable sleep and physical activity metrics with task-evoked dlPFC haemodynamics, measured by time-domain functional near-infrared spectroscopy (TD-fNIRS). Log-transformed peak dlPFC activation was negatively associated with response latency during the Switching Stroop task in both hemispheres (r = -0.32 to -0.38), with stronger associations for the maximum response gradient (r = -0.46 to -0.48), such that greater haemodynamic responses accompanied faster responses. Peak activation showed moderate test-retest reliability (intraclass correlation coefficient, ICC = 0.57-0.69), with between-person variance exceeding within-person fluctuation. Activation was lower in older age groups and higher in females across both tasks. In a subset of 36 participants with complete wearable data, exploratory models combining demographic, lifestyle and scan-quality features predicted bilateral activation under participant-grouped cross-validation (R-squared = 0.29-0.37), more consistently than task performance, with sex, recent change in REM sleep and age among the strongest participant-level contributors. Together, these findings identify task-evoked dlPFC haemodynamics as a repeatable, behaviourally relevant candidate functional marker, with potential for longitudinal investigation of lifestyle-associated variation in brain function.

papers.title: Early Pitx2 modulation of Fgf10 directs asymmetric lung morphology
papers.abstract: Most of the visceral organs are anatomically asymmetric across the left-right axis. These asymmetries can be traced to a well-studied molecular cascade leading to left-sided expression of a series of genes in the early embryo. One of the key genes in this left-sided cascade is the transcription factor Pitx2, which is transiently expressed throughout the left lateral plate mesoderm. Yet how these early differences in gene expression are converted into differential shaping of organs at later stages remains incompletely understood, and for many organs, such as the lung, the question has not even been explored. Similarly, while the signaling pathways responsible for the branching morphogenesis of the lung have been intensively studied, no insight has been reported regarding how the described gene regulatory network is modified to produce differences in morphology on the left and right sides. Here we identify Fgf10 as a Pitx2-sensitive signal in the mesenchyme of the developing mouse lung. Fgf10 expression increases as Pitx2 decreases, making the right lung, which lacks Pitx2 expression, grow faster than the left during the budding stage. Modulating Fgf10 dosage in the left mesenchyme is sufficient to alter lung budding asymmetry. At the cellular level, Fgf10-dependent lung growth is due to increased levels of epithelial proliferation, without significant differences in directional migration into the mesenchyme. Conditional genetics further show that Pitx2 activity is required exclusively during the early budding stage. Early Pitx2 is sufficient to establish differences in the primary airway branches. These differences in initial conditions are sufficient to direct the subsequent asymmetric branching patterns that eventually manifest as the left-right differences in lung morphology. Thus, Pitx2 converts left-right mesenchymal identity into organ asymmetry by quantitatively tuning Fgf10-dependent epithelial growth during early lung organogenesis.

papers.title: TCR signal strength during positive selection shapes CD25 expression patterns on thymically derived regulatory T cells
papers.abstract: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are a suppressive subset of CD4 T cells that maintain immune homeostasis. Most Tregs develop in the thymus but how thymic selection impacts peripheral Treg fate remains unknown. Here we show that the strength of TCR signal experienced during positive selection in the thymic cortex impacts how CD4 SP thymocytes respond to Treg inducing signals in the medulla. Thymocytes that experienced weak signals during positive selection (identified as CD5LO CD4 SP) show a greater dependence on TGF-{beta} than IL-2 for Treg induction and produce Foxp3+ cells that lack constitutive expression of the classic Treg marker CD25. Moreover, CD4 clones that give rise to CD25- thymic Tregs also produce CD25- peripheral Tregs. These data indicate that positive selection provides critical context for how CD4 T cells respond to TCR agonist and cytokine signals, leading to an alternative lineage of Tregs that lacks constitutive CD25 expression.

papers.title: Physics-driven self-supervised learning for quantitative high-fidelity structured illumination microscopy
papers.abstract: Structured illumination microscopy (SIM) enables rapid, long-term super-resolution (SR) imaging of live-cell dynamics. However, current SIM reconstruction methods, although achieving high structural fidelity, generally lack reliable intensity quantification. Here we present qHiFi-SIM, a physics-driven self-supervised learning framework for quantitative high-fidelity SIM imaging. By leveraging the wide-field (WF) image as a physical intensity reference and conventional SIM reconstruction as a structural continuity prior, qHiFi-SIM enables self-supervised training without ground-truth intensity data. It achieves structural fidelity comparable to HiFi-SIM while maintaining excellent intensity linearity at the SIM point-spread function scale (R2 > 0.986, mean intensity ratio near 1). The framework transfers across diverse SIM setups and typical samples, and directly improves the intensity linearity of other state-of-the-art algorithms without retraining. We demonstrate its utility for live-cell quantitative visualization of mitochondrial intensity dynamics and high-fidelity SIM-FRET functional imaging, offering a practical tool for SR structural visualization and quantitative functional imaging in live cells.

papers.title: A Plasmodium falciparum Pangenome Resource to Drive Structural Variant Discovery and to assist Malaria Control
papers.abstract: Plasmodium falciparum, the deadliest causative agent of malaria, harbours extensive structural variation that underlies key biological processes including drug resistance and diagnostic evasion. Here, we present PfPan, a P. falciparum pangenome constructed from 13 geographically diverse high-quality reference genomes using Minigraph-Cactus, adding 4.77 Mb of sequence beyond the 3D7 linear reference. We identify over 5,000 structural variants (SVs) across the reference genomes and demonstrate improved genotyping using the vg toolkit compared to linear reference-based approaches, with comparable performance for small variant discovery. Benchmarking against assembly-derived truth sets confirms pangenome superiority for structural variant detection, particularly at complex and hypervariable loci. Applying PfPan to 878 globally sampled P. falciparum whole-genome sequences, we characterise biologically and clinically relevant SVs, including the complex drug resistance-linked gch1 locus, and explore deletions upstream of the coding sequence for the diagnostic target HRP2. PfPan provides a foundational resource for mitigating reference bias in P. falciparum genomic surveillance and establishes a framework for improved detection of variants associated with drug resistance and malaria control in monoclonal P. falciparum samples that have not undergone selective whole-genome amplification.

papers.title: Obligate multicellularity circumvents population genetic barriers to collective-level adaptation
papers.abstract: 'Complex' multicellularity has evolved in five eukaryotic lineages, all of which develop clonally and are obligately multicellular (i.e., lack a reproductive unicellular phase). Clonal development is well-established as a critical factor promoting multicellular adaptation by limiting within-group conflict, but little is known about the evolutionary consequences of obligate multicellularity itself. Here, we show that obligate multicellularity alleviates an establishment barrier to collective-level adaptation. We engineered a single strain of snowflake yeast ( Saccharomyces cerevisiae ) capable of exhibiting obligately multicellular, facultatively multicellular, or obligately unicellular life cycles, and evolved them under selection for larger group size. All five obligately multicellular populations rapidly evolved larger groups, primarily through whole genome duplication. Facultative populations were far more constrained, with tetraploidy evolving in only 2/10 populations, despite this trait being strongly beneficial across the full life cycle. Mathematical modeling suggests that group formation and opposing selection across life cycle phases interact, increasing the chance that mutations beneficial across the full life cycle are lost before they establish. These results suggest that clonality and obligate multicellularity jointly create the conditions for complex multicellularity to evolve, one by suppressing within-group conflict, the other by removing population genetic barriers to collective-level adaptation.

papers.title: Coarse-graining metabolic networks via feature learning reveals cross-species growth predictors
papers.abstract: Bacterial growth and the underlying metabolic networks are highly dissimilar across species, posing a fundamental challenge for various bioengineering tasks. For a given species across nutrient environments, growth is regulated via proteome allocation, which gives rise to linear relationships between growth and the fractions of coarse-grained proteome sectors. However, it remains unclear whether there are coarse-grained predictors that correlate with growth across species monocultures in a given environment. Here, simulating genome-scale metabolic models, we discover two conserved growth predictors: the number of nutrients utilized, and a set of metabolic sectors that we identify by coarse-graining metabolic networks via feature learning. We find evidence supporting both predictors in recent experiments; notably, the proteome fractions of the sectors correlate with growth across species in a gene expression dataset. We further analyze coarse-grained networks to show that interactions between sectors improve growth predictions. Our work provides a framework to investigate how coarse-grained growth predictors emerge across diverse metabolic networks.

papers.title: A Rarefaction Approach to Identify Local Introgression in a Three Population Tree
papers.abstract: The $D$ statistic, also known as the $ABBA-BABA$ statistic, is widely used to detect the presence of archaic genome-wide introgression between two non-sister taxa. $D$ counts the imbalance between the number of biallelic sites where either the second and third taxa (ABBA site) share the derived allele or the first and third taxa (BABA site) share the derived allele in a four taxa tree. Here, the fourth taxon acts as an outgroup to determine the ancestral allele. When there is no introgression, these counts are expected to be equal, and a discordance between counts suggests introgression from the third taxon into either the first or second. D is limited to the detection of genome-wide introgression and exhibits a high false-positive rate when applied to smaller genomic segments. Here, we present a new method, D STatistic with Allelic Rarefaction ($\dstar$), to address these limitations. $\dstar$ uses multiple lineages and does not require an outgroup to calculate the imbalance between the number of alleles found exclusively in the second and third taxa and the number of alleles found exclusively in the first and third taxa. $\dstar$ employs a rarefaction technique to correct for unequal sample-size and allows multiallelic sites. We use simulations to show that $\dstar$ has better precision and recall for detecting introgressed segments of DNA when compared to other methods. We conclude by recovering Denisovan DNA related to immune function in modern day Papuans. Precompiled executables, the manual, source code, and simulation and analysis scripts used in this study can be found at \url{https://github.com/TQ-Smith/DSTAR}

papers.title: BRIDGE prioritizes human and mouse gene correspondences using functional and disease evidence
papers.abstract: Selecting mouse genes to model human disease requires evidence that a perturbation represents the biological function of interest. Orthology provides an evolutionary reference, but does not by itself resolve disease-related functional differences between species. We present BRIDGE, a framework that combines species-labelled disease associations and functional annotations through graph representations, optimal transport and rank fusion to prioritize human-mouse gene correspondences. The rankings include non-orthologous candidates and distinguish alternative effectors, distributed signalling modules and multiple human genes linked to one mouse counterpart. BRIDGE achieved 61.8-66.7% Recall@5 across three functional-correspondence benchmarks. In 25 curated drug-translation cases, 15 parsed mouse targets ranked first; a separate phenotype-informed screen retained 54 of 533 candidates in the final processed dataset. These results organize gene selection around the function a disease experiment must interrogate and nominate hypotheses for individual or combined perturbations. Because the benchmarks partly reuse annotation evidence, retrieval does not establish phenotypic or pharmacological equivalence. BRIDGE provides a basis for reviewing mouse genes before disease-model construction or drug screening, and for investigating how disease-associated functions are distributed across mammalian genes. These applications require disease-specific experimental validation.

papers.title: A knowledge graph-guided framework for multitask single-cell analysis
papers.abstract: Connecting cell identity to biological function is central to understanding how tumors change during treatment. Here, we introduce scKNIFE, a knowledge-guided nonnegative matrix factorization framework that integrates gene expression with a heterogeneous graph of functional annotations, metabolic reactions and metabolites, and signaling interactions. scKNIFE jointly learns cellular rep resentations and biological-entity loadings, linking the factors that organize cells to their constituent genes and connected functions. Across breast-cancer cohorts, the learned representations retained broad cellular organization without using per-cell identity labels as factorization targets. scKNIFE identified baseline tumor programs associated with subsequent clinical response or T-cell clonotype expansion and resolved treatment-associated functional variation within immune and stromal popula tions. In a seven-patient triple-negative breast cancer atlas, analysis alongside tissue metabolomics identified distinct trajectories of inferred fatty acid activation and carnitine-associated activities, in cluding higher myeloid L-octanoylcarnitine scores at biopsy in all seven patients. Communication analysis further resolved an endothelial-perivascular PDGF connection with lower inferred scores at surgery in six patients. scKNIFE brings cellular identity, metabolic programs and candidate intercellular communication into one representation, enabling functional interpretation of tumor heterogeneity across patients and treatment states.

papers.title: Uptake of CD36 and its natural and therapeutic ligands by clathrin-mediated endocytosis
papers.abstract: The scavenger receptor CD36 mediates cellular uptake of diverse extracellular ligands including long-chain fatty acids. Recent work has demonstrated that CD36 is also required for uptake of bulky, amphipathic therapeutic compounds including proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs). However, because the mechanism by which cells internalize CD36 itself remains unknown, how its diverse ligands enter cells has remained mysterious. CD36 has been thought to associate with caveolae, flask-like invaginations of the plasma membrane, yet recent reports have cast doubt on the role of these structures in protein trafficking. Using live cell imaging, we show that CD36 strongly colocalizes with sites of clathrin-mediated endocytosis, where it concentrates both long-chain fatty acids and PROTACs. In contrast, neither CD36 nor its ligands colocalized substantially with caveolae. Further, we identify previously unrecognized binding interactions between CD36 and the clathrin machinery, which help to explain recruitment of CD36 and its ligands to endocytic sites. Importantly, disruption of clathrin assembly inhibits endocytic uptake of both long-chain fatty acids and PROTACs, and abolished PROTAC-induced degradation of multiple target proteins that utilize diverse E3 enzymes. These results suggest that clathrin-mediated endocytosis is essential for internalization of CD36 and its ligands, offering new insights into diverse diseases that rely on CD36 for ligand import, and potentially inspiring new strategies for optimizing targeted protein degraders.

papers.title: Bacterial metabolites alter the consequences of reduced insulin signaling in C. elegans via increasing the expression of the acid sphingomyelinase asm-3.
papers.abstract: Individuals consuming an identical diet often exhibit vast differences in their physiological response to the same nutrients. Studies of identical twins and genetically identical laboratory animals have both shown that much of this variability cannot be explained by differences in genetics. Differences in gut microbes and local microflora have emerged as a leading potential source of this variability, but mechanistic investigations of three-way host-microbe-diet interactions are difficult in most animals. Here, we find that dietary sugar availability suppresses the longevity, dauer formation and gene expression changes of daf-2 (insulin-like receptor) mutants fed Escherichia coli OP50, but not daf-2 mutants fed many other bacteria. To determine how sugar availability and bacteria intersect to affect C. elegans insulin signaling we conducted transposon mutagenesis screens and found that the effects of sugar availability on C. elegans insulin signaling depend on bacterial pyruvate dehydrogenase activity. We further found that reducing bacterial pyruvate dehydrogenase activity results in increased pyruvate and lactate accumulation and induced host expression of the acid sphingomyelinase asm-3. Lastly, we find that asm-3 is required for the loss of pyruvate dehydrogenase activity to alter the phenotype of daf-2 mutants. Collectively, our findings establish a novel link between bacterial pyruvate metabolism and host insulin signaling that is mediated by altering the expression of a host acid sphingomyelinase.

papers.title: The distribution of fitness effects of new mutations in regulatory regions of the D. melanogaster genome
papers.abstract: Although non-coding regions play important roles in gene regulation and contribute to individual fitness, the precise distribution of fitness effects (DFE) of new mutations in these regions remains poorly understood. Here, we carefully compile experimentally validated regulatory regions in non-coding regions in the Drosophila melanogaster genome and identify putatively neutral sites near them. Incorporating a realistic genomic architecture that mimics the placement of the regulatory and coding regions, as well as a realistic heterogeneity in recombination and mutation rates across the genome, we use forward-in-time simulations to assess the power and accuracy of population genetics approaches that infer the DFE of new mutations in these regions. While the parameters of DFEs primarily comprising moderately and strongly deleterious mutations are estimated accurately, those of DFEs comprising mostly mildly deleterious mutations are misinferred. Applying these insights to three African D. melanogaster populations, we find that a large fraction of new mutations in functionally important non-coding regions are moderately deleterious, as opposed to strongly deleterious in coding regions. While the fraction of beneficial substitutions in regulatory regions (0.25-0.45) was also lower in coding regions (~0.5), our results suggest that non-coding regions contribute a majority of new deleterious mutations and beneficial substitutions in D. melanogaster populations. By incorporating both the genomic distribution and the inferred DFE of non-coding regions, we demonstrate that the effects of background selection across the genome are more accurately captured than with coding regions alone, highlighting the importance of considering selection on non-coding regions when interpreting patterns of genomic variation.

papers.title: Individual-to-individual mapping of color similarity structures: Is my "red" relationally your "red"?
papers.abstract: Is my "red" the same as your "red"? Although we cannot directly test whether two individuals' experiences (qualia) are identical, we reframe this question as an empirical one: whether my "red" is relationally your "red". We addressed this question by finding the best possible mappings between color similarity structures across individuals, without using color labels. We collected a complete set of similarity judgments across 93 colors from each of 11 participants and compared their structures. These comparisons revealed two groups of four participants in this sample whose structures aligned robustly within each group: the best possible mappings matched the same color stimuli, such as my "red" to your "red". Between groups, however, the best mappings did not match the same stimuli. The remaining participants showed structural variations that did not fit either group. This framework opens a path to classifying diverse color experiences through their relational structures.

papers.title: Anaerobic methane oxidation by ANME-2a at 2 M chloride in the Orca Basin halocline
papers.abstract: Anaerobic methane oxidation, typically mediated by consortia of archaea and bacteria, is a key process in the global methane cycle, but little is known about its upper salinity limits. We characterized the microbial methane cycle in the anoxic, hypersaline Orca Basin using metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, fluorescence in situ hybridization, and geochemical measurements at sub-meter resolution. In the brine, we detected transcriptional activity of the halophilic methylotrophic methanogen Methanohalophilus, consistent with a biological source for Orca Basin methane. In the particle-rich halocline (~2 M Cl-; ~2235 meters depth), high mcrA transcription by a novel ANME-2a species was co-located with a positive shift in {delta}13C-CH4 consistent with anaerobic oxidation of methane. ANME-2a also transcribed genes for biosynthesis of the osmolyte N({epsilon})-acetyl-{beta}-L-lysine, supporting adaptation to hypersaline conditions. At the same depth, consortia of sarcina-like archaea, likely ANME-2a, were observed in association with vibrioid and filamentous bacteria. Members of a halotolerant Desulfobulbales genus (family SURF-16, which includes the previously identified ANME partner Seep-DBB) were active at the same depth. At and above the oxic-anoxic interface, aerobic methane oxidation appears to be mediated by three genera of uncultivated Methylococcales bacteria. Our results extend the known upper salinity range of ANME-2a to ~2 M Cl- and reveal the key microbial players in the methane bio-filter between the Orca Basin brine and overlying seawater.

papers.title: TAG-IN, a modular strategy for swappable endogenous gene tagging in Caenorhabditis elegans
papers.abstract: Endogenous gene tagging allows researchers to study genes in their native genomic context, underscoring the need for efficient gene tagging approaches. Here, we report TAG-IN, a streamlined strategy for swappable gene tagging in C. elegans. TAG-IN begins with generating a seed allele for a gene of interest by inserting a small landing pad containing two distinct recombination sites (FRT and FRT3) into the desired tagging locus using CRISPR. Fusion or co-expression tags from reusable tag donors can then be easily swapped into the seed allele using Flp recombinase-mediated cassette exchange (RMCE). Successful TAG-IN alleles can be conveniently identified via drug selection without PCR screening. The tag-swapping step can be accomplished by simple genetic crossing, in addition to traditional microinjection. To facilitate the use of TAG-IN, we also built a library of plug-and-play tag donor strains that can be crossed with seed alleles to insert the corresponding tags and a set of vectors to construct new tag donors. The TAG-IN strategy is both modular and combinatorial: only a single seed allele for each tagging locus is needed to insert any tag; a single tag donor strain can be used to swap the tag into any compatible seed allele. Furthermore, TAG-IN allows iterative tag insertion because the FRT and FRT3 sites are preserved during RMCE, so each TAG-IN allele can serve as a landing pad for further rounds of tag exchange. Thus, TAG-IN provides an efficient, flexible, and scalable platform for endogenous gene tagging in C. elegans, accelerating comprehensive functional studies.

papers.title: Pannexin-1 regulates cellular identity and excitability in the developing cortex
papers.abstract: Mutations in genes encoding a range of ion-conducting proteins disrupt development of the cerebral cortex in humans, often causing polymicrogyria (PMG); yet how ion conduction guides the development of cortical architecture is not clear. Here, we describe three individuals with brain malformations including PMG and microcephaly in whom de novo, missense mutations were identified in PANX1--encoding an ATP and ion conducting channel. We show that these PMG-associated PANX1 mutations (p.D14H, p.M37R, and p.N338T) disrupt normal glycosylation and confer gain-of-function with respect to ATP release and channel conductance. In vivo modeling of mutant PANX1 in cortical progenitor cells demonstrated disrupted cell migration and excess cell death in both mice and ferret models. In vitro modeling of the p.N338T allele in human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived neurons further revealed changes in neuronal morphology and increased excitability, and dysregulation of key transcription factors critical for neurogenesis and cell fate. In addition, p.N338T iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells displayed increased PANX1 activation. Our results show that normal PANX1 function contributes to cortical structure through regulation of ion conductance and ATP release and provides insight into how these processes influence corticogenesis and cytoarchitecture more broadly.

papers.title: Structural basis for start codon selection by eIF5-mimic proteins
papers.abstract: Start codon selection extensively regulates the cellular proteome and is implicated in cancer and other diseases. The eIF5-mimic proteins (5MPs: 5MP1/BZW2 and 5MP2/BZW1) restrict non-AUG start codon usage and thereby reprogram proteoform expression from mRNAs with alternative start sites, such as the oncogenic c-Myc. Here, using in extracto cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and biochemical assays, we report how 5MP represses translation dependent on the sequence context at start codons. Cryo-EM structures of 48S pre-initiation complexes (PICs) reveal 5MP1 bound at the A site of the small ribosomal subunit. 5MPs act as initiation factors that stabilize an open PIC conformation, promoting mRNA scanning and inhibiting initiation at suboptimal start codons. We propose to designate 5MP as eIF1S (eukaryotic Initiation Factor 1 Scanning). These findings reveal the structural basis for proteome modulation by 5MPs and may help correct dysregulated translation in disease.

papers.title: spaTransfer: transfer learning for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data using non-negative matrix factorization
papers.abstract: Recent advances in spatially-resolved transcriptomics have enabled profiling of gene expression in a spatial context, which has led to the generation of large-scale single-cell and spatial atlases with computationally-derived cell type or spatial domain labels. An increasingly important task with these data has become the transfer of cell type or spatial domain annotations from a given reference (or source) atlas into a new target tissue or sample. The reference and target datasets could be at different resolutions or measured on different experimental platforms. Here, we present a method to perform cross-platform transfer learning that takes as input single-cell or spatial domain labels from a reference atlas or dataset and transfers the labels to a target dataset at a similar or different resolution. Specifically, we use non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) on the reference data to identify factors associated with labels of interest and project these factors into the target dataset to label each new observation. We use a multinomial model with the factors as covariates and labels as the response to predict labels in the target dataset. In contrast to existing approaches, the advantage of our approach is interpretability, without compromising on accuracy. We demonstrate the performance of the method in two human brain tissues and show that our model identifies spatially coherent domains in the target datasets with concordance of marker gene expression. We implement spaTransfer in open-source software as an R package (github.com/cindyfang70/spaTransfer).

papers.title: Genotype-associated transcriptional differences among grapevine lines carrying single and pyramided Rpv resistance loci
papers.abstract: Downy mildew caused by Plasmopara viticola is a major threat to grapevine production, yet the molecular organization of multilocus resistance remains poorly understood. We generated 36 time-resolved transcriptomes from grapevine genotypes carrying single (Rpv12), double (Rpv12+1), or triple (Rpv12+1+3) resistance loci together with a susceptible control and integrated co-transcriptional network analysis with systematic AlphaFold2-Multimer screening to identify candidate immune receptor complexes. A SOBIR1-associated receptor network emerged as a candidate interaction hub, with seven predicted partners enriched for leucine-rich repeat receptor-like proteins and kinases. Five partner genes showed coordinated transcript upregulation at inoculation (0 hpi) specifically in Rpv12 genotypes, whereas this signature was absent in multilocus backgrounds, suggesting genotype-specific regulatory restructuring rather than additive immune activation. Four of the seven partners were also predicted to interact with a grapevine EIX1 homolog, which itself was predicted to associate with SOBIR1 (ipTM = 0.81), consistent with the established tomato LeEIX-SOBIR1 co-receptor architecture. We additionally identified predicted structurally conserved EDS1-SAG101 candidate complexes despite substantial sequence divergence from Arabidopsis orthologs. Multilocus genotypes displayed distinct temporal transcriptional trajectories and altered co-transcriptional network organization, indicating that resistance stacking reshapes immune regulatory architecture. However, whether these transcriptional differences correspond to enhanced, equivalent, or reduced resistance requires quantitative phenotypic validation. Together, these results provide a structural and transcriptomic framework for investigating immune receptor organization in grapevine and generate testable hypotheses for functional dissection of multilocus resistance.

papers.title: Bayesian causal inference unifies perceptual and neuronal processing of center-surround motion in area MT
papers.abstract: Center-surround interactions are a hallmark of visual processing and are especially prominent in area MT, where surround motion can either suppress or facilitate neuronal responses depending on context. However, existing mechanistic descriptions, including divisive normalization, do not explain the full diversity of these effects or their relationship to motion perception. Here, we show that both perceptual and neuronal center-surround phenomena can be understood as consequences of Bayesian causal inference over reference frames. Building on a normative model of motion perception, we derived predictions for the mean responses and variability of single MT neurons across the full four-dimensional space of center and surround directions and speeds. The model generates structured patterns of suppression, facilitation, and coordinate-frame selectivity that qualitatively match the diversity of center-surround effects reported in primate MT. Our results provide a unified computational account linking motion integration and segmentation in perception with contextual response modulation in MT, and yield testable predictions for how the visual system infers and represents reference frames.

papers.title: Refining Feulgen: low-cost and accurate genome size measurements for everyone
papers.abstract: Feulgen image analysis densitometry (FIAD) has been extensively used for decades to measure genome sizes, but is usually considered less precise and less reproducible compared to other methods such as flow cytometry (FCM). However, FCM requires fresh tissue samples, which is a major impediment to using it on specimens collected in the field far from the lab. By contrast, FIAD works on ethanol-preserved samples kept at room temperature, which is a huge advantage for biodiversity genomics. In this study, we present refinements on the Feulgen protocol and downstream analyses that produce measurements at least as reliable and precise as those obtained using whole-genome sequencing. We verify using seven standards (including both animals and plants) that our refined approach yields accurate results across a 440-fold range of genome sizes. To illustrate the usefulness of our approach, we use it to measure for the first time the genome size of the red bald uakari monkey Cacajao rubicundus using the American cockroach Periplaneta americana and the black garden ant Lasius niger as standards, and confirm our 2.67 pg result by comparing it with a whole-genome assembly obtained from nanopore sequencing of the same individual.

papers.title: A Nonlinear Dynamics Framework for Mutation-Selection Balance Reveals Dominance-Dependent Bistability in Auto- and Allotetraploids
papers.abstract: Polyploidy and whole genome duplication (WGD) are widespread biological phenomena with substantial cellular, meiotic, and genetic effects. Despite their prevalence and significance across the tree of life, population genetics theory for polyploids is not well developed. The lack of theoretical models limits our understanding of polyploid evolution and restricts our ability to harness polyploidy for crop improvement amidst increasing environmental stress. To address this gap, we developed and analyzed deterministic models of mutation-selection balance for tetraploids under polysomic (autotetraploid) and disomic (allotetraploid) inheritance patterns and arbitrary dominance relationships. We also introduced a new mathematical framework based on ordinary differential equations and nonlinear dynamics for analyzing the models. We find that the autotetraploid and allotetraploid models generally exhibit negligible differences in mutation load and allele frequency at mutation-selection balance. Our model also reveals two bistable points of mutation-selection balance for dominant alleles with biased mutation rates over a wide range of selection coefficients in the tetraploid models compared to bistability in only a narrow range for diploids. In addition, for overdominant mutations, we find a distinct equilibrium structure with bistable equilibria in only the allotetraploid model. Finally, using discrete time simulations, we explore the temporal dynamics of allele frequency and fitness change and show that the presence of bistability and bifurcations fundamentally alters the temporal dynamics of allele frequency and load. Overall, this work develops foundational theoretical models that will facilitate the development of population genetic models and methodologies to study evolution in empirical tetraploid populations.

papers.title: Cortex-Wide, Cellular-Resolution Volumetric Imaging with a Modular Two-Photon Imaging Platform
papers.abstract: Mapping cortex-wide neuronal activity at single-cell resolution has been limited by the physical trade-off between numerical aperture and field-of-view (FOV) in two-photon microscopes. We present Meso2P, a modular two-photon platform that decouples excitation and detection by introducing a lateral paraboloid fluorescence collector. The design sustains an effective NA 0.87 over a contiguous 6 * 6 mm^2 FOV at high speed (2,048 * 2,048 pixels at 7.67 Hz). The modular platform can be upgraded with optional modules for simultaneous multi-plane imaging (1-4 planes at full resolution and speed), volumetric imaging (6 * 6 * 0.5mm^3, 2,048 * 2,048 * 28 voxels at 1Hz capturing > 210,000 neurons), and holographic two-photon optogenetic stimulation for targeted perturbations. To handle the resulting large-scale data, we provide an open-source deep-learning pipeline that automates motion correction, segmentation, and spike inference. We demonstrate cortex-wide sensory responses, layer-specific network synchrony during anaesthesia, and in-vivo tracking of micro- and nanoplastic distribution. Meso2P therefore provides a reproducible route to high-throughput volumetric imaging across almost the entire cortex with high detection efficiency.

papers.title: Amendable decisions in living systems
papers.abstract: A distinct feature of living systems is their capacity to take decisions based on uncertain environmental signals. Examples span from the microscopic scale of cell differentiation guided by the concentration of a morphogen, to complex choices made by animals and humans. The current paradigm in decision theory assumes that decisions, once taken, cannot be revoked. However, living systems often amend their decisions if new evidence favors an alternative hypothesis. In this paper, we characterize the optimal strategy for such amendable decisions. We find that, unlike irrevocable decisions, optimal amendable decisions can be made in a finite average time with zero error probability. Our theory successfully predicts the outcome of a visual experiment involving human participants and the accuracy of cell-fate decisions in early development. We also present possible implementations of amendable decision-making by means of either biochemical reactions or transcription regulation. Our study reveals that amendments lead to a substantial advantage in decision making, that is likely to be widely exploited by living beings.

papers.title: Widespread and Abundant CRISPR-Cas Systems in the Deep Ocean
papers.abstract: CRISPR-Cas systems have revolutionized modern biology. Most CRISPR-Cas systems used for biotechnological applications derive from cultivated bacteria, but evidence suggests that environmental microbiomes harbor an untapped diversity of these systems. Understanding of which environmental and biological factors drive the prevalence of CRISPR-Cas systems remains limited. A search for CRISPR-Cas systems was conducted among 176 globally-distributed marine metagenomes from the Malaspina expedition, including free-living and particle-attached microbiomes with emphasis on the deep ocean. CRISPR-Cas systems were more abundant in the deep ocean than in the surface and among free-living compared to particle-attached communities, reflecting the higher abundance of archaea and their viruses in these habitats. We identified 1,146 CRISPR-cas loci, some displaying unique architectures. A total of 48 Cas9 proteins were identified, many of which are potentially novel. These discoveries expand the diversity of CRISPR-Cas and point at the deep-sea as a reservoir for future bioprospecting efforts of these resources.

papers.title: VIOLIN: A modular framework for scalable reconciliation of heterogeneous interaction graphs
papers.abstract: Automated extraction of molecular interactions from scientific literature has outpaced the development of systematic methods for integrating this information with curated models and knowledge graphs. Here we present VIOLIN (Versatile Interaction Organizing to Leverage Information in Networks), a configurable, attribute-aware reconciliation framework that formally compares newly extracted interaction lists against structured baseline graphs. VIOLIN classifies each interaction as a corroboration, contradiction, flagged case, or extension, and supports configurable attribute inclusion strategies and mismatch semantics to adjust reconciliation strictness. We evaluate VIOLIN using interaction lists generated by two traditional NLP systems (REACH, INDRA) and two large language models (GPT-4.1, Llama 3) across multiple literature corpora and structurally distinct baseline graphs. Across all conditions, reconciliation outcomes were stable and interpretable, with extensions dominating and corroboration-contradiction balance reflecting intrinsic structural relationships between baseline graphs and extracted evidence. Sensitivity analyses demonstrate that attribute inclusion and classification scheme selection shift category boundaries predictably. Benchmark evaluations confirm high algorithmic correctness and alignment with expert curation. VIOLIN is publicly available as a Python package and through web-based interface (https://nmzlab.github.io/Tools-UI).

papers.title: Transiently-elevated dopamine triggers plasticity that preserves motor function, striatal neuron morphology, and thalamostriatal input in a mouse model of Parkinson's disease
papers.abstract: Loss of nigrostriatal dopamine (DA) neurons in Parkinson's disease (PD) produces motor symptoms by disrupting the normal circuitry of striatal projection neurons. Here, we report that the Transient Elevation of Dopamine (TED) within a defined window of 6-OHDA-induced DA depletion preserves normal motor behaviorfor months. We also observed a preservation of mature spines specifically on direct pathway striatal projection neurons (dSPNs) and not indirect pathway striatal projection neurons (iSPNs). Preservation of motor behavior and dSPN spines required enhanced activation of striatal D1 receptors. Circuit mapping showed input from primary motor cortex was reduced, while input from parafascicular thalamus was unchanged in both TED mice and controls of both sexes, suggesting rewiring of excitatory inputs to dSPNs from other cortical or thalamic areas in TED mice. Lastly, thalamostriatal paired pulse facilitation, normally depressed following DA depletion, is preserved in TED mice. Although the causal basis of motor preservation remains unresolved, our findings reveal that a schedule of transiently increasing striatal DA surrounding the depletion of dopamine can engage a long-lasting plasticity that markedly delays the onset of motor impairment

papers.title: Alignment-free sequence composition based features can distinguish paralogous proteins
papers.abstract: Paralogous proteins have a common ancestor but have diverged in functionality. Homology- and similarity-based methods often fail to distinguish paralogous proteins, due to a nuanced sequence-function relationship that remains largely intractable. Going beyond these methods, we extract various sequence composition based feature representations from proteins and use the same to train classifiers for distinguishing paralog pairs. We consider 20 paralog pair datasets and train a linear support vector machine (SVM) classifier for each dataset to distinguish among them. Amino acid composition (AAC) and 2-ordered amino acid composition (2-OAAC) features achieve high predictive performance across these datasets, despite the low sample size and potential label noise. Furthermore, we utilise the marginal contribution feature importance (MCI) to identify specific amino acids driving classification. We show that retaining only the top-$k$ MCI-ranked amino acids preserves nearly all predictive power while acting as a regularizer. Structural mapping of these top-ranked features in families such as globins, tubulins, and histones reveals that they frequently localise to critical functional and oligomerisation interfaces. Ultimately, our interpretable machine learning framework successfully bridges sequence composition and protein activity, providing a scalable computational method for identifying potential functional determinants that can guide future wet-lab site-directed mutagenesis experiments to study protein function.

papers.title: Scalable subclonal reconstruction of cancer cells in DNA sequencing data using a penalized likelihood model
papers.abstract: Background Characterizing intratumor heterogeneity and subclonal architecture from bulk DNA sequencing provides important insights into cancer evolution. However, existing subclonal reconstruction methods remain computationally demanding, hindering iterative quality control and reproducible application across large genomic cohorts. Methods Distinct from existing likelihood-based and Bayesian approaches, we developed CliPP (Clonal structure identification through Pairwise Penalization), utilizing machine learning to add pairwise fusion penalty to the full likelihood, in order to simultaneously estimate mutation cellular prevalence and fuse compatible estimates into clusters without prespecifying the number of clusters. We benchmarked CliPP in three simulation datasets comprising 5,256 tumors for accuracy, and further evaluated its concordance with consensus calls in 2,008 tumors profiled by whole-genome sequencing from the Pan-Cancer Analysis of Whole Genomes (PCAWG) study. We then applied a standardized, quality-controlled workflow to whole-exome sequencing data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), yielding a high-confidence cohort of 5,424 tumors across 31 cancer types. Within this cohort, we mapped the clonality of 13,960 high-confidence driver mutations in 4,375 tumors.
